Congress of Graduate Students
Room 3251, New Student Union, Student Government Association, Florida State University
So, what is COGS?
The Congress of Graduate Students (COGS) is the official representative body of all
post baccalaureate, special, masters, specialist, professional, and doctoral students at
Florida State University.
In accordance to the Student Government Constitution, COGS is a funding board of the
Student Government Association solely responsible for allocating all of the A&S fees it
receives from graduate students to graduate students each year.
Who will I be representing?
Each college and school of FSU is represented through liaisons (representative of
COGS, hopefully you) to lobby and address needs of their prospective school.
Representatives are not limited to just their college, school, or department, but
represent SGA and the Florida State University as a whole.
What services and programs does COGS provide to graduate students?
COGS provides outstanding services and programs to enrich graduate student life.
COGS provides funding for various registered student organizations, (RSOs) and
graduate students who wish to engage themselves through research and professional
exchanges (e.g., conferences). Furthermore, COGS funds projects throughout Florida
State that assist graduate students.
What is time commitment?
General Assembly meetings are held twice every month on Mondays starting at
6:30pm in the Senate Chambers at the New Student Union.
Committee meetings and other special events are also part of a representative’s service
in COGS. COGS is systematically structured to not be a burden on graduate students.
Many of our processes are productive, allowing graduate students time to focus on
academics, research and family.
What are the perks?
Service to the graduate student community Don’t you want to serve your graduate
student body? These students study just like you do and need support, and additionally
we have some more perks for you below:
 Interdisciplinary relationships that will enhance your network
 Leadership and professional development
 A hands-on experience in academic and administrative budgeting and policy.
 Enhancement of your professional CV/Resume
 Allocate A&S fees to graduate RSO’s from colleges, schools, and departments.
 Create policies and programs that will shift graduate students’ lives in a forward
direction.
Though COGS representatives are not paid, this small but impactful allocation of time
bears huge significance to you and the FSU student body and community. It is also a
great way to meet people and become involved in campus life.
E-mail: SGA-COGSJudicial@fsu.edu
Web: https://sga.fsu.edu/student-government/congress-graduate-students

sections.heading: Page 4

Congress of Graduate Students
Room 3251, New Student Union, Student Government Association, Florida State University
General Duties and Responsibilities of COGS
 Defend the interests of graduate, special, masters, specialist, professional,
doctoral and post-baccalaureate students in graduate student life, services, and
academics.
 Manage the funds within its purview in a fiscally responsible manner.
 Work to ensure the greatest participation by graduate students in the immediate
governance of, and policy development for, the Florida State University.
 Provide an official voice through which the opinions of the Graduate Student
Body may be expressed.
Committees
There are currently three (3) standing committees in COGS. All representatives are
expected to serve on a committee. Members are appointed by the Speaker, and
with the exception of the Budget Committee, meets at least once every two
months.
Each committee has a chair who is elected by its members. Committees (with the
exception of the budget committee) reports to the Congress on their activities at
each meeting of the Assembly.
Internal Affairs:
A) Prepare and distribute the monthly COGS newsletter
B) Keep website information updated
C) Outreach to fill vacant seats in the Assembly
D) Relations between COGS and the SGA, MSC, and LSC
E) Oversight all COGS funding expenditure
F) Train new COGS members
G) Make/Propose amendments to the COGS Code
H) Hear cases of impeachment and removal prior to the full Assembly
I) Maintain attendance records, and initiate removal proceedings for members
who are no longer in compliance with attendance requirements
J) All other areas in which the Chair and the Speaker agree the committee
should focus
Student Affairs:
A) Academics and Honor Policy
B) Parking and Transportation
C) Housing and Dining
D) Library
E) Health and Wellness

I am ready to serve as a COGS representative! Now what?
Completing the petition
You will need to find fellow graduate students that support your petition to
become aCOGS representative. Your “Petition to Fill a Vacant Seat” will be
attached to this packet. .
Obtain 20 signatures from graduate/professional students in your college/school,
or anumber that represents 10% of your college’s/school’s graduate/professional
population, whichever is less.
Or, if you are petitioning for an advocacy seat, obtain 20 signatures from any
graduate/professional students at Florida State. They need not be students in
yourcollege/school.
Submitting your petition to COGS
The completed petition can be submitted to Ridwan Balogun, Deputy Speaker
for Judicial Affairs (SGA-COGSJudicial@fsu.edu), or in Room 3251, New
Student Union. They will verify that everything is in order and let you know
about the next meeting to which you will need to be present in order to be
sworn in. You will also receive an e-mail or phone call from them, or another
COGS officer, to ensure that you are prepared.
What to expect at your first meeting
 First of all, relax! Being a Representative in COGS is not only a great
professional experience, it is also very fun! You will meet many new people from
across many different colleges and schools on the campus of FSU, so make sure
you are prepared to make some new friends. Here are a few tips for preparing for
your first meeting:
E-mail: SGA-COGSJudicial@fsu.edu
Web: https://sga.fsu.edu/student-government/congress-graduate-students

Congress of Graduate Students
Room 3251, New Student Union Student Government Association, Florida State University
 You will be introducing yourself to the body so make sure you look presentable.
Business casual should be fine. You should be able to tell us what college you
are from, any experience you have in student government here at FSU or at
another institution, experience you have in service-related activities, why you
would be a good representative of COGS, and any other information you might
want us to know. Keep in mind that you will only have a couple of minutes to do
this.
 After your introduction the floor will be open to questions. Some typical questions
that members of the body might ask include, but are not limited to:
1. Do you know about our committees, and do you know which one you
would like to serve in? (You can find in the front of this packet and in our
code, which is available on the cogs.fsu.edu website.)
2. Do you know of any current issues in your college or at the university that
you are looking forward to working on?
3. How did you hear about COGS?
4. Have you ever worked with COGS as a student?
Most information about the COGS code, the internal rules of procedure, grant information,
and past COGS minutes can be found on our website. We invite you to take a quick look to
get yourself acquainted.
At our meetings, we follow the internal rules of procedure as well as parliamentary
procedure. Don’t worry if you don’t know about these, you will! We will help you throughout
the meetings.
You may want to “like” us on Facebook, “Follow” us on Twitter and Instagram @COGSFSU.
Please tell your friends, too! ALWAYS, feel free to ask questions! We are so happy you are
here to learn, teach, serve, and work hard!
See you at our next COGS meeting!

Student Senate in the form of a bill or resolution.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses of entities funded in this budget, the Vice
President of Student Affairs, the SGA Advisor, the Senate President, and the
Student Body President shall meet to review options. No decisions shall be
made without a majority vote of the Student Senate.
C. The FY 2024-2025 Budget was created under the current $12.86 per credit
hour A&S Fee. Should the Local Fee Committee propose a per credit hour
increase that is accepted by the Board of Trustees, the Budget Committee
should reconvene to allocate the additional projected funds prior to the
beginning of the fiscal year.
D. The FY 2024-2025 Budget was created under the terms of the Agreement
between the Division of Student Affairs and the Office of the Student Body
President, as approved by the 76th Student Senate in Resolution (#?). The
Budget Committee, and the Student Senate as a whole, intend to fully comply
with the Agreement and are of the opinion that any proviso language regarding
the covered entities help ensure quality of service and compliance with various
state and university policies, rather than non-compliance with the Agreement.
E. SGA Budgeted Offices, Agencies, Bureaus, Affiliated Projects, Organizations,
and Departments are encouraged to utilize the Sweepings Process for one-time
purchases.
F. Monies allocated in the Food category shall be held in compliance with Student
Body Statute 803.7(A) which states “No SGA branch, office, agency, bureau, or
affiliated project shall be allocated more than fifteen percent (15%) of its annual
budget in the Food category.”
G. Any and all budgeted organizations found in violation of Student Body Statutes
shall be subject to the appropriate sanctions contained in the Finance Code and
recommended by the Finance Committee, the Budget Committee, and the
Student Senate.

Recreation Center, the Fitness and Movement Clinic, the Intramural fields, the

recommendation that the Campus Recreation Board determine its designation.

student dollars and that these facilities' primary purpose is for supporting the
student experience.

students with valid identification. Non-FSU students shall be subject to
admission fees.

BILL 2023
I. GENERAL
Activity and Service Fee Budget Proviso Language
Special Instructions
A. No A&S funded account may pay any stipend, wage, salary, or salary increase to any positions
not funded in Bill 2023 without express consent of the Student Senate in the form of a bill or
resolution.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses of entities funded in this budget, the Vice President of Student
Affairs, the SGA Advisor, the Senate President, and the Student Body President shall meet to review
options. No decisions shall be made without a majority vote of the Student Senate.
C. Budget Bill 2023 was created under the current $12.86 per credit hour A&S Fee. Should the Local
Fee Committee propose a per credit hour increase that is accepted by the Board of Trustees, the
Budget Committee should reconvene to allocate the additional projected funds prior to the
beginning of the fiscal year.
D. SGA Budgeted Offices, Agencies, Bureaus, Affiliated Projects, Organizations, and Departments are
encouraged to utilize the Sweepings Process for one-time purchases.
E. Monies allocated in the Food category shall be held in compliance with Student Body Statute
803.7(A) which states “No SGA branch, office, agency, bureau, or affiliated project shall be
allocated more than fifteen percent (15%) of its annual budget in the Food category.”
F. Any and all budgeted organizations found in violation of Student Body Statutes shall be subject to
the appropriate sanctions contained in the Finance Code and recommended by the Finance
Committee, the Budget Committee, and the Student Senate.
II. CAMPUS RECREATION
A. It is the position of the 74th Student Senate that the Bobby E. Leach Student Recreation Center,
the Fitness and Movement Clinic, the Intramural fields, the Rez Lakefront Park and Retreat
Center, and the Rec SportsPlex have been primarily funded by student dollars and that these
facilities' primary purpose is for student recreational purposes.
B. Monies were allocated as a lump sum in the expense category with the recommendation that the
Campus Recreation Board determine its designation.
III. UNION
A. It is the position of the 74th Student Senate that the Union Department, including various buildings
and programs across campus, has been funded by student dollars and that these facilities'
primary purpose is for supporting the student experience.
B. Any event or entertainment provided by the Union shall be free and open to all students with valid
identification. Non-FSU students shall be subject to admission fees.DocuSign Envelope ID: D7F7FA82-387D-43CA-A339-335901333C41

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
C. Revenue placed in the Headliner Account shall be used for the express purpose of bringing major
concert acts for the entertainment of the Student Body. This account shall be administered by the
Union with input from the Headliners Committee, appointed by the Student Body President. An
admission price may be charged to students in conjunction with the monies used from this
account. The Headliner Account shall not be swept at the end of the fiscal year.
D. It is the opinion of the 74th Student Senate that the Headliners account should support the FSU
Homecoming expenses of Homecoming Live.
E. Monies were allocated as a lump sum in the expense category with the recommendation that the
Union Board determine its designation.
IV. SGA STUDENT ACTIVITIES AND ORGANIZATIONS
A. Agencies, Bureaus, and Affiliated Projects are strongly encouraged to utilize the event planning
and contract negotiation services offered by the Student Governance & Advocacy Accounting
Office and the Union throughout the planning and execution of any A&S funded events. Events
involving a contractual service (speaker, musician, comedian, trainer, performer, etc.) exceeding
$3,000 are to be planned and negotiated in consultation with a representative from the Student
Governance & Advocacy Accounting Office and the Union prior to any verbal or written
commitment of such A&S funds. This clause shall only pertain to the contractual service (speaker,
musician, comedian, trainer, performer, etc.) for negotiation and not necessarily for other
arrangements such as space reservations, advertisement, or any other component of the
program.
B. Monies in the Food category shall never be used for Executive Board meetings and not more than
three times each semester for General Body meetings.
C. Monies allocated to the Student Government Administration Account are expressly intended for
the payment of the FSView, telephone, computer assessment, the Holopaw, maintenance
contracts, office supplies, technology, copier and printing, advertisement, and miscellaneous
expenses.
D. SGA organizations funded in Expense should prioritize programming and event needs. It is the
opinion of the 74th Student Senate that Student Publications should be utilized for all printing,
emphasizing digital publishing and distribution of publications, specifically the SCURC Owl
Publication.
E. Monies allocated to Homecoming shall be in compliance with Student Body Statute 615.5 (A)(3)
that states: “HEC Shall: Submit the annual Homecoming Budget for the entire student body to the
Senate Budget Committee”.
F. Monies allocated to Homecoming and expended shall contain the language “Paid for by SGA” on
all necessary expenditures as defined in Student Body Statutes Chapter 800 of the Finance Code.
G. Homecoming shall not endorse, affiliate with, or publicize any activities associated with the Burning
Spear organization. This decision is based on the Senate’s opinion as expressed in Resolution 9
of the 73rd Student Senate.
H. Monies allocated to the Sports Club Executive Council shall be held in compliance with Student
Body Statute 801.1(B)(1)(a) which states “These budgets shall be sent to the Student BodyDocuSign Envelope ID: D7F7FA82-387D-43CA-A339-335901333C41

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
Treasurer, the Senate Finance Committee, and the Senate Budget Committee. RTAC and PAC
are exempt from this requirement”.
I. Monies allocated to the Pride Student Union in the Expense Category shall expend no more than
$11,000 towards conference travel and registration fees.

A. The 74th Student Senate recommends in good faith that any and all budget cuts in the Child Care
Center and the Globe Building line items be covered by the Congress of Graduate Students.

President, Student Senate Pro Tempore, Homecoming Director, Homecoming Live Director, and
Inter Residence Hall Council Director or their designees, on the Homecoming Planning
Commission.
D. The Senate Branch is recommended to spend no more than $75 in the food category per meeting
which serves food.

G. Monies within the OGA Expense account shall not go to travel expenses for Washington D.C.

tags.
I. Monies allocated to the Medical Response Unit shall not be used for the NCEMSF conference, but
can be used for required uniforms.

coincide with the FSU Fall, Spring, and Summer Academic Calendars.

weeks in which they perform the duties and responsibilities of their position. The Pro Tempore of the Student Senate
shall receive minimum wage for seven (7) hours per fourteen (14) semester weeks in which they perform the duties
and responsibilities of their position. For the Summer Semester, the President of the Student Senate shall receive
minimum wage for five (5) hours per ten (10) term weeks in which they perform the duties and responsibilities of their
position. For the Summer Semester, the Pro Tempore of the Student Senate shall receive minimum wage for three (3)
hours per ten (10) term weeks in which they perform the duties and responsibilities of their position. Thirty-eight (38)
calendar weeks of pay have been made available for each position at these rates; these weeks of pay shall coincide
with the FSU Fall, Spring, and Summer Academic Calendars.

which they perform the duties and responsibilities of their position. Thirty-two (32) calendar weeks of pay have been
made available to this position at this rate; these weeks of pay shall coincide with the FSU Fall and Spring Academic
Calendars.

semester weeks in which they perform the duties and responsibilities of their office. Starting two weeks before each
election week, the Supervisor of Elections shall receive minimum wage for twenty (20) hours for five (5) semester
weeks in which they perform the duties and responsibilities of their office. Thirty (30) calendar weeks of pay have been
made available to this position at this rate; these weeks of pay shall coincide with the FSU Fall and Spring Academic
Calendars.

Student Union shall each receive minimum wage for seven (7) hours per calendar week in which they perform the
duties and responsibilities of their position. Thirty (30) calendar weeks of pay have been made available to these
positions at these rates; these weeks of pay shall coincide with the FSU Fall and Spring Academic Calendars.

receive minimum wage for ten (10) hours per calendar week in which they perform the duties and responsibilities of
their position, the Director of Operations shall receive minimum wage for seven (7) hours per calendar week in which
they perform the duties and responsibilities of their position, and the Director of Administration shall receive minimum
wage for five (5) hours per calendar week in which they perform the duties and responsibilities of their position. Thirty
(30) calendar weeks of pay have been made available to these positions at these rates; these weeks of pay shall
coincide with the FSU Fall and Spring Academic Calendars.

workers. Forty (40) calendar weeks of pay have been made available to these positions at these rates; these weeks of

BILL 2018
Activity and Service Fee Budget Proviso Language
Special Instructions
I. GENERAL
A. No A&S funded account may pay any stipend, wage, salary, or salary increase to
any positions not funded in Bill 2018 without express consent of the Student
Senate.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses, the Vice President of Student Affairs, the
SGA Advisor, the Senate President, and the Student Body President shall meet
to review options.
C. The suggestion for A&S Fees shall be $12.86 per credit hour.
II. CAMPUS RECREATION
A. It is the position of the 69th Student Senate that the Bobby E. Leach Student
Recreation Center, the Fitness and Movement Clinic, the Intramural fields, and
the Rec SportsPlex have been primarily funded by student dollars and that these
facilities' primary purpose is for student recreational purposes.
B. Monies were allocated as a lump sum in the expense category with the
recommendation that Campus Recreation determine its designation.
Ill. OGLESBY UNION
A. Any event or entertainment provided by the Oglesby Union shall be free and
open to all students with valid identification with the exception of Friday Night
Bites. Non-FSU students shall be subject to adm ission fees.
B. Revenue placed in the Headliner Account shall be used for the express purpose
of bringing major concert acts for the entertainment of the Student Body. This
account shall be administered by the Student Activities Office with input from the
Headliners Committee, appointed by the Student Body President and approved
by Senate. An admission price may be charged to students in conjunction with
monies us.ed from this account. The Headliner Account shall not be swept at the
end of the fiscal year.
1. At least $10,000 from Union expense allocation shall be designated for
the Headliner.
C. It is the opinion of the 69th Student Senate that Headliners Artist Series support
the FSU Homecoming expenses of Warchant and Powwow.

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
D. Monies were allocated as a lump sum in the expense category with the
recommendation that Oglesby Union determine its designation.
IV. SGA STUDENT ACTIVITIES, AND ORGANIZATIONS
A. Agencies , bureaus and affiliated projects are strongly encouraged to utilize the
event planning and contract negotiation services offered by the Student Activities
Center throughout the planning and execution of any A&S funded events. Events
involving a contractual service (speaker, musician, comedian, tra iner, performer,
etc.) exceeding $3,000 are to be planned and negotiated in consultation with a
representative from the Student Activities Center prior to any verbal or written
commitment of such A&S funds. This clause shall only pertain to the contractual
service (speaker, musician, comedian, trainer, performer, etc.) for negotiation
and not necessarily for other arrangements such as space reservations,
advertisement or any other component of the program.
B. Monies in the Food category shall never be used for Executive Board meetings
and not more than three times each semester for General Body meetings.
C. Monies allocated to the Student Government Administration Account are
expressly intended for the payment of the FSView, telephone, computer
assessment, the Milestone, the Torch, the Holopaw, maintenance contracts,
office supplies, printing, advertisement, and miscellaneous expenses.
D. In regards to the Office of Elections, following the spring elections any A&S fees
not needed for the Black Student Union elections shall be reverted back to the
Senate Projects account.
E. The Office of Elections shall budget for 16 election weeks and 14 non election
weeks for OPS wages.
V. SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS
A. Any A&S monies not spent on Homecoming shall be remanded to the Headliners
Artist Series.
B. The 69th Student Senate requires that at least one (1) Senate Representative
serve on all Homecoming Committees that involve A&S fees.
C. The 69th Student Senate recommends the Congress of Graduate Students fund
the remaining needs of the Childcare Center.
D. The 69th Student Senate recommends the Congress of Graduate Students fund
the remaining needs of the SGA Salary Account in the salaries category.
E. The Golden Tribe Lecture Series shall limit the amount of speakers to three (3) or
less per academic year; with the recommendation of one (1) speaker in the fall,
one (1) speaker in the spring, and one (1) speaker for MLK Week activities.

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
1. The Golden Tribe Lecture Series Account shall not be swept at the end of
the fiscal year.
F. Executive Projects and Senate Projects are recommended to evenly share the
affiliate fee for PeaceJam.
G. Senate Branch is recommended to spend no more than $75 in the food category
per meeting which serves food.
H. The Food category of Senate Projects is designated for the SGA Fall
Inauguration.
I. The Food category of the Executive Branch is designated for the SGA Spring
Inauguration.
J. At least $3,000 from Senate Projects shall be allocated to the CLC previously
funded in Bill 2017, but not those CLCs funded in the 2017 CLC Funding Board
Committee Meeting.
K. Senior Class Council is recommended to not exceed two (2) away game
viewings without the approval of senate in the form of a resolution.
L. $3,000 from the OGA Expense account shall be allocated to pay for FSU's
Evening Reception at the Capitol. It is recommended that any additional funding
that may be needed be provided by Senate Projects.
M. The Center for Global Engagement shall prioritize their OPS Wages for evening
and weekend space reservations for student organ izations.
N. The Budget Committee recommends that the Organizational Fund statutes shall
be restructured to additionally include RSOs who have not received A&S Fees in
the past.
VI. SEVERABILITY CLAUSES
A. All clauses in the Proviso Language for Bill 2018 shall be considered fully
severable.

I. GENERAL
A. No account funded by A&S fees may pay any stipend, wage, or salary increase to any
positions not funded in Sweepings 2022 without the express consent of the Student Senate.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses, the Vice President of Student Affairs, the SGA Advisor,
the Student Senate President, and the Student Body President shall meet to review options.
C. All purchase requests shall be received prior to May 31, 2023.
D. Any unspent funds shall be returned to the Sweepings account.
II. OPS WAGES
A. Monies allocated to the Union in the OPS Wages Category shall be used to pay wages for
student workers for the 2022-2023 fiscal year.
B. Monies allocated to the Elections Office in the OPS Wages Category shall pay for the Deputy
Supervisors of Elections for the 2022-2033 fiscal year.
1. The most senior Deputy Supervisor of Elections shall be paid at a rate of $10/hour at 5
hours per week, for six weeks; $11/hour at 10 hours per week for the 3 weeks pertaining
to Elections Week; and $11/hour at 5 hours per week for 6 weeks, totaling $960.
2. The junior Deputy Supervisor of Elections shall be paid at a rate of $10/hour at 5 hours
per week, for six weeks; $11/hour at 5 hours per week for the 9 weeks pertaining, totaling
$795.
C. Monies allocated to the Center for Health Advocacy & Wellness in the OPS Wages Category
shall be used to pay wages for a student facilitator for the Substance Use Intervention Training
(SUIT) Program.
D. Monies allocated to the RISE Office in the OPS Wages Category Shall be used to pay wages
for a student assistant i n the 2022-2023 fiscal year.
III. SGA OFFICES
A. Monies allocated to the Department of Student Engagement shall pay for storage lockers for
Recognized Student Organizations, Lounge Furniture, Certiport software for one (1) year, two (2)
Power Bars, sixteen (16) HON Pillow-Soft Bonded Leather High-Back Chairs, and window
frosting for the 3rd floor of the new Student Union Building offices. Any remaining funds shall be
used at the discretion of the recipient.
IV. SGA BUDGETED ORGANIZATIONS AND DEPARTMENTS
A. Monies allocated to Campus Recreation in the Expense Category shall be used to purchase
sixteen (16) paddleboards, sixteen (16) kayaks, and two (2) SportsPlex Zero Turn Mowers.
V. AGENCIESDocuSign Envelope ID: 46AD6E51-6FAD-4CE8-B467-66C33A462F5F

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
A. Monies allocated to the Pride Student Union in the Expense Category shall be used for
expenses pertaining to their planned travel to the 2023 Creating Change conference in San
Francisco, CA. This conference must be open to all members of the Student Body.
B. Monies allocated to the Womens’ Student Union in the Contractual Services Category shall be
used to pay for a musician to perform at FSU for Women’s History Month in March 2023. $2,500
in the Expense Category shall be reserved for start-up funds for programming pertaining to the
Nineteen Ten Women’s Honorary.
C. Monies allocated to the Jewish Student Union in the Food Category shall be used to purchase
food for Passover meals in Spring 2023.
D. Monies allocated to the Asian American Student Union shall not be used to purchase office
supplies.
VI. AFFILIATED PROJECTS
A. Monies allocated to the Medical Response Unit shall be used to purchase two (2) Stop the
Bleed training kits and two (2) Electric Golf Carts.
B. Monies allocated to WVFS in the Expense Category shall be used to purchase an Orban
Optimod 5700i Processor and for engineering and labor costs pertaining to a podcasting studio.
Monies allocated in the Operating Capital Outlay (OCO) Category shall be used to purchase an
MDL 102102 Standard Model Whisper Room.
VII. OUTSIDE DEPARTMENTS
A. Monies allocated to the Career Center at FSU shall be used for an Iris Headshot Booth, and
related shipping fees, installation fees, and three years worth of annual services.
B. Monies allocated to the FabLab at the Innovation Hub shall be used for four (4) Prusa MK3s+
3D printing machines and four (4) Prusa enclosures for said machines. Additional funds shall be
used to pay for related shipments and estimated customs duty.
C. Monies allocated to the Innovation Hub in the Food Category shall be used for the Seminole
Innovators’ Lunch Hour with Featured Innovators.
D. Monies allocated to the RISE Office in the Clothing & Awards Category shall be used for the
V-rak-ke-ce-tv ceremony and the Lavender Graduation.
VIII. RECOGNIZED STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS
A. Monies allocated to the African Student Association shall not be used towards any
scholarships or fellowships.
B. Uniforms or costumes purchased with monies allocated in the Expense Category to the Attack
Dance Crew shall be reusable and available to the entire team, regardless of members’ ability to
pay dues.DocuSign Envelope ID: 46AD6E51-6FAD-4CE8-B467-66C33A462F5F

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
C. Monies allocated to Hillel FSU shall be used to purchase food for Passover meals in the
Spring of 2023.
D. Monies allocated to iGem in the Expense Category shall only be used for the 2023 team
competition. Monies allocated in the Clothing & Awards Category shall only be used for iGem
apparel.
E. Monies allocated to Florida PIRG Students shall not be used towards any scholarships or
fellowships.
F. Monies allocated to the Master of Public Health Student Association shall be put towards their
FSU Health Conference in Spring 2023.
G. Monies allocated to the FSU Chapter of the NAACP shall be used for contractual services,
expenses, food, and clothing & awards related to their collaborative programming with Florida
Agricultural & Mechanical University (FAMU) in Spring 2023. Goods bought with A&S fees must
go to Florida State University students.
H. Uniforms or costumes purchased with monies allocated in the Expense Category to the
Nolettes shall be reusable and available to the entire team, regardless of members’ ability to pay
dues.
I. Monies allocated to the FSU Chapter of the Tau Beta Sigma Fraternity shall be used for their
Greater Music Benefit Concert.
J. Monies allocated to TEDx FSU shall be used for the food in the reception in the 2023
TEDxFSU conference, and all food purchased with A&S monies must be available to all
attendees of the conference.
K. Monies allocated to White Mouse Productions shall be used for a 192 sq ft. Portable Stage
System.
L. Monies allocated to the World Affairs Program shall be explicitly spent on travel, lodging, gas,
mileage, and registration fees pertaining to conferences and be spent in line with the provisions
of the Finance Code and Student Body Statutes.
IX. SEVERABILITY CLAUSE
A. Any part, provision, or representation of this Bill which is prohibited or which is held to be void
or unenforceable shall be ineffective to the extent of such prohibition or unenforceability without
invalidating the remaining provisions hereof.DocuSign Envelope ID: 46AD6E51-6FAD-4CE8-B467-66C33A462F5F

I. GENERAL
A. No A&S fee funded account may pay any stipend, wage, or salary increase to any positions not
funded in Sweepings 2021 without the express consent of the Student Senate.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses, the Vice President of Student Affairs, the SGA Advisor, the
Senate President, and the Student Body President shall meet to review options.
C. All purchase requests shall be received prior to May 31, 2022.
D. Any unspent funds shall be returned to SGA.
II. OPS WAGES
A. Monies allocated to the Congress of Graduate Students in the OPS Wage Category shall be used
to pay for CPR and AED trainers during CPR and AED training sessions under the supervision of
Campus Recreation during the Fall and Spring Academic Calendars.
B. Monies allocated to the Center for Global Engagement in the OPS Wage Category shall be used to
pay for Event Staff through the 2021-2022 fiscal year. Event Staff shall receive minimum wage for
twelve (12) hours per calendar week in which they perform the duties of their position during the FSU
Fall and Spring academic calendars. The event staff shall receive a minimum wage of ten (10) hours
per calendar week during the Summer Academic Calendar. Twenty-seven (27) calendar weeks of pay
have been made available to these positions at these rates; these weeks of pay shall coincide with
the remainder of the 2021-2022 fiscal year.
C. Monies allocated to the Student Governance & Advocacy office in the OPS Wage Category shall
be used to pay for OPS Wage deficits that occurred from the minimum wage increase for SG&A OPS
employees at the determination of their administration.
D. Monies allocated to TEDxFSU in the OPS Wage Category shall be used to pay for a parking
attendant for an event. The parking attendant shall be paid at twenty-five (25) dollars per hour for
eight (8) hours.
E. Monies allocated to the Jewish Student Union in the OPS Category shall be used to pay for the
Jewish Student Union Director’s wages during the Spring Academic Calendar. The Director shall
receive minimum wage for five (5) hours a week in which they perform the duties and responsibilities
of their position. A total of fifteen (15) calendar weeks of pay have been made available for this
position at this rate.
F. Monies allocated to FSU Libraries in the OPS Wage Category shall be used to pay for tutors during
the 2021-2022 fiscal year.
G. Monies allocated to Campus Recreation in the OPS Wage Category shall be used to cover wage
deficits that occurred from the minimum wage increase for Campus Recreation OPS employees at the
determination of their administration.
H. These terms and stipulations on OPS waged individuals shall only apply to the positions and
offices mentioned in this section. All remaining ops waged positions may be paid at the rate and hours

sections.text:
SGA PAC Funding Policies & Guidelines for RSOs
2020-2021
RSO Eligibility
To request funds from PAC, an organization must first:
• be recognized at Florida State University
• have at least two eligible officers complete the financial certification exam through SGA
Accounting, and
• have submitted the Statement of Understanding Form to SGA Accounting prior to
submitting a request.
RSOs that received funds from SAP or any other A&S Funding board, committee, or line item in
the annual budget (with the exception of PAC, RTAC or Senate Projects) are ineligible to
receive funding from PAC the same fiscal year in which they receive other funding.
No RSO may be allocated funds from PAC more than twice per fiscal year. This rule can be
waived by a 2/3 vote of PAC and a majority vote in Senate. Any amount requested by a single
organization over $2000 requires a 2/3 vote of the Committee, and a 2/3 vote of Senate.
RSOs can only request for funds that will be used within 90 days. A 2/3 vote of PAC can
override this rule.
PAC Guidelines
• PAC will only fund in the Expense, Food, Contractual Services and Other (Clothing &
Awards) categories. PAC may not allocate funds for OCO items.
• All events and activities paid for by SGA funds must be publicly advertised and open to
all students via a flyer, social media, chalking, etc.
• Food funding requests must include a plan for advertising and an estimated number of
FSU students who will attend and consume the food. PAC will not fund events that are
likely to only have group or board members attend.
• RSOs may only request t-shirts from PAC once per fiscal year. Shirts must be used to
promote the organization which is requesting them. PAC will not allocate more than $8
per shirt (including all applicable screening and art fees). PAC will not purchase polo shirts.
• All requests must be submitted at least 21 business days prior to the event. A request
submitted within 18 business days may be considered for funding at the discretion of the
chair. Any request outside of this timeline may not be considered for funding.
• Requests must be line item in nature with a letter explaining need and an explanation of
the benefits to the student body in general. Requests must be in line with SGA Student
Statutes and the SGA Financial Manual guidelines.
• Only completed requests submitted by noon on Fridays will be forwarded and heard by
PAC the following week.
Submitting a PAC Request
• All requests must be submitted online through the PAC online application by noon, 12pm
on Friday before the hearing, 21 business days prior to the event.
• All submissions must have three (3) supporting/competitive quotes for each category
which funds are being requested.
• RSOs must submit additional material including quotes (t-shirt costs, performer costs,
reservation costs, equipment rental, facility rental, etc), a letter of explanation regarding
need, breakdown of all costs, and justification of the benefit to the student body in general.

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
PAC Funding Process
• PAC applications that are complete from RSOs that are recognized, with proper financial
certifications and the Statement of Understanding Form on file with SG&A Accounting will
receive confirmation that the request has been forwarded to the PAC Chair on Friday
afternoon. Should materials be missing, it is possible that a request cannot be heard by
PAC until the following week.
• The PAC Chair will email the RSO on Friday and within 24-hours of the PAC Hearing to
invite requesting RSOs to the meeting. PAC meets on Mondays or Tuesdays during the Fall
and Spring semesters.
• At least one financially certified officer for each requesting RSO must be present at the
hearing. They should bring 8 printed copies of the entire request and any pertinent
additional information to the PAC Hearing.
• PAC will hear requests, ask detailed questions, ensure compliance with SGA Student Body
Statutes, and make a recommendation regarding funding via Senate Resolution.
• The resolution will be presented at the next Finance Committee meeting and shall only be
debated on if there are objections.
• Once passing the Finance Committee, the PAC Resolution will be forwarded to Senate, and
placed on the Consent Calendar and online.
• Once on the Consent Calendar, the PAC resolution shall be presented at the next Student
Senate meeting (Wednesday evening). Debate on the resolution will only be heard upon an
objection to the resolution. In order for an amendment to pass in Finance Committee or
Senate, there must be a 2/3 vote.
• A one-tenth (1/10) vote is required for an objection to be upheld. If a one-tenth (1/10) vote
of Senate is not reached after an objection to the Consent Calendar, then the resolution
shall pass as presented.
After the Senate Meeting
At the Senate meeting on Wednesday evening, a requesting RSO will know if they have
received funds from SGA, and the correct amounts.
In order to receive and spend the funds from PAC, RSOs must complete a Purchase Request in
Nole Central. Failure to submit a Purchase Request in Nole Central within the week funds
were allocated by Student Senate can result in no funding for an RSO. RSOs are
encouraged to review the SGA Financial Manual section regarding Purchase Requests to
ensure they are in compliance with all SGA Policies and Procedures.
RSOs must electronically submit their receipts within 10 days of spending funds to ensure
payments are processed and that RSOs can continue to request SGA funds. Receipts must be
uploaded via the SGA Funding Evaluation Receipt Submission Qualtrics, sga.fsu.edu/receipts.
Summertime
Fund Distribution Committees shall not meet during any summer semesters. RSOs
requesting funds to be used in May or June shall request before the end of the Spring term.
RSOs requesting funds to be used after July 1, should go directly to Senate to ask for money
out of Senate Projects.

73RD STUDENT SENATE
Senate Resolution
Resolution #: 83
Primary Sponsors: Hunter
Whereas: The Florida State University Student Government Association's Office of
Government Affairs is tasked with advocating and representing the interests of the
student body at the university, local, state, and federal levels, and
Whereas: The Board of Directors of the Office of Governmental Affairs compiled,
debated, and approved a legislative agenda for the upcoming 2022 regular Florida
legislative session, and
Whereas: The Florida State University Student Government Association (FSU SGA)
recommends the following to the Florida Legislature to enhance student life and learning
in the State of Florida, and Textbook Affordability
Whereas: FSU SGA strongly supports making textbooks more affordable by reinstating
the Bright Future Book Stipend, and
Whereas: FSU SGA supports improving an Open Educational Resources grant program
in the State of Florida similar to SB 602 which was introduced in the 2020 Legislative
Session ,and Equitable Education
Whereas: FSU SGA urgently supports enhanced efforts of a broadened education
curriculum and supports HB281 high school students on requiring instruction in the
history of the Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, and
Whereas: FSU SGA supports enhanced training for students, faculty, and staff in the
areas of religious and racial awareness, and
Whereas: FSU SGA supports educating students on the diverse life experiences of
minority populations by opposing the restrictive measures in HB57, and
Whereas: FSU SGA recognizes the opportunities for students provided by the out of
state tuition waiver for high school children of undocumented immigrants and supports
the continuance of the program and the expansion to graduate students, and
Whereas: FSU SGA supports funding for the creation of an interdisciplinary Center for
Native American & Indigenous Studies, as recommended by the FSU President's Task-
Force on Anti-Racism, Equity, and Inclusion, and as supported by former President John
Thrasher, and
Legislative Priorities of the Florida State University
Whereas: FSU SGA supports the legislative priorities of the Florida State University with
a specific emphasis on renaming B.K. Roberts Hall and funding for Critical Electrical
Infrastructure at the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory, Integrated Advancement
for the Joint College of Engineering, and the Veterans Legacy Complex, and
Whereas: FSU SGA supports the renaming of the Doak Campbell Stadium to a name
that is inclusive and supportive of the entire student body, and
Whereas: FSU SGA supports increasing local fees for students if recommended by the
FSU Local Fees Committee, and Accessibility
Whereas: FSU SGA supports efforts increase voter accessibility by implementing
automatic voter registration in the State of Florida, andDocuSign Envelope ID: 7FB31D66-A82A-4359-8D86-DDE7FB08BA25

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Whereas: FSU SGA urges the University Administration to utilize chosen names on all
official documentation from the application process to graduation, and Health
Whereas: FSU SGA supports expanding Medicaid eligibility as allowed under the
Affordable Care Act in alignment with thirty-nine (39) other states, and
Whereas: FSU SGA supports a requirement for all students to have health insurance
upon enrollment in a State University System or Florida College System institution, and
Whereas: FSU SGA urges the Florida legislature to support adoption of a third party
telehealth program throughout the State University System and Florida College System
to support students’ mental health and reduce the strain on college health centers and
Whereas: FSU SGA supports the addition of mental health counselors in individual
colleges in order to best support the tailored needs of students as well as creating a
better method of ensuring that students need counseling are able to, in spite of a session
limit, and Safety
Whereas: FSU SGA supports the continuous enhancement of campus safety and
strongly opposes the efforts to introduce guns on campus within HB6007, and

prohibition on entertainment and/or alcoholic beverage expenses. This provision may
only be waived by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of COGS. Florida State University – Congress of
Graduate Students Administrative Code - 29
202.5 No RSO shall receive COGS Funds for travel as a group more than twice in a fiscal
year. This can be waived by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Assembly.
A) Group travel is limited to tabling as a promotional entity on behalf of the RSO
and Florida State University, or a panel discussion in which at least three-fourths
(3/4) of the members are leading.
202.6 RSOs can receive up to $2,000 per fiscal year Travel. This rule can be waived by a
two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Assembly.
202.7 RSOs can send up to four (4) representatives from their organization to the event
for which the travel request is intended. This rule can be waived by a two-thirds (2/3)
vote of the Assembly and must be voted upon independent of the legislation for which
the travel request is intended.

sections.heading: Page 1
sections.text:
FSU Congress of Graduate Students
Internal Affairs Committee Meeting
August 26, 2022
Start Time: 3:05 pm
Attendance: Sara Collins, Nella Delva, Rachel Neale, Ethan Vouzas
Special Guests: Ariana Genovese (President, Medical Student Council), Joshua Davis (Treasurer,
Medical Student Council)
Introductions:
Dep. Speaker Delva:
• Today, we are going to discuss the financial changes we are making to the code. These
will be approved at our next assembly meeting. Our second goal, is to discuss
clarification for the travel application for MSC. This concerns clarification and
interpretation. The details of what we will be making today are from Chapter 207 in the
Code, in addition to 208 and 209.
New Business:
Changing COGS Code to reflect budget changes for conference attendance/presentation:
• Delva reviews that presentation grants (domestic) are increasing to $250.
• Vouzas: Section 205 outlines what students can get within a specific time point = $500 a
year for 5 years. This is reflected in the second sentence in 207.5. The proposed change
here is $600 instead of $500, so we increase presentation at international conferences
from $500 to $600. The other change would be $3,000 in 5 years, to reflect the increase
in domestic presentation/attendance grants.
• Vouzas: In 208, the change reflects a change from $200 to $250, which is what we voted
on from this fiscal year. This would yield a $100 increase for international travel, a $50
increase for presentation and attendance grants.
• Vouzas: My proposal is we would eliminate 208d, since this provision is concerned with
the time period that extended to June 11, 2011.
• Vouzas: Concerning 209, we realize there is no language that dictates attendance grants.
I propose adding language that indicates how much money will be awarded for
attendance grants. I propose we copy paste this language from 208, and show this $50
increase but for attendance grants rather than presentation grants for 209. So now we
will have language that reflects that attendance grants can be up to $150 each and
presentation grants up to $250 per grant.
• Neale: So, should we indicate that conference attendance is eligible for up to $150.00 in
attendance grants. This change is reflected in 209.1 D.
• Neale: Did we adjust the pool of funds that will be dedicated to each funding period?
• Vouzas: It will not matter, since the resolution already passed.
• Neale: I was just wondering. Students might be more vigilant about applying now.

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
• Vouzas: At the moment, I see that we did increase the amount dedicated toward grants.
We had $160,000 in the last funding period (split within three funding periods). For this
fiscal year, we have over $66,000 per funding period, which is a total of about $200,000.
• Neale: Now will this go on the budget packet under New Business?
• Collins: Yes, and we will vote on it with pros and cons. And the item we are voting on is
just the language we used to describe these changes.
• Neale: I saw another line that might need adjusting, it’s Chapter 108.3 F and E.
• Neale: This concerns information about committees. This line includes a date that has
already expired (February 5, 2018). I propose to remove E and F given this language has
expired and the tasks there mentioned have already been completed.
• Delva: I move to call to question the vote for budget changes.
• Collins: Second.
• Chapter 207 changes
o Vote: 4-0-0
• Chapter 208 changes (208.2A, 208.2B)
o Vouzas objects to call to question for Chapter 208. Proposes to remove the
language “(outside 100 miles)” in 208.2A.
o Adjustment is made to 208.8A.
• Delva: I motion to call to question.
• Collins: Second
• Chapter 208 changes
o Vote: 4-0-0
• Chapter 209 changes
o Vote: 4-0-0
• Delva: I motion to call to question the vote for Chapter 108.
• Collins: Second
• Chapter 108 changes
o Vote: 4-0-0
Clarification with Travel Application Funding / Re: MSC Individual Grant Funds:
• Neale: I was reading Chapter 202 on travel, particularly 202.5. It notes that no RSO shall
receive COGS travel funds as a group more than twice in a fiscal year. Also, B discusses
provisions on tabling. Therefore, allocating group travel funds to RSOs would not be
appropriate.
• Vouzas: This makes it very clear that when it comes to group travel, group travel cannot
be defined as a set number of individuals as a set number applying together and
traveling for a conference. I think that it makes it clear that it has to be a tabling event
to promote a single group entity.
• Ariana Genovese (President of MSC):
o A huge portion of this is to promote student presentations, and we get a very
large number of students who need to present research. So I think this should be
a promotional movement.

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
o Neale: I believe you will need to be limited to tabling for a promotional
movement.
o Genovese: So how would you like us to go about processing grants? Because I
get a lot of students from different schools.
o Vouzas: I am responsible for processing all of these requests. I can assure you
that it will not add more to my plate to process requests from students in the
medical school because I am already processing the requests of every other
graduate student at the university.
o Davis: We’ve seen the requests increase, so we can help our students go forth
and present this research. Conferences are also not intended for only research
purposes. We had 21 students from the COM travel to a conference that
supports minority students – it is great for networking. Every member of the
COM is a member of every RSO. There must be a way where suballocation can
be changed.
o Vouzas: Tabling and conference travel are very different processes. There are
different components that must be considered. Every graduate student at FSU
pays the same A&S fees. The second part is that almost definitionally, MSC is
COGS. Even though it is a separate entity that can allocate funds within that
umbrella, so it cannot operate separately from that part of COGS. Third, every
travel to a conference, at the end of the day, it is travel to attend or present.
Within the COGS code, they all need to be treated the same way. So when a
person from the math department comes to COGS to ask to present, it is treated
the same as an individual person in MSC. They are each presenting at a
conference in the continental US. At the end of the day, COGS code is the
principal document that overshadows everything else in COGS. This is the way I
view things because I also think it’s a matter of fairness. If you look at the
amount of money that we have, we have to understand how it trickles down to
each student individually. Unfortunately, this pool includes all the A&S funds
grad students pay. Then SGA is responsible for giving COGS its own funding. At
the moment, the amount of money we get is 50% of A&S fees graduate students
pay. The previous fiscal year, a few people worked together to increase our pool
of funding. A small percentage of A&S fees actually goes to
presentation/attendance grants. So subsequent to that, our job as funding
boards is to ensure that that money is distributed equitably across every
graduate student at the university.
o Genovese: When you speak about students from different departments,
something really resonated with other members. Some students range in where
they’re traveling. We take into account every single thing, and the things you
don’t have time to do, we do this for you. We only provide money to each
student only what they need. So if you add up and take the average of what each
student gets, it’s still the full amount of what we can allocate. I think this is a lot
for COGS to handle themselves, especially since we’ve been doing the heavy
lifting for you guys over the last few years.

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
o Vouzas: We award up to $200. To explain, this is resulted in the accounting
department at FSU and SGA so at the end of the day, when the student submits
their receipts to their conference, accounting goes in and reimburses the
appropriate amount. On paper, it says they were awarded $200, they will not
automatically get $200. Something that needs to be considered, what you
explained about the cost averaging out across all students, this is not something
else that is afforded to every student at the university. So, this is a matter of how
much each student can receive, regardless of how much money their conference
costs. We need to account for how much money students are planning to spend.
We are not debating about what the rules should be, we’re looking at what
COGS code dictates. The entire goal of this is to ensure every member under
COGS abides by the COGS code.
o Delva: I want to reinforce what Ethan said. I want this COGS to be more fair and
abide the code. Another concern I had was double dipping. How do we know
who you’re funding is not asking for more funding from COGS directly.
o Neale: There have already been examples of double dipping.
o Vouzas: I had a student ask for conference funding from Canada. The only reason
we knew that the student got money from MSC and COGS is because the student
told us – otherwise, we would not have known.
o Delva: Maybe they didn’t know, but this has happened before and this can
continue to happen. In terms of fairness, I think we should stick to the code and
reroute everybody to the funding and travel presentation grants.
o Davis: In regards to some of the code, there are some students that present 3
times a year. I think the code should be modified to reflect this challenge.
There’s a chance that there won’t be any funding left.
o Vouzas: The whole first-come-first-served thing comes into play specifically for
the submission for the request, not the conference itself. COGS has 3 separate
funding periods. If a student knows they are going to a conference October 1st,
they can submit their request on July 15th. It’s a matter of when you submit your
application. There is flexibility as to where the money comes from. Even though
we have three separate windows, the money that is allocated in that window is
not always fixed. There have been times where we needed to transfer money to
another funding period window. The only time that this can really come into play
is the very end of June. And that would only happen if COGS straight up ran out
of money.
o Davis: In the instance, should students just be applying through COGS? Will they
get turned away?
o Vouzas: No. We do not turn away students unless they cannot provide proof of
conference.
o Genovese: So, some students get conference acceptances with short notice.
What will happen if that is the case?
o Vouzas: Every student is treated the same and given the same chance to get
each grant.

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
o Davis: So I greatly believe this will decrease the number of students who can
attend and showcase their work at MSC, which will decrease match rates,
residency networking, etc.
o Collins: I just want to apologize for all of the information you’ve been given from
previous executive committees. We are trying to set a new precedent to make
sure we follow COGS code. And that is giving students equitable access to these
funds.
o Delva: Yes, I agree. We want to ensure that we are providing each student the
same access to these funds.
o Davis: Do you know if individual labs get funding?
o Vouzas: Yes, but however, that does not always fund the student for conference
travel.
o Davis: This greatly limits the ability for people to attend and present at
conferences.
o Vouzas: We are greatly limited by the university and what they will approve.
That’s something that is not our role as a body.
o Delva: Unfortunately, there’s no money for us to travel, as well. When
addressing the generalization of the whole student body, and bring our own
experience and access to this, we have to understand privilege as opposed to
others who are not given funding at all.
o Genovese: I just want to express why we are all here today. Med students
cannot advance to residency, or match, if they do not have a suitable amount of
publications. I want to make sure we are following the same rules, I want to
make sure we give what we have to COGS students while abiding by COGS code.
I would consider amending the code that includes tabling. If we don’t spend the
money, it will go into sweepings.
o Vouzas: This situation was born from a general lack of understanding of COGS
code, including my on misunderstanding. There are many members that are
brand new and don’t pay too much attention. Honestly, when the budget was
approved, the meetings were some of my first in COGS. I think this is something
that we can work out for the current fiscal year. I don’t think this is something
we can work out today. Most likely, we are going to need to come up with some
creative solutions to move past this point. I’d like to organize some meetings
that include MSC, COGS, and our COGS advisor to discuss alleviating this issue for
the future. These meetings can be unofficial, and we can set them up in the next
few weeks. Then we can draft something that will help us get through this fiscal
year.
o Delva: There is further discussion to be had. It will be an official executive board
meeting with the full purpose of how to handle this solution. Hopefully we can
come up with an agreement. But, it will not be today.
o Davis: In the meantime, let’s say a student wants to present research, is there
any way to help them with that funding.
o Neale: They will need to go through the application for attendance and
presentation grants. What’s black and white in the code is that students will

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
need to go through COGS for conference funding. I apologize for any
miscommunication and errors from the previous executive boards. There’s no
reason to completely lose hope – there have been students who have come
through the entire assembly to decide if we can fairly give them the funds for
that life changing experience. But any individual grant requests need to go
through the COGS funding committee.
o Genovese: Thank you. I’m glad we are going to reach a compromise, and
everyone is getting on the same page.
End time: 5:07 pm

provide the reimbursement money from their own budget

allow any reimbursements
• Reimbursement is not the technical term for what it is – need
better wording
o If an RSO does not fill out the proper forms for funding and
does not receive the funds they requested, how they can
go about re-requesting funds (or make it not possible to
re-request funds)

o Maybe limit the amount they can be reimbursed – only a
proportion

either majority or 2/3

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
o If person who would be reimbursed is financially certified
or not
§ If person who receive funds is financially certified,
then they cannot be reimbursed because they are
responsible for submitting the forms in a timely
manner and know the proper time window
§ If person who receives funds is not financially
certified, then it is not purely their fault since the
financially certified member of the RSO is the one
who submits forms
§ If person who receives fund is not financially
certified and they did not submit their receipts or
other materials in a timely manner, then they
cannot receive funds since they are responsible for
froms not being submitted on time and they knew
the time window to submit their materials (unless
the financially certified person did not let them
know )
§ All of this is hard to determine and may not be
entirely possible to prove – therefore this should
not be included because it is too complicated
o Reimbursements would first be requested from MSC and
LSC – they can decide if they want to reimburse they own
RSO or not

or LSC says yes then the request must be approved
by Congress by 2/3 vote

submit proper paperwork

§ 607.9 ““COGS may establish procedures in the COGS

complaint student organizations within its jurisdiction,
subject to appeal to any competent body or officer in
accordance with Chapter 805 of these statutes.”
o President/treasurer (or whoever is financially certified) will

position in an RSO that requires them to be financially
certified

Student Advocacy Committee Meeting
March 31st 2023 @ 5:00pm
Representatives present Galeano, Salimi, Burns, Elmi, and Ilesanmi.
Excused Absence: Mostbauer
Unexcused Absence:
Guests:
Discussion Points:
1. Medical student COGS code
• During the recent COGS meeting, a resolution was passed that permits the
Medical School Council to modify their constitution. Furthermore, an updated
COGS code is in the process of being drafted and is expected to be voted on
before the semester concludes.
2. Parking citations
• In terms of parking citation policies, Representative Salimi has initiated a project
to address the issue of steep fines and is pushing for policy change that gives
warnings to first offenders. Communications have been established with Richard
Rind, the Director of Transportation and Parking Services. A meeting is scheduled
for April 14th at 1 pm in Mr. Rind's office to discuss how to move forward with
policy changes and how parking citations fit within the FSU infrastructure.
3. Pride Student Union
• Representative Burns held a productive meeting with the Pride Student Union,
where they discussed connecting graduate students to the union through
expanded networks within colleges. The conversation highlighted that the
existing Pride Student Union is predominantly undergraduate-focused. It was
also mentioned to have COGS issue a statement similar to SGA's recent
resolution that opposes new state legislation targeting education and LGBTQ+
rights. This is particularly relevant for prospective out-of-state graduate students
whom the legislation may deter. Potential next steps include creating a document
outlining students' rights despite the new legislation and possibly establishing a
graduate student RSO to help facilitate LGBTQ+ networking amongst graduate
students. The Pride Student Union's support will be sought, and a resolution will
be drafted and sent to the committee.
4. International Student Lawyers
• Efforts to assist international students through legal counsel have not yielded
significant results thus far. Representative Elmi contacted various sources,
including the Law School Council (LSC) and current law students, and
implementing such a service may be unlikely. Despite the lack of resources

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
currently available, a possible next step for getting international students legal
advice is to facilitate collaborations between LSC and the Center for Global
Engagement (CGE) in providing these services. Currently, it is best to see how LSC
responds, then move forward with collaboration efforts if needed.
5. The Globe
• Unofficial conversations between Representative Ilesanmi and Jesse revealed
that room 3500 is typically available for graduate RSOs, although serving food in
the room is prohibited. Alternate options include using the Globe's kitchen if
available or providing food to go. The CGE's operating hours, which currently end
at 6 pm, pose accessibility challenges for evening events. Right now, they are
extending these hours on a case-by-case basis, but the number of RSOs that have
done this is limited. Thus, further discussion is needed to understand the
approval process for evening event requests and how RSOs are selected for
extended hours.
Message to representatives: Remember it is best to keep everyone in the loop by copying the
other representatives on emails and even have other committee members join in on meetings.
Next meeting: April 28th at 5 pm.
Meeting adjourned: 5:30 pm.

This event will feature two of our moot court team members presenting oral arguments in front of the team and prospective new
members. This showcase is an integral part of the team's recruiting and association. The team members will present ten minutes of oral
argument and receive questions from a selected panel of team judges. This event serves not only as recruitment for new members but
as a practice execution for our future competitors. The event is taking place on February 28th, in Robert's hall room 102. The event is
one that will hopefully attract many 1 and 2Ls who would like to join the moot court team. This showcase will allow our team to
advertise exactly what our team does in competition, and provide a benchmark skill level for applicants to analyze and shoot to
emulate in their oral arguments for legal writing. Our event is meant to show applicants the nuances and stature of our team.
Established in 1968, the Florida State College of Law Moot Court Team is one of the nation's leading university moot court teams.
The Moot Court Team annually contends in regional, national and international competitions where teams of two to three members
compete against other law school moot court teams. Issues in past competitions have included the First Amendment, Criminal Law,
Intellectual Property, Sports Law, International Law, Environmental Law, Evidence, Workers' Compensation, Cyber Law, Corporate
Law, Securities, Labor and Employment, Entertainment and Communications Law. These competitions are the main event of being on
the moot court team. Academic credit is also available for competitions. Each competition earns the team member two credits during
the semester of the competition. Coaches for the team are drawn from the College of Law faculty, alumni and surrounding legal
community. This event helps us outline these facts to potential members.

Purpose of funds: Graduate Policy Committee: Student Feedback Meeting
The Graduate Policy Committee shall consider university-wide policies relating to graduate education. Members of this Committee
shall be appointed by the Steering Committee, with the advice and consent of the Senate, for staggered three-year terms. Each college
or school shall have one representative; the Colleges of Education, Business, and Social Sciences shall have one additional
representative; and the College of Arts and Sciences shall have four additional representatives. The Vice President for Academic
Affairs, or his or her designee, and the Dean of Graduate Studies, or his or her designee, shall be ex-officio members; and membership
shall include two graduate student representatives from different colleges or schools appointed for a one-year term by the President of
Student Government. The Committee shall annually elect its chairperson from the faculty representatives. The Committee will make
its recommendations to the Steering Committee, which will transmit the recommendations to the Senate for action. Every 7 years,
Florida State University conducts an evaluation of its graduate programs. One aspect of this evaluation involves gathering feedback
from law students. This meeting will provide a forum for law students to give their feedback to external graduate program reviewers.

Organization: Black Law Students Association
Date/time of event: --
Amount requested: $536.37, amended to $1,800 for stoles and $70 for COGs logo stickers
Purpose of funds: To award graduating students with stoles to be worn at graduation
Details of event: BLSA will advertise the giveaway of these stoles through the student
announcements to award and celebrate students successfully completing law school. The
stoles are hand-woven and shipped from Ghana. They are $18/person
Notes:
- Stoles are regularly $22.95 but received a discount code from National BLSA
- 100 stoles will be purchased
- We originally approved this request on February 16th but the COGs speaker had issues
with it. In order to get the rest of the requests approved from that meeting we put this
request on the back burner. We are still in approval of this request and we disagree with
the COGs speaker’s assessment of why he denied it in the February 16th minutes.
- We are classifying these stoles as awards and more specifically as trophies.
- According to the SGA Financial Manual section 803.8:
o The Clothing & Awards Category shall be used to pay for clothing (t-shirts and
polo shirts) for the purpose of promoting an SGA-funded entity or event, and
awards (trophies, plaques, and certificates) for the purpose of recognizing an
individual or group.
§ (A)Clothing shall be restricted to T-shirts, tank tops and polo shirts, unless
otherwise approved by a three-fourth (3/4) vote of the Senate Finance
Committee.
• 1. T-shirts and polo shirts must be made available free of charge
to all FSU members of the entity purchasing them. There shall be
no separate Executive Board shirts. Executive Board shirts can be
waived in the form of a resolution with approval by a three-
fourths (3/4) vote of the Senate Finance Committee and a two-
thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate.
§ (B) Awards shall be restricted to trophies, plaques, and certificates.
• 1. The manner in which the recipient of any award was (or will be)
decided must be submitted to the Student Body Treasurer at the
same time as the expenditure. Under no circumstances may this
category be used to purchase personal gifts.
- The definition of a trophy is “a cup or other decorative object awarded as a prize for a
victory or success.”
o A stole is a decorative object. These stoles are going to be awarded to graduating
students who will wear them as a prize for graduating.
- There is no definition of trophy indicated in the SGA financial manual which means that
these can be classified as awards being that they are decorative in nature and being

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
awarded as a prize to graduating 3Ls. On the vendor website, it describes the stoles as
“Native to the to the Ashanti Region in Ghana, Kente Cloth has a long tradition of be
worn for the most prestigious occasions.”
- The stickers will be purchased from stickermule. They are high quality logo stickers that
will be added to each stole to satisfy the requirement that awards and clothing have the
COGs logo on them.
Member Abby Alison Destinee Justin Lakiera Reinaldo Ryan Shaina Madison

VOTE: 8 yes 1 no 0 abstain

- Celebrates the accomplishment of graduating students.
- Shows that we support our RSOs wanting to celebrate graduates
- After the year we’ve had, everything deserves a little more celebration

- None

Organization: Student Bar Association
Date/time of event: March 19, 2021 7:30pm-9:30pm
Amount requested: $12,289.65
Purpose of funds: FSU Law Drive in Movie at the Civic Center
Details of event:
As part of FSU Law's Wellness Week, the Office of Student Advancement and the Student Bar
Association are putting together a socially distant drive-in movie night on Friday, March 19th,
2021 in the Tucker Center Main Parking lot. The estimated attendance is 100 people. This is not
a ticketed event. The goal of the event is to provide a fun activity for students in
acknowledgment of the importance of mental health. Wellness week is the Law School’s way to
help offset the fact students are not getting a spring break this year. In other years, we would
not approve a cost this large from an organization for a singular event however this year has
been unusual in many senses which leads an event like this to be able to do some good for law
school students more broadly. The students would stay in their cars to watch this movie in the
Civic Center parking lot. There is not food being provided.
Notes:
The costs of the event include:
- The cost to lease the space (Tucker Center Main Parking Lot) - $1,500.00.
- Event staff, including the changeover crew, cleaning staff, EMT, Parking Lot Attendant,
and Police Officer - $1,675.65.
o This cost is required by the Civic Center
- Portable restrooms on the site and a hand-washing station - $445
o This prevents students from going in and out of the law school or the civic center
to use the restroom keeping it as Covid friendly as possible.
- The total cost of the Civic Center is $3,620
- Production company cost quote to display the movie outside - $8,669.0.
Totals $12,289.65.

803.8

SGA-funded entity or event, and awards (trophies, plaques, and certificates) for the purpose of recognizing an individual or
group.

by a three-fourths (3/4) vote of the Senate Finance Committee and a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate.

Treasurer at the same time as the expenditure. Under no circumstances may this category be used to purchase personal gifts.

Notes of the event/Item:
Our guest speaker is Dr. David Bobb, a successful forensic psychiatrist based in Houston Texas who
practices in a number of settings. He will be giving a talk about his journey from a medical student to his
current career in forensic psychiatry. He will speak about the factors that played into his choosing of
psychiatry as a specialty and then forensic psych as a subspecialty. He will also give an overview of the
field, describing the types of settings where a forensic psychiatrist may practice, what a typical day on
the job looks like, and some typical cases he encounters
Psychiatry and specifically, forensic psychiatry, are fields of medicine which students rarely get detailed
exposure to early in their medical education. A goal for this event is to expose 1st and 2nd year medical
students to the field of psychiatry earlier in their education by providing an in-depth look from our guest
speaker into the life of a practicing psychiatrist. He will also share typical cases, highlighting the unique
needs and nuances of the patients served by forensic psychiatry. This increased awareness can foster a
better understanding among future physicians in training about this often-overlooked patient
population. We also hope that Dr. Bobb's reflection on his journey to picking his specialty and unique
career path will provide insight and perspective for medical students who are discerning which specialty
they will apply to after medical school. This talk will also display a career path for students interested in
working in the intersection of medicine and law. These goals align with PSIG's purpose to enrich the
education of FSU medical students regarding mental health, increase awareness of mental illness and
the diversity of the patient population who are in need of patient-centered mental health care.

o We will be learning about medicinal herbs as well as taking a tour of FSUs very own
herb garden. First we will do our herb garden walk and as we walk we will be taught
about the medicinal uses of the different herbs by Phoenix Fermin. Phoenix Fermin is an
educator, herbalist, author, and illustrator. She will be teaching us how to explore the
depth of whole plant medicine as we discuss how plant constituents work together
synergistically creating an effective way to restore balance. This will provide a whole
new perspective into holistic medicine for the attendees and will hopefully encourage
FSUs medical students to learn about the impact plant medicine can have on treatment
ideas for future patients.

Questions:
• What are the funds for?
o FSU Sun Champs is a volunteer program established by the Dermatology Interest Group
that supplies sunscreen to those with little to no access but also educates the
importance of skin cancer prevention. Sun Champs aims to make its impact on
communities in Leon County and allow medical students interested in dermatology to
interact with the underserved directly. Some of our sites of volunteer work include
Frank Hartsfield Elementary School and Grace Mission Church. This event will involve
putting goodie bags together to be handed out to students at the school and those in
need at Grace Mission Church. Goodie bags will include items for sun protection
including sunscreen, sunglasses, and hats. In addition to receiving goodie bags, children
and the underserved will be educated on the importance of sun protection.

o We will be using the field, rock wall, and pavilion at the Rez to host our Medical Survival
Fitness event. Attendees will arrive, check in to receive their name-tags and team
assignments, and be served lunch before beginning the event activities. They will then
disperse to the multiple stations they will be cycling through. Stations will include and
obstacle course, a wilderness first aid training (with splints, tourniquets, and other first
aid demonstration), a litter/carry training station, a high intensity vital sign reading &
emergency hydration station, rock climbing for medical evacuation, and a hands-on
cricothyrotomy workshop. After each team has been to all the stations, they will
participate in a race to demonstrate the skills they learned.
All supplies will be used by participants throughout the training stations and race. Each
participant will have their own "nick fixer" survival kit with tools and an emergency
blanket needed to complete various challenges. Each team will have backpacks filled
with other necessary supplies (trauma shears, ace wraps, rolled gauze, water bottles &
hydration packets). The backpacks will be weighted for the rock wall station so that
participants can practice patient management while climbing. Bottles will be used at the
emergency hydration station along with hydration packets as part of an exposure
training session. During the final race, participants will use these tools to complete their
final challenge.
