sections.text:
e. Unanimous decision by the Executive Board and Advisor(s) pertaining to any
potential conflicts of interest
12. The IRHC Executive Board, by a majority vote, may elect to temporarily suspend a particular
requirement of an Executive Board position with the exception of GPA, judicial standing, and
residency requirements.
13. All IRHC Executive Board candidates must complete the application process as specified by
the current board.
14. The Director must reside in Tallahassee for a Summer session, with exceptions granted by
the Advisor(s).
15. Other IRHC Executive Board members do not have to live on campus during the Summer
Session. However, they must provide summer contact information for the Director in order for
business to be conducted.
16. IRHC Executive Board members shall be assigned, at minimum, one Hall Buddy at the start
of each semester through a joint decision by the Director and the Advisors. As a Hall Buddy, an
Executive Board member must:
a. Attend meetings and events of the Hall Councils when possible.
b. Act as a primary resource to the Hall Council and Advisors in terms of questions and
concerns they have.
c. Under no circumstances afford their Hall Buddy special privileges or treatment,
which shall be determined by the majority of the Executive Board as anything that
provides that Hall Council with a unique or unfair advantage and/or disadvantage over
other Hall Councils. Doing so is grounds for impeachment.
d. In the case of an IRHC Executive Board member failing/struggling to meet their
other responsibilities as outlined in the bylaws, have their duties as a Hall Buddy
lessened/eliminated as determined by the Director and Advisors. In this instance, the
responsibilities of a Hall Buddy will be transferred to another member of the IRHC
Executive Board, determined by the Director and Advisor(s) of IRHC.
17. The IRHC Executive Board will meet weekly before Board of Director Meetings, on Mondays
at 7 pm.

Section D – Specific Duties of the Board of Directors (all voting members)
1. Unless specifically stated otherwise, the quorum is defined as 50% + 1 of all voting
members. This is defined as all Vice-President(s) (or their approved representative member) and
the IRHC Executive Board, excluding the Director.

sections.heading: Page 11

a. This excludes all vacant positions.

3. The Board shall meet weekly, on Mondays at 8:30 pm.
a. If a Board member is unable to attend, they shall send a representative from their
hall.
i. A Board member must inform the Assistant Director of Operations of their
potential absence at least 48 hours before the meeting.
ii. If a Board member does not inform the Assistant Director of Operations of
their absence and send a representative in the aforementioned manner, they will
be marked as unexcused with the exception of extenuating circumstances.
iii. Assigned representatives do not have voting rights unless the said
representative is an elected Hall Council member who has attended at least one
prior Board of Directors Meeting.

one semester, that member shall enter the impeachment process.

conducted through video conferencing, such as Zoom, instead. Notification for meeting
medium changes will be given no later than five hours prior to the start time of the
meeting.

meeting will be canceled.

Article V – Committees
Section A – Committees
1. The following Committees may be created at the discretion of the IRHC Executive Board:

i. The Director shall chair the Presidents’ Roundtable.
ii. The President of each Hall Council will be a member of the President’s
Roundtable (hereafter referred to as “the Roundtable”).
iii. The Roundtable shall meet at the discretion of the Director.
1. At least 48 hours notice shall be given to the scheduling of a
Roundtable meeting.
iv. The purpose of the Roundtable is to engage in discussion and present
information about topics pertinent to running a Hall Council.
v. The members of the Roundtable may elect a vice chair at the beginning of
each semester to assist the Chair with the efficient organization of the
Roundtable.

i. The Director shall chair this committee, and the Assistant Director of Equity
and Inclusion shall co-chair this committee.
ii. The committee shall meet at the discretion of the chair.
1. At least 48 hours notice shall be given to scheduling a committee
meeting.
iii. The purpose of this committee is to give voice to residents’ concerns and
needs in order to enhance the on-campus living experience.
iv. Members of the committee will process residents’ submissions,
communicate with stakeholders, and provide guidance in the IRHC advocacy
process.
v. Any student living on campus may serve on the committee.

Article VI – Elections
Section A – Hall Council Elections
1. The general election of Hall Council Officers shall begin no later than the third week of the
Fall Semester.
2. All candidates for Hall Council positions must submit an application.
3. All candidates for Hall Council positions must meet and maintain the following eligibility
requirements, as set by IRHC and SGA Statute:
a. Have a 2.5 or higher GPA (no GPA necessary if holding position in their first
Semester at FSU, but must have a 2.5 or higher after the first Semester).
ii. GPAs will be re-checked after the conclusion of the Fall semester to
ensure members are maintaining their grades while serving in their role.
1. If their GPA for the Fall semester is lower than 2.5 the Hall Council member will
enter a period of academic probation. They will be required to set up a plan for their
academics with their advisor and show proof by midterms. If they fail to set a plan and
show proof of improving grades, they will be removed from Hall Council. If they are

sections.heading: Page 16
sections.text:
holding any extra positions within IRHC (i.e. committee member, chair, etc.) they must
relinquish their duties immediately.
2. This will take effect starting in the Fall 2024 semester.
b. Be a full-time registered FSU student.
c. Be in good judicial standing. Good judicial standing is defined as not under Conduct
or Disciplinary probation at the time of election or while in office.
d. Live in the on-campus residence hall they are elected to represent during their term
of office.
4. The eligibility requirements set forth in VI.A.3 may not be waived or amended by individual
Hall Councils at any time.
5. If any of the eligibility requirements set forth in VI.A.3 are not met at any time during the
academic year, the Advisor of the individual Hall Council and/or IRHC will enforce the removal of
the Officer that no longer meets eligibility without advice or vote of the individual Hall Council.
6. The IRHC Executive Board shall reserve the right to establish rules and specifications not
codified in the IRHC By-Laws concerning the elections of Hall Council Officers.
7. Once elected, Hall Council Officers must attend the training program in the Fall Semester
with the exception of an excused absence, as approved by the Assistant Director of Operations.
Section B – IRHC Executive Board Elections
1. Executive Board positions shall be advertised via SGA a minimum of 2 weeks’ notice prior to
the election.
a. Executive Board qualifications are stated in IV.A.1-4.
b. Elections for the National Communications Coordinator shall take place prior to
attendance at the Regional Business Conference. The NCC In-Training shall assume full
NCC responsibilities once sworn in at the Torch Awards accordingly stated in VI.B.4.
2. Applications for Executive Board positions shall be due at least one week prior to elections.
3. Executive Board elections shall take place no later than two weeks prior to Torch Awards
(unless that position remains vacant).
4. The newly elected Executive Board members shall be sworn into office at Torch Awards at
the end of the Spring semester.
5. The format of the election process shall proceed at the discretion of the Director as specified
in the IRHC By-Laws, and other relevant rules of procedure.

sections.heading: Page 17
sections.text:
a. A candidate for an office will have two minutes to speak about themselves, which
may be extended by two minutes by a majority vote of the Board for a total of four
minutes.
b. Each Board member will have one vote with the exception of the Director who will
vote only in the case of a tie.
c. Board members will have the option of voting for the candidate for a particular office
or a vote of “no confidence” or abstain.
d. The candidate who receives a plurality of the votes cast shall be the elected Officer
to that position.
e. In the event an executive position is not filled during the general election,
applications shall remain open for that position each week. An election shall occur exactly
one week after a nomination is made for a vacant executive Board position that was not
filled during the general election.
Section C – Vacancies
1. Pursuant to Statutes, if the position of Director becomes vacant, the Associate Director shall
immediately assume that position.
a. If the Associate Director is unable to permanently assume the position of the
Director, the vacancy can be held, subject to the provisions in VI.B.2-3.
2. If any IRHC Executive Board position besides the Director becomes vacant, there will be a
special election to fill the vacancy.
3. Special elections shall be subject to the provisions in VI.B.2-3.

the IRHC Executive Board.
5. Pursuant to Statutes, if less than 4 weeks remain before the installment of members, the

Executive Board with Advisor(s) approval.

has not been filled, the IRHC Executive Board may appoint any qualified University Housing
resident to the position as a temporary IRHC Executive Board member until an election is able to
be held, with the approval of the Advisor(s).
a. With the exception of the Director and Associate Director
7. In the event that a member of the IRHC Executive Board is impeached or removed
involuntarily, they are not permitted to run in a general election for any open position on the IRHC
Executive Board.

sections.heading: Page 18
sections.text:
8. In the event that a member from the IRHC Executive Board vacates their position under
extenuating circumstances, they will be permitted to run in a general election for any open
position(s) on the IRHC Executive Board the following academic semester.
a. Extenuating circumstances are at the discretion of the Advisor(s).
Article VII – Impeachment and Removal
Section A – Pursuant to Statutes and the IRHC By-Laws, the Executive Board may remove any member
of the Executive Board, except the Director, by a majority vote.
Section B – Pursuant to Statutes and the IRHC By-Laws, the Executive Board may recommend the
impeachment of the Director to the SGA Senate by a majority vote.
Section C – The following shall be grounds for impeachment:
1. Gross negligence and/or ineffectiveness.
2. Excessive absences (excused and/or unexcused).
3. Acting in defiance of the By-Laws and Statutes of the Student Body, IRHC By-Laws, IRHC
Executive policies, or Student Code of Conduct.
4. Not completing required duties as outlined by SGA Statutes or IRHC By-Laws.
5. Showing excessive and/or intentional bias towards or against any Hall/Complex or Hall
Council.
6. The Board of Directors reserves the right to entertain the validity of grounds for
impeachment not specifically codified above.
Section D – The impeacher(s) must submit a written statement of the grounds for impeachment to the
IRHC Executive Board and Advisor(s) at an executive meeting before an impeachment may begin.
1. Impeachment proceedings shall automatically be recognized as the last item of business.
2. Emergency meetings may be called for impeachment proceedings.
Section E – Any Board member directly involved with impeachment proceedings may not act as chair for
said proceedings.
1. The Director may temporarily appoint a non-Executive Officer to act as chair for
impeachment proceedings if necessary.
Section F – Advisor Removal of Executive Member

sections.heading: Page 19
sections.text:
1. In the chance that an executive member of the Inter-Residence Hall Council is not
completing their constitutional duties, and/or not upholding the values of Florida State University,
the advisor can remove them pending the below protocol is followed:
a. Verbal Warning
i. Verbal Warning notice must be documented via email and a signed letter to
be stored in the student’s file.
b. Written Warning
i. Written Warning notice must be documented via email and a signed letter to
be stored in the student’s file.
ii. The advisor and executive member will create an action plan to be followed.
c. Probationary Period
i. 1-month probationary period to improve actions to align with constitutional
duties and/or Florida State University values
ii. Probationary period notice must be documented via email and a signed
letter to be stored in the student’s file.
iii. The advisor and executive member will revisit the action plan to be followed
that was created in the written warning phase of removal.
iv. The probationary period must be approved by the Associate Director for
Residences Education.
d. Removal of Executive Member
i. Pending items A-C are completed, and there is no improvement, the next
step is the removal of the executive member.
ii. Removal of Executive Member notice must be documented via email and a
signed letter to be stored in the student’s file.
iii. The advisor must obtain permission from the Director of Residential Student
Experience as well as the Executive Director of University Housing prior to the
removal of the executive member.
iv. If the executive member is removed, they must reimburse University
Housing for the housing discount for that semester. Pending they are removed in
the Fall semester, they will also forfeit the housing discount and Dining Dollars
for the following Spring semester.

sections.text:
Article VIII – Hall Councils
Section A – Membership
1. The membership of each Hall Council shall be composed of the residents in the respective
Hall/Complex.
Section B – Elected Council Members
1. Elected Council Members of each Hall Council shall consist of the following:
a. President
b. Vice-President(s)
c. Secretary
d. Treasurer
e. Historian
f. Equity and Inclusion Rep
2. Vice-Presidents shall be determined by the maximum occupancy of the Hall/Complex in
which they reside.
a. A Vice-President shall be elected for every 500 residents in a Hall/Complex.
b. If a residence Hall/Complex exceeds 500 residents, an additional Vice-President
shall be elected.

a. Have a 2.5 or higher GPA.
i. Any Hall Council Member living in a living learning
community must follow the GPA requirements outlined by
that community.
b. Be a registered full-time FSU student.
c. Be in good judicial standing. Good judicial standing is defined as not under Conduct
or Disciplinary probation at the time of election or while in office.
d. Must live in the hall/complex that they represent.
2. Responsibilities of Hall Council members shall be as follows:

Section D – Impeachment, Succession, and Resignation
1. Hall Councils may enter the impeachment process with a majority vote of the Hall Council
and Advisor approval.
2. Grounds for impeachment shall be as follows:
a. Gross negligence and/or ineffectiveness.
b. Excessive absences (excused and/or unexcused).
c. Acting in defiance of IRHC By-Laws and/or policies set forth by University Housing,
Florida State University, or the Student Government Association.

sections.heading: Page 24
sections.text:
d. Hall Council reserves the right to entertain grounds for impeachment that are not
specifically codified above.
3. The three-step impeachment process is as follows:
a. With the entire Hall Council and Advisor present, formally state the grounds for
impeachment and, by a majority vote, advance to mediation.
b. Hold mediation with necessary parties and Advisor present.
c. If circumstances have not improved, after a minimum of two weeks, a vote to
remove the said officer from the Hall Council may be held, with the full Hall Council and
Advisor present.
i. In order to remove an officer from the Hall
Council, a majority vote is required with Advisor approval.
d. Under extenuating circumstances, the Advisor may immediately remove a Hall
Council member from office.
4. All steps of the process must be recorded, and their results reported to the IRHC Executive
Board and the IRHC Advisor(s) at the conclusion of the process in a timely manner.
5. The President will Chair impeachment trials.
a. Any Hall Council member directly involved with the impeachment proceedings may
not act as chair.
b. If the President is directly involved in the impeachment process, the Hall Council
shall appoint another member to serve as chair for the proceedings.
c. In the event that any Hall Council Member is no longer in office, a replacement
process shall be decided upon by the Hall Council and approved by the Advisor. Ideally,
an application shall be sent out to the residents of a Hall/Complex and all applications will
be reviewed and voted on by the Hall Council to determine a replacement.
Section E – Floor Representatives
1. Appointment of Floor Representatives shall be decided by the Hall Council and Advisor(s).
2. The responsibilities of the floor representatives shall be as follows:
a. Inform their floor of the activities within the Hall Council.
b. Assist in the responsibilities of the Hall Council members on a volunteer basis.
3. As long as all Hall Council Presidents or Advisors contact the IRHC Executive Board at least
three weeks before any official IRHC function, the IRHC Executive Board will adjust the event to
accommodate the additional members in terms of food and supplies.

Board and Advisors.

policies.

So I'm just gonna go over what women's accounting is first. I don't know if anyone's an
accounting major or familiar with women's accounting or profession, but we meet every
week, and we bring in lead accounting firms. So if you've heard of the Big Four, EY,
PwC, RSM, and KPMG, we bring in all of those every week, and then we also bring in
some regional and mid-sized firms as well. And so our goal is to have professionals in
our meeting. We're talking about their firm, how students can get involved with the
accounting profession is and what they can do. And then at the club, we also provide a lot
of professional development opportunities. So we'll go over resumes, LinkedIn, interview
tips—all that kind of stuff. The reason why accounting, in my opinion, is super important
for the College of Business is it's really one of the only avenues for accounting students
to get internships and network with professionals. So if anyone's in the College of
Business or is an accounting major, you get your internship after your junior year, you
apply for it, and then you intern after you graduate, and then you also get a job offer
through that. And so one of the huge ways that you get an internship is through this
networking. So we provide the one-on-one networking for members, and then we give
them all the resources. We walk them through how to get your internship, how to dress
like business casual, and everything that you could need for that. So we're really huge
resources for accounting students on campus. As you can tell, we're female-focused, so
really working to empower and connect female accounting majors. If you've heard there's
also a beta alpha psi, they're kind of like a huge honors organization. So the big
difference with us is that we're way smaller, so it's easier to network with professionals,
have them know we were, and then get internships as well. All of our members who are
actively seeking out internships secure an internship if it's the big four. The majority of
them go to the Big Four if they want to, and then everyone else applies for and secures
internships and jobs with some local and smaller firms as well. We also talk about getting
your master's, the program at FSU, the CPA, and all the credentials that are required to
enter the accounting profession. I don't know if any of you guys are, but in order to
practice accounting, you need your CPA, which is a really kind of extensive process. So
we go through that in depth. Um, I'll just walk you through what I'm requesting. I think in
the quote I sent you, I included food, but I we don't need money for that anymore, so I'm
just requesting funding for the banner and the tablecloth. And the goal with these is that
we really want to set the right tone for our organization. So the accounting industry is
rooted in professionalism, and we really want to show the 4 professional organizations
we're very established. We want students to take this seriously and we want professionals
to take us seriously—and I think that the first step we can do with that is really having the
right outward appearance. So as I mentioned, we meet every week in SSB 203, or the
globe. So if we can have the right setup, I think that'll really put us in the right direction

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
for our first impression. We also require everyone to dress business casual, and then our
presentations are very formal. So I think this is my request. It's really about setting the
right tone, engaging students, and having them really understand the importance of
professionalism within accounting and within our organization as well. And then
additionally, my goal as president this year is to really redefine women in accounting. So
I really want students to be super engaged and know what they're getting into really have
all the resources they can for accounting, for getting involved in FSU campus. So again, I
just want to set the right tone for the organization and make the best impression with our
students.

Hello, all. I'm Helena Carino. I am the president of CRU and I am Carson, the treasurer of Cru.
So over this presentation, we're just going to go over what is Cru, our future goals, our PAC
requests ranked in order of importance, our request breakdown, and then our contribution to
SGA strategic goals. So to begin, what is Cru, it's not an acronym, it's just Cru. We are a
Christian ministry, a spiritual resource for students. We believe you belong before you believe.
So it's a safe space to ask questions, if you come from a religious background or not, or you're
just curious, like, what do Christians believe? Or a space for like, yeah, safe space to ask
questions, and we do foster the opportunity for students to know Jesus. We do present the gospel,
and we are firm believers in Jesus so we’re open. So some future goals that we have with the
funding is to provide scholarships for some retreats that we have throughout the year. We know
students can have financial strains, and we want to be there to provide scholarships for them,
whether that be a discount or total like pay for the whole thing, also meals at Cru before Cru will
also allow community. In the Bible, it talks about Jesus eating with his disciples, and so that's a
great time for us to, yeah, just be a community and have fellowship with one another. And also,
we know food can also be a stressor for students, so that can also promote or combat food
insecurity. And then also, if we get funding for flyers and yard signs, it will help us to expand
our reach across campus because we're a global organization, but at FSU, we're not the largest so
we do want to get our name out there, and that will help. So overall, our PAC request breakdown
and as for our Fall getaway, the event per individual is $121 with the totals all being on the right
hand side, right there. And then the fall getaway shirts, $1379, per student, which would be
included in the total price for the scholarships we pay for. And then for Cru socials, we have a
bunch throughout the semester, like a Halloween event, a Christmas event, like chili cook-offs,
just a bunch of different ones. So $200 just gives us the opportunity to provide food, drinks, and
different activities for us all to do together. And then for the monthly Cru meetings, which
Kirsten just mentioned, we just, like picked Chick-fil-A as like an easy option with $873 being
the price per meal, and then food and drinks for tabling, for like we do at the beginning of each
semester, and just throughout the semester, $13 for, like a box of Cheez-Its or like some drinks,
waters, everything like that. And then yard signs are $25 per yard sign. So for our request, an
order of importance is also listed on the previous slide, but it's just funding for the Fall getaway

o Preliminary Questions:

o Notes of the Event/Item:
▪ Opening:
● The Vietnamese Student Association is an organization that helps
to create an inclusive environment to support Vietnamese culture.
Tally by Night is inspired by Paris by Night and is a free event
open to all FSU students and the public. We hope to improve our
external relations as well as at FSU. The theme this year is inspired
by Beauty and the Beast. We will have live performances from
different AASU Affiliate organizations and several interactive

sections.text:

be covering the venue with our own funds. We settled on Seminole
Dining catering and Publix after reviewing our quotes.

could you cut to maintain the event?

venue, we would likely cut one of the appetizers from
Publix if we needed. We also have a sponsorship and share
it night to increase our organizational funds.

o RSO Representative: We opened up a new merchandise line
to raise funds. I don’t have the exact amount fundraised, but
we currently have around $800 that has gone toward
funding our GBMs and our banquet last semester.

o RSO Representative: We’ve never posted flyers on/off
campus before but that is a current plan of ours.
● Chair Wyatt: Are you aware you need to acknowledge SGA
funding?
o RSO Representative: Yes.

but had heard negative experiences from other
organizations. We also looked at a local country club but
because it was a private entity is was much more expensive.
Wesley center is the most accessible and cheap.
o Ellison: How much was the quote for the Union?
o RSO Representative: We have it as $750 for the rental plus
the required service fee.

the event?

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
● This semester we have been revamping the yoga club because the
leach has reduced their classes. We’ve seen overwhelming demand
to put on more classes. We’ve had over 60 people wanting to attend
our events on landis and we’ve had to instate an RSVP form. It’s
difficult to get instructors for our classes because they want to be
paid. Our past administration gave us nothing for funding, so we
reached out to all our instructors and got their individual rates
which are all listed here on the document. We’ve hosted a variety
of fun classes and hope to offer more in the future. All of this
would be beneficial to the student body because college is stressful.
We have over 600 people in our groupme chat and over 1,000
followers on instagram. All our instructors listed here are FSU
Students and they’re all certified, experienced teachers. To explain
our quotes, a lot of FSU students don’t have their own yoga mats
and we only have very few old ones. This funding would help us
provide the equipment.
▪ Questions:
● Borges: There are two main things you;re looking for, wages and
funding for mats, correct?
o RSO Representative: Yes.
● Borges: All of these instructors are students, correct?
o RSO Representative: Yes, and they’re all yoga certified.
● Ellison: Is there a future where you can fundraise for your club in
instances we cannot fund you?
o RSO Representative: Yes we are looking to do class fees
and sell tshirts as a method of raising our own funds. Our
last administration really dropped the ball.
● Ellison: Is there a difference in the quality of the yoga mats you’re
requesting?
o RSO Representative: The main difference is the thickness,
thicker mats are more comfortable.
● Borges motioned to enter roundtable discussion, seconded by
Ellison.
▪ Roundtable:
● Borges: The instructors are certified. This would be a contractual
service I assume so would they need a written contract with each
instructor? It looks like there are four separate instructors.
o Chair Wyatt: I think what they’re provided is fine.
o Borges: If this gets approved, can they cut checks?
o Chair Wyatt: Accounting really handles all of that, I’m not
too sure how it works but I know it won’t be an issue.
● Borges: Is there an issue with the instructors being students? I
don’t have an issue with it personally but I see a conflict of interest
because students are involved in the club?

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
o Boisvert: I don’t see it being an issue
● Borges: For the mats, are they good as far as quotes or would they
need to provide more?
o Chair Wyatt: I think it’s fine, we can see the base price for
mats.
o Ellison: Is that included in the total for contractual
services?
o Jariwala: I think it is separate so we would have to add on
to expenses. The $1,360 is only for the instructors.
● Ellison: Would the yoga mats need to be FSU property?
o Chair Wyatt: I got some clarification on this, and I think
they should be fine. They wouldn’t be FSU property.
● Jariwala: I just don’t think we talked more about it, but I would say
to fund between the 3mm and 4mm mats because someone said
they had the 4mm and it was fine.
o Borges: I like the 4mm.
● Jariwala: For the special events they mostly mentioned the
weekend classes, so if we had to cut the headphone yoga would
that be okay with the sponsors?
o RSO Representative: We have done the headphone yoga
twice and received high demand for it, if something needs
to be cut I would say maybe the sound bath one because we
don’t have as much experience with it.
● Borges: Have you all had any opportunities for fundraising?
o RSO Representative: Yes we can plan events in the future.
● Borges: If they receive the funds, it has to be spent in a matter of
time, correct?
o Chair Wyatt: Yes, it is supposed to be 90 days but we can
waive that. They should be fine.
● Ellison motioned to approve the line item for Contractual
Services to $1360 and $340 for the category of Expenses
seconded by Borges.
▪ Closing:
● We source our instructors from local yoga studios and our special
event classes are professional instructors that aren’t FSU Students.
▪ Vote:
● Yay: Jariwala, Borges, Daniel, Boisvert.
● Nay: None
● Abstain: None

▪ Opening:
● The Society of Women Engineers mission is to empower women to
achieve their full potential in careers as engineers and leaders.
Their annual banquet will be open to all students and faculty for
networking and connections throughout the community.
Advertising will be done through social media and at their GBM
meetings. They are having the event at Township in The Garden.
They are requesting money for food from the venue. They are
requesting money for shareables like quesadillas, chicken tenders,
sliders, and dips. There is a $1,500 minimum on food to rent out
the venue space. The service charge for Township is $332.20. The
sales tax is $113.25. The total cost of the event will cost $1,955.45.
Their sample flier that will be posted on their social media includes
SGA acknowledgement.
▪ Questions:
● Mausam: How much have you fundraised?
o RSO Representative: Yes, we have done substantial
fundraising but most of the money goes towards our
conference in the Fall.
● Daniel: Is this the first year you are hosting the event?
o RSO Representative: Last year we hosted the event at
Georgio’s but it was a lot more expensive because we had
to do a sit-down dinner. We wanted to make the event more
casual and less expensive this year.
● Chair Wyatt: Will this event be open to all FSU students?
o RSO Representative: Yes, it will be.
● Daniel: How much was the cost last year at Georgio’s?
o If we went with Gerogio’s this year, it would be $3,072.75.
Last year, we also had appetizers, so it cost even more.
● Daniel: How did you fundraise for the event last year? Did you get
funding from PAC?
o Our advisor planned last year’s event and she used our
conference money.

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
● Mausam motioned to enter roundtable discussion, seconded by
Juilo.
▪ Roundtable:
● Daniel: I’m a bit concerned about how they funded a more
expensive event last year but need PAC funds this year?
● Point of Information from Julio: Can you explain the funding
situation from last year a bit more?
o RSO Representative: We had an old advisor last year who
used up a lot of our club funds to put together this event.
We are still in the process of finding a new advisor so we
have had to take on this task ourselves. We want to make
sure that we are saving the club funds for our main
conference.
● Point of Information from Daniel: Would you be able to use any
organization funds to help fund this event?
o RSO Representative: We could, but we would have to
probably ask for additional funds in the Fall to pay for our
conference then.
● Point of Information from Mausam: How often have you received
money for the conferences?
o RSO Representative: It depends. The cost changes each
year because of new locations. This last year we had to fly
from Jacksonville to Texas. This year, this will probably
double for each girl because the conference will be in
California. It is hard to get companies to donate this much
money.
● Daniel: They have not received any PAC money this year.
● Point of Information from Mausam: If you had to come back to
PAC to ask for additional money, would that be this semester or
next semester?
o RSO Representative: Our conference would be funded from
RTAC in the Fall. It usually takes place in October. For this
banquet, we are also taking on a lot of the costs ourselves
already. We have other ceremonies and expenses that we
will be paying for. We are just requesting money from PAC
for the venue and food.
● Daniel: I want to fund this event, but I’m concerned with the
limited funds we have left for this semester.
● Point of Information from Mausam: I think we are just a bit
confused on how the money was spent this year versus last year.
How were you able to afford last year’s event without a PAC
request?

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
o RSO Representative: Our advisor chose to spend our
money on this dinner instead of on the conference last year.
She spent more money than a majority of us agreed on.
● Daniel: I think we should reduce the line item by a bit.
● Mausam: I think we should cut funding because of the limited
funds that PAC has.
● Point of Information from Chair Wyatt: What possible fundraising
events could your organization do to pay for the event and
conference if PAC had to cut funding?
o RSO Representative: In the past we did t-shirt fundraising
at Madison Social, took donations at the Career Fair, and
reached out to companies to see if they would like to donate
to the club.
● Daniel: I think we should cut funding. They can use some of their
club funds to pay for this event and still have time to fundraise
additionally for the conference in October. Also, RTAC’s budget
will be updated and they can request more money from them.
● Daniel Elison moved to amend the line item to $1,555.45 in the
category of Food. Seconded by Mausam Jariwala.
▪ Closing:
● These funds do help so thank you.
▪ Vote:
● Yay: Daniel Elison, Mausam Jariwala, Julio Cesar Borges
● Nay: None
● Abstain: None

● We are requesting money for our animation convention. Each year,
our convention brings an experience to those who would not be
able to spend the money to travel or attend these types of Japanese
cultural conventions. We will hold a cosplay contest, drawing
contest and more. This is a free event for anyone in the FSU public
to attend. We are trying to provide funding for one of our featured
guests who will be speaking in a panel about Japanese culture. We
want to pay for her hotel room of $346.
▪ Questions:
● Chair Wyatt: I would like to confirm the amounts that you are
asking for.
o RSO Representative: Originally, we requested money for
food, clothing, and other expenses. Now, we just need
funding to pay for the guest hotel room.
● Daniel: Could you elaborate on the guest you are funding the hotel
room for?
o RSO Representative: The guest is a cosplay guest who has
won various awards for costume construction. She is
hosting a panel about handmade cosplays. She is also going
to be a judge in the convention’s cosplay contest. She will
be staying at the Four Points on Sheraton Hotel. She is
checking in on March 3rd and checking out on March 5th.
● Chair Wyatt: Did you look at any other hotels?
o We looked at other hotels but this is the hotel that was
already booked and reserved.
● Chair Wyatt: So the hotel is already booked?
o RSO Representative: Yes, they are requesting
reimbursement.
● Chair Wyatt: Unfortunately, PAC is not able to do any
reimbursements according to SGA statutes.
● Daniel motioned to enter roundtable discussion, seconded by
Mausam.
▪ Roundtable:
● Daniel: Are we allowed to fund hotels normally?
● Chair Wyatt: Yes, I believe that would fall under the expense
category but we are not allowed to give reimbursements.
● Mausam motioned to zero fund the line item, seconded by
Daniel.
▪ Closing:
● None
▪ Vote:
● Yay: Daniel Ellison, Mausam Jariwala
● Nay: None

o Notes of the Event/Item:
▪ Opening:
● ASU is hosting this event to honor the month of Ramadan. ASU is
not a religious organization but a cultural one. Still, many
individuals within our community are Muslim and we want to
show our support and celebrate their religion alongside them. Last
year, we had a massive amount of people attend and it went very
successfully. We are asking to fund two different events. The Persis
Quote is for the first Iftar. The 64 Tally is for the second event. We
used Persis last year because they are easy to work with and the
Indian food is popular. They will cost us $1,525.68. We chose 64
Tally for the second Iftar because there is not much Middle Eastern
food in Tallahassee. We share a lot of culture and religious customs
with the Turkish people so we wanted to do an event to celebrate
that union. 64 Tally is also a new business. 64 Tally will cost
$3,016.04. They are providing a lot more diverse food options,
deserts, and cutlery. We will be advertising on social media with
“Paid for by SGA” included.
▪ Questions:
● Mausam: Are you asking for money for both quotes for two
events?
o RSO Representative: Yes, each quote correlates with its
own event.
● Chair Wyatt: What type of fundraising do you do as an
organization and can you contribute to the banquet with those
funds?
o RSO Representative: We usually budget for the cutlery
expenses. We fundraise mostly through share-it-nights for

sections.heading: Page 9
sections.text:
these expenses. Whenever we have needed t-shirts, we have
gone through PAC. We have about $300 that we can
contribute to this event. We help out with other events and
GBM expenses throughout the year.
● Daniel: Have you thought about other ways to improve fundraising
efforts?
o RSO Representative: We fundraise for what we know we
need. We have a lot of international students and graduate
students and like to emphasize that SGA gets to give back
to this community that SGA doesn’t get to help often.
● Chair Wyatt: If you were not able to get fully funded from PAC,
how would the event change or what would you do to fundraise the
rest?
o We could try to cut down the quote price. For example, we
could take out the dessert from 64 Tally. We still want to
make sure that we are giving 200 people a full meal,
however. We learned last year that after a full day of
fasting, people will need a substantial meal and not just
“samples” of everything. We could cut how many people
we would let into the event.
● Mausam motioned to enter roundtable discussion. Seconded by
Daniel.
▪ Roundtable:
● Daniel: This is a big request so I think we should try to cut the
amount.
● Chair Wyatt: It appears that they are almost having two different
banquets - one on the 29th of March and one on April 19th.
● Daniel: Didn’t we fund the Muslim Student Union last week for a
Ramadan Event?
● Chair Wyatt: Yes, we funded them for $3,140 last week for their
event on March 28th.
● Daniel: What if MSU and ASU collaborated on the event on March
28th and only funded the ASU event on April 19th?
● Mausam: Yes, I think we could propose that. They still would have
some time to fundraise additionally if needed.
● Chair Wyatt: The Persis quote is for the 29th. The 64 Tally is for
the April event. If this committee wanted to recommend that ASU
partner with MSU for the MSU event on the 28th, the April event
that ASU wants to hold would still cost $3,016.
● Mausam: I think we should fund the April 19th event and ask them
to collaborate with MSU for their March event.
● Daniel: I agree.

sections.heading: Page 10
sections.text:
● Point of Information from Mausam: As you know, we are running
low on funds. Would you be okay with attending the MSU banquet
on March 28th and us only funding you April 19th event?
o RSO Representative: Was MSU funding approved by PAC?
o Chair Wyatt: Yes, MSU was approved last week by PAC.
We obviously cannot speak on behalf of MSU, but we
believe that you could possibly have a joint event.
o RSO Representative: Yes that sounds great. Are we able to
table the request so that we have time to reach out to MSU?
o Chair Wyatt: If approved by PAC, there are a few more
steps that the request needs to go through before you
actually have access to those funds. So, at any point in
those meetings the amount can change. You could speak on
behalf of your organization to ask for more money or
further change the line item in the Finance Committee or
Senate.
● Mausam motioned to amend the line item for $3,016 in the
category of Food, seconded by Daniel.
▪ Closing:
● We appreciate the diligent work of this committee. Also, thank you
for funding 64 Tally as they are a new business. I’m sure this is
helping them a lot.
▪ Vote:
● Yay: Daniel Ellison, Mausam Jariwala, Patrick DuChêne
● Nay: None

public health issues. The organization will serve to help improve
and promote the importance of quality health for minorities. They
seek to empower the minds of future public health works through
the strategies and community service they implement. They do

● We are trying to renew our website/domain. Our studio H space is
an all encompassing platform for us to show off our events and
allow virtual opportunities for therapy workshops. This will span
from 2022-2024. We want a space that we found through covid to
allow students more free time to seek therapy. We are a mental
health awareness club, we have done events through landis as well
as some joint groups and graduate programs. We are student led,
and our main point is to make therapy more accessable for
students. Squarespace is an easy-access website for our team and
our members. Through our website, we have our home page, about
us, FAQ’s, and an archive journal of our future/past events. We also
include workshops and art therapy online events into our website.
Our website has grown since the last year and we’ve noticed more
people signing up to the website. This renewal is necessary to
maintain our domain name. Our more budget-friendly option will
keep our domain alive, but will be more difficult for our officers to
manage and won’t show us our analytics. Our current plan will be
$260 which has been a great budget/productivity plan for us -
overall its been a great plan. The more upgraded option would be
$344 and would allow us more opportunities to promote
fundraising options and include more editing features.
▪ Questions:
● Ellison: Could you go back to the slide with the upgrade? What
exactly are you upgrading to?
o RSO Representative: We don’t have a fundraising option
with the other plan, but we would be able to fundraise and
edit with this option. It would expand our opportunities as a
whole.
● Jariwala: If we were to fund you, would you be okay with the
current plan?
o RSO Representative: We would.
● Chair Wyatt: You don't charge club dues, so how do you pay for
your programs?
o RSO Representative: Last year we had a lot of funding for
art materials which will last us until the end of this year. We
use things like cardboard boxes which allows us to be very
resourceful. We also collaborate with other clubs to keep
costs low.
● Chair Wyatt: Have you received pac funding for this website
before?
o RSO Representative: This will be our third year. We also
got funding for our “Impact” event.
● Ellison motioned to enter roundtable discussion, seconded by
Jariwala.

definitely reaching their audience. Especially because
they’ve been coming to pac for years we can potentially
fund higher.

o Opening:
▪ The mission of Special Olympics at FSU is to promote inclusion at Florida
State and in the community through sports training, competitors, and
campaigns for people with and without intellectual disabilities. They

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
provide year-round sports training and athletic competition in a variety of
sports for children and adults with intellectual disabilities, giving them
continuing opportunities to develop physical fitness, demonstrate courage,
experience joy and participate in a sharing of respect, skills, and friendship
with their families, other Special Olympics athletes and the community.
They are requesting $4,045 for their Spread the Word Week. The week is
centered around a national event. Registration opens first for FSU students
and then the general community. The event is free for everyone. The week
begins on February 25th with a kickball tournament on the main campus
fields. Student organizations will be invited to table and any student or
community member can participate. On February 26th, they will be
hosting a cookout at the Rez. Most of the funding they are requesting is for
food for this day. On February 27th, they will be having a social media
contest challenging people to increase their water intake. On the 28th, they
will be having a crafts day and will be chalking across campus. On the
29th, they will be tabling around campus. The next day, they will be
having Dinner & Discussion @ the Inclusion Benches. On the 3rd, they
will be playing the As Far as They Can Run movie.
o General Questioning:
▪ Chair Wyatt: Since we will not be able to fund any prizes that you will be
giving away at the event, will you be okay with funding that elsewhere?
▪ RSO representative: Okay, that’s fine.
▪ Chair Wyatt: What is the breakdown of who is getting what? Is it more for
the athletes or FSU students?
▪ RSO representative: Everything is open to everyone who participates. FSU
students will have priority and be able to sign up first. There are only a
limited number of athletes that actually participate, so a strong majority of
everything funded will go to FSU students. Everything goes first to
students.
▪ Chair Wyatt: What is your advertising strategy?
▪ RSO representative: Student organizations that we are partnering with will
be helping spread the word. Members from the media will also be coming
out to some of the events. We will be posting on our social media with all
the information for the week.
▪ Chair Wyatt: Will you be acknowledging SGA funding on the posts?
▪ RSO representative: Yes, we will have the logo. Our t-shirts also say “Paid
for by SGA”.
▪ Daniel Elison: Do you have a percentage breakdown of partners vs.
athletes that will be participating?
▪ RSO representative: We expect there to be 120 FSU students and faculty.
There will be about 30 athletes. There will also be a lot of spectators but
only participating FSU students, faculty and athletes will be served.
▪ Motion to enter roundtable by Jackson Boisvert, seconded by Daniel
Elison

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
▪ Chair Wyatt: I want us to go through these quotes line by line so that we
are making sure that everything follows SGA statutes.
● First, there is the quote from Full Press for their table cloth of
$222.13.Next, they have two other quotes from Full Press for
shirts. One quote is for short sleeve shirts and one is for
long-sleeve shirts. We can fully fund the short-sleeve shirts
because they fall under the maximum amount we can fund on a per
shirt basis. They are looking to purchase 30 small, 35 medium, 30
large, 30 XL, 15 XXL, and 10 XXXL. This comes out to
$1,277.64. On the long-sleeve shirt quote, we would have to cut
funding because the per shirt amounts are too expensive. They are
also requesting the same sizing breakdown. If we funded the
maximum amount that we could for the shirts, it would be a total
of $1,550. The total Clothing & Awards category would be
$3,049.77 for the table cloth, long sleeve shirts, and short sleeve
shirts.
● Next, let’s look at the Expense category. The committee wants to
fund the printer paper, printer ink multi-pack, printer black ink,
clear spray paint, gold spray paint, garnet spray paint, and business
cards, table cloths, and postcard paper and stamps. The committee
is also funding for soil that will go towards their Arts and Craft day
when they will be planting flowers in pots as an activity. The posts
and seeds are already being donated. The committee will also fund
for the renting of tables and chairs from FSU Facilities.
● Next, let’s look at the Food category. The committee wants to fund
for their Dinner Meal ($500) from Legacy Catering, chips and
candy ($41), food for their Movie Day from Publix ($108), Boxed
Lunches from Subway ($400),
● The committee decided to cut funding for a wagon, portable power
station, iPad, Plaque, Instagram Ads, Drying Rack, iPad Case with
Screen Protector, Cricut Paper, Laundry Soap, and Dryer Sheets.
▪ Point of Information from Chair Wyatt to RSO sponsor: Do you want
funding for the short-sleeve shirts or the long-sleeve shirts.
▪ RSO representative: We included the quote for the short-sleeve shirts
because we knew it fell under the maximum allotted per t-shirt. We believe
we can fundraise additional money to cover what SGA cannot cover for
the long-sleeve shirts, so we would like for you to fund those.
▪ Motion to amend by Jackson Boisvert for $1,772 in the Clothing &
Awards category, $1,049 in the Food category, and $527 in the Expense
Category. Seconded by Daniel Elison.

▪ Yay: Anneliese Pruim, Jackson Boisvert, Zach Hansen, Daniel Elison

▪ Abstain: None

o Notes of the Event/Item:

Opening statement:
Treasurer: Alyssa Goosby
- They are a mentorship group at FSU for Black women. They go to
different high schools and middle schools in Leon county to talk
about what it means to be a college student, and how they can
make their pathway to becoming a student.

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
- They are requesting money for t-shirts. There are 60 girls in the
club but asking for 50 shirts. She presented 3 quotes. The shirts
will have their logo in purple and the shirt will say “paid for by
SGA”. cheapest option was full press for $440.64
- They are asking for $400 and they will pay the difference. The
money they will use to pay the difference are from dues and
fundraising events from this semester and last semester. This is a
new club at FSU, they started in fall 2021. They exist at FAMU
and some other campuses nationwide.
General Question:
- Senator Marshall Widmann: On your application, it says you
have 50 active members, but in your speech you said there were
about 60 members. So if you do have more members than shirts
that you are requesting. What is the deciding factor on who gets
the tshirt?
- Alyssa Goosby: I’m assuming after we get approved for the shirts,
this semester will end. We have girls graduating this fall so they
probably won’t get a shirt. We plan on giving them out in the
spring. If they are part of that sign up, they will base it off of that.
- Chair Austin wyatt: Your shirts, your just handing them out to
members or how do you plan on distributing them?
- Alyssa Goosby: We were going to distribute to dues paying
members but since we are open to anyone on campus who is open
to joining and if they can’t afford dues they can talk to treasurer.
But yes anyone is able to get the t-shirts but member paying dues
are first priority.
- Chair Katie Feldkirchner: I didn't see paid for by SGA, do you
guys plan to add that to put on the side or back?
- Alyssa Goosby: Yes they will add it to the shirts on the bottom.
Daniel Ellison: I motion to move to enter roundtable discussion.
Marshall Widmann: Second
Roundtable:
- Austin Wyatt: Entertain a motion to call to question on line item.
Marshall Widmann: I move to call a question on the line item for $400.
Daniel Ellison: Second
Closing statement:
- We are a mentorship for black girls. This is our first round of T-
shirts. We’ve never gotten fundings from SGA, but we’ve been to
sweepings. It is important to us to have a name on campus. We go
to the market every wednesday. The funding of t-shirts will
improve our image on campus and help us grow on campus.

● Best Buddies at FSU – Best Buddies Friendship Walk
o Preliminary Questions:
▪ Asking for: $150 for Contractual Services, $800 for Food, $4,000 for
Expenses, and $94 for Clothing & Awards ($5,044 total)
▪ Date Request Submitted: 10/9/22
▪ Date of Event: 4/1/23 from 2-6pm
▪ Number of Active Members: 150
▪ Number expected to come: 250
▪ Fundraised: $20,000
o Notes of the Event/Item:
▪ Notes:
Opening statement:
Representative from best buddies: Carly and Caitlyn
- They are requesting money for the friendship walk in April. Best
Buddies is an international organization advocating for people with
intellectual disabilities. A friendship walk is an annual event that
all chapters hold. It is a fundraising event and a celebration. People
from the community come out and it is a great way to spread
inclusion and knowledge about people with intellectual disabilities.
Typically chapters, like Jacksonville, have multiple chapters that
come together to hold this event. In Tallahassee, they are alone,
they are the only chapter here so they have to put on this event by
themselves.
- This event celebrates all the inclusion and friendships made in best
buddies this year. At the end of the year it gives the best buddies
the chance to see how incredible our mission is and see the
opportunity it brings in our community. Our buddies have faced
social isolation for their whole life and now a new scale with
covid, by having this event we’re giving our buddies a once in a
lifetime opportunity,we want them to feel included, especially
now, more than before. It would show the FSU body what best
buddies goals are and the friend walk is so joyful and it benefits
the buddies and provides them something to look forward to every
year.
General Question:
- Senator Marshall Widmann: You said this is a fundraising event,
how are you raising funds?

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
- Caitlyn: The funds we raise do not specifically go to our chapter.
Throughout the year we have different share it nights, and different
fundraising opportunities like doing events such as the walk kick
off party. Where we have people donate baskets and then raffle
them off with the funds. All the money raised goes into the main
friendship walk page for best buddies international. They take that
money once the walk is over, and break it up to decide how much
the chapter at FSU gets and then around nationwide.
- Senator Marshall Widmann: Are you raffling off these baskets at
the end of the event?
- Caitlyn: They will give them away at the walk kick off party.
They work to fundraise for the walk. They take the money
internationally through the friendship walk pages. They do not
keep the money they fundraised for the walk..
- Chair Kaite Feldkirchner: Would like to see the breakdown for
the total cost.
- Caitlyn: Explains breakdown of food. They wanted treats for the
buddies so they wanted to get dippin dots. They also want to get
pizza and snacks. One of the snacks they will get is popcorn but
they don’t have seasoning so they want to buy popcorn seasoning.
They want the tent rentable, bounce house, arts and craft and
decor. They used all the money from sweeping they got last year.
They want to make a sensory table with orbeez kinetic sand, paint-
a-pot and coloring pages. Getting balloons for a balloon arch and
table clothes since they requested tables at the old IM field. They
also want to provide goodie bags for the buddies so they have
something because you can only get the shirts provided by best
buddies international you have to raise $35. Also want to get
custom buttons. They only have $1,000 in their account to spend
on the friendship walk and two other events, which they believe is
not enough.
Breakdown:
Food: 1,165.71
Expenses: $2,184
Clothing and awards: 653.75
Final total: $5,196
- Marshall Widmann: So you said you have $1,000 budgeted to
this, so do you have other funds available if needed. In the event
you weren’t fully funded all of it, would you still be able to have
this event?
- Caitlyn: She will not have extra funds to pull from. If they do not
get the full funding, technically they can put up the event but not to
the scale they had it last year. Because they will not be able to have
all the food requested. Taking away money won't allow them to
have a lot of activities and be a smaller event. Maybe some field
game but they already have another event like that. So They are

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
trying to differentiate it. They also want to try to get the friendship
to look like areas where best buddies are bigger.
- Austin Wyatt: Did you say you're going to have 80 buddies?
- Caitlyn: Yes, there are 80 buddy pairings. So the 80 buddies will
be there plus the members and their families. People from the
Tallahassee community come as well. There were 100 volunteers
last year and they stayed for the event. There were 500 people last
year and expected to be around the same.
- Marshall Widmann: Will you need security or have you reached
out to fsu pd?
- Caitlyn: They have reached out to them. But they said that they
don't need security or EMS. They did not have it last year.
- Kaite Feldkirchner: I saw on your budget request, you had water.
Those are individually water bottles, correct?
- Caitlyn: We were going to do individually packaged. We did that
last year as well.
- Katie Feldkirchner: PAC cannot fund for individual water
bottles. So if you want to switch that to coolers. But we cannot
make individual water bottles.
- Caitlyn: If we can keep the $100 and get coolers and cups that
would be great.
- Austin Wyatt: Where is the walk taking place?
- Caitlyn: The walk is happening at the old IM fields.
Senator Marshall Widmann: Motion to move to roundtable discussion.
Chair Katie Feldkirchner: Second.
Roundtable:
- Chair: Austin Wyatt: Original PAC request was for $5,044. The
Request they brought in today was $5,196
- Chair: Katie Feldkirchner: Can you pull up budget cheat
- Senator: Marshall Widmann: The buttons and bags requested on
etsy, did u get multiple quotes on those?
- Caitlyn: she was going to order them through, because it's easier
to checkout online since its a set price.
- Katie Feldkirchner: Fully supports funding the water coolers but
takes out the popcorn seasoning and wants to fund for $5,100.
- Senator Marshall Widmann: Are you planning on doing the
bounce house or not?
- Caitlyn: They are still planning on getting the bounce house.
Keagan Barrett: I move to amend it to $5,100.
Marshall Widmann: Second.
Closing statement:

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
- They originally asked for $5,196 but we took out the cost of
popcorn seasoning which was $98.85, then changed to $5,100.
- Breakdown:
Contractual Services: $150
Food: $1,069.64 (originally what they asked for: $1,165.71)
Expenses: $3,226.61

Total: $5,100

o Preliminary Questions:

▪ Date Request Submitted: 11/03/22
▪ Date of Event: 11/22/22 at 7pm
▪ Number of Active Members: 17
▪ Number expected to come: 15
▪ Fundraised: $0
o Notes of the Event/Item:
▪ Notes:
Opening statement:
Representatives of VEG FSU: Tori Noonan, Jessica Murphy
- The are asking for funding for their potluck. Their main goal is to
get the campus more focused on sustainable living when it comes
to living off the land and having a plant based diet. They aren't just
a vegan club, they also care about intersectionality and
environmental protection. They also care about equal rights such as
human rights and ending speicism.
- They’ve had potluck for the past 3-4 years but this is the first time
asking for funding. They want to expand their reach on campus.
They want to make it more inclusive and accessible to provide a
little bit more food than usual.
- They want to cater to everyone. Everything is vegan. They also ask
members to bring in their own items. And they have been
successful in the passed. This is their biggest event of the semester.
- It is open to the public. It isn't about food but also education. Focus
mainly on thanksgiving and the history of it. And how sustainable
living is still able to happen even if you aren't on a plant based diet.
Everything that will be served is vegan and all foods brought to
this event are vegan.
General Question:

sections.heading: Page 7
sections.text:
- Chair Austin Wyatt: Your cheapest item is walmart for $80 and
then public. Were you guys requesting a specific place or
rounding?
- Tori: We were estimating. We weren't sure what we were going to
make.
- Senator Marshall Widmann: With the mini water bottles, are
those single used plastic?
- Tori: Yes, they're zephyrhills.
- Senator Marshall Widmann: We are unable to fund water bottles
through SGA.
- Senator Marshall Widmann: Do you have any plans on doing
fundraising in the future?
- Tori: We have had a rocky background. We have not requested
any money because we were undergoing a lot of e-board
challenges. We did not have much of anything to work with. Was
put into this position with nothing. This is practically their first
year as a club. So they have not fundraised yet. This is a
completely new e-board but in the future, we do have a lot planned
for next semester. They found a new advisor. At the moment no
fundraising but yes in the future.
- Chair Katie Feldkirchner: Do you have a preference between the
three places and why?
- Tori: We do not have a preference. We did pick whole foods but
we need the same ingredients so it doesn’t matter what store we get
it from. And they all provide it. No preference since its the same
everywhere.
- Chair Austin Wyatt: how do you plan on advertising?
- Tori: They are posting on social media, specifically, Instagram.
The post will include- what they do and what they are having.
Invited ESP and the gbm was in the sustainable newsletter. Mainly
through instagram. And advertise it on groupme. They put a poll
for who can and cannot attend.
Senator Marshall Widmann: Motion to enter roundtable.
Senator Keagan Barrett: Second.
Roundtable:
- Senator Marshall Widmann: I move to amend to $77.
- Mausam Jariwala: Second.
- Chair Katie Feldkirchner: Would like to raise to $90. Being
vegetarian and being here during thanksgiving, i would like to
invited my friends. And because FSU doesn’t provide anything
like this i would like to attend it. It will allow for more flexibility.
- Chair Katie Feldkircher : Motion to move to $90
- Senator Marshall Widmann: Second.
Senator Keagan Barrett: motion to call question of $90

sections.heading: Page 8
sections.text:

- There isn’t anything like this on campus. People stay here during
thanksgivings and its great to have a little bit more for people.
- Funding $90 for food.

Opening statement: Camille Eynard
- Previous PAC fundings they have gotten has gone to printing their
magazines. The money they've got was allocated to magazine
printing. The purpose for printing is to distribute free magazines
and organize an event: magazine release event. They have funded
half the publication through fundraisers.
- The purpose for printing a diverse world fashion magazine is to
highlight the diversity of our student-body on campus and embrace
how different cultures embody various trends and fashion
movements through the production of one entirely student-run
fashion magazine per semester.. They give out free copies to fsu
students. Members get priority for the magazines.
- The purpose of this event is to celebrate their members.

sections.heading: Page 10
sections.text:
General Question:
- Senator Marshall Widmann: How many magazines did you print
last year?
- Camille: I don’t have an exact number. I cannot say.
- Senator Marshall Widmann: How many magazine copies did
you have left over?
- Camille: We don't have any leftovers. We handed and distributed
them all out.
- Senator Marshall Widmann: If we fund $150, what does this
mean? Would you give them out on campus?
- Camille: We give out a lot of magazines to people who worked on
it and their friends. After the event, we give away during market
Wednesday to attract people.
- Senator Austin Wyatt: What is the target number yall are asking
for? You guys were only requesting $250 in the original request.
- Camille: We can afford printing and the magazine and for a
release event and a safety net for next semester if we don't have
enough funding for next semester.
- Senator Marshall Widmann: If we funded you just for printing,
would you have enough funds to hold the event?
- Camille: I don't know. We would have to push dues. They turned
dues due for tomorrow. They could try to work with it. They
wanted to do something for their members. So the extra money
would help.
- Chair Austin Wyatt: You're asking for printing cost, food costs
but do not have an estimate for that and vendor cost?
- Camille: Yes. They have to print before the event, printing before
thanksgiving break. They want to print before November 19th
- Chair Austin Wyatt: The cost in your spreadsheet is for 100
copies?

requesting the lowest margin of $1,067.

food, you are asking for $50, is that correct? And are there quotes
- Camielle: No, there are no quotes.

- Camille: We can cover the cost for the venue and printing. not
comfortable, but we can make it work.
- Senator Marshall Widmann: The event is plausible but the target
margin is to have a perfect amount to have?
- Camille: The target margin is a little bit higher. Lowest margin is
doable
- Senator Marshall Widmann: You can still have events without
having financial strain.

74th Student Senate
Programming Allocation Committee
October 6th, 2022
Call to Order: 5:01
Members Present: Chair Wyatt, Katie Feldkirchner, Mausam Jariwala
Members Tardy: NA
Members Absent: NA
Guests: Senator Folwell, Chair Diaz, Chair Rider
Announcements:
● Chair – NA
● Vice Chair – NA
● Members – NA
Committee Business:
● Society of Undergraduate Mathematics Students
o Preliminary Questions:
▪ Asking for: $100.60
▪ Date Request Submitted: 9/23/22
▪ Date of Event: Wednesday, October 26th, 2022 at 7pm
▪ Number of Active Members: 73
▪ Number expected to come: 40
▪ Fundraised: $0
o Opening Statement:
▪ Organization aims to create a better sense of community amongst
mathematics students at FSU. They want to fund food for their
meeting/movie night in order to promote the club. They have only had one
meeting so far this year, so they are trying to create a community amongst
like-minded individuals. They want to fund cookies and apple juice. They
will also use funds for pizza or subs. They are just starting again after
Covid, so having a successful next meeting is crucial for their growth.
Beside creating a sense of community, the club holds events with faculty,
holds competitions, and further educates its members.

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
o General Questioning:
▪ Chair Wyatt asked if the event was open to all students, not just club
members. The movie night is open to everyone.
▪ Chair Wyatt asked if PAC could only fund for snacks instead of the pizza
and if they would still hold the event. The event would still be held but
more students would be interested in attending if additional food was
funded.
▪ Senator Folwell asked if there would be food items for those with dietary
restrictions available. The representative said he will look into these
options when purchasing the items.
▪ Chair Rider asked about fundraising that the RSO has done. The rep
explained that since the organization is still trying to start up again, they
do not want to charge dues. They were not able to fundraise or collect any
dues in the previous year. They are looking into fundraising for the future.
▪ Senator Folwell moved to call the question on the line item. Seconded by
Chair Rider.
o Senator Folwell and Chair Rider expressed support of funding the organization
fully.
o Senator Folwell moved to fully fund the organization for $101. Seconded by
Chair Rider. No objections.
o Vote:
▪ YAY: Chair Rider, Senator Folwell, Katie Feldkirchner, Mausam Jariwala
▪ NAY: NA
● Classical Guitar Society at Florida State University – Florida Guitar Festival
o Preliminary Questions:
▪ Asking for: $1,500??
▪ Date Request Submitted: 9/22/22
▪ Date of Event: 10/21/22 at 1:30pm
▪ Number of Active Members: 12
▪ Number expected to come: 200
▪ Fundraised: $0
o Opening Statement:
▪ Seaks to host events that will further the knowledge, understand, and
appreciation of guitars
▪ They hope to provide FSU and the greater community to opportunity to
experience one of the greatest classical guitar artists at The Florida Guitar
Festival. It is a festival/competition where artists can host masterclasses,
performances, and compete in order to win a cash prize.
▪ Alec Holcomb is a former FSU student who the Classical Guitar Society at
FSU wants to hire for $1,500. The organization wants to bring in Alec
because their professor is celebrating his 50th year teaching at Florida
State and they want to celebrate him by bringing in some past students.
o General Questioning:
▪ Chair Wyatt asked if the organization had fundraised. Due to Hurricane
Ian, they had to cancel the fundraising planned for the previous week.

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
▪ Chair Wyatt asked if this was the only organization hosting the event or if
they were partnering with other groups. They are the only organization
hosting the event.
o Chair Rider motioned to call to question the line item. Seconded by Senator
Folwell.
▪ Senator Folwell expressed support for the event. Chair Rider Agreed.
o Vote:
▪ Yay: Chair Rider, Senator Folwell, Katie Feldkirchner, Mausam Jariwala
▪ Nay: NA
▪ Abstain: NA
● FSU South Asian Student Association – Diwali Banquet
o Preliminary Questions:
▪ Asking for: $1,500 for food
▪ Date Request Submitted: 9/23/22
▪ Date of Event: 10/22/22
▪ Number of Active Members: 150
▪ Number expected to come: 175
▪ Fundraised: $211
o Opening Statement:
▪ Requesting funds for the Diwali event, which is the festival of light event
for Hindus. The Diwali event represents the triumph of light over evil.
▪ The FSU South Asian Student Association wants to provide students a
home during the celebration by hosting the banquet at Miller’s Hall from
6:30-9:30pm.
▪ Yielded with 4 minutes and 8 seconds
o General Questioning
▪ Chair Rider asked for the line items and amounts to be restated. The
representative shared with us their expense statement. They are funding
traditional decorations, tealights and centerpieces, as well utensils and
plating items. Finally, they will be catering from Indian Kitchen America
for a multitude of food items. They will be buying water bottles to hand
out. In total, it will be $1915.25. They also shared with us their
promotional advertisement that they have already shared on their social
media accounts.
▪ Chair Folwell asked if there will be food items available for those with
dietary restrictions. The rep explained that food items adhere to cultural
practices.
▪ Chair Folwell explained that SGA is not allowed to fund plastic water
bottles due to environmental and sustainability concerns. Chair Folwell
explained that they can purchase these water bottles themselves, but they
cannot be funded with SGA money.
o Chair Rider motioned to Call the Question on the Line Item. Seconded by
Senator Folwell
▪ Excluding the water bottles, the total amount is $1,763

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
o Closing Statement:
▪ The reps thanked us for our support. They expressed how important the
event is for the campus and South Asian students.
o Vote:
▪ Yay: Chair Rider, Senator Folwell, Katie Feldkirchner, Mausam Jariwala
▪ Nay: NA
▪ Abstain: NA
● Turkish Student Association at Florida State University – Caput Bağlama (Wish
Tree) Afternoon with TSA
o Preliminary Questions:
▪ Asking for: $885.95 for expenses and clothing
▪ Date Request Submitted: 9/26/22
▪ Date of Event: TBD
▪ Number of Active Members: 50
▪ Number expected to come: 50
▪ Fundraised: $0
o Opening Statement:
▪ The Turkish Student Association is submitting a PAC request for their
Wishing Tree Event. TSA develops projects and activities to create
awareness of Turkish cultures, arts, and history. They also promote social
relations and cooperation among the members of the Turkish community
in Tallahassee. Finally, they help new students arriving from Turkey to
better incorporate in the system of FSU.
▪ The Association has not had the opportunity to fundraise in the past.
▪ The Wishing Tree Afternoon with TSA event will be from 5-9pm in The
Globe. They will be funding 144 t-shirts (with the SGA logo). This is the
minimum amount that the shirt company will make. TSA also expects a
lot of growth through the next few semesters.
▪ No time yield for closing.
o General Questioning
▪ Chair Wyatt asked if TSA will be following the recommended shirt sizes
provided in the financial manual. The rep said that they are complying.
▪ Katie asked if the rep could go over the other three items being requested.
The rep explained that they are asking for funds for cloth so they can do
the Wishing Tree event in traditional Turkish ways. They will also be
asking for markets to write the wishes and quotes on the cloth. Finally,
they will be funding a banner to advertise this event and all future TSA
events.
▪ Senator Folwell moved to call the question on the line item for $886.
Seconded by Mausam Jariwala.
o Vote:
▪ Yay: Chair Rider, Senator Folwell, Katie Feldkirchner, Mausam Jariwala
▪ Nay: NA
▪ Abstain: NA

o Preliminary Questions:
▪ Asking for: $1,200 for clothing
▪ Date Request Submitted: 9/18/22
▪ Date of Event: 10/13/22
▪ Number of Active Members: 150
▪ Number expected to come: 60
▪ Fundraised: $630.55
o Opening Statement:
▪ PRSA’s mission is to represent cultural, social, and informative events
about Puerto Rico and advocate on behalf of Puerto Rico. They hold social
events for not only Puerto Ricans but anyone interested in learning more
about their culture.
▪ The shirt they are designing resembles the jersey of the Puerto Rican
National Baseball Team because it is a major sport on the island. In the
spring, The World Baseball Classic is being held. It is a time where Puerto
Ricans unite and celebrate. PRSA wants to give their members a shirt to
show their pride and community. They have 01 as the number on their
jersey to recognize the year they were established as an RSO at Florida
State.
▪ They want to buy 150 shirts for $8 a shirt for a total of $1,200 from Full
Press.
▪ Yielded with 27 seconds for closing.
o General Questions:
▪ Chair Wyatt was concerned by the size of the “Paid for by SGA” wording
on the side of the sleeve. One of the reps explained that they could get it
changed to be bigger.
▪ Katie asked about the quantity of shirts bought. One rep said that along
with being distributed at general body meetings, they will be handed out at
Market Wednesday.
▪ Chair Wyatt asked about fundraising. They explained that they have
fundraised but PAC funds are necessary for t-shirts because they money
goes towards other events and programs.
o Closing Statement:
▪ They explained that they want to give back to the community, especially
during Hispanic Heritage Month.
▪ Motion to fully fund the line of $1,200 items by Folwell. Seconded by
Chair Rider. No objections.

74th Student Senate
Programming Allocation Committee
September 15, 2022
Call to Order: 6:05
Members Present: NA
Members Tardy: NA
