Amendment #6: Updating the Constitutional Amending Process.
Statement of Intent: The amendment would raise the threshold for the Senate to propose
constitutional amendments to a 3/4 vote. This would not impact the number of signatures needed
for students to propose an amendment or the threshold for ratification at an election. The
amendment also clarifies the process for processing a proposed amendment and ensures that
amendments related to the Congress of Graduate Students receive the support of graduate
students prior to ratification.
Article VI, Sections 1 and 5, of the Student Body Constitution shall be amended to read:
Section 1 CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS
1. Amendments to this Constitution may be proposed by two-thirds (2/3) three-fourths
(3/4) vote of the Student Senate, by petition of 1,500 members of the Student Body,
or by recommendation from the Constitutional Review Commission, and shall become
part of this Constitution upon ratification by two-thirds (2/3) of the votes cast in an
election of the Student Body, provided that the proposed amendments have been
published in a campus newspaper at least one week prior to the vote of the Student
Body.
1. Statutes shall adopt procedures by which notice is given when a constitutional
amendment is introduced in the Senate for consideration and at least one week
prior to the election where the amendment is to be voted on.
2. Each amendment shall be accompanied by a Statement of Intent, as shall be
further defined by statute, that explains the text of the amendment.
3. If an amendment is proposed by the Senate or Constitutional Review Commission,
the Senate President shall deliver the amendment unto the Supervisor of Elections
within forty-eight (48) hours of the Senate or Commission proposing the
amendment, who shall then place the amendment on the ballot and ensure the
amendment’s compliance with the requirements of this article. Failure of either
officer to carry out such duties constitutes nonfeasance and, additionally, the
Supreme Court may compel the officer(s) to carry out such duties by writ of
mandamus.
4. The Senate may, by statute, provide the form for petitions to amend this
Constitution.
5. Procedures for timely review of proposed constitutional amendments by the
Student Supreme Court may be made by statute, provided that such review may
not invalidate a proposed amendment unless there is a finding that the proposed
amendment violates state or federal law.
6. Except as provided for in this Article, no further requirements may be placed on
the amending process by statute.

Amendment #7: Referendum and Opinion Questions Reform
Statement of Intent: The amendment removes obsolete language pertaining to the SGA Budget
and streamlines the referendum process. Additionally, the amendment consolidates the work of
setting opinion questions for the ballot into a commission, which shall be created by statute, and
provides a method by which the Student Body can place opinion questions in front of the
commission for potential inclusion on the SGA Ballot.
Article VI, Sections 2, 3, and 4, shall be amended to read:
Section 2 REFERENDUM
The Student Body may demand a referendum election upon the properly signed petition
of at least five hundred (500) students. The Student Body President can also demand a
referendum election with a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate. The result of the election
shall serve as a mandate for the Student Body Government provided that ten percent
(10%) of the Student Body shall have participated in the election. At no time shall a
referendum election demand any result that would violate the provisions of the Student
Body Constitution or any result contrary to federal, state, local or university law.
Article VI Section 3
In cases where Senate votes on a budget that would result in an A&S Fee increase greater
than five percent (5%) over that of the previous year (subject to later approval by the
Activity and Service Fee Committee) it shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote to pass such a
budget. This must be done by a roll call vote, and is a special type of referendum election
that is uniquely carried out by the Senate.
Section 4 3 OPINION QUESTIONS
1. It shall be possible to place questions on the ballot to determine student opinion on issues.
2. Such questions shall be placed on the ballot in the same manner as referenda, although
they shall only require a properly signed petition of at least two hundred (200) students,
or a majority vote of the Senate at the request of the Student Body President. However,
they may only be used to access student opinion on issues and shall not be binding on
Student Government, nor subject to Court Review before being placed on the ballot.
1. There shall be a commission that shall have the authority to place opinion questions
regarding issues of the university on the SGA ballot. The composition and procedures of
this commission shall be further defined by statute.
2. Students may petition the commission to consider adding a question to the ballot after
receiving the signature of two hundred (200) students on a petition. The Senate may
prescribe the form of the petition by statute.
3. The Senate may place opinion questions on the ballot by majority vote.
4. Opinion questions shall not be binding on the Student Government.

Amendment #8: CRC Amendment
Statement of Intent: The amendment clarifies the timeline for Constitutional Review
Commission meetings and ensures that student voices are sought out as part of the
Commission’s work by requiring that the Commission adopt procedures for seeking public

Article VI, Section 6, of the Constitution shall be amended to read:
Section 6 5 CONSTITUTIONAL REVIEW COMMISSION
1. There shall be a Constitutional Review Commission to review the Student Body
Constitution and present amendments for ratification by the Student Body.
2. The Commission shall have the authority to directly propose amendments to the
Student Body Constitution for ratification at the next general election.
3. The Commission shall meet every three years, starting in the fall semester of 2021,
and submit all proposed amendments before the following Spring Election.
4. The Commission shall consist of the following 10 members:
a. The Student Body President shall appoint 3 members.
b. The Student Senate President shall appoint 3 members from the Student Senate
and shall serve as a member.
c. The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court shall appoint 3 members.
d. All members of the commission must be enrolled students at Florida State
University.
5. The Commission shall be organized as follows:
a. The Senate President shall serve as the Commission's chair, and shall be a non-
voting member except in the event of a tie.
b. The Commission shall elect a Vice Chair by majority vote.
c. Any proposals to be forwarded for ratification by the Student Body must pass the
commission by majority vote.
d. The Commission shall adopt a rules of procedure at its first convening by majority
vote. The rules of procedure shall include the process by which the Commission
collects and seeks out public feedback on its work from university entities and the
student body, at large.

sections.text:
Amendment #9: Recall Amendment
Statement of Intent: The amendment will bring FSU SGA in compliance with Florida Statutes
§ 1004.26(4)(b) by allowing appointed officials in SGA to be recalled by petition of 2% or 800
members of the Student Body, whichever is greater.
Article VII, Sections 1 and 2 of the Student Body Constitution shall be amended to read:
Section 1 METHOD OF RECALL
Every elected and appointed official of the Florida State University Student Body is subject,
as herein provided, to recall by the legal voters of the Florida State University Student
Body. The person or persons demanding recall shall set forth in a petition the reasons for
the demand of recall. If the elected official in question offers their resignation it shall be
accepted and take effect on the day it is offered, and the vacancy shall be filled as provided
by law. If they do not resign within thirty days an election will be held to determine whether
the people will recall the officer. On the sample ballot at the election shall be printed in not
more than two hundred (200) words the reasons for demanding recall and in not more
than two hundred (200) words the officers justification of their course in office. They shall
continue to perform the duties of their office until the results of their official election shall
be officially declared. The recall petition shall be filed with the officer with whom the petition
for nomination to such office should be filed, and the same officer shall order the special
election when it is required. No such petition shall be circulated against any officer until
they have actually held office for three months. After one such petition and special election,
no further recall shall be filed against the same officer during the term for which they were
elected.
Section 2 NUMBER OF SIGNATURES REQUIRED FOR A PETITION OF RECALL
1. Pertaining to the recall of campus-wide elected officers (Student Body President,
Student Body Vice President, Student Body Treasurer, Campus Recreation Board
Members, Elected Agency, Bureau, and Affiliated Project personnel, and Union Board
Members, or any other campus-wide elected officer as dictated by statute) five percent
(5%) of all students or 1,500 signatures, whichever is greater.
2. Pertaining to the recall of Senators, COGS Representatives and Senior Class Council
officers: ten percent (10%) of those enrolled in the division in which the seat in question
is located or fifty (50) signatures from that division, whichever is greater. In the event
that a particular division has less than fifty (50) students enrolled, then the number of
signatures required shall be two-thirds (2/3) of all the students in that division.
3. Pertaining to the recall of appointed officers: two percent (2%) of all students or 800
signatures, whichever is greater.

ARTICLE VI AMENDMENT PROCESS AND REFERENDUM ELECTIONS
Section 1 CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS
Amendments to this Constitution may be proposed by two-thirds (2/3) vote of the
Student Senate, or by petition of 1,500 members of the Student Body, or by
recommendation from the Constitutional Review Commission, and shall become
part of this Constitution upon ratification by two-thirds (2/3) of the votes cast in an
election of the Student Body, provided that the proposed amendments have been
published in a campus newspaper at least one week prior to the vote of the
Student Body.
Section 2 REFERENDUM
History: Revised by Constitutional Amendment 10, 56th Senate.
The Student Body may demand a referendum election upon the properly signed
petition of at least five hundred (500) students. The Student Body President can
also demand a referendum election with a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate. The
result of the election shall serve as a mandate for the Student Body Government
provided that ten percent (10%) of the Student Body shall have participated in the
election. At no time shall a referendum election demand any result that would
violate the provisions of the Student Body Constitution or any result contrary to
federal, state, local or university law.
Section 3 In cases where Senate votes on a budget that would result in an A&S Fee
increase greater than five percent (5%) over that of the previous year (subject to
later approval by the Activity and Service Fee Committee) it shall require a two-
thirds (2/3) vote to pass such a budget. This must be done by a roll call vote and
is a special type of referendum election that is uniquely carried out by the Senate.
Section 4 A. It shall be possible to place questions on the ballot to determine student
opinion on issues.
B. Such questions shall be placed on the ballot in the same manner as
referenda, although they shall only require a properly signed petition of at
least two hundred (200) students, or a majority vote of the Senate at the
request of the Student Body President. However, they may only be used to
access student opinion on issues and shall not be binding on Student
Government, nor subject to Court Review before being placed on the
ballot.
Section 5 Constitutional Review Commission
A. There shall be a Constitutional Review Commission to review the Student
Body Constitution and present amendments for ratification by the Student
Body.

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
B. The Commission shall have the authority to propose amendments to the
Student Body Constitution.
C. The Commission shall meet every three two years and submit all proposed
amendments before the following Spring Election.
D. The Commission shall consist of the following 10 members:
1. The Student Body President shall appoint 3 members.
2. The Student Senate President shall appoint 3 members from the
Student Senate and shall serve as a member.
3. The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court shall appoint 3 members.
4. All members of the commission must be enrolled students at Florida
State University.
E. The Commission shall be organized as follows:
1. The Senate President shall serve as the Commission's chair, and
shall be a non-voting member except in the event of a tie.
2. The Commission shall elect a Vice Chair by majority vote.
3. Any proposals to be forwarded for ratification by the Student Body
must pass the commission by majority vote.
4. The Commission shall adopt a rules of procedure at their first
convening by majority vote.

Florida State University Student Supreme Court
Fall 2006
ORIGINAL
Wherefore, the Florida State University Student Supreme Court has received and
reviewed a request from Senator Keith Halpern to issue an advisory opinion based on
Amendment #2 to Article IX of the Florida State University Student Constitution,
And, in reviewing this document the Florida State University Supreme Court
weighed its design, intent and purpose against all applicable laws, including the Florida
Statutes, Florida Administrative Code, and the United States Constitution,
Therefore, the Florida State University Supreme Court finds that Amendment #2
does not appear to facially violate any applicable laws, including the Florida Statutes,
Florida Administrative Code, and the United States Constitution.
Done and Ordered this 2nd day of October, 2006.
/Signed Electronically/
Brett Renton, Acting Chief Justice
Melanie Shoemaker, Associate Justice
Eric Gardner, Associate Justice
* This Opinion is merely advisory only and does not carry any indication or presumption
of acceptance should the Amendment be challenged. Additionally the Court does not
endorse or support anything it is asked to review, merely this opinion is an indication that
the amendment does not facially violate any known applicable law.

73RD STUDENT SENATE
Constitutional Amendment #: 10
Primary Sponsor(s): Linsky & Randall
BE IT ENACTED BY THE SEVENTY THIRD STUDENT SENATE:
A Constitutional Amendment to increase the Congress of Graduate Students’ ability to allocate Activities
and Services Fees on behalf of graduate students at Florida State University.
Article IX, Section 2
Resolved by the Student Senate at Florida State University (with two-thirds concurring
therein), that the following article is proposed as an amendment to the Constitution of the
Student Body, which shall be valid to all intents and purposes as part of the Constitution
when ratified by two-thirds vote of the Student Body electorate, and
Further resolved, that the following article be placed on the Ballot of the Election in the Fall
Academic term of the year 2021.
This amendment corrects the registration classifications to be in accordance with current policy and
increased the allocation of graduate student Activities and Services fees to fifty percent of their annual
yield.
Read 1st Time: July 21st, 2021
Referred to Committee: Budget / Judiciary
Committee Report: Passed Budget 9/8; Passed Judiciary 9/8
Read 2nd Time: 9/8/2021
Senate Vote: 44-0-0
PASSED: September 8th 2021

ARTICLE IX CONGRESS OF GRADUATE STUDENTS
Section 2 Graduate students shall receive fifty percent (50%) of Activities and
Services (A&S) Fees paid by students classified by the Registrar as Master’s,
Specialist, Doctoral, Juris Doctor, Doctor of Medicine, or otherwise notated as post-
baccalaureate and/or graduate students. These fees shall be allocated to COGS by
SGA at the start of the annual budget process and shall be administered by the
elected representatives in the Congress of Graduate Students. COGS financial
administration shall be consistent with and subject to the Student Body Constitution,
and Statutes.

76th STUDENT SENATE
Senate Resolution
Resolution #: 45
Primary Sponsor(s): Cofer, Gorelick
Co-Sponsor(s): Khosh
Date: March 26, 2024
Whereas: The Executive Branch’s Cabinet “Policies” shall be adopted as follows:
“SECTION ONE – Authority and Purpose
1.1. In accordance with the Student Body Constitution, there shall be a cabinet in
the Executive Branch to assist the constitutional officers in the execution of their
duties. The Constitution delegates the authority to define the positions and their
duties to Statutes.
1.2. Pursuant to 301.2 of Student Body Statutes, this policy shall outline the
cabinet of the Student Body President, including the processes and procedures
thereof.
SECTION TWO – Revision Procedure
2.1. Revisions to this document may be initiated by the Student Body President or
their designee, and shall be written in the form of a consent resolution sent to
Senate to be placed on their consent calendar. Senate shall then have the
authority to approve, deny, or amend any changes rendered, if the revision is
objected to on the floor. Revisions shall be enacted immediately upon approval by
the Senate.
2.2. Any revisions made shall be sent to the Webmaster within one business day,
who shall then post these revisions on the website. This document must be kept
up-to-date at all times.
SECTION THREE – Executive Office of the President
3.1. The Executive Office of the President shall be defined as the vehicle through
which the Student Body President and Vice President execute their constitutional
powers and carry out their administration's programs, projects, and agenda.
3.2. The Executive Office derives its authority from the Student Body President
and has no authorization, power, or authority to act unless specifically granted byDocuSign Envelope ID: 545645AA-68C5-4F35-A62A-24780F1102DC

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
the Student Body President or Vice President. It shall not have the authority to
pass resolutions or acts.
3.3. The Executive Office of the President shall have the following duties:
A. Assist the Student Body President and Vice President in the execution of the
plan for the Executive Branch.
B. Represent segments of student body quality of life in accordance with the
structure issued by the Student Body President.
C. Fulfill the obligations of the job descriptions for each office.
D. Work for the improved quality of life of the student body.
E. The Executive Office of the President shall meet on a regular basis no less
than once every two weeks during the fall, spring, and summer semesters. Minutes
of these meetings will be recorded and kept on record.
3.4. The Student Body President may organize the Executive Office as deemed
necessary and proper within the limits imposed by the Student Body Statutes.
3.5. If a new Executive Office of the President position is created, the Student
Body President must notify, in writing, the Student Senate of its creation.
3.6. Within two (2) weeks of inauguration, the Student Body President, in
consultation with the Student Body Vice President, shall address the Student
Senate and present the plan for the organization of the Executive Office of the
President. Each position, whether created near the inauguration or later in the
term, must have a title and a description not totaling fewer than fifty (50) words
detailing the responsibilities and privileges of the position. Such a plan must be
published on the Student Government Association Website.
3.7. All members of the Executive Office of the President must be confirmed by the
Student Senate as “Cabinet Offices” and major level positions within the Executive
Branch.
3.8. The Chief of Staff who is appointed by the Student Body President and is
subject to Student Senate confirmation, directs the activities of the Executive
Office, and is subject to the will of the Student Body President.
3.9 The Student Body President has sole power of appointment within the Executive
Office and may dismiss any individual serving under them at their discretion.”DocuSign Envelope ID: 545645AA-68C5-4F35-A62A-24780F1102DC

76th STUDENT SENATE
Senate Resolution
Resolution #: 46
Primary Sponsor(s): Cofer, Gorelick
Co-Sponsor(s): Khosh
Date: March 26, 2024
Whereas: The Presidential Appointment “Policies” shall be adopted as follows:
“SECTION ONE – Authority and Purpose
1.1. These rules of procedure shall lay forth the processes and procedures in
which the Student Body President and Executive Branch as empowered through
the President shall exert their constitutionally-granted power of appointment and
dismissal. This document is empowered by the Senate through 304.1 of Student
Body Statutes.
SECTION TWO – Revision Procedure
2.1. Revisions to this document may be initiated by the Student Body President or
their designee, and shall be written in the form of a consent resolution sent to
Senate to be placed on their consent calendar. Senate shall then have the
authority to approve, deny, or amend any changes rendered, if the revision is
objected to on the floor. Revisions shall be enacted immediately upon approval by
the Senate.
2.2. Any revisions made shall be sent to the Webmaster within one business day,
who shall then post these revisions on the website. This document must be kept
up-to-date at all times.
SECTION THREE – Candidate Search
3.1. No position requiring Student Senate confirmation may be filled until the
position has been advertised properly.
3.2. The Chief of Staff, assisted by one designee from the Executive Branch, will
conduct all candidate searches.
a. This designee from the Executive Branch shall be chosen by the Chief of
Staff.DocuSign Envelope ID: FAD6F5CC-D094-42FB-8FA7-2E6E4D92806C

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
b. In the absence of a designee, the Chief of Staff retains all responsibility for
conducting the work of the Candidate Search Process.
3.3. All positions shall be advertised for at least one week on the SGA Website.
SECTION FOUR – Candidate Screening Process
4.1. Upon the receipt of applications for a vacant position in Student Government
Association, a screening process shall be overseen by the Student Body President
to determine the most qualified candidate.
4.2. The Candidate Screening Process shall take no longer than ten (10) school
days from the end of the candidate search period.
4.3. The Candidate Screening Process, conducted by the Chief of Staff, or
designee as stipulated in Section Three of this document, shall include the
following:
a. The Chief of Staff, or designee as stipulated in Chapter 304.2 shall interview
all candidates.
b. All candidates shall provide the appropriate application as defined in Chapter
307.3, in completed format, demonstrating their qualifications for the position.
c. The interview shall be conducted in a standardized and professional form for
all candidates, and shall draw at least five interview questions from the forwarding
interview questions published on the SGA Website.
d. The interview shall consist of a basic questionnaire outlining the candidate’s
experience, qualifications, and goals for the respective position.
e. After all candidates have been interviewed, the Student Body President shall
forward the candidate deemed most qualified to the Student Senate for
confirmation.
4.4. The Student Body President may forego the candidate screening process with
the exception of subsection 4.3, subsection c, in cases where the candidate is
forwarded to the Student Body President, with a written notice of a proper interview
being conducted, by the Student Government Entity to which the candidate is
applying for a position.
4.5. It is the responsibility of the Student Body President, the Chief of Staff, or
designee to ensure that this process is carried out in a fair and constitutional
manner. To that end, any person(s) conducting the interviews shall recuse
themselves from the Candidate Screening Process and the processes ofDocuSign Envelope ID: FAD6F5CC-D094-42FB-8FA7-2E6E4D92806C

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
determining the most qualified candidate in situations where a candidate for any
position has a conflict of interest with the President, Chief of Staff, or designee.
They shall select, for that particular set of candidates, a non-biased actor or actors
to interview candidates for said office and deem the most qualified of those
candidates to then be forwarded by the President.
a. The forwarding letter sent to the Senate must include a notice when any
recusal occurs for any selection of Officers, stating that there was a recusal and a
signed statement from the non-biased actor(s) of their lack of conflict of interest.
4.6. If during the candidate screening process, the Student Body President finds
that a candidate is better suited for another position within the same Student
Government entity to which the candidate applied, the Student Body President may
reserve the right to forward the candidate, with their consent, for another position
for which they meet all Constitutional and statutory requirements.
a. If a candidate is forwarded to the Student Body President by an agency,
bureau, or other SGA entity for confirmation pursuant to Section 4.4, any changes
to the position for which a candidate is being forwarded to Senate shall also require
the consent of the head of the respective SGA entity.
b. Agency, Bureau, and SGA entity heads may also reserve the right to change
the position that a candidate is being forwarded for with the consent of the
applicant before forwarding the candidate to the Student Body President pursuant
to Section 4.4.
c. The forwarding letter sent to the Senate must include a notice in all cases
when candidates are forwarded to the Senate for positions that are different from
those which they applied for.
SECTION FIVE – Executive Office Positions
5.1. The Student Body President shall appoint all Executive Cabinet Officers as
defined in Section 4.1.
5.2. The Chief of Staff shall, upon recommendation by the appropriate Executive
Cabinet Director, appoint all Deputy Directors and administrative support office
staff.
5.3. The Student Body President may create any office or position deemed
necessary and proper provided that the Student Senate is notified of the action in
writing.
5.4. Any individual appointed to a Cabinet position as indicated in the Student
Body Statutes shall require confirmation by the Student Senate.DocuSign Envelope ID: FAD6F5CC-D094-42FB-8FA7-2E6E4D92806C

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
5.5. The Student Body President may appoint an Acting Executive Cabinet Officer
who shall serve in the role, but shall not receive compensation, until a nominee can
be forwarded to the Student Senate.
5.6. No individual may serve as an Acting Executive Cabinet Director for longer
than six (6) weeks.
5.7. The Student Body President-elect, as defined in Chapter 704, shall have the
power to designate and forward to the Student Senate for confirmation, the Cabinet
nominees for their administration after all appeals and violations have been
exhausted or ruled on.
a. The nominees must be confirmed by a majority vote of the Student Senate
b. The confirmed nominee shall be referred to as the "designee" (i.e. Chief of
Staff designee).
c. Upon installation of the Student Body President-elect, all Cabinet Officer
designees shall assume the positions for which they were confirmed and all duties,
responsibilities, rights, and compensation vested with their position.
5.8. The terms of all Executive Office appointees shall end when they are
dismissed, impeached, or upon installation of their successors.
5.9. The Student Body President may dismiss any appointee to the Executive
Office at their discretion.
SECTION SIX – Executive Bureau & Agency Positions
6.1. The selection process for Executive Bureau Directors shall occur as follows:
a. The Student Body President shall conduct a candidate search as outlined in
Section Four beginning the first week of the new administration.
b. The Chief of Staff shall conduct a screening process as defined in Section 4.
c. The outgoing Director shall submit a written recommendation to the Student
Body President on the replacement Director.
d. The Student Body President shall choose a Director and submit the name to
the Student Senate for confirmation.
e. A majority vote of the Student Senate, with a quorum being present, isDocuSign Envelope ID: FAD6F5CC-D094-42FB-8FA7-2E6E4D92806C

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
necessary for confirmation.
f. The terms of all Executive Bureau Directors shall end when they are
dismissed, impeached, or upon installation of their successor.
g. Should a directorship become vacant, the Student Body President may
appoint an Acting Director, who shall not receive compensation, to serve in the
position until a nominee can be forwarded to the Senate.
h. No individual may serve as Acting Director for longer than six (6) weeks.
i. If the Student Body President wishes the existing Director to remain in office,
the individual must be forwarded to the Student Senate for reconfirmation.
j. In accordance with the Article III, Section 3 (H), of the Student Body
Constitution, the Student Body President may remove the Director at President’s
discretion.
6.2. The selection process for Executive Bureau Assistant Directors shall occur as
follows:
a. The Director shall conduct a candidate search.
b. The Director shall interview the applicants and make a recommendation to the
Student Body President.
c. The Student Body President may choose to either reject the nominee or
forward the name to the Student Senate for confirmation.
d. Student Senate confirmation requires a majority vote of the Student Senate
with a quorum being present.
e. If the Student Body President rejects the nominee, then the Director must
submit another name.
f. The term of the Assistant Director shall be the same as the Director of that
Bureau. This term length shall not be affected by the early dismissal, resignation,
or impeachment of said Director.
g. In accordance with Article III, Section 3 (I) of the Student Body Constitution,
the Student Body President may remove the Assistant Director from office at
President’s discretion.
6.3. The selection process for other Executive Bureau personnel shall occur as
follows:DocuSign Envelope ID: FAD6F5CC-D094-42FB-8FA7-2E6E4D92806C

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
a. The selection process and appointment of all Bureau personnel below the
Assistant Director shall be delineated by their individual Chapters in Title XI of
Student Body Statutes.
6.4. The selection process for Executive Agency Directors shall occur in
accordance with Section Four unless otherwise stipulated in their individual rules of
procedure, as outlined in Title X of Student Body Statutes.
6.5. For all non-elected Agency Director positions, the outgoing Executive Board of
Directors of each respective agency may shall choose one (1) nomination by a
majority vote for Agency Director and forward said applicant to the Student Body
President. The Student Body President will then choose a candidate from the
applications forwarded from the Agency Executive Board of Directors and forward
said candidate to the Student Senate within ten (10) school days for confirmation.
6.6. In the event that the Student Body President feels that any of the candidates
are unqualified, an additional candidate search period may be conducted.
6.7. Within two (2) weeks of the Director's confirmation, that Director will appoint
any non-elected Assistant Director. This appointment shall be ratified by majority
vote of the Board and then forwarded to the Student Senate.
a. In the event that the Agency Directorship is vacated, the Assistant Director
shall assume the Directorship and proceed with filling the Assistant Directorship as
outlined in Chapter 304.6.
b. Agency Directors and Assistant Directors who are appointed shall remain in
office until they are dismissed, impeached, or upon the installation of their
successors.
6.8. The selection process for Executive Agency Assistant Directors shall occur as
follows:
a. The Assistant Directors shall be chosen in the same manner as Executive
Agency Directors.
b. The Student Body President may dismiss the Assistant Director. The
dismissal may be appealed through the same process as the agency director's
termination.
6.9. The selection process for Executive Agency personnel shall occur as follows:
a. Staff appointments shall be made in the manner mandated by the agency's
individual Rules of Procedure statute.DocuSign Envelope ID: FAD6F5CC-D094-42FB-8FA7-2E6E4D92806C

sections.heading: Page 7
sections.text:
b. The Student Body President may not dismiss any agency staff person below
the Assistant Directors that the President have not directly appointed.
6.10. The selection process for all other Executive Agency’s Board of
Directors shall occur as follows:
a. Members of the Executive Board of Directors, not including the treasurer and
secretary, shall be appointed following the process outlined in each agency’s
respective Rules of Procedure statutes.
b. The terms of all Executive Board members shall last one (1) year.
c. In accordance with Article III, Section 3 (H) of the Student Body Constitution,
the Student Body President may dismiss any Agency Executive Board member, at
the President’s discretion, that the President directly appointed.
SECTION SEVEN – Vacancies in Elected Positions
Vacancies in Elected Positions shall be filled as other positions are, but shall require
2/3 of a Senate quorum for confirmation.”

Article III -

Executive Order #7806 of 7/21/2023
Student Accessibility Commission
By the authority vested in me as President by the Student
Body Constitution and the Student Body Statutes, it is hereby ordered as
follows:
Section 1: Purpose. The Student Accessibility Commission
(“Commission”) is created to serve as an informal vehicle for growth
and change of the accessibility policies that govern the University.
Section 2: Authority. Title III, Chapter 300, Section 300.3, Subsection C
and D provides:
C. The Executive Branch shall be responsible for the planning and
execution of programs, projects, and services provided to the
students through the Student Government Association.
D. The Executive Branch shall be responsible for researching and
developing programs to enhance the health, education, safety, or
welfare of the Student Body of Florida State University.
Furthermore, the power of entities within the Executive Branch
is derived from the Student Body President's constitutional
investiture of the executive powers.
The above-referenced Commission is established in furtherance of these
statutory allowances.
Section 3: Objectives. The objectives of the Commission will
be to encourage policies facilitating a more inclusive Florida State
University campus which is available and accessible to all people
regardless of disability. The objectives of the commission will include,
but shall not be limited to, the following:

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
1. Encourage University Administration to create and support a
“transition team” within the University to help students with
disabilities prepare for postsecondary education, including
connecting these students with available services on campus.
2. Ensure that all buildings on campus are accessible to all persons.
3. Collaborate with partners throughout the university community to
continually enhance the accessibility of Florida State University
facilities, programs, and initiatives.
Section 4: Membership. The membership of the Commission shall
include, but shall not be limited to, the following officers and
representatives:
Student Body President, or a designee; and
Student Body Vice President, or a designee; and
Two Members of the Union Board; and
Two Members of the Student Senate.
Section 6: Duration. This Executive Order shall be in perpetuity or in
such time that this Executive Order is repealed.
THIS EXECUTIVE ORDER IS DONE AND ORDERED.
______________________________________
Jack Hitchcock
Student Body President

The Seal was designed to include Lady Justice, wearing a blindfold,
carrying a sword and a set of scales. A common symbol on many
courthouses in America. Lady Justice symbolizes “fair and equal
administration of the law, without corruption, favor, greed, or
prejudice”.
"Lady Justice originates from the personification of Justice in
Ancient Roman art known as Iustitia or Justitia after Latin: Iustitia,
who is equivalent to the Greek goddesses Themis and Dike."
“The blindfold represents objectivity and impartiality, that justice
should be meted out without fear or favor, regardless of money,
wealth, or power.”
“She holds scales to represent the weighing of evidence, evidence
must be weighed on its own merit.”
“The sword represents punishment, signifying that justice can be
swift and final. She holds the sword below the scales to show that
evidence weighted on its merit in a court of law come before
punishment.””

MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE FLORIDA STATE
UNIVERSITY STUDENT GOVERNMENT ASSOCIATION AND THE DIVISION OF
STUDENT AFFAIRS FOR THE PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF AN HVAC UNIT
AT THE FSU FLYING HIGH CIRCUS
This Memorandum of Understanding ("MOU") is entered into by and between the Florida
State University Student Government Association ("SGA") and the Florida State University
Division of Student Affairs ("DSA"), acting through the FSU Flying High Circus, for the purpose
of administering funds appropriated by the Student Senate for the purchase and installation of an
HVAC unit serving the FSU Flying High Circus. Pursuant to Senate Resolution No. 78-040, the
Student Senate authorized the use of $70,000 from the Campus Advancement and Development
Fund to support this project.
Section 1: Grant Amount
SGA agrees to provide reimbursement funding to DSA in an amount not to exceed Seventy
Thousand Dollars ($70,000.00) for the purchase and installation of one HVAC unit for the FSU
Flying High Circus.
Section 2: Eligible Expenses
Grant funds may be used solely for expenses directly related to:
1. Purchase of the HVAC unit;
2. Installation of the HVAC unit;
3. Associated project costs.
Section 3: Reimbursement Procedure
a. DSA shall initially incur the project expenses and submit documentation of completed
expenditures to SGA.
b. Documentation shall include invoices, receipts, proof of payment, and any other records
reasonably requested by SGA.
c. Upon verification of eligible expenses, SGA shall reimburse DSA for approved costs up to
the maximum grant amount of $70,000.
d. Reimbursement shall not exceed actual expenditures incurred for the project.
Section 4: Project Completion
a. DSA agrees to make reasonable efforts to complete the purchase and installation of the
HVAC unit in accordance with applicable University procurement, facilities, and fiscal
requirements.
b. The HVAC unit shall be purchased, installed, and placed into operational service no later
than June 30, 2027.
c. Upon competition of the project, any subsequent maintenance, replacement, or other costs
associated will be the responsibility of DSA.Docusign Envelope ID: 1086496A-0012-8F8E-82C1-5FF837232396

sections.heading: Page 2

d. If circumstances beyond the reasonable control of DSA delay completion beyond June 30,
2027, DSA may request a written extension from SGA. Any request for extension must be
submitted at least thirty (30) days prior to June 30, 2027. Any extension must be approved
in writing by the Student Body President or designee.
e. Any portion of the grant not reimbursed by June 30, 2027, or by an approved extension
date, shall remain in or revert to the appropriate SGA account unless otherwise authorized
by Student Senate action.
Section 5: Recognition of Student Government Funding
As a condition of this grant, DSA shall provide a permanent and conspicuous acknowledgment of
SGA's contribution. Such acknowledgment shall consist of signage, a commemorative plaque, or
another prominently displayed recognition located at or near the Flying High Circus facility. The
acknowledgment shall include substantially the following language:
"This HVAC improvement was funded through a $70,000 allocation from the
Florida State University Student Government Association Campus
Advancement and Development Fund."
Section 6: Reporting
Within a reasonable period following project completion, DSA shall provide SGA:
1. Confirmation that the HVAC unit has been installed and is operational;
2. A summary of project expenditures; and
3. Documentation demonstrating compliance with the acknowledgment requirement.
Section 7: Return of Unused Funds
Any funds approved but not reimbursed under this MOU shall remain in or revert to the appropriate
SGA account and shall not be available for any purpose other than as authorized by Student Senate
action.
Section 8: Term
This MOU shall become effective upon execution by both parties and shall remain in effect until
June 30, 2027, or until all reimbursement, reporting, and closeout obligations have been satisfied,
whichever occurs later. In the event an extension is approved pursuant to Section 4, this MOU
shall remain in effect through the approved extension period.
Executed in good faith, this MOU reflects the mutual understanding of the Parties and supersedes
all prior agreements in these matters.

This Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) is entered into by and among the Florida
State University Student Government Association (SGA), the Department of Student Engagement,
and the Florida State University Center for Undergraduate Research and Academic Engagement
(CRE), herein referred to collectively as “the Parties.”
WHEREAS, the Student Government Association created the Undergraduate Research
Travel Grant (“the Grant”) as a student-led initiative to provide financial support to undergraduate
students attending or presenting at academic conferences; and
WHEREAS, the Student Government Association has increased funding for this initiative
to $16,000 annually to expand student access and impact; and
WHEREAS, in order to better streamline the processing of reimbursements and fund
disbursements, the administration of these funds will be transferred to the CRE, subject to the
availability of funds in the annual SGA budget; and
WHEREAS, the SGA intends to preserve the student origin, oversight, and branding of the
program while CRE provides administrative support.
NOW, THEREFORE, the Parties agree as follows:
Section 1: Purpose of the Grant Program
a. The Grant program shall be titled and advertised exclusively as the “Student Government
Association Undergraduate Research Travel Grant.”
b. Grant program funds shall remain open and accessible to all Florida State University
undergraduate students, not limited to students traditionally served by CRE.
Section 2: Oversight and Authority
a. The SGA Department of Academic Affairs and its SGA-designated student leadership shall
retain primary authority over administration, selection, and oversight of awards.
b. The SGA Department of Academic Affairs shall meet with CRE staff at a minimum of
every other week to ensure the timely approval and facilitation of the Grant program.
c. CRE may override student decisions in emergency or compliance situations (e.g., financial
irregularities, violation of University policy). If CRE overrides student decisions, it shallDocusign Envelope ID: 681E6F86-BBDF-4960-83BB-20035060C80F

four (24) hours.
d. CRE shall not alter decisions or redirect funds with the intent of complementing or
duplicating other CRE-managed initiatives.
Section 3: Branding and Attribution
a. The Grant program shall not be misrepresented in institutional reports, metrics, or
publications as a solely CRE initiative.
b. All advertisements, promotional materials, and communications shall clearly identify the
Grant program as an SGA-funded initiative and must include the official SGA logo or seal
along with the exact verbiage: “Established and Paid for by the Student Government
Association.”
Section 4: Financial Administration
a. SGA shall transfer funds annually to CRE for the sole purpose of administering the Grant
program, subject to availability of funds in the SGA budget.
b. Any program funds remaining at the end of each fiscal year shall be transferred back to
SGA to be reallocated during SGA’s following budget cycle.
c. Reports of applications, awards, and expenditures shall be provided to SGA upon request.
Section 5: Term and Termination
a. This MOU shall become effective upon the signature of all parties hereto and shall coincide
with the University’s fiscal year. Any renewals of this MOU shall be limited to a one-year
period and each renewal shall require the written consent of all parties hereto.

in writing within thirty (30) days.

final appeal shall be to a three-person panel consisting of one student appointed by theDocusign Envelope ID: 681E6F86-BBDF-4960-83BB-20035060C80F

The Pittman Law Group boasts a team of skillful legal minds that provide effective counsel to a
diverse client list. Senior Attorney and Managing Partner Sean Pittman will serve as primary

ATTORNEY SEAN PITTMAN is the Senior Attorney and Managing Partner of Pittman Law Group,
P.L., which specializes in the areas of government, administrative, education, and corporate law.
Sean represents a diverse client list of private citizens, local governments, small businesses, and
Fortune 500 companies. Sean serves as trusted legal counsel to cities, counties, hospitals, banking
institutions, aviation and port authorities, universities, industries, corporations, and various
professional associations.
As a local government lawyer, Sean represents Florida counties and municipalities before the
Florida Cabinet, Florida Legislature, and other tribunals. As an administrative lawyer, Sean has a
strong understanding of the Florida Administrative Procedures Act, advising clients on matters
before the Department of Administrative Hearings and various State of Florida boards and
agencies.
Sean received his Bachelor of Science degree in Political Science in 1990 and earned his Juris
Doctor degree in 1994 from the Florida State University College of Law. While at FSU, Sean’s
leadership qualities led him to become the Student Body President and two-time Chairman of the
Florida Student Association Board of Directors, and member of the Florida Board of Regents. In
compilation of his many years of work and service, in 2021 Sean was selected to interview and
ultimately a semi-finalist for the Presidency at Florida State University.
Sean served as the 2018-2019 President of the Orange Bowl Committee, is the General Counsel
for the National Bar Association, is the Founder and Chairman of the Big Bend Minority Chamber
of Commerce and served on the Board of Directors for Hancock Whitney Bank. In addition, he
serves on the Big 10 Equality Coalition and is a member of the Florida State University Hall of
Fame Committee. For his contributions to the Orange Bowl Committee and his tireless efforts to
bring Glades Pioneer Park to Palm Beach County, Sean was awarded with special recognition by
the Palm Beach County Sports Commission in 2019. Sean was also selected to serve on the Florida
State University Foundation’s Board of Trustees in 2018 and the Jim Moran Institute Advisory Board.
In 2017, Sean was inducted into the Tallahassee Barristers Legal Hall of Fame and in 2015, Sean
received the Distinguished Member Award for Leadership Florida. In 2022 Pittman Law Group was
awarded the Seminole 100 award in recognition as one of the fastest-growing alumni owned
businesses by the Florida State University Alumni Association. In the Spring of 2022, Sean received
the FSU Alumni Association and Omicron Delta Kappa’s Grads Made Good Award during their
Alumni Awards ceremony.DocuSign Envelope ID: EC6FAFCB-DD2A-44FB-89E2-F8C2596A1842

3.1 RESPONSE TO ITN SPECIFICATIONS
1. ESTABLISH STRATEGIES AND LOBBYING EFFORTS THAT FURTHER THE POLICY GOALS OF FSU
SGA AS ARTICULATED BY THE STUDENT BODY LEGISLATIVE AGENDA, WHICH HAS BEEN PASSED
THROUGH THE OFFICE GOVERNMENTAL AFFAIRS (OGA) BOARD OF DIRECTORS, AND
SUBSEQUENTLY, PASSED AS A RESOLUTION THROUGH THE STUDENT SENATE AND SIGNED BY
THE STUDENT BODY PRESIDENT.
“Challenge us with the issues that challenge you” is not just our slogan but a guiding principle for
our commitment to issues. Early implementation of strategies coupled with our experience and
aggressive advocacy is the cornerstone of our success, particularly in the legislative and
appropriation process. Included in this proposal are specific examples of our success in directing
legislative efforts. Specifically, we have outlined our ability to present policy recommendations to
agencies and elected officials, monitor legislation and policy, and secure public sector funding. We
utilize a forward-thinking approach to continuously be aware and proactive on policy and funding
legislation. Our clients are serious about accomplishing objectives and look to create long lasting
relationships with key players in the political arena. Our presence in Tallahassee allows for strategic
monitoring of governmental activities and direct access to state legislators, agency officials and
their staff. We are positioned to influence state ad hoc committees and task forces for aggressive
representation of our clients. By also using the latest technology in policy tracking, we can alert our
clients in real time of any substantive proposed policy changes.
2. STAY IN REGULAR CONTACT WITH THE DIRECTOR OF THE SGA OFFICE OF GOVERNMENTAL
AFFAIRS AND/OR STUDENT BODY PRESIDENT TO INFORM THE DIRECTOR/PRESIDENT OF THE
CURRENT STATUS OF THE OBJECTIVES OF SGA AND COORDINATE STRATEGY TO ACHIEVE THOSE
OBJECTIVES. PHONE AND EMAIL INTERACTION ON A WEEKLY BASIS IS CONSIDERED REGULAR
CONTACT.
The legislative process moves very quickly. Often times, meetings are noticed a week or less than
48 hours before they begin. We work with our clients to facilitate their presence at relevant
meetings and draft policy notes and comments for their use. Due to the fast nature of the legislative
process our team utilizes multiple forms of communication and levels of analysis to provide updates
to our clients. We are also available 24/7 to field questions in regards to updates to our clients
during committee weeks, the budget process, and legislative session.
3. DRAFT BACKGROUND INFORMATION ABOUT PERTINENT LEGISLATION AND/OR AMENDMENTS
THAT AFFECT POLICY ISSUES OF FSU SGA AS ARTICULATED BY THE STUDENT BODY PRESIDENT
AND/OR THE OGA BOARD OF DIRECTORS.
The PLG team is comprised of attorneys and consultants that have worked with each branch of
government. We are well versed in the Florida constitution, statutes, administrative code, and
relevant local ordinances. We utilize our legal and legislative experience to draft special and
general legislation that is in line with our client’s goals as well as analysis. In addition, we utilize our
legal research tools and platforms to create policy memoranda for our clients, legislative members,
and staff.DocuSign Envelope ID: EC6FAFCB-DD2A-44FB-89E2-F8C2596A1842

YEAR. THE SECOND SHALL EXPLAIN INFORMATION, UPDATES, AND ANALYSIS
REGARDING COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS.

DURING COMMITTEE HEARINGS, ONCE IN THE MIDDLE OF LEGISLATIVE SESSION FOR

FIRST SENATE MEETING OF THE NEWLY INAUGURATED SPRING SENATE) AND ONCE AT
THE END OF SESSION BUT NOT AFTER THE FINAL SENATE MEETING.

Additionally, we have facilitated training and preparatory sessions for the FSU SGA in advance of

accustomed to appearing before the Student Senate, Noles Engaged in Politics, and other events
for legislative updates at each stage of the legislative process. We will continue to provide these
updates if retained by FSU SGA.

Our team, upon the request of FSU SGA, has appeared before the OGA Board of Directors for
legislative updates and as requested by the Director. We are committed to providing professional
representation to our clients and will continue to provide these updates if retained by FSU SGA. It
is extremely helpful to our own team and efforts to meet regularly with our clients
7. ASSIST THE DIRECTOR OF THE SGA OFFICE OF GOVERNMENTAL AFFAIRS IN FORMULATING A
LEGISLATIVE AGENDA FOR FSU SGA.
Having represented the interests of higher education for over twenty years, our team has significant
experience identifying legislative policies and appropriations that will advance FSU’s long term
strategic goals. Upon engagement by FSU SGA, we will work with student leadership and
designated staff to develop a legislative package. Building a strong legislative package requires
a collective of information from stakeholders within government. In an effort to provide such
information to our clients, our team works with our contacts to learn the priorities of the Governor,
Speaker, and Senate President. This information helps our clients’ set priorities that will align with
presiding officers. Further, we closely monitor agencies and judiciaries to understand rulings and
decisions that may impact the SGA.DocuSign Envelope ID: EC6FAFCB-DD2A-44FB-89E2-F8C2596A1842

OFFICIAL, WITH MEMBERS OF GOVERNMENTAL ENTITIES, GOVERNING BODIES, COMMITTEE
STAFF MEMBERS, OR RELATED POSITIONS.
We work at designated staff and student leadership’s direction to coordinate meetings with state
officials regarding FSU SGA’s priorities. In the era of term limits, the team understands the
importance of cultivating relationships with members on both sides of the aisle. Long standing
relationships with key officials have significantly enhanced our team’s success. The team’s consultants
have established a positive working relationship with current and future leaders.

hearings, meetings, Board of Governor Meetings, and rulemaking proceedings, we will also meet

most efficient technology to connect directly to legislative and executive meetings and activities.

positions are on the record and will promote the interests of the FSU SGA as directed. In addition
to attending and when needed speaking at Board of Governors Meetings, Board of Trustees
Meetings, and rulemaking proceedings, we will also meet with staff and elected officials on our
client’s behalf in the interim periods.

INTERESTED NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS (NGO’S), AND OTHER CONTRACTED FIRMS

SUPPORTIVE OF THE POLICY ISSUES AND GOALS OF THE FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY STUDENT
BODY LEGISLATIVE AGENDA.
The PLG team meets regularly with and attends legislative updates of organizations relevant to
higher education. We monitor their list of “radar bills” and work to tailor our advocacy of those
bills to the impact that it will have on our individual clients. As former student leaders and officers
within FSA, we understand, firsthand the importance of collectivity. We have also frequently
convened with other university lobbyists to collectively work together for or against issues at the
guidance of FSU SGA.DocuSign Envelope ID: EC6FAFCB-DD2A-44FB-89E2-F8C2596A1842

AND OBJECTIVES INCLUDED IN THE STUDENT BODY LEGISLATIVE AGENDA. ADDITIONALLY, THE

Legislative Committees and State Agencies release information throughout the year that impacts
public sector agencies. To communicate the same to clients, our team prepares briefing reports for
key stages of the legislative and budget processes. These include but are not limited to:
• Fiscal Analysis in Brief
• Long Range Financial Outlook
• Governor's Budget Priorities
• State Agency Requests
• Interim Committee Week Reports
• Weekly Session Reports
• Final Session Reports
• Daily Budget Conference Reports
• Grant Notices
Each report is customized to address FSU SGA’s legislative agenda. Specifically, the weekly interim
committee and session reports provide an overview of events impactful to higher education and
bills related to FSU SGA’s legislative agenda. Our team works to ensure that we provide in-depth
analysis of bills and their fiscal impact.
Additionally, during committee weeks, legislative session (apart from budget conference), and
special session, our team provides weekly reports to clients. Because the Budget Conference is
exceptionally fast paced, the team works to ensure that clients are the first to hear of important
developments and provide daily reports on their appropriation requests.
Reports about the events of the budget making process including the fiscal analysis in brief, the
long-range financial outlook, and the Governor's budget priorities are provided to clients upon
release. In addition, we also provide monthly reports which detail activities and legislative services
provided in the previous month as well as an end of session report which includes analyses on all
enrolled texts filed, all bills signed by the Governor, and the final budget. The firm strives not to
simply regurgitate information but to analyze it and provide a detailed yet succinct overview of
the budget documents and how they will impact the upcoming legislative session. Please see samples
in the Appendix.DocuSign Envelope ID: EC6FAFCB-DD2A-44FB-89E2-F8C2596A1842

8.2 SAMPLE INTERIM COMMITTEE WEEK REPORT
SESSION WEEK EIGHT REPORT
Last week the Legislature began the Conference Committees process. Unfortunately, the Subcommittee
Chairman had the difficult task of addressing the billion-dollar difference between the two budget
packages. The subcommittee chairman worked diligently to finish a budget in the short window. On
Saturday evening, Conference Chairman bumped items that they were unable to agree on to the
Conference Chairman.
PUBLIC WORKS PROJECTS
Last week, legislation relating to public works projects passed both chambers. The legislation prohibits
local governments from requiring contractors and subcontractors to meet the following provisions:
- Pay employees a predetermined amount of wages
- Provide employees a specific type of benefit
- Set staffing requirements
- Recruit, train, or hire employees from a designated, restricted, or single source.
The legislation will only apply when the state provides fifty percent or more of the funding for a project
or if any federal funding goes to the project.
VACATION RENTALS
SB 188 permits local governments to amend certain vacation rental laws, ordinances, or regulations to be
less restrictive, including providing regulatory relief for certain military personnel and disabled veterans.
The bill maintains the prohibition in current law against local laws, ordinances, or regulations that prohibit
vacation rentals or regulate the duration or frequency of rental of vacation rentals. The bill permits a local
ordinance relating to vacation rentals that is subject to the grandfather provision in s. 509.032(7)(b), F.S.,
to maintain its grandfathered status, if the ordinance is ratified in a local referendum by at least a two-
thirds of the electors voting in the referendum. Current law permits local laws, ordinances, or regulations
“exclusively relating to property valuation as a criterion” for vacation rental if the law, ordinance or
regulation is required to be approved by the state’s land planning agency pursuant to an area of critical
state concern designation. The bill expands the exemption to include local laws, ordinances, or regulations
governing vacation rentals. The legislation passed in the House and will be heard in the Senate on May
03, 2017.
HOMESTEAD EXEMPTION
HB 7105 and the companion implementing bill were heard in the Senate today on third reading. The
legislation was amended to reduce the fiscal impact to local governments by changing the exemption on
the assessed valuation. The bill previously exempted the assessed valuation greater than fifty thousandDocuSign Envelope ID: EC6FAFCB-DD2A-44FB-89E2-F8C2596A1842

exemption the property appraiser must remove the exemption from previous tax rolls.
HB 7065 - Relating to Local Government Fiscal Responsibility
House Sponsor: House Ways & Means Committee
House Status: Senate received and referred
HB 7065 contains several provisions to increase the fiscal transparency of local government. The
legislation requires local governments to publish their voting records related to tax increases and issuance
of tax-supported debt. The provision would be implemented in phases over four years. The legislation also
required local governments to provide easy online access to property tax Truth in Millage (TRIM) notices.
These notices usually include information regarding property taxes, millage rates, and proposed increases
to both. The legislation also requires local governments to host additional public meetings and the
expansion of public notice requirements for local option tax increases and new long-term tax-supported
debt issuances. Further, local governments must conduct a debt affordability analysis prior to approving
the issuance of new long-term tax-supported debt. Finally, this bill would require an auditor to report
whether local governments are in compliance with the provisions of the new "Local Government Fiscal
Transparency Act." Also, the Auditor General must request evidence that corrective action has been
initiated from local governments found not to be in compliance with the Act.
SB 80 – Relating to Public Records
Senate Sponsor(s): Senator Steube (R), Senator Garcia (R), Senator Campbell (D)
Status: Enrolled text filed
The legislation requires attorney's fees and enforcement costs if the court determines that an agency
unlawfully refused access to a public record or if the court finds that the plaintiff requests the records for
an improper use. The legislation also defines that the plaintiff must file a request for the public records at
least five days before filing the action. The legislation also defines improper purpose as one in which
person requests records mainly to harass an agency, cause a violation, or for frivolous purposes.
HB 13/SB 1770– Relating to Community Redevelopment Agencies
House Sponsor: Representative Raburn (R)
Senate Sponsor: Senator Lee (R)

Senate Status: Unfavorable in Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Tourism, and Economic

temporarily postponed.
House Bill 13 would alter the function and responsibilities of Community Redevelopment Agencies (CRAs).
Under this bill, commissioners of the CRA would be required to participate in ethics training. Additionally,
starting in 2018, the CRA would be required to submit an annual report by the end of March to the county
or municipality that created it. HB 13 would also terminate all CRAs in existence on the expiration of the
agencies charter as well as prevent the creation of any new CRAs after July 1, 2017. CRAs that have not
reported expenses or revenue for three (3) consecutive fiscal years will be deemed inactive by the
Department of Economic Opportunity. Inactive CRAs may not expend any funds unless for the service of
outstanding bond debt. SB 1770 is almost identical to HB 13. There are three (3) proposed amendments
on SB 1770 that were adopted by HB 13 and would make it identical to the House’s version of the bill.DocuSign Envelope ID: EC6FAFCB-DD2A-44FB-89E2-F8C2596A1842

From: Ian Seibert, Student Body President
Subject: Intent to Hire
As we continue with executive initiatives in the Seibert-Teplin-Goodman administration,
we have assessed needed additional support for the Departments of Administrative Affairs
and Campus Life.
Department of Administrative Affairs
Candidate Affairs Coordinator (2 out of 2)
Created to support the Secretary in managing the volume and complexity of SGA personnel
processes. Assists with administering appointments for vacated positions, support internal
recordkeeping and onboarding coordination, and helps maintain organizational continuity
during transitions. Reports to the Secretary of Administrative Affairs.
Department of Campus Life
External Affairs Coordinator
Created to support the external outreach initiatives and events led by the Department of
Campus Life and the Executive Branch. Attend campus events, table at recurring events
such as Market Wednesday, and connect with the greater student body as well as champion
projects developed to benefit campus life. Reports to the Secretary of Campus life.
Go Noles!

From: Ian Seibert, Student Body President
Subject: Intent to Hire
As we continue to build the Executive Branch, we have seen a need for one more
supporting role in the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Department. This Intent to hire
includes an additional Community Advocacy position.
Department of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
Community Advocacy Coordinator (1 out of 2)
Created to bridge the DE&I department with both the Executive Agency network and the
Legislative branch, ensuring marginalized student concerns are translated into actionable
policy. Works with political education and social advocacy chairs within Executive
Agencies, meets semesterly with those chairs, develops policy proposals to advocate for
marginalized students' needs, and serves as the direct liaison between the department and
the Legislative Branch. Reports to the Secretary of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.

From: Ian Seibert, Student Body President
Subject: Intent to Hire
With the confirmation of our Attorney General, Chief of Staff, Secretary of Academic
Affairs, and Secretary of Health, Wellness, and Safety, we have finally concluded the
confirmation for all Department Head positions. This Intent to hire includes the coordinator
positions reporting to the recently confirmed Secretaries.
Department of Academic Affairs
Research Grants Coordinator
Created to ensure students have access to information regarding funding for their undergraduate
research projects spanning various topics and disciplines. Reports to the Secretary of Academic
Affairs.
Undergraduate Research Publications Coordinator
Created to implement sustained institutionalized support for students and their endeavors in
publishing research in research journals and publications. Reports to the Secretary of Academic
Affairs.
Professional Development Coordinator
Created to be the main liaison to the FSU Career Center, where they will guarantee students are
aware of and have access to opportunities to build their professional experience. Reports to the
Secretary of Academic Affairs.
Department of Health, Wellness, and Safety
Health Advocacy Coordinator

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Created to serve as the liaison to CAPS and UHS as well as convey student needs alongside
student-focused initiatives while expanding the reach of health services provided by FSU. Reports
to the Secretary of Health, Wellness, and Safety.
Campus Wellness Coordinator
Created to serve as the liaison to CHAW, ensuring the nine dimensions of wellness are addressed
through student advocacy and initiatives.Reports to the Secretary of Health, Wellness, and Safety.
Safety Innovation Coordinator
Created to serve as the liaison to TAPS and FSUPD and prioritize initiatives such as pedestrian
safety and improving blue light services to ensure students are not endangered on campus. Reports
to the Secretary of Health, Wellness, and Safety.
Department of Legal Affairs
Legislative Coordinators (2)
Created to communicate all legislative activity from the Student Senate and Congress of Graduate
Students to ensure policies are coherent with and addressed by the executive branch. Reports to
the Attorney General.
Go Noles!

Ian Seibert
Student Body President
