resolution read in Student Senate or by appearance of a
delegate from COGS, on the following matters:
a. Legislation that changes Chapter 607 of the Student Body
Statutes.
b. Legislation which is a resolution of COGS
concerning university- wide matters.
c. Other matters as the SGA shall request COGS
representation.
d. Other matters as COGS shall request to be
represented before SGA.
3. COGS shall hold at least one (1) regular meeting per month.
4. All legislation approved by COGS shall be done so upon
simple majority vote of quorum.
5. COGS may establish a policy pursuant to Chapter 421 which
shall be called the “COGS Code.” Changes to the COGS
Code shall not require approval by the Student Senate, but
the adoption or revision of the COGS Code shall be approved
by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of COGS quorum. Legislation

serve on COGS, its committees, and its task forces as
necessary.

4. To construct a budget for each fiscal year for portions of the
Activity and Service Fee revenue apportioned to COGS. This
revenue will total thirty (30%) percent of all main FSU campus
A&S monies collected from students designated by the
Registrar as five (5) or seven (7).
5. To approve the expenditure of monies allocated to the
COGS budget, with the authorizing signature of two
members of the COGS Executive Committee.

7. To submit a copy of its budget to the Student Senate detailing
its categorical spending in a timely fashion.
8. COGS will be offered a non-voting ex-officio seat on all

freeze funds or otherwise sanction non-complaint studentDocuSign Envelope ID: 09EC7097-3091-445F-ABD3-4A23FE1FE590

organizations within its jurisdiction, subject to appeal to

Short Title: Due to the Board of Trustees deleting the position of SGA University Defender
from university regulations on February 28th, 2025, this bill will reflect that change in SGA
statute and Rules of Procedure
Summary of Legislation: A bill and accompanying resolution eliminate the University
Defender position by removing all references to it from the state statutes and the university’s
rules of procedure.
Background Information: The Office of the University Defender would assist students upon
request who have been accused of violations of the Student Conduct Code, or a Student
Government Rule or Regulation. University Defenders would also represent impeached
officers of the Student Body at their trial before the Supreme Court, if they are requested by
the defendant to do so. This bill and resolution will remove all references to that position.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This will remove all references to the University Defender position in rules of procedure and
statutes.

Short Title: The Executive Departments Act of 2025
Summary of Legislation:
The Executive Departments Act of 2025 aims to set a precedent for future Executive cabinets
to create a comprehensive framework for the execution of policy projects and the improvement
of Florida State University’s campus. It defines positions with the Executive
Departments/Cabinet, reorganizes entities into other categories, and streamlines legislation
pertaining to appendages of the executive branch.
Background Information:
The Dale - Ramirez-Romero – Wyatt administration developed a framework for an outline of
am Executive cabinet during the Spring 2025 semester. After communication with Senate
leadership, a working group was formed to codify the executive cabinet into statutory
language.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The Executive Departments Act of 2025 amends major offices, outlines the Executive
Departments, and renumbers certain SGA entities into Affiliated Projects.

Short Title: Establishment of New Student Organization Funding Programs and Operating
Policies & Procedures
Summary of Legislation:
Bill #77-034 creates two new student organization funding programs in the Student Body
Statutes: the RSO Allocation Committee and the RSO Development Fund. It also repeals
outdated provisions and refines the Statutes to streamline the allocation of A&S fees. The
accompanying Resolution #77-060 formally adopts operational policies and procedures for the
RSO Allocation Committee, including funding guidelines, meeting structure, and evaluation
criteria.
Background Information:
In recent years, SGA and the Department of Student Engagement have received feedback
from Recognized Student Organizations (RSOs) on campus indicating that RSOs have faced
obstacles in accessing student government funding due to duplicative, outdated, and overly
complex policies.
The Student Senate has recognized the need to restructure and simplify the process to
promote accessibility, equity, and efficiency; the FY 2025-26 SGA budget adopted by the
Student Senate contemplates eliminating the Programming Allocation Committee (PAC), the
Resource for Travel Allocation Committee (RTAC), the Organizational Fund, and the RSO
Budget Fund and replacing those funding programs with a more consolidated, streamlined
funding process that will reduce confusion and provide a “one-stop shop” for RSOs to seek
funding from SGA.
This legislation is the product of collaboration between the Student Senate, the SGA Executive
Branch, the Department of Student Engagement, and campus partners and reflects best
practices for financial governance and student engagement.Docusign Envelope ID: 6EC0BA51-9D81-4FC0-B77B-FD6D09FCE19B

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation will:
• Establish the RSO Allocation Committee (RSOAC) to centralize and standardize
supplemental funding for undergraduate RSOs;
• Establish elections for members of the RSO Allocation Committee to increase
transparency, democratic participation, and student voice in the allocation of A&S fees;
• Create the RSO Development Fund, providing small grants to support new and
developing RSOs;
• Repeal outdated chapters (e.g., Chapters 807 and 815) and replace them with a more
robust and efficient framework for allocating SGA funding to RSOs;
• Clarify funding eligibility, limitations, and approval processes;
• Adopt a transparent and merit-based rubric to guide allocation decisions;
• Improve communication of funding opportunities through required social media
outreach; and
• Enhance transparency in SGA’s funding allocation process and ensure that these
programs are evaluated regularly to identify recommendations for further program
enhancement in the future.
Ultimately, this legislation will enhance accountability, transparency, and equitable access to
funding for student organizations.

78th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 016
Primary Sponsor(s): Perantoni, Bigenho
Co-sponsor(s): Fernandez, Ramos, Garcia
Short Title: Restructuring the Executive for Visibility, Accountability, Modernization, and
Performance (REVAMP) Act of 2026
Summary of Legislation:
This legislation would reform many processes for the appointment of officers under the Student
Body Statutes, specifying exactly which offices in the Executive Branch require confirmation by
the Student Senate. The bill discusses many ‘staff roles’ throughout the Executive Branch and
clarifies their functions and appointment process. The bill also creates a new role of special
advisor, an individual with an 8 week acting capacity to help assist the President on larger
projects on a temporary basis.
Background Information:
The current appointment structure of the Executive Branch has had frictions between the
Legislative and Executive arms of the SGA, which has caused issues relating to opposing
memorandums, judicial filings, and disagreements about interpretation. To rectify this, the
Legislative Branch has conferred with the Executive Branch to find a middle point that solves
problems on all sides.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Outreach has included the Senate President, the Chair and Vice Chair of Internal Affairs,
Office of Attorney General and the President of the Student Government. It has also been
drafted in direct with the Student Body President, the Student Body President Elect, the
Student Body Vice President Elect, and the Student Body Treasurer Elect.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation would: specify the exact offices that need to be forwarded and confirmed by the
Senate; allow for Executive appointment of staff roles; specifying promotion procedures;
establish special advisors; create nonfeasance procedures; and correct many grammatical
errors.

Short Title: Update to Statutory Subdivision
Summary of Legislation:
This bill amends Chapter 100.3 of Student Statute, which addresses the formatting of subdivisions
within Statute. This bill intends to give a better example of what subdivision within Statute should look
like, as well as change our current formatting to better reflect that of the Florida legislature.
Background Information:
With the current language, our Student Statute’s subdivisions go against this statute, and all of our
current legislature is improperly formatted. In addition, the language used in this clause makes it difficult
to understand how formatting should be done, making the process of drafting legislation more difficult
for newer Senators.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This legislation was drafted in consultation with the Senate President. Given that the primary
stakeholders for this legislation will be Senators, having input from their primary representative was
crucial.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted by the Student Senate, this bill will amend Student Statute to reflect a better example of how
subdivisions should be formatted, providing clearer guidelines to new Senators regarding how they
should format their drafted legislation. Moreover, this change would allow our Student Statutes to better
reflect the current formatting adopted by the Florida Legislature, which our Student Statutes are
modeled after.

Short Title:
The A.R.C.H.I.V.E Act - An Act for the Reorganization, Codification, and Historical Indexing of
Verified Enactments
Summary of Legislation:
This comprehensive 65-page bill updates our Student Body Statutes to remove all reserved chapters
from Municode, moving all 67 unused sections to a renamed “Archive Book”, simultaneously relocating
all “Historical Senate Documents” to their own tabs under “Enrolled Legislation”. It renumbers chapters,
titles, and the citations within them accordingly so that our governing document is up to date with itself
in all sections. The accompanying resolution explains all chapters and titles being removed and
updated, while detailing how future updates to the Archive Book shall take place by working alongside
the Office of Student Governance & Advocacy.
Background Information:
Through 78 years of Senate excellence, productivity, and monumental change, our Statutes have
undergone more revisions, deletions, and additions than any other document in the SGA space. As
such, they are riddled on Municode with sections no longer in active use, citations that are incorrect,
and numbered chapters that should be far higher than they are given their active role in our
governance. This bill updates all of that and explains specific changes and the path to maintain those
changes in the resolution.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
The Office of Student Governance & Advocacy, Student Body President Ian Seibert, Vice President for
Student Affairs Dr. Amy Hecht
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation will make Municode and Student Body Statutes far easier to read for both Senators and
the public alike by removing confusing sections while preserving our vital SGA history in a section
specifically made to highlight it. It will set up a framework for future necessary changes to ensure that
additional repeals have a clear path after being taken out of use.Docusign Envelope ID: AE1BE061-FA6B-8C12-8107-440517B74FC7

Sunshine Law
History: Revised by the 59th Senate Bill 85.
This Act is to be entitled the "Florida State University
Student Government in the Sunshine Act" referred to hereafter
as the "Sunshine Act."
Definitions
The following definitions shall be fully applicable for the
purpose of this act.
A. "The Public" shall be defined as any member of the
Student Body who is neither an officer nor candidate for
office in the Student Government Association, as well as
University faculty and staff unaffiliated with Student
Government, as well as any person not affiliated with
the Florida State University or the Student Government
Association.
B. "Student Government Affiliates" shall be defined as all
officers and candidates for office in the Student
Government Association, as well as all staff members of
the same.
All meetings held under the auspices of Student Government,
except as otherwise provided in the Constitution, at which
official acts are to be taken, are declared open to the public
at all times. No resolution, rule, or formal action shall be
considered binding, except if enacted at such meeting.
Student Government Affiliates shall be entitled to attend all
meetings held under the auspices of Student Government except
as provided for in these statutes, in the Senate Rules of
Procedure, or any other duly authorized Rule of Procedure.
There shall be no less than five ( 5) minutes aggregate
reserved at the beginning of any meeting held under the
auspices of Student Government for members of the Public and
all Student Government Affiliates to address those assembled

The minutes of any meeting under this chapter shall be
recorded at the time of the meeting and such records shall be
open to the public and to Student Government Affiliates. The
Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction to issue injunctions to
enforce the purposes of this chapter upon application by any
member of the Student Body.
Any person may be requested to leave any meeting held under
the auspices of Student Government; however they must be
explicitly informed of their respective rights under the
Sunshine Act.
No provision with this Act shall be construed so as to
prohibit the Chair of a meeting from maintaining decorum
necessary to the facilitation of business, nor to waive any
officer's right to call upon law enforcement officials in the
event of criminal disturbance.
Any meeting held without twenty-four {24) hours prior public
notice shall be considered in violation of the provisions of
this chapter.
Public notice shall consist of an announcement of the meeting
time, place and purpose.

Legislative intent and declaration of policy.
A. It is essential to the proper conduct and operation of
the Student Body that its officials be independent and
impartial, and that public office not be used for

It is the intent of this act to protect the integrity of
Student Government by prescribing conflicts of interest
and unethical practices. It shall serve as the basis of
discipline for those who violate its provisions.
Any student has the right to file a complaint when they
feel that a violation of the Code of Ethics has occurred
with the Student Supreme Court.
1. Any organization has the right to establish
additional ethical criteria or penalties in its

Standards of Conduct
A. In order to preserve the integrity of the Florida State
University Student Government Association, its officers
and employees must disclose all potential or actual
conflicts of interests.
1. Conflict of Interest means any business or
professional activity or direct or indirect
financial interest that would place a person in a
position where there is an opportunity to disregard
the public interests of the student body for his or
her own private interests.
2. No officer or employee will judge or vote on any
matter which would affect his or her private gain.
No Executive Board member of a SGA funded
organization may vote within a funding committee of
Senate on an allocation to the organization in
which they serve as an Executive Board member which
reauires Senate confirmation. This restriction will
not apply to members' vote on the final annual
budget, sweepings, or central reserves.
3. Any vote, action, or judgment performed by an
officer or employee who has a conflict of interest
may be appealed with the Student Supreme Court.
This must be done in a written, signed complaint
submitted no later than three (3) days after the
vote, act, or judgment in which the conflict
occurs.
a. In Student Senate, a written and signed
complaint shall be filed with the chair of

SGA Bills
I have been asked to review several SGA bills and provide feedback on any potential
conflicts with law or policy. Below please find a synopsis and analysis for each of the
eight bills identified as possibly problematic.
210.4.A
The bill requires that all legislation be posted to the SGA website. Unless the item has
consent of the Senate President, the posting must occur 24 hours prior to first reading. As
each piece oflegislation moves through the process, the website must be updated to show
the most recent activity (in committee, first reading, vote, etc.) within 24 hours of the
event. The Senate Journal must also be published on the SGA website.
It is unclear from the bill who would be responsible for maintaining the postings and
ensuring that the 24-hour requirement is met. If it is the SGA Advisor or another staff
member, I would have serious concerns about the workload and the ability of SGA to
require staff members to comply. If it is a student SGA officer, I would have similar
workload concerns. Depending on the volume of bills and how quickly they move, it
may be wholly unreasonable to expect that they could be posted within 24 hours. The bill
provides no enforcement provisions or explanation of what happens if the 24-hour
requirement is not met. There is no appreciation for the possibility that posting is not
possible due to an internet outage, or what should happen if an outage occurs.
2 10.4.B
The bill requires that the names and offices of all Senators and Officers appear on the
website, as well as the committees on which they serve, their contact information and
photos.

"\ Photographs of students are not considered "directory information" by FSU. Therefore,
any University-held photograph (such as the one on an FSUCard) is considered an
education record under FERP A. If SGA wants to take their own photographs, they may
do so, but they cannot require that a student have his photograph taken for public
consumption. Additionally, if the student requests a privacy flag and does not want his or
her directory information disclosed, SGA cannot post the student's name, contact
information, or any other data. I would recommend that the photograph provision be
stricken and that language be inserted that all names of Senators and Officers be cleared
with the University Registrar to ensure that no private information is posted.
210.4.C
Revision shortens the transmittal time from five days to 24 hours and requires that the
transmittal be in digital format.
The workload issues present in 21 0.4.A are a concern here, as well as the possibility that
a digital transmission within 24 hours may be impossible due to unforeseen
circumstances. I would suggest that, at a minimum, there be an alternate delivery method
provided for, such as posting on the door of the SGA office, and that the 24-hour
requirement be revisited.
210.4.0
Revision provides ~hat minutes be taken at each committee meeting for each piece of
legislation and that the minutes be posted on the SGA website.
It appears the committee report is already required by another statutory prov1s1on.
However, "minutes" and "reports" are two different things and should not be conflated.
Additionally, the provision is poorly worded and contains some grammatical errors.
304.8
Revision requires dissemination of "non-personal information" of applicants to Senators
via e-mail at least 24 hours before the applicants' appearance before the Senate. "Non-
personal information" includes, but is not limited to "experience, references, acaden1ic
standing, and the "committee report" of internal affairs.''
I am uncomfortable with the idea that SGA members can determine what is and is not
relevant information and what is and is not "non-personal," especially because it appears
they have no idea what that should include or how state and federal laws could prevent
publication of such information. Academic standing, to the extent it includes something
beyond major field of study and dates of attendance, is not directory information and is
protected under FERPA. TI1e "committee report" could include all sorts of infonnation
obtained during the internal affairs meeting that is not public and should not be
published. Allowing untrained students to publish, at will, any information they deem
"relevant" or "non-personal" is ill-advised. Publication of incorrect or inaccurate
information could have serious legal consequences.

304.3.F
Revision requires that a written report be completed after each candid~te interview. If the
candidate is denied, the report must include the reason for the denial. The report must be
made available to any SGA official who requests to view it.
I would be interested in the reasons behind this revision, as I am generally opposed to
record creation for the sake of record creation. Furthermore, there are no guidelines as to
what the report should or should not include. If it includes infonnation that is FERP A-
protected, then the portion of the revision that allows SGA officials to see it is unlawful.
It is also unclear whether only SGA officials could see the record (which would probably
not be legal), or if it would be open to any person, including the candidate. Either way,
the provision is pre-empted by Florida's public records law and/or FERPA. SGA cannot
determine who may and who may not see records that would otherwise be public, nor can
they open FERPA-protected documents to a select set of viewers. Additionally, as in
304.8, the publication of inaccurate or incorrect information could have serious legal
consequences.
401.2.B and 401.7.A
Revisions, which are exactly the same, provides that proposed legislation must be posted
24 hours before first reading unless it has the Senate President's consent, and that all
legislation must be posted for one week prior to second reading. If legislation is not
posted in compliance with these requirements, it cannot move forward.
The same issues are present here as with 210.4.A. There is no safety net if online
publication is not possible. The "one week" provision is ambiguous, and I would suggest
that SGA use the "class day" method of computing time, as in the Student Conduct Code
and other University regulations.
409.2
Revision provides that all bill titles, referenda, and constitutional amendments and a
description be published on the SGA website, replacing ''widely published forum"
language.
I would argue that this change is unnecessary. If SGA wants to designate its website as
its forum for publication, it can do so under the existing "widely published fotum"
language. As in the publication bills above, there is no provision for publication in
another form if the website is unavailable.
The overarching question here is, what are the issues that SGA is trying to address? Are
people unhappy with a lack of access to this information? If so, there is an easier way to
ensure access. The inflexibility of 24-hour deadlines is going to lead to all sorts of issues,
and there appears to be no enforcement provisions or explanations of what happens if the
deadlines are not met.
I would suggest that, if SGA wishes to send a message that they are going digital and are
going to post everything on their website and do it quickly, they do so by issuing a policy

sections.heading: Page 9

statement that explains their goals. The policy statement could include guidelines for
digital publication and goals of posting within a certain time period. Phrases like ''as
soon as practicable" and "within a reasonable amount of time" are common in public
records laws and regulations and meet all legal standards.
I hope this information is helpful to you. Please do not hesitate to contact me if there is
any additional assistance I can provide. Thank you.

78th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 035
Primary Sponsor(s): Gaynor, Bigenho
Co-sponsor(s): Rivas, Gurtis, Aihe
Short Title: Amending Chapter 201 to Create Suggested Qualifications for Executive Branch
Appointments
Summary of Legislation:
This bill would allow the Student Body President, through the annual policy on the organization of the
executive branch, to create a list of Suggested Qualifications for all Executive appointed positions, not
including vacant Senate seats. It also designates power to allow unqualified applicants to be
disqualified with appropriate Senate checks.
Background Information:
Through the last cycle of Executive Appointments, the volume of applicants received has created
increasing levels of complexity for the Executive Branch. This bill seeks to offer a commonsense lever
for which the Executive Branch can use to decrease their overall workload endured by ineligible
applicants while also increasing transparency and accountability within the appointment process. By
creating a cohesive structure for the executive branch to use for appointments, the applicant
experience, and interviewer experience, becomes better over time.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Office of the Student Body President, Office of the Attorney General, Office of the Senate President,
Secretary of Administrative Affairs.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This bill allows the Student Body President to set an objective list of suggested qualifications as part of
the annual policy on the organization of the executive branch. The Student Body President, or designee
thereof, can disqualify candidates for positions that do not meet the qualifications set within Executive
Policy. When disqualifying candidates, the Executive Branch will be required to keep records of said
disqualification with details of which qualifications were not met. If candidates are improperly
disqualified, this bill defines the recourse Senate could take to investigate the matter.

77th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 051
Primary Sponsor(s): Goldstein, LoBianco
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: Amending the Student Body Statutes to Establish Procedures for the
Organizational Session and Create Oaths of Office for the Senate President and Senate
President Pro Tempore
Summary of Legislation:
This bill amends Chapter 400 of the Student Body Statutes to codify the Organizational
Session of the Student Senate pursuant to the newly amended Student Body Constitution, and
creates new Sections 202.9 through 202.10 establishing distinct Oaths of Office for the Senate
President and Senate President Pro Tempore. The bill defines the Dean of the Senate’s role,
outlines the timing, certification, and ratification of the Organizational Session, and ensures the
statutory framework aligns with the new constitutional requirements.
Background Information:
Following the 2025 constitutional amendment to Article II, Section 4, the Student Senate is
now required to convene an Organizational Session before each new term to elect its presiding
officers. The current Student Body Statutes do not provide procedures for this session, nor
distinct oaths for the Senate’s leadership positions. This bill establishes those provisions to
provide clarity, transparency, and continuity of governance. It also re-introduces the Dean of
the Senate, still defined as the most senior, concurrently serving Senator not returning to the
next Senate, as the neutral presiding officer for the Organizational Session. These reforms
were drafted to modernize Senate transitions, prevent procedural uncertainty.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
1. Add 400.8 to create the statutory framework for the Organizational Session, including
timing, presiding officer, quorum, voting, oath administration, and certification.
2. Add 202.9–202.10 to establish distinct oaths for the Senate President and Senate
President Pro Tempore and to assign the Dean of the Senate as the official to
administer those oaths.
3. Update cross-references within Chapter 400 to reflect these changes.
Together, these updates align statute with the amended Constitution, ensure fair and
transparent leadership elections, and strengthen the ethical and institutional framework
of the Student Senate.Docusign Envelope ID: AC6C724C-AA43-4B2B-A77F-1001287A47D6

up for confirmation who do not communicate with Student Senate leadership about their confirmation
hearing attendance, as well as establishing the applicable Committee Chair(s) as the main point of
contact for the candidate as well as the one responsible for notifying the Student Senate if and when

78th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 003
Primary Sponsor(s): Bigenho
Co-sponsor(s): Bischof
Short Title: Amending Chapter 203, Student Body Statutes, to Strengthen Transparency,
Notice, and Public Participation under the SGA Sunshine Act
Summary of Legislation:
This legislation promotes accountability, transparency, and openness within the Florida State
University Student Government Association (SGA). It updates and clarifies existing provisions
of the Student Body Statutes to ensure SGA operations, communications, and decision-
making processes remain accessible to all students and consistent with the principles of public
trust and representative governance.
Background Information:
This legislation is being submitted following the direct request of the 77th Student Senate to
hear this measure at the beginning of the 78th Student Senate. This legislation has been in
development for several months in close collaboration with the Executive Branch’s Office of
the Attorney General. Throughout this process, amendments and revisions have been
incorporated in consultation with the Judiciary Committee and the Student Life Committee to
address their specific recommendations and concerns. Several provisions within this act were
drafted at the direct request of the Attorney General to safeguard judicial independence from
Sunshine enforcement conflicts and to formally authorize the Office of the Attorney General to
participate in Sunshine enforcement procedures.
This act does not expand or impose new Sunshine transparency requirements beyond those of
public notice and public comment. Rather, it restores critical rights and accessibility measures
that have lapsed in recent years. Specifically, this legislation reinstates the protected right for
students to submit public comment ahead of meetings, non-anonymously and in writing,
ensuring their voices can be heard even when they cannot attend a 7:30 p.m. Senate session
in person that takes place on a school night. It also creates a process for students with
disabilities or other barriers to request to address the Senate virtually, improving ADA
accessibility and inclusion across SGA proceedings.
This act raises the public notice requirement (aka when we tell the student body when, where,
and why we are meeting) for major SGA entities, such as a meeting of the full Senate, the full
Executive Cabinet, Supreme Court hearings, etc from twenty-four (24) hours to forty-eight (48)Docusign Envelope ID: FB22A51C-B8ED-4D3C-82E4-5E6A5F3B743D

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
hours. This change ensures that students have adequate time to know when meetings are
occurring and to review any materials or issues that will be discussed. To maintain workflow
and flexibility, the bill also adds a specific clause allowing Senate committees and sub-entities
of these major bodies to continue meeting during that 48 hour notice period, preserving the
ability of standing committees of the Senate to meet on Mondays or Tuesdays before
Wednesday Senate sessions.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
The sponsors would like to extend their appreciation to the Executive Branch’s Office of the
Attorney General, specifically Legislative Affairs Director Logan Rubenstein and Attorney
General Madeleine Siegel, for their consistent collaboration, input, and technical guidance
throughout the drafting process. The sponsors also wish to thank Chair Leila Jackson and Vice
Chair Maria Fernandez of the Judiciary Committee, along with Chair Sara Mendez Arango and
Vice Chair Camille Friall of the Student Life Committee, for their thoughtful feedback and
engagement before, during, and after committee deliberations in the 77th Student Senate.
Their sustained involvement and attention to detail have substantially strengthened this
legislation, ensuring it reflects both practical needs and the priorities of the student body.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation will modernize and strengthen transparency, accessibility, and
accountability across all branches of the Student Government Association. It raises the public
notice requirement for major governing bodies from twenty-four (24) hours to forty-eight (48)
hours, ensuring students have sufficient time to review agendas, prepare public comments,
and attend meetings on matters of importance. At the same time, it preserves operational
efficiency by explicitly permitting committees and sub-entities of these bodies to continue
meeting during the notice period. The legislation also restores statutory protections for written
online public comment submissions, enabling students to provide non-anonymous input in
advance of meetings, and creates a process for students to request to address the Senate
virtually, improving ADA accessibility and inclusivity for those unable to attend in person.
Finally, it incorporates provisions developed with the Office of the Attorney General to clarify
judicial independence under the Sunshine Act and formally integrate the Attorney General into
Sunshine enforcement procedures. Collectively, these changes strengthen open government
practices within SGA while balancing accessibility, accountability, and functional governance.

Chapter 205 Code of Ethics
205.1 This act shall be entitled "the Student Government Code of
Ethics." The intent of this code is to strengthen the faith
and confidence of the Student Body in Student Government.
205.2 Legislative intent and declaration of policy.
205.3
A. It is essential to the proper conduct and operation of
Student Government that its officials be independent and
impartial, and that public office not be used for
private gain. Student Government officers and employees
hold their position for the benefit of the Student Body.
Such officers and employees are bound to observe in
their official acts, the highest standards of ethics
consistent with this code recognizing that promoting the
public interest and maintaining the respect of the
student body in their Student Government must be the
foremost concern.
B. It is the intent of this act to protect the integrity of
Student Government by prescribing conflicts of interest
and unethical practices. It shall serve as the basis of
discipline for those who violate its provisions.
C. Any student have the right to file a complaint when they
feel that a violation of the Code of Ethics has occurred
with the Student Supreme Court.
1. Any organization has the right to establish

A. In order to preserve the integrity of the Florida State
University Student Government Association, its officers
and employees must disclose all potential or actual
conflicts of interests.
1. Conflict of Interest means any business or
professional activity or direct or indirect
financial interest that would place a person in a
position where there is an opportunity to disregard
the public interests of the student body for his or
her own private interests.

77th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 56
Primary Sponsor(s): Rios, Jackson
Co-sponsor(s): Benner, Musso, Murphy, Ferris, Friall
Short Title: The Eddie Fordham Act amends chapter 205, “code of ethics” in student body
statutes. To allow students with prior convictions, who have been reviewed and admitted to
Florida State University through the Judicial Review Committee, to serve in Student
Government.
Summary of Legislation:
This bill amends Chapter 205, “Code of Ethics,” to allow students with prior convictions, who
have been reviewed and admitted to Florida State University through the Judicial Review
Committee, to serve in Student Government. It reaffirms FSU’s belief in second chances,
personal growth, and the power of education to transform lives.
Background Information:
Eddie Fordham’s resilience and unwavering commitment to justice have shone brightly since
his very first day at Florida State University. His refusal to let his past dictate his future
embodies the very essence of what this bill stands for, a belief in redemption, growth, and the
limitless potential of the human spirit.
Last spring, when Eddie expressed interest in joining Student Government, the discovery that
he was ineligible due to his conviction status was profoundly disheartening. College is a place
of transformation, a space where students are meant to grow, to lead, and to redefine their
paths. Eddie’s dedication to bettering himself and uplifting those around him exemplifies the
true spirit of the FSU community. Yet, a door so central to the student experience remained
unjustly closed to him. This realization illuminated a greater truth: this was not only about one
student, but about every justice-impacted individual who has fought to rebuild their life and
deserves the right to fully participate in the FSU experience.
Through the collaboration of Legislative Affairs Coordinator Logan Rubenstein, the SGA
Attorney General Madeleine Siegel, the Office of the Attorney General, and the FSU Office of
General Counsel, crucial updates were made to the language of the Student Body Statutes.
This amendment ensures that students who have already been reviewed and admitted through
the judicial review process, those whom the university has deemed worthy of belonging, are
also worthy of serving in its Student Government.Docusign Envelope ID: 512D4F50-9CF7-4819-94D1-CF4565A3514F

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
This bill represents far more than a procedural change; it stands as a testament to fairness,
empathy, and the enduring belief that one’s past should never overshadow their capacity to
lead, serve, and inspire. It is a declaration that every student who chooses growth over regret
and community over isolation deserves a seat at the table, and a voice in shaping the future of
Florida State University.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If passed, this amendment will allow justice-impacted students who have been reviewed
through the judicial review committee to hold office in Student Government. It creates a more
inclusive and compassionate campus environment, one that reflects FSU’s core values of
integrity, growth, and community. It ensures that students like Eddie, who have turned
adversity into purpose, can help shape a university they call home.

206.2 Students with grievances will submit a written complaint to the Student Supreme Court.
Upon finding a violation of 206.1, the Court will assign recommend penalties to be carried
out by the executive and legislative branches such as: freezing of funds, with possible
suspension/loss of Student Government Association status, permanent loss of existing
Student Government funding, removal from office, and/or probation. The Student Supreme
Court may assign additional penalties based on the severity of the violations. Funds will
remain frozen until proof of correction is provided to the Student Senate.
A. Upon finding a violation of 206.1, the Court, at their discretion, may inform the
Student Government Association Attorney General to begin proceedings as per
204.6.
A. The Senate Finance Committee freezing already allocated Student Government
Association funds in the guilty party’s university recognized bank account, or;
B. The Student Body President may issue an executive order which recommends
the suspension or permanent removal of the entity’s Student Government
Association Status should they fall within the purview of the executive branch, or;
C. The Senate may permanently remove any Student Government Association
funding from the entity by a resolution, or;
D. The Senate Judiciary Committee may initiate impeachment proceedings against
any Student Government officers, members, or employees of the entity found in
violation of Statute 206.1, or;
E. This chapter shall not preclude the Student Supreme Court from making other
recommendations they deem appropriate for the corresponding severity of the
violation.
1. Nothing in this chapter may preclude the Court from pursuing all types of
relief allowable under university policies, state law, and federal law.
B. F. Any Student Government Association Officer, employee, branch, agency, affiliated
projects, recognized student organization or any entity that receives Student
Government Association funding may appeal sanctions imposed by Student
Senate to the Vice President for Student Affairs.
G. All funds that have been frozen by the Senate shall remain as such until a proof of
correction is provided to the Student Senate with a deadline that was voted upon
by the Student Senate as a whole.
1. The aforementioned “proof of correction” must be provided by a designee
or representative of the entity found guilty of the violation. The proof must
be physically presented in a form of writing and in person to the Student
Senate with all required amends made as well as proof that relief for the
discrimination was made to the afflicted victim.

History: Added by the 48th Senate Bill 165. Revised by

The purpose of this legislation is to insure that all
officials of the Florida State University, Student
Government Association have received adequate training
in the areas of fiscal and ethical responsibility in the
allocation and expenditure of state funds collected
through the Activity and Service Fee.
All SGA officials holding a major office as well as
members of the Congress of Graduate Students are
required to conform to the provisions of this Statute.
The Student Body President, Chief Justice of the Supreme
Court, Chairperson of the Union Board, Chairperson of
the Campus Recreation Board, Senior Class Council
President, Speaker of the Congress of Graduate Students,
and the Directors of all Executive Agencies, Bureaus and
Affiliated Projects, as well as all Funding Board
Chairpersons shall conduct an appropriate training
program suitable to the needs of the members of their
respective organizations within four (4) weeks of the
fall SGA elections in which the members of their
respective organizations have been elected. The content
of such training programs shall be at the discretion of
the officers listed in the beginning of this section,
and shall be directed at teaching new members about the
SGA Constitution and St~tutes, and all pertinent
procedures encountered during the operation of their
respective organizations.

chooses. The seminar will be a training session..:... to

78th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 021
Primary Sponsor(s): Gaynor
Co-sponsor(s): Bigenho, Gurtis, Rivas, Iarossi, Macalintal, Hidalgo, Holliday
Short Title: The “Better Ed” Bill of 2026
Summary of Legislation:
This bill alters Chapter 207 of the Student Body Statutes to address shortfalls found in current training
requirements throughout SGA. Additionally, this bill codifies transition documents, ensuring a smooth
transfer of power and preventing information deficits. Lastly, this bill seeks to revitalize the Professional
Development opportunities that are available for the SGA space, creating a comprehensive list of local,
state, and national events that are accessible for FSU students.
Background Information:
Previously, Chapter 207 had loose guidelines for the expectations and responsibilities for SGA entity
leaders for the trainings given to its members. Due to the lack of oversight and accountability, this
expectation was not uniformly applied, resulting in a patchwork of training provided across the SGA
space. This bill seeks to close that gap, while still respecting autonomy and nuances within each entity.
While on the mission of filling gaps, the gap of information that newly elected leadership receives from
their predecessor is solely dependent on that person’s willingness to cultivate a strong relationship with
them. We seek to codify the practice that all elected leaders should follow; assisting those who will
come after them. Lastly, the Professional Development clause in Chapter 207 is underutilized in the
status quo, which harms the SGA’s ability to produce well-rounded leaders throughout their time at
FSU. By reimagining what Professional Development can look like in the SGA space, we ensure that
this Senate, and the student body, continue to progress into the future.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Senate President, Senate President Pro Tempore, Office of Student Governance and Advocacy,
Student Body President, Student Body Treasurer, Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court, Chair of
the Union Board, Chair of the Campus Recreation Board, Class Council Presidents, Speaker of the
Congress of Graduate Students, Directors of Affiliated Projects, Funding Board Chairs, Student Body
Vice President, Student Body Attorney General, Senate Standing Committee Leadership, Senate
College Delegation Leadership, Executive Institute Directors, Homecoming Director.Docusign Envelope ID: 1E588EE1-E54C-80AD-83A6-D8A200F22D54

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation would reorganize the list and requirements for SGA entities regarding training. It would
create a requirement for transition documents to be gathered, kept, and transferred through the Office
of Student Governance and Advocacy after new leadership assumes office. It specifies requirements,
outside of New Senate Orientation, for Committee Leadership and College Delegation Leadership
training. It creates a mechanism for compliance through the Office of Student Governance and
Advocacy. It creates a running document, managed by an administrative officer within the Office of the
Student Body President, to inform SGA officeholders of on-campus, local, state, and national
opportunities for professional and leadership development.

Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 033
Primary Sponsor(s): Goldstein
Co-sponsor(s): Add any Co-Sponsors here
Short Title: The SGA External Transparency and Digital Records Act
Summary of Legislation:
This bill repeals and replaces Chapter 210 of the Student Body Statutes to establish the “SGA
Digital Records Act of 2025.” It creates comprehensive standards for publishing, preserving,
and managing all digital records, websites, and social media under SGA. It aims to strengthen
transparency, ensure compliance with public records laws, and safeguard institutional memory.
Background Information:
Chapter 210, first enacted as the SGA Website Act of 2007, no longer adequately addresses
modern digital operations, multi-platform communication, or compliance with Florida Sunshine
and SGA Public Records laws. As SGA has expanded its online presence, clearer standards
are needed for official records, archives, websites, and social media to avoid inconsistent
practices and data loss. This legislation was developed through review of current statutory
gaps. It also aligns with trends in peer institutions’ digital governance.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation will formally codify the platforms and standards for SGA websites,
CivicPlus, Municode, and official social media, defining publication timelines, branding
requirements, credential protocols, and enforcement mechanisms. It will enhance transparency
by requiring timely posting of records and protecting digital continuity during officer transitions,
with remedies for violations including judicial enforcement.

Short Title: Communications and Accessibility Regulation for Engagement Act.
Summary of Legislation:
This Bill would amend Chapter 210.3 of Student Body Statutes to add the use of accessibility features
in social media to better connect with the Student Body. The language is kept broad in order to not limit
what kind of social media accounts may be used or included in the future.
Background Information:
A vast majority of social media has developed accessibility features in order to be more inclusive.
These are options like adding close captioning for short video formats, and alternative text descriptions
for images. These features are often underutilized and create a gap in connecting to students that may
be visually impaired or hard of hearing.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Student Senate President, Student Government Press Secretary
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The legislation would lessen the gap between the disabled community that attends Florida State and its
Student Government by implementing the use of accessibility features on social media posts. The
language is kept broad in order to be applicable to a multitude of social media apps, and any new
accounts that may be created in the future.

Summary of Legislation:
This bill would amend Chapters 301.4, 816.10, and 1116.12, Student Body Statutes, following the
university-wide platform change from NoleCentral to FSU HQ on June 30th, 2026. The bill replaces two
mentions of “NoleCentral” with “the University-designated student organization management platform”,
eliminating the need for future statute updates regarding platform changes. This resolution would
resolve Section 4, Criteria for Evaluation of Funding Requests, Table #1: RSO Allocation Committee
Full Evaluation Rubric, Column 4, Row 1A, with the same changes, updating one instance of
“NoleCentral”. If the platform were to change from “FSU HQ” in the future, no additional statute
changes would be required due to this bill & resolution.

Beginning June 30, 2026, FSU HQ will replace NoleCentral. FSU HQ will become the new home
platform for student involvement opportunities, student events, registered student organizations and
pathways and badging for students enrolled at Tallahassee and Panama City campuses. With the new
platform, all instances of “NoleCentral” in student body statutes must be updated to reflect current
changes.

Andrew Johnson, Program Director, FSU Student Governance & Advocacy. Stormy McGivern,
Program Director, Academic & Student Services. Raeshawn Coonce, Student Program Coordinator,
Department of Student Engagement.

This bill keeps the Student Body Statutes up to date regardless of platform change, highlighting the

211.2 The Indigenous Land Acknowledgment Statement shall be as follows:
The Student Government of Florida State University acknowledges that it is located on
land that is the ancestral and traditional territory of the Apalachee Nation, the
Miccosukee Tribe of Florida, the Muscogee Creek Nation, and the Seminole Tribe of
Florida. We pay respect to their Elders past and present and extend that respect to their
descendants and to all Indigenous people. We recognize this land remains scarred by
the histories and ongoing legacies of settler colonial violence, dispossession, and
removal. In spite of all this, and with tremendous resilience, these Indigenous Nations
have remained deeply connected to this territory, to their families, to their communities,
and to their cultural ways of life. We recognize the ongoing relationships of care that
these Indigenous Nations maintain with this land and extend our gratitude as we live and
work as humble and respectful guests upon their territory. We encourage all to learn
about and educate others on the contemporary work of the Indigenous Nations whose
land we are on and to endeavor to support Indigenous sovereignty in all the ways that
we can.DocuSign Envelope ID: D9CB2406-CBFB-4F1B-9F52-750DA919894CDocuSign Envelope ID: CC567C7E-3BDD-437E-B225-32878B05FE40DocuSign Envelope ID: B582BA50-FFB4-4D13-A39B-1806C43DDB5D

300.4 Independent Executive Officers
All executive powers of the Student Body shall be vested in the President of the Student
Body, assisted by the Student Body Vice President, Student Body Treasurer, and such
administrative officers as the President shall appoint in accordance with the Constitution of
the Student Body and by Statute. The Student Body President shall hereinafter be referred
to as the President, the Student Body Vice President as the Vice President, and the Student
Body Treasurer as the Treasurer.
The President Shall:
A. Administer and enforce all laws of the Student Body.
B. Appoint Cabinet members as specified in the Statutes. Such appointments shall require a
majority vote of the Student Senate to be approved.
C. Have the power to veto or sign acts of the Student Senate, provided that such power is
exercised, within five (5) school days of its presentation to the Student Body President. A
veto may be overridden by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of not less than a quorum of the Student
Senate.
D. Call and preside over meetings of the Student Body.
E. Recommend legislation to the Student Senate.
F. Address the Student Senate at the beginning of each semester and at other times upon
invitation by the Student Senate.
G. Instruct and require reports from Cabinet members and approve all policies made from them.
H. Remove any officer who has been appointed to a position in the Executive Branch.
I. Have the power to call for a referendum subject to two-thirds (2/3) majority Student Senate
concurrence.
J. Represent the Student Body on the FSU Board of Trustees.
K. Prepare the budget of the Executive Branch with the assistance of the Treasurer.
L. Provide strategic oversight to the Executive Cabinet through the coordination of the Vice
President.
The Vice President shall:
A. Assume the duties of the President in the absence of the President or upon that individual’s
request.
B. Coordinate the efforts of the Cabinet and serve as coordinator for the formulation and
completion of Cabinet projects.
C. Coordinate with the Student Body President, Student Body Treasurer, and Executive
Cabinet to accomplish executive projects
D. Direct grievances and ideas to the proper functionary and see that the grievances and ideas
are acted upon.
E. Meet at least once a month with the directors of executive agencies, affiliated projects,
bureaus, and class councils to review performance, address questions and/or concerns,
receive feedback and/or advice on the functioning of the Executive Branch, and discuss
possibilities of new projects.
F. Serve as the vehicle throughout the Executive Branch to support programming events and
accomplish agency, bureau, and council projects

sections.heading: Page 1
sections.text:
300.6 Office of the Attorney General
A. The Student Body Attorney General shall hereinafter be referred to as, the Attorney
General.
B. The Office of the Attorney General is responsible for the enforcement of Student Body
Statutes and the Constitution of the Student Body as well as any rules and procedures
that govern a student or organization, provided such provisions fall within the jurisdiction
of the SGA.
C. The Attorney General shall be the head of the Office of the Attorney General.
D. The Attorney General shall serve at the pleasure of the Student Body President.
E. The Student Body President may assign other duties and responsibilities to the Office
of the Attorney General, so long as these do not violate the Student Body Statutes or the
Constitution of the Student Body.
F. When the position of Attorney General is vacated, the most senior deputy Attorney
General shall assume the position of Acting Attorney General.
1. The acting Attorney General shall serve as the Attorney General until a new
Attorney General is confirmed.
300.7 Powers and Responsibilities of the Office of the Attorney General
The Office of the Attorney General shall,
A. Investigate and/or initiate proceedings against any SGA funded RSO, Bureau,
Agency, Affiliated Project, funding board, member/entity of the executive branch, or
student, for violations of the Florida State University Student Body Statutes, Florida
State University Student Body Constitution, or any rules or procedures governing the
student or organization as it relates to SGA.
B. Launch an investigation into possible violations of these provisions.
C. Only initiate proceedings regarding a possible violation following an approved
investigation by either the Director of Student Governance and Advocacy or The Student
Body President.
D. If necessary, petition the Student Supreme Court to obtain records as may pertain to
any investigation, subject to applicable public records exemptions.
E. Recommend to the Senate potential changes to Statutes and the Constitution of the
Student Body.
F. Work with the Student Body President and their Cabinet to follow the proceedings of
both the Judicial and Legislative Branch, in order to keep the Student Body President
and their Cabinet knowledgeable on what is occurring in the other Branches and any
actions they may wish to take.

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
G. Provide counsel and represent the Executive Branch and members/entities of the
Executive Branch in all SGA legal proceedings heard before FSU authorities.
1. Any member/entity of the Executive Branch may choose to waive this
counsel and representation if they so desire.
2. If this counsel and representation is waived then, the member/entity
may choose to have other individuals or groups to counsel and
represent them.
H. Appoint a designee to represent the Executive Branch on behalf of the Office of the
Attorney General when so desired, with prior notice to the appropriate parties.
I. Work with the Student Body President to appoint at least one, but no more than two,
Deputy Attorneys General.
J. Assist in the creation and/or filing of executive orders at the request and approval of
the Student Body President.
K. Assist Executive Branch officers in understanding their roles, duties, and
responsibilities.
L. Create internal Rules and Procedures to help execute the duties and responsibilities
of the Office of the Attorney General, including, but not limited to, the parameters for
investigations and prosecutions. These Rules and Procedures shall be made available
to the public.
M. Render public memorandums on the activities of the Office of the Attorney General
including, but not limited to, investigations and/or proceedings made on behalf of the
Executive Branch.
N. Execute any other duties and responsibilities delegated to them as enumerated in the
Student Body Statutes.

Statute/Amendment Text
301.1
A. Authority
In accordance with the Student Body Constitution, there shall
be a cabinet in the Executive Branch to assist the
constitutional officers in the execution of their duties. The
Constitution delegates the authority to define the positions and
their duties to Statutes.
B. Purpose
The purpose of this chapter is to define and outline
the structure of the Executive Cabinet.
C. Composition
The Executive Cabinet shall be composed of the Executive
Office of the President, and the Advisory Cabinet. Only
members of the Executive Office of the President shall be
considered under the “cabinet officers” mantle of major
offices.
301.2 Definition
A. The Executive Office of the President: the vehicle through
which the Student Body President and Vice President
execute their constitutional powers and carry out their
administration's programs, projects, and agenda.
B. The Advisory Cabinet: the group that shall exist for the
purposes of coordination among executive branch
groups, projects, and offices, and to provide information
and assistance to the Student Body President and Vice
President.
301.3 Authority and duties of the Executive Office of the President
The Executive Office derives its authority from the Student Body
President and has no authorization, power, or authority to act
unless specifically granted by the Student Body President or Vice
President. It shall not have the authority to pass resolutions or
acts.
The Executive Office of the President shall have the following duties:
A. Assist the Student Body President and Vice President in
the execution of the plan for the Executive Branch.DocuSign Envelope ID: EA5E27F8-91DB-41BA-B660-A95168EF3076

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
B. Represent segments of student body quality of life in
accordance with the structure issued by the Student
Body President.
C. Fulfill the obligations of the job descriptions for each office.
D. Work for the improved quality of life of the student body.
E. The Executive Office of the President shall meet on a
regular basis no less than once every two weeks during
the fall, spring, and summer semesters. Minutes of these
meetings will be recorded and kept on record.
301.4 Membership
The Chief of Staff who is appointed by the Student Body President and
is subject to Student Senate confirmation, directs the activities of the
Executive Office, and is subject to the will of the Student Body
President.
The Student Body President has sole power of appointment within the
Executive Office and may dismiss any individual serving under them at their
discretion.
301.5 Organization and appointments of the Executive Office of the President
A. The Student Body President may organize the Executive
Office as deemed necessary and proper within the limits
imposed by the Student Body Statutes.
B. If a new Executive Office of the President position is
created, the Student Body President must notify, in
writing, the Student Senate of its creation.
C. Within two (2) weeks of inauguration, the Student Body
President, in consultation with the Student Body Vice
President, shall address the Student Senate and present the
plan for the organization of the Executive Office of the
President. Each position, whether created near the
inauguration or later in the term, must have a title and a
description not totaling fewer than fifty (50) words detailing the
responsibilities and privileges of the position. Such a plan must
be published on the Student Government Association Website.
D. All members of the Executive Office of the President must
be confirmed by the Student Senate as “Cabinet Offices”
and major level positions within the Executive Branch.
301.6 Composition of the Advisory Cabinet
The Advisory Cabinet shall be composed of ex-officio members including:DocuSign Envelope ID: EA5E27F8-91DB-41BA-B660-A95168EF3076

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
A. Agency, Bureau, and Affiliated Project Directors or Assistant
Directors to serve in the absence of the Directors.
B. The Senior Class Council
C. Any student organization by the Student Body President,
provided written notice is given to the Student Senate
President.
301.7 Advisory Cabinet duties and restrictions
A. The Advisory Cabinet shall not be permitted to pass
binding resolutions or legislation.
B. The Advisory Cabinet shall advise the Student Body
President and Vice President on general matters and
assist in the coordination of the Executive Branch.
C. The Advisory Cabinet shall meet as deemed necessary
by the Student Body President to discuss activities and
events of the Executive Branch for the purpose of
increasing the amount and level of cooperation and
interdependency and reducing duplication and wasted
effort.
D. The Advisory Cabinet shall pool wisdom and experience of
its members to suggest to the Student Body President and
Vice President methods to reduce waste in material and
time as well as to ensure the greatest impact for Executive
Branch projects.
E. When directed, the Advisory Council may assist the
Executive Office of the President.
F. When necessary, the Student Body President may hold a
meeting of just agency directors or bureau directors or
affiliated projects. However, meetings of the entire
Advisory Cabinet are preferable to individual meetings and
must occur as necessary.DocuSign Envelope ID: EA5E27F8-91DB-41BA-B660-A95168EF3076

Short Title: The REACH (Redefining External Affairs for Coordination and Harmony) Act
Summary of Legislation: This bill adds on to the Executive Departments Act by expanding on
the Department of External Affairs, including establishing and elaborating on its Office of
Governmental Affairs, Office of Public Relations, and Office of University Relations and their
positions and duties.
Background Information: This bill was made in consolidation with the Executive branch’s
goal of reworking SGA’s internal structure to make the executive branch more communicative
and connected. This includes restructuring bureaus into departments rather than keeping them
as floating entities with limited executive oversight. This bill is a product of the Structural
Reform Working Group within the Student Senate.
Effect of Proposed Legislation: This bill would formally establish the Office of Governmental
Affairs, Office of Public Relations, and Office of University Relations while elaborating on the
duties, structure, and responsibilities of the Department of External Affairs.

The REACH (Redefining External Affairs for Coordination and Harmony) Act

14 1. Creation and Purpose:
15 a. This act, as it relates to the establishment of the Department of External Affairs, its
16 duties, positions and goals, shall be called “Redefining External Affairs for Coordination
17 and Harmony Act”, hereinafter referred to as “The REACH Act”.
18 b. Purpose: To establish and define the Department of External Affairs in its entirety,
19 including the Office of Governmental Affairs, the Office of Public & Media Relations, and
20 the Office of University & Community Relations.
21 2. Definitions:
22 a. The Department of External Affairs (DEA): Serves as the official liaison between the
23 SGA and external stakeholders, including government entities, the University
24 administration, and the broader public. Comprising the Office of Governmental Affairs

28 body.
29 b. The Secretary of External Affairs: This role is responsible for overseeing all outward-
30 facing communications, advocacy efforts, and strategic relationships between SGA and
31 external stakeholders. This role ensures SGA maintains a strong presence within the
32 university and in the broader community and governmental affairs. The Secretary works
33 closely with the Student Body President to develop and execute high-level advocacy
34 strategies while supervising key personnel responsible for media relations, content
35 creation, and governmental outreach. They shall supervise all efforts related to
36 collaborative action with the Florida Student Association and the Florida Board of
37 Governors.
38 3. The Office of Governmental Affairs
39 a. Purpose:
40 (1) The Office of Governmental Affairs (OGA) is the official advocate for advancing
41 student interests in local, state, and federal government. The office promotes
42 civic engagement and public policy participation through initiatives such as voter
43 registration drives, student advocacy, testimony before legislative bodies, and
44 policy education. OGA provides training in advocacy skills, supports student
45 involvement in government internships, and works closely with the FSU Office of
46 Governmental Relations to coordinate events like FSU Day at the Capitol.
47 Additionally, OGA partners with student organizations to mobilize students
48 around key legislative and policy issues relevant to the student body.
49 b. Structure:
50 (1) OGA shall be structured as follows:
51 (A) Director of Governmental Affairs
52 a. This role manages student government advocacy and policy
53 initiatives by coordinating lobbying efforts and serving as the
54 primary liaison with institutional and governmental bodies at the
55 local, state, and federal levels.
56 (2) The structure of OGA shall be further defined by policy in accordance with
57 Chapter 301.4.c.
58 c. Noles Engaged in Politics:
59 (1) The Noles Engaged in Politics (NEP) Program is a professional development
60 initiative under OGA. Its primary purpose is to engage and educate students on
61 political systems, current issues affecting the state of Florida and higher
62 education, and to provide leadership and mentorship opportunities in preparation
63 for FSU Day at the Capitol.
64 (2) Participation in the NEP Program is open to all FSU students who demonstrate a
65 commitment to civic engagement and public service. The selection process shall
66 be conducted by OGA leadership.
67 d. The Student Body Legislative Agenda:
68 (1) Authority & Purpose
69 (A) The OGA shall have the authority to create and advocate for a legislative
70 agenda representing the interests of the FSU student body at the local,Docusign Envelope ID: 829ED7B5-F98C-4C27-82C0-7EC327A88AE0

72 legislative stances aligned with student needs and the current
73 administration’s goals.

75 (A) OGA may draft and submit policy proposals for consideration by
76 legislative bodies. To inform priorities, OGA should engage in outreach to
77 solicit student input. While student feedback should be considered, it is

100 (A) Following lobbying efforts, OGA shall deliver a report to the Senate

109 initiatives, impact, and services to the FSU community and beyond. It works to
110 maintain transparency, enhance visibility of SGA actions, and foster trust
111 between SGA and the student body.

Short Title:
Amending Chapters 301.4, 816.10, and 1116.12, Student Body Statutes, and resolving
RSOAC Section 4 of rules and procedures, replacing all instances of “NoleCentral” with “the
University-designated student organization management platform”.
Summary of Legislation:
This bill would amend Chapters 301.4, 816.10, and 1116.12, Student Body Statutes, following the
university-wide platform change from NoleCentral to FSU HQ on June 30th, 2026. The bill replaces two
mentions of “NoleCentral” with “the University-designated student organization management platform”,
eliminating the need for future statute updates regarding platform changes. This resolution would
resolve Section 4, Criteria for Evaluation of Funding Requests, Table #1: RSO Allocation Committee
Full Evaluation Rubric, Column 4, Row 1A, with the same changes, updating one instance of
“NoleCentral”. If the platform were to change from “FSU HQ” in the future, no additional statute
changes would be required due to this bill & resolution.
Background Information: tgh
Beginning June 30, 2026, FSU HQ will replace NoleCentral. FSU HQ will become the new home
platform for student involvement opportunities, student events, registered student organizations and
pathways and badging for students enrolled at Tallahassee and Panama City campuses. With the new
platform, all instances of “NoleCentral” in student body statutes must be updated to reflect current
changes.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Andrew Johnson, Program Director, FSU Student Governance & Advocacy. Stormy McGivern,
Program Director, Academic & Student Services. Raeshawn Coonce, Student Program Coordinator,
Department of Student Engagement.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This bill keeps the Student Body Statutes up to date regardless of platform change, highlighting the
example of the current change of “NoleCentral” to “FSU HQ” and taking into account any future
platform changes.Docusign Envelope ID: 1099CFFD-E77B-869C-8317-DB55E8B6E306

Chapter 302 Class Councils
302.1 Title
This act shall be entitled "The Class Council Act of 2014." The Senior Class Council.
Junior Class Council. and Sophomore Class Council shall be hereinafter be referred to
as the SrCC . JCC .. and SoCC respectively.
302.2 The Class Councils fGG) shall work to instill unity in the Florida State
University's Senior. Junior. and. Sophomore classes to enhance their college
experience and encourage active participation in the Florida State community as both
students and alumnus.
302.3 Membership
A. Senior Class Council
1. The President. Vice President. Treasurer and Secretary
of the Senior Class shall be officers of the SrCC
a. The President. Vice President. Treasurer. and
Secretary shall have at least 72 semester credit
hours by the semester they run for office.
b. The President. Vice President. Treasurer. and
Secretary shall be elected in the Spring Student Government
Association elections as stipulated in Chapter 705.1 of the FSU
Student Body Statutes.
c. All officers of the SrCC are to be enrolled as undergraduate
students at Florida State University for the entire designated term
of service.
2. There shall be at least five (5) members-at-large of the Senior Class
selected by the President of the Senior Class with the majority approval
of the remaining officers of the SrCC. This selection process shall be
completed within 60 days of the-SrCC inauguration.
B. Junior Class Council
1. The President. Vice President. Treasurer. and Secretary shall be
officers of the JCC.

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
a. The President. Vice President. Treasurer. and Secretary shall
have at least 42 semester credit hours by the semester they run
for office and must have been enrolled in FSU for one year.
b. The President. Vice President. Treasurer. and Secretary shall
be appointed through the application process as stated in Chapter
302.4 B following the Spring Student Government Association
elections.
c. All officers of the JCC are to be enrolled as undergraduate
students at Florida State University for the entire designation of
their term of service.
2. There shall be up to ten (1 0) members-at-large of the Junior Class
selected by the President of the Junior Class with the majority approval of
the remaining officers JCC. this selection process shall be completed by
the first week of classes for Summer Session A.
C. Sophomore Class Council
1. The President. Vice President. Treasurer. and Secretary shall be
officers of the SoCC.
a. The President. Vice President. Treasurer. and Secretary shall
have at least 12 semester credit hours by the semester they run
for office.
b. The President. Vice President. Treasurer. and Secretary shall
be appointed through the application process as stated in Chapter
302.4 C following the Spring Student Government Association
elections.
c. All officers of the SoCC are to be enrolled as undergraduate
students at Florida State University for the entire designation of
their term of service.
2. There shall be up to ten (1 0) members-at-large of the Sophomore
Class selected by the President of the Sophomore Class with the majority
approval of the remaining officers SoC C. this selection process shall be
completed no later than the last week of classes for Summer Session A.

L 302.4 Selection & Terms of Office
A. Senior Class Council
1. All applications to run for the SrCC will follow the deadlines pursuant to
Student Body Statutes Chapter 705.3
2. The members of the SrCC shall hold office from the time of their
appointment until the end of the Spring Semester one year from the start
of their term. The members of the SrCC shall fundraise and represent the
respective graduating classes encompassed within their term (Summer.
Fall. and Spring).
B. Junior Class Council
1. All applications for the JCC must be publicly released within five (5)
business days after the Spring Student Government Association election.
Completed applications must be received by the newly elected SrCC no
later than 5pm ten (10) business days after the applications are released.
The deadline for applications may be postponed. for up to one week
under extreme circumstances.
2.The members of the JCC shall hold office from the time of their
appointment until the end of the Spring Semester one year from the start
of their term. The members of the JCC shall fundraise and represent the
respective upcoming graduating classes encompassed within their term
(Summer. Fall. and Spring).
3. Selection
a. Once the incoming Senior Class has been elected they may.
with the Advisor for the Class Councils and the Student Body Vice
President Elect. begin conducting interviews for the positions of
President and Vice President.
b. Once the incoming SrCC has been inaugurated. they must.
within ten (1 0) business days. submit their nominations for the
positions of President and Vice President to the Student Body
President and Chief of Staff for appointment. with confirmation by
the Student Senate.

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
c. Interviews for the positions of Secretary and Treasurer will be
held by the newly appointed President and Vice President of the
Junior Class and the Advisor of the Class Councils.
d. Once the President and Vice President have been confirmed
they shall appoint the Treasurer and the Secretary.
C. Sophomore Class Council
1. All applications for the SoCC must be publicly released within five (5)
business days after the Spring Student Government Association election.
Completed applications must be received by the newly elected SrCC no
later than 5pm ten (1 0) business days after the applications are released.
The deadline for applications may be postponed. for up to one week
under extreme circumstances.
2. The members of the SoCC shall hold office from the time of their
appointment until the end of the Spring Semester one year from the start
of their term. The members of the SoCC shall fundraise and represent
the respective upcoming graduating classes encompassed within their
term (Summer. Fall. and Spring).
3. Selection
a. Once the incoming Senior Class has been elected they may.
with the Advisor for the Class Councils and the Student Body Vice
President Elect. begin conducting interviews for the positions of
President and Vice President.
b. Once the incoming SrCC has been inaugurated. they must.
within ten (1 0) business days. submit their nominations for the
positions of President and Vice President to the Student Body
President and Chief of Staff for appointment. with confirmation by
the Student Senate.
c. Interviews for the positions of Secretary and Treasurer will be
held by the newly appointed President and Vice President of the
Junior Class. the Advisor of the Class Councils. and the Senior

d. Once the President and Vice President have been confirmed

A. Senior Class Council
1. The SrCC shall strive to keep all Seniors informed and apprised of all
graduation requirements and deadlines.
2 The SrCC shall raise funds for the Senior Class gift.
A. The SrCC shall provide programming to build community and pride for

302.5 Duties and Responsibilities of the Class Councils
A. Senior Class Council
1. The SrCC shall strive to keep all Seniors informed and apprised of all
graduation requirements and deadlines.
2. The SrCC shall raise funds for the Senior Class gift.
3. The SrCC shall provide programming to build community and pride for
graduating year and/or benefit of the members of the Senior Class.
4. The SrCC shall meet at least twice a month.
5. The SrCC shall provide guidance and information to the Junior and
Sophomore Class Councils and students of the university who are
interested in being a part of the entity
6. The SrCC shall work with the Homecoming Executive Council to choose
and present a gift on behalf of their class to the President of Florida State
University during the Homecoming Faculty and Staff reception in the Fall.
7. The SrCC shall send one of their officers to give monthly updates to the
Student Senate about the current projects and upcoming goals of the
SoCC, JCC, and SrCC.DocuSign Envelope ID: 0FCDE2A0-EE47-4BC4-A41F-FABDD3C81377

BE IT ENACTED BY THE SEVENTY FOURTH STUDENT SENATE THAT:
A revision is made to the Student Body Statutes 302.3, 302.4, 302.5, 302.7 (See attached).

issues includes references to incorrect statutes, general legislative vagueness, conflation of an
