AN ACT
Updating the Registered Student Organization Allocation Committee
1 Be it enacted by the 77th Student Senate at Florida State University that:
2 Section 1. Amendment to Student Body Statutes Chapter 816, "RSO Allocation Committee"
3 Chapter 816, Florida State University Student Body Statutes, is hereby amended and shall read as
4 follows:
5 1. Purpose
6 The Registered Student Organization Allocation Committee (RSOAC) shall be responsible for
7 reviewing and recommending funding allocations in support of Registered Student Organizations
8 (RSOs) that meet established eligibility requirements. This program is designed to assist RSOs in
9 carrying out their missions and enhancing campus life through student-led programming, events, travel
10 opportunities, and other initiatives. Funding is available on a first-come, first-served basis and is
11 contingent upon the availability of funds. The RSOAC shall be recognized as a Funding Board of the
12 Student Senate and shall be considered a entity of the Senate solely for purposes of administrative
13 function, including but not limited to Senate Leadership oversight, the ability of Senate Leadership to
14 attend meetings as voting ex officio, attendance and meeting minutes, and other related procedural or
15 administrative matters.
16 2. Committee Structure
17 a. The RSOAC shall be comprised of seventeen (17) fifteen (15) voting student members:
18 1. The Chair and Vice Chair of the Student Senate Finance Committee;
19 2. Two (2) additional Senators appointed by the Student Senate President;
20 3. Five (5) students-at-large elected during the Fall SGA elections, pursuant to
21 Section 13 of this Chapter;
22 4. Three (3) Two (2) students-at-large designated by the Student Body President;

50 the Student Body Treasurer, as required by Section 11 of this Chapter, in order
51 to understand past performance, challenges, and recommendations for program
52 improvement.
53 h. Transitional Appointments Prior to the Fall 78th Student Senate Inauguration
54 1. Purpose and Scope
55 (1) To ensure the RSO Allocation Committee is able to begin operations in
56 accordance with this Chapter prior to the full seating of the 78th Student
57 Senate, a one-time transitional appointment process is authorized for Fall
58 2025. The goal of this transitional process is to convene the committee's
59 first meeting during Week One of the Fall Semester in order to establish
60 leadership, confirm logistics, and prepare for the semester's funding
61 responsibilities.

199 5. Funding Recommendation Process
200 a. The Student Senate shall retain final authority over the approval of all RSOAC funding
201 recommendations.
202 b. Funding recommendations made by the RSO Allocation Committee shall be transmitted
203 to the Student Senate in the form of an allocation resolution sponsored by the sponsored
204 by the Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee, and co-sponsored by the Chair and Vice
205 Chair of the Senate Finance Committee, and co-sponsored by any Senators serving on
206 the RSOAC.
207 c. Allocation Resolutions must be submitted by the Finance Committee Chair Chair of the
208 RSO Allocation Committee via the Senate Legislation Submission form no later than
209 11:59 PM (midnight) on the Friday following the Thursday RSOAC meeting, to be
210 included on the next week’s Senate agenda with all other legislation.
211 d. Funding resolutions Allocation Resolutions shall be placed on the agenda for the
212 following Wednesday Senate meeting. The Senate President shall have the discretion to
213 place these resolutions on either the Consent portion or the Second Reading portion of
214 the agenda.
215 e. If the Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee is absent from the Senate Meeting The the
216 Chair and Vice Chair of the Senate Finance Committee shall present the funding
217 resolutions to the Senate. The Vice Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee must be
218 present at any Senate meeting in which a recommendation from the committee is
219 considered, in order to answer any questions from the Senate.
220 f. Before any allocation resolution may be amended, a motion to open the allocation
221 resolution must be made and unanimous agreement, which shall be
222 followed by an opening and debate. Upon adoption of such motion by a two-thirds (2/3
223 roll-call vote, individual amendments may then be entertained. Each amendment shall
224 require a separate motion, debate, and two-thirds roll-call vote. The Student Senate may
225 amend recommendations made by the committee at its discretion, which shall require a
226 two-thirds (2/3) roll-call vote. However, the Student Senate shall not increase funding for
227 any Registered Student Organization that the RSO Allocation Committee voted to
228 recommend zero funding for.
229 1. All adopted amendments must be documented and emailed to the Senate Clerk,

254 7. Funding Guidelines and Restrictions
255 a. All requests must be for eligible uses of Student Activity & Service Fee revenues, as
256 provided in the SGA Financial Manual.
257 b. The Student Body Treasurer shall coordinate with the Department of Student
258 Engagement to establish an online system for submitting funding requests.
259 c. Funding requests shall generally be required to include a description of the intended use
260 of funds and why the requested funding is needed. Student organizations shall be
261 required to provide an estimate of the number of FSU students that are likely to attend
262 an event or travel opportunity funded by SGA.
263 d. Pursuant to §1009.24, Florida Statutes, SGA funding may only be used to benefit the
264 student body in general. As such, funding from the RSO Allocation Committee may not
265 benefit activities for which an admission fee is charged to students. Further, student
266 organizations that charge membership fees may not exclude any student from
267 participation in any events or programs funded by SGA as a result of a student’s inability
268 to pay such fees.
269 e. Funds may not be used to cover membership dues or fees associated with a student’s or
270 organization’s national or international affiliations.
271 f. The committee shall not recommend funding for events or programs that are likely to
272 have only group members attend and/or have no general benefit to the student body.
273 g. The committee shall not recommend funding for events that are exclusive to a club or
274 organization’s executive board. This restriction may be waived by a three-fourths (3/4)
275 vote of the committee and a three-fourths (3/4) vote of the Student Senate, which must
276 be a roll call vote.
277 h. Requests for clothing may only be approved once per fiscal year. Any clothing funded by
278 SGA must directly promote the student organization.
279 i. Organizations seeking funding for service trips must first demonstrate that they made a
280 good-faith effort to participate in an open or public service opportunity offered by the
281 Center for Leadership and Service, if such an opportunity was available. If participation
282 in such a trip was not feasible due to scheduling, availability, or capacity, theDocusign Envelope ID: DA749738-5F11-4EB4-9252-E3DBA0849FF4

333 10. Post-Award Requirements
334 a. All events funded by SGA must be publicly advertised on NoleCentral in a manner
335 visible to the general student body. This shall serve as the baseline standard for public
336 advertisement. Additional promotion through means such as social media, digital
337 signage, newsletters, or tabling is encouraged but not required.
338 b. Any events, programs, travel, or other activities supported by SGA funding must comply
339 with the FSU Student Organization Conduct Code as well as all federal, state, and local
340 laws.
341 c. Every organization receiving funding from SGA must submit a post event evaluation
342 form, along with receipts for any purchases made, to the SGA Accounting Office, within
343 ten (10) business days following the event.
344 d. If the requirements above are not followed by an organization, they shall be barred from
requesting any further funding until their post-award violations are rectified with SGA
accounting.
345 11. Annual Review Requirement
346 a. No later than the end of the Fall semester each year, the Student Body Treasurer shall
347 conduct an evaluation of the RSOAC program. This review shall assess the overall
348 effectiveness of the program and identify any areas for potential improvement.
349 b. The evaluation shall include:
350 1. The number and nature of instances in which standard funding rules or limits
351 were waived;
352 2. An analysis of how such waivers impacted student organizations and the broader
353 student body;
354 3. The adequacy of the current funding level for the program; and
355 4. Recommendations for enhancing the program’s structure, parameters, and
356 allocation limits.Docusign Envelope ID: DA749738-5F11-4EB4-9252-E3DBA0849FF4

Senate Bill #: 010
Primary Sponsor(s): Bigenho
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: Amending Chapter 401 and Chapter 402, Student Body Statutes, to Clarify Forms
of Legislation and Approval Procedures
Summary of Legislation:
This bill amends Chapter 401, “Forms of Legislation,” to clearly define the purpose, voting
thresholds, sponsorship requirements, and enacting clauses for Bills, Resolutions, Allocation
Resolutions, Proclamations, and Constitutional Amendments. The legislation also amends
Chapter 402, “Procedure for Approval of Bills,” to clarify submission timelines, veto
procedures, and approval processes involving the Student Body President and Vice President
for Student Affairs. Collectively, these changes modernize statutory language, remove
ambiguities, and improve procedural transparency within the Student Senate.
Background Information:
Chapter 401 of the Student Body Statutes currently outlines the various forms of legislation
available to the Student Senate; however, inconsistencies in language, overlapping definitions,
and procedural ambiguities have created confusion regarding appropriate usage, voting
thresholds, and sponsorship authority. In particular, the distinction between Resolutions and
Proclamations has lacked clarity, especially concerning commendations, condemnations, and
formal expressions of Senate opinion. Chapter 402, governing the approval and veto process
for bills, similarly benefits from clarification regarding transmission deadlines and DocuSign
procedures,. As Senate operations continue to evolve, codifying these procedures in a clearer
and more comprehensive manner promotes institutional continuity, ensures compliance with
University regulations, and strengthens transparency for Senators, SGA officers, and the
broader student body.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This legislation was drafted in collaboration with Senate Leadership and the Senate Rules and
Procedures Working Group.

Short Title: Legislative Enrollment Act
Summary of Legislation:
This bill amends Chapter 401.7 of the Student Body Statutes by removing the requirement that the
Student Senate President Pro Tempore sign enrolled copies of legislation in a ministerial capacity.
Under this legislation, enrolled copies would instead require only the signature of the Student Senate
President before proceeding to the enrollment process.
Background Information:
The current language of Chapter 401.7 requires both the Senate President and Senate President Pro
Tempore to sign enrolled legislation following Senate approval. Since both officers serve largely
ministerial rolls in this process, requiring two Senate officer signatures can create unnecessary
procedural redundancy within the legislative enrollment process.
The amendment is intended to streamline internal Senate procedures while preserving the Senate
President’s authority to certify legislation passed by the Student Senate. The proposed changes aim to
improve efficiency in the enrollment process without altering the substantive review and approval
structure for legislation.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
The Student Senate President was consulted regarding the proposed amendment and its effect. SG&A
was consulted regarding the proposed amendment and in favor of the change. The Student Senate
President Pro Tempore was also notified of the proposed changes. Discussion centered on the
administrative nature of the enrollment process and whether the existing dual-signature requirement
remains necessary to ensure proper certification of Senate-approved legislation.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The proposed legislation would simplify the enrollment process for Student Senate legislation by
removing redundant signature requirements for the Student Senate President Pro Tempore. This
change is expected to improve efficiency and reduce administrative obstacles while maintaining proper
oversight of Senate-approved legislation.Docusign Envelope ID: 7E6E997E-C41A-8E1F-80C1-45528830AF5F

Statute/Amendment Text:
402.2 Veto and Veto Amendment Process
A. Upon presentation of a bill, the Student Body President shall have five (5) school
days to approve or veto the legislation. If no action is taken within the five (5) day
limit, then the bill shall be treated as approved by the Student Body President.
This five (5) day limit shall begin on the first school day after the Bill is passed by
the Student Senate received by the Student Body President via email. If
approved, the The Student Body President shall then submit the bill to the Vice
President for Student Affairs for consideration. Attorney General. The Attorney
General shall refer approved bills to the Vice President for Student Affairs within
three (3) school days of receipt. In the absence of an Attorney General, the
Student Body President shall be responsible for referring approved bills to the
Vice President for Student Affairs.
B. The Student Body President must submit written justification/reasoning to the
Student Senate, within the five (5) day limit, of receipt to sustain any veto of
legislation. The Student Body President or a designee must also deliver an oral
justification to the Student Senate for the reason for the veto(es) within two (2)
Senate meetings. The copy of the President’s justification/reasoning for the
veto(es) must be e-mailed from the Student Body President to the Senate
President so that the Senate President may e-mail distribute it to all Senators at
least 48 hours prior to the President’s oral justification to the Senate. The Senate
President must send the originally vetoed bill to all Senators. If the Vice President
for Student Affairs vetoes a bill, it is suggested that they send a request be
submitted to submit that individual requesting an email notification/reasoning of
the veto to the Senate President. If this occurs, a copy of the emailed
justification/reasoning must be emailed distributed to all Senators.
C. Bills not acted upon within ten (10) school days after being received by the Vice
President for Student Affairs shall be treated as approved unless the Student
Body President, Senate President and Student Body Attorney General are notified
by the Vice President for Student Affairs within the ten (10) day limit as to why the
bill will not be acted upon within that limit and when action will be taken. Bills not
acted upon within eighteen (18) school days after being passed by the Student
Senate shall be treated as approved. The provisions of Subsection 402.2 (C) shall
not apply to the annual A&S budget bill, which shall be governed by Chapter
416.3.
D. If a vetoed bill from either the Student Body President or Vice President for
Student Affairs is amended on the floor of the Senate during the reconsideration
of the bill, that bill will be considered new legislation and be resubmitted to the
Student Body President and Vice President for Student Affairs for approval or
veto, all preceding statutes on time constraints to bill consideration applying.
E. If a presidential veto is overridden, that bill shall then go directly to the desk of the
Vice President for Student Affairs for consideration as soon as possible; the
preceding statutes on time constraints to the bill consideration applying again
upon presentation the following school day.DocuSign Envelope ID: EC4E8344-6491-44C7-88E6-8071B83BD42D

F. Chapter 402.2 shall nullify and supersede any conflicting statute or rule.
Chapter 416 Annual Budget Procedures Act of 2016 (updated)
416.1 Purpose
This act is to establish a procedure by which the annual Activity and Service Fee
(A&S) Budget of the Student Senate is produced and passed.
416.2 Scope
The Annual A&S Fee Budget hereby referred to as the Budget shall be passed in
compliance with the provisions of this act and all applicable provisions within the
State of Florida Administrative Code. No exceptions are authorized other than
those specified within.
416.3 Procedures for Passage of the Budget
A. The Budget shall not be approved by the Student Senate in a Summer
Session.
B. An estimated amount of the Budget shall be used to submit to the Senate
President for First Reading by the Chair of the Budget Committee. After
which, hearings shall be held and operated at the discretion of the Chair of
the Budget Committee.
1. Each prospective recipient of monies from the Budget shall make a
budget request. The Budget Committee shall hold hearings during
which budget requests are defended. Each prospective recipient of
the Budget shall have a separate hearing.
2. The hearings shall be administered by the Chair of the Budget
Committee and shall require a minimum of three (3) Senators. The
Budget Committee will in good faith obtain quorum.
3. The Budget Committee shall have the authority to deliberate
monies to requesting and non-requesting prospective recipients.
The Budget Committee shall also be authorized to deliberate more
or less than the amount requested.
C. When the Budget has been deliberated and approved in whole by the
Budget Committee it will be heard on Second Reading. All Senators shall
be presented copies of the proposed allocations. The Budget shall be on
the calendar for second reading for a minimum of five (5) business days
with proposed allocations before passage. The budget and proviso must
properly be advertised on the Student Government website while on
Second Reading.
D. The Budget shall be approved by the Senate before the beginning of the
fiscal year of which it affects. The Chair of the Budget Committee shall
make a good faith effort to complete the Budget no later than October 31
of each year.DocuSign Envelope ID: EC4E8344-6491-44C7-88E6-8071B83BD42D

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
E. The Budget and Proviso language cannot be approved separately.
Changes to the Proviso language may be made via resolution at any point
before the Budget is approved by the Board of Trustees. This resolution
shall be passed with a two- thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate.
F. Amendments to the Budget, on the Senate floor, must follow a majority
vote to unlock a specific line item and category of the Budget or a line of
the Proviso language. Any amendment that affects the allocation amount
in any line of any recipient shall require a three-fourth (3/4) vote of the
Senate.
1. Amendments may only be made to a specific category of one
recipient.
G. Hearings, deliberations, and meetings of the Budget Committee are public
and shall be advertised in the Senate. The Chair of the Budget Committee
shall not exclude any student from witnessing the hearings or deliberations
in accordance with Chapter 409 of the Student Body Statutes.
H. The Budget shall be passed by a roll-call vote. A simple majority is
required for passage.
I. If the Budget is failed in Senate, the Budget Committee shall create a new
budget in due time, following the guidelines in these statutes.
J. The University President or their designee shall retain line-item veto power
over the budget bill and have fifteen (15) school days from the date of
presentation of the budget to act on the allocation and expenditure
recommendations, which shall be deemed approved if no action is taken
within the 15 school day limit.
1. If any line item or portion within the budget is vetoed by the
University President or their designee, the Student Senate shall,
within fifteen (15) school days, make new budget recommendations
for expenditure of the vetoed portion of the bill. These new
recommendations shall be made in the form of a new bill, which
shall be deliberated by the Budget committee without the need for
new budget request hearings.
2. If the University President or their designee, vetoes any line
item or portion thereof within the new budget revisions, the
University President, or their designee, may reallocate by line item
that vetoed portion to bond obligations guaranteed by Activity and
Service fees pursuant to F.S.1010.62.
3. The University President or their designee, may also veto the
budget bill in its entirety, in which case the Budget Committee shall
create a new budget in due time, following the guidelines in these
statutes.DocuSign Envelope ID: EC4E8344-6491-44C7-88E6-8071B83BD42D

Senate President to ensure the creation and publication of this newsletter. +Ats

Chapter 411 Senator's Committee Rights
411 .1 The Standing Committees of the Senate shall be: Budget, Finance, Judiciary,
Student Affairs Student Life and Academic Affairs, Internal Affairs, and Rules
and Calendar.
Chapter 418 The Senate Projects Account
A. Purpose
The purpose of the Senate projects account is to create an account of the Senate of
the student body from which initiatives of said branch may be funded.
B. Guidelines
1: The Senate Projects account should be used to fund oow projects that would
further the image of Student Government Association to the Florida State
University student body, provide oow services or opportunities to students, or to
fulfill an observed need on campus. During Summer Session RSOs requesting
funds out of PAC & RTAC to be used after July 1 shall go directly to the Student
Senate to ask for money out of Senate Projects.
C. Process
1. Funds from the Senate Projects Account shall be allocated via a transfer bill.
£. Before the next Senate meeting the Student Life and Academic Affairs
Committee is required to meet before the Budget comm ittee.
3. The transfer bill shall go to the Student Life and Academic Affairs Committee in
order to determine the impact the project has on the academic experience
and/or welfare of the student body.
4 . Upon passage of the bill by the Student Life and Academic Affairs, the Budget
Committee shall determine the fiscal aspect of the bill.

sections.text:
A. Senate members shall take office upon inauguration.
B. Senators shall terminate office when one of the following circumstances occurs:
1. At the inauguration of their successors.
2. If occupying an upper-division seat, and changing their major, or field of study, would change
their division classification.
3. Upon their graduation, be it at either the undergraduate or graduate classification.
a. An exception to this applies when the Senator graduating with their undergraduate degree will
be enrolled as a graduate student in the same academic division, and will be permitted a
“Leave of Absence” for any Summer or Winter break between their graduation as an
undergraduate and enrollment as a graduate student
4. If they are no longer an enrolled student at Florida State University.
a. An exception to this applies where an official “Leave of Absence” has been granted for the
summer session, pursuant to Chapter 100.6.
C. Installation of Senators shall occur at the inauguration ceremony for the term that they are
elected. Any Senators not formally sworn in at inauguration shall be sworn in at the next
available Senate meeting.
D. All Senators enrolled as students during any of the summer academic terms shall be members
of the summer meetings upon fulfillment of the following requirements.
1. Senators must file a notice of intent with the Senate President two (2) weeks prior to the last
Student Senate meeting of the Spring semester. At the discretion of the Student Senate
President or by a majority vote of Senate, the Senate may accept a late notice of intent. If a
notice of intent is not provided or not accepted according to this rule, the Senator's seat shall
be considered vacant and available for appointment for the entire summer.
2. This notice of intent must include the dates which the Senator intends to serve during the
summer session.
E. The number of Senators available to serve during any summer term shall at no point fall below
thirty (30). Should occasion arise wherein there are fewer than thirty available serving
Senators, the Student Body President shall make appointments to maintain a total of thirty
(30) Senators. In this case Senate and its committees may meet for the sole purpose of voting
on new Senators even if there are less than 5 voting members in each standing committee.
F. Appointed Summer Senators shall be on notice that their duties are of a temporary nature.
Their term of office shall be terminated upon the return of the absent Senator, whose seat the
appointee is occupying.
G. Senators, by virtue of their office and the public trust, may not apply to be appointed to any
vacated Seat within the Student Senate. Additionally, upon resignation or removal from their
Seat, no former Senator may apply to be appointed to any vacated Seat within the Student
Senate apportioned for the opposite semester from the seat which they originally held until
after the said opposite semesters elections are completed and certified, but shall always be
permitted to run in said election.

405.4 Impeachment Proceedings
A. Impeachment of a student body officer shall require a majority vote of the Student
Senate Judiciary Committee followed by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the full Senate.
B. Before the Senate Judiciary Committee votes to initiate impeachment proceedings, the
committee must notify the accused officer via the official's FSU email address, at least
one week prior to the impeachment hearing. Such notification shall also include the time,
date, and place of the Judiciary Committee hearing pertaining to the impeachment
proceedings. The accused shall have the right to speak in their defense at the hearing,
to refuse to appear, to remain silent, and to refer to counsel at any time. At the
conclusion of the hearing, the committee shall openly deliberate and then vote by open
ballot on whether or not to recommend impeachment to the full Senate.
C. If the Judiciary Committee votes to recommend impeachment, the impeachment charge
shall be brought before the Student Senate at the next scheduled Senate session and
presented for a vote at that session.
D. The full Student Senate shall determine its own rules of procedure oonoerning any oases
of impeachment, however, the proceedings must oonolude with a vote by open ballot on
whether or not to formally impeach the aooused officer.
D. The officer considered for impeachment shall have 5 minutes to speak in their defense.
This time may be split between an opening statement and a closing statement. Following
the opening statement of the accused, the Senate shall openly deliberate until a motion is
made to vote on the candidate for impeachment. The accused will then have the option to
make a closing statement. only if there is time yielded from the opening statement. The
Senate will then vote by open ballot on whether or not to formally impeach the accused
officer.

405.5 Removal from Office
A. Upon impeachment of a Student Body Officer, the President of the Senate
shall deliver to the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, within three (3) days,
the Articles of Impeachment.
B. The Senate Judiciary Committee shall elect a Senator by majority vote to act
as Special Prosecutor to present the Student Senate’s case to the Supreme
Court. This Senator must be a member of the Judiciary Committee, as they
are the most involved in the impeachment proceedings and can therefore
present the most informed case for impeachment to the Supreme Court.
1. The Special Prosecutor may appoint, at their discretion, Assistant
Special Prosecutors to serve at the pleasure of the Special Prosecutor
through the duration of the impeachment proceedings. Any member
of the Florida State University Student Body who is in good academic
standing and without any active conduct sanctions may be appointed
as an Assistant Special Prosecutor.
C. The Student Supreme Court shall have sole jurisdiction over cases involving
removal of any officer of the Student Body impeached by the Student Senate.
In the case of Supreme Court Justices being impeached, temporary justices
shall be appointed pursuant to Article VII, Section 4 B, of the Student Body
Constitution.
1. Any officer who is impeached by the Senate shall be suspended from
office until a decision is reached by the Student Supreme Court.
Suspension is defined as the temporary loss of all rights and privileges
of office.
D. The impeached officer shall be removed upon conviction by a majority vote of
the justices. If the Student Supreme Court fails to convict the impeached
officer, this individual shall be declared not guilty and shall be reinstated to
office immediately.
E. The President of the Student Body may remove, at their discretion, any officer
who has been appointed to a position in the Executive Branch.
F. Any officer of the Student Body may resign at any time. Such resignations
must be in writing and delivered to the head of the officer’s respective branch.
G. Any elected or appointed Student Government Officer who has been
disciplined, suspended, or removed from office shall have the right to directly
appeal such decision to the Vice President of Student Affairs or another
senior university administrator designated to hear such appeals. The exercise
of such right and its resulting decision shall not be construed as to condition
precedent on any student panel.DocuSign Envelope ID: 009F2636-8CC1-45E6-976C-3B07B390E14E

Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 011
Primary Sponsor(s): Larossi
Co-sponsor(s): Holliday
Short Title: Specifying Florida Statute 1004.26 in Chapter 405: Impeachment And Removal
From Office
Summary of Legislation:
This bill would amend the Student Body Statues Chapter 405, “Impeachment And Removal
From Office”. This bill clarifies the jurisdiction and procedures for impeachment, suspension,
removal, resignation, and appeal of Student Government officers and guarantees officers the
right to appeal disciplinary actions to the Vice President of Student Affairs or a designated
senior administrator pursuant to Florida Statute 1004.26(4)(d).
Background Information:
This bill was requested to be adopted by the FSU General Council as it not a SGA policy, but a
State of Florida Law.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
The FSU General Council, Senate President Holliday, Student Governance & Advocacy
Advising Staff.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This provision establishes a formal right of appeal for any elected or appointed Student
Government officer who has been disciplined, suspended, or removed from office. It allows the
officer to directly appeal the decision to the Vice President of Student Affairs or another
designated senior university administrator pursuant to Florida Statute 1004.26(4)(d). The
legislation further clarifies that exercising this right to appeal, and any resulting administrative
decision, does not serve as a condition precedent to or override the authority of any Student
Government judicial or student panel proceedings, thereby preserving institutional due process
while maintaining student governance autonomy.1004.26(4)(d).Docusign Envelope ID: E8F0EF39-8545-406B-A5E2-7EF3CD1DA085

Chapter 406 Investigative Rights of the Senate
A. The Student Senate shall have the right to initiate and conduct an investigation in
order to examine any impropriety or to question any action of any Student
Government Association officer, appointed official, or Student Government
Association funded organization agency, bureau, affiliated project, or funding board.
B. An investigative Board may only be initiated by:
1. A 2/3 vote by the Student Senate in the form of a resolution, or
2. Whenever a standing or ad hoc committee deems necessary by
2/3 vote, and
3. The Student Senate President.
C. An Investigative Board will consist of the Judiciary Committee unless otherwise
deemed by a Student Senate resolution.
D. All conclusions of any Investigative Board will be reported to the Student Senate
in the form of a resolution.
E. An Investigative Board may make a recommendation for action to the Student
Senate in the form of a resolution.
F. If the Investigative Board produces a resolution containing the results of the
investigation or any recommendation for action, upon passage by the senate, the
resolution shall be published in the Senate minutes.
G. In order to carry out its duties, an Investigative Board or standing committee
shall be empowered with the right and authority to issue a legislative subpoena upon
an SGA Officer for any private records related to the investigation, unless prohibited
by the Student Body Constitution, state law, or federal law (such as FERPA or
HIPPA),. provided that:
1. The text of the subpoena includes:
a. The name of the SGA Officer upon whom the subpoena is
to be served;
b. The names of all acting Senators on the Investigative Board
or standing committee which has authorized the issuance of the
subpoena by majority vote;
c. The date and time wherein the Investigative Board or
standing committee authorized the issuance of the subpoena by
majority vote;
d. The date and time wherein the Student Senate President
authorized the issuance of the subpoena;DocuSign Envelope ID: 20FAE976-0E27-4381-848B-1F18E6210B4A

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
e. The nature of the specific evidence sought by issuance of
the subpoena;
f. A legitimate investigative purpose for the evidence sought
within the context of the investigation;
g. Sufficient reason as to why the evidence sought is not
unreasonably burdensome to produce; and
h. A designated time and place, at least fifteen (15) days after
the Investigative Board or standing committee’s majority vote to
authorize the subpoena’s issuance, wherein the information
compelled for disclosure may be inspected and examined by the
Investigative Board or standing committee under the direct
supervision of an impartial custodian of the public record.
2. The subpoena is approved using the following timeline:
a. The investigative board or standing committee approves the
text of the legislative subpoena by a majority vote, the Chair of the
Investigative Board or standing committee authorizes the
subpoena by signature, and sends the subpoena to
the Student Senate President for further authorization;
b. The legislative subpoena is subsequently authorized by the
Senate President by signature and sent by the Student Senate
President to the Chair of the Investigative Board or standing
committee within eight (8) business days of the Investigative
Board or standing committee’s majority vote;
i. Upon the decision to deny a legislative subpoena for
issuance, the Student Senate President shall, within
twenty-four (24) hours of the subpoena’s denial, provide
the Chair of the Investigative Board or standing
committee with the full and unrelenting rationale as to
why the legislative subpoena was denied so that the
Investigative Board or standing committee may attempt
to cure those deficiencies by drafting and authorizing a
revised subpoena, or alternatively, appeal the Student
Senate President’s decision to the Student Supreme
Court pursuant to Article IV, section 3(C)(1) of the Student
Body Constitution.
c. The Chair of the Investigative Board or standing
committee shall present the subpoena to the Senate via a
resolution which must be heard on the Senate floor and affirmed by
a majority vote of the Senate at that meeting.DocuSign Envelope ID: 20FAE976-0E27-4381-848B-1F18E6210B4A

Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 046
Primary Sponsor(s): Goldstein, Rios
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: Guiding Oversight of Legislative Disbursements Act of 2025
Summary of Legislation: This bill consolidates and restructures the financial governance
framework of the Student Senate by amending multiple chapters of the Student Body Statutes.
It eliminates the Senate Budget Committee as a standing body, reassigns oversight to the
Finance Committee, and updates procedures for budget amendments, transfers, reserve
accounts, and fund usage. The legislation establishes a standardized project proposal process
for CAD Fund requests and revises thresholds for Senate Projects and other allocations.
Background Information: The Student Senate’s fiscal process has long been divided
between overlapping committees, leading to inefficiencies, confusion, and limited
transparency. The bill draws from best practices in financial oversight to clarify committee
roles, streamline review procedures, and improve long-term fiscal stewardship of Activity &
Service (A&S) Fees. It also strengthens accountability by introducing new statutory
requirements, including a standardized proposal form and revised voting thresholds for major
allocations.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The legislation centralizes fiscal responsibilities under the Finance Committee, establishes
clearer budget amendment processes, and revises procedures across the Budget Act, Senate
Projects, CAD Fund, CLC Funding, and Reserve Account statutes. It modernizes and
normalizes Senate financial operations, ensuring more consistent oversight, stronger
accountability, and greater efficiency in the allocation of A&S Fees.

Chapter 412 Sweepings Regulations Act of 1995
History: Added by 47th Senate Bill 93. Revised by the 48th Senate Bill 167. Revised by the
49th Senate Bills 14 and 54. Revised by the 52nd Senate Bill 19. Revised by the 56th
Senate Bill 10. Revised by 60th Senate Bill 69. Revised by the 68th Senate Bill 61.
412.1 Sweepings Allocation Process
A. Monies from sweepings may not be allocated by Student Senate, except
through one sweepings bill per year. It must be completed and passed by
Student Senate no later than the end of the fall term.
1. In the event that a veto results in unallocated sweepings monies an
additional sweepings bills may be done.
2. In the event that the Vice President for Student Affairs holds
sweepings funds in an A&S Fee Reserve and later returns that
money to the Student Senate, the monies shall be allocated in a
sweepings bill. This may result in an additional sweepings bill.
B. Sweepings monies may not be attached as a rider to other bills.
B. The Student Senate President shall call the Sweepings Committee to order
each fall semester, after consultations with the Vice President for Student
Affairs, the Student Body President, and the Student Senate Advisor.
C. Committee Members
1. The Sweepings Committee shall be a special standing committee,
and members shall enjoy all rights of committee members under
Chapter 411, unless otherwise stated in this statute.
2. Senators may serve on this committee as voting members while
serving on other committees. The Committee shall consist of two
(2) members from each standing committee (except Rules and
Calendar) elected by their committee. The Chair and Vice Chair of
the Sweepings Committee shall be elected by the Sweepings
Committee upon its creation in the Fall.
1. The Sweepings Committee shall be a special standing committee of
the Senate, and senators who serve on the committee shall enjoy all
rights of committee members under Chapter 417, unless otherwise
stated in this chapter. The heads of the respective entities shall appoint
their respective representatives within one (1) week of the Committee
being called to order by the Senate President.
2. The Sweepings Committee shall be composed of the following
members:DocuSign Envelope ID: 277DF099-1A1C-4EBA-9472-91451B277FEE

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
a. One (1) representative from the Campus Recreation Board
b. One (1) representative from the Union Board
c. Six (6) representatives from the Student Senate
d. One (1) representative from the Executive Branch
e. Two (2) representatives from the Congress of Graduate Students
f. The Deputy Treasurer
3. The Chair and Vice Chair of the Sweepings Committee shall be
elected at the first meeting of the committee by the entire committee
body, selecting only from the pool of serving senators.
D. An estimated amount of the Budget shall be used to submit to the Senate
President for First Reading by the Chair of the Sweepings Committee.
After which, hearings Hearing shall be held and operated at the discretion
of the Chair of the Sweepings Committee.
1. Each prospective recipient of monies from Sweepings shall make a
request. The Sweepings Committee shall hold hearings during
which requests are defended. Each prospective recipient of
Sweepings shall have a separate hearing.
2. The hearings shall be administered by the Chair of the Sweepings
Committee and shall require a minimum of three (3) members to be
present. The Sweepings Committee will in good faith obtain
quorum.
3. Each prospective recipient of monies shall have fifteen (15)
minutes for an opening presentation, after which they may be
questioned by any member of the Sweepings Committee. This time
limit may be waived by the Chair, or by majority vote of the
Committee.
3. The Sweepings Committee shall have the authority to deliberate
monies to requesting and non-requesting prospective recipients.
The Sweepings Committee shall also be authorized to deliberate
more or less than the amount requested.
E. Upon the completion of hearings, the Sweepings Committee shall meet in
open deliberations to determine the allocations to be disbursed.
1. The Committee shall have the authority to deliberate monies to
requesting and non-requesting prospective recipients.
2. The Committee shall vote on each line item, which shall require a
majority vote of the committee to pass.
3. Committee members shall not vote on matters for which they have
a conflict of interest pursuant to Statute 205.3(A)(2).DocuSign Envelope ID: 277DF099-1A1C-4EBA-9472-91451B277FEE

members of the Sweepings Committee, per Section 400.4.
E. F. Any amendment that affects the proviso language or allocation amount in
any line of any recipient shall require a two thirds (2/3) vote of the Student
Senate. Each amendment shall require a separate two thirds (2/3) vote of
the Student Senate.
1. An amendment must be made to a specific line and category.
F. G. The completed and committee approved Sweepings Bill must be published
and available to the student body no less than three (3) days prior to the
hearing of the bill on Second Reading in the Senate.
G. The Sweepings Bill shall be passed by a roll call vote.

413.8 The Senate Hall of Fame
History: Added by the 54th Senate Bill 64. Revised by the 56th
Senate Bill 78. Revised by the 60th Senate Bill 69. Revised by the
62nd Senate Bill 91. Revised by the 72nd Student Senate Bill 6A.
Membership in the Senate Hall of Fame is the highest honor a student Senator can
achieve. This honor shall be bestowed upon any Senator who has performed their
duty as a member of the Senate with the highest standard of excellence, beyond
that normally expected of a Senator at the Florida State University.
A. Prospective candidates for this award shall be nominated by the Student
Senate in Resolution format. Included in the Resolution should be the
name of the Senator to be nominated, the Senate(s) in which the
individual served and reasons why the Senator is deserving of this honor.
When this resolution is debated on the Senate
Floor, two rounds of pro may be given, but no rounds of con will be
permitted. If the Resolution is approved by the Senate, by two-thirds
(2/3) vote, the Senator will be automatically considered a member of the
Senate Hall of Fame.
1. The Senate shall determine the criterion for selecting the
recipients of the award. The following exceptions to this apply:
a. Only the Senator’s accomplishments in the Student
Senate shall apply.
b. Holding a position of Senate leadership shall not be the
sole basis for determining if a nominee is qualified.
c. Only senators who have served two calendar years or
two full terms of office or more in the Student Senate
may be considered.
i. The length of the Senator's term beyond this
threshold shall not count for or against the
nominee.
ii. Time served shall count time served in Senate
Officer positions such as Senate Clerk, Senate
Press Secretary, and Senate Parliamentarian.
iii. This stipulation may be overruled by a ¾ 2/3
vote of the senate in situations where the senate
determines a nominee’s work is exceptional
(emphasis added) in a shorter amount of time.
a. Except for the original members of the Senate Hall of
Fame, no person shall be considered for membership
following their graduation from Florida State University.
b. No more than four (4) Senators shall be inducted in the
Hall of Fame per year.
C. Once a nominee has been selected to be a member of the Senate Hall of
Fame, they will be notified in a timely manner as to the award. The
Senators placed in the Senate Hall of Fame shall have their names
placed on a plaque that will be permanently displayed in the hall outside
of the Senate Chamber.DocuSign Envelope ID: A67A137E-3547-479A-9D46-2A143257F2BC

413.3 The FSU Student Senate Award for Excellence
A. Each Senator may nominate one FSU student, faculty/staff member, or campus
entity for an FSU Student Senate Award for Excellence per year though a
maximum of five (5) such awards shall be given each year. The FSU Student
Senate Award for Excellence is to be granted for distinguished service to the
Florida State University or to the community, or for outstanding performance in
representing this university.
B. A Senator wishing to nominate an individual or entity for the Student Senate
Award for Excellence must do so by submitting a resolution for referral to the
Student Life Committee containing the nominee’s name and a description of why
they are deserving of the award. Upon approval by the Student Senate, the award
shall be presented to the recipient in any fashion deemed fit. The FSU Student
Senate Award for Excellence shall be a certificate or other memento designed
and provided by the Student Senate President.
1. When nominating resolutions are debated on the Senate Floor, two rounds of
pro may be given, but no rounds of con will be permitted. If the resolution is
approved by the Senate by two-thirds (2/3) vote, the nominated individual or
entity will be considered a recipient of the Student Senate Award for
Excellence.
2. The provisions in 413.3 (b) shall not preclude the Student Senate President
from immediately placing a nominating resolution on the calendar for second
reading if that right is granted to them by the Senate Rules of Procedure.DocuSign Envelope ID: C7F47048-342B-4936-A204-5D113D5595B8

413.2 Senator of the Month
A. The Student Senate shall, by majority vote, select a “Senator of the Month” for
the previous month, on the first regular Senate meeting of each month.
1. If the legislative session ends prior to the following month, a vote for Senator
of the Month shall occur at the last meeting of the respective month.
B. The nomination and voting process shall be conducted in a manner that the
Senate President shall determine.
C. The Senate Press Secretary shall publish an announcement with the winner of the
award on the SGA website and applicable social media.
D. After winning the award, that Senator shall not be eligible for nomination again
until 180 days has passed.
E. The Student Senate President and Student Senate Pro Tempore shall not
be eligible for this award.DocuSign Envelope ID: 058AFFD7-7458-4800-A37B-038A3D130B61

77th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 49
Primary Sponsor(s): Holliday
Co-sponsor(s): Berg, Bent, Bigenho, Collantes, Fernandez, Friall, Goldstein, Nicholson,
Noumena
Short Title: Adding New Senate Awards and Revising Chapter 413
Summary of Legislation:
This legislation amends Chapter 413 “Senate Awards” to reorganize the awards system and
structure and to add six (6) new awards to present to members of the Senate community in
recognition of their leadership, service, and dedication. Fall awards will gain “The Mores Award
(Vice-Chair of the Year)” [previously The Ethics Award] and “The Flame Award (Senate Officer
of the Year),” while spring awards will gain “The Bridge Builder Award,” “The Statecraft Award,”
and “The Advocate Award.” The “Legislative Certification Program Excellence Award” will be
added as an addition to the awards section and be available for both fall and spring awards.
Background Information:
This legislation originated upon the discovery that there was no Vice Chair of the Year Award.
After further brainstorming, it also included adding a few additional awards to recognize
members in the Senate community who are not just Senators with the Legislative Certification
Program Participants. It also re-establishes the Senate Officer of the Year Award, which has
existed in the past but is not in statute. Finally, it organizes and cleans up the structure of the
Senate Awards chapter as a whole, since there were some outdated sections and areas of
overlap, as well as structural weakness in certain places. It adds more spring awards focused
on styles of Senate leadership.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If passed, this bill would allow more members of our Senate community to be recognized at
Inauguration for their hard work and admirable service to our space. Ideally, it will foster more
motivation to succeed and appreciation for one another amongst the Student Senate.

Chapter 415 Senate Legislative Certification Program
History: Added by the 54th Senate Bill 40. Deleted by the 56th Senate Bill 27. Added by
the 71st Senate Bill 19.
415.1 Purpose
This act is to establish a program administered by the Student Senate Pro
Tempore for students who are neither currently nor former members of the FSU
Student Senate who are interested in gaining knowledge of how the Senate
operates through first-hand experiences.
415.2 Name
The name of this program shall be “The Senate Legislative Certification Program.”
415.2 415.3 Administration of Program
The Senate Pro Tempore shall create an application and make it available to
students on the SGA website each semester the program is offered. The Senate
Pro Tempore shall have discretion over which applicants are to be admitted to the
program. The Senate Pro Tempore shall be responsible for holding an orientation
session for admitted applicants to explain the program and answer questions they
may have.
415.3 Professional Development Requirement
The Senate Pro Tempore shall develop a requirement which will help each
candidate develop professional skills.
415.4 Certification Requirements
A. Each candidate enrolled in the Student Senate Certificate Program shall
complete the following requirements:
1. Attend three (3) Student Senate meetings and take notes about
each meeting.
2. Attend three (3) committee meetings and take notes about each
meeting.
a. A candidate must attend the meeting of at least two (2)
different committees, to include no less than one standing
committee meeting.
3. Complete the Professional Development Requirement as
developed and given to the candidates by the Senate Pro
Tempore.
4. 3. Participate in writing a bill or resolution.DocuSign Envelope ID: 16A5DEB1-0EE1-4A66-BFFA-E266EED0AABA

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
5. 4. Meet with a Senate liaison to discuss their role as a liaison and
how they serve the campus entity they are a liaison to.
6. 5. Meet with the Senate Pro Tempore after all other requirements
have been completed to discuss the experiences had through this
program.
415.5 Verification of a Candidate’s Completed Requirements
A. Each candidate shall notify the Senate Pro Tempore upon their completion
of all requirements of the program from the certificate, and the Pro
Tempore shall verify that all requirements have been completed.
1. If the Pro Tempore finds that a candidate has not successfully
completed all requirements by the end of the semester that
candidate is enrolled in this program, that candidate shall not
receive a certificate of completion as outlined in Student Body
Statute 415.5B.
B. Upon the Pro Tempore’s verification, the candidate shall be awarded a
certificate of completion of The Student Senate Certification Program at
the next student government inauguration.DocuSign Envelope ID: 16A5DEB1-0EE1-4A66-BFFA-E266EED0AABA

proposed allocations before passage.

faith effort to complete the Budget no later than

416.3 Procedures for Passage of the Budget
A. The Budget shall not be approved by the Student Senate in a
Summer Session.
B. An estimated amount of the Budget shall be used to submit to the
Senate President for First Reading by the Chair of the Budget
Committee. After which, hearings shall be held and operated at the
discretion of the Chair of the Budget Committee.
1. Each prospective recipient of monies from the Budget shall
make a budget request. The Budget Committee shall hold
hearings during which budget requests are defended. Each
prospective recipient of the Budget shall have a separate
hearing.
2. The hearings shall be administered by the Chair of the
Budget Committee and shall require a minimum of three (3)
Senators. The Budget Committee will in good faith obtain
quorum.
3. The Budget Committee shall have the authority to deliberate
monies to requesting and non-requesting prospective
recipients. The Budget Committee shall also be authorized
to deliberate more or less than the amount requested.
C. When the Budget has been deliberated and approved in whole by
the Budget Committee it will be heard on Second Reading. All
Senators shall be presented copies of the proposed allocations.
The Budget shall be on the calendar for second reading for a
minimum of five (5) business days with proposed allocations
before passage. The budget and proviso must properly be
advertised on the Student Government website while on Second
Reading.
D. The Budget shall be approved by the Senate before the beginning
of the fiscal year of which it affects. The Chair of the Budget
Committee shall make a good-faith effort to complete the Budget
no later than October 31 of each year.

Changes to the Proviso language may be made via resolution at

416.3 Procedures for Passage of the Budget
A. The Budget shall not be approved by the Student Senate in a Summer Session.

and operated at the discretion of the Chair of the Budget Committee.

defended. Each prospective recipient of the Budget shall have a separate hearing.

obtain quorum.

requesting and non-requesting prospective recipients. The Budget Committee shall also

Committee it will be heard on Second Reading. All Senators shall be presented copies of
the proposed allocations. The Budget shall be on the calendar for second reading for a
minimum of five (5) business days with proposed allocations before passage. The budget
and proviso must properly be advertised on the Student Government website while on
Second Reading.

which it affects. The Chair of the Budget Committee shall make a good faith effort to

Short Title: Adding the Finance Vice Chair into the Annual Budget Committee
Summary of Legislation:
This bill will guarantee the Student Senate Finance Vice Chair is also bound to be a member of
the Annual Budget Committee in correlation to the large role the Finance Vice Chair already
serves in establishing and planning the Annual Budget Process.
Background Information:
Amongst the many responsibilities the Vice Chair has in ensuring the Annual Budgeting
Process for the Student Government Association. Representing the Student Senate as a
member of the Budget Committee is not included. With the amount of work and responsibility
that the Finance Vice Chair does, it is deemed appropriate for the position to be included in the
actual process by default. This will raise the committee membership to twenty members all
selected from different represented bodies of the Student Government Association, while
keeping quorum rules the same, in a combined effort to allow students appointed to the
committee academic and professional flexibility with less of a threat of missing quorum while
allowing the Student Senate Vice Chair of Finance to partake in the annual budget process.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The Student Senate Vice Chair of Finance will now serve annually in the budgeting process as
a member of the Budget Committee.

Chapter 418 The Senate Projects Account
418.1. Purpose
A. The purpose of the Senate Projects account is to create an account of the
Senate of the student body from which initiatives of said branch may be funded.
418.2. Guidelines
A. The Senate Projects account shall fund projects that further the image of Student
Government Association to the Florida State University student body, provide
services or opportunities to students, or to fulfill an observed need on campus.
B. During summer sessions, the Senate Projects account shall also fund RSOs
requesting money from PAC and RTAC.
418.3. Process
A. Funds from the Senate Projects account shall be allocated via a transfer bill.
B. This bill shall be sent to the Student Life and Finance Committees.
1. The Student Life Committee shall determine whether or not the bill will
have a positive impact on student life.
2. The Finance Committee shall determine whether or not the bill is fiscally
responsible.
418.4. Funding
A. The account may be replenished by the annual budget, central reserves,
sweepings, or by transfer from any other account.
B. At the final Senate meeting of the summer semester, the Senate Projects
account shall be reimbursed by the appropriate funds distribution committee for
funds allocated. These transfer bills shall be drafted by the Chair of the Finance
Committee and shall not exceed $2,000 per committee.DocuSign Envelope ID: 6EB619DA-08D7-43AB-A6BB-D73476EB3908

Chapter 420: Major Legislation
420. 1 Defining Major legislation
Major legislation shall include the Budget Bill, the Sweepings Bill, the Central Reserves Bill, and
the Legislative Agenda Resolution. The Senate President has the authority to determine if any
other bill, resolution, or allocation shall be deemed major legislation.
420. 2 Scheduling of Major Legislation
If the Senate session that major legislation is scheduled to be voted on coincides with a
Holy Day, any member of the Florida State University Student Body whom it affects may
express their concerns to the Student Senate President. The Student Senate President,
with the consultation of the Student Senate President Pro Tempore, may then ensure that
the major legislation is scheduled to be voted on during a senate session that does not
conflict with that Holy Day. The Student Senate President has the discretion to change
the voting date for major legislation before a concern is raised.

Statute/Amendment Text:
Chapter 422 The Campus Advancement and Development Fund
422.1 Establishment
A. The establishment of a fund to facilitate substantial infrastructure
improvements and long-term projects that advance the Student Government
Association's mission and enrich the collegiate experience for the entire
student body.
422.2 Funding and Contributions
A. The SGA Project Fund The fund shall receive a minimum allocation equivalent
to 0.25 percent (0.25%) of the yearly budget collected from A&S fees.
B. A line item must be included in the yearly budget bill that shall be explicitly
allocated to this fund titled “CAD Fund”.
422.3 Purpose
A. The Fund is established to provide financial backing for large-scale projects
and initiatives that benefit the student body and enhance the capabilities of the
Student Government Association.
B. The Fund may also act as a strategic resource for mitigating minor budgetary
shortfalls, by empowering the Student Government Association to effectively
manage its finances without needing to access the Central Reserves account.
422.4 Usage of Funds
A. Expenditure from the fund shall be approved through the following process:
1. A bill proposing the use of funds shall be presented to the Senate.
2. The Budget Committee shall determine whether the bill is fiscally
responsible by a three-fourths (3/4) majority vote.
3. The Student Life Committee shall determine whether the bill shall
provide substantial improvement or enrichment to the student body.
4. If the bill is being used to mitigate a minor budgetary shortfall the
Finance Committee shall objectively verify if this fund is needed to
address the budgetary constraint by a three-fourths (3/4) majority vote.
5. Following passage by the required standing committees, the bill shall
require a two-thirds (2/3) majority vote of the Senate.
6. Following approval from the Senate, the Student Body President and
Student Body Treasurer must approve the bill by signature.DocuSign Envelope ID: ABFBDD4A-B321-4119-815F-78659A5F0B27

B. This fund shall be a non-sweepable account. All monies allocated to the fund
shall be held in the fund for at least two (2) fiscal years prior to being
transferred or used. This provision can be waived by a three-fourths (3/4)
majority vote of the Senate.
C. The Congress of Graduate Students shall be given the opportunity to
contribute to this fund, should COGS contribute to this fund, COGS shall have
voting representation on the Budget Committee during the usage of these
funds.
422.5 Fund Administration and Oversight
A. The Student Body Treasurer shall be responsible for the management,
investment, and oversight of the fund, ensuring its compliance with this

B. An annual report detailing the inflows, outflows, and project funding from the

Advancement and Development Fund.

3 and Development Fund”.

9 2. A line item must be included in the yearly budget that shall be explicitly be allocated to this fund

11 Section 3. Effective Date.

13 Affairs.

Section 1: §500.3 is amended as follows:
500.3 Jurisdiction of the Court
A. The Student Supreme Court shall be an appellate court for cases tried
in other bodies at FSU that recognize the Supreme Court’s appellate
jurisdiction. The Supreme Court shall also have original jurisdiction
over such matters as defined in Article IV, Section 3 of the Student
Body Constitution. Supreme Court Justices shall be selected through
the procedures outlined in the Student Body Constitution, although the
Chief Justice shall have the power to appoint the Clerk, and Deputy
Clerks of the Court, in addition to any other powers granted to the
Chief Justice by the Student Body Constitution.
B. The Chief Justice shall appoint FSU law students to the University
Defender Program to assist FSU students accused of violations of the
Student Conduct Code, Academic Honor Policy, University Housing
Code, Student Government Statutes, Student Body Constitution, or
any other established University Policy.
Section 2: Chapter 504 shall be repealed and replaced by:
Chapter 504 The University Defender Program
504.1 Purpose
This Chapter implements the University Defender program as prescribed in
Florida State University Regulation FSU-3.006.
504.2 Execution
Pursuant to Chapter 500, the Chief Justice shall be tasked with appointing
FSU law students to the University Defender Program. Any law student
appointed to the program shall be confirmed by the Student Senate prior to
performing their duties.
504.3 Selection Process
The process of selection and fulfilled requirements shall be further stipulated by
Florida State University Regulation FSU-3.006, any further stipulation not
otherwise outlined in University Regulations or Student Body Statutes shall be
done by the Supreme Court through established policy overseen by the Chief

A. Title and Purpose
1. This act shall be called the "Student Supreme Court Constitutional
Amendment and Referendum Review Act of WW 2017,"
hereinafter referred to as the "Court Review Act".
2. The purpose of this act is to provide for an effective procedure forthe
review of all constitutional amendments and referenda, collectively
referred to as "provisions" for the purpose of this chapter, before the
provisions are placed on the ballot as a means to insure thatall
provisions voted on by students are fair and not deceptive in terms of
the provision's language, and do not violate the Student Body Statutes.
the Student Body Constitution. the Board of Governors Regulations.
University Policy or Regulation, or any local, state. or federal law.

opinion. In no case may the Supreme Court prevent the student body
from voting on a proposed constitutional amendment from the ballot
unless such amendment is found to clearly violate federal, state, or

BILL 72
Chapter 510 Leaves of Absences During the Summer Session for Members
of the Judicial Branch
Purpose
~ The purpose of this chapter shall be to allow for
certain members of the Judicial Branch to take a
leave of absence during the summer session, and to
set forth the procedures to select their temporary
replacements during that term .
.!!.:.. Applicability and Scope
~ The orovisions of this chanter shall apply to the
following officers of the Judicial Branch.
.5l:.. The Associate Justices of the Supreme Court
!h The University Defenders.
~ The General Counsels
~ The Clerk of the Court
~ The Deputy Clerks of the Court
~ The Chief Justice of the Florida State University
is an integral part of the Judicial Branch and has
the responsibility to oversee the student judicial
system as well as to appoint all other officers of
the Judicial Branch, with the exception of the
Associate Justices. For these reasons, the Chief
Justice shall ·not be permitted to take a leave of
absence during the summer session .
.Q..:,. Procedure
~ All eligible officers shall notifv the Chief
Justice in writing on or before the last day of
final examination at the College of Law of their
intention to take a leave of absence during the
summer session.
At the conclusion of final examinations at the
College of Law, the Chief Justice shall appoint
temporary officers to fill all or some of the
vacated seats at his/her discretion. These
temporary officers must meet all of the
qualifications for the office to which thev are
being appointed as if they were being appointed in
the normal , permanent manner. In keeping with
Article IV of the Student Body Constitution, the

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
Student Bodv President and the Student Bar
Association do not need to be contacted for
temporary appointments. However, all temporary
summer appointees to the Judicial Branch must be
confirmed by a majority vote of the Senate. These
nominations by the Chief Justice shall go directly
to the floor at the earliest summer session of the
Senate.
All appointees to the Judicial Branch during the
summer session shall be on notice that their
appointments are of a temporary nature. Their term
of office shall terminate on the last day of final
examinations for the summer academic term.
All temporary officers of the Judicial Branch who
are entitled to compensation shall be compensated
for the summer term as if they were permanent
officers. This compensation shall cease at the
close of the summer academic term or should they
resign from office. which ever comes first.
All of the permanent officers of the Judicial
Branch who take a leave of absence for the summer
term shall receive no compensation for the summer
term. Such compensation shall only resume when they
assume their permanent offices at the opening of
classes in the fall semester.
All temporary judicial officers are entitled to
serve throughout the summer session, even if their
permanent counterparts come back from the summer
early. Permanent members only resume their offices
at the opening of classes during the fall semester.
All temporary judicial officers are subject to
impeachment by the Student Senate during the summer
session according to the procedures listed in
Chapter 405 of the Student Body Statutes.

Chapter 607 Congress of Graduate Students
607.1 A. An organization entitled Congress of Graduate Students
{hereafter referred to as COGS} is established on the
main campus of the Florida State University to implement
the general policies of the Florida State University
Student Government Association {hereafter referred to
FSU-SGA} and the specific policies of COGS.
B . Purpose of COGS
1. To provide graduate and professional students at
FSU, through COGS, an opportunity to participate in
the decision-making process.
2. To consider, make recommendations and act upon
phases of graduate/professional student life at
FSU.
3. To serve as the principal forum for decisions on
matters of broad concern to the
graduate/professional students at FSU.
4. To serve as the chief means by which
graduate/professional students may express their
university concerns for FSU-SGA.
c. Membership
1. COGS shall be composed of representatives as
defined by the COGS Constit~tion Code.
2. The COGS Faculty Advisor shall be an ex-officio
member of COGS.
3. The Speaker of COGS shall preside over COGS and
shall vote only in the case of a tie among the
representatives.
4. A Financial Officer shall be elected by COGS to
serve in the absence, removal, or resignation of
the Speaker, until election of a new Speaker.
5. Any graduate, professional or post-baccalaureate
{graduate special) student admitted at FSU, taking
course{s}, maintaining a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or
better, and in good standing with the University,
shall be eligible to seek and hold a position in
COGS.

77th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 025
Primary Sponsor(s): LoBianco
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: A Resolution Congratulating the Student Body President on Being Elected Chair
of the Florida Student Association and Proposing a Revision to Chapter 607, Student Body
Statutes
Summary of Legislation:
The resolution congratulates President Carson Dale on his election as Chair of the Florida
Student Association and proposes an amendment to Chapter 607, Student Body Statutes,
designating the COGS Speaker as FSU’s representative on the Florida Student Association’s
Graduate Student Committee.
Background Information:
The Florida Student Association (FSA) is the official nonprofit organization representing the
more than 400,000 students in the Florida State University System.1 The FSA’s board of
directors is made up of the student body presidents of the twelve state universities, who elect a
chair from among themselves.2 The chair of the FSA serves as a member of the Florida State
University System Board of Governors, which regulates the entire Florida State University
System.
On May 30, 2025, FSU Student Body President Carson Dale was elected Chair of the FSA by
the FSA Board of Directors. In consultation with Speaker Rowan, President Dale proposed an
amendment to the FSA constitution that created a Graduate Student Committee, comprised of
a graduate student representative from each of the twelve state universities. The amendment
was adopted by the Board of Directors. As a result, FSU SGA needs to designate, by statute,
an official to serve on the Graduate Student Committee.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The resolution congratulates President Carson Dale on his election as Chair of the FSA.
Additionally, the resolution proposes an amendment to Chapter 607, Student Body Statutes,
which governs COGS. Per § 607.1(d)(1), SBS, COGS may directly propose legislation to
Senate. When COGS proposes legislation, the legislation must be introduced by the Senate
President or the Senate Judiciary Committee.

AN ACT
Designating the Speaker of the Congress of Graduate Students as FSU’s Representative on
the Florida Student Association’s Graduate Student Committee
Be it enacted by the 77th Student Senate at Florida State University that:
Section 1. Amendment to Student Body Statutes Chapter 607, “Congress of Graduate
Students”.
Section 607.1(h) of the Florida State University Student Body Statutes is hereby amended to read
as follows:
(h) COGS Speaker Duties and Responsibilities:
(1) To plan and coordinate the execution of all administrative work necessary for the efficient
operation of COGS.
(2) To be the chief liaison between COGS and SGA.
(3) To be empowered to represent the graduate, professional, and post-baccalaureate FSU
Student Body officially within the university and serve as spokesperson for COGS.
(4) To be responsible for the supervision/hiring/firing of authorized COGS OPS employees
funded by A&S Fees, with the final approval by majority vote of COGS.
(5) To authorize the expenditure of A&S allocations as described in the COGS budget.
(6) To perform other duties and responsibilities as delineated in the COGS Code.
(7) To serve as FSU’s representative on the Florida Student Association’s Graduate Student
Committee unless the Speaker, in writing, designates another COGS Representative to serve
on the Committee.
Section 2. Effective Date.
The provisions of this bill shall take effect upon signature of the Vice President for Student Affairs.

Short Title: Awarding the FSU Marching Chiefs with the Student Senate Award for Excellence
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution recognizes the extraordinary work of the FSU Marching Chiefs and their directors:
Patrick Dunnigan, David Plack, and Devan L. Moore. This resolution acknowledges the historical
significance as the FSU Marching Chiefs will be the first collegiate university from Florida to be invited
to perform in the 2027 Macy's Thanksgiving Parade.
Background Information:
This resolution and this award recognize the extraordinary achievements of the FSU Marching
Chiefs, directors, and other related contributors to the program in being invited to the highly
distinguished 101st Macy's Thanksgiving parade. This celebrates the Florida State Marching Chiefs
being the first collegiate marching band from Florida selected to perform in the parade. The Macy's
thanksgiving parade generates over 30 million viewers from across the globe for its historically beloved
performance that has existed since 1924. Over 400 marching chiefs will attend the parade,
representing FSU on a global platform; however, this is not the first time the Marching Chiefs have
represented FSU on a global platform. The marching chiefs have famously performed in Syria, Jordan,
England, France, and Ireland; they have continued their reputation for excellence with their cordial
invite to the prestigious Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Outreach with Senate leadership, and directors Patrick Dunnigan, David Plack, and Devan L. Moore
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This resolution would award the FSU Marching Chiefs as a collective the highly esteemed Student
Senate Award for Excellence. It will highlight the hard work and dedication of all staff, students, and
alumni who have played an active and significant role in the media attention and positive reputation of
Florida State. This resolution will also show appreciation to the graduating Marching Chief students
who have dedicated their collegiate careers towards this organization and are graduating into the next
phase of their lives before the 2027 Macy's Thanksgiving Parade performance.Docusign Envelope ID: D9A6A55F-9E62-83ED-81FF-0F75D1673E56

History: Added by the 58th Senate Bill 71. Revised by the 59th Senate Bill 50. Revised by the 60th
Senate Bill 32. Revised by the 62nd Senate Bill 105. Revised by the 66th Senate Bill 1. Revised by

612.1
A. Adoption
There shall be a joint initiative of the Executive Branch, Legislative Branch, and
Union Productions called the Golden Torch Lecture Series.
B. Purpose
The purpose of this act is to provide the student body with a series of speakers
sponsored by the Student Government Association. The Golden Torch Lecture
Series will be an academically focused speaker series that attempts to connect
students to outstanding individuals who are either experts in their field or working
at the forefront of a relevant political or social issue. The mission of the series is to
engage students in issues and dialogue that will positively benefit their overall
academic, scholastic, or humanitarian experience.

purposes of this statute as “The committee”, shall consist of the following:

c. Student Body President or designee

President

i. Union Productions Programming Director

one (1) year, thereafter reappointment shall be conducted as per statutes.

I appreciate the conversation yesterday that Avi and I were able to have concern ing this bill that cleans up some of the
statutory language related to Homecoming. Finding an organization for Homecoming that wor ks well, responds to
students' feedback, and is susta inable over the yea rs is something that we have been working on for several years- I
think we are close!
Unfortunately, I am writing to let you know that I am vetoing Bill 24 because section 616 .7 is unclear and needs to be
modified. As we have learned, the SG accounting office is not able to handle the number of transactions that are
generated for Homecoming. In addition, #2 is unclear about the signature requirements for purchases over
$1,000. Further, SG's desire for more input and accountability can be adequately addressed w ithin the current
structure. And finally, the need to quickly respond to booking agents for major performers w ould get too bogged dow n
w ithin the SG legislative and accounting structures. If there are clear directives on types of performers and expenditures
that the SG leadership desires during Homecoming, that needs to be made clear very early in the process.
You know that vetoing a bill is action that I take with great hesitancy and only in cases w here I feel the outcome would

Senate Bill #: 037
Primary Sponsor(s): Holliday
Co-sponsor(s): Goldstein
Short Title: An Act Amending Chapter 615 “The Homecoming Executive Council” and
Repealing Chapter 616 “The Homecoming Planning Commission” and Chapter 617 “The
Homecoming Live Planning Committee”
Summary of Legislation: This bill aims to remove the Homecoming Planning Commission
from SGA statutes to better fit the current allocation of budget to the Homecoming Executive
Council and updates Chapter 615 to reflect that change. This Bill also updates Chapter 617
adding it as a new section under Chapter 615 to better fit the current structure of Homecoming
Executive Council.
Background Information: The Homecoming Planning Commission was established in 2003
to serve as a governing body responsible for suballocating Activity and Service (A&S) fees to
other organizations annually. Since the Commission’s creation, the process by which the
Homecoming Executive Council receives funding has evolved. This creates an unnecessary
procedural step in accessing funds already allocated during the annual A&S budget
distribution.
Effect of Proposed Legislation: This bill would create a more streamlined process for the
allocation of A&S fees to the Homecoming Executive Council every year.
