The Student Performing Arts Council
Title
There shall be an entity of the Student Government
Association known as the Student Performing Arts
Council.
Purpose and Intent
The Student Performina Arts Council, hereinafter
referred to as SPAC, shall unite the Florida State
University's student oerformance arts groups in an
effort to promote the arts on the campus of the Florida
State University and to educate the student body through
an arts initiative.
Membership
SPAC shall be led by two (2) members appointed by the
Student Body President and confirmed by the Senate:
A.:_ Director of SPAC.
~ Assistant Director of SPAC
h The Director/President of all participating
organizations or his/her designee shall serve as a
board member of SPAC.
~ All Student performing arts groups shall be
welcomed as affiliated members of SPAC.
Powers and Duties
A.:_ SPAC shall:
~ Encourage cooperation between student
performing arts groups on campus .
.£.:.. Produce and distribute a monthly calendar
that details the events being put on by SPAC
affiliated organizations.
Promote the student performance arts to the
Florida State University student body.

Florida State University Sarasota Campus A&S Fees Fund
Guidelines
Purpose
The purpose of these guidelines are:
A.:_ To provide students at the FSU Sarasota Camous,
through Sarasota Campus Student Council, (SCSC) an
opportunity to participate in the decision making
process.
12..:.. To consider, make recommendations, and act upon
certain phases of student life at the Sarasota
Campus.
~ To serve as the principal forum for decisions on
matters of broad concern to the students at the
Sarasota Campus.
To serve as the chief means by which Sarasota
Campus students mav express their university
concerns to FSU-SGA.
E..:.. To facilitate effective interaction between the FSU
university staff and sese in the expenditure of
funds derived from A&S Fees.
~ To provide a mechanism that assures that continued
compliance with State statutes, university rules,
regulations, and policies are not impeded.
Definitions
A.:_ The term "A&S Fee funded entity" as used throughout
these guidelines means: officially recognized
student activities, and group-sponsored. or
individually sponsored projects that may be
allocated A&S Fees by the Sarasota Campus Student
Council.
Sarasota Campus Student Council (SCSC) is an A&S
Fee funded entity comprised of two {2) student
representatives from each of the Asolo Conservatory
for Actor Training Graduate Program classes, Year
One (1), Two (2) and Three (3).

sections.text:

619.4
General Policies
A.:_ The SCSC shall be bound by the Student Body
Constitution and bound by the statutes of the
Florida State University Student Government
Association.
~ The exoenditure of Sarasota Campus A&S Fees shall
be determined by the sese in accord with the
applicable orovisions of the Florida State
University policies and procedures, and the laws of
the State of Florida. The policies, procedures and
controls governing the allocation and expenditure
of the Sarasota Campus A&S Fees shall be governed
by this statue.
~ The authority and responsibility of sese to
determine the expenditure of A&S Funds does not
include:
1...:.. Administrative authority over the exoenditure
of funds by the A&S Fee funded entity, except
where provided by the Florida Administrative
Code 6C2. 3. 035 and in accordance with FSU
fiscal policy.
Authority to enter into contractual
agreements not otherwise authorized.
~ Authority to in any way deviate from laws,
regulations and orocedures pertaining to
budgeting, allocation and/or expenditure of
funds of the State of Florida.
~ Authority to impose upon an A&S Fee funded
entity a requirement to obtain sese
.2....:_ Authority to hire, suoervise or terminate
personnel of the A&S Fee funded entities.
h Authority to make operational decisions of
the A&S Fee funded entities except where
provided by the Student Body Statutes.
~ No A&S Fee funded entity may discriminate in
membership or otherwise on basis of race, creed,
color. sex, sexual orientation, age, national
origin or disability.
Elections and General Organization
Elections of the SCSC Student Representatives: The
Graduate Students for second and third year classes
shall nominate and elect two (2) representatives

Orientation oeriod in the first week of the
academic year. The first year student class shall
nominate and elect two (2) representatives by the
end of the second week of the academic year. All
elections under this subsection will be cast and
decided by a majority vote.
Student representatives shall serve a one (1) year
term.
~ In the event a representative can no longer serve
on the sese or is requested to step down, the
request should be made in writing to the Director
(Director, Asolo Conservatory for Actor Training).
The Director will meet in counsel with the student
representative.
~ In the case of a vacancv, an election will be held
by the respective class for which the vacancy
exists to fill the student representative position.
The student organizations that my be subsequently
established at the Sarasota Campus must be an
officially Recognized Student Organization (RSO) to
be eligible to submit a request to spend A&S Fee
funds. Requirements for official recognition by the
camous are delineated and monitored by the FSU
Office of Student Affairs.
~ The sese shall hold meetings during the academic
year: one in October, January and April. Meetings
may be scheduled if announced at least 48 hours in
advance and posted in a centrally located public
place consistent with Chapter 203 of the FSU
Student Body Statutes.
~ A methodology for documenting and maintainina
minutes of the meetings and expenditure proposals
shall be established, published and maintained in
a set of sese bylaws not to be inconsistent with
the FSU Student Body Statutes.
The sese shall schedule an orientation-training
workshop in the · fall term after sese
representatives are elected. The workshop shall
include an explanation of the sese A&S Fee Fund
Guidelines and information regarding A&S Fees, the
budget process, legal aspects, terms of reference,
SGA organizational structure, SGA role and
responsibility and A&S Fee expenditure regulations.

comprise the A&S Fee funds available for the fiscal

and be available to the public upon request. The

Financial Provisions and Accountability
The College Leadership Council program as a whole will
be eligible for block funding in the annual Student
Government Budget. The block of funds will then be
proportionally appropriated to each individual council
based on the student population size of their respective
college.
The College Leadership Council is an entity of the
Executive Branch and shall be directly accountable to
the Office of the Student Body President.
The Chair of each College Leadership Council will
provide the Student Body President and Student Senate
President with an annual report on the programs,
activities, guidelines and finances of the Council.
Each Student Senate liaison for the College Leadership
Councils may choose to make frequent reports to Senate
during regular meetings.
College Leadership Councils must follow all statutes,
guidelines and policies related to the spending and
management of Student Government finances.
The College Leadership Council cannot act as a funding
board for recognized student organizations {RSOs).
The College Leadership Council cannot allocate funds to
recognized student organizations {RSOs) in the areas of
contractual services, expense, events, clothing, awards,
travel, organization materials, lodging or registration.
Recognized Student Organization Funding Process
A. Each Fund Distribution Committee shall be allocated a
lump sum of funds during the annual budget process by
the Senate Budget Committee. These funds will be
dispersed to the committee in intervals that are
determined in budget proviso.
B. RSO's seeking to receive funds will print a Funding
Request Form from the SGA Website and fill it out
accordingly. The RSO will turn in their Funding
Request Form to the SGA Accounting Office.

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
c. Only the RSO President or Treasurer and/or financially
certified designees may appear before the respective
Fund Distribution Committee for the allocation
hearing. At this hearing the respective Fund
Distribution Committee will hear the request and ask
any questions relating to the request of the RSO.
Upon completion of the hearing, the committee will
deliberate and vote on whether or not to approve the
expenditure.
D. The information at the meeting will be compiled into a
resolution by the committees Student Senate liaison.
This resolution will be presented at the next possible
Budget Committee meeting and shall only be debated on
if specifically objected to. The sponsor of the
resolution shall forward the resolution to the Student
Government Webmaster. If not objections are
entertained, the resolution shall be forwarded to the
Senate and placed on the Consent Calendar.
E. Once on the Consent Calendar, the resolution shall be
presented to the Student Senate. Debate on the
resolution will only be heard upon an objection to the
resolution. Any amendment which affects the allocation
amount to any recipient shall require a majority vote
of the Senate.
F. Recognized Student Organizations (RSOs) cannot request
or receive funds in the areas of contractual services,
expense, events, clothing, awards, travel,
organization materials, lodging or registration from
the College Leadership Council.

The Purpose of the College Leadership Councils will be to:
A. Act as the ambassadors of their respective college~

C. Create and oversee beneficial programming for
students in an attempt to improve opportunities for
personal and professional growth.
Organization of the Councils

Chapter 622 College Leadership Council Funding Committee
622.1
622.2
622.3
Purpose
To create the College Leadership Council Funding
Committee, hereinafter referred to as the CLC Funding
Committee, and establish a funding process for these
Councils.
Definition
A CLC shall be defined as a leadership council formed
within each academic college that operates as an entity of
the Executive Branch that promotes academic, personal and
professional growth within each college.
CLC Funding Process
A. CLC Funding Committee
1. The CLC Funding Committee shall be comprised of two
(2) students appointed by the Student Body President,
one (1) student Senator appointed by the Senate
President, the Senate Budget Chair, and the Student Body
Treasurer. The Committee shall be formed after July l 5 t,
but no later than eight (8) weeks prior to Budget Week.
2. The Chair shall be the Student Body Treasurer.
In the absence of the Student Body Treasurer, he or she
may appoint a proxy.
B. CLC Funding Procedures
1. The committee shall issue a letter to the CLCs
promptly once the date of Budget Week hearings is
determined. Each College Leadership Council will need
to, upon receiving their letter from the CLC Funding
Committee, prepare a packet containing their budget
reguests for the following academic year as well as
their plans for the current upcoming year. In
addition, each College Leadership Council must book a
hearing date with the Committee.
2. The CLC Funding Committee shall determine all
allocations and hearing dates.

sections.heading: Page 7
sections.text:
3. After hearings have taken place the CLC Funding
Committee will determine the amounts and how the funds
will be distributed to the CLCs. The CLC Funding Committee
Chair shall then present their findings to the Budget
Committee at Budget Week to request the entirety of the
Block Funds to then be distributed to the CLCs the
following academic year.
4. Once the CLC Funding Committee Chair has presented the
committee findings to the Budget Committee if the Budget
committee reduces the entirety of the Block Funds then the
CLC Funding Committee as a whole will then follow the new
process for distr1bution.
5. The new process for distribution of the Block Funds
after budget determines the final amounts, will be: if the
amount differs from the original reguest, then the new
amount will be subtracted from the old amount. The
subtraction process will yield an amount to then be
divided by the number of CLCs receiving funds, to finally
create an amount to be subtracted from each CLC's
allocation individually.
6. Xf the amount to be subtracted after this process is
larger than the budget, or too large for the operation of
a CLC then the CLC Funding Committee along with the CLC in
question and the SGA Advisor may sit down to determine
where else to responsibly cut from each of the CLCs.
7. A11 reasoning of the reapportionment of funds budget
cuts either by the CLC Funding Committee or Budget Week
shall be made available to any student upon reguest.

As many know, our College Leadership Councils (CLC) have a troubled history. Not

Bill 55 focuses mostly on the funding process of th e CLCs as they requ est money

History: Revised by the 68th Senate Bill 57.

110
To create the College Leadership Council Funding Comm ittee, hereinafter referred to

622.2 Definition
A CLC shall be defined as a leadership council formed within each academic college
that operates as an entity of the Executive Branch that promotes academic, personal
and professional growth within each college.
622.3 CLC Funding Process
A. CLC Funding Committee
1. The CLC funding committee shall allocate funds to CLCs, from a block
amount decided by the Budget committee allocation, for the next fiscal
year.
2. The CLC Funding Committee shall be comprised of two (2) students
appointed by the Student Body President, two (2.:t-) student Senators
appointed by the Student Senate President, and the Student Body
Treasurer. The Committee shall be formed after July 1st, but no later
than eight (8) weeks prior to Budget Week by the second week of the
spring semester.
3. The Chair shall be the Student Body Treasurer. In the absence of the
Student Body Treasurer, the Student Body Treasurer may appoint a
proxy.
B. CLC Funding Procedures
1. The Student Body Treasurer shall promptly issue a letter to the
CL Cs' Chair. Treasurer. and Advisor by on July 1st, the last week of
classes in the fall semester. informing them that they need to begin
preparing a packet containing their budget requests for the following
academic upcoming fiscal year, as well as their plans for the
upcoming current fiscal year. At this time, the CLCs will also be
informed of how the funding process works, and what they should
expect from it.
a. This announcement will also be made public on SGA's website. A
link will be provided that allows for the CLC's budget requests to
be received.

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
b. The CLC Funding Chair shall remind the CLCs' Chair, Treasurer,
and Advisor of the budget request deadline one (1) week prior to
the deadline.
2. Once the dates of Budget VVeek hearings are determined, and the
committee is established, each College Leadership Council must
book a hearing date with the Committee to present the above
information. CLCs shall submit their requests to the provided link
by the second Friday of the spring semester.
3. If a request is submitted after the deadline, but before the hearing,
the committee will vote by majority on whether or not the request
shall be heard.
a. If a CLC misses their hearing, the committee will review the
submitted request.
4. The CLC Funding Committee shall hold hearings during which budget
requests are defended by the third Friday of the spring semester. Each
CLC shall have a separate hearing.
a. The CLC Funding Committee Chair shall inform the CLCs' Chair,
Treasurer, and advisor of when hearings will take place as soon as
the committee is formed .
b. The hearings shall be administered by the Chair of the CLC
Funding Committee and shall require a minimum of (3) members.
The CLC Funding Committee will in good faith obtain quorum.
c. If a CLC does not make a good faith effort to submit their budget
request packet, and/or schedule a hearing date time with the
committee, by September 15#\, they ',viii not be eligible to receive
funds from the committee.
5. After hearings have taken place, the CLC Funding Committee will
determine how much they will request from the Senate Budget
Committee, and how those funds will be allocatea to the CLCs from the
Budget Committee's block funding . Deliberations shall be completed by
the third Friday of the spring semester.
6. The CLC Funding Committee Chair shall then present their findings to
the Budget Committee, during Budget VI/eek, to request the entirety of
the Block Funds then be distributed to the CLCs the following academic
yeai:,....Two Senators from the CLC Funding Committee shall draft a
resolution to recommend approval or disapproval in whole or part. The
resolution must be submitted for Student Senate hearings no later than
one (1) school week after hearing the proposed allocations.
7. Approval of the allocation requires a {2/3) vote of the Budget
Committee.

Chapters 700 through 719 of the Student Body Statutes
shall be known and hereby referred to as the "Student
Body Election Code".
The Election Code shall not be changed within three (3)
weeks of an election.
Chapter 701 Definitions
701.1 The following words and phrases, when used in this title shall
be defined as follows:
A. Campaigning - The publicizing or solicitation of support
for or against a ballot item or candidate for an
elective office of the student body, and calling forth
the action to vote.
B. Campaign Contribution - The gift or furnishing of money,
materials, supplies, professional services, or any in-
kind contribution to any campaign in any form.
C. Campaign Expenses - The fair market value of any goods
or services paid for or received by the campaign for the
purpose of advertising candidates, advertising political
parties during active campaigning, and/or calling for
an action to vote. This shall include setup or
production fees, sales tax, or any other secondary costs
for goods and services.
1. All items posted prior to the beginning of active
campaigning that do not call for the action to vote
shall not constitute a campaign expense. This
shall include all campaign materials.

sections.heading: Page 3

D.
2. Fair Market value of a single item shall be defined
as the retail (non-discounted) value of that single
item.
3. Discounted items that are available to all persons
and parties at the time of purchase shall be
exempted from fair market value criterion.
4. This section shall not be construed to apply to
speakers, volunteers, and other campaign workers of
a purely voluntary, unpaid nature.
5. To question the "fair market value" of a good or
service declared by a candidate or party, the
questioning party must obtain and submit an
affidavit from the contractor or merchant in
question disputing the candidate or party's claim
of fair market value, when such claims understates
fair market value.
Campaign Materials - any material, including but not
limited to posters, placards, signs, signboards,
leaflets, folders, handbills, fliers, banners, tee
shirts, buttons, chalk, paint, handwritten announcements
or circulars of any size and consistency that publicize
a candidate for an elected office of the student body,
and calling the action to vote.
E. Candidate - Any student seeking to be elected as an
officer of Student Government.
F. Current Inflation Adjustment - A multiplier to the
campaign expense limits based on the current Consumer
price Index (CPS) used to index campaign expense limits
to inflation or deflation. The Current Inflation
Adjustment, hereinafter referred to as the CIA, shall be
determined as follows:
CIA=(Current CPI)/(Based CPI).
The Base CPI is the CPI of September 1998 (163.6). The
Current CPI is the CPI reported for the first month of
the semester during which the election is held, or the
most recent CPI report by the US Government at the
beginning of the filing period should that month's CPI
not yet be available. In all cases, the CPI for All
Urban Consumers (the CPI-U) reported by the US
Government shall be used. The Supervisor of Elections
and the SGA Business Manager shall be responsible for
promulgating the adjusted expense limits to all
candidates and political parties.

Recall Elections
The Elections Supervisor shall conduct recall elections in
accordance with Article VII of the Student Body Constitution.
The official ballot shall state the name of the office of the
official in question, and two hundred words or less, the
reasons for demanding recall of the officer(s) as set forth in
the recall petition(s), and in no more than two hundred words
of the officer's defense. The ballot must include the
statement: "Shall the following officers retain their seats."
Voters shall vote "YES" or "NO" on the recall. A sample
ballot shall be available at each polling site in accordance
with Article VII of the Constitution.
If a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the students voting elect to
recall the official, his term of office shall cease upon
certification of the election results by the Elections
Commission. The vacancy created shall be filled as provided
by the Student Body Constitution and the Student Body
Statutes.

and the officer's defense in a campus newspaper during the

Chapter 700 Short Title
Chapters 700 through 719 of the Student Body Statutes
shall be known and hereby referred to as the "Student
Body Election Code".
The Election Code shall not be changed within three (3)
weeks of an election.
Chapter 701 Definitions
701.1 The following words and phrases, when used in this title shall
be defined as follows:
A. Campaigning - The publicizing or solicitation of support
for or against a ballot item or candidate for an elected
office of the ~tudent ~ody, and calling forth the action
to vote.
B. Campaign Contribution - The gift or furnishing of money,
materials, supplies, professional services, or any in-
kind contribution to any campaign in any form.
c. Campaign Expenses - The fair market value of any goods
or services paid for or received by the campaign for the
purpose of advertising candidates, advertising political
parties during active campaigning, and/or calling for
an action to vote. This shall include setup or
production fees, sales tax, or any other secondary costs
for goods and services.
1. All items posted prior to the beginning of active
campaigning that do not call for the action to vote
shall not constitute a campaign expense. This
shall include all campaign materials.
2. Fair Market value of a single i tern shall be defined
as the retail (non-discounted) value of that single
item.
3. Discounted items that are available to all persons
and parties at the time of purchase shall be
exempted from fair market value criterion.
4. This section shall not be construed to apply to
speakers, volunteers, and other campaign workers of
a purely voluntary, unpaid nature.
s. To question the "fair market value" of a good or
service declared by a candidate or party, the
questioning party must obtain and submit an
affidavit from the contractor or merchant in

campaign expense limits based on the current Consumer
price Index (CPS) used to index campaign expense limits
to inflation or deflation. The Current Inflation
Adjustment, hereinafter referred to as the CIA, shall be
determined as follows:
CIA=(CUrrent CPI)/(Based CPI).

Current CPI is the CPI reported for the first month of
the semester during which the election is held, or the
most recent CPI report by the US Government at the
beginning of the filing period should that month's CPI
not yet be available. In all cases, the CPI for All
Urban Consumers (the CPI-U) reported by the US
Government shall be used. The Supervisor of Elections
and the SGA Business Manager shall be responsible for

706.10 Black Student Union
A. Elections shall be carried out subject to the provision of Chapter 1003.3.
1003.3 Board of Directors
A. Membership
The Board of Directors, hereinafter collectively referred to as “Board”, shall consist of chairs
and co-chairs of respective BSU committees, of which four (4) shall be elected officers of the
BSU, hereinafter referred to as “officers”, and shall consist of staff which includes the house
manager, or any other positions created by the elected BSU officials.
B. Term of Office and Elections
1. BSU elections shall be run in accordance with Title VII of the SGA Student
Body Statutes with the exception of the rules of procedure outlined in
1003.3 B (3) and 1003.3 B (6).
a. For the purpose of BSU elections, an academic week shall be
defined as a calendar week during a semester in which classes are
in session.
2. The BSU shall have four (4) elected officers. The elections shall take place
the first Wednesday in April each year. Following the election, elected
officers shall officially take office the first week of the summer A semester.
The elected members of BSU (whose roles are defined in this chapter) are
the Director (President), Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer.
a. If the date of elections is a religious holiday, it shall be moved one (1) week by
the Supervisor of Elections. This must be done prior to
the filing deadline. i. If the Elections are moved, the Supervisor of Elections
shallinform the President of the Black Student Union, the Student Body
President, the Senate President, and the Speaker of the Congress of
Graduate Students no less than two weeks prior to the new date of the
elections or the original date of elections, whichever is earliest.
REVISED/UPDATED – January 2022193
b. The date of the election shall not be set in any manner other than
described in this chapter. This election shall be advertised as described in
Chapter 702.
3. The Black Student Union election shall follow the rules and procedure as
outlined in Title VII, with the exception of the declaration of candidacy and
party registration, which are outlined in 1003.3 B (5).
4. Campaigning is prohibited before 12:00 a.m. on the Wednesday that is one week
prior to the date of the elections.DocuSign Envelope ID: D7D84386-933E-446D-B8C5-CD72994C9666

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
5. BSU political parties must register with the Office of Elections as an SGA political party
per Chapter 704. All candidates for office shall submit their declaration of candidacy with
the Supervisor of Elections no later than 4:00 p.m. on Wednesday, two weeks before the
election.
6. No Recognized Student Organization receiving A&S Fees shall supportor
endorse an independent candidate or political party.
7. The Supervisor of Elections shall organize a debate pursuant to Chapter 702 during
the academic week of campaigning, where all candidates seeking office shall be given
fair and equal time to debate and answer questions from the electorate. The Supervisor
of Elections shall have the sole discretion to determine which questions will be asked.
8. The following shall constitute a Schedule 2 Violation, as outlined in Chapter 715.7, with
penalties, as outlined in Chapter 716.3:
a. Campaigning prior to the academic week of campaigning.
9. The BSU officers shall select the committee chairs and co-chairs of the
Board by three-fourths (3/4) majority vote. The committee chairs and cochairs shall take
office the first week of the summer session and shall serve a one (1) year term.
A. Term of Office
1. The Black Student Union President, Vice-President, Secretary, and Treasurer
shall each serve a one-year term. The President, Vice-President, Secretary, and
Treasurer’s term of office shall take effect one week after appointment, and end
one week after confirmation of the new President, Vice-President, Secretary, and

2. The term of office for the Board members shall be one year. President, Vice-
President, Secretary, and Treasurer shall not be limited to the number of terms

initial procedures.DocuSign Envelope ID: D7D84386-933E-446D-B8C5-CD72994C9666

President and confirmed by two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Senate.

Student Senate meeting of the fall semester.

must be appointed by the Student Body President
immediately be subject to Senate confirmation.

elections code. This exam shall be taken by candidates for

Student Senate shall administer the exam.
a. The candidates above must pass the exam within two (2)
attempts per semester, with at least eighty (80) percent or
more of the questions answered correctly.
3. No Supervisor of Elections shall be a candidate for any Student
Government Association office or be affiliated with any SGA
political party.

1. Deputy Supervisors of Elections shall be appointed by theDocuSign Envelope ID: 3B86F891-26DC-42FF-B93B-A4D1C9A03442

The Supervisor of Elections shall perform the following duties:
A. Ensure that SGA political parties follow the Student Body election code.
B. Ensure that all candidates meet the qualifications of the office they are
running for within three academic days following the filing deadline.
C. Employ no more than three (3) impartial Deputy Supervisors to serve an
election and assist the Office of Elections.
1. Hire, train, assign duties to, and supervise any Deputy
Supervisors of Elections.
2. Dismiss any Deputy Supervisors due to malfeasance,
misfeasance, or nonfeasance.
D. Create and implement marketing strategies to improve voter turnout for
all SGA elections.
1. At least two (2) weeks prior to the Elections, the Supervisor of
Elections shall advertise the available seats, deadlines, and
election date.
E. Enforce the Election Code subject to the approval of the Elections
Commission, when appropriate.
F. Verify the fair market value of each campaign expense, discount, or
donation through various means including but not limited to job quotes
and receipts.
G. Verify the Final Expense Statements for all candidates and political
parties.
H. Refer questions of interpretation of the Election Code to the Student
Supreme Court. The Student Supreme Court must render a written
advisory opinion within forty-eight (48) hours of any submission of a
request for an interpretation of the Election Code.
I. Supervise the approval of campaign materials. The Supervisor of
Elections shall keep records of all election results, financial information,
and campaign materials. All records shall be kept for a minimum of three
(3) years.DocuSign Envelope ID: 3B86F891-26DC-42FF-B93B-A4D1C9A03442

Elections shall be responsible for convening this meeting.

the right to request a recusal of any member of the Elections

of original jurisdiction and will hear only those cases which are forwarded
by the Supervisor of Elections pursuant to Chapter 702.4(E) of the

703.2 Powers and Duties of the Elections Commission
The Elections Commission shall have the following Powers and Duties:
A. All actions of the Elections Commission shall require the approval by a
majority present of voting members.
B. The Supervisor of Elections shall preside over Elections Commission
hearings as chair and must abstain from voting unless to break a tie. In
the event that the Supervisor of Elections recuses themselves or is
otherwise unavailable, the Vice Chair of the Elections Commission will
chair the hearing, in which case the Vice Chair must abstain from voting
unless to break a tie.
C. Submit recommendations regarding the Elections Code to the Student
Senate.
D. Appoint a Secretary selected by majority vote of the Elections
Commission, who shall record the minutes of the Elections Commission.
E. Decide and validate the agenda of the Elections Commission.
F. Upon the receipt of a complaint from the Supervisor of Elections
pursuant to Chapter 702(E)(2), the Elections Commission will schedule a
hearing to take place within five (5) business days. The Rules of
Procedure for Elections Commission hearings for appeals or alleged
violations shall be the following:
1. The Elections Commission shall notify all concerned entities
involved at least 24 hours prior to a scheduled hearing.
2. The meeting time shall not conflict with Student Senate, thereforeDocuSign Envelope ID: 3B86F891-26DC-42FF-B93B-A4D1C9A03442

sections.text:
not allowing a candidate running for re-election to attend. If a
conflict of schedule exists, the affected candidate has until five (5)
hours prior to the Elections Commission meeting to notify the
Supervisor of Elections. Candidates shall provide the Supervisor
of Elections with documentation regarding the scheduling conflict
and any excuse granted shall be in accordance with University
Policy. If no such excuse is provided to the Supervisor of
Elections, the alleged violation shall be dismissed and cannot be
resubmitted.
3. Once convened the presiding officer of the Elections Commission
shall then read aloud each appeal or alleged violation that the
Commission will hear during the meeting.
4. The Elections Commission shall hear each appeal or alleged
violation in the order that it was received.
5. Beginning with the entity who alleged an Elections Code violation,
the Elections Commission shall hear each entity’s opening oral
arguments for a maximum of five (5) minutes.
6. Once opening oral arguments are concluded, the Elections
Commission shall direct each concerned entity, beginning with
the entity who alleged a violation of the Elections Code, to
present their cases in chief by way of oral arguments not
exceeding ten (10) minutes.
7. After the first three (3) minutes of an entity’s case in chief have
expired, any currently empaneled member of the Elections
Commission is entitled to ask questions of the entity making oral
arguments. Questioning shall not penalize any entity’s respective
time limit.
8. Following the presentation of each entity’s case in chief, each
shall be entitled to a five (5) minute closing, beginning with the
entity who alleged an Elections Code violation.
9. After closing arguments have commenced, the Elections
Commission shall adjourn to deliberate for no more than one (1)
hour per violation, at which time a final majority vote must be
taken to determine if the alleged violation shall be sustained, and
the respondent found responsible for violating the Elections
Code.
10. The Elections Commission shall immediately notify all relevant
entities of the case’s disposition and shall submit to the SGA
Webmaster for posting to the SGA website, including any
concurring or dissenting opinions, within five (5) business days of
the final vote in any given case.

Constitution and Statutes.

the College that they seek to represent. Senators who file in divisions in
which they are not registered shall be removed from the ballot.

division in which they run under in that given election, unless a

declaration of candidacy form. No student may declare candidacy for
more than one office at a time. Submission of a declaration of candidacy
form shall indicate an understanding and acceptance of all filing
procedures, campaign restrictions, and the elections code and ethics

Chapter 705 Election Procedures
705.1 General Elections
A. All candidates in a general election shall declare their candidacy with the
Supervisor of Elections no later than 4 p.m. Eastern Time on
Wednesday, three (3) weeks before election day.
B. General Elections shall take place on the eighth Wednesday of the
semester in which they take place. In the case of a conflict or a religious
holiday, the Supervisor of Elections shall determine the date of election
day to be on a Wednesday between the sixth and eighth week of the
semester. The Supervisor of Elections shall announce the date of
election day no later than the third Wednesday of the semester.
1. The Supervisor of Elections shall notify the relevant SGA
governing bodies for each General Election.
a. For the Fall General Election, the Supervisor of Elections
shall notify the Student Body President, Student Senate
President, COGS Speaker, the Chair of the Campus
Recreation Board, and the SGA Advising Office of the
date and seats up for election no later than twenty-four
(24) hours after deciding the date of the Fall General
Election.
b. For the Spring General Election, the Supervisor of
Elections shall notify the Student Body President, the
Student Senate President, the Senior Class President, the
Chair of the Union Board, and the SGA Advising Office ofDocuSign Envelope ID: 3B86F891-26DC-42FF-B93B-A4D1C9A03442

sections.heading: Page 18

the date and seats up for election no later than twenty-four
(24) hours after deciding the date of the Spring General
Election.
2. Once the date of the election is determined, the Supervisor of
Elections shall send the elections calendar to the SGA
Webmaster to be published on the SGA website.
C. Campaigning is prohibited prior to 12:00 a.m. Eastern Time on the
Wednesday one week prior to the date of the elections.
705.2 Special Elections
Any Special Election shall follow the same procedure for the General Election of
the semester in which the Special Election falls in. The Senate shall provide the
funds for conducting a special election by a majority vote. The date and timeline
of any Special election shall be determined at the discretion of the Supervisor of
Elections within a three (3) week period.
A. The Supervisor of Elections shall call a Special Election for any race or
seat in which one or multiple of the following have occurred:
1. The winning candidate is disqualified in an election.
2. A campus political party is disqualified in an election where they
have won seats.
3. The results for an individual and/or an entire election are declared
invalid by the Supervisor of Elections.
705.3 Referendum Elections
The Supervisor of Elections shall conduct Constitutional Amendment and
referenda elections during the fall or spring General Elections. The admission of
referenda shall be placed on the ballot in accordance with Article VI of the

A. An electronic ballot shall be defined as the official format chosen by the
Supervisor of Elections that shall include the official rules, instructions,
candidates and other information pertinent to elections.
B. The official ballot contains the list of all offices to be elected, referendum
questions, and constitutional amendments.
1. No colors shall be used to designate or accentuate any choices
on the official ballot, including, but not limited to candidates for
office, political party affiliation or lack thereof, referendum
questions, and constitutional amendments.
C. Candidates shall be listed by seat in alphabetical order of their last
names and the name shall be printed in the same form as requested at
the time of filing. Each candidate’s last name shall appear on the ballot,
and the name must be the same as it appears on the candidate’s myFSU
account.
1. Candidates can request to have a different preferred first name
on the ballot and can request to change their name up until
twenty-four (24) hours before the election.
2. For the election of the Student Body President and Vice
President, the names of the candidates for President and Vice
President within the same party (if applicable) must appear on the
ballot as one voting bloc.DocuSign Envelope ID: 3B86F891-26DC-42FF-B93B-A4D1C9A03442

sections.text:
D. For elections to office, the ballot of a general or special election shall only
contain the names of candidate who:
1. Properly filed a Declaration of Candidacy with the Supervisor or
Elections in accordance with Chapter 704.2 of the Student Body
Statutes.
2. Are qualified to hold the office they seek as specified in Chapter
704.3 of the Student Body Statutes.
E. Candidates omitted from the ballot may petition to be reinstated by the
Elections Commission and may be reinstated following an Elections
Commission hearing no later than (3) business days prior to any election.
F. Party designation for candidates of recognized political parties who run in
an election shall be placed on the official ballot.
G. The ballot may not be changed or altered within the twenty-four (24)
hours preceding any election.
711.2 Statement of Intent
A. All ballot questions proposing constitutional amendments and referenda
shall display a “Statement of Intent” to be placed above the amendment
or referenda text.
1. The Statement of Intent shall be no longer than one hundred
(100) words.
2. The Statement of Intent shall be written by the primary sponsor of
the produced constitutional amendment and/or the sponsor’s
designee.
3. The Statement of Intent shall be presented to the Student Senate
when the amendment is put up for Student Senate approval. The
Statement of Intent shall be considered part of the piece of
legislation being voted on for approval by the Senate and shall
pass or fail jointly with its accompanying legislation.
B. The provisions of 711.2 apply to both measures proposed by the Senate
and by the petition process as enumerated in Article VI of the Student
Body Constitution.
C. The provisions of 711.2 shall not apply to any proposed constitutional
amendment pending the ballot at the time of its enactment.
711.3 Counting of Ballots and Vote Tabulation
A. The method of counting shall be done electronically.DocuSign Envelope ID: 3B86F891-26DC-42FF-B93B-A4D1C9A03442

B. The Supervisor of Elections shall announce the complete “unofficial”
results on the night of elections in the Senate Chamber during the New
Business portion of the Senate Calendar if the election is held on a day
during which there is a regularly scheduled Senate meeting. If there is no
regularly scheduled Senate meeting, the results shall be announced in
the Senate Chambers upon completion of tabulation.
1. In the event of an extended election as a result of an electronic
failure, the Student Senate President may call a special Senate
meeting the day of the extended election.
Chapter 712 Polls
712.1 Voting Process
A. Voting shall take place entirely on an electronic poll accessible to the
student body through the Student Government Elections Website on
election day. The link to the poll shall be sent in an email to the entire
student body the day of the election when polls open at 8 a.m. Eastern
Time.
B. In the event of an electronic failure of longer than two (2) hours total, the
Supervisor of Elections shall extend the election time from 9 a.m. to 2:30
p.m. the next day. The Student Senate shall appropriate the necessary
funds on the election day in question.
712.2 Recall Elections
A. An online electronic poll shall be open in the event of a recall election of
the following officials:
1. Student Body President
2. Student Body Vice President
3. Student Body Treasurer
4. Student Union Board Members
5. Campus Recreation Board Members
6. Senior Class Council Officers
7. Student Senators
712.3 Hours
A. Online polls shall be open from 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time to 7:00 p.m.
Eastern Time on the day of the election.
B. The Supervisor of Elections may extend poll hours for a period not toDocuSign Envelope ID: 3B86F891-26DC-42FF-B93B-A4D1C9A03442

1. The Supervisor of Elections shall notify all parties, candidates,
and individuals of the extension.
712.4 Polling Rules
A. No candidate nor person affiliated with a political party shall serve as an
election official.
B. When voting on the online poll, the student shall login using their FSU ID
and password.
Chapter 713 Conditions for Victory
713.1 Votes Required for Victory
A. All elected offices will be won by whoever attains a plurality of the vote.
B. In the event of a tie between two or more candidates, all candidates
involved will go before the Student Senate to determine a winner at the
next scheduled regular session of the Senate prior to Inauguration.
1. The Student Senate shall conduct the election through secret
paper ballot, and the candidate receiving the most votes shall be
declared the winner. The Student Senate President shall ensure
equal time for all candidates to speak, and equal time for
Senators to speak in favor of each candidate. The process shall
include both pro and con debate for each candidate.
2. If in the event that a candidate has an excused absence, based
on the University’s Attendance Policy, the tie-breaking vote shall
be rescheduled by the Senate President.
C. The presiding officer of the Senate shall only vote to break a tie in the
Senate.
713.2 Victory by Acclamation
A. In the event of candidates or voting blocs running unopposed in any
election at the deadline of declaration of candidacy filing, the candidates
or voting blocs shall be declared the winner of the election.
Chapter 714 Winners – Assuming Office
714.1 Announcement
A. After the results have been verified by the Supervisor of Elections, the
Supervisor of Elections shall release the final election results.
B. All results and announcements of the unofficial and/or final electionDocuSign Envelope ID: 3B86F891-26DC-42FF-B93B-A4D1C9A03442

714.2 Certification of Election
A. No Certificate of Election shall be issued to a candidate whose election is
being contested.
B. No candidates shall be installed, given the oath of office or take elective
office unless a Certificate of Election has been authorized for that
candidate by the Supervisor of Elections. This shall not apply to those
candidates appointed to fill vacancies in accordance with the Student
Body Constitution and Student Body Statutes.
C. Certificates of Election shall be given to a candidate when 701.1 R, S,
and T, have been fulfilled in a form presented by the Supervisor of
Elections.
714.3 Transition of Student Body Officers
A. Following the election, all elected officials shall be expected to have at
least one (1) transition meeting with their successor.
B. The purpose of this meeting is to review details regarding how best to
navigate the responsibilities associated with the position and any other
pertinent information that the current official sees fit for their successor to
know.
C. This shall not be misconstrued as a requirement for election certification,
but rather as an expectation of all elected student body officers.
714.4 Installation
A. The Supervisor of Elections shall provide for appropriate installation
ceremonies for duly elected candidates.
B. Any duly elected officers that are not in attendance of the formal
installation ceremony shall be installed separately by the Student Senate
within three (3) Senate meetings after the formal installation ceremonies.
No elected official shall be sworn in before the formal ceremony.
1. If a duly elected officer misses the formal installation ceremony
and is not sworn in by the Student Senate, the duly elected officer
shall immediately vacate the office in question.
C. Newly elected officers shall assume office immediately upon installation
by the Supervisor of Elections.
D. Installation ceremonies for those elected shall be held between two (2)
and five (5) weeks after the conclusion of an election.DocuSign Envelope ID: 3B86F891-26DC-42FF-B93B-A4D1C9A03442

700.1 Once the date of elections has been announced, any further amendments to the

during the fifth and final week of the election period.

77th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill/Resolution/Proclamation/PCA #: 005
Primary Sponsor(s): Cruz, Noumena
Co-sponsor(s): Brown, Lalani
Short Title: Title VII Reform: Comprehensive Amendments to the Elections Code
Summary of Legislation:
This legislation overhauls Title VII, the Elections Code, to enhance transparency,
accountability, and fairness in elections. Key provisions include replacing the campaign
materials approval system with an online public registry, revising financial disclosure
requirements, codifying processes for handling violations, halving campaign spending limits,
and altering debate and timeline procedures. Other changes and explanations for each
amendment can be found in attachment 1.
Background Information:
An election system must be clear, robust, replicable, and democratic. Unfortunately, the
current Elections Code falls short of meeting these standards. The Elections Commission lacks
key due process mechanisms, creating potential for inconsistent or unfair rulings. Loopholes in
the code enable systematic fraud. Basic errors, including typos, render some sections
unenforceable, while candidates frequently encounter unnecessary bureaucratic hurdles.
Incremental edits made over recent years have only deepened these systemic flaws. This
legislation represents the culmination of months of collaboration with members from every
branch of Student Government, addressing these issues comprehensively to build a functional,
transparent, and fair election system.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation implements a comprehensive overhaul of Title VII, the Elections Code,
introducing several major reforms to enhance transparency, accountability, and fairness in the
election process. Key provisions establish an online public registry for campaign materials,
requiring candidates and parties to submit materials for public disclosure with standardized
disclaimers; this registry eliminates the prior approval system, streamlining compliance while
improving transparency. The bill codifies processes for handling violations, emphasizing due
process by instituting clearer mechanisms for penalty assignments, default judgments for
unexcused absences at hearings, increasing reporting requirements from the Supervisor, and
restructuring point penalties. Financial disclosure requirements are revised to improve clarity
and efficiency, reducing confusion for candidates while ensuring accurate reporting and
enforcement. Campaign spending limits are halved. Debate and timeline procedures are
altered to make fall debates optional while increasing public participation opportunities for
spring debates. The bill contains several other provisions designed to further strengthen
transparency, accountability, and fairness in the election process.Docusign Envelope ID: 40C86981-F852-425F-B2EE-75BB444822FC

78th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 022
Primary Sponsor(s): Gurtis
Co-sponsor(s): Holliday
Short Title: Free Rights in Elections & Expression Act
Summary of Legislation:
This bill goes through the entire Election Code (Chapter 7 of Student Statute) and changes current
regulations pertaining to time, place, and manner restrictions. It opens up the campaigning period to be
year-round, changes locational restrictions to reflect University policy, and changes current policies
relating to posting materials, campaign finances, and free speech protections.
Background Information:
This legislation is needed because our current Election Code and the restrictions within it restrict
expression rights that are protected by both the United States and Florida Constitutions. While the
University can restrict certain forms of expression based on location and potential harm to others, they
cannot restrict a specific form of free speech such as campaigning, as our Election Code does.
Once it was found that our Election Code needed to change, other universities’ election codes and
statutes were examined to see how they imposed election restrictions while also ensuring that students’
right to expression was protected. Universities such as the University of Alabama had similar problems
of election code being too restrictive, so served as good framework to begin drafting our own changes.
Once it was found that current time restrictions on campaigning would need to be removed, the
question was raised of how this would impact campaign finances. This bill pertains almost entirely to
free speech and expression rights, so including additional section to change campaign finances
seemed extensive. There are plans to follow up this bill, should it be approved, with additional
legislation that addresses the changes that need to be made to campaign finance expenditures.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This bill was worked on extensively with Senate leadership and SG&A. The document went through 3
separate drafts before eventually being proposed to University Admin, as well as General Counsel.
From there a final draft was created and looked over by all parties, as well as the Student Body
President. Party leadership was also contacted and notified of the legislation so that they are prepared
for the changes being made to campaigning and other areas of the Election Code.Docusign Envelope ID: 9DB9DD63-A505-806B-8149-9E2FF7CAF73B

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Should this legislation be approved, it will lift current campaign restrictions to allow for year-round
campaigning. It also removes the locational ban of campaigning from dining halls, academic buildings,
the Student Union, and libraries. It also adds additional free speech protections to ensure that students
retain their right to expression and election violations pertaining to expression have set guidelines to be
followed. It also changes rules related to the Spring Debate and Executive Question and Answer Event
to set better guidelines to be followed by the Supervisor of Elections.
Finally, this bill sets more narrow restrictions on expression. Any locational time, place, and manner
restrictions are those that are already in place for all forms of speech by the University, such as posted
quiet hours in residence halls and appropriate conduct in the Student Union. All relevant time, place,
and manner restrictions are cited directly in the bill for easy access and can be updated by SG&A if and
when these citations need to change.

Proposed Amendments to Title VII (The Election Code) of the Student Body Statutes
I. Purpose
This document reviews the 12 chapters of Student Body Statutes that are being amended; specifically,
Title VII ("The Election Code"), starting at 700 and ending at Chapter 710. For each section, this
document provides the following for each amendment within the section: (1) the current statutory text; (2)
proposed amendatory language, with deletions shown in strikethrough and additions shown in underline;
(3) explanations behind changes and intent of change.
Given that Florida State University is a public institution created by the Florida Legislature, its Student
Government Association is authorized by Florida Statute Section 1004.26, and its officers take oaths of
office prescribed by statute. When SGA officials enforce the Election Code against students, they act
under color of state law. The First Amendment, therefore, constrains every provision of Title VII that
regulates the content of student speech.
II. Proposed Amendments
Section 1: Amendments to Chapter 700
Current Text, Section 700.1:
 Once the date of elections has been announced, any further amendments to the election code shall have
specific restrictions. During the five (5) week election period, amendments to the election code shall
require approval by two-thirds (2/3) of the Student Senate within the first and second weeks of the
election period, and unanimous approval of the Student Senate within the third and fourth weeks of the
election period. No amendments to the election code shall go into effect during the fifth and final week
of the election period.
Proposed Amendment:
(1) Once the date of elections has been announced, any further amendments to the election code shall have
specific restrictions. During the five (5) week election period, amendments to the election code shall
require approval by two-thirds (2/3) of the Student Senate within the first and second weeks of the
election period, and unanimous approval of the Student Senate within the third and fourth weeks of the
election period. No amendments to the election code shall go into effect during the fifth and final week
of the election period.
a. During the five (5) week election period, amendments to the election code shall require
approval by two-thirds (2/3) of the Student Senate within the first and second weeks of the
election period, and unanimous approval of the Student Senate within the third and fourth
weeks of the election period. No amendments to the election code shall go into effect during
the fifth and final week of the election period.
b. Any amendment to the Elections Code must be approved by two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate
Judiciary Committee and two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate Internal Affairs Committee.
Explanation:
This is a fairly simplistic change; it reorganizes already present information within this section to be more
easily readable, and so information of similar content is all found within the same section. This change
also strikes the current Section 700.4, since it moves that information to a clause under 700.1.Docusign Envelope ID: 9DB9DD63-A505-806B-8149-9E2FF7CAF73B

Proposed Addition Section 700.4:
(1) Protection of Free Expression
a. Nothing in this Election Code shall be construed to restrict the right of any student to engage
in political speech protected by the First Amendment to the United States Constitution and
Article I, Section 4, of the Florida Constitution.
b. All provisions of this Code shall be interpreted narrowly to avoid infringing on constitutionally
protected expression.
c. Any restriction imposed under this code on the time, place, or manner of election-related speech
must be content-neutral and narrowly tailored to serve a significant institutional interest, must
leave open ample alternative channels for communication, and must be applied equally to
campaign speech and all other categories of student expression as defined in Florida State
University guidelines.
d. No provision of this Code shall be enforced in a manner that discriminates against speech on
the basis of its political content or the viewpoint of the speaker.
Explanation:
This additional section serves as an overarching protection of free speech for students in relation to
elections and campaigning, a stipulation that doesn’t currently exist in Student Statute. The intent behind
this text is to give both the Supervisor of Elections and the Student Supreme Court a Statute to refer back
to in matters relating to free speech. Clause (a) refers to specific rights given to students by both the U.S.
and Florida Constitution to ensure that if this code is amended in the future, they understand the necessity
behind this section and its purpose of protecting students’ expression.
Sections 2 and 4: Amendments to Chapter 701
The amendments made in Chapter 701 alter Section 701.1, “Definitions,” so they are separate sections to
prevent excessive text from the abundance of definitions in this section.
Section 2: Current Text, Section 701.1(a):
Campaigning: The distribution of campaign materials, use of campaign materials, or the solicitation of
support for or against a ballot item, political party, or candidate for an elected office of the Student Body.
Campaigning shall begin the Monday at 12 a.m., one week prior to the day of the Election.
Proposed Amendment:
Campaigning: The distribution of campaign materials, use of campaign materials, or the
solicitation of support for or against a ballot item, political party, or candidate for an elected
office of the Student Body. Campaigning shall begin the Monday at 12 a.m., one week prior to
the day of the Election.
Explanation:
This sentence needs to be struck due to its overarching ban on any type of campaigning save for the one
week before elections; a lack of time, place, and manner restrictions, and this blanket prevention goes
against students’ right to expression.

Section 4: Current Text, Section 701.1(z):
False or Malicious Charges: Allegations that knowingly, deliberately or recklessly mislead, or attempt to
mislead a student regarding alleged violations of the Student Body Election Code.
Proposed Amendment:
False or Malicious Charges: Allegations that knowingly, deliberately or recklessly with knowledge of their
falsity mislead, or attempt to mislead a student regarding alleged violations of the Student Body Election Code,
filed for the purpose of harassing, intimidating, or gaining an unfair competitive advantage over the accused
party. A complaint filed in good faith based on a reasonable interpretation of the facts and the Election Code
does not constitute a false or malicious charge, even if the complaint is ultimately not sustained.
Explanation:
Under the current statute, a student who files a complaint based on an honest but ultimately
incorrect understanding of the facts or the law could be charged with a Schedule 2 violation carrying three
penalty points. The "recklessly mislead" standard is also unconstitutionally vague. The proposed
amendment raises the mental state requirement to actual knowledge of falsity, adds a purpose element,
and creates an express safe harbor for good-faith complaints.

Explanation:
This section’s amendments intend to ensure that individuals have the right to finance SGA politics and events
using their own personal funds, regardless of their affiliation to an SGA entity. While SGA entities do not have
the right to express formal opinion in relation to SGA campaigning, the individuals within the SGA entity do
and may do so through monetary expression. This reaffirms this, while also further formalizing that SGA entities
do not have the right to spend mandatory student fees or A&S fees to support or oppose an SGA item.
The additional clause is intended to clarify how campaign expenditures are reported, given that campaigning
will now be allowed on a year-round basis; the plan currently is to follow up this legislation with an additional
bill that will further address changes to financial reporting and expenditures relating to elections, but we wanted
the scope of this bill to almost entirely pertain to students’ rights and speech regulations.

a. The burden that a party alleging a violation of the Student Body Election Code must meet in
order to prove a violation shall be by “clear and convincing evidence”. Burden of Proof
(1) The burden of proving an alleged violation of the Student Body Election Code shall
rest at all times with the petitioner.
(2) The applicable standard of proof for all alleged Election Code violations shall be a
“preponderance of the evidence,” meaning that the existence of a fact is more likely
true than not true.
(3) Procedural Protections for Schedule 4 Findings
(A) A finding of responsibility for any Schedule 4 violation shall require the
affirmative vote of no fewer than two-thirds (2/3) of the members of the
Elections Commission present and voting.
(B) Any disqualification imposed on the basis of a Schedule 4 violation shall be
subject to automatic review by the Student Supreme Court, regardless of
whether the respondent files an appeal under Chapter 711.
(4) Failure to satisfy the applicable burden shall result in dismissal of the alleged violation
with prejudice for the current election cycle.
b. Students shall not be prohibited from properly registered campaign materials which are
clothing, except in the Student Senate Chambers.
(1) Wearing clothing which is a campaign material is strictly prohibited in the Student
Senate Chambers. The only exception to this rule is when the results of an election are
read aloud to the Senate by the Supervisor of Elections on the day of an election.
Explanation:
We’ve reorganized the burden of proof requirements to give both the Supervisor of Elections and the Student
Supreme Court clear guidelines as to how different Schedule violations should be treated.
While having a “preponderance of evidence” for Schedule 4 violations as well as Schedule 1, 2, and 3
violations may seem illogical, we have reasoning for this decision. Schedule 4 violations are generally done
knowingly, and as such are covered up and relatively difficult to find evidence for. If the standard for Schedule
4 violations were to be “clear and convincing evidence,” it would become very difficult to prove an
individual/party’s guilt, which removes the purpose of a Schedule 4 violation. By keeping this at “a
preponderance,” more discretion is given to both the Supreme Court, the Elections Commission, and the
Supervisor of Elections. Moreover, keeping other Schedule violations at “a preponderance” makes sense
because evidence for these violations is easily obtained via photographs and paper trail.
It’s also important to note that by making the burden of proof for all Schedule violations a preponderance of
evidence, it follows Florida Statutes regarding disciplinary proceedings (Title IX, Academic Honor Policy,
etc.).
Given the severity of Schedule 4 violations (immediate disqualification of an individual or party), further
safeguards make sense; the Election Commission’s oversight provides further ability for Schedule 4 violations
to remain at “a preponderance,” in addition to any disqualifications immediately being review by the Student
Supreme Court.
The striking of Clause (h) is done because it has been moved to an above section given that it is somewhat out
of place here.

77th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 017
Primary Sponsor(s): Noumena
Co-sponsor(s): Jackson
Short Title: Title VII Reform: Comprehensive Amendments to the Election Code
Summary of Legislation:
This Elections Omnibus Bill proposes a comprehensive set of updates to the Student
Government Election Code, aimed at resolving persistent technical and procedural issues. The
bill focuses on improving clarity, correcting outdated references, and eliminating redundancy
across multiple chapters of the Code. Notably, the authority to appoint the Supervisor of
Elections and their Deputy is shifted from the Student Body President to the Supreme Court
Chief Justice, aligning the Code with recent constitutional amendments. Several provisions
regarding campaign materials and finance reporting are also revised. The outdated campaign
material registry is removed, with oversight instead maintained through Final Expense
Statements. This reduces bureaucratic burden while preserving financial accountability.
Definitions of campaign expenses are clarified to include fair market value, while exempting
publicly available discounts. The bill also extends the time for the Elections Commission to
publish decisions from two to five business days, ensuring thorough and reasoned rulings.
Additional edits correct inaccurate statute citations, eliminate duplicative language, and
remove provisions already covered by other sections of the Code or by the Congress of
Graduate Students' electoral procedures. Collectively, these changes modernize the Election
Code by improving its legal precision, aligning it with governing documents, and promoting
transparency and fairness in the electoral process.
Background Information:
In recent years, the Student Government Association has undertaken efforts to modernize and
clarify its governing documents, including the Election Code. While past reforms made
meaningful progress, technical issues and outdated procedures have continued to cause
confusion and inefficiencies during election cycles. Ambiguities in legal language, incorrect
statute references, and redundant or unnecessary provisions have complicated enforcement
and compliance. Additionally, procedural inconsistencies and outdated responsibilities—such
as the appointment authority for election officials and the requirement to register campaign
materials—no longer reflect the current governance structure or best practices for electoral
transparency. The need for clearer rules and streamlined processes became especially evidentDocusign Envelope ID: 50A04DB7-A071-4817-845A-A4A668121A29

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
through recent election cycles, where inconsistencies in the Code impeded fair enforcement
and created administrative burdens. This bill emerges from a continued commitment to uphold
election integrity by ensuring the Election Code is legally sound, procedurally efficient, and
consistent with constitutional amendments. The proposed changes are designed to reduce
ambiguity, promote transparency, and realign responsibilities in a way that supports a fair and
accountable student government election process.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, the Elections Omnibus Bill would revise the Student Government Election Code to
address longstanding technical and procedural inconsistencies. Key changes include updating
incorrect statute references, eliminating vague or redundant clauses, and clarifying ambiguous
language—ultimately making the Code more accessible and enforceable. The bill transfers the
authority to appoint the Supervisor of Elections and Deputy Supervisor from the Student Body
President to the Supreme Court Chief Justice, aligning the Code with recent constitutional
amendments. It also simplifies campaign finance procedures by removing the outdated
requirement to register campaign materials, instead relying on final expense statements for
financial transparency. Procedural timelines are also revised to allow more time for due
process—for instance, extending the window for the Elections Commission to publish opinions
from two to five business days. Several outdated or duplicative clauses, such as mandatory
seminar rules for graduate candidates and unnecessary apportionment provisions, are removed
to reduce confusion. Overall, the legislation modernizes the election framework, enhances
accountability, and aligns legal procedures with practical enforcement, ensuring a clearer and
fairer electoral process.

Short Title:
Campaign Finance Transparency Act of 2025
Summary of Legislation:
This bill amends Chapters 701 and 709 of the Student Body Statutes to clarify the definition
and required components of Final Expense Statements. It expands financial documentation
requirements and mandates submission of a Financial Recap Summary for political parties.
Background Information:
Final Expense Statements are essential for ensuring financial transparency during Student
Government elections. However, ambiguity surrounding required documentation has led to
inconsistent reporting and oversight. This legislation was drafted in response to concerns
raised by the Office of Elections and student organizations regarding financial accountability. It
seeks to create a more structured and enforceable standard for campaign finance reporting.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation will require candidates and political parties to provide detailed
financial records, including itemized expenses, donor reports, and a verified Financial Recap
Summary. This would be for the entire year after the election season as well. It standardizes
the required documentation and aligns submission expectations with templates provided by the
Supervisor of Elections, ensuring consistency and transparency in the electoral process.

Short Title: An Amendment to Chapter 702, Chapter 705(1), and Chapter 712: ACCESS
(“Advancing Convenience and Comprehensive Electoral Scheduling”) Act
Summary of Legislation:
The aim of this bill is to make amendments to establish an extended polling period and modify
the date of the debate. General Elections shall now take place from a Monday to a Tuesday,
where online polls are open from 8:00AM to 8:00PM both days. The results of the election will
be announced prior to 11:00PM on the second day of the elections (Tuesday). The debate
must also take place during the nine (9)-day campaign period.
Background Information:
Upon the results of the election poll question regarding extending polling hours, which was
favored by the population of FSU students who votes, this bill executes this want voiced by the
Student Body. It also ensures the schedule is logistical, maintainable, and can accommodate
the various schedules of candidates and members of SGA parties. It also streamlines the
schedule so that it is clear in statutes.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This bill establishes the eighth Monday and the following Tuesday of the semester as the
election days. Polls will be open online from 8AM-8PM on both Monday and Tuesday. This
makes it a full twenty-four (24) hour window between both days for students to vote for their
representatives. Campaigning is prohibited prior to 12:00AM on the Monday one week before
the first day of elections. The Supervisor of Elections (SOE) shall announce the results prior to
11:00PM on the second day of elections/open polls. The method of this announcement shall
be up to the SOE. The debate for spring elections shall occur during the nine (9) – day
campaign period.

Senate Bill #: 036
Primary Sponsor(s): Nucatola, Collantes
Co-sponsor(s): Add any Co-Sponsors here
Short Title: Implementing Ranked Choice Voting for Elections with Three or More Candidates
Summary of Legislation: The bill amends Chapters 701 and 713 of the Florida State
University Student Body Statutes to introduce and define “Ranked Choice Voting” as a
recognized electoral method. It establishes that Ranked Choice Voting will be used in any
election where three or more candidates appear on the ballot for a single seat. This includes
positions in the Student Senate, Congress of Graduate Students, Union Board, Campus
Recreation Board, and future Student Government Association bodies to follow. This bill also
clarifies the procedure for determining a winner in case of ties, assuming no individual
candidate initially receives a majority of first-choice votes. Each ballot containing ranked choice
voting shall include, in a clear and conspicuous manner, written instructions that explain how
the ranked choice voting process functions and how to correctly mark the ballot.
Background Information:
To correlate with any possible rise in electoral candidates in future elections, ranked-choice
voting becomes an appropriate electoral structure for any rising political diversity that FSU may
foster. The global use of Ranked Choice Voting has been shown to effectively capture voter
intent when it comes to a greater variety of political candidates.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Implementation of Ranked Choice Voting ensures that elected candidates have broader
support from the student body by requiring a majority through a ranked system. It eliminates
the need for potential runoff elections, streamlining the electoral process and reducing the
administrative burden. The change encourages a more representative and inclusive voting
system. Once signed by the Vice President for Student Affairs, this legislation will go into effect
and apply to all future qualifying student elections.

Senate Bill #: 033
Primary Sponsor(s): Gurtis
Co-sponsor(s): Mendez-Arango, Gaynor, Le, Bigenho, Perantoni
Short Title: Campaign Expenditure Clarification
Summary of Legislation:
This bill is a follow-up to the previous #78-022. It clarifies expenditures outside of the election
period, and sets procedure for how expense submission works for these non-election periods.
All expenses will now be submitted in the Final Expense Statement due at the end of each Fall
and Spring’s election period; the method of submission is left to the Election Office’s discretion.
In addition, a limit is set for expenses outside of the election period to ensure that there is
framework for campaigning outside of the election period.
Background Information:
During the drafting of Bill #78-022, it was clear that finances and expense limits would need to
be addressed to account for the increased campaign time. At the time due to increased
pressure to submit the legislation in time for it to be enrolled by the end of summer, it was
decided to submit the speech regulation bill first, and follow it up with campaign expense
legislation that had the time to see proper stakeholder outreach and drafting.
The proviso already present for campaign expenses during election periods was kept entirely
intact to ensure that there was previous language that was strong enough to be built off of. The
non-election period expenses were originally proposed by a former Senator, and then built off
of with Stakeholder outreach.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This legislation was originally drafted with former and current Senators, as well as Senate
leadership. It was then reviewed by members of the Executive Branch, as well as the Elections
Office supervisor in the Office of Student Governance & Advocacy.
The Elections Office sent their recommendations regarding submission processes, which were
taken into account during the drafting process. In addition, their proposal of how to divide the
year into submission periods was used to inspire the ‘election period’ and ‘non-election period’
system proposed in this legislation.Docusign Envelope ID: 4EE5BA9A-B843-89A6-835E-031E2BE4D0D1

Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If passed, this legislation would set clear framework for how parties and independent
candidates can use campaign expenditures in the non-election periods. It also sets a clear
timeline for when these expenses are due, which will be with election period expenses in the
Final Expense Statement. Finally, this legislation will divide the year into election and non-
election periods, during which there is clearly defined procedure for expenses.
