Short Title: Amending Rule Five, Senate Rules of Procedure, to Establish a Committee
Adjournment Time
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution establishes a three-hour maximum committee meeting duration, with meetings
adjourning no later than 11:30 PM unless extended by a majority vote. This guideline is
intended to support effective student leadership within committee operations.
Background Information:
Members of the Student Senate serve as full-time students balancing academic, professional,
and personal responsibilities in addition to their legislative service. Committee meetings that
extend late into the evening may reduce productivity, weaken the quality of deliberation, and
contribute to unnecessary fatigue. Effective committee operations depend upon focused
discussion, structured agendas, and responsible use of time. Establishing a clear committee
adjournment time would encourage efficient agenda planning while reinforcing the Senate’s
commitment to effective governance.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The proposed legislation would formally establish a recommended committee adjournment
guideline for regular meetings. While committees would retain flexibility to extend meetings by
vote when necessary, this resolution promotes efficiency, intentional leadership, and improved
meeting practices within the 78th Student Senate.

a. Committee elections shall occur immediately after the reading of committee assignments
following fall and spring inaugurations. Senate shall move to enter committee caucus for
the purpose of electing Committee Chairs and Vice-Chairs.
b. The overseer of the nominations, speeches, pro-debates, and vote for the Chair position
of each of the standing committees shall be one of the following: SGA Director, Student
Senate President, and Student Senate Pro Tempore. In the event that one or more of
these overseers are absent, the Student Senate President shall designate any additional
overseers as they see fit.
c. Nominations for Committee Chair and Committee Vice-Chair shall be taken from the
committee members and shall require a second. The nominee must accept the
nomination. Each candidate shall be allowed, in alphabetical order, to address the
standing committee for no more than three (3) minutes in the form of a speech.
d. The overseer shall allow no more than two (2) committee members to speak in general,
untimed questioning.
e. The overseer shall allow no more than two committee members to speak in pro during
debate. Each committee member’s pro-debate shall last no longer than two (2) minutes.
No con-debate shall be permitted during the election process. All nominees not
addressing the standing committee shall be requested to leave the immediate area when
not speaking, including during all debate on the candidates.

including the nominees. If no candidate receives a majority, a runoff election will be held
between the two candidates who received the most votes in the first round. In the event
of a tie in the final round, the Student Senate President shall cast the tie breaking vote.
g. At this point, the overseer’s role in the election is completed. The Chair now conducts
the election for Vice-Chair. The process for the nominations, speeches, and pro-debates
for the Vice-Chair shall be the same as that for Chair. The Chair shall cast a vote in the
event of a tie.

prior to the resumption of that committee’s business. When a Senator vacates a Vice
Chair position, the Chair may appoint an interim Vice Chair for the remainder of the
meeting or immediately hold elections for the Vice Chair position. If an interim Vice Chair
is appointed, an election for the Vice Chair position must be held at the end of the
meeting where the vacancy occurred.

Vice Chair wishes to be a candidate for the position. The Student Senate President, or
member of the Office of the Student Senate President as designated by the Student

candidate for Chair, in which case the responsibility shall fall to the next most senior
member.

keep order and decorum of the meetings.

required.

and place of the committee and shall have the authority to call a meeting of the

committee meeting, the Vice-Chair shall assume the duties of the Chair, and the Chair shall

Short Title: Committee Election Procedure Reform Act
Summary of Legislation:
This Resolution amends rule 5.5 of Senate Rules of Procedure, affecting Committee Election and
Removal Procedure. This changes who is permitted to oversee election procedures for Committee
Chair Elections, and also changes the structure of debate for Committee Leadership elections.
Background Information:
The current structure of both the Senate Organizational Session and the Senate Committee Election
leaves procedure vastly different, causing confusion and not allowing for a more efficient process for all
Senate election processes. If committee leadership elections were restructured to reflect the current
procedure for the Senate Organizational Session, there would be less confusion surrounding Senate
leadership elections. Additionally, it was found that the current list of officers who are allowed to
oversee Committee elections is outdated, including a position that no longer exists within SGA.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This legislation was worked on and discussed with former and current Senate leadership and officers,
as well as former and current Committee leadership, including both Chairs and Vice Chairs. This
legislation was also written to reflect a previously passed Resolution by a former Senator that altered
the structure of the Senate Organizational Session.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If passed, this legislation will allow Senate Committee Elections to more closely resemble the
Organizational Session in terms of procedure; rather than restricting committees to only pro-debate,
this change allows for a longer period of debate that is structured according to Robert’s Rules of Order
Newly Revised, allowing Senators to have open discussion about qualities regarding their leadership.
Additionally, this legislation gives the Senate President better guidelines regarding their discretion of
who is allowed to oversee Committee Chair Elections, restricting it to members of the Office of the
Senate President with the exception of allowing non-officers to oversee Chair elections if there are not
enough officers there. This legislation also streamlines the transition from the overseer to the Chair
running the Vice Chair election proceedings.Docusign Envelope ID: F2C5B4DC-D896-8B3D-8180-B7D8524E4FCC

Short Title: Restructuring Forms of Legislation Resolution
Summary of Legislation:
This Resolution removes specific reference to legislation forms and instead refers to them as
“legislation.” This is to ensure that if legislation forms change in the future, Senate Rules of
Procedure don’t need to be largely altered to reflect the given changes.
Background Information:
Due to recent clarifications regarding forms of legislation, it was decided to reclarify how legislation
should be referred to in Senate Rules of Procedure. Because of this, an agreement was made to refer
to forms of legislation broadly in order to prevent large alterations of Senate Rules of Procedure, should
forms of legislation once again change.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This legislation was written in correspondence and discussion with the Senate President, to reaffirm the
language being used and replaced.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation will prevent large changes to Senate Rules of Procedure every time a change is made
to legislative forms, as we’ve seen increased alterations of in the past few Senates. All lists of types of
legislation will be shortened to “legislation” and singular references to a legislative type will be amended
to “piece of legislation” in order to ensure these desired effects.

72ND STUDENT SENATE
Senate Resolution
Resolution #: 94
Primary Sponsor: Gonzalez
Whereas: According to the 72nd Student Senate Rules of Procedure, the Senate
Oversight Committee has the authority to confirm or deny all nominees for appointments
approved by the committee, and
Whereas: According to the 72nd Senate Rules of Procedure, the Senate Judiciary
Committee and the Senate Rules and Calendar Committee have the authority to approve
or disapprove of nominations or appointments, and
Whereas: As per a more than three-year precedent, Senate committees have confirmed
and denied candidates for Student Government offices, without the need for denied
candidates to be considered by the Student Senate as a whole, therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-second Student Senate at Florida State University
that: The following changes be made to the 72nd Student Senate Rules of Procedure:
6.3 The Senate Judiciary Committee shall:
a. Debate, amend, reject, or recommend for passage measures pertaining to the Student
Body Constitution or Statutes.
b. Review the Student Body Constitution and Statutes and suggest possible amendments to
these documents.
c. Confirm or deny appointments or nominations to the Student Government Supreme
Court, University Defender’s Office, and General Counsel’s Office.
d. Review, consider, and if necessary, initiate impeachment proceedings against any officer
of the Student Body, as mandated in the Student Body Constitution and Statutes.
e. Conduct other hearings and undertake such other business as the Senate may
determine.
RULE SEVEN - The Rules and Calendar Committee
7.1 Composition: The President, Pro Tempore, the Chairs of each of the standing
committees outlined in Rules Six, and the chairs of the Senate Funds Distribution
Committees outlined in Rule 5.15, the Senate President Pro Tempore shall serve as the
Chair of the committee.
a. In the event a Chair of the standing committee is unable to attend a Rules and Calendar
committee meeting due to an excused reason, they may designate their vice chair to
serve in their place for that meeting upon submitting a written declaration to the Senate
President Pro Tempore.
b. In the event a Chair and vice chair of a standing committee is unable to attend a Rules
and Calendar meeting due to excused reasons, the Chair may designate another
member of that committee to serve in their place for that meeting upon submitting a
written declaration to the Senate President Pro Tempore.
7.2 The Rules and Calendar Committee shall:
a. Debate, amend, reject, or recommend passage of any amendments to the Senate Rules
of Procedure.
b. Review and suspend Senators for excessive absences as provided for in these Rules.
c. Confirm or deny the nominations of appointed Senators.
d. Facilitate communication between the officers of the Senate and ensure that a contact list
of all Senators is made and distributed to Senators.
e. Set the Calendar for the Senate.
f. Provide oversight for maintaining attendance for the Senate table in the Union during
Market Wednesday.
RULE TEN - Submission and Consideration of Measures
10.1 Definitions:
a. A "Constitutional Amendment" shall be any measure proposing a change, deletion or
addition to the Student Body Constitution.
b. A "Bill" shall be any measure proposing an amendment to the Student Body Statutes or
any measure appropriating money.DocuSign Envelope ID: E87904B8-C7DA-400D-82D9-B6268AC5AD60

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
c. "Resolutions" shall be any substantive measure which is not a bill, or constitutional
amendment.
d. A "Nomination" shall be the name of any person who has been named to candidacy to fill
a vacant position in Student Government that requires confirmation by the Senate.
e. “Confirmation” shall be defined as the approval of a nominee by the Senate, in which
case the nominee shall then immediately assume office.
f. “Statement of Dissent” shall be defined as a written explanation expressing disagreement
with any motion, action, or measure made by majority decision of the Senate.
10.2 A Senator shall file all bills, constitutional amendments or resolutions for
consideration by the Senate in the manner prescribed by statute and these Senate Rules.
10.3 Any bill or resolution filed on time shall be drawn up by the Senate Program
Assistant and distributed to members of the Senate via email and/or packets distributed
to Senate.
10.4 Any bills affecting Student Government funds which are restrictive shall state all
restrictions, earmarks, stipulations and provisions as part of the body of the bill.
10.5 All appropriations bills, unless they concern the Senate accounts, must be
accompanied by an information form detailing the need for the money, the specific uses
for the money, and alternative methods of funding which have been investigated. Any bill
appropriating money to a student organization shall include a copy of their expense
statement. This information shall be provided and signed by a member of the requesting
group or organization and shall be provided at the time bills are placed on first reading.
10.6 All bills and resolutions shall include a statement of legislative intent. All bills and
resolutions shall be written in “people-first” language. No bill shall be placed on second
reading without a statement of legislative intent or without “people-first” language.
10.7 All constitutional amendments, bills, and resolutions shall be submitted on the
appropriate forms as designated by the President.
10.8 Any measure being brought before the Senate for the first time shall be placed on
first reading, unless otherwise moved. Measures will be considered read by publication,
unless a senator objects and moves that a bill be read in its entirety by the presiding
officer. After first reading, all measures will be referred pursuant to rule 5.08.
10.9 Any measure reported out of committee(s) and committee amendments shall be
placed on second reading. Any measure on second reading is in order for consideration
by the Senate.
10.10 Confirmations: All nominees to Student Government offices requiring Senate
confirmation shall have their completed applications forwarded to the appropriate Senate
committee for consideration. The committee shall interview and question the nominee
and then vote on whether to confirm or deny them. Following the vote of the committee,
all confirmed nominees shall be called to the floor of the Senate at its next meeting and
may be questioned by any Senator wishing to do so, for a period of time to be determined
by the presiding officer. Following questions, any Senator shall move to confirm the
nominees individually.
a. Prior to any vote for confirmation being taken, but after the questioning period has
expired, any Senator may move to enter into a period of pro/con debate on any of the
nominees, which must be approved by a majority vote of the Senate. Such a motion shall
state which nominees are to be debated, and they shall be permitted to remain in the
Senate Chamber during debate if they so choose. After all rounds of debate have
expired, each nominee being debated shall have five (5) minutes to give a closing
statement as to why they should be confirmed.
b. At no time shall the presiding officer allow any debate that involves personal attacks or
slander against a nominee, although pertinent debate related to character and suitability
for office shall be permitted.
Be it further resolved that: A copy of this resolution be sent to the following individuals:

Alexander Harmon, Student Senate Pro-Tempore
Da’Shaun Scott, Student Governance and Advocacy Coordinator
Dr. Brandon Bowden, Student Governance and Advocacy Interim Director

Short Title: Due to the Board of Trustees deleting the position of SGA University Defeder from
university regulations on February 28th, 2025, this bill will reflect that change in SGA statute
and Rules of Procedure
Summary of Legislation:
A Resolution and accompanying Bill eliminate the University Defender position by removing all
references to it from the state statutes and the university’s rules of procedure.
Background Information:
The Office of the University Defender would assist students upon request who have been
accused of violations of the Student Conduct Code, or a Student Government Rule or
Regulation. University Defenders would also represent impeached officers of the Student
Body at their trial before the Supreme Court, if they are requested by the defendant to do so.
This bill and resolution will remove all references to that position.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This will remove all references to the University Defender position in rules of procedure and
statutes.

The 77th Senate made the decision to make Market Wednesday the responsibility of the

should not fall entirely on the committee to table, it falls within their scope to be in charge of
organizing such efforts in order to better connect to the student body.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This resolution would officially make it the duty of Student Life to organize tabling and outreach
opportunities, including Market Wednesday.

Senate Resolution #: 74
Primary Sponsor(s): Holliday, Mendez Arango
Co-sponsor(s): Friall
Short Title: Adding Affiliated Project Review to the Student Life Committee
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution amends the Senate Rules of Procedure to add more oversight of Affiliated
Projects in line with current precedent set in Student Body Statutes.
Background Information:
This legislation was drafted with the update from Bureau Review to Department Review in
mind. In Chapter 1100: The Affiliated Projects Act of the Student Body Statutes, section 5 says
that “the Student Life Committee, each year, shall consider whether each affiliated project
should continue in existence and receive funding, and make such recommendations in writing
to the Student Senate President. This shall occur no later than the seventh week of the Spring
semester.” This overlaps with the purpose the Internal Affairs Committee serves of reviewing
and assessing the functionality of Departments. Therefore, this legislation was created to
formalize and specifically outline the process and guidelines in which the Student Life
Committee shall evaluate Affiliated Projects in Senate Rules of Procedure.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation would create a duty in Rules of Procedure for the Student Life
Committee to evaluate Affiliated Projects, given their role to do so that is already in statute. It
will give the committee more business to hear on a regular basis during the Spring semester. It
will mirror the Internal Affairs Committee’s Department Review process.

Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Resolution #: 026
Primary Sponsor(s): Mendez Arango
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: Amending Rules of Procedure to adjust Affiliated Project Review.
Summary of Legislation:
This Resolution would amend Rule Six of Senate Rules of Procedure, adjusting Affiliated Project
Review to match recommendations from Senate Advisors. This would include shifting the review
process to the fall semester, granting more time for deliberations to be held, and establishing a four
year staggered cycle in order to not overwhelm the committee.
Background Information:
Affiliated Project Review has been the responsibility of the Student Life Committee since the passing of
the Affiliated Project Act of 1994. During the 77th Student Senate, this process was also codified in the
Student Senate Rules of Procedure to ensure the continued process for future Student Life Leadership.
However, the offices of Student Governance & Advocacy and Student Engagement have expressed
concerns over the process coinciding with the budget cycle in the Spring Semester, and possible
redundancy. Therefore, the process is being moved per their recommendations to the Fall. It was also
under their recommendation that the process is being shifted to a staggered four year cycle, in order to
have a broader view of the project in the long-term efficiency rather than the changes on a yearly basis.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Andy Johnson and Veronica Nelson, Student Senate President
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The legislation would move Affiliated Project Review to the Fall Semester, grant more time for the
Student Life Committee to visit the projects and host the deliberations, and establish four year cycle in
which the projects would be reviewed in a staggered manner. It would also establish guidelines for the
review of new Affiliated Projects.

77th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Resolution #: 062
Primary Sponsor(s): Goldstein
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: Amending the Senate Rules of Procedure to Add Vice Chairs as Ex-Officio
Members of the Rules Committee and to Establish the Senate Historian as Vice Chair of Rules
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution amends Rule Seven of the Senate Rules of Procedure to add Vice Chairs of
standing committees as ex-officio voting members of the Rules Committee, with restrictions on
voting in disciplinary and condemnation matters. Additionally, it creates a new provision
designating the Senate Historian as the Vice Chair of the Rules Committee, unless otherwise
assigned by the Chair of Rules.
Background Information:
With the deletion of PAC and RTAC Committees, the Rules Committee lost two permanent
members, reducing its ability to consistently deliberate and provide meaningful input on
legislation. At the same time, Vice Chairs of standing committees hold significant
administrative responsibilities but have limited opportunities to contribute to substantive Senate
business outside of their own committees. The Rules Committee often serves as the last stop
for legislation, yet it frequently lacks strong debate and review, limiting its effectiveness.
Including Vice Chairs as ex-officio members provides them with a constructive outlet to
exercise their leadership responsibilities while strengthening the deliberative function of Rules.
Assigning the Senate Historian as the Vice Chair of Rules ensures stable leadership support
and continuity in committee administration.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation will:
1. Expand Rules Committee membership to include Vice Chairs of standing committees as
ex-officio voting members, except on matters of suspension, unsuspension, or
condemnation resolutions.
2. Ensure Vice Chairs can contribute substantively to at least one committee, balancing
their administrative responsibilities with meaningful deliberation.Docusign Envelope ID: FCF9F602-4362-43F8-912E-79F0C6713388

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
3. Establish the Senate Historian as the Vice Chair of the Rules Committee (unless
otherwise designated by the Chair), strengthening the committee’s administrative
structure.
4. Together, these changes will enhance both the membership and effectiveness of the
Rules Committee, while empowering Vice Chairs with greater responsibility and voice in
Senate business.

78th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Resolution #: 015
Primary Sponsor(s): Bigenho
Co-sponsor(s): Add any Co-Sponsors here
Short Title: Amending Rule Ten, Senate Rules of Procedure, to Clarify Definitions and
Streamline and Codify the Amendment Process
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution updates Rule Ten of the Senate Rules of Procedure to clarify definitions of
legislative instruments and establish a structured, transparent, and uniform amendment
process. The changes align Senate procedural rules with recently adopted statutory standards,
improve clarity for Senators and the public, and enhance efficiency and predictability during
floor consideration of measures.
Background Information:
Rule Ten governs the submission, consideration, and amendment of measures before the
Student Senate. Prior to this amendment, several key terms were either undefined or
inconsistently applied, and procedures for submitting and considering amendments lacked
sufficient structure. This resulted in confusion during debate, last-minute changes to
legislation, and reduced transparency for both Senators and the public. Following the adoption
of statutory reforms to the amendment process, it became necessary to revise Rule Ten to
ensure consistency between the Senate Rules of Procedure and the Student Body Statutes,
as well as to formally codify best practices that had developed informally over time.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This bill was drafted with direct input from the Senate Rules Committee, Senate Leadership,
and the outgoing Senate Officer Team.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This resolution clarifies the definitions of legislative instruments, including bills, resolutions,
amendments, committee substitutes, and late-filed amendments. It codifies procedures for
submitting amendments in advance of Senate meetings, establishes clear voting thresholds
and debate procedures for late-filed amendments, and formalizes processes for committee
substitutes, confirmations, and statements of dissent. Collectively, these changes improveDocusign Envelope ID: 406F73AD-7203-4482-A093-B11456CACC3A

sections.heading: Page 2

legislative transparency, protect public notice, reduce administrative confusion, and ensure a
more orderly and deliberative amendment process on the Senate floor.

8 Senate on matters of policy, governance, or advocacy, and therefore should be clearly
9 distinguished from ceremonial proclamations; and
10 WHEREAS, clarifying the definitions and procedural treatment of bills, resolutions, and proclamations
11 promotes transparency, consistency, and orderly legislative practice; and

13 Senate Rules of Procedures outdated and inconsistent;
14 NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the 78th Student Senate at Florida State University that:
15 Rule 10, 8.5, and 8.6 of the Senate Rules of Procedure entitled “Submission and Consideration of
16 Measures” and “Senate Business” is hereby amended and shall read as follows:

18 1. Definitions:
19 a. A "Constitutional Amendment" shall be any measure proposing a change, deletion or
20 addition to the Student Body Constitution.Docusign Envelope ID: 406F73AD-7203-4482-A093-B11456CACC3A

agenda item “Report of the SGA Accounting Office” to “Report of Remaining Fund Balances.” This
change aligns the Rules of Procedure with the new monthly financial reporting requirements
established under the companion bill amending Chapter 409, Student Body Statutes.
Background Information:

409 (“Senate In The Sunshine”) of the Student Body Statutes. Because Rule 8.3 currently refers to this
recurring Consent Calendar item as the “Report of the SGA Accounting Office,” a title that does not
reflect the substance of the report or the new statutory language, this resolution updates the Rules of
Procedure to use consistent terminology.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:

feasibility of monthly reporting and recommended this rule change alongside the companion Chapter
409 bill.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:

“Report of Remaining Fund Balances,” consistent with the terminology used in the companion bill
amending Chapter 409.

Short Title: Senate Debate and Rules of Procedure Clarification
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution restructures Rule Nine of Rules of Procedure to move Statements of Dissent
under New Business, and Rule Ten to update Senate debate procedures. These procedural
changes will set a maximum time for debate and integrate Robert’s Rules of Order more
clearly.
Background Information:
After looking over Robert’s Rules of Order and sitting through recent Senate meetings, it has been
made clear that the current procedure adopted by Senate does not comply with Robert’s Rules of Order
Newly Revised, and is also somewhat contradictory of itself when pertaining to statements of dissent.
When looking over sections of Robert’s Rules and having discussions of what best applies to our
Senate culture and what should be revised, this resolution was drafted in order to ensure efficiency and
fairness in how debate works in the Second Reading process, while still maintaining Senate
leadership’s discretion in running an efficient meeting.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This legislation was written with particular research done into Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised
and our own current Rules of Procedure. In addition, outreach was done with the current Senate
Parliamentarian and the former Senate Parliamentarian to ensure that Robert’s Rules were being
correctly applied and that the implementation was appropriate for our Senate. In addition, this
legislation was reviewed by Internal Affairs Committee leadership, Finance Committee leadership, and
former Senators to receive input and commentary prior to submission. SG&A was contacted and sent a
copy of the legislation, and any feedback received back will be promptly taken into account.
After receiving Senator input, there was a comment of allowing sponsors the opportunity to respond to
statements made in debate. After some communication with the Senate Parliamentarian, a fair
compromise was found to allow sponsors to comment should the recognized Senator yield them the
time to do so.Docusign Envelope ID: 5C4F3720-00AC-835E-81DA-ED2A6869D442

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Should this legislation pass through the Senate, Statements of Dissent will fall under ‘New Business’ on
the Senate meeting agenda, rather than having their own distinct agenda item. In addition, our structure
of debate will slightly shift; round table will now be called ‘open debate,’ and will almost entirely contain
pro or con statements towards the given agenda item. Questions are no longer permitted outside of
general questioning unless they are asked in the form of a point of information once in open debate.
This resolution would also set a maximum amount of debate time, but allow Senators to specify a given
amount of time for debate as long as it falls under that minimum.
The definition of filibuster would also be added and addressed in this new debate structure. The
presiding officer is allowed to end a filibuster, but this may be overridden by a majority vote of the
Senate if they so choose. Finally, Robert’s Rules of Order would be more clearly cited under this new
structure of debate: motions to move into open debate, call the question, or table are all nondebatable
motions under Robert’s Rules, so if objected they will go immediately to a vote won by simple majority.
Finally, should the need arise (e.g., if several Senators are all wishing to be recognized within a short
amount of time), the presiding officer is allowed to set an amount of time for each Senator to be
recognized, but this can’t be less than 3 minutes. In addition, any time not used by the recognized
Senator can be yielded to the sponsor or candidate to allow them opportunity to comment on the
previously given statement.

Short Title: Amending Rule 9, Senate Rules of Procedure, to Fix the Implementation of Robert’s Rules
of Order and Adding a Table to Reference Vote Totals and Thresholds.
Summary of Legislation:
This legislation would amend Rule 9 of the Senate’s ROP to clean up the implementation of Robert’s
Rules of Order Newly Revised, ensure there is a clear, in text, definition of governing documents and
supremacy clauses, and creates a table to reference vote thresholds, totals, and other important pieces
of information. We include this in Rule 9 because of its already existing title, Governing Authority, which
we amend to fully read “Outlined Vote Thresholds and Governing Authority”, this properly captures
what we are trying to do with this Resolution. To the table itself, we outline most of the in-statute
requirements for different thresholds of voting, with descriptions attached and statute references
attached as well, and place a mandate on the Senate to constantly update this table with any new vote
thresholds. The table is divided into the following categories: Constitutional and Executive, Legislative
Operations and Awards, Finance and Budget, and Elections and External Acts.
Background Information:
Over the history of the Senates’ existence, different thresholds have been sprinkled into the Statutes.
Three Fourths to amend Chapter 210, two thirds to impeach, majority vote to confirm, these are
outlined in statutes not in ROP. The point of this legislation, is to make the job of a Senator easier, in
history to prepare for Senate meetings the Parliamentarian, Senate Officers and Senators themselves
were forced to find the appropriate title being amended, the statute they found relevant to this, or some
other case before they could feel confident in voting and before it could be a legal vote. This table
would provide an easy reference for the Senators.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Senate Parliamentarian Simon Monteleone, Student Governance and Advocacy Advisor Veronica
Nelson, Legislative Certification Program Participant Enock Nturbika, Senate President Alexia Holliday,
Senators in the Governing Documents Working Group, Senate Advisor Veronica, and the Senate
Officers team.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Reduce time spent by Senators attempting to cross reference information and understand vote
thresholds for each vote, along with adding clarity to the Senates operating procedures in regard to
which laws are applicable over the other.Docusign Envelope ID: D2B78E10-CBCB-489A-A880-B4F7255E5058

Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Resolution #: 042
Primary Sponsor(s): Gurtis
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: Bureau Clean Up Resolution
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution will remove any remaining mentions of bureaus from Senate Rules of
Procedure and insert Institutes into areas where other Executive Entities are being referenced,
to ensure that Rules of Procedure are reflective of all entities under the Executive Branch.
Background Information:
This legislation originated from Senate leadership, who had written similar legislation in the past that
never got enrolled. Bureaus no longer exist within SGA, and have been all but removed from virtually
every other area of Municode. In addition, given that Institutes are considered to be a part of the
Executive Branch, it was decided to include them in areas where other Executive entities such as
Agencies and Affiliated Projects were being discussed.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This legislation was reviewed by Senate leadership, and was written with guidance from Internal Affairs
Committee leadership to ensure correct information was being put into place. In addition, the
recommendation for this legislation came from the Student Senate Advisor in SG&A.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation would remove final mentions to Bureaus within Senate Rules of Procedure, and would
ensure that Institutes are being included in the relevant areas of Rules of Procedure where other
Executive entities are being included.

proposed the attached changes to the 73rd Student Senate Rules of Procedure.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-Third Student Senate at Florida State University that:
the following changes be made to the 73rd Student Senate Rules of Procedure:
RULE TEN - Submission and Consideration of Measures
10.1. Definitions:
a. A "Constitutional Amendment" shall be any measure proposing a change,
deletion or addition to the Student Body Constitution.
b. A "Bill" shall be any measure proposing an amendment to the Student Body
Statutes or any measure appropriating money.
c. A "Resolution" shall be any measure which is not a bill, constitutional
amendment, confirmation, or statement of dissent.
d. A "Nomination" shall be the name of any person who has been forwarded to
fill a vacant position in Student Government that requires confirmation by the
Senate.
e. “Confirmation” shall be defined as the approval of a nomination by the
Senate, in which case the nominee shall then immediately assume office.
f. “Statement of Dissent” shall be defined as a written explanation expressing
disagreement with any motion, action, or measure made by the Senate.
10.2. Any bill or resolution filed on time shall be drawn up by the Senate Staff and distributed to
members of the Senate via email and/or packets
10.3. Any bills affecting Student Government funds which are restrictive shall state all
restrictions, earmarks, stipulations and provisions as part of the proviso of the bill.
10.4. All appropriations bills must be accompanied by an information form detailing the need
for the money, the specific uses for the money, and alternative methods of funding which
have been investigated.
10.5. All bills, constitutional amendments, and resolutions shall include a purpose and
description section detailing a statement of legislative intent. No bill shall be placed on
second reading without a statement of legislative intent
10.6. All constitutional amendments, bills, and resolutions shall be submitted on the
appropriate forms as designated by the Student Senate President.
10.7. Any measure being brought before the Senate for the first time shall be placed on first
reading, unless otherwise moved.
10.8. Any measure reported out of committee(s) shall be placed on second reading to be heard
by the full Senate at the next meeting.DocuSign Envelope ID: C77635EF-E174-4284-A3B3-B09B925895A0DocuSign Envelope ID: 72311F71-302B-4C95-98AB-AF6135C17D69

sections.text:
10.9. All nominees to Student Government offices requiring Senate confirmation shall have
their completed applications forwarded to the appropriate Senate committee for
consideration. The committee shall interview and question the nominee and then vote on
whether to forward or deny them. Following the vote of the committee, all nominees
forwarded by the committee shall be called to the floor of the Senate at its next meeting
and shall be allowed to give an opening statement, lasting no longer than five (5)
minutes, with their remaining time being allocated to their closing. Upon conclusion of all
opening statements, candidates may be questioned by any Senator. During questioning,
any Senator may move to enter debate via a majority vote or confirm the nominees
individually via a 2/3 (two-thirds) vote.
a. A motion to enter pro/con debate shall state which nominees are to be
debated, and they shall be permitted to remain in the Senate Chamber
during debate if they so choose.
b. Upon the passage of a motion to confirm the nominees individually or to call
the question, each nominee shall have the time remaining from their opening
statement to give a closing statement as to why they should be confirmed.
10.10. The primary sponsor of any bill, constitutional amendment, or resolution may withdraw
consideration of the document from the Calendar of the Senate at any time without the
need for a formal motion.
10.11. Any amendment to a measure must be submitted in written form and must contain the
exact language of the proposed amendment including that which shall be inserted and/or,
deleted,
a. Motions to amend may be made during any round of debate and shall
require a second. If the proposed amendment is germane and receives no
objections, the presiding officer shall ask the primary sponsor if the
amendment is favorable. If the sponsor finds the amendment favorable, the
original measure shall be amended and debate shall proceed on the
measure as amended.
b. If the motion to amend is objected to or the sponsor does not find the
amendment favorable, debate on the primary measure shall halt and the
Senate shall consider the amendment as a stand-alone measure. The
Senator who made the motion to amend shall be considered the sponsor for
purposes of debate.
1. Debate on the amendment shall not address the merits of the original
measure, unless it is pertinent to the merits of the amendment.
Additionally, questions and points of information should only inquire on
the facts of the amendment itself.
c. Unless otherwise specified by the Student Body Constitution or Student
Body Statutes, a motion to amend shall require a majority vote to pass.
d. All amendments that appropriate or transfer funds to organizations that are
not part of the originally submitted bill must be individually debated on the
Senate floor, regardless if the sponsor accepts them as friendly or unfriendly.
10.12. The Senate may, at any time following the proper motion, move to committee caucus for
the purpose of expediting the consideration of any measure. A motion to move to
committee caucus shall require a two-thirds vote of the Senate. The Student Senate
President, or other presiding officer, shall reconvene the Senate at the end of the caucus.
10.13. Any Senator may, at any time, move to meet as a committee of the whole for the purpose
of discussing any Senate business. A motion to convene as a committee of the whole
may pass by consent or, if objected to, shall require a two-thirds vote of the Senate. A
motion to adjourn such a committee meeting and return to a regular Senate meeting shall
require a majority vote.DocuSign Envelope ID: C77635EF-E174-4284-A3B3-B09B925895A0DocuSign Envelope ID: 72311F71-302B-4C95-98AB-AF6135C17D69

78th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Resolution #: 027
Primary Sponsor(s): Bigenho
Co-sponsor(s): Holliday
Short Title: Amending Rule Ten, Senate Rules of Procedure, to Clarify Definitions and
Streamline and Codify the Amendment Process
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution updates Rule Ten of the Senate Rules of Procedure to clarify definitions of
legislative instruments and establish a structured, transparent, and uniform amendment
process. The changes align Senate procedural rules with recently adopted statutory standards,
improve clarity for Senators and the public, and enhance efficiency and predictability during
floor consideration of measures.
Background Information:
Rule Ten governs the submission, consideration, and amendment of measures before the
Student Senate. Prior to this amendment the procedures for submitting and considering
amendments lacked sufficient structure. Clerks, and Senate Leadership, were often burdened
with tracking down specific language for amendments, and Senators experienced confusion on
how to properly amend bills given statutory and procedural requirments to submit amendments
in writing. This resulted in confusion during debate, last-minute changes to legislation, and
reduced transparency for both Senators and the public. To aid in clarity, and fix an
administrative discrepancy with no clear outlet to submit amendments, this amendment helps
to create an Amendment Form.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This bill was drafted with direct input from the Senate Rules Committee, Senate Leadership,
and the outgoing Senate Officer Team.
A special thanks is given to SGA Webmaster Ben Young, Senate Program Coordinator
Veronica Nelson, the Senate President and Pro Tempore, Judiciary Committee Chair Leila
Jackson, and the Senate Rules Committee for its invaluable input in making this measure the
successful, clear, and concise solution it is.Docusign Envelope ID: D2AEB30F-464D-8C6E-8394-D313CF2A08A7

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This resolution codifies procedures for submitting amendments in advance of Senate meetings
and on the Senate floor. Collectively, these changes improve legislative transparency, protect
public notice, reduce administrative confusion, and ensure a more orderly and deliberative
amendment process.

72nd Student Senate
Senate Resolution #: 57
Primary Sponsor(s): Murcia
WHEREAS: There has been confusion as to when the Presiding officer of the Senate
may recognize motions to cease debate and proceed to a vote on Legislation and
pertinent motions within the current language of Senate Rule 11.10, and
WHEREAS: It is in the best interest for the Senate to offer equal opportunities for debate
to Senators in rounds of Pro and Con on the floor of the Senate, and
WHEREAS: Article II, Section 5, Clause A (1) of the Constitution of the Student Body
states, “(Senate shall) Enact its own Rules of Procedure, which shall require a two-thirds
(2/3) vote”, therefore
BE IT RESOLVED BY THE SEVENTY-FIRST STUDENT SENATE THE FLORIDA
STATE UNIVERSITY THAT: The following Senate Rules be amended as follows:
11.10 Any motion to end debate and proceed to a vote shall not be made or entertained until
one of the following instances:
a. Following the expiration of time for a round of con debate, but before it is announced by
the Presiding officer that there has been a transition into a round of pro debate.
1. If an objection is made to this motion to vote during this instance, the motion itself will
then be subject to debate.
b. At the beginning of a round of pro debate, if no time has expired and no Senators are
attempting to be recognized to debate.
1. If an objection is made to a motion to vote during this instance, the motion
shall automatically fail and the round of pro debate shall resume.
c. If there is time remaining in a round of con debate, but no Senators are attempting to be
recognized to debate.
1. If an objection is made to a motion to vote during this instance, the motion
shall automatically fail and the round of con debate shall resume.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT: A copy of this resolution is sent to the following:

Ben Young, SGA Webmaster

73RD STUDENT SENATE
Senate Resolution
Resolution #: 61
Primary Sponsors: Linksy and Little
Co-Sponsors: Nemeth, Randall, and Tackett
Whereas: The Rules of Procedure Ad Hoc committee met in Summer 2021 and
proposed the attached changes to the 73rd Student Senate Rules of Procedure.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-Third Student Senate at Florida State University that:
the following changes be made to the 73rd Student Senate Rules of Procedure:
RULE TWELVE - Student Senate Conduct Code
12.1. All individuals in attendance of a Senate meeting shall demonstrate the proper respect for
the business and procedures of the Student Senate and all other individuals in
attendance.
12.2. All individuals shall refrain from creating disturbances, especially loud conversation and
noise, during official Senate proceedings.
12.3. All Senators shall wear appropriate business or business casual attire while in the Senate
chambers. Failure to act in accordance with the said rule shall result in the dismissal of
the individual from Senate chambers at the discretion of the presiding officer.
12.4.
12.5. The presiding officer shall ensure that no Senator refers to or personally attacks another
Senator or speaker by name or gesture during debate. This rule shall exclude pertinent
debate during elections and confirmation hearings related to character and suitability for
office.
12.6. The presiding officer shall ensure that no on-campus political party is advertised in the
Senate Chambers or committee meetings. Such advertising shall consist of, but is not
limited to, t-shirts, stickers and buttons that advertise party names. No International,
Federal, State, or Local candidate or political party shall be advertised in the Senate
Chambers. This shall not limit a person in announcing a statement of fact, such as they,
or another person are running for office.
12.7. A member of the Senate shall accept nothing which reasonably may be construed to
improperly influence their official act, decision or vote.

73RD STUDENT SENATE
Senate Resolution
Resolution #: 5
Primary Sponsor: Villacorta
WHEREAS: There has been confusion over the manner in which Senators who are
unsuspended by the Rules & Calendar Committee due to excessive absences may be
absent for future meetings following their acquittal, and
WHEREAS: Article II, Section 5, Clause A (1) of the Constitution of the Student Body
states, “(Senate shall) Enact its own Rules of Procedure, which shall require a two-thirds
(2/3) vote”, therefore
BE IT RESOLVED BY THE SEVENTY-SECOND STUDENT SENATE THE FLORIDA
STATE UNIVERSITY THAT: These following Rules be amended as follows:
13.8 Penalties:
a. If a Senator is absent for three (3) committee meetings, they shall be required to meet
with their Chair to determine whether or not they should be reassigned. If a decision is
not reached in that meeting, the committee may, by a majority vote, expel a member who
has received three (3) absences. The expelled member shall be reassigned to a different
committee by the Senate President.
1. If a senator knows that they will not be able to attend the regularly scheduled
meetings of a committee, it is their responsibility to meet with the Senate
President regarding a reassignment prior to absences being accrued.
b. Any senator who accumulates seven (7) absences, both excused and unexcused, shall
be automatically suspended and forwarded to the Rules & Calendar Committee for
review over the senator’s absences. Suspended senators shall not be considered in
determining quorum, nor shall they be entitled to any rights or privileges of a Senator,
except for those related to due process of potential impeachment proceedings.
1. Taking the number of both excused and unexcused absences into consideration,
the Rules & Calendar Committee shall decide if the Senator is capable of
continuing their work as a Senator in good faith. If the Rules & Calendar
Committee finds that the Senator is no longer capable on consistent attendance,
they shall then forward the Senator to the Judiciary Committee for impeachment
proceedings, and the Judiciary Committee and shall conduct those meetings
according to all of the laws and rules related to impeachment contained in these
rules, Statutes, and the Constitution.
2. If the Rules & Calendar Committee finds that the Senator is capable of continuing
their work as a Senator in good faith, they shall unsuspend the Senator, then
propose and vote on any number of additional absences that the Senator may
accumulate before being suspended and subject to review by the Rules &
Calendar committee again.
Be it further resolved that: A copy of this resolution be sent to the following:

Senate Resolution
Resolution #: 31
Primary Sponsor: Lessard
Co-Sponsor(s): Marcus, Soto, Randall
Whereas: the only option for suspended senators is to choose to take a leave of
absence or face impeachment, and
Whereas: there is currently no rule allowing for an administrative leave of
absence, leaving suspended senators to either choose to take a leave of
absence or face impeachment, therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-third Student Senate at Florida State
University that: The Senate Rules of Procedure be amended as follows:
Rule 13- Senate Attendance
13.9. Leaves of Absence:
a. Administrative Leave of Absence: In the event of the suspension of a senator the
Rules and Calendar Committee may choose to place a senator on an
administrative leave of absence in lieu of forwarding the senator for
impeachment.
1. The duration of this leave of absence must be a minimum of one month or the
end of their term, whichever comes first, and may be extended or reduced by
a two-thirds vote of the Rules and Calendar committee
2. If the duration of the leave of absence is greater than three months, the
seat shall be temporarily vacated and filled in the same manner as other
vacant seats. The Senator on leave shall resume office at the end of the
leave of absence.
b. Summer Leave of Absence: All Senators shall be permitted to take a leave
of absence during the summer session by informing the SGA Advisor in
writing at least 2 weeks before the last Senate meeting in the Spring
Semester. Any Senate seats temporarily vacated in this manner shall be
advertised and filled in the same manner as other vacant Senate seats,
although any Senator who takes this leave of absence shall resume office
at the beginning of the fall semester.

Whereas: The Rules of Procedure Ad Hoc committee met in Summer 2021 and
proposed the attached changes to the 73rd Student Senate Rules of Procedure.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-Third Student Senate at Florida State University that:
the following changes be made to the 73rd Student Senate Rules of Procedure:
RULE THIRTEEN – Senate Attendance
13.1. Attendance at the following meetings shall be considered mandatory for all Senators and
Senate Officers. A roll call will be conducted at the beginning and end of each meeting for
the purpose of determining quorum and attendance:
a. Regularly scheduled meetings of the Student Senate as a whole.
b. All standing committees, sub committees, and ad hoc committees on which a Senator or
Senate Officer serves.
c. Any properly called special session of the Senate.
d. Any other meeting, upon concurrence of the Student Senate President and Student
Senate President Pro Tempore, with at least twenty-four (24) hour notice to all the
members required to attend.
1. The Senate may overturn this provision at any time before or after the meeting with a
two-thirds (2/3) vote.
13.2. When roll is called at any meeting and a Senator is absent or tardy, the presiding officer
must publicly state if the absence or tardy is excused or unexcused.
13.3. A Senator shall be considered as having no absences at the beginning of their term in
office. Absences will accumulate over their term in office and will be counted against the
Senator regardless of any change in the academic semester, or any intervening election
in which their seat is not up for consideration.
13.4. Failure to attend any meeting listed in this rule in its entirety shall constitute one full
absence.
13.5. Failure to be present for any one roll call that determines attendance or quorum shall
count as one-half absence.
a. Senators who are not present during the initial roll call are tardy and must check in with
the presiding officer upon entry into the meeting.
b. If a tardy Senator does not check in with the presiding officer, they will accrue one-full
absence in circumstances where a previous roll call is accepted as final roll call.
13.6. A quorum shall be defined as more than half of the voting members of the body that is
meeting.
13.7. At any time, any senator may move for a roll call to determine quorum.DocuSign Envelope ID: 7AF20540-A706-4C41-BDD8-3E5F813F9C42

a. Before a quorum call is conducted, the presiding officer shall call a three-minute recess to
allow Senators to return to the chamber.
b. In cases where quorum is not achieved and business must end, that quorum call shall be
considered the final roll call of that meeting.
13.8. Under no circumstance shall any Senator receive more than one full absence during any
one meeting, even if multiple quorum or roll calls are conducted.
13.9. Senators shall notify the appropriate presiding officer of a planned absence or tardy in
writing prior to any missed Committee Meeting or Senate Meeting.
a. If prior notice is not possible, any Senator who receives an absence or tardy shall be
required to provide a written excuse to the presiding officer of the missed meeting within
six (6) school days of the meeting. Failure to submit a written excuse within this period
will result in the absence or tardy being declared unexcused.
b. With proper documentation, the following shall be considered excused in addition to
excuses listed in the university policy on attendance:
1. Documented illness.
2. Documented attendance of a class or class-related activity.
3. Study session(s) or studying for a documented exam on the day following the absence.
4. Religious holy days
5. Calls to active military duty or jury duty.
6. Deaths in the family.

Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Resolution #: 040
Primary Sponsor(s): Rios, Tumuluri
Co-sponsor(s): Goldstein
Short Title: Amending Rule thirteen sections four, nine, and ten of the Student Senate’s Rules
of Procedure.
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution seeks to amend the Student Senate’s attendance policies by revising the
number of absences a senator may accumulate before facing penalties, as well as clarifying
the procedures for reassignment, suspension, and potential impeachment.
Background Information:
The Student Senate plays an essential role in representing the student body and making
decisions that directly impact campus life. Nevertheless, serving as a Student Senator is a
commitment that requires time, effort, and active participation. When senators miss committee
or Senate meetings, they miss important discussions and decisions that affect the students
they represent. In hopes of encouraging senators to regard their positions with the utmost
respect and commitment, we have decided to amend the attendance polices and penalties for
absences.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation will tighten the attendance requirement for the Student Senate, by amending
our rules of procedure regarding committee attendances, absences, and the penalties for
excessive absences. By strengthening the policies surrounding absences and reinforcing clear
accountability measures, we are upholding the integrity of the Student Senate and ensuring
that every elected representative fulfills their duty to serve with dedication. As elected officials
entrusted with representing the interests of the student body, we bear the responsibility of
treating these positions with the highest level of commitment, respect, and professionalism.
Through these amendments, we reaffirm our commitment to active participation and
responsible governance ensuring that the Senate remains a body that students can rely on to
advocate for their best interests.

Senate Resolution #: 014
Primary Sponsor(s): Perantoni, Naem
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: Amending Senate Rule of Procedure to Exclude Religious Holy Days from
Absence Penalties
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution amends Senate Rule of Procedure 13.4 to clarify that absences taken in
observance of a religious holy day, as recognized under Rule 13.9(b)(4), shall not constitute a
half absence. While religious holy days are currently classified as excused absences, they still
result in a half-absence penalty under existing language. This amendment ensures that the
Senate Rules of Procedure and Student Body Statutes § 206.1, which states that Student
Government Officers shall not be penalized for observing a holy day.
Background Information:
Under current Senate Rules of Procedure, excused absences result in a half absence being
assessed to the Senator. Rule 13.9(b)(4) explicitly includes religious holy days as a valid
excused absence reason. However, Student Body Statues § 206.1 provides that Student
Government Officers shall not be penalized for choosing to observe a holy day. This creates a
procedural inconsistency in which religious observance is recognized as excused yet still
carries a penalty. As members of the Student Senate represent a diverse student body with a
variety of religious backgrounds and obligations, it is important that Senate policies allow
inclusivity and statutory compliance. This legislation is presented to ensure the consistency
between both governing documents.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
In drafting this resolution, consultation occurred with student leaders representing faith-based
organizations at Florida State University. Sam Nunnally, Director of the Catholic Student
Union, expressed support for ensuring that students are not placed in a position where they
must choose between their religious observances and their civic responsibilities within Student
Government. Rameen Ahmad, President of the Muslim Student Union, also voiced support for
the amendment and affirmed the importance of protecting religious holy day observances from
penalty within Senate attendance policy. Sela Teplin, Director of the Jewish Student Union,
also voiced support for the amendment and affirmed the importance of protecting religious holy
day observances from penalty within Senate attendance policy.

Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Resolution #: 018
Primary Sponsor(s): Fernandez
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: Amending Rule Thirteen of the Senate Rules of Procedure to Codify Disability
Related Accommodations and Leaves of Absence
Summary of Legislation:
This legislation amends Rule Thirteen of the Student Senate Rules of Procedure to establish a
formal process allowing Senators to request a temporary leave of absence during their term
due to serious health conditions, family emergencies, or other significant circumstances. The
amendment also clarifies that disability-related attendance exceptions may be approved by
Senate leadership or the Rules Committee. The goal is to maintain accountability while
providing reasonable flexibility for Senators facing circumstances that affect their ability to
attend meetings.
Background Information:
The Student Senate maintains attendance requirements in order to ensure that Senators fulfill
their responsibilities, maintain quorum, and effectively represent the student body. These
expectations are essential for the orderly conduct of Senate business and for maintaining
consistent representation of the student body.
While the existing rules provide a structure for excused absences, they do not clearly establish
a process for Senators who may need a temporary pause in participation due to significant
personal circumstances. Situations such as serious health conditions, family emergencies, or
other major disruptions may make it difficult for a Senator to maintain regular attendance for a
limited period of time.
Additionally, while the Senate has historically exercised discretion when evaluating attendance
circumstances, the rules do not explicitly recognize that disability-related attendance
exceptions may sometimes be appropriate. Clarifying this possibility ensures that Senate
leadership has clear authority to make reasonable attendance determinations when necessary.
Establishing a defined leave of absence process and clarifying the possibility of disability-
related attendance exceptions helps provide transparency and predictability for both Senators
and Senate leadership. It also helps ensure that Senators facing temporary challenges are
able to communicate openly with leadership while maintaining the overall functioning of the
Senate.Docusign Envelope ID: 4D5C5986-21A0-4970-9B7E-95BC5FF44E70

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Consultation occurred with current Student Senators and Senate leadership regarding the
structure of Rule Thirteen and existing attendance practices. Outreach also included
communication with the Director of the Office of Accessibility Services (OAS) to gather
feedback regarding the inclusion of language recognizing disability-related attendance
exceptions.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation would amend Rule Thirteen of the Student Senate Rules of
Procedure to establish a formal process through which Senators may request a temporary
leave of absence during their term for serious health conditions, family emergencies, or other
significant circumstances.
The legislation also explicitly states that disability-related attendance exceptions may be
approved by the Student Senate President, Student Senate President Pro Tempore, and/or the
Rules Committee. This clarification provides Senate leadership with the authority to make
reasonable determinations regarding attendance when appropriate.
During an approved leave of absence, the Senator would not accrue absences and would not
be counted toward quorum. The Rules Committee would review leave requests and determine
the conditions under which a Senator may return to active service.

Summary of Legislation:

reform including senators who are the sole member of their delegation being exempt from the
typical responsibilities of College Delegations, as well as updating Chair and Vice-Chair
responsibilities, Constituency reports, and simplifies the oversight responsibilities of the Senate
President Pro-Tempore.

Toward the end of the 77th Student Senate, College Delegations were implemented after
substantial outreach was started from senators who organized within their college to hear from
constituents. After review and analysis, College Delegations has been presented with reform
as it relates to the scope of responsibilities and logistics.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Senate Leadership has been consulted due to the context of College Delegation’s
responsibilities and formation.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Streamline and simplify the scope and responsibilities of Student Senate College Delegations.

Senate Resolution #: 022
Primary Sponsor(s): Gaynor
Co-sponsor(s): Macalintal, Bigenho, Rivas, Ramos, Gurtis, Aihe
Short Title: The I.D.E.A. Act (Integrity of Delegation Elections Act)
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution would amend Rule 16 of Senate Rules of Procedure to change College Delegation
elections to match Committee Leadership elections. This ensures Senators who were previously unable
to vote for College Delegation leadership now can represent their interests through the election
process.
Background Information:
College Delegations were recently established to unite the members of a given college to collaborate
on issues pertaining to their constituents. Currently, Rule 16.2 defines leadership elections for College
Delegations as needing to be held yearly after the Fall inauguration. This is inconsistent with Standing
Committee leadership elections, which occur after each Inauguration. The purpose of holding
leadership elections after each inauguration, both Fall and Spring, ensures that every elected senator,
even those sworn in in the spring, can cast a vote regarding their leadership.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
The Office of the Senate President, The Office of the Senate President Pro Tempore.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This resolution seeks to apply the same principles of representation to College Delegation leadership
and clarifies the timeline in which College Delegation elections should occur. This will codify the
process by which Delegation elections should take place, taking place after Standing Committee
leadership elections.

Short Title: Establishment of New Student Organization Funding Programs and Operating
Policies & Procedures
Summary of Legislation:
Bill #77-034 creates two new student organization funding programs in the Student Body
Statutes: the RSO Allocation Committee and the RSO Development Fund. It also repeals
outdated provisions and refines the Statutes to streamline the allocation of A&S fees. The
accompanying Resolution #77-060 formally adopts operational policies and procedures for the
RSO Allocation Committee, including funding guidelines, meeting structure, and evaluation
criteria.
Background Information:
In recent years, SGA and the Department of Student Engagement have received feedback
from Recognized Student Organizations (RSOs) on campus indicating that RSOs have faced
obstacles in accessing student government funding due to duplicative, outdated, and overly
complex policies.
The Student Senate has recognized the need to restructure and simplify the process to
promote accessibility, equity, and efficiency; the FY 2025-26 SGA budget adopted by the
Student Senate contemplates eliminating the Programming Allocation Committee (PAC), the
Resource for Travel Allocation Committee (RTAC), the Organizational Fund, and the RSO
Budget Fund and replacing those funding programs with a more consolidated, streamlined
funding process that will reduce confusion and provide a “one-stop shop” for RSOs to seek
funding from SGA.
This legislation is the product of collaboration between the Student Senate, the SGA Executive
Branch, the Department of Student Engagement, and campus partners and reflects best
practices for financial governance and student engagement.

Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation will:
• Establish the RSO Allocation Committee (RSOAC) to centralize and standardize
supplemental funding for undergraduate RSOs;
• Establish elections for members of the RSO Allocation Committee to increase
transparency, democratic participation, and student voice in the allocation of A&S fees;
• Create the RSO Development Fund, providing small grants to support new and
developing RSOs;
• Repeal outdated chapters (e.g., Chapters 807 and 815) and replace them with a more
robust and efficient framework for allocating SGA funding to RSOs;
• Clarify funding eligibility, limitations, and approval processes;
• Adopt a transparent and merit-based rubric to guide allocation decisions;
• Improve communication of funding opportunities through required social media
outreach; and
• Enhance transparency in SGA’s funding allocation process and ensure that these
programs are evaluated regularly to identify recommendations for further program
enhancement in the future.
Ultimately, this legislation will enhance accountability, transparency, and equitable access to
funding for student organizations.

with the RSOAC modernization initiative (Senate Bill 77-052) to ensure consistent application
of funding criteria across all RSOs. The updated policy and rubric were created collaboratively
by members of Senate leadership, RSOAC leadership and student stakeholders. These
changes enhance procedural clarity, define the committee’s meeting and voting processes,
and ensure compliance with SGA Statutes and the Sunshine Act. All RSOs will now be
evaluated under a unified scoring framework that reflects FSU’s values of equity, fiscal
stewardship, and student development.

Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Resolution #: 030
Primary Sponsor(s): Gurtis, Iarossi
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: Judiciary Committee Rules of Procedure Amendments
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution changes parts of the current Judiciary Committee Rules of Procedure to include
all of their duties as a committee, including interviewing candidates forwarded for the Judicial
Branch and certain Executive positions. It also reorganizes information so that governing
documents are clearly noted, and citations are included when necessary. Finally, the resolution
addresses special meetings, attendance requirements, and when the roll is called.
Background Information:
After the special election, it felt prudent to look over the current Rules of Procedure for the Committee.
Upon doing so it was discovered that there is no history on the SGA website of when it was updated,
suggesting that it has been several years since the last change; thus, there was missing information
and structural changes that needed to be made.
Most of the new language in this legislation was created from the framework of others committee’s
Rules of Procedure; given that Internal Affairs is heavily focused on interviews and has clear guidelines
for how they are carried out, the language for interviews in Judiciary Committee is based on that of the
language for interviews in Internal Affairs.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This resolution was drafted by Judiciary Committee leadership and consulted on with Senate leadership
to ensure that all information was correct, and there were no contradictions between committee Rules
of Procedure and other governing documents.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation would restructure current Judiciary Committee Rules of Procedure to be more reflective
of more recently created committee Rules of Procedure, and clarify the authority and powers of the
committee. This does not introduce any new power to the committee or its leadership; it just clarifies the
information and makes it easy to access. In addition, this resolution establishes clear procedure for the
interviewing of candidates, since that is a responsibility of the committee that is carried out frequently.Docusign Envelope ID: A75FC207-D3BC-886E-80F2-CB3CF42735DA

, General
$ No A&S funded account may pay any stipend, wage, salary, or salary increase

of the Student Senate in the form of a bill or resolution, except as may be funded
in the COGS FY 2026-2027 Budget.
% In the event of shortfalls or excesses of entities funded in this budget, the Vice
President of Student Affairs, the SGA Advisor, the Student Body President, the
Senate President, the Student Body Treasurer, the Chair of the Senate Finance
Committee, and the Vice Chair of the Senate Finance Committee, shall meet to
review options. The COGS Speaker shall be invited when the shortfall involves
entities funded by COGS. No decisions shall be made without a majority vote of
the Student Senate.
& Monies allocated in the Food category shall be held in compliance with Student
Body Statute § 803.7(A) which states “No SGA branch, office, agency, bureau, or
affiliated project shall be allocated more than fifteen percent (15%) of its annual
budget in the Food category.” The Budget Committee recommends the Student
Senate shall review the 15% statutory cap and pursue possible legislative action.
' Any and all budgeted organizations found in violation of Student Body Statutes
shall be subject to the appropriate sanctions contained in the Finance Code and
recommended by the Finance Committee and the Student Senate.

items bought with A&S Fees to solely go to non-FSU students.

Short Title: Adopting the Annual Student Government Association Budget for Fiscal Year

Summary of Legislation:
This bill established the Activity & Service (A&S) Fee Budget for the 2025-2026 fiscal year,
totaling $15,391,628. It outlines the allocation of these funds among the Student Sente,
Congress of Graduate Students (COGS), and the Division of Student Affairs (DSA) for student
engagement, Union operations, and Campus Recreation.
Background Information:
The A&S Fee budget is a fundamental component of student government funding, supporting
student organizations, leadership initiatives, and university services. This allocation ensures
continued access to student resources, programming, and operational support. The budget
process follows the Florida State University Body Statutes and is subject to approval by the
77th Student Senate.
This will be the inaugural year we recognize the annual Activity & Service (A&S) Fee Budget
as Senate Bill 1851.

sections.heading: Page 9
sections.text:
I. General
A. No A&S funded account may pay any stipend, wage, salary, or salary increase to
any positions not funded in the FY 2025-2026 Budget without express consent of
the Student Senate in the form of a bill or resolution, except as may be funded in
the COGS FY 2025-2026 Budget.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses of entities funded in this budget, the Vice
President of Student Affairs, the SGA Advisor, the Senate President, and the
Student Body President shall meet to review options. The COGS Speaker shall
be invited when the shortfall involves entities funded by COGS. No decisions
shall be made without a majority vote of the Student Senate.
C. The FY 2025-2026 Budget was created under the current $12.86 per credit hour
A&S Fee. Should the FSU Board of Trustees approve an increase to the A&S
Fee, the Student Senate Budget Committee should reconvene to allocate any
additional projected funds for the remainder of the fiscal year.
D. The FY 2025-2026 Budget was created under the terms of a Memorandum of
Understanding (“MOU”) among the FSU Division of Finance and Administration,
the Division of Student Affairs, and the Student Government Association, as
approved by the 76th Student Senate in Resolution 33. The Budget Committee,
and the Student Senate as a whole, intend to fully comply with the MOU and are
of the opinion that any proviso language regarding the covered entities help
ensure quality of service and compliance with various state and university
policies, rather than non-compliance with the MOU.
E. Monies allocated in the Food category shall be held in compliance with Student
Body Statute § 803.7(A) which states “No SGA branch, office, agency, bureau, or
affiliated project shall be allocated more than fifteen percent (15%) of its annual
budget in the Food category.”
F. Any and all budgeted organizations found in violation of Student Body Statutes
shall be subject to the appropriate sanctions contained in the Finance Code and
recommended by the Finance Committee, the Budget Committee, and the
Student Senate.
G. It is the position of the Budget Committee and the Student Senate that the
current organization for the Student Government Association is no longer
providing students with the value that should come with such a large budget.
Therefore, the Senate shall enact statutory changes to reorganize the Student
Government Association in accordance with the funding structure laid out in the
FY 2025-2026 Budget.
1. In order to ensure accountability and responsibility within SGA entities,
the Senate shall introduce legislation converting executive bureaus into
departments under the Executive Branch that, either directly or through
an Executive officer who the Student Body President has ultimate
responsibility for, report to the Student Body President or redesignating
executive bureaus sufficiently affiliated with a university entity (such as
MHC) to an Affiliated Project. The legislation shall redesignate the Office
of Governmental Affairs as the Department of External Affairs.

unique circumstances, the Senate shall introduce legislation
redesignating the Homecoming Executive Council as an Affiliated

programming, the Senate shall introduce legislation making the Class

this bill, provide a written memorandum to each budgeted entity detailing the
allocated budget and any proviso language on said allocation.
