Special Instructions
I. GENERAL
A. No A&S funded account may pay any stipend, wage, salary, or salary increase to any positions not funded in Bill
2022 without express consent of the Student Senate in the form of a bill or resolution.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses of entities funded in this budget, the Vice President of Student Affairs, the
SGA Advisor, the Senate President, and the Student Body President shall meet to review options. No decisions shall
be made without a majority vote of the Student Senate.
C. Budget Bill 2022 was created under the current $12.86 per credit hour A&S Fee. Should the Local Fee Committee
propose a per credit hour increase that is accepted by the Board of Trustees, the Budget Committee should reconvene
to allocate the additional projected funds prior to the beginning of the fiscal year.
D. SGA Budgeted Offices, Agencies, Bureaus, Affiliated Projects, Organizations, and Departments are encouraged to
utilize the Sweepings Process for one-time purchases.
E. Monies allocated in the Food category shall be held in compliance with Student Body Statute 803.7(A) which states
“No SGA branch, office, agency, bureau, or affiliated project shall be allocated more than fifteen percent (15%) of its
annual budget in the Food category.”
F. Any and all budgeted organizations found in violation of Student Body Statutes shall be subject to the appropriate
sanctions contained in the Finance Code and recommended by the Finance Committee, the Budget Committee, and
the Student Senate.
II. CAMPUS RECREATION
A. It is the position of the 73rd Student Senate that the Bobby E. Leach Student Recreation Center, the Fitness and
Movement Clinic, the Intramural fields, the Rez Lakefront Park and Retreat Center, and the Rec SportsPlex have been
primarily funded by student dollars and that these facilities' primary purpose is for student recreational purposes.
B. Monies were allocated as a lump sum in the expense category with the recommendation that the Campus
Recreation Board determine its designation.
III. UNION
A. It is the position of the 73rd Student Senate that the Union Department, including various buildings and programs
across campus, has been funded by student dollars and that these facilities' primary purpose is for supporting the
student experience.
B. Any event or entertainment provided by the Union shall be free and open to all students with valid identification.
Non-FSU students shall be subject to admission fees.
C. Revenue placed in the Headliner Account shall be used for the express purpose of bringing major concert acts for
the entertainment of the Student Body. This account shall be administered by the Union with input from the Headliners
Committee, appointed by the Student Body President. An admission price may be charged to students in conjunction
with the monies used from this account. The Headliner Account shall not be swept at the end of the fiscal year.
D. It is the opinion of the 73rd Student Senate that the Headliners account should support the FSU Homecoming
expenses of Homecoming Live.
E. Monies were allocated as a lump sum in the expense category with the recommendation that the Union Board
determine its designation.
IV. SGA STUDENT ACTIVITIES AND ORGANIZATIONS
A. Agencies, Bureaus, and Affiliated Projects are strongly encouraged to utilize the event planning and contract
negotiation services offered by the Student Governance & Advocacy Accounting Office and the Union throughout the
planning and execution of any A&S funded events. Events involving a contractual service (speaker, musician,
comedian, trainer, performer, etc.) exceeding $3,000 are to be planned and negotiated in consultation with a
representative from the Student Governance & Advocacy Accounting Office and the Union prior to any verbal orDocuSign Envelope ID: 776A1916-40AE-4B02-B486-77CE2BDAF4DA

sections.text:
written commitment of such A&S funds. This clause shall only pertain to the contractual service (speaker, musician,
comedian, trainer, performer, etc.) for negotiation and not necessarily for other arrangements such as space
reservations, advertisement, or any other component of the program.
B. Monies in the Food category shall never be used for Executive Board meetings and not more than three times each
semester for General Body meetings.
C. Monies allocated to the Student Government Administration Account are expressly intended for the payment of the
FSView, telephone, computer assessment, the Holopaw, maintenance contracts, office supplies, technology, copier
and printing, advertisement, and miscellaneous expenses.
D. SGA organizations funded in Expense should prioritize programming and event needs. It is the opinion of the 73rd
Student Senate that Student Publications should be utilized for all printing, emphasizing digital publishing and
distribution of publications, specifically the SCURC Owl Publication.

expenditures as defined in Student Body Statutes Chapter 800 of the Finance Code.

organization. This decision is based on the Senate’s opinion as expressed in Resolution 9 of the 73rd Student
Senate.

801.1(B)(1)(a) which states “These budgets shall be sent to the Student Body Treasurer, the Senate Finance

conference travel and registration fees.

A. The 73rd Student Senate recommends that any budget cuts in the Union and Campus Recreation line items be
covered under the Central Reserves process.
B. The 73rd Student Senate recommends in good faith that any and all budget cuts in the Child Care Center and the
Globe Building line items be covered by the Congress of Graduate Students.
C. Any A&S monies not spent on Homecoming shall be remanded to the Headliners Artist Series.

includes the Student Body President, the Student Body Vice President, Student Senate President, Student
Senate Pro Tempore, Homecoming Director, Homecoming Live Director and Inter Residence Hall Council
Director or their designees on the Homecoming Planning Commission.

speakers for the 2022-2023 fiscal year.

Students’ budget.

Monies within the Expense account shall not go to travel expenses for Washington D.C.

Bill 2019
Activity and Service Fee Budget Proviso Language
Special Instructions
I. GENERAL
A. No A&S funded account may pay any stipend, wage, salary, or salary increase to
any positions not funded in Bill 2019 without express consent of the Student
Senate.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses, the Vice President of Student Affairs, the
SGA Advisor, the Senate President, and the Student Body President shall meet
to review options.
C. Budget Bill 2019 was created under the current $12.86 per credit hour A&S Fee.
Should the Local Fee proposal of $13.55 per credit hour be accepted by the
Board of Trustees, the Budget Committee should reconvene to allocate the
additional projected funds prior to the beginning of the fiscal year.
D. SGA Budgeted RSO and Departments are encouraged to utilize the Sweepings
Process for one time purchases.
II. CAMPUS RECREATION
A. It is the position of the ?0th Student Senate that the Bobby E. Leach Student
Recreation Center, the Fitness and Movement Clinic, the Intramural fields, and
the Rec SportsPlex have been primarily funded by student dollars and that these
facilities' primary purpose is for student recreational purposes.
B. Monies were allocated as a lump sum in the expense category with the
recommendation that Campus Recreation determine its designation.
Ill. OGLESBY UNION
A. Any event or entertainment provided by the Oglesby Union shall be free and
open to all students with valid identification. Non-FSU students shall be subject to
admission fees.
B. Revenue placed in the Headliner Account shall be used for the express purpose
of bringing major concert acts for the entertainment of the Student Body. This
account shall be administered by the Student Activities Office with input from the
Headliners Committee, appointed by the Student Body President. An admission
price may be charged to students in conjunction with the monies used from th is
account. The Headliner Account shall not be swept at the end of the fiscal year.

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
C. It is the opinion of the 70th Student Senate that Headliners Artist Series support
the FSU Homecoming expenses of Warchant and Powwow.
D. Monies were allocated as a lump sum in the expense category with the
recommendation that Oglesby Union determine its designation.
IV. SGA STUDENT ACTIVITIES, AND ORGANIZATIONS
A. Agencies, bureaus and affiliated projects are strongly encouraged to utilize the
event planning and contract negotiation services offered by the Stu dent Activities
Center throughout the planning and execution of any A&S funded events. Events
involving a contractual service (speaker, musician, comedian , trainer, performer,
etc.) exceeding $3,000 are to be planned and negotiated in consultation with a
representative from the Student Activities Center prior to any verbal or written
commitment of such A&S funds. Th is clause shall only perta in to the contractual
service (speaker, musician, comedian, trainer, performer, etc.) for negotiation
and not necessarily for other arrangements such as space reservations,
advertisement or any other component of the program.
B. Monies in the Food category shall never be used for Executive Board meetings
and not more than three times each semester for General Body meetings.
C. Monies allocated to the Student Government Administration Account are
expressly intended for the payment of the FSView, telephone , computer
assessment, the Milestone, the Torch, the Holopaw, maintenance contracts,
office supplies, technology, printing, advertisement, and miscellaneous
expenses.
D. In regards to the Office of Elections, following the spring elections any A&S fees
not needed for the Black Student Union elections shall be reverted back to the
Senate Projects account.
E. The Office of Elections shall budget for 16 election weeks and 14 non election
weeks for OPS wages.
V. SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS
A . Any A&S monies not spent on Homecoming shall be remanded to the Headliners
Artist Series.
B. The 70th Student Senate requires that at least one (1) Senate Representative
serve on all Homecoming Committees that involve A&S fees .
C. The 70th Student Senate recommends the Congress of Graduate Students fund
the remaining needs of the Childcare Center.

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
D. The ?0th Student Senate recommends the Congress of Graduate Students fund
the remaining needs of the SGA Salary Account in the salaries category.
E. The Golden Tribe Lecture Series shall limit the amount of speakers to three (3) or
less per academic year; with the recommendation of one (1) speaker in the fall,
one (1) speaker in the spring , and one (1) speaker for MLK Week activities.
1. The Golden Tribe Lecture Series Account shall not be swept at the end of
the fiscal year.
F. Executive Projects and Senate Projects are recommended to evenly share the
affiliate fee for PeaceJam.
G. Senate Branch is recommended to spend no more than $75 in the food category
per meeting which serves food .
H. The Food category of Senate Projects is designated for the SGA Fall
Inauguration.
I. The Food category of the Executive Projects is designated for the SGA Spring
Inauguration.
J. $3,000 from the OGA Expense account shall be allocated to pay for FSU's
Evening Reception at the Capitol. It is recommended that any additional funding
that may be needed be provided by the Senate Projects Account.
K. The Center for Global Engagement shall prioritize their OPS Wages for evening
and weekend space reservations for student organizations.
VI. SEVERABILITY CLAUSES
A. All clauses in the Proviso Language for Bill 2019 shall be considered fully
severable.

purposes.

the Intramural fields, and the Rec SportsPlex for activities other
than student recreational purposes must be approved by the Campus

frozen immediately until corrective action is taken.

A. Agencies, bureaus and affiliated projects are strongly encouraged

contractual service (speaker, musician, comedian, trainer,
performer, etc.) exceeding $2000 are to be planned and negotiated
in consultation with a representative from the Student Activities
Center prior to any verbal or written commitment of such A&S
funds. This clause shall only pertain to the contractual service
(speaker, mus1c1an, comedian, trainer, performer, etc.) for
negotiation and not necessarily for other arrangements such as
space reservations, advertisement or any other component of the
program.
B. No travel shall be authorized to the Florida Student Association,
the United States Student Association, or other legislative
conferences other than the money provided in the Office of
Legislative Affairs expense budget. The Student Body President,
Senate President, and the Director of Legislative Affairs shall be
given priority for travel to these conferences. Other students may
apply to be funded for travel to these events and shall be selected
by the Office of Legislative Affairs Board of Directors.
C. The Office of Legislative Affairs expense account shall be used to
fund only the following: membership in the Florida Student
Association, membership in the United States Student Association,
no more than $21,000 for travel to conferences or meetings of FSA

money under $40,000 not used in the contract of the lobbyist in the
Contractual Services line of the Office of Legislative Affairs
shall revert to Senate Unallocated.

BILL 2006
Activity and Service Fee Budget
Proviso Language
Specia1 Instructions
I. General
A. Bill 2006 does not establish precedent for future funding levels of
annual budgets.
B. The Student Body Auditor shall insure that no A&S recipient charge
admission to students to any funded event, except as provided for
in the A&S Fee Guidelines, and shall recommend to the Student Body
President that any recipient that violates this provision have
their entire budget frozen immediately.
C. No A&S funded account may pay any stipend, wage, salary, or salary
increase to any positions not funded in Bill 2006 without express
consent of the Student Senate.
D. The Student Senate must be notified of any position
reclassification request before such requests are initiated through
the University Personnel Office which concerns moneys allocated in
Bill 2006. New budgets submitted to the A&S Fee Committee and
Senate Budget Committee shall note in writing any positions
reclassified during the previous year.
E. Monies allocated for the Homecoming PowWow may be used in
conjunction with a ticket price charged to students.
F. In the event of shortfalls in the budget due to clerical errors,
funds shall be withdrawn from Senate Projects, Senate Unallocated,
and Central Reserves, in that order. In the event of excess funds
in the budget due to clerical errors, the funds shall be deposited
into Senate Projects.
G. The 57th Student Senate strongly suggests that the VPSA consult
with the Student Senate in cases where projects will result in
future A&S fee increases.
H. The 57th Student Senate strongly recommends to the VPSA that
whenever USPS and A&P positions become vacant she consult with the
Student Senate in order to review the need for the positions.
II. CAMPUS RECREATION
A. It is the position of the 57th Student Senate that the Bobby E.
Leach Student Recreation Center and Intramural fields have been
primarily funded by student dollars and that these facilities'
first purpose is for student recreational purposes.

sections.heading: Page 7
sections.text:
~
r
B.
2
Any and all use of the Bobby E. Leach Student Recreation Center and
Intramural fields for activities other than student recreational
purposes must be approved by the Campus Recreation Board. If the
policies of this Board are violated, or if the Board is not
consulted, the Senate will recommend to the Student Body President
that the funds for the entire Bobby E. Leach Center be frozen
immediately until corrective action is taken.
C. No A&S dollars shall be used for the construction nor maintenance
of any facilities where students are not privy to at least 50% of
the usage.
III.UNIVERSITY UNION
A. All mini entertainment under Student Campus Entertainment shall be
free of charge to students with valid FSU identification cards,
excluding Breakfast for a Buck.
B. Revenue placed in the Headliner account shall be used for the
express purpose of bringing major concert acts for the
entertainment of the student body. This account shall be
administered by the Student Campus Entertainment office with input
from a committee appointed by the Headliners Concert Committee,
appointed by the Student Body President and approved by Senate. An
admission price may be charged to students in conjunction with
moneys used from this account. The Headliner Account shall not be
swept at the end of the fiscal year.
C. The 57th Student Senate recommends that any A&S affiliate of the
Union to include Union Administration, consult with the Senate
before committing A&S dollars to any prospective program or
construction resulting in A&S dollar liability. Furthermore, the
57th Student Senate requests that a representative sit on all
committees that govern the Union expenditures of A&S dollars.
IV. STUDENT ACTIVITIES AND ORGANIZATIONS
A. Monies allocated to the Student Government Administration
Account/Other are expressly intended for the payment of the
Newspaper Readership Program, membership within the Florida Student
Association, WRC, lobbyist, and telephones.
B. No SA&O recipient shall fund any Salary or OPS Wages position
without approval of the Student Senate.
c. Under no condition may A&S money be allocated to any organization
that is involved in political activity with the exception of the
lobbying office in the Executive Branch.
D. Funds for Greek Council shall be used only for activities that are
available to all FSU students. No more than thirty percent (30%) of

sections.heading: Page 8
sections.text:
3
the Greek Council budget shall be allocated for travel, food, other
materials and supplies (trophies}, and other. No OPS Wages shall be
funded by Greek Council.
E. OPS Wages for SA&O Accounting and Elections will be funded in a
lump sum.
F. The 57th Student Senate and its graduate representatives request
that COGS provide appropriate funding for OPS wages needed by
Alumni Village.
G. Funding Boards may not allocate more than 20% to the food category
total for any organization.
H. Any expenditure from the Safer Connection allocation requires the
signature of both the student body president and senate president.
They may only act upon recommendations from the Safer Connection
committee.
I. The 57th Student Senate recommends that future senates fully fund the
WRC and the SGA lobbyist.
Specific Instructions
A. Any monies not spent on Homecoming shall be shifted to the Senate
Projects Account.
B. The 57th Student Senate recommends that at least 1 Senate
Representative serve on all Homecoming Committees that involve A&S
fees.
VI. SEVERABILITY CLAUSES
A. All clauses in the Proviso Language for Bill 2005 shall be
considered fully severable.

Nicole Karwowski, Overall Director, Homecoming Executive Council
RE: Approval of FY 2025-26 Homecoming Planning Commission Allocations
The Homecoming Planning Commission (HPC) is required by Chapter 616, Student Body
Statutes, to distribute the funding appropriated to Homecoming in the fiscal year (FY)
2025-26 Activity & Service Fee Budget. This year, the Student Senate appropriated
$292,350 for homecoming-related activities. The HPC heard presentations and deliberated
Homecoming requests on July 16, 2025, and approved allocations as follows:
$17,000 to the Student Alumni Association for Expenses
$275,350 to Homecoming and Homecoming Live with:
$4,250 allocated in the Food category
$15,100 allocated in the Clothing and Awards category
$248,650 allocated in the Expense category
$7,350 allocated in the OPS wages category, with recipients prescribed in the
annual budget proviso
I am grateful to the Homecoming Planning Commission for their work and look forward
to seeing the incredible events to be put on by the Homecoming Executive Council later this
year. Minutes and a recording of the HPC meeting are available to the public on CivicPlus.
77th Senate President Pro Tempore
Chair, 2025-26 Homecoming Planning Commission

Whereas: Chapter 815, Student Body Statutes establishes a “Recognized Student Organization
(RSO) Budget Fund” to provide financial support for operational expenses and event planning,
creating a stable budget for otherwise independent Recognized Student Organizations; and
Whereas: The FY 2024-25 SGA Budget included an allocation of $150,000 for the RSO Budget
Fund; and
Whereas: The RSO Budget Fund Committee opened an application window on October 25,
2024, through November 1, 2024, to receive funding applications from RSOs on campus; and
Whereas: The Committee leadership and Student Body Treasurer’s office evaluated all of the
applications received and developed a list of recommended funding allocations reflecting the
most effective and efficient use of this funding, which was presented to the Student Senate
Budget Committee for consideration at its December 2, 2024, meeting; and
Whereas: The Student Senate Budget Committee met on December 2, 2024, to consider this
list of recommended allocations and made several amendments to best meet the needs of the
student organizations on campus and the Florida State University student body.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-seventh Student Senate at Florida State University that:
Allocations from the RSO Budget Fund are made for FY 2024-25 as provided in Attachment #1
to this Resolution.
Be it further resolved that: In order to best support student activities on campus, the
remaining balance of $13,649.74 from the RSO Budget Fund shall be reallocated to the
Resource for Travel Allocations Committee (RTAC) for the remainder of Fiscal Year 2024-25.

2023 SWEEPINGS PROVISO
I. GENERAL
A. No account funded by A&S fees may pay any stipend, wage, or salary increase to any
positions not funded in Sweepings 2023 without the express consent of the Student
Senate in the form of a resolution separate to that of the Sweepings Allocation.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses, the Vice President of Student Affairs, the SGA
Advisor, the Student Senate President, and the Student Body President shall meet to
review options.
C. All purchase requests shall be received prior to May 31, 2024.
D. Any unspent funds shall be returned to the Sweepings account.
II. OPS WAGES
A. Monies allocated to the Union in the OPS Wages Category shall be used to pay wages
for student workers for the 2023-2024 fiscal year.
B. OPS Wages allocated to the Student Government Executive Branch shall be used to
make the Chief of Staff an OPS paid position in accordance with §803.5.
C. OPS Wages allocated to the Black Student Union shall be used to create an OPS paid
front desk receptionist position to be funded at a rate of $12/hour at 20 hours/week for
16 weeks in the Spring 2024 semester in accordance with §803.5.
D. OPS Wages allocated to the Center for Leadership and Service shall be used to create
an OPS paid TedXFSU Intern position, and an OPS paid ServeScript Intern Position.
III. SGA OFFICES
A. Part of the monies allocated to the Student Governance and Advocacy office in the
expense category shall be used to purchase two (2) SGA Seals, three (3) flagpole kits
and flags, one (1) conference table, one (1) TV, one (1) PC, and one (1) conference
room webcam.
B. None of the monies allocated to the Student Governance and Advocacy office shall be
used to develop the “Let’s Budget” Simulation Game.
C. Of the funds allocated in the category of expense to The Office of Student Agencies and
Institutes, $3,000 shall be used for Lavender Celebration Stoles, $3,000 shall be used
for V-rak-ke-ce-tv Cultural Celebration stoles, and $1,000 shall be used to purchase
merchandise for Graduate Student Kickback.
IV. SGA BUDGETED ORGANIZATIONS AND DEPARTMENTS
A. Monies allocated to Campus Recreation in the expense category shall be allocated to
Leach Center Fitness Flooring Replacement, Outdoor Pursuits equipment, the LakefrontDocuSign Envelope ID: A0C70111-343C-4E40-85BD-3FC66869D5F4

sections.heading: Page 7
sections.text:
Shuttle Program, and climbing wall upgrades. Any remaining funds may be used at the
discretion of the department.
1. Monies allocated to The Sports Clubs Council should first be used to purchase
scuba equipment and water polo goals. Remaining funds shall be used at the
department’s discretion.
B. All monies allocated in the expense category to the Student Union shall be controlled by
the sole discretion of the student-elected Union Board members.
C. All monies allocated to the Student Union shall not be transferred to the Replacement
and Renovation Account.
D. Monies allocated to FSU Class Councils shall be used to fund the Senior toast, the
movie screening in partnership with the Askew Student Life Cinema, and the Spring
Fair.
E. Funds allocated to FSU Class Councils shall not be used to purchase merchandise.
V. AGENCIES
A. The Hispanic Latinx Student Union is encouraged to request the Senate to consider a
transfer bill to effectuate the purchase of t-shirts under the Expense category.
B. The Jewish Student Union is encouraged to request the Senate to consider a transfer bill
to effectuate the purchase of t-shirts under the Expense category.
VI. AFFILIATED PROJECTS
A. No more than $2,000 in the Expense category of WVFS Tallahassee 89.7 FM shall be
used to purchase Chairs for the facility.
VII. OUTSIDE DEPARTMENTS
A. Monies allocated to FSU Libraries shall only be used for the purchase of physical books
for the Pop-Lit Section.
B. Monies allocated in the O.C.O category to the Academic Center for Excellence Learning
Studio shall be used to purchase upgrades to furniture.
C. Monies allocated to the University Health Services department shall not be used for the
purchase of a spinning wheel.
D. Monies allocated to the FABLAB-Innovation Hub shall be used to fund two (2) Large XL3
Printers, and two (2) Medium MK4 Printers.
VIII. RECOGNIZED STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS
A. Monies allocated to the Business Case Club must be used for travel to conferences.DocuSign Envelope ID: A0C70111-343C-4E40-85BD-3FC66869D5F4

Hanukkah Party.

D. Monies allocated to the Caribbean Students’ Association shall be used for Pageant
Catering and T-Shirts.
E. Monies allocated to Every Nation Campus Tallahassee shall be distributed evenly
amongst all FSU student travelers for registration fees.
IX. SEVERABILITY CLAUSE

I. GENERAL
A. No account funded by A&S fees may pay any stipend, wage, or salary increase to any
positions not funded in Sweepings 2022 without the express consent of the Student Senate.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses, the Vice President of Student Affairs, the SGA Advisor,
the Student Senate President, and the Student Body President shall meet to review options.
C. All purchase requests shall be received prior to May 31, 2023.
D. Any unspent funds shall be returned to the Sweepings account.
II. OPS WAGES
A. Monies allocated to the Union in the OPS Wages Category shall be used to pay wages for
student workers for the 2022-2023 fiscal year.
B. Monies allocated to the Elections Office in the OPS Wages Category shall pay for the Deputy
Supervisors of Elections for the 2022-2033 fiscal year.
1. The most senior Deputy Supervisor of Elections shall be paid at a rate of $10/hour at 5
hours per week, for six weeks; $11/hour at 10 hours per week for the 3 weeks pertaining
to Elections Week; and $11/hour at 5 hours per week for 6 weeks, totaling $960.
2. The junior Deputy Supervisor of Elections shall be paid at a rate of $10/hour at 5 hours
per week, for six weeks; $11/hour at 5 hours per week for the 9 weeks pertaining, totaling
$795.
C. Monies allocated to the Center for Health Advocacy & Wellness in the OPS Wages Category
shall be used to pay wages for a student facilitator for the Substance Use Intervention Training
(SUIT) Program.
D. Monies allocated to the RISE Office in the OPS Wages Category Shall be used to pay wages
for a student assistant i n the 2022-2023 fiscal year.
III. SGA OFFICES
A. Monies allocated to the Department of Student Engagement shall pay for storage lockers for
Recognized Student Organizations, Lounge Furniture, Certiport software for one (1) year, two (2)
Power Bars, sixteen (16) HON Pillow-Soft Bonded Leather High-Back Chairs, and window
frosting for the 3rd floor of the new Student Union Building offices. Any remaining funds shall be
used at the discretion of the recipient.
IV. SGA BUDGETED ORGANIZATIONS AND DEPARTMENTS
A. Monies allocated to Campus Recreation in the Expense Category shall be used to purchase
sixteen (16) paddleboards, sixteen (16) kayaks, and two (2) SportsPlex Zero Turn Mowers.
V. AGENCIESDocuSign Envelope ID: 46AD6E51-6FAD-4CE8-B467-66C33A462F5F

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
A. Monies allocated to the Pride Student Union in the Expense Category shall be used for
expenses pertaining to their planned travel to the 2023 Creating Change conference in San
Francisco, CA. This conference must be open to all members of the Student Body.
B. Monies allocated to the Womens’ Student Union in the Contractual Services Category shall be
used to pay for a musician to perform at FSU for Women’s History Month in March 2023. $2,500
in the Expense Category shall be reserved for start-up funds for programming pertaining to the
Nineteen Ten Women’s Honorary.
C. Monies allocated to the Jewish Student Union in the Food Category shall be used to purchase
food for Passover meals in Spring 2023.
D. Monies allocated to the Asian American Student Union shall not be used to purchase office
supplies.
VI. AFFILIATED PROJECTS
A. Monies allocated to the Medical Response Unit shall be used to purchase two (2) Stop the
Bleed training kits and two (2) Electric Golf Carts.
B. Monies allocated to WVFS in the Expense Category shall be used to purchase an Orban
Optimod 5700i Processor and for engineering and labor costs pertaining to a podcasting studio.
Monies allocated in the Operating Capital Outlay (OCO) Category shall be used to purchase an
MDL 102102 Standard Model Whisper Room.
VII. OUTSIDE DEPARTMENTS
A. Monies allocated to the Career Center at FSU shall be used for an Iris Headshot Booth, and
related shipping fees, installation fees, and three years worth of annual services.
B. Monies allocated to the FabLab at the Innovation Hub shall be used for four (4) Prusa MK3s+
3D printing machines and four (4) Prusa enclosures for said machines. Additional funds shall be
used to pay for related shipments and estimated customs duty.
C. Monies allocated to the Innovation Hub in the Food Category shall be used for the Seminole
Innovators’ Lunch Hour with Featured Innovators.
D. Monies allocated to the RISE Office in the Clothing & Awards Category shall be used for the
V-rak-ke-ce-tv ceremony and the Lavender Graduation.
VIII. RECOGNIZED STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS
A. Monies allocated to the African Student Association shall not be used towards any
scholarships or fellowships.
B. Uniforms or costumes purchased with monies allocated in the Expense Category to the Attack
Dance Crew shall be reusable and available to the entire team, regardless of members’ ability to
pay dues.DocuSign Envelope ID: 46AD6E51-6FAD-4CE8-B467-66C33A462F5F

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
C. Monies allocated to Hillel FSU shall be used to purchase food for Passover meals in the
Spring of 2023.
D. Monies allocated to iGem in the Expense Category shall only be used for the 2023 team
competition. Monies allocated in the Clothing & Awards Category shall only be used for iGem
apparel.
E. Monies allocated to Florida PIRG Students shall not be used towards any scholarships or
fellowships.
F. Monies allocated to the Master of Public Health Student Association shall be put towards their
FSU Health Conference in Spring 2023.
G. Monies allocated to the FSU Chapter of the NAACP shall be used for contractual services,
expenses, food, and clothing & awards related to their collaborative programming with Florida
Agricultural & Mechanical University (FAMU) in Spring 2023. Goods bought with A&S fees must
go to Florida State University students.
H. Uniforms or costumes purchased with monies allocated in the Expense Category to the
Nolettes shall be reusable and available to the entire team, regardless of members’ ability to pay
dues.
I. Monies allocated to the FSU Chapter of the Tau Beta Sigma Fraternity shall be used for their
Greater Music Benefit Concert.
J. Monies allocated to TEDx FSU shall be used for the food in the reception in the 2023
TEDxFSU conference, and all food purchased with A&S monies must be available to all
attendees of the conference.
K. Monies allocated to White Mouse Productions shall be used for a 192 sq ft. Portable Stage
System.
L. Monies allocated to the World Affairs Program shall be explicitly spent on travel, lodging, gas,
mileage, and registration fees pertaining to conferences and be spent in line with the provisions
of the Finance Code and Student Body Statutes.
IX. SEVERABILITY CLAUSE
A. Any part, provision, or representation of this Bill which is prohibited or which is held to be void
or unenforceable shall be ineffective to the extent of such prohibition or unenforceability without
invalidating the remaining provisions hereof.DocuSign Envelope ID: 46AD6E51-6FAD-4CE8-B467-66C33A462F5F

I. GENERAL
A. No A&S fee funded account may pay any stipend, wage, or salary increase to any positions not
funded in Sweepings 2021 without the express consent of the Student Senate.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses, the Vice President of Student Affairs, the SGA Advisor, the
Senate President, and the Student Body President shall meet to review options.
C. All purchase requests shall be received prior to May 31, 2022.
D. Any unspent funds shall be returned to SGA.
II. OPS WAGES
A. Monies allocated to the Congress of Graduate Students in the OPS Wage Category shall be used
to pay for CPR and AED trainers during CPR and AED training sessions under the supervision of
Campus Recreation during the Fall and Spring Academic Calendars.
B. Monies allocated to the Center for Global Engagement in the OPS Wage Category shall be used to
pay for Event Staff through the 2021-2022 fiscal year. Event Staff shall receive minimum wage for
twelve (12) hours per calendar week in which they perform the duties of their position during the FSU
Fall and Spring academic calendars. The event staff shall receive a minimum wage of ten (10) hours
per calendar week during the Summer Academic Calendar. Twenty-seven (27) calendar weeks of pay
have been made available to these positions at these rates; these weeks of pay shall coincide with
the remainder of the 2021-2022 fiscal year.
C. Monies allocated to the Student Governance & Advocacy office in the OPS Wage Category shall
be used to pay for OPS Wage deficits that occurred from the minimum wage increase for SG&A OPS
employees at the determination of their administration.
D. Monies allocated to TEDxFSU in the OPS Wage Category shall be used to pay for a parking
attendant for an event. The parking attendant shall be paid at twenty-five (25) dollars per hour for
eight (8) hours.
E. Monies allocated to the Jewish Student Union in the OPS Category shall be used to pay for the
Jewish Student Union Director’s wages during the Spring Academic Calendar. The Director shall
receive minimum wage for five (5) hours a week in which they perform the duties and responsibilities
of their position. A total of fifteen (15) calendar weeks of pay have been made available for this
position at this rate.
F. Monies allocated to FSU Libraries in the OPS Wage Category shall be used to pay for tutors during
the 2021-2022 fiscal year.
G. Monies allocated to Campus Recreation in the OPS Wage Category shall be used to cover wage
deficits that occurred from the minimum wage increase for Campus Recreation OPS employees at the
determination of their administration.
H. These terms and stipulations on OPS waged individuals shall only apply to the positions and
offices mentioned in this section. All remaining ops waged positions may be paid at the rate and hours
deemed appropriate by the respective department or organization in accordance with the funds
available.
III. SGA OFFICESDocuSign Envelope ID: 4FE036F3-9B59-44C0-9226-9CFDDA1708E1

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
A. Monies allocated to the SG&A Administration in the Expense Category shall be used for the
purchase of Dell Towers, Dell Laptops, Dell Docking Stations, and Dell Monitors. Any remaining funds
shall be used at the discretion of the recipient. Under no circumstance shall these funds be used to
compensate for outstanding legal fees or to hire legal services.
IV. SGA BUDGETED ORGANIZATIONS AND DEPARTMENTS
A. Monies allocated to the Congress of Graduate Students (COGS) shall be used to purchase AEDs
to be installed in 23 dormitories, as well as for contractual services and food. All funds must be spent
by the end of the fiscal year. Any unspent funds shall be returned to SGA.
B. Monies allocated to the Center for Global Engagement in the Operating Capital Outlay (OCO)
Category shall be used to purchase a replacement of the Globe Dining Room Hot Line Serving
Station.
C. Monies allocated to the World Affairs Program in the Expense Category shall not be used to fund
international travel or international competitions of any kind.
V. AGENCIES
A. Monies allocated to the Pride Student Union in the Expense Category shall be used for the
purchase of eighteen (18) sets of professional clothing for their clothing closet.
VI. AFFILIATED PROJECTS
A. Monies allocated to the Medical Response Unit in the Expense Category shall be used for the
purchase of lights & branding for the 2021 Ford F-150, branding for the command center trailer,
vehicle maintenance, new responder bags, and golf cart storage.
B. Monies allocated to WVFS V-89 in the Operating Capital Outlay (OCO) Category shall be used to
purchase a full compact FM transmitter and two MF Digital Ripstation 7000 models 7602 II and 7604
II.
VII. FUNDING BOARDS
A. Monies allocated to the Sports Club Council in the Expense Category shall be used exclusively to
cover travel expenses for its club teams and the requested amount of basketballs. Any unspent funds
shall be returned to SGA.
VIII. OUTSIDE DEPARTMENTS
A. Monies allocated to the Center for Academic Retention and Enhancement in the Operating Capital
Outlay (OCO) Category shall be used to purchase two (2) seventy-five (75) inch VIBE Boards. Monies
allocated in the Expense Category shall be used to purchase ten (10) fifty-five (55) inch VIBE Boards
and furniture for the twenty-six (26) Thagard Building study rooms.
B. Monies allocated to the Center for Health Advocacy and Wellness in the Operating Capital Outlay
(OCO) Category shall be used to purchase a massage chair. This massage chair shall be open to the
entire student body for use.
C. Monies allocated to iGem in Operating Capital Outlay (OCO) Category shall be used to purchase
an Ultra-Low Temperature Freezer.
D. Monies allocated to the Global Scholars in the Clothing and Awards Category shall be used to
purchase t-shirts at no more than eight (8) dollars per unit. Any extra cost per unit shall be covered by
Global Scholar’s non-A&S fee budget.DocuSign Envelope ID: 4FE036F3-9B59-44C0-9226-9CFDDA1708E1

shall be used for the purchase of a three-door commercial refrigerator.
F. Monies allocated to Florida State University Libraries in the Operating Capital Outlay (OCO)
Category shall be used for the purchase of an electronic catalogue of course materials and workshop
materials.
H. Monies allocated to the RISE Office in the Expense Category shall be used for regalia for their
cultural graduation.
IX. REGISTERED STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS
A. Monies allocated to the Catholic Student Union in the Expense Category shall be used to purchase
a tent. In ordinance with Student Body Statute 802.5(E), this tent shall not be used for proselytizing.
B. Monies allocated to the Chinese American Student Organization in the Clothing and Awards
Category shall be used to purchase seventy-five (75) t-shirts at no more than eight (8) dollars per unit.
Any extra cost per unit shall be covered by the Chinese American Student Organization’s non-A&S
fee budget.

Category shall be used to purchase t-shirts at no more than eight (8) dollars per unit. Any extra cost
per unit shall be covered by the Chinese Student and Scholar Association’s non-A&S fee budget.
D. Monies allocated to the College Republicans at Florida State University in the Contractual Services
Category shall be used to compensate for the services of a speaker. In ordinance with Student Body
Statute 803.6(B), all contractual expenditures in excess of $3,000 require the approval of the Student
Senate by resolution. Any unspent funds shall be returned to SGA.
E. Monies allocated to DREAM in the Clothing and Awards Category shall be used to purchase t-

To: Caroline Chance, 63rd Student Senate President, and 63rd Student Senate
From: Dustin R. Daniels, 20 I 0-20 II Student Body Pres ident
Date: December 7'" , 20 10
Re: Justification for Vetoing of Bill 8
Dear Madame President Chance and members of the 63rd Student Senate:
Below is my justification for the presidential veto of Senate Bill 8.
As the elected officials of the student body, we are charged with supporting and preserving the
success and happiness of our fellow students. The large part of our business revolves around the
Activity and Service Fee, which through State Statute 1024 3(c)l0 gives the student government
the right to control and allocate. As you are well aware, it is the Student Senate's responsibility to
allocate and in some ways manage the money of students, with the checks, balances, and
collaboration of the Executive Branch. The Student Body Constitution and Statutes~ s the
Student Body President the responsibi li ty and priv il ege to veto all major legislation forn the
Senate. It is the responsibility of the executive not to take this charge lightly, and veto ly if
such legislation is fo und, in the executi ve's mind, to be: repugnant, ill-advised, illegal, or harming
of SGA or the student body in any way.
With that said, I am line-i tem vetoing the recommended allocations for the First Responders,
Senate Proj ects, and the $5,000 in contractual services for the Office of Greek Life. After careful
consideration and seeking counsel from some members of my administration, I feel that these
allocation recommendations are ill-advised and a poor use of money in these harsh economic
times. The begin with, the First Responders allocation of$12,544 to pmchase a golf cart is an
unneeded expense and ties one of our affiliated projects to a capital investment that requires
constant re-investment and repair. The allocation recommendation of $9,000 to Senate projects,
especially with the already large sum in this account, without an outline, proposal, or plan is in
my view very unfair to the organizations and SGA entities that put hours of work into their
proposals. Finally, the allocation recommendation of$5,000 to the Office of Greek Life for a
speaker in the Spring seems to be aga in an ill-advi sed decision, as Greek Life has had problems
thi s year with following accounting protocol and it now is seemingly being rewarded for this
mismanagement, not to mention the fact that the Office of Greek Life is not a line-item in our
annual budget, leaving the possibility of them getting funds from PAC. Unfortunately the latter
point is untrue for all the organizations and entities that requested funds from sweepings. For
these reasons I respectfull y veto the sa id allocations.
Dustin R. Daniels
2010-2011 FSU Student Body President

\ Attached you will find that I have signed the sweepings bill. I feel that it is
r
important to note, however, that I am concerned about the allocation to the
executive branch for $33,500 for contractual services.
My concern focuses on two areas. First, the University is required to bid any
contracts over $50,000. While your initial allocation is less than that, the proviso
recommends matching that which would clearly exceed the minimum level to bid.
Secondly, the bid process would guarantee that you are receiving the best product
for the best price. It is my understanding that another university will be paying
much less for what appears to be the same services.
By way of this memo, I am asking you to work with Joyce Howard and Marcie
Doolittle, Director of Purchasing to prepare a request for proposal to comply with
state law.
Thank you.

Line Item Vetoes ofthe Sweepings Bill
Issue 1- Environmental Service Program
The veto of the ESP budget was based solely on the premise that the funding of the
Assistant Director's salary wou ld require the use of non-recurring revenue for recurring
costs. The Executive Branch has since learned that the Assistant Director' s position~ill
be funded in the upcoming budget, and thus the veto is RESCINDED.
Issue 2- Cultural Diversity Conference
It is the position of this administration that student Activity and Services Fees shall not be
allocated to any facet of the university administration no matter how worthy the cause.
The Division of Student Affairs has a budget, and the Executi ve Branch would urge the
division to strongly consider Dean Bowen's proposal. I take this action not only to
administer fiscal responsibility on these specific dollars, but also to prevent students
being double charged for administrative services from both tuition and fees in the future.
Issues 3 &4 - FSU NORML and FSU Students Against Sweatshops
The funds allocated to both of these groups was specifically intended, by the Sweepings
Committee, to be used for very specific programs, and not simply for supplemental
funding. I strongly believe that these groups must carry out these intentions in the
spending of their allocations. As the bill currently stands, the funding is not binding, and
this is the reason for the vetoes. If the 55th Student Senate would like to issue binding

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
-..
l
proviso language for the dollars allocated to FSU NORML and USAS, the Student Body
President's office would support this measure.
Issue 5- The Women's Center
Diversity and inclusive representation is of paramount importance to the success of our
institutions. The Women's Center must then actively seek and include programming that
appeals to all students on our campus, regardless of personal views or precedent. As a
part of the Executive Branch, I cannot allow the Women's Center to put forth and be
funded for programming that continuously alienates this portion of campus.
With this in mind, Ms. Davida Silverman and myself have come to an agreement to
resolve this issue. Ms. Silverman and her board will produce a plan within ten business
days of Wednesday, January 08,2003, that shows a programming schedule that
accomplishes these goals. These programs will be added to the already scheduled slate of
programming that is set for Women's History Month. If this is not accomplished, or the
programming does not come about, funding for the Women's Center will then be frozen.
Per this agreement, the veto is RESCINDED.

Art Ulrich, SGA Advisor

The Sixtieth Student Senate - 2008 Central Reserves
PROVISO LANGUAGE
1. We, the 60th Student Senate, hereby authorize Central Reserves recipients to transfer funds
between the Expense and OCO category as needed, within a specific line-item allocation.
2. The 60th Student Senate recommends that Crenshaw Lanes set aside some time period on a
routine basis for free bo\vling by FSU students with appropriate ID.
3. It is the opinion of the 60th Student Senate that the Krentzman Lounge TV bear a sign
indicating that it \Vas funded by SGA with students' A&S Fees.
4. The funds designated for the Oglesby Union Art Center's portable walls may only be spent
to that end. If the Art Center decides not to invest in the walls, these funds should be not
spent and returned to the 60th Student Senate through the Sweepings process.
5. If the Women's Center is unable to wire a Swipe Card, the 60th Student Senate asks that a
comparable locking mechanism is substituted.
6. The 60th Student Senate supports the creation of an OPS Assistant for the Pride Student
Union. This position was funded at $9 an hour and 20 hours a week for eight weeks. After
July 1, the 60th Student Senate strongly encourages the transfer of funds into the OPS
category to continue fmancing this new addition to Pride.
7. Of the expense allocation to Pride, only $1000 is authorized to be used as a blanket purchase
order to Lo\ve's. No fountain is to be purchased with these funds.
8. The OCO allocation to the Alumni Village Childcare Center will cover the cost of
purchasing the larger playground plus freight charges. The 60th Student Senate strongly
recommends that the Center place signage recognizing the contributions made by SGA and
the students of the Florida State University.
9. It is the express intent of the 60th Student Senate that the $400 allocated to Student
Publications for the purchase of 2 digital cameras available for check out by RSOs. The
availability of these cameras should be advertised.
10. The CMAC allocation on behalf of All Night Yahtzee is only to be used for travel to ICCA
Semifinals or Finals. In the case that ANY does not qualify for ICCA Finals, these funds
may not be spent and must be returned to the 60th Student Senate through the Sweepings
process.

Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 005
Primary Sponsor(s): Fernandez
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: Amending Chapter 709 to Prohibit Physical and Verbal Campaigning in Academic
Classrooms.
Summary of Legislation:
This bill amends Chapter 709 of the Student Body Statutes to reclassify campaigning in
academic buildings from a Schedule One to a Schedule Two violation. The legislation also
explicitly prohibits verbal campaigning and in-person solicitation inside classrooms and other
instructional spaces to close existing gaps in the Election Code.
Background Information:
During review of the current Election Code, it was identified that while posting campaign
materials in academic buildings is regulated, verbal campaigning inside classrooms was not
explicitly prohibited or classified under the existing violation schedules. This created a loophole
that allowed candidates to engage in in-class solicitation without clear consequences. The
sponsors consulted directly with the Supervisor of Elections, who reviewed and approved the
proposed changes to ensure alignment with election administration standards and fairness
principles. This legislation is particularly important for smaller colleges and academic
programs, where classroom sizes are small and students often know each other personally. In
these environments, in-class campaigning can exert disproportionate influence and
significantly impact election outcomes, raising concerns about coercion and equity. Academic
spaces are intended to remain neutral environments dedicated to learning. Allowing
campaigning within these spaces risks disrupting instruction and placing pressure on students
in a setting where they cannot easily opt out.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation will reclassify campaigning in academic buildings as a Schedule Two
violation, increasing penalties to better reflect the seriousness of the misconduct. It will
explicitly prohibit verbal campaigning and in-person solicitation inside classrooms and
instructional spaces, close existing loopholes in the Election Code, strengthen election
integrity, and ensure greater fairness across campus by preventing undue influence in
academic settings.VETOED

This was vetoed due to the following:
Per the RSO guidelines https://brand.fsu.edu/recognized-student-organizations:
Recognized Student Organization must include the word “club” or similar identifier in the
name of the organization. Identifiers include but are not limited to: Club, Society,
Association, Sorority, Fraternity, Council, Institute, Group, Committee, Students,
Students For…, Campus Ministry, Ambassadors, Recruiters, Fellowships, Community,
Greek Letters and/or Chapter.
Recognized Student Organization names cannot imply the RSO is endorsed by the
university or otherwise affiliated with the university
Recognized Student Organizations may include the words “at Florida State University”
along with or as part of their organization’s name. Acceptable alternatives include “at
Florida State” or “at FSU.” This designation may not appear larger than the rest of the
Recognized Student Organization name.
Recognized Student Organizations logos may not incorporate any additional Florida
State University trademarks or references into the logo. FSU’s trademarks include
standard character marks such as the letter combination FSU, as well as the words
Florida State, Florida State University, Fear the Spear, Doak, Seminoles, Seminole, and
Noles.
Appropriate alternative names for this RSO could be:
Students Involved in Politics at FSU
Students for Political Engagement at FSU
Students Engaged in Politics at FSU
Based on this, neither “Noles Involved in Politics” or “Seminoles Involved in Politics” would be
permitted, as both include protected standard character marks and do not have a club
identifier. However, given that the organization has used this “Noles in Politics" for some time,
we are OK letting this name stand, but we will leave that option open to your final decision.
They may run into licensing issues if they choose to purchase merchandise with their name on
it as “Noles” is a protected standard character mark.

to accurately reflect its current operations and role in preparing students for FSU Day at the

Affairs and serves as a professional development and civic engagement initiative for Florida
State University students. This bill is presented to ensure consistency between the Student
Body Statutes and the program’s existing structure, mission, and operations. By formally
defining SEP within Chapter 301, the amendment provides clarity for future students,
administrators, and Student Government leadership regarding the program’s purpose,
oversight, and selection process.

This bill updates and standardizes statutory language related to the Seminoles Engaged in
Politics Program without altering its operational authority or mission. If enacted, it will ensure
accuracy, clarity, and continuity within the Student Body Statutes regarding the program’s
name, purpose, and placement under the Office of Governmental Affairs.

Short Title: Allocating $2,000 from Senate Projects for the Class of 2026 Senior Class Gift
Summary of Legislation: This legislation seeks to allocate $2,000 from the Senate Projects
account to the Senior Class Council for the procurement and installation of communal seating
as the Class of 2026 Senior Class Gift. These funds will cover all costs associated with the
purchase and shipping of high-quality couches to be permanently placed in the Oglesby
Student Union terrace, providing a lasting enhancement to campus lounge spaces. By funding
this initiative, the Senate will ensure a tangible contribution to the Florida State student
experience.
Background Information:
The Class Councils are an executive entity of the FSU Student Government Association
dedicated to fostering campus traditions and leaving a lasting impact on each graduating class.
For the first time in years, the Senior Class Council is taking donations from Registered
Student Organizations and the local community to furnish the Oglesby Student Union’s
second-floor terrace. This legislation aims to allocate $2,000 from Senate Projects to procure
and install communal seating for the student body to enjoy.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This bill was drafted with the co-sponsorship of Senate President Holliday and the Senior
Class Council's leadership.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation will officially transfer $2,000 from the Senate Projects account to the
Senior Class Council to finalize the funding for the Class of 2026 Senior Class Gift. This
transfer will result in the permanent installation of communal seating on the Oglesby Student
Union’s second-floor terrace, directly enhancing the quality of shared lounge spaces for all
students. Beyond the physical beautification of the Union, this bill strengthens the collaborative
relationship between the Student Senate and the Class Councils by supporting shared
student-led initiatives. Ultimately, the project fosters a more visible and engaged on-campus
presence for student government while providing a lasting benefit to the Florida State
community.Docusign Envelope ID: 482D4D2A-4819-4766-A911-DF541AF92F5E

78th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 018
Primary Sponsor(s): Bigenho, Nucatola
Co-sponsor(s): Mendez Arrango, Tumuluri
Short Title: Creating Chapter 511, The Office of Auditor General, for Consolidated Oversight
and Review Improvements.
Summary of Legislation:
This bill creates Chapter 511 of the Student Body Statutes, establishing the Office of the
Auditor General as an independent oversight entity within the Student Government
Association. It outlines the structure, selection process, qualifications, term length, renewal
procedures, removal standards, and vacancy procedures for the Auditor General and Deputy
Auditors General.
The bill establishes a five-member Auditor General Selection Board composed of the Student
Body President, Student Senate President, Student Body Treasurer, Chief Justice of the
Supreme Court, and Speaker of the Congress of Graduate Students. The selected nominee
must be confirmed by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Senate.
The legislation further defines the powers and duties of the Office, including auditing financial
activity, reviewing compliance with statutory and fiscal regulations, maintaining anonymous
reporting mechanisms, issuing public reports, ensuring non-retaliation for whistleblowers, and
publishing findings. Additionally, the bill amends Chapter 100 to designate the Auditor General
and Deputy Auditors General as major offices within Student Government.
Background Information:
The Florida State University Student Government Association manages significant Activity &
Service (A&S) fee funds and oversees numerous executive departments, agencies, boards,
and affiliated projects. While existing statutes establish financial procedures and transparency
requirements—including the Sunshine Act (Chapter 203), the External Transparency and
Digital Records Act (Chapter 210), and Title VIII: The Finance Code—there is currently no
independent internal oversight body charged exclusively with auditing compliance,
investigating violations, and safeguarding institutional accountability across all branches of
Student Government.

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
In light of the increasing complexity of Student Government operations and financial
allocations, the establishment of a structurally independent Office of the Auditor General would
strengthen transparency, deter misconduct, ensure adherence to appropriations and proviso
language, and provide a formal mechanism for anonymous reporting and systematic review.
Creating this office codifies a permanent, neutral oversight authority within Student
Government.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This bill was drafted with the direct input of the Student Body Treasurer and other members of
the Student Body Treasurers Office and RSO Allocation Committee. It was also discussed with
members of the Department of Student Affairs, and with contact to the Office of Audit and
Advisory Services.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Upon passage, this legislation formally establishes a new, independent Office of the Auditor
General within Student Government, creating a centralized authority responsible for
investigations, audits, compliance review, and financial oversight. The bill introduces structured
appointment and confirmation procedures, conflict-of-interest safeguards for the Selection
Board, defined qualifications for service, and clear standards for removal.
The Office will gain administrative access to relevant record systems, require the preservation
of documents under review, and mandate the publication of audit reports and semesterly
summaries. It also creates statutory protections for anonymous reporting and whistleblower
non-retaliation, while ensuring that audited officers retain the right to respond before the
appropriate Senate committee.
By amending Chapter 100 to classify the Auditor General and Deputies as major offices, the
bill subjects these positions to the same accountability and ethical standards applicable to
other high-level Student Government officials. Overall, the legislation strengthens institutional
transparency, enhances fiscal accountability, and establishes an enduring internal oversight
framework within the Student Government Association.

Senate Bill #: 028
Primary Sponsor(s): Macalintal, Gurtis
Co-sponsor(s): Rico, Costello, Gaynor, Iarossi, Ramos, Perantoni, Kaul, Torres, Aihe
Short Title: A transfer of $3,050 to Think Twice Inc.
Summary of Legislation:
This bill will facilitate a transfer of $3,050 to Think Twice Inc. for the purchase of Drink Test
Strips to determine if a drink has been tampered with. These strips will be distributed to the
Student Body after the efficacy is confirmed by members of SGA.
Background Information:
The idea for this legislation was derived from the previous legislation that purchased ‘Night Caps’ for
drinks to be distributed to students; it was found at other universities that when these testing strips were
provided to students, they felt safer and they felt protected.
Several different manufacturers were contacted regarding how their strips worked, what they tested for,
whether students found them to be successful, and prices were also taken into consideration when
looking for the right manufacturer to use. Think Twice Inc. was the manufacturer that was eventually
determined because of their success with other universities such as the University of Florida, and they
offered a deal to give a discounted price and also post the SGA logo on the packaging for each kit so
that when the strips are distributed to students they know who purchased them, and that SGA is
representing them and their needs to the best of their ability.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This legislation was derived from a group that formed specifically to facilitate a project that could make
students feel safer. This went through several talks with Senate leadership, as well as varying entities
on campus, such as the FSU PD, CHAW, FSL, and Administration. Before even looking into
manufacturers, there was discussion on what the best methods for a project of this focus to look like,
and the best ways to move forward; FSUPD was a great resource that gave insight and advice into
different reports on campus, steps to move forward, and ideas that were and weren’t going to work.
In addition, several manufacturers were contacted so that the best fit for SGA’s needs could be found.
Price was one of the considerations, but also how many different substances the strips tested for, since
there wasn’t solid evidence that one substance was used more than others in reports on campus. Once
Think Twice was decided on, Senate leadership was consulted further to ensure that this was a project
that would work to benefit students.

If this legislation were to pass, the funds would be transferred from Senate Projects to Think Twice Inc.
for the purchase of the testing strips. These strips would first be distributed to members of SGA to test
the efficacy is varying locations, before further consultation with stakeholders to then distribute the
strips to members of the Student Body. This will primarily be done through CHAW and FSL, with FSL
focusing on Panhellenic chapters to start.

Summary of Legislation:
In partnership with the Department of Governmental Affairs in the Executive Branch, and the Civic
Engagement Board in the College of Social Sciences and Public Policy, SGA will be hosting a Voter
Registration drive for the 2026 Midterm Elections to encourage civic participation and community. This
event will take place on October 1st, 2026, on Landis Green and will feature food from 4 Rivers
Smokehouse and a raffle.
Background Information:
The money being allocated will cover the cost of catering 4 Rivers Smokehouse and the tent required
for their service from In Tent Events. The total cost of both services is $4,520.24 but will be split
between the Executive Branch and Senate. The Civic Engagement Board will be covering the
decorations, raffle expenses, CES fees if applicable, or any overages not covered by money being paid
by SGA. All students are welcome, and the event will feature tabling from student organizations,
agencies, and the Leon County Supervisor of Elections, who will be assisting with the Voter
Registration effort. No student will be required to prove or check voter registration to receive food or be
entered into the raffle.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Department of Student Affairs, Department of Government Affairs, Office of the Senate President,
Office of the Student Body President, Civic Engagement Board
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
$2,260.12 will be transferred from Senate Projects to Executive Projects, representing the Legislative
Branch’s financial contribution to the event on October 1st, 2026.

Short Title: Funding the purchase of an HVAC unit for the Flying High Circus
Summary of Legislation:
This Transfer Bill would allocate $70,000 from the Campus Advancement and Development fund for the
purchase and installation of a brand new HVAC unit for the Flying High Circus. The funds would be set
aside, and an accompanying resolution would ensure there is a Grant Agreement between the Student
Body President and the Director of the Flying High Circus.
Background Information:
The FSU Flying High Circus was established in 1974, and has served as a point of pride in the school’s
history since its inception. While many students are able to enjoy the circus every year, the rising
temperature increase the chances of an emergency for performers and the audience alike. The circus
has other projects to incorporate HVAC units into its main practice building, but due to the tornadoes
that ripped up the foundation in 2024, many of these projects to increase air conditioning have been
delayed. This Transfer Bill seeks to match this need and provide the funds to help cover for one HVAC
unit for the Circus tent, as there are projects established with facilities for the other main building,
commonly known as “The Hut”.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Student Governance and Advocacy, Senate President, Senate President Pro-Tempore, Student Body
President, Union Board, FSU Flying High Circus.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Fund the purchase of one HVAC unit up to the amount of $70,000

Applicant Guidance and Project Proposal Form
Applicant Guidance
What Is the CAD Fund?
The Campus Advancement and Development (CAD) Fund is a Student Government funding
source dedicated to long-term, non-recurring projects that improve the Florida State University
campus and provide a lasting benefit to students. The CAD Fund is not meant to support routine
operations or short-term activities. Instead, it supports projects that advance the campus in a
meaningful, durable way.
Who Can Assist in Requesting CAD Funds?
CAD Fund requests may be co-sponsored by:
o Student Senators
o Campus Departments and University Entities
o Local, State or Federal Governments
o Other student-led initiatives, when sponsored through the Student Senate
All requests must be introduced through a Student Senate bill and include a completed CAD
Fund Project Proposal Form.
Who Types of Funds Are Appropriate?
CAD Fund projects generally fall into one or more of the following categories:
o Campus improvements or enhancements
o Infrastructure, equipment, or installations
o Projects with a clear, long-term or permanent benefit
o Initiatives that address an unmet student need or service gap
o Projects that benefit a broad segment of the student body
Examples may include (but are not limited to):
o Permanent or semi-permanent campus installations
o Improvements to student spaces or shared resourcesDocusign Envelope ID: D2ED2E85-7682-8608-8158-F184491A2873

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
Page 2 of 13
What the CAD Fund Cannot Be Used For:
The CAD Fund has specific limitations. Requests should not include:
o Recurring or annual operating expenses
o Travel, conferences, or lodging
o Food, catering, or hospitality expenses
o Wages, stipends, or salaries
o Items primarily benefiting individuals or a single organization
o Expenses that should be funded through normal SGA operating budgets
If a project requires recurring funding to exist, it is likely not appropriate for the CAD Fund.
Key Things the Student Senate Looks For in Evaluating CAD Fund Proposals:
When reviewing CAD Fund requests, Student Senators and committees typically consider:
o Campus-wide impact: Does this benefit more than a small group?
o Longevity: Will students benefit beyond the current year?
o Clear need: Is there a demonstrated gap or unmet need?
o Financial responsibility: Are costs reasonable and well-documented?
o Sustainability: Can the project continue without repeated CAD funding?
o Accessibility: Is the project usable by all students, including students with disabilities?
Financial Expectations:
Requests are expected to:
o Provide an itemized budget
o Identify any matching funds or partners, if applicable
o Explain long-term costs, such as maintenance or replacement
o Demonstrate that the project will not rely on repeated CAD Fund requests
The Student Body Treasurer’s Office will conduct a risk and financial review before final
consideration.
Required Documentation:
To be considered complete, a CAD Fund request must include:
o A completed CAD Fund Project Proposal Form
o Supporting documentation (quotes, diagrams, letters of support, etc.), if applicable
o Student Senate sponsorship and proper bill submission
Incomplete or non-compliant proposals will not be considered by the Student Senate.
Important Reminder:
This guidance sheet is a plain-language summary of CAD Fund expectations. Final eligibility
and compliance are governed by Chapter 422 of the Student Body Statutes, and the Student
Senate retains full authority over approval or denial.
If you are unsure whether your project is appropriate for the CAD Fund, you are strongly
encouraged to consult:
o Your Student Senate sponsor
o The Student Body Treasurer’s Office
o The Student Senate leadership teamDocusign Envelope ID: D2ED2E85-7682-8608-8158-F184491A2873

Section II: Project Description and Purpose
Project Description:
Provide a clear and detailed description of the proposed project or initiative.
The project aims to help fund the purchase and installment of a new HVAC Unit in the Flying High
Circus Tent. The quotes are taken from vendors used by the current director of the FSU Circus, Chad
Mathews. This project was originally pushed back due to the tornadoes of Spring 2024, which ripped up
the tent and its foundation and created an entire rebuilding of the complex. With the new foundation,
there were gaps specifically made in the plans that would permit for the installation of up to four
portable HVAC units which could be retired due to any extreme weather or other extenuating
circumstances which could chut down the Circus tent. The purpose of the project is to help fund the
purchase and installation of one of these units in order to benefit not just the Circus members, but the
student body and family members who may also come to see this show. The Student Government
would draft a grant agreement, done by the Student Body President and the Student Body Attorney
General, which would stipulate the reimbursement process, quantity of funds allotted, and the
expectations timeline wise for the project.
Statement of Purpose:
Explain how this project aligns with the mission of the Student Government
Association.
The Student Government of Florida State has a mission to not just support students, but the traditions
that have made Florida State what it is today. The FSU Flying High Circus is one of the core traditions
of the University and a point of pride in our history. The continuation of providing resources and a more
comfortable environment would allow this tradition to continue and ensure the comfort of students and
families that come to enjoy this beautiful part of FSU history.
Unmet Need or Gap in Services:
Identify the unmet need or gap in services currently provided by SGA or the University.
With the continued rise in temperatures, it becomes increasingly crucial to have HVAC units in areas
with high traffic to prevent heat-related emergencies. Unfortunately, that is not something currently
found within the Circus complex. Neither the practice building, commonly referred to as “The Hut”, nor
the circus tent have any AC units. This means practices and for all whom attend and/or participate in
the shows in the Fall and Spring Semesters have to be conducted in increasingly hotter temperatures.
Providing an HVAC unit would help meet part of the gap, and make the shows and practices, which are
free for students to visit, more comfortable for the performers and accessible to everyone.Docusign Envelope ID: D2ED2E85-7682-8608-8158-F184491A2873

Risk Description:
The Treasurer’s Office identifies the following risks. (1) Documentation risk: vendor quotes for the unit
range from approximately $66,700 to $69,000, with the vendor preferred by the Circus Director quoting
$66,749. These quotes, along with the email agreement with FSU Facilities, are held in email
correspondence and are in the process of being transmitted to the Treasurer’s Office; final certification
of this assessment is contingent on their receipt and attachment to the legislative record. The margin
between the preferred quote and the requested amount serves as contingency for installation and
incidental costs, and any expenditure beyond the approved amount falls outside SGA obligation. (2)
Maintenance obligation: long-term upkeep has been agreed to by FSU Facilities via email
correspondence, with costs drawn from the Union’s yearly budget allocation for the Circus rather than
recurring SGA funds. This satisfies the CAD Fund’s sustainability requirement, contingent on the written
record being on file. (3) Asset/weather risk: the Flying High complex was destroyed by the tornadoes of
May 10, 2024, and remains exposed to severe-weather events, which is the sole risk factor outside the
control of any party to this project. This risk is mitigated but not eliminated by the rebuilt foundation and
site improvements completed during the 2024–2025 reconstruction, which per the reconstruction plans
incorporate designated infrastructure provisions and weather-preventative measures for portable HVAC
units, including the ability to retire units in advance of extreme weather.
Mitigation Strategies:
(1) Attach the vendor quotes and the Facilities email chain to the bill as supporting documentation; the
sponsor has been directed to transmit both to the Treasurer’s Office and to have them on hand during
Senate deliberation. (2) Structure the allocation strictly as a reimbursement capped at the approved
amount, payable only against itemized invoices and receipts, with any unspent balance reverting to the
CAD Fund. (3) Memorialize the maintenance arrangement and reimbursement terms in the formal grant
agreement to be executed by the Student Body President and Student Body Attorney General. (4)
Require milestone reporting to the Treasurer’s Office — purchase confirmation, installation
confirmation, and the final cost report described in Section IX — as conditions of reimbursement.

78th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Bill #: 046
Primary Sponsor(s): Gurtis
Co-sponsor(s): Holliday, Torres, Rivas, Perantoni
Short Title: Restructuring Forms of Legislation Act
Summary of Legislation:
This Bill removes specific reference to legislation forms and instead refers to them as
“legislation.” This is to ensure that if legislation forms change in the future, Student Body
Statutes don’t need to be largely altered to reflect the given changes.
Background Information:
Due to recent clarifications regarding forms of legislation, it was decided to reclarify how legislation
should be referred to in Student Body Statute. Because of this, an agreement was made to refer to
forms of legislation broadly in order to prevent large alterations of Student Body Statutes, should forms
of legislation once again change.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This legislation was written in correspondence and discussion with the Senate President, to reaffirm the
language being used and replaced.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation will prevent large changes to Student Body Statutes every time a change is made to
legislative forms, as we’ve seen increased alterations of in the past few Senates. All lists of types of
legislation will be shortened to “legislation” and singular references to a legislative type will be amended
to “piece of legislation” in order to ensure these desired effects.
