Short Title: Improvements Regarding Union Plaza Infrastructure
Summary of Legislation: This resolution expresses the Florida State University Student
Senate’s support for the potential redevelopment of the Union Plaza. The project includes
installing a canopy structure to provide shade, weather protection, and greater functionality for
the area. Once completed, the Union Plaza can serve as both an event venue and an
expanded outdoor seating space for students. The resolution emphasizes collaboration
between the Student Senate, Union Board, Union Operations, University Facilities, Student
Government Association, and the Department of Student Engagement and Student
Organizations and Involvement to ensure the project aligns with student needs and long-term
campus development goals. It reaffirms the Senate’s commitment to supporting initiatives that
enhance student engagement, accessibility, and community spaces across campus.
Background Information: In the development of this legislation, members of the Student
Senate engaged in discussions with representatives from Union Operations and Program
Directors from Academic and Student Services to better understand the scope and impact of
the Union Plaza redevelopment. These meetings highlighted the university’s ongoing efforts to
create a more functional and inclusive campus environment through the redesign of key
communal spaces. Union Operations provided insight into the logistical and infrastructure
aspects of the project, including the planned installation of a canopy structure designed to offer
weather protection and expand the usability of the plaza. Program Directors from Academic
and Student Services emphasized the importance of accessible and flexible student spaces
that can accommodate both engagement activities and daily student use. Through these
conversations, the Student Senate identified the redevelopment of the Union Plaza as a
significant opportunity to enhance student life, accessibility, and community engagement,
aligning with broader university goals for long-term campus improvement.
Effect of Proposed Legislation: The proposed legislation would contribute to the continued
enhancement of the Union Plaza, directly supporting improvements to the overall Union area
at Florida State University. Through the installation of a canopy structure and theDocusign Envelope ID: 01D85886-31C8-4B62-AA89-9FC201190A49

Senate Resolution #: 2
Primary Sponsor(s): Jackson

Short Title: A Transfer of $1,139.50 for the FSU Libraries Cooperative Collection
Summary of Legislation:
After the FSU SGA Affiliated Project “Cooperative Collection at FSU Libraries” was ratified by
the 77th Student Senate, funding was needed to purchase addiction awareness materials. This
includes books and pamphlets that pertain to education students about recovery strategies,
finding community, and more.
Background Information:
Those between the ages of 18 and 25 exhibit the highest prevalence of illicit opioid use among
all age groups, and overall drug abuse rates remain alarmingly high—45% for female college
students and 44.8% for male college students. Many college students suffer in silence with
their addictions, which can sometimes result in severe consequences, such as seizures in the
libraries due to drug use and lack of sleep.
As FSU Libraries deeply care about the university community but often lack opportunities to
engage directly with students in distress, they want to make their support more visible. The
Wellness Nook is therefore an initiative between CHAW, FSU Libraries, and the Student
Government Association aimed at supporting students who are struggling and providing them
with accessible, judgment-free resources.
The Cooperative Collection will allow students to discreetly and anonymously check out helpful
materials, offering a pathway to recovery and understanding for individuals who might not
otherwise seek help
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation will fund the start of this initiative and strengthen the partnership among
CHAW, SGA, and FSU Libraries to promote holistic student wellness and proactive care. It is
human to struggle, but that doesn’t mean it has to be done alone. This initiative will foster a
compassionate and supportive campus environment where students can prioritize their well-
being without fear or shame.Docusign Envelope ID: AAC69122-FC00-4E17-A2D6-39707F1A2488

Summary of Legislation:

order to protect pedestrian safety.
Background Information:
After discussing with the FSU Visitor Center, a crosswalk is needed on Convocation Way
specifically so that there is a safe way for FSU Ambassadors and families who visit our
campus to have a safe way to walk to Wescott Fountain. Currently, the FSU Visitors Center
sends 2-3 tours out a day where families are jay walking to the fountain to end their tour. This
resolution has been reviewed and approved by Catalina Greico; Campus Safety Coordinator.

This resolution would recognize that there is a crosswalk needed on an FSU owned road. By
working with FSU Transportation and Parking Services, facilities, and the FSU Visitor Center,
we can fund this project as soon as possible to ensure pedestrian safety for not only students,
but anyone who visits our campus.

Short Title: Reimbursing the Division of Finance & Administration for Prior Year Payments
and Transferring Funds to the Division of Student Affairs for Current Year Invoices
Summary of Legislation:
This transfer resolution transfers a total of $40,000 to the Division of Student Affairs from the
A&S Central Reserves Account to reimburse both entities for funds relating to contractual
services with the Pittman Law Group.
Background Information:
According to Fla. Stat. § 11.062 (2025), the use of state funds for lobbying services is
prohibited for state universities. The Student Government Association of Florida State
University has been in a contract with the Pittman Law Group for over the past decade, and
has used funds out of its Activity and Services Fee Budget for this purpose. To correct this
misstep, university administration must be reimbursed for the amount paid to the lobbying firm
for this year and all previous years.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This legislation has been created in consultation with university administration, Student
Governance & Advocacy staff, Senate leadership, Executive Branch leadership, and the
Pittman Law Group.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If passed, this legislation will ensure that SGA is in compliance with state law while course
correcting how we approach lobbying contracts for future years.

Short Title: Intention Resolution for the Micromobility Investment Act of 2026
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution discusses the background of the issue of micro mobility charging access at
FSU, notably for the lack of charging stations. The resolution includes major legislative
background encouraging new charging stations, as well as the statement of the TAPS Director
for the necessity to fund micro mobility charging stations. It ends off by suggesting a course of
action to fund 4 new micro mobility charging stations, and suggests their locations.
Background Information:
In Senate Resolution #77-65, the Senate recognized the acute need for charging stations for
e-bike and e-scooters around campus. FSU currently has no e-bike and e-scooter charging
stations, and the TAPS Director Richard Rind has indicated the need for it. As of now, the
many students who use e-bikes and e-scooters do so against the University regulations
against bringing their vehicles inside buildings. The students who do so bring up a potential fire
hazard for dorms on campus. To resolve these two issues, this bill intends to fund the
construction of 4 new charging stations across campus.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This legislation is being made at the behest and consultation of Transportation and Parking
Services, along with Housing being notified of the project. Senators Perantoni and Bischof
have introduced the legislation together, aiming for discussion and additional co-sponsors of a
later bill.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation declares the intent of the Senate to fund the project via the method discussed,
and recognizes the importance of infrastructure access across campus.

Short Title: Expanding First Aid Kit Accessibility
Summary of Legislation: This resolution expresses the Senate's commitment to the
implementation of new first aid kit locations on campus. The resolution commits the Senate to
continue stakeholder engagement with FSU's Emergency Management, University Health
Services, Medical Response Unit (MRU), Center for Health and Wellness (CHAW), SGA's
Executive Branch, and any other relevant stakeholders to fully execute this implementation.
Background Information: FSU's current public first aid resources include Stop The Bleed Kits
and AEDs. These are resources that require certification and preparedness training for
effective use. While they are crucial in saving lives during emergencies, they are not intended
to address the more common injuries that occur across our campus. Especially those which
are associated with our University's most physically active spaces, such as the HCB and
Wescott Fountain. The lack of first aid kit resources for areas that reflect students' safety
needs served as the origin of this initiative. The development of this initiative has been in
conversation with FSU's Emergency Management Preparedness Coordinator, SGA's
Department of Health, Wellness, and Safety, University Health Services, and the Center of
Health and Wellness. Currently, FSU's University Health Services has agreed to purchase first
aid kit supplies with SGA funds, yet no set amount has been determined. This will depend on
the extent to which first aid kits are allowed to expand across campus. Next steps will pertain
to securing building administration approval. This will include holding conversations with
individual building managers across campus, as they hold respective authority over the
approval of introducing any new permanent fixtures, such as first aid kits. Afterwards, options
to ensure proper maintenance must be developed.
Effect of Proposed Legislation: The passage of this resolution will signal to the student body
that the Senate is committed to improving campus safety in areas of need. It will reaffirm the
Florida State University Student Government Association's mission in creating a campus that
is focused on students' safety.

sections.text:
Current First Aid Kit Use On Campus
• Many first-aid kits are meant for staff use at desk stations
• Skaters at the HCB are a strong example of students who are
in need but unable to utilize those first-aid kits because they
are not considered the primary users.
• There are also many other student groups who use the HCB
as a space for physical activity, (roller-skating, dancing, color
guard, etc.)
• This along with the general lack of accessible first-aid kits
solely for student use in emergency is worth addressing.Docusign Envelope ID: 72F8399E-DF30-482D-B488-B09DB6BF9265

sections.heading: Page 7
sections.text:
Distinction between Stop the Bleed Kits and First Aid
Kits for Student Use
• There are Stop the Bleed kits inside each AED on campus.
• Those kits require certification and training for usage.
• First Aid Kits for Student Use are meant for injury of low to
moderate scale and for immediate use.Docusign Envelope ID: 72F8399E-DF30-482D-B488-B09DB6BF9265

sections.heading: Page 8
sections.text:
Project Purpose
• To provide students who face low-to-moderate injuries with
easy-to-access appropriate medical supplies
• Especially in areas where risk is expected as part of physical activityDocusign Envelope ID: 72F8399E-DF30-482D-B488-B09DB6BF9265

sections.heading: Page 9
sections.text:
Implementation Expectations
• Picking locations that are easily noticeable and clearly
demarcated for student use.
• Having signage that conveys use can be for any and all
injuries, no matter the degree.
• This is to prevent first aid kits from being ignored because a sense of
“no need”
• Assigning maintenance responsibilities to upkeep first-aid kit
supplies.
• Placing a QR code on the kit to notify the appropriate personnel
responsible for upkeep purposes.
• Monthly/Semesterly Checks (?)
• Potentially CERV (?)
• Recording usage as proof of needDocusign Envelope ID: 72F8399E-DF30-482D-B488-B09DB6BF9265

• The first-aid kits would be a solid metal kit with pre-labeled
sections, ensuring the content is not manipulated or a risk to
allergy concerns

Short Title: Declaring the Senate’s Intent for an Electric Scooter Certificate Program
Summary of Legislation:
This legislation will declare the Senate’s official intent to pursue an Electric Scooter Certificate Program
with FSUPD. The Resolution details exactly what the Senate wishes to see of the program, and states
the Senate’s intent of supporting the project with a contribution of free u-lock bike locks for graduates of
the program.
Background Information:
Administration wishes to see tangible steps on increasing pedestrian safety on campus, prior to
pursuing previously intended investments in electric scooter infrastructure by the SGA across campus.
This is one of many avenues that the Senate may take to increase pedestrian safety on campus, by
uniting campus partners to educate the population.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Initial project ideas were passed by the VP of Finance, Kyle Clark. Senate Advisor Andy Johnson was
also consulted in regards to the project. TAPS Director Richard Rind additionally supports this
measure.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This resolution would give the authority to the Sponsors to speak with FSUPD on behalf of the Senate
for an official certificate program they wish to be implemented, and measure the ability of such a
program to be implemented.

Primary Sponsor(s): Gurtis

Short Title: Communications and Accessibility Regulation for Engagement Act
Summary of Legislation:
This is a follow-up resolution to go with the associated bill. It regulates SGA affiliated social
media accounts, including Agencies and Departments, and requires them to use available
accessibility features to accommodate students with sight and hearing impairment. In addition,
this resolution states that Senate will work with the Press Secretary to put out educational
materials showing how to use accessibility features, so there is no confusion on how to use
available tools.
Background Information:
This issue was brought to attention by a former Senator with impaired vision. The goal of this resolution
is to ensure that those who are impaired, either by vision or hearing, can still access necessary
information from social media posts, given that SGA social media posts are generally used to advertise
events and other important media. In addition, this resolution also proposes that the Press Secretary
release educational materials regarding how to use social media accessibility tools.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This resolution was drafted in consultation with the Press Secretary, as well as the current Student Life
Chair. In addition, this resolution was sent to the Senate President for review.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This resolution would follow up the codification of accessibility features being used on SGA-affiliated
posts with a statement that educational materials will be released relating to how to use these tools. It
also ensures that the Press Secretary and Department of Communication are aware of this change and
support it.

Senate Resolution #: 034
Primary Sponsor(s): Gaynor
Co-sponsor(s): Macalintal, Owens, Rico, Rodriguez, Dawkins
Short Title: A Resolution to Encourage the Use of Self-Compacting Trash Cans
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution would encourage this SGA to begin exploring, and ultimately installing, self-compacting
trash cans in “hot spot” areas around campus to reduce the unsightly and environmentally damaging
waste around overfilled trash cans. This resolution would direct both the legislative and executive
branches of this SGA to pursue this project as a joint initiative.
Background Information:
Around campus, particularly in food services areas or areas with high pedestrian traffic, the current
Victor Stanley open-top trash receptacles are prone to becoming overly full and ultimately spilling waste
into the surrounding areas. Additionally, when these receptacles begin to overflow, pedestrians often
throw undesignated waste into the recycling bins, which contaminates the recycling source, making
sustainable recycling initiatives much less effective than possible. Self-compacting trash cans, which
contain a hopper that removes the air between trash within the receptacle, allow each bin to have far
greater capacity than a traditional can. These cans are also equipped with tracking software that allows
FSU Facilities and SGA to evaluate the effectiveness of this program for further expansion.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
The Office of Finance and Administration, FSU Facilities, Office of Business Services, Aramark
Partners, Office of Student Governance and Advocacy, Office of the Senate President, Executive
Branch.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
By pursuing an alternative method of waste collection with self-compacting receptacles, we seek to
reduce the amount of spillover waste that impacts high-traffic areas. This contributes to a cleaner and
more sightly campus environment, while also reducing the workload of our Waste Management team.
Additionally, by limiting the amount of recycling contamination, we hope to improve the efficacy of our
campus-wide recycling programs.

Senate Resolution #: 035

Short Title:
The A.R.C.H.I.V.E Act - An Act for the Reorganization, Codification, and Historical Indexing of
Verified Enactments
Summary of Legislation:
This comprehensive 65-page bill updates our Student Body Statutes to remove all reserved chapters
from Municode, moving all 67 unused sections to a renamed “Archive Book”, simultaneously relocating
all “Historical Senate Documents” to their own tabs under “Enrolled Legislation”. It renumbers chapters,
titles, and the citations within them accordingly so that our governing document is up to date with itself
in all sections. The accompanying resolution explains all chapters and titles being removed and
updated, while detailing how future updates to the Archive Book shall take place by working alongside
the Office of Student Governance & Advocacy.
Background Information:
Through 78 years of Senate excellence, productivity, and monumental change, our Statutes have
undergone more revisions, deletions, and additions than any other document in the SGA space. As
such, they are riddled on Municode with sections no longer in active use, citations that are incorrect,
and numbered chapters that should be far higher than they are given their active role in our
governance. This bill updates all of that and explains specific changes and the path to maintain those
changes in the resolution.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
The Office of Student Governance & Advocacy, Student Body President Ian Seibert, Vice President for
Student Affairs Dr. Amy Hecht
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation will make Municode and Student Body Statutes far easier to read for both Senators and
the public alike by removing confusing sections while preserving our vital SGA history in a section
specifically made to highlight it. It will set up a framework for future necessary changes to ensure that
additional repeals have a clear path after being taken out of use.Docusign Envelope ID: BFFC9C90-E43B-8116-8080-0E142D9F80BA

Senate Resolution #: 036

Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: CAD Fund Cash Management and Interest Review Resolution
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution acknowledges that Florida law authorizes universities to invest available agency and
activity funds and to use the resulting earnings for student scholarships and loans. It respectfully
requests a written legal and accounting determination regarding the treatment of investment earnings
attributable to Activity & Service Fee balances, including the Campus Advancement and Development
(CAD) Fund, and whether any lawful mechanism exists for such earnings to be credited to CAD or
another Student Government-administered purpose benefiting the student body. The resolution does not
direct an investment, transfer funds, or assert that the Student Government presently controls University
investment decisions.
Background Information:
The FY 2026–27 Activity & Service Fee budget adopted by the 78th Student Senate separately identifies
“CAD - Campus Advancement and Development Fund” at $43,121.17, described as the required 0.30%
of FY-26 A&S Fee Revenue. Florida Statutes § 1011.42 places university deposits and investment
transfers under University and Board of Trustees authority. Florida Statutes § 1011.43 separately
authorizes each university to invest available agency and activity funds and use the earnings for student
scholarships and loans. FSU’s Investment Policy assigns administration of the University investment
program to University financial officials and prioritizes safety, liquidity, and lawful return. The sponsor
has also been advised that unexpended A&S balances are presently invested by the University and that
investment earnings support University-administered scholarships. Because the statutes distinguish
Student Government authority over allocation and expenditure from University authority over custody
and investment, clarification is needed regarding whether earnings attributable to A&S balances are
themselves A&S revenues, scholarship funds under § 1011.43, or funds that may lawfully be credited
for Student Government administration.Docusign Envelope ID: 2ED52735-94C4-8D02-81B3-7D4E6E134A22

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This resolution is being drafted in cooperation with the Senate Finance Committee Chair and is intended
for referral to the Senate Finance Committee upon introduction. Under the Senate Rules, finance reviews
measures pertaining to fiscal matters and Chapter 800 of the Student Body Statutes, while Budget
reviews the annual A&S fee budget and budget revisions/transfers. Because this measure is limited to
requesting legal/accounting review of CAD Fund cash management and does not itself change a budget
line or appropriate additional funds, Finance is the proper primary referral. Stakeholder outreach to the
Senate President, Finance Committee Chair, and Student Body Treasurer were being handled by the
primary sponsor.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If adopted, the resolution will place the Student Senate on record requesting a written determination of
how unexpended A&S and CAD balances are currently invested and accounted for; and whether
earnings attributable to those balances are governed by Florida Statutes § 1011.43 and must be used for
scholarships and loans. It will also ask whether Student Government’s authority over A&S allocation
and expenditure extends to any investment earnings; and whether the University may lawfully establish
a transparent mechanism to credit attributable earnings to CAD or another SGA-administered student-
benefit purpose. It will not amend the Student Body Statutes, alter the adopted budget, appropriate
funds, or authorize Student Government officers to open accounts, transfer University funds, or purchase
financial instruments.

Short Title: Funding the purchase of an HVAC unit for the Flying High Circus
Summary of Legislation:
This Resolution would allocate $70,000 from the Campus Advancement and Development fund for the
purchase and installation of a brand new HVAC unit for the Flying High Circus. The funds would be set
aside, and it would ensure there is a Grant Agreement between the Student Body President and the
Director of the Flying High Circus for reimbursement procedures.
Background Information:
The FSU Flying High Circus was established in 1974, and has served as a point of pride in the school’s
history since its inception. While many students are able to enjoy the circus every year, the rising
temperature increase the chances of an emergency for performers and the audience alike. The circus
has other projects to incorporate HVAC units into its main practice building, but due to the tornadoes
that ripped up the foundation in 2024, many of these projects to increase air conditioning have been
delayed. This Transfer Bill seeks to match this need and provide the funds to help cover for one HVAC
unit for the Circus tent, as there are projects established with facilities for the other main building,
commonly known as “The Hut”.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Student Governance and Advocacy, Senate President, Senate President Pro-Tempore, Student Body
President, Union Board, FSU Flying High Circus.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Establish the process by which the executive branch will create a Grant Agreement Document
alongside Chad Mathews, the director of the FSU Flying High Circus. This will allow for the process for
the Circus to buy the new HVAC Unit and be reimbursed up to the amount set by the accompanying
transfer bill.

Summary of Legislation:
This resolution approves the proposed Memorandum of Understanding between the Florida State
University Student Government Association and the Division of Student Affairs governing the
administration of the $70,000 Campus Advancement and Development Fund allocation previously
approved for the purchase and installation of a new HVAC unit at the FSU Flying High Circus. The
resolution also authorizes the Student Body President to execute the agreement on behalf of SGA.
Background Information:
On July 22, 2026, the Student Senate approved Bill #78-038, which allocated $70,000 from the
Campus Advancement and Development Fund to support the purchase and installation of a new HVAC
unit for the FSU Flying High Circus. At the same meeting, the Senate also adopted Resolution #78-040,
directing the Student Government Association to pursue a grant agreement establishing the terms and
conditions governing the allocation. The proposed Memorandum of Understanding has since been
developed in collaboration with the Division of Student Affairs and the Flying High Circus and
establishes requirements regarding eligible expenditures, reimbursement procedures, project
completion, reporting obligations, and recognition of Student Government funding. The agreement
provides for reimbursement funding of up to $70,000, requires project completion by June 30, 2027
(unless extended), and includes accountability measures to ensure responsible stewardship of student
funds.
The Student Senate's approval of the agreement is the final legislative action necessary to implement
the allocation authorized by Bill #78-038 and contemplated by Resolution #78-040. Execution of the
agreement will enable the Division of Student Affairs and the Flying High Circus to proceed with the
project while ensuring compliance with Senate intent and applicable fiscal controls.

Short Title: Recognizing the Seminole Boosters New Towing Policy for Fountain Throws
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution encourages continued discussions with Seminole Boosters around the protection of
campus traditions, specifically regarding concerns around Heritage Fountain. Additionally, it informs the
Student Senate of the delayed towing enforcement before gamedays for “Booster Parking Lot C –
University Center A North” in response to student concerns.
Background Information:
On September 2nd, 2026, during a regular meeting of the Student Senate, members of the student
body raised concerns regarding pre-gameday towing procedures near Heritage Fountain. Previously,
on August 28th (prior to the first football home game), a towing company responsible for enforcing the
rule brought a large fleet of tow trucks to the lot closest to Heritage Fountain and began towing vehicles
immediately as it turned midnight. This resulted in students, who often look forward to this tradition for
their entire collegiate careers, having to immediately run back to their cars in hopes that their car
remained in the lot. Outreach was immediately conducted after learning of this issue, and in partnership
with the Seminole Boosters, it was agreed to begin pre-gameday towing enforcement at 1 AM for
“Booster Parking Lot C – University Center A North.”
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Student Senate, Executive Branch, Transportation and Parking Services, Office of Student Governance
and Advocacy, Seminole Boosters.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This resolution seeks to recognize the quick work of all SGA partners involved and affirm this Senate’s
commitment to educating the student body on this change. Additionally, it encourages continued
feedback on the effectiveness of this change as it is implemented.

Primary Sponsor(s): Bigenho, Gurtis

Short Title: Amending various sections of the Student Body Constitution for the Removal of
Obsolete and Revised Language.
Summary of Legislation:
The constitutional amendment would update Articles II, III, and V to eliminate references to institutions
and practices that no longer exist in Student Government operations. The amendment deletes
references to executive Beuraus, which no longer exist, and elected positions in Agency and Affiliated
Project leadership, which now use what is considered an appointment process. The constitutional
amendment also clarifies language within the Constitution relating to the naming of the Student Body
Treasurer, consistently referring to the office as “Treasurer” to mirror references made to “President”
and “Vice President.”
Background Information:
Every three years, pursuant to the Student Body Constitution Article VI Section 6, the Constitutional
Review Commission is formed to update the Student Body Constitution. The body proposes
amendments to put the document in line with current SGA practices, and to streamline overall SGA
structure and operation. However, with fast and important structural changes in SGA happening in the
in between years, constitutional updates sometimes are necessary sooner. Sometimes also several
commissions can miss small but important provisions in our constitution in need of change.
Since 2013 Student Body Statutes have not dictated the election of Agency leaders, instead stipulating
appointment pursuant to Section 304 and Agency Rules of Procedure. However, even after the Uniform
Agency Act of 2023 confirmed no Agency leader is to be popularly elected by the Student Body,
references to popular election in the Student Body Constitution remain. Similarly, while records are
harder to trace, Affiliated Projects were overhauled in 2013 to presumably eliminate the election of their
leadership, yet constitutional reality has yet to change. Finally, after the passage of the CORE, or
Executive Departments Act, of 2025, Executive branch Bureaus were retired for executive departments.
The Student Body Constitution, SGA’s most important governing document, lacking practical daily
operations such as mechanism of Director institution and the existence of part of the executive branch,
must be updated in light of these changes.Docusign Envelope ID: DE83A24A-1460-836A-82B5-201C41D98E9E

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Senate and Executive Branch leaders were consulted in the drafting of this constitutional amendment.
Sponsors give a special thanks to the Student Body Treasurer, Deputy Student Body Treasurer, and
the Student Senate President for extra attention given in drafting.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The constitutional amendment would change no operation, enforcement, or structure within SGA.
Agency and Affiliated Project Leadership would continue to be selected as Student Body Statutes and
their respective rules of procedure provide. Obsolete constitutional language referring to election would
be brought up to date with statutes. Removal of reference to nonexistent Bureaus would allow further
constitutional accuracy, and consistent reference to “Treasurer” would enable consistency in the
document. Overall, the adoption of the amendment would provide SGA’s bedrock document with more
authority and utility as it properly depicts current operations.

78th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Allocation Resolution #: 002
Primary Sponsor(s): Nucatola
Co-sponsor(s): Ferris
Short Title: Approving funding recommendations from the RSO Allocation Committee
(RSOAC)
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution proposes the allocation of $22,772.13 to various RSOs who request funding
from the RSOAC:
• American Marketing Association (AMA) - $2,000.00
o The American Marketing Association is aiming to attend their 2026 International
Collegiate Conference (ICC) March 12th-14th in Chicago, Illinois—this is unusual
as the ICC is usually held in New Orleans, Louisiana—and compete nationally in
competitions for categories like marketing strategy, pitch perfect, sales, etc.
While their overall request was $7,442.60, the RSOAC cannot fund travel for
more than $250.00 per student attending the trip. With 8 members signed up, the
maximum fundable amount was $2,000.00, but they are working with the College
of Business and its faculty to fund more students’ participation.
• Japanese Animation Club of Tallahassee (JACT)- $3,000.00
o JACT is hosting a community wide event called FreeCon 22 on Saturday, April
4th and Sunday, April 5th. FreeCon is an “anime, gaming, and pop culture
convention held annually on FSU’s campus.” The event is supposed to be free
for both the student body and general public, and with over 2700 attendees in
last year’s event. JACT looks to receive funding from RSOAC to cover venue
costs for their 22nd annual FreeCon being held in the Student Union. With the
most the RSOAC committee could allocate was the $3,000.00, the only question
the committee preferred the Student Senate to decide was on Chapter 802,
Section 5, Limitation on Outside (Non-FSU) Benefits:
▪ b.)Items/services purchased with A&S money may not be used for the
primary benefit of community programs outside of FSU, or for donations to
such programs. This provision shall not be construed so as to prevent
organizations from receiving funding as outlined in Chapter 811 of the
Student Body Statutes.Docusign Envelope ID: 3C0C325E-154B-40AF-97D5-320171324B2B

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
o The Committee deemed the Student Senate should create the subjective opinion
on the matter, as the Student Senate is capable and responsible for interpreting
statute, whereas the RSOAC Committee is intended to be objective in concept.
• Black Future Female Attorneys - $450.00
o This RSO aims to gain funding from the RSOAC to cover food for their induction
ceremony for their new members on April 24th, 2026. This event is open to all,
with the group providing the following: law school support, law panels with law
students and practicing attorneys, BFFA shirts, graduation chords, pins, and
other merch. They will be getting Harry’s Seafood Bar and Grille catered for
$450.00 which would match their last request from Fall 2024 that SGA previously
granted.
• Alpha Epsilon Delta - $3,750.00
o Alpha Epsilon Delta is aiming to take a medical mission trip to San Jose, Costa
Rica with the trip beginning March 15th and ending March 21st. AED is a National
Health Pre-Professional Honor Society dedicated to the encouragement and
recognition of excellence in pre-professional health scholarships, including
medicine, dentistry, veterinary, and others. On this trip, they will be working with
small communities that have limited or no access to healthcare and be putting in
a total of 30 hours of volunteer work per attendee. The total cost would be
$28,380 for 15 participants, meaning they can only be funded with the $250.00
per person rate bringing the total request to $3,750.00.
• NCNW – $5,000.00
o This RSO was established on FSU’s campus in 1999 with a mission to lead,
empower, and advocate for women of African descent, their families, and their
communities. The organization now has 48 members all interested in attending
their annual New Orleans community service trip to partner with groups like
Sprout Nola, the Xavier University Chapter, Hagars House for women and
children, then conduct their own clothing drive. With requests dating all the way
back to 2013, this organization has a long history of requests for SGA funding;
they provided us the total cost: $13,510.00 but were content with the maximum
funding amount available of $5,000.00.
• THE Color Stack Chapter – $105.13
o THE Color Stack Chapter is requesting Chick-Fil-a for their upcoming GBM to
boost attendance. Being focused on helping students find a career in
technological fields. Having only had two attendees at their 11/03/25 GBM and
eight at their 02/05/26 GBM, the organization aims to bolster its attendance with
food. Compared to their GBMs that had food with thirteen, fourteen, and twenty-
one attendees, respectively.
• American String Teachers Association - $1,750.00*
o The American String Teachers Association is requesting funding for their Spring
2026 American String Teachers’ Association Conference on February 25th-28th inDocusign Envelope ID: 3C0C325E-154B-40AF-97D5-320171324B2B

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
San Francisco, California. The Conference is an internationally renowned
opportunity for networking, community building, and sharing pedagogical
knowledge of all things related to string music education. As a premier string
music education program, the FSU string music education department strongly
supports students attending the conference to learn valuable knowledge on string
pedagogy which they can bring back with them and disseminate not only in their
classrooms, but in the FSU community at large. With seven members going, the
$250 per person rule applies, totaling $1,750.00 on the allocation.
• Theta Tau - $4,992.00
o Theta Tau is a professional development fraternity for engineering that aims to
provide a community to engineering students, creating not only a network, but
lifelong friendships. They are at 94 active members, engaging in professional
development, brotherhood, and service. They are requesting funding to attend
the 2026 Regional Open Conference in Orlando, Florida, at the University of
Central Florida from February 27th to March 1st. Then host volunteer events while
they are in Orlando. The total cost will be $8,246.00, but they requested $128 per
person, equaling $4,992.00 for 39 people.
• The Big Event - $1,725.00*
o The Big Event Tallahassee is the city’s largest student-led service initiative,
bringing hundreds of college students together to say ‘thank you’ to the
Tallahassee Community. This request pertains to The Big Event this Spring
which will be February 21st, 2026, with over 1,500 students expected to attend.
This funding will cover a stage for speakers, such as the Tallahassee Mayor,
chairs, and tables for the organization’s volunteers to set up for the kick-off
ceremony. Ultimate Sound and Light provided a quote of $1,725.00 which is the
option the committee and organization agreed to.
*All requests meet the required deadline of submission and have been cleared by SGA
Accounting and Senate Leadership.
Background Information:
Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) are integral to the cultural, educational, and social
fabric of the campus community. They play a critical role in promoting diversity, leadership
development, and student involvement. This funding will support these organizations in
carrying out impactful programming or travel that aligns with FSU's values of community
building, professional development, and discovery.
The RSO Allocation Committee was created as a means for RSOs to obtain SGA funding for
programming and travel needs. All events and travel opportunities funded must be available
and/or beneficial to all members of the Student Body.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Following approval by the Student Senate, funds will be transferred to the RSO for the statedDocusign Envelope ID: 3C0C325E-154B-40AF-97D5-320171324B2B

purpose in the resolution. They will be required to submit receipts and an event evaluation
From the SGA Accounting Office within ten (10) business days of the event or travel. The
financial support provided will empower the RSOs to carry out impactful activities to drive
cultural engagement and professional growth.

Senate Allocation Resolution #: 003
Primary Sponsor(s): Nucatola

Short Title: Approving funding recommendations from the RSO Allocation Committee
(RSOAC)
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution proposes the allocation of $11,769.04 to various RSOs who request funding
from the RSOAC:
• All Night Yahtzee - $2,056.88*
The organization, now in its 26th year, is requesting funding for lodging to attend
the ICCA quarterfinals in Mississippi from March 6-8. The request covers five rooms
for two nights for 19 students. During questioning, the representative clarified that
while a higher quote was provided as a benchmark for quality, they were requesting
the lowest quote of $2,056.88. The committee discussed the organization's history
of SGA funding and confirmed that auditions are open to the entire student body.
The event is intended to benefit the student body through national representation
and a subsequent free showcase concert.
• C.A.L.O.R - $1,077.00
o C.A.L.O.R is requesting funding to purchase 120 organizational T-shirts to foster
inclusivity and unity among members and the FSU community. The shirts are
intended to be distributed for free at tabling events to encourage involvement.
The committee questioned the representative on student impact, noting the
organization's large social media following, and verified that the shirts would
include the "Paid for by SGA" disclaimer. The final recommended amount was
adjusted to $1,077.00 to comply with statutory funding caps of $10 per shirt,
specifically regarding the higher cost of XXL sizes.
• Women in Sports Association - $1,341.70
o This organization is seeking funding for a professional networking trip to Atlanta
from March 20-29, which includes tours of Mercedes-Benz Stadium and a Braves
game. The representative noted that the trip is open to the student body and
serves to empower women in the industry. The committee opted to fund the tripDocusign Envelope ID: BE9DBF8F-B830-4B0F-9BD6-D89F9F01D794

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
based on the lowest quotes provided for lodging and gas to maintain fiscal
responsibility. A secondary request for merchandise was deferred to a later date
to comply with committee procedures.
• National Association for Business Economics at FSU - $1,250.00*
o The request is for airfare and lodging for five students to attend the NABE Policy
Conference in Washington D.C. February 21st-24th. While the organization has a
history of attending this conference, the committee raised concerns regarding the
attendee selection process, as the group consisted primarily of Executive Board
members (5). After verifying that the opportunity was advertised to the general
body, the committee applied the statutory travel cap of $250 per student,
resulting in a recommended allocation of $1,250.00
• Special Olympics at FSU - $849.03
o The organization is requesting funds for "Spread the Word Week," a series of
events from March 1-6 promoting inclusion through activities such as a Unified
Kickball Day and Bowling Night. The funding covers equipment rentals,
reservations, and food. The committee discussed the efficiency of combining
multiple events into a single "sprint week" request and determined the total
amount was reasonable for the projected impact on approximately 60 students
and 20 athletes.
• Blacks in Computing - $1,000.00
o Funding is requested for registration fees for four students to attend the National
Society of Black Engineers (NSBE) conference in Baltimore, March 17th-22nd.
The organization is coordinating with the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering to
minimize travel and lodging costs, which the students are self-funding. In
alignment with Student Body Statutes, the committee applied the $250 per
student travel cap, reducing the requested 1,500 (375 per student) to a
recommendation of $1,000.00.
• Kappa Kappa Psi Gamma Nu - $2,961.43
o This honorary band fraternity is requesting funding to attend the Southeast
District Convention in South Carolina on March 19th-22nd to participate in
networking and professional workshops. The representative highlighted that their
service directly supports the Marching Chiefs and the College of Music. The
committee verified that membership is open to any student who has participated
in a band ensemble. The allocation was capped at the statutory limit of $3,000 for

Background Information:
Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) are integral to the cultural, educational, and social
fabric of the campus community. They play a critical role in promoting diversity, leadership
development, and student involvement. This funding will support these organizations in
carrying out impactful programming or travel that aligns with FSU's values of community
building, professional development, and discovery.
The RSO Allocation Committee was created as a means for RSOs to obtain SGA funding for
programming and travel needs. All events and travel opportunities funded must be available
and/or beneficial to all members of the Student Body.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Following approval by the Student Senate, funds will be transferred to the RSO for the stated
purpose in the resolution. They will be required to submit receipts and an event evaluation
From the SGA Accounting Office within ten (10) business days of the event or travel. The
financial support provided will empower the RSOs to carry out impactful activities to drive
cultural engagement and professional growth.

sections.heading: Page 101
sections.text:
Questions to Ask for Each Section
1. What is the core purpose of your event or trip?
2. How does this activity directly support the mission of FSU or the Student Government Association
3. Which specific student needs or gaps does this proposal address?
4. How will you measure whether your purpose was achieved
1. Approximately how many students will this program serve or impact?
2. How are you ensuring access for students outside your organization’s membership?
3. What tangible benefits will participants or the wider student body gain (skills, exposure, service, community)?
4. How do you plan to promote this event to ensure broad participation?
1. How does this proposal enhance FSU’s image, reputation, or visibility at the local, state, or national level?
2. If travel, how will participants represent FSU and report back to the campus community?
3. What lasting contribution does this program make to FSU’s academic or cultural identity?
1. How does this program strengthen the sense of community or inclusion at FSU?
2. Does this event build on existing campus traditions or create new ones?
3. How does your organization plan to engage other student groups or departments in this initiative?
1. What is your plan for encouraging student involvement and turnout?
2. How will participants be actively engaged during the event (not just attendees)?
3. How will you evaluate engagement success?
1. How is this event accessible to all students, financially, physically, and socially?

o The Muslim Student Union at Florida State University is hosting an Iftar to bring

understanding. By creating an inclusive space centered on community and

accessible opportunity for students to learn about Ramadan and engage in
meaningful cultural and interfaith exchange through shared experience and
conversation. By offering a welcoming community space and a shared meal, the
event promotes inclusion, understanding, and student well-being. The event will
provide a complete dinner including rice, chicken, and a variety of Indian cuisine
dishes. The meal will be served buffet-style to accommodate a large number of
attendees and offer culturally diverse food options. The Iftar is expected to serve a
large number of students and provide a meaningful social and educational

Summary of Legislation:

Muslim Student Union - $2,900.00
The Muslim Student Union is requesting funding for a cultural night banquet designed to
unite diverse cultures within Islam while creating an educational environment for the
entire student body. The event will include traditional attire, live cultural perf ormances
such as storytelling, spoken word, poetry, and nasheed, as well as henna art and halal
catering. The organization aims to establish the event as an ongoing campus tradition
similar to gala-style programs hosted at other universities. The event will be free and open
to all students and heavily advertised to encourage broad participation.

The Japanese Student Association is requesting funding to attend the East Coast Asian

culture, heritage, and language to form a network of shared interests and cultural

the Tallahassee area. Those looking to learn and promote the language and culture will find

Background Information:
Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) are integral to the cultural, educational, and social
fabric of the campus community. They play a critical role in promoting diversity, leadership
development, and student involvement. This funding will support these organizations in
carrying out impactful programming or travel that aligns with FSU's values of community
building, professional development, and discovery.
The RSO Allocation Committee was created as a means for RSOs to obtain SGA funding for
programming and travel needs. All events and travel opportunities funded must be available
and/or beneficial to all members of the Student Body.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Following approval by the Student Senate, funds will be transferred to the RSO for the stated
purpose in the resolution. They will be required to submit receipts and an event evaluation
From the SGA Accounting Office within ten (10) business days of the event or travel. The
financial support provided will empower the RSOs to carry out impactful activities to drive
cultural engagement and professional growth.

Short Title: Approving funding recommendations from the RSO Allocation Committee

Summary of Legislation:
This resolution proposes the allocation of $2,399.43 to various RSOs who request funding
from the RSOAC:
From conversations with RSOAC Stakeholders, the committee decided to equally disperse the
remaining budget in this meeting, capped at $400.00; this cap can be discussed during this
meeting.
Bioethics Association - $500.00
- The Bioethics Association at Florida State University - $1,712.00 Request Overview: The
organization is requesting $1,712.00 to fund travel for four students to attend the
National Bioethics Bowl 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The trip is scheduled for
April 10–12, 2026, and the request includes both airfare and lodging expenses. Funding
Breakdown: Airfare ($1,334.00): The request covers commercial economy flights from
Jacksonville (JAX) to Pittsburgh (PIT). While the estimated per-person fare was listed as
$263.42, the subtotal requested for the group of four is $1,334.00. Lodging ($378.00):
The organization plans to stay at the Hilton Garden Inn Pittsburgh University Place.
They are requesting one room for two nights at a rate of $189.00 per night, maintaining
an occupancy of four students per room. Purpose and Benefit: This is the organization's
first time participating in this national competition, hosted by the University of
Pittsburgh. The trip aims to place FSU in good standing within the bioethics community
and provides professional experience for students interested in healthcare, science, and
ethics. Upon their return, the attendees plan to share their findings and experiences
through the organization's GroupMe and Market Wednesdays. Organizational Status
and Compliance: The request was submitted by Treasurer Avery Cronin and President
Hannah Swota . The RSO is currently active and in good standing on Nole Central. Both
officers have completed the required financial certification, and the organization has
submitted the SGA Statement of Understanding for the current academic year. TheDocusign Envelope ID: 59095DE3-5388-4F5D-8D9A-7C6BF4416B45

collect membership dues. The request was submitted more than 45 days in advance of
the travel date, meeting the statutory deadline for Senate approval
The Venezuelan Student Association - $ 500.00
- Request Overview: The organization is requesting a total of $3,000.00 to host the
VENSA Gala, an end-of-the-year cultural celebration. The event is scheduled for April 4,
2026, at the FSU Alumni Center. The organization expects an attendance of
approximately 120 students. Funding Breakdown: Contractual Services ($2,000.00):
These funds are designated for a one-hour comedy and entertainment performance by
Abelardo, a nationally renowned Hispanic artist. The organization noted that depending
on the final allocation, they intend to coordinate with this year's performer or renew
their previous contract with this artist. Food ($1,000.00): The organization is
requesting catering from two vendors to provide a traditional Venezuelan cultural
experience. Traditions Catering: Requested for a main buffet featuring Sweet Plantains,
White Rice, Black Beans, Pollo Mechado (shredded chicken), Pabellon Criollo (pulled
beef), and Quesillo (flan) at a cost of approximately $18.77 per person. VeneBites:
Requested to provide 230 Tequeños (cheese sticks) as appetizers at a cost of
approximately $3.27 per person. Purpose and Campus Benefit: The VENSA Gala serves
as a safe space for FSU students—particularly those who are first-generation
immigrants—to reconnect with their language and heritage. By featuring a national
artist and traditional cuisine, the event aims to foster unity across the diverse campus
community and supports FSU's goals of becoming a Hispanic Service Institution. The
event is free and open to all FSU students and will be promoted via Instagram, Nole
Central, flyers, and tabling. Organizational Status and Compliance: The request was
submitted by Treasurer Sebastian Felice and President Carlos Garrido. VENSA is an
active RSO in good standing and has previously been recognized as the HLSU Affiliate of
the Year. The organization reported $4,000.00 in an off-campus bank account and does
not currently collect membership dues. The request was submitted more than 30 days
prior to the event, and the organization has confirmed awareness of the 45-day Senate
approval rule for travel (though this is a programming request) and the 10-day receipt
submission deadline. Dietary and Accessibility Considerations: The proposed menu
includes options for gluten-free, dairy-free, and vegetarian students to ensure
inclusivity.

organization is requesting $2,100.00 to send eight students to the ASC Southern
Conference 2026 in Atlanta, GA, from April 3–5, 2026. This trip is primarily for students
to participate in the ChemE Car competition, which serves as a senior design capstone
project. Funding Breakdown: Lodging ($800.00): Covers two rooms for two nights at a
base rate of $600 with $200 in mandatory fees. The organization will follow theDocusign Envelope ID: 59095DE3-5388-4F5D-8D9A-7C6BF4416B45

o Request Overview: The organization is requesting $1,101.36 to fund lodging for nine
students to attend the ADEA Go Dental Recruitment Event in Montréal, Canada, from
March 20–22, 2026. This conference, hosted by the American Dental Education
Association (ADEA), provides pre-dental students the opportunity to network with
dental school admissions officers and receive direct professional advice to improve
their chances of admission. Funding Breakdown: The allocation covers three rooms
for two nights at the Holiday Inn Montréal Centre‑Ville Centre des Congrès. The
nightly rate is set at $153.56 per room, with an estimated $30 in mandatory fees per
night (covering parking or city-specific fees). Occupancy & Compliance: To comply
with fire codes and university co-ed housing standards, the organization has
established the following occupancy plan for the nine travelers: Room 1: Four male
students Room 2: Three female students Room 3: Two female students This
arrangement ensures all travelers are accommodated while remaining within safety
and housing guidelines. Campus Benefit & Publicity: The trip aims to represent
Florida State University’s pre-dental community on an international stage,
highlighting the commitment of FSU students to professional healthcare programs.
To benefit the broader student body, the organization will host a post-trip
presentation during a general club meeting to share insights, admissions advice, and
recruitment strategies gained from the event. The opportunity was publicly
advertised through Nole Central, flyers, and club meetings to ensure accessibility for
interested members. Organizational Standing: The request was submitted by
President Veronica Kelada and Treasurer Katie Weiss, both of whom have
completed the required SGA financial certification. The organization is currently in
good standing and has a current Statement of Understanding on file. The
organization confirmed that travel begins more than 45 days from the request date,
satisfying all statutory requirements for funding consideration. At present, the RSO
reports $431.72 in an off-campus bank account and has collected $1,087.12 in
membership dues for the current fiscal year at a rate of $20 per member.
Japanese Animation Club - $500.00
- Request Overview The organization is requesting funding to host FreeCon 22, the 22nd
iteration of Tallahassee’s premier anime, gaming, and Japanese pop culture convention. The
event is scheduled for April 4–5, 2026, at the Florida State University Student Union, with
an expected attendance of approximately 3,000 people. Funding Breakdown Total
Requested (Qualtrics): While the organization’s total cost for contractual security services
amounts to $4,618.80, the committee’s recommendation is $3,000.00, which is the
maximum statutory cap for a single RSOAC programming request. Contractual Services
FSUPD Security – $2,380.00 This allocation covers two FSUPD officers on duty for security
throughout the weekend: Saturday: 11:00 AM – 8:00 PM Sunday: 11:00 AM – 5:00 PM
Sentry Event Services – $2,238.80 This allocation covers five security personnel and one
supervisor, as required by FSUPD for an event of this scale. Purpose and Campus Benefit
FreeCon serves as a free and accessible alternative to professional conventions, which are
often cost-prohibitive for students. The event includes: A housekeeper café Cosplay
contests Video game rooms Panels and discussions. Many panels and activities feature FSUDocusign Envelope ID: 59095DE3-5388-4F5D-8D9A-7C6BF4416B45

sections.text:

the public, aiming to foster goodwill and provide a welcoming space for diverse interests
within the campus community. Relevant Questions and Senate Discussion Statutory
Interpretation The committee specifically requested that the Student Senate review this
request in the context of Student Body Statute Chapter 802, Section 5, which limits the use
of A&S funds for the primary benefit of community programs outside of FSU. Because
FreeCon had over 2,700 attendees last year, many from the broader North Florida
community, the Senate must determine whether the community-wide nature of the event

Tabling Email Outreach Market Wednesday

Background Information:
Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) are integral to the cultural, educational, and social
fabric of the campus community. They play a critical role in promoting diversity, leadership
development, and student involvement. This funding will support these organizations in
carrying out impactful programming or travel that aligns with FSU's values of community
building, professional development, and discovery.
The RSO Allocation Committee was created as a means for RSOs to obtain SGA funding for
programming and travel needs. All events and travel opportunities funded must be available
and/or beneficial to all members of the Student Body.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
Following approval by the Student Senate, funds will be transferred to the RSO for the stated
purpose in the resolution. They will be required to submit receipts and an event evaluation
From the SGA Accounting Office within ten (10) business days of the event or travel. The
financial support provided will empower the RSOs to carry out impactful activities to drive
cultural engagement and professional growth.

This resolution proposes the allocation of $4,000.00 to one RSO who requested funding from the

Association of Latino Professionals for America (ALPFA) - $4,000.00
- ALPFA requested a sum of $5,000 for the travel of 16 persons to their organization’s national
conference on August 9-13th, 2026, in Charlotte, NC.
o Pursuant to regulations under SBS § 816, the organization was capped at the possible
maximum funding of $4,000, with 16 persons at $250 per head. The organization was
then given 85.4625% of their requested funding based on the rubric consensus of the
RSO Allocation Committee members.
o ALPFA is requesting money for reimbursement of travel expenses, including flights from
Fort Lauderdale and Tampa to Charlotte, round trip. They are additionally requesting
money for lodging expenses. The travel is to a business conference for their
organization, where they will meet and discuss with numerous companies and engage
with other members of the national organization.
o The organization presented their requests well, maintained a strong legacy of traveling
to this conference, did not have any probation or punishments for A&S Fee misuses, and
had a clear leadership team established for proper monetary stewardship.
o The organization did not come with three quotes from their Tampa flights, and did not
come with three quotes for their hotel costs. The Chair of the RSOAC ruled that they did
not violate minimum rules, as the organization presented three quotes for their Fort
Lauderdale flights and the conference rate for their hotel lodging. However, many
committee members considered the lack of quotes in their grading scale.
 The request from the organization at the RSOAC did not match the same request
breakdown of that in their application, which also caused the committee to
decrease their funding.
 Questions were raised about the ability for the organization to share the lessons
of the conference to the general student body, which also had an impact in
rankings.Docusign Envelope ID: EBC2E1C2-28FA-845F-836F-2404015696AA

sections.text:

offers to the students traveling, as well as viewing what the companies seek at this

markets.
o The organization also has value in building a tradition of going to this conference,

Summary of Legislation:

RSOAC:
White Mouse Productions - $921.93
- White Mouse Productions requested a sum of $1149 to fund a keyboard for their club’s
continued musical productions on campus.
o Pursuant to regulations under the Finance Code, the RSOAC defaulted to the lowest
quote provided by the organization to fund a keyboard at $939. The organization was
then given 98.1818% of their requested funding based on the rubric consensus of the
RSO Allocation Committee members.
o White Mouse Productions had a good presentation, with clear measurable impact on the
student body through performances and opportunities for the arts for members of the
organization.
o White Mouse Productions indicated their willingness to self-fund the remaining sum in
order to get the keyboard they originally requested, out of their off-campus bank account
of around $3000.
o White Mouse Productions have requested money from the RSOAC before.
o This organization does not collect dues.
Theta Eta Chapter of Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity - $1010.54
- The Theta Eta Chapter of the Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity requested a sum of $1167 for their
World Cup event on July 16th, 2026.
o Pursuant to regulations under the Finance Code, the RSOAC zero funded the requests
for Water Bottles and the DJ contract request. For the former, the SGA is disallowed
from funding Water Bottles besides from natural disasters, and the SGA is not allowed to
fund contractual requests under 30 days before the final approval from Senate. This
brought the final total to $1025. The organization was then given 98.5889% of their
requested funding based on the rubric consensus of the RSO Allocation Committee
members.Docusign Envelope ID: A465B190-5DAE-87B2-80B7-F80B2E0A3AD7

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
o KAP had amazing quotes for all of their events, and reductions were mainly focused on
statutory guidelines and limitations around event funding.

supported by their own organization should the need arise.
o KAP charges dues, collecting $11,200 in dues over the course of the Fiscal Year.
o KAP has $7800 in an off campus bank account.
o Pursuant to regulations under the Finance Code, final event funding approval must be
15 days prior to the day of event, of which the Senate meeting on July 1st meets this
requirement precisely.

- Women in Business requested $4000 for 16 students to travel to their conference in Boston,
MA.

organization attempted to minimize costs as much as possible by traveling to
Jacksonville to fly to Boston.

system based on engagement, to remove bias as much as possible.

- The Kudzu Review sought $2,672.38 to fund club merchandise, printing costs, and venue rental

o The Kudzu Review is a literary magazine that publishes works by undergraduates on a
semesterly basis.
o The organization’s merchandise, while above the $10 cap, is being subsidized with the
club paying out of pocket the difference.
o The organization is unable to use student publications for their printing costs due to their
inability to print the literary magazine format.

- Willow Partners requested $4,750 to fund their travel to New York for 19 people.
o The Committee voted to fund their request at 99.17%, putting their total allocation to
$4,710.42.

mainly for supporting accommodations.

learn about their field on their trip to NYC.

Charlotte, NC.

allocated out in another semester during a prior semester.

Short Title: Recognizing National Blood Donor Month
Summary of Legislation:
This proclamation recognizes January as National Blood Donor and affirms the importance of
student awareness, participation, and civic engagement in blood donation. It highlights the role
of blood donation in medical care and campus safety, particularly as winter blood shortages
affect the Tallahassee community and Florida State University student population.
Background Information:
Blood is a critical component of emergency response, supporting trauma care, surgical
procedures, and treatment for both chronic and acute conditions. During the winter months,
blood donation rates decline while hospital demands remain steady. The Tallahassee area
relies on a regional blood supply network, meaning that seasonal shortages can directly impact
hospitals and emergency responders that serve locals and students. Therefore, Florida State
University students are both potential donors and patients within this healthcare system, as
access to donated blood affects emergency care available following accident, injuries, and
urgent care situations. January represents a high impact opportunity for increased
engagement as students return to campus at a time when blood donation levels are at their
lowest.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Dr. Stephen Chelko, Dr. Marshall A. Frank, D.O, MPH, Light the Night FSU.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This proclamation highlights faculty and student involvement and is presented to educate while
recognizing leadership and service in health advocacy. It formally recognizes January as
National Blood Donor Month and emphasizes the importance of student involvement in blood
donation as a matter of campus safety to affirm the values of civic responsibility, student
leadership, and encourages increased awareness among the student body.Docusign Envelope ID: 320354D8-DB67-4078-8AC7-C3A45E29967D

Short Title: Recognizing the Holy Month of Ramadan
Summary of Legislation:
This proclamation formally recognizes the holy month of Ramadan and honors its significance
to Muslim students, faculty, staff, and community members at Florida State University. It
acknowledges Ramadan as a time of reflection, service, self-discipline, and community, and
affirms the Student Senate’s commitment to inclusion and cultural awareness.
Background Information:
Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar and is observed by Muslims as a period of
fasting from dawn to sunset, prayer, self-reflection, and community service. Members of the
Florida State University community observe Ramadan through charity, devotion, and
mindfulness while balancing academic and professional responsibilities. Recognizing
Ramadan promotes cultural understanding, religious diversity, and supports an inclusive
campus community aligned with the values of Florida State University.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This proclamation was informed by conversations with Muslim students and members of the
Florida State University community, including the Muslim Student Union (MSU) and the Arab
Student Union (ASU). Additional consideration was given to the principles of inclusion,
diversity, and religious accommodation within the Student Government Association.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this proclamation will formally recognize the holy month of Ramadan within the
Student Senate record, affirm support for Muslim members of the FSU community, and
encourage awareness, respect, and inclusivity across campus.

Senate Proclamation #: 006
Primary Sponsor(s): Gurtis, Kaighin
Co-sponsor(s): Ferris, Jackson
Short Title: Improved Infrastructure Near DeGraff Hall
Summary of Legislation:
This Proclamation aims to bring awareness to the current lack of infrastructure near DeGraff
Hall. Specifically, this looks at a lack of crosswalk on the intersection of Dewey Street and W
Virginia Street, a lack of a walkway from this area to the DeGraff Tunnel, and better
maintenance for the gravel lots in this area. It also refers to contacts that will be contacted in
the future to facilitate the construction of this infrastructure, namely the City of Tallahassee and
Transportation and Parking Services.
Background Information:
There are currently 3 different apartments on W Virginia Street, and by the Fall there will be 4.
In the future, there have been discussions of further construction and off-campus student
housing in this area. Currently, the only method these students have to access campus without
crossing Tennessee Street is going through the DeGraff tunnel, which is inaccessible without
jaywalking due to a lack of a crosswalk on W Virginia St; this street sees speeds of 25 mph or
higher, so this is a large pedestrian risk that needs to be addressed. In addition, the area
around DeGraff Hall is not well-maintained, as a lack of a sidewalk is forcing pedestrians to
walk across the grass and parking lots, leading to the grass dying and further pedestrian risk
as they navigate around vehicles. Finally, the gravel lots near DeGraff Hall have been known
to cause damage to cars, as there are severe potholes and a lack of maintenance.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
So far I have been in preliminary talks with FSU Maintenance and TAPS contacts regarding
the crosswalk specifically. The OGA Director has also been contacted to try to find a contact
for the City of Tallahassee regarding future resolutions.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
To bring awareness to changes the Senate wishes to see as further construction and off-
campus student housing is developed in this area. In addition, bringing awareness to potential
pedestrian safety risks in the area that need to be resolved.Docusign Envelope ID: 692EDDAE-EB9D-47B9-958E-3F9AE2D180B9

Senate Proclamation #: 008
Primary Sponsor(s): Perantoni
Co-sponsor(s): Ramirez, Bigenho
Short Title: Recognizing the Holy period of Lent
Summary of Legislation:
This legislation would recognize the Holy period Lent, as well as go over the key components
of Lent and how it affects the lives of our campus community. It also discusses the perspective
of the Catholic Student Union’s director, and the importance of recognizing religious Holy
periods.
Background Information:
Lent is the 40 day period of fasting, prayer, and almsgiving emulating the Christ’s pilgrimage
through the desert for 40 days and 40 nights. The period begins on Ash Wednesday, which in
the Western Rite is February 18, and ends on Maundy Thursday, April 2, the night before the
Christ was to die on the Cross. Lent is an important background for many Christian students,
emphasizing the duties of the faith to recognize the believer’s faults, improve on one’s
character, and keep one’s heart open for the downtrodden and the destitute.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
Catholic Student Union was consulted on this legislation, as well as language inspired from the
US Conference of Catholic Bishops.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation would recognize Lent and its significance to students across campus,
recognizing its cultural and religious importance to our campus community.

Senate Proclamation #: 009
Primary Sponsor(s): Cohen
Co-sponsor(s): Holliday
Short Title: A proclamation encouraging the Student Senate to donate professional clothing to
the 2026 Spring Cleaning With Meaning Clothing Drive organized by the Career Center
Summary of Legislation: This proclamation encourages the Student Senate to donate
professional clothing to the 2026 Spring Cleaning With Meaning Clothing Drive organized by
the Career Center, running from March 2nd to April 3rd, 2026. This resolution sets a goal of
acquiring 100 items from senators and officers throughout the duration of the drive.
Background Information: The Professional Clothing Closet provides professional attire at no
cost to all part-time and full-time students at Florida State University. Access to professional
clothing is essential for students participating in interviews, internships, networking events, and
other career related opportunities. The Spring Cleaning With Meaning Clothing Drive supports
the Professional Clothing Closet by increasing available inventory and ensuring access to
professional resources for students across campus.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation: Senate President Holliday, Heather Lazar, Stormy
McGivern
Effect of Proposed Legislation: If enacted, this proclamation would formally encourage
Student Senate members to participate in the 2026 Spring Cleaning With Meaning Clothing
Drive by donating professional clothing. While non-binding, this action promotes engagement
and reinforces the Student Senate’s commitment to professional development and equity by
helping expand access to career ready resources for the student body.

Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Proclamation #: 010
Primary Sponsor(s): Naem
Co-sponsor(s): Holliday, Rodriguez , Mendez Arango, Bigenho, Macalintal, Staszak, White
Short Title: Recognizing the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory for its Scientific Contributions,
Educational Outreach, and Partnership with Florida State University
Summary of Legislation:
This proclamation recognizes the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory (MagLab) for its leadership
in scientific research, innovation, and education. It highlights the MagLab’s contributions to advancing
scientific knowledge, supporting student involvement from universities all over the nation, and
developing community outreach within nearby elementary schools and individuals interested in learning
about their processes. Additionally, this proclamation expresses support for continued collaboration
between Florida State University and the MagLab
Background Information:
The National High Magnetic Field Laboratory is the largest and most powerful magnet laboratory in the
world. It serves as a place for research in fields such as physics, chemistry, materials science and
engineering, The MagLab also provides students of all ages with opportunities to engage with scientific
concepts, research and collaboration with scientists.
Through its outreach, including tours, elementary school visits, and community events, the MagLab
plays a vital role in promoting science and inspiring future generations of researchers and scientists. A
recent visit by the Student Senate has further highlighted the impact of the MagLab on the university
community and the entire nation.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
This proclamation was developed in consultation with Student Senate members who attended the
scheduled MagLab tour, students involved in research at the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory
and a representative at the MagLab who guided the Senate tour. Additional information was gathered
from public information posted on the MagLab website regarding their initiatives, mission, and research
impact.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If adopted, this proclamation will formally recognize the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory for its
contributions to Florida State University and the scientific community. It will also demonstrate the
Student Senate’s support for continued collaboration, student engagement, and outreach with the
MagLab.Docusign Envelope ID: 4784E0CB-F837-4FE1-BFCD-80C3D0E35D89

Senate Proclamation #: 011
Primary Sponsor(s): Collantes, Fernandez
Co-sponsor(s): Rodriguez, Abreu Diaz
Short Title: Honoring the Life and Legacy of Marco Perez-Vazquez
Summary of Legislation:
This Proclamation demonstrates the character, involvement, and spirit of Marco Perez-Vazquez in his
invaluable time here at Florida State University. Through the voices of affected individuals, Marco's
character is exemplified. This piece of legislation recognizes Marco's contributions to the campus
community as they are told from the community itself. In this proclamation, we don't intend to capture
his impact through description, but through student perspectives.
Background Information:
In Fall 2025, Marco Perez-Vazquez sadly passed away, leaving a hole in the Florida State University
community.
Legislative Outreach and Consultation:
The sponsors reached out to Marco's family, Marco's close friends and Marco's affiliated organizations.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This piece of legislation honors and preserves the spirit of Marco Perez-Vazquez, whose legacy
persists through his acts of leadership, kindness, and service towards others.
