Senate Resolution #: 004
Primary Sponsor(s): Patel
Co-sponsor(s): Naranjo Abraham, Prieschl
Short Title: Resource for Travel Allocation Consent Resolution on January 13, 2025
Summary of Legislation: This resolution proposes the allocation of $34,202.18 from the
Resource Travel Allocation Committee (RTAC) fund to support 13 registered student
organizations, Student Academy of Audiology, The Business Case Club at FSU, All Night
Yahtzee, Kappa Delta Chi Sorority Inc., Seminole Dance Force at FSU, Alpha Epsilon Delta,
Lambda Alpha Epsilon, Medical Brigades at FSU, We Raise the Bar, Cricket Association at
FSU, Dental Brigades at FSU, FSU Flying High Circus Club, and American Marketing
Association with travel expenses for their respective trips.
Background Information: Student Academy of Audiology is a planning to attend a
conference in New Orleans, where their members will be able to attend seminars by
professionals regarding graduate success, speak to faculty and current students at prospective
graduate programs and demo new hearing technology that recently became available, allowing
audiology interested students to become familiar with hearing devices. 8 students will be
traveling from 3/25 till 3/29. Students will participate at a cost of $212.50 per person
(excluding personal meals). This event was advertised on social media platforms, GroupMe
and at their meetings.
The Business Case Club at FSU is an organization focused on enabling students to obtain real
world business experience through case competitions. Their trips will allow students to
showcase their business skills and provide an opportunity to network with other students and
employers. Students will attend two competitions, The McDonough Business Strategy
Challenge (2/20-2/22) and Milgard Invitational Undergraduate Case Competition on Social
Responsibility (2/27-3/1). There are 4 students attending each and they will participate at a
cost of $200 per person (excluding personal meals). Attendees will be chosen by an interview
process.
All Night Yahtzee is an organization for students interested in exploring the A Cappella world.
Members are able to gain professional singing, dancing, performing and recording experience.
They are planning to attend ICCA quarterfinals (2/7-2/9), which is a yearly acapella
competition. About 14 students will attend and will participate at a cost of about $74 per
person (excluding personal meals).Docusign Envelope ID: 67CC3F50-B36B-4112-8456-CFB3F206EB6D

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Kappa Delta Chi Sorority Inc. is a part of the Multicultural Greek Council and promotes the
values of unity, honesty, integrity and leadership. They have service events, sisterhood
retreats,and academic and cultural workshops. 10 of their members are planning to attend a
regional conference (4/3-5/46) where their sisters will be able to expand their professional
networks through a variety of educational conferences as well as participate in service
activities. Members will participate at a cost of $300 per person (excluding personal meals).
Seminole Dance Force mission is to offer dedicated dances the chance to represent FSU
through performance and competition. The purpose of their trip is to participate in a dance
competition (NDA nationals from 4/9 till 4/13) against other D1A collegiate dance teams.
About 25-28 students will participate at a cost of about $75 per person (excluding personal
meals).
Alpha Epsilon Delta is an organization dedicated to the encouragement and recognition of
excellence in pre professional health scholarship, including medicine, dentistry, veterinary, and
others. Their trip on 3/9 till 3/25 provides knowledge and experience in a different culture’s
medical practice. 12 students are planning to attend this trip and will participate at a cost of
$300 per person (excluding personal meals).
Lambda Alpha Epsilon is an organization aimed at improving criminal justice through
educational activities fostering professionalism is law enforcement personnel and agencies,
and promoting professional, academic, and public awareness of criminal justice issues. They
are attending a national conference on 3/28 till 4/6 and students will be able to learn more
about the criminal justice field. 14 students are planning to attend this trip and will participate
at a cost of about $107 per person (excluding personal meals)
Medical Brigades at FSU is a movement of students and medical professionals working
alongside communities to implement sustainable health systems. Their trip to Honduras will
allow students to get hands on learning experience with patients and the opportunity to
volunteer and serve in communities in dire need. Their trip was advertised on social media, at
the involvement fairs and in classrooms. The trip is from 3/7 till 3/15 and 65 students are
planning to attend and will participate at a cost of about $61 per person (excluding personal
meals).
We Raise the Bar is an organization aimed at inspiring black individuals to pursue a career in
law. Their members are planning to go on Law School Tours in the Boston area. This trip was
advertised across social media platforms. Their trip is from 4/3-4/6 and 14 students plan to
attend and will participate at a cost of about $187.50 per person (excluding personal meals).
Cricket Association at FSU is a cricket organization. They are planning to travel to Texas for
NCCA (Nationals for Cricket). At this competition, they have the opportunity to be scouted by
the U.S. national team and other professional club teams for cricket. Their trip is from 3/10 till
3/17 and 15 students will be attending and will participate at a cost of about $206 per person
(excluding personal meals).Docusign Envelope ID: 67CC3F50-B36B-4112-8456-CFB3F206EB6D

underserved communities worldwide. Their trip to Panama (5/5-5/11) will provide students to

Medical Brigades at FSU, We Raise the Bar, Cricket Association at FSU, Dental Brigades at

Short Title:
This legislation transfers $2,000 from Executive Projects to the Food for Thought Pantry to aid in the
creation of a Natural Disaster Surplus.
Summary of Legislation:
This legislation matches the funds previously acquired from Senate Projects in Bill #105 from the 76th
Student Senate Session for the creation of the Food for Thought Pantry’s Natural Disaster Surplus.
This surplus will consist of pre-packaged, nonperishable bags of food to be made, managed, and
distributed by The Pantry in cases of hurricanes, major tropical storms, and other instances of natural
disaster.
Background Information:
Florida State University’s student government does not currently have any bills or programs in place to
secure food resources for our campus’ food pantry during natural disaster emergencies. The university
has faced such situations in the past and will likely face similar, if not worse, situations in the future.
The Food For Thought Pantry’s Director, Haley Gentile, has provided the following examples:
- On August 29, 2023, in the Fall 2023 Term, in preparation for Hurricane Idalia, FSU’s Food
for Thought Pantry served 305 students non-perishable and non-refrigerated perishable
food items.
- In the week following the May 10, 2024, tornados the Pantry experienced a 148% increase
in unique users relative to the previous week.
- During Hurricane Helene, on September 24, 2024, the Pantry handed out 215 prepackaged
bags and subsequently assisted 171 students in the Student Refuge Center with snacks
during the storm itself.
In all such circumstances, the Pantry ran out of resources, leaving them no choice but to turn students
away. This stems from a lack of safekeeping of emergency resources that the pantry did not have at
their disposal. Given the university’s location in Florida, a region highly susceptible to natural disasters
such as hurricanes, it is imperative to establish a framework that enables our food pantry to support
students during crises that disrupt their access to basic necessities – like food.
The Food for Thought Pantry’s Director, has been a strong advocate for this initiative. They have
meticulously calculated the most cost-effective and nutritious non-perishable items to include in pre-Docusign Envelope ID: 5824457A-8DFF-4F84-AAB3-B31C679590AC

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
packaged food bags that the surplus would consist of. While $2,000 was secured through Senate
Projects to support this effort, it represents only half of the funds required to fully implement the
initiative. This partial funding was a deliberate decision to allow both branches of Student Government
to play an active role in this project, with the remaining $2,000 requested in this bill from Executive
Projects to complete the match. Most importantly, this matched funding has already received approval
from the Executive Branch.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation will ensure that students who rely on the Food for Thought Pantry have access to
essential food resources during natural disasters. By creating a surplus of supplies, the Pantry will be
better equipped to meet demand, preventing future shortages in these unprecedented situations.

Summary of Legislation:
This resolution proposes the allocation of $655 from the Programming Allocation Committee
(PAC) fund to support two Registered organizations: Women in Accounting and The Institute of
Electrical and Electronics Engineers with programming expenses for their organization. The
additional RSO’s mentioned within the Consent Resolution were zero funded by the committee

Background Information:
Women in Accounting (WIA) at Florida State University is dedicated to informing and
empowering students, especially women, about the diverse opportunities in accounting and
finance. The organization connects students with potential employers, turning these
connections into successful career paths. WIA equips its members with valuable knowledge,
leadership skills, and professionalism that are essential in today’s business world. By offering
resources like leadership training and networking events, WIA plays a crucial role in enhancing
professional development for students who might otherwise lack access to such opportunities.
Supporting WIA helps students gain the insights and connections needed for post-graduation
success. Beyond career growth, WIA fosters a strong community of female accounting
students, promoting empowerment and a sense of belonging on campus. This community not
only supports individual career goals but also builds lasting relationships, helping women thrive
in the accounting and finance industries as they transition from academia to their professional
lives.
IEEE is a non-profit organization dedicated to advancing electrotechnology and related
sciences for the benefit of humanity and the professional development of its members.
Originally standing for the "Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers," IEEE promotes
the practice of electrical engineering, computer engineering, and associated fields. This
purchase benefits the Florida State University student body by fostering a sense of community
and pride among members while enhancing campus visibility. Custom shirts serve as a
unifying symbol for the club, encouraging student involvement, promoting school spirit, and
showcasing the diverse interests and accomplishments of FSU students. Ultimately, these
efforts help create a more vibrant and connected campus culture.Docusign Envelope ID: 128856C0-E53F-45C1-9485-E1A6BD5D3523

Resolution #: 008
Primary Sponsor(s): Wong
Co-sponsor(s): Rios
Short Title: This consent resolution requests $10,471.50 to support various RSOs on campus,
enhancing their ability to host cultural, educational, and community-building events. The
funding will strengthen student engagement, promote inclusivity, and enrich the campus
environment by investing in diverse programming and student leadership.
Summary of Legislation:
This consent resolution requests the allocation of $10,471.50 to be distributed among various
Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) on campus to help supplement their programming
needs for the upcoming semester. This funding will play a crucial role in enhancing the student
experience by providing necessary financial support for events, activities, and initiatives
organized by RSOs. The requested funds will enable these organizations to host a wide range
of programming, from cultural and educational events to social and community-building
activities, which contribute to a vibrant campus atmosphere. This allocation will ensure that
RSOs have the resources needed to engage students, foster a sense of belonging, and enrich
the overall campus environment. By supporting these organizations, we are investing in
student leadership, creativity, and the development of diverse and inclusive programming that
benefits the entire student body.
Background Information:
Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) are integral to the cultural, educational, and social
fabric of the campus community. They play a critical role in promoting diversity, leadership
development, and student involvement. This funding will support these organizations in
carrying out impactful programming that aligns with the values of inclusivity and community-
building at FSU.
Chabad@FSU:
Chabad@FSU is a student-led organization dedicated to fostering Jewish life and culture on
campus. They provide a welcoming space for Jewish students through events like Shabbat
dinners, Jewish holiday celebrations, social activities, and educational opportunities aboutDocusign Envelope ID: A679A3FE-9791-47F9-979A-388B9DC8BD20

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Jewish traditions. Chabad serves as a community for students to connect with their faith and
peers.
Chinese Students and Scholars Association (CSSA):
The CSSA at FSU aims to promote Chinese culture and strengthen the sense of community
among Chinese students and scholars. The association organizes cultural events, academic
seminars, and social gatherings to help Chinese students adjust to life in the U.S., while also
fostering cross-cultural understanding with the broader FSU community.
Sisters 2 Service:
Sisters 2 Service is an organization focused on empowering women through service-based
leadership. The group engages in community service projects and fosters personal and
professional growth among its members. Their initiatives are centered on social justice,
volunteerism, and creating a positive impact on both the FSU campus and beyond.
Dental Brigades:
FSU's Dental Brigades is a chapter of the global organization that works to provide dental care
and education to underserved communities. The group organizes medical and dental brigades,
where students travel to rural areas to offer free dental services, health education, and
preventative care, all while developing hands-on skills in the field of dentistry.
National Organization for the Professional Advancement of Black Chemists and
Chemical Engineers (NOBCChE):
NOBCChE at FSU is a chapter of the national organization that focuses on the advancement
and support of Black professionals in the fields of chemistry and chemical engineering. The
group works to provide resources, mentorship, and networking opportunities for Black
students, while advocating for diversity, equity, and inclusion in STEM fields.
Alpha Kappa Delta Phi:
Alpha Kappa Delta Phi (aKDPhi) is a sorority dedicated to empowering women and promoting
academic excellence. It is known for its strong commitment to community service,
philanthropy, and fostering leadership among women. aKDPhi is also a member of the
National Panhellenic Conference, emphasizing diversity, inclusivity, and sisterhood.
Effect of Proposed Legislation: This resolution will provide vital financial support to the
RSOs, empowering them to carry out transformative activities that drive cultural engagement
and professional growth. These funding requests are not just investments in individual
organizations, but in the future of the FSU community, advancing inclusivity, fostering
leadership, and creating invaluable career opportunities for students.

Summary of Legislation:
This bill provides funding allocations to various RSOs through the Organizational Fund, as
outlined in Chapter 814: The RSO Organizational Fund Act of 2023. It details the funding
amounts awarded, criteria for eligibility, and reasons for denied funding requests
Background Information:
The Organizational Fund was established by the 75th Student Senate Bill 68 to support newly
formed, returning, or revitalized RSOs. It provides funding for essential startup costs such as
tabling materials, marketing supplies, and other necessary resources. The fund ensures
equitable distribution and accessibility of financial support for student organizations at FSU.
Meetings to evaluate applications occur every Monday from 3 PM to 5 PM via Zoom, where
applications are reviewed, and recommendations are forwarded to the Student Senate Finance
Committee for consent resolution drafting.
Recent funding allocations include:
• $466 to College of Music Black Alliance – Approved for a tablecloth, stickers, and
other tabling materials.
• $113.04 to Business Students from Abroad at FSU – Approved for tabling materials.
• $0 to White Mouse Productions – Denied due to a request for an iPad, which is not
aligned with the purpose of the fund.
• $0 to Lebanese Social Organization – Denied as all requested items were already
purchased in the past month, and reimbursements are not permitted.
The fund aims to simplify and streamline the funding process for RSOs, setting a standard for
accessible financial support

Legislation Cover Sheet
Resolution #: 015
Primary Sponsor(s): Patel
Co-sponsor(s): Naranjo Abraham, Prieschl
Short Title: Resource for Travel Allocation Consent Resolution on February 10, 2025
Summary of Legislation: This resolution proposes the allocation of $4,275.08 from the
Resource Travel Allocation Committee (RTAC) fund to support 4 registered student
organizations, All Night Yahtzee, Pre-Veterinary Club at FSU, International English Honor
Society, American Institute of Chemical Engineers, with travel expenses for their respective
trips.
Background Information:
All Night Yahtzee is an a Cappella group on campus which aims to create a welcoming
environment where members can gain exceptional and professional singing, dancing,
performing, and recording experience. Their ICCA competition on 3/7-3/9 will allow their
members to compete in the semi finals. 14 students are attending and will participate at a cost
of about $73 per person (excluding personal meals).
Pre-Veterinary Club at FSU is an organization aimed at expanding students' interest in
veterinary medicine and/or animal related fields. Their trip on 3/14-3/16 will allow 6 students to
participate in labs, lectures, and tabling expos, which will allow them to network and learn more
about the veterinary field. Students will participate at a cost of $150 per person (excluding
personal meals).
International English Honor Society is an organization that allows its members to access
scholarship and award opportunities, conferences, and internship possibilities. Their
convention on 3/19-3/23 will allow members to network and listen to guest speakers. 10
students plan to attend at a cost of $110 per person (excluding personal meals).
American Institute of Chemical Engineers is an organization that aims to provide professional
enrichment and social support to its members. 24 students are planning to attend their
conference on 3/28-3/29 where students will be able to enter competitions to win awards and
network with potential employers. Students will participate at a cost of $52 per person
(excluding personal meals).Docusign Envelope ID: D497A74E-013D-44E2-8FC5-F24E686FA01F

community’s growth, fostering inclusivity, leadership, and career advancement opportunities
for students.

Legislation Cover Sheet
Resolution #: 019
Primary Sponsor(s): Holliday, Vandermeulen
Co-sponsor(s): Goldstein
Short Title: Proposing questions created and voted on by the Campus Pulse Commission to
be included in the Spring 2025 SGA Election.
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution would add three questions to the ballot provided to the student body on election
day. These questions are with regard to the voting window, adequate organization funding,
and nighttime transportation.
Background Information:
These questions were the result of an in-depth discussion by the Campus Pulse Commission,
which consists of representatives from multiple SGA factions. This is in effort to seek tangible
answers as they relate to opinions of the student body at large. The questions proposed allow
for potential adjustments to future elections as well as to SGA initiatives.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If passed, this resolution would add these three questions onto the ballot for the Spring 2025
SGA Election ballot:
1. The Student Government Association elections currently have a single-day voting
window from 8:00 AM to 7:00 PM. Should the voting period be extended beyond one
day?
2. Do you believe student organizations receive adequate funding from SGA?
3. Should the SGA advocate for university initiatives to expand and improve student
nighttime transportation services?

Resolution #: 020
Primary Sponsor(s): Wong
Co-sponsor(s): Rios
Short Title: Consent Resolution for the allocation $5,032.24 to be allocated amongst various
RSOs.
Summary of Legislation:
This consent resolution proposes the allocation of $5,032.24 to be distributed among various
Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) on campus to support their programming needs for
this semester. This funding will be essential in enhancing the student experience by providing
financial support for events, activities, and initiatives organized by the RSOs. With these funds,
the organizations will be able to host a variety of programs, including cultural, educational,
social, and community-building events, all of which contribute to a lively and engaging campus
environment. This allocation ensures that RSOs have the resources necessary to engage
students, foster a sense of community, and enrich campus life. By supporting these
organizations, we are investing in student leadership, creativity, and the creation of diverse,
inclusive programming that benefits the entire student body.
Background Information:
Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) are integral to the cultural, educational, and social
fabric of the campus community. They play a critical role in promoting diversity, leadership
development, and student involvement. This funding will support these organizations in
carrying out impactful programming that aligns with the values of inclusivity and community-
building at FSU.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This resolution will provide vital financial support to the RSOs, empowering them to carry out
transformative activities that drive cultural engagement and professional growth. These funding
requests are not just investments in individual organizations, but in the future of the FSU
community, advancing inclusivity, fostering leadership, and creating invaluable career
opportunities for students.

fabric of the campus community. They play a critical role in promoting diversity, leadership
development, and student involvement. This funding will support these organizations in

building at FSU.

transformative activities that drive cultural engagement and professional growth. These funding
requests are not just investments in individual organizations, but in the future of the FSU
community, advancing inclusivity, fostering leadership, and creating invaluable career
opportunities for students.

process for RSOs, setting a standard for accessible financial support

that student organizations receive the necessary financial support to facilitate their operations.

requests.

Short Title: Establishing a Free Printing Program
Summary of Legislation:
This proclamation seeks to formally recognize the need to implement a free printing quota for
enrolled students. The exact details of the proposal will be available after research is
completed by Business & Administration.
Background Information:
Printing is often required for career fairs, essays, and other academic documents. However,
on-campus printing currently requires a minimum deposit of $10 and a cost of 11c per sheet.
This legislation seeks to remove that financial barrier. 4 different parties have been met with
and are listed below.
University of South Florida Student Government:
- USF provides $3 per day in printing credits for all enrolled students. This credit does not
roll over daily and is valid only for black and white printing. I was provided with the
budget for FY2023 and the printing line-item averages to 37c per student, per year.
- USF uses the same technology, Pharos Print Management Software, along with
Kyocera printers. This makes costs near identical.
Student Publications:
- Melissa Gibbs and Miranda Hawkins agreed that financials could be run through them
as opposed to creating a new line-item.
Libraries:
- Crystal Mathews and Eleanor Cleveland are both committed to executing this proposal
and to handle advertising and marketing of program once released.
OBS:
- Tom Murphy (Administrative Services) and Matt Sugrue (IT) agreed to act as liaisons
and gave the plan a preliminary approval. There would be no issues with execution on a
technology basis.
- Shooting for a Spring 2026 rollout with OK of senate.

industries. Their trip on 3/6-3/8 in Tampa, FL will allow attendees to gain industry insights,
professional connections, and hands-on experiences. 6 students plan to attend at a cost of
$100 per person (excluding per person).
American Society of Civil Engineers helps bring students together and increase interest in the
civil engineering discipline not only through meetings but with events such as community
service and student conferences. Their trip on 3/5-3/9 in Georgia will expose their students to
many opportunities that will advance their career. Additionally, students will be able to

students, foster a sense of community, and enrich campus life. By supporting these
organizations, we are investing in student leadership, creativity, and the creation of diverse,
inclusive programming that benefits the entire student body.

Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) are integral to the cultural, educational, and social
fabric of the campus community. They play a critical role in promoting diversity, leadership
development, and student involvement. This funding will support these organizations in
carrying out impactful programming that aligns with the values of inclusivity and community-
building at FSU.

Short Title: Allocating Funding for FSU Day at the Capitol Catering
Summary of Legislation: This legislation allocates $5,000 from the OGA expenses category
to the OGA food category to fund catering for FSU Day at the Capitol.
Background Information:
FSU Day at the Capitol: FSU Day at the Capitol is an annual event celebrating the
university’s academic achievements, athletic success, and contributions to the state of Florida.
The event features display from various colleges and departments set up on the first three
floors of the Capitol, as well as an outdoor pep rally showcasing FSU leadership, student
organizations, and school spirit. Additionally, a reception co-hosted by the FSU Student
Government Association provides an opportunity to recognize legislators and university
stakeholders. This event serves as a key opportunity to highlight the university’s impact and
strengthen relationships with state policymakers. To ensure the continued success of this
event, this legislation allocates $5,000 to the OGA food category to fund category at FSU Day
at the Capitol.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation will allow the Office of Governmental Affairs to fulfill their responsibility and
purchase catering for FSU Day at the Capitol.

Senate Resolution #: 029
Primary Sponsor(s): Holliday, Foy
Co-sponsor(s): Benner, Cappel, Leger, Mani, Mendez Arango, Noumena, Rios, Tumuluri,
Williams
Short Title: This resolution describes in detail the ADA Accessibility Ad Hoc Committee’s
recommendations for a series of ‘Accessibility Surveys’ to be conducted in tandem with the
Executive Branch and other university stakeholders, after recommendation and guidance from
the Office of Accessibility Services.
Summary of Legislation: This resolution outlines in clear detail the current plan the ADA
Accessibility Ad-Hoc Committee has been working on for ‘Accessibility Surveys’. As outlined in
the resolution, these surveys shall be a joint effort between the ADA Accessibility Ad-Hoc
Committee and the Student Government Association’s Executive Branch, with insight from the
Office of Accessibility Services, FSU Facilities, FSU PD, FSU Housing, and any other pertinent
entities.
Background Information: Established as an ‘ad-hoc’ or temporary committee, the ADA
Accessibility Ad-Hoc Committee has been tasked with identifying areas lacking ADA
accessibility on campus while gathering input from various university entities. After numerous
conversations with the Director of the Office of Accessibility Services Amber Wagner and
deliberation within the committee, the members have decided a series of ‘Accessibility
Surveys’ would be the most effective way to gather the information needed to help students
and increase campus access for all.
Effect of Proposed Legislation: If passed, this resolution would act as an outline for and
binding plan to the committee and the Executive Branch for the execution of these surveys.
Once conducted, the data recorded from these surveys will be distributed to various University

The ADA Accessibility Ad Hoc Committee’s recommendations for a series of ‘Accessibility
Surveys’ to be conducted in tandem with the Executive Branch and other university
stakeholders, after recommendation and guidance from the Office of Accessibility Services.
WHEREAS, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990 mandates that public institutions,1
including universities, provide equal access and accommodations to individuals with disabilities;2
and3
WHEREAS, Florida State University (FSU) and the 77th Student Senate is committed to fostering an4
inclusive and accessible campus environment for all students, faculty, staff, and visitors; and5
WHEREAS, numerous instances of ADA issues have been identified on FSU’s campus, creating6
barriers that hinder the full participation of individuals with disabilities, which have been reported to7
the Office of Accessibility Services (OAS); and8
WHEREAS, these issues include but are not limited to inaccessible building entrances, inadequate9
signage, lack of proper ramps, malfunctioning or absent automatic doors, inaccessible restroom10
facilities, and insufficient accommodations within classrooms and common areas; and11
WHEREAS, it is necessary to take proactive steps to assess and address these accessibility concerns12
in order to ensure that FSU remains in compliance with ADA regulation; and13
WHEREAS, the creation of an ADA Accessibility Ad Hoc Committee within the Student Senate enables14
a dedicated group of senators to identify and propose solutions for ADA-related issues on campus;15
and16
WHEREAS, after numerous meetings and extensive communication, this committee will conduct a17
series of ‘Accessibility Surveys’ of campus buildings and facilities to assess ADA accessibility and18
compile a report of necessary improvements, per suggestion and guidance from OAS; and19Docusign Envelope ID: 6CE9D81F-0652-41F1-876D-0878F0329B63

WHEREAS, these surveys shall be conducted jointly with the Executive Branch of the Student20
Government Association; and21
WHEREAS, all relevant stakeholders must be included in the execution of these surveys, such as OAS,22
FSU Facilities, FSU PD, FSU Housing, and any other pertinent entities; and23
WHEREAS, the committee recommends conducting these numerous surveys on different days,24
splitting the campus up into different quadrants to report on as many buildings as possible as close25
as possible; and26
WHEREAS, each individual quadrant may be further divided and delegated amongst groups of 2-427
volunteers, so as much ground is covered as possible and limited time constraints are put upon28
participants; and29
WHEREAS, to record accessibility or lack thereof across campus, a spreadsheet shall be provided to30
volunteers with simple yes or no questions to answer related to basic accessibility, such as “Are all31
entrances wheelchair accessible?” and “Are there ramps available where there are stairs?”; and32
WHEREAS, volunteers may record the answers to these questions in the given rows of their delegated33
buildings and areas, providing photographic evidence and elaboration where necessary; and34
WHEREAS, after each location and building on campus is surveyed, this data shall be compiled in35
another resolution and both it, the spreadsheet, and any other important information shall be sent to36
all relevant campus entities, specifically University Administration, FSU Facilities, and OAS, with37
possible solutions outlined; and38
WHEREAS, ensuring ADA compliance and enhancing accessibility will contribute to a more inclusive39
campus culture and improve the overall experience for all members of the FSU community; and40
WHEREAS, it is necessary to take proactive steps to assess and address these accessibility concerns41
in order to ensure that FSU remains in compliance with ADA regulation and helps its population of42
students with disabilities; and43
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the 77th Student Senate at Florida State University that:44
this committee and SGA’s Executive Branch shall conduct a thorough review of campus45
accessibility, engage with affected students and faculty, and propose actionable solutions to46
address identified barriers; and47
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that: the committee shall provide regular updates to the Student Senate48
and work in partnership with university administration to implement necessary changes, ensuring49
that FSU meets and exceeds ADA standards for accessibility.50

Short Title: Senate Project Transfer for kNOw More Student Advisory Board’s “Take Back the
Night” event
Summary of Legislation:
This Transfer Resolution would allocate $1,088 from the Senate Projects account to help fund
the creation of t-shirts for the kNOw More Student Advisory Board’s annual “Take Back the
Night” event.
Background Information:
The kNOw More Student Advisory Board (SAB) is facilitated by The Center for Health
Wellness and Advocacy (CHAW). Their mission is to provide a student perspective and voice
to power based personal violence prevention, response, and policy initiatives on campus.
Power based personal violence is defined as sexual assault, relationship violence, and
stalking.
Since April is Sexual Assault Awareness Month (SAAM), kNOw More SAB does an annual
“Take Back the Night” event. Nationally, this event’s purpose is to protest sexual violence,
empower victims to reclaim their right to feel safe at night, along with public spaces, and raise
awareness on campus. This year Florida State’s “Take Back the Night” will consist of a march,
guest speakers, a survivor speak out, and a variety of tabling via RSO’s as well as campus
partners.
A key aspect of raising awareness and promoting solidarity is through t-shirts that support the
cause. These will be passed out during the “Take Back the Night” event which is on April 10th
from 5-9PM in the Commons Courtyard and is therefore accessible to all Florida State
students. However, kNOw More SAB doesn’t get any specific funding from CHAW and the
small amount that is allocated is not enough for t-shirts. In 2024, there were no t-shirts due to a
lack of funding. However, in 2023, kNOw More SAB received $1,100 in funding from Senate’s
sweepings and were thus able to have t-shirts. Additionally, since kNOw More SAB is not an
RSO, requesting funds through PAC is not a feasible option.
According to the FSU Toolkit on Healthy Relationships, 1 in 4 women will be sexually
assaulted or experience an attempt while in college. To put that into perspective, according to
a report by US News, as of fall 2023, there are 24,643 female students at FSU and 6,160
would be a victim of sexual assault or attempts before graduation. As a Student Senate,Docusign Envelope ID: 60F35557-E3A0-4381-931F-75BD89932C4B

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
providing funds that enable events like “Take Back the Night” to be more successful is key to
exemplifying that sexual assault awareness is a topic that we deem of high importance.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation would allocate $1,088.00 from the Senate Projects account to the kNOw More
Student Advisory Board for creation of t-shirts supporting the annual “Take Back the Night”
event. On a larger scale, Senate’s enactment would exemplify solidarity and support against
sexual assault both nationally and on Florida State’s campus.

Short Title: Amending Rule thirteen sections four, nine, and ten of the Student Senate’s Rules
of Procedure.
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution seeks to amend the Student Senate’s attendance policies by revising the
number of absences a senator may accumulate before facing penalties, as well as clarifying
the procedures for reassignment, suspension, and potential impeachment.
Background Information:
The Student Senate plays an essential role in representing the student body and making
decisions that directly impact campus life. Nevertheless, serving as a Student Senator is a
commitment that requires time, effort, and active participation. When senators miss committee
or Senate meetings, they miss important discussions and decisions that affect the students
they represent. In hopes of encouraging senators to regard their positions with the utmost
respect and commitment, we have decided to amend the attendance polices and penalties for
absences.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation will tighten the attendance requirement for the Student Senate, by amending
our rules of procedure regarding committee attendances, absences, and the penalties for
excessive absences. By strengthening the policies surrounding absences and reinforcing clear
accountability measures, we are upholding the integrity of the Student Senate and ensuring
that every elected representative fulfills their duty to serve with dedication. As elected officials
entrusted with representing the interests of the student body, we bear the responsibility of
treating these positions with the highest level of commitment, respect, and professionalism.
Through these amendments, we reaffirm our commitment to active participation and
responsible governance ensuring that the Senate remains a body that students can rely on to
advocate for their best interests.

Summary of Legislation:
This resolution seeks to authorize a budget transfer of $523.46 from the Clothing and Awards
category of the Hispanic/LatinX Student Union’s (HLSU) budget to the Contractual Services
category. The transfer will provide necessary funding to support this year’s annual gala, “Baile
Enmascarado”. This is an event dedicated to uniting the entire Hispanic/LatinX community.
From affiliate organizations and Juana Bordas Mentorship Program participants to allies
among the student body, it’s an opportunity to recognize and celebrate all of the hard work that
went into uplifting their community this past year.
Background Information:
The Hispanic/LatinX Student Union is an integral agency that’s dedicated to cultural
awareness, advocacy, professional development, and serves as a safe haven within the
greater Florida State University community. HLSU is organizing its annual gala, a night that
includes commemorating graduating seniors, awarding dedicated affiliate organizations, and
celebrating the Hispanic/LatinX with food along with cultural performances. Thus, additional
funding is necessary to successfully provide food via a catering contract for the over 200
attendees and HLSU has identified surplus funds in the Clothing and Awards category of their
budget that can be reallocated to support event expenses.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
A budget transfer in the amount of $523.46 if authorized from the Hispanic/LatinX Student
Union’s Clothing and Awards category to the Contractual Services category, would aid in
covering costs for this year’s “Baile Enmascarado” or annual gala.

of this venture is included.
Background Information:
Issues surrounding availability of umbrellas on campus has been an issue for a long time,
especially as the spring months come around and rain becomes more frequent. Students and
staff should not need to get soaked on their way to class due to sporadic weather. With a
rental system, they would be able to rent out umbrellas for the duration that they need and
then they’d be able to return it for the next student to use. Important factors within researching
this topic were accessibility of use, accountability, and affordability for all those who wished to
use the service. After extensive research, a company called “RentBrella” was found (of which
information is attached to this legislation) that could help with this issue.
Because SGA cannot enter contracts with outside companies on its own, this resolution is to
help coordinate SGA with the appropriate campus partner(s) to make this happen. Contracts of
this nature have been, in the past, coordinated with the Office of Business Services; therefore,
this resolution would direct SGA to coordinate with them as a first step.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This resolution’s intended purpose is to connect all stakeholders that could be involved into
researching feasible options to make this a venue for students, faculty, staff and visitors alike
to rent out umbrellas on campus. This resolution would, additionally, direct the Senate liaison
to the Executive Branch to start conversations and coordinate with the Office of Business
Services to explore what venues are available for this venture.

Short Title: Resolution seeking to authorize a budget transfer of $1,000 from the Contractual
Services category of the Pride Student Union’s budget to the Clothing and Awards category to
aid in expenses for their upcoming end-of-year events.
Summary of Legislation:
Pride Student Union has several large, end-of-year events planned that need to be funded.
This legislation simply moves their funds from one category to another, allowing these events
to be funded with the existing money the Pride Student Union has already.
Background Information:
The Pride Student Union is a monumental organization on campus that provides a safe,
supportive environment to a marginalized community. Due to recent state legislation, Pride has
had to bear a heavier financial burden than in the past for some of these events, including the
Lavender Celebration. The Lavender Celebration recognizes the accomplishments of
graduating LGBTQ+ students, both undergraduate and graduate levels. This event is a
significant milestone for the community as a whole and the individuals within it: it provides a
safe space to celebrate both accolades and identities.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation would allow Pride Student Union to fully fund their end-of-year events. These
events, like the Lavender Celebration and Pride Prom, provide safe places where students of a
marginalized community can celebrate while being safe and happy. This legislation would help
ensure all parts of the FSU student body are healthy and happy.

Short Title: A Resolution Advocating for Student Representation in Florida State University’s
Post-Incident Review Process
Summary of Legislation:
This proposed resolution urges Florida State University to include formal student
representation—through the Executive Branch, Student Senate, and Congress of Graduate
Students—in the University’s forthcoming post-incident review of the April 17, 2025, tragedy. It
outlines the Student Government Association’s position that meaningful student involvement is
critical to developing thoughtful, effective campus safety reforms.
Background Information:
On April 17, 2025, an active shooter opened fire inside the FSU Student Union, killing two
members of the university community and injuring six others. In the days that followed, over
30,000 individuals signed a public petition calling for improved safety infrastructure, particularly
locks on classroom doors. Students, faculty, and staff across campus have since expressed a
strong desire to be heard and included in the recovery and prevention process.
This proposed resolution responds to that moment by formally requesting that student voices
be integrated into the University's after-action review. It further affirms the Student Government
Association’s readiness to coordinate student feedback and support a comprehensive,
prevention-focused approach to future safety planning.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If adopted, this resolution would establish the official position of the Student Government
Association that students must be active participants in the University’s institutional review and
future safety initiatives. It would authorize the Student Body President to formally transmit this
position to university leadership on behalf of the SGA.

Short Title: A resolution awarding the FSU Student Senate Award for Excellence to the first
responder agencies whose swift and courageous actions during the April 17, 2025, tragedy at Florida
State University exemplified distinguished service to the university and the broader community.
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution formally recognizes and honors the coordinated efforts of law enforcement, emergency
medical services, and supporting agencies whose immediate and professional response to the April 17,
2025 campus shooting at Florida State University prevented further loss of life and provided critical aid
to the campus community.
Background Information:
On April 17, 2025, between 11:56 and 11:57 a.m., the first shot was fired by Phoenix Ikner at the FSU
Student Union. Within one minute, multiple 911 calls were made reporting an active shooter. By 12:00
p.m., officers engaged the suspect, who was taken into custody. The rapid, coordinated actions of the
Florida State University Police Department (FSUPD), Tallahassee Police Department (TPD), Leon
County Sheriff’s Office (LCSO), Tallahassee Fire Department (TFD), Leon County Emergency Medical
Services (LCEMS), Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE), Florida Highway Patrol (FHP), and
other supporting agencies ensured the safety of the campus and limited further harm.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this resolution will award the FSU Student Senate Award for Excellence to the identified first
responder agencies in recognition of their valor, professionalism, and distinguished service to the FSU
community. It also extends a formal invitation to representatives from each agency to be honored at the
Fall 2025 SGA Inauguration Ceremony.

Short Title: A Resolution awarding the FSU Student Senate Award for Excellence to Florida State
University staff, faculty, and administration for their leadership, compassion, and decisive actions during
and after the April 17, 2025, tragedy.
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution awards the FSU Student Senate Award for Excellence to various members of Florida
State University’s staff, faculty, and administration in recognition of their distinguished service during
and following the April 17, 2025, active shooter incident. The resolution commends their critical
leadership, student support efforts, and contributions to community healing. It further directs that
representatives from each honored department be formally invited to receive this award during the Fall
2025 Student Government Association Inauguration Ceremony.
Background Information:
In the immediate aftermath of the April 17 tragedy:
• President Richard McCullough provided ongoing communications and compassionate
leadership to the university community.
• Dr. Amy Hecht and the Division of Student Affairs coordinated a university-wide response and
hosted a support center for students at the Askew Student Life Center.
• Michael Alford, Athletic Director, collaborated with Legends Hospitality to repurpose food and
keep Dick Howser Stadium open to support students.
• The Department of Student Support and Transitions, led by Shelly Ducatt, opened a Family
Assistance Center offering victim services and crisis support.
• Counseling and Psychological Services, under Carlos Gomez, and the Victim Advocate
Program, led by Sarah Lull Castillo, mobilized immediate and sustained mental health support.
• The Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offered free counseling for university employees.
• The Institute for Family Violence Studies, under Dr. Karen Oehme, held a TEDxFSU event on
resilience and distributed trauma recovery tools to students.
• Countless faculty, instructors, and classroom staff helped secure spaces and calmly evacuated
students during the incident.
• Campus staff, including custodial, facilities, and support personnel, were critical in safety
management, emotional support, and post-event recovery.
• Provost Jim Clark, Senior VP Kyle Clark, and the Faculty Senate helped implement flexible
academic and operational policies to ease the transition back to campus.Docusign Envelope ID: 9ABCF4D2-4690-4C98-9324-2CB62081216B

Short Title: Approval of Legacy Hall Pedestrian Safety Project
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution would recognize the improvement of pedestrian safety measures surrounding
Legacy Hall as a priority of the Student Senate. Thus, creating a Legacy Hall Pedestrian
Safety (LHPS) liaison entrusted to facilitate meaningful legislation surrounding the effort of
implementing improvements for pedestrian safety for the new College of Business, Legacy
Hall, as well as its neighboring properties (i.e., The Donald L. Tucker Civic Center, St.
Augustine Parking Garage, and other future developments).
Background Information:
Following a meeting with the Dean of the College of Business, Dean Hartline, the plans for the
opening of the new College of Business—Legacy Hall—will be an immediate transfer of all
college of business students. A mass migration of over 8,000 students is currently underway,
and with the 3,600 incoming admits into the College of Business for the 2025-2026 school
year, the opening of Legacy Hall is on track to open in Spring 2026. Legacy Hall’s opening is
expected to cause an increase of pedestrian traffic along roads: St Augustine St, W Madison
St, W. Pensacola St, and other neighboring streets. Paired with the fact that the 160 added
parking spots being built with Legacy Hall will be designated for faculty and staff only. Leaving
many students to find different modes of transportation to the new building. Prior requests
were made with the city of Tallahassee but have delayed certain requests to implement
pedestrian safety measures surrounding Legacy Hall; therefore, to guarantee the safety and
implementation of these solutions, the LPHS liaison will take on the proceedings of this effort
to ensure proper safety measures are enforced out of an act of precaution and with advanced
foresight.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The 77th Student Senate formally recognizes the improvement of pedestrian safety measures
surrounding Legacy Hall as a legislative priority. The Student Senate President shall appoint a
Florida State University Senator to act as the Legacy Hall Pedestrian Safety (LHPS) liaison
responsible for collaboration with Florida State University Parking and Transportation Services
for any initiatives that may further this project, via proper approval.Docusign Envelope ID: D622C7A6-0B4D-459A-BB8D-59659AB62F31

Short Title: Resolution requesting a transfer from Senate Projects to the Election Office
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution requests funds from Senate Projects for the Election Office. This allocation
would ensure that student elections attain hybrid status, installing 2 kiosks and 2 tablets at the
Student Union for the purpose of promoting voter turnout through alternate options.
Background Information:
The Election Office is tasked with the goal of promoting voter turnout. While the usage of fully
electronic elections has widened our reach to the student body, our elections lack a physical
space for candidates to direct voters towards. The addition of an established space at one of
the most populous student locations could provide for voters in ways that fully virtual voting
may lack. The funds will be used to address the possible gaps within our fully electronic voting
system and thus increase voter turnout.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
This legislation would fund alternate physical voting options to promote voter turnout.

Senate Bill/Resolution #: Bill #77-034 and Resolution #77-060
Primary Sponsor(s): Goldstein, Rios
Co-sponsor(s): Add any Co-Sponsors here
Short Title: Establishment of New Student Organization Funding Programs and Operating
Policies & Procedures
Summary of Legislation:
Bill #77-034 creates two new student organization funding programs in the Student Body
Statutes: the RSO Allocation Committee and the RSO Development Fund. It also repeals
outdated provisions and refines the Statutes to streamline the allocation of A&S fees. The
accompanying Resolution #77-060 formally adopts operational policies and procedures for the
RSO Allocation Committee, including funding guidelines, meeting structure, and evaluation
criteria.
Background Information:
In recent years, SGA and the Department of Student Engagement have received feedback
from Recognized Student Organizations (RSOs) on campus indicating that RSOs have faced
obstacles in accessing student government funding due to duplicative, outdated, and overly
complex policies.
The Student Senate has recognized the need to restructure and simplify the process to
promote accessibility, equity, and efficiency; the FY 2025-26 SGA budget adopted by the
Student Senate contemplates eliminating the Programming Allocation Committee (PAC), the
Resource for Travel Allocation Committee (RTAC), the Organizational Fund, and the RSO
Budget Fund and replacing those funding programs with a more consolidated, streamlined
funding process that will reduce confusion and provide a “one-stop shop” for RSOs to seek
funding from SGA.
This legislation is the product of collaboration between the Student Senate, the SGA Executive
Branch, the Department of Student Engagement, and campus partners and reflects best
practices for financial governance and student engagement.

Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation will:
• Establish the RSO Allocation Committee (RSOAC) to centralize and standardize
supplemental funding for undergraduate RSOs;
• Establish elections for members of the RSO Allocation Committee to increase
transparency, democratic participation, and student voice in the allocation of A&S fees;
• Create the RSO Development Fund, providing small grants to support new and
developing RSOs;
• Repeal outdated chapters (e.g., Chapters 807 and 815) and replace them with a more
robust and efficient framework for allocating SGA funding to RSOs;
• Clarify funding eligibility, limitations, and approval processes;
• Adopt a transparent and merit-based rubric to guide allocation decisions;
• Improve communication of funding opportunities through required social media
outreach; and
• Enhance transparency in SGA’s funding allocation process and ensure that these
programs are evaluated regularly to identify recommendations for further program
enhancement in the future.
Ultimately, this legislation will enhance accountability, transparency, and equitable access to
funding for student organizations.

schedule. The committee must meet on Thursdays.30

Statutes “7he S*A Sunshine Act”34

coPPittee’s funding recoPPendations41

date certain.44
g. The Chair shall endeavor to schedule meetings and such that no more than eight (8) funding45
requests are heard per week. The Chair may, however, at their discretion, schedule46
additional requests as needed.47
h. The order in which requests are heard shall be based primarily on the chronological order in48
which funding requests are received. The Chair may adjust the order to prioritize requests49

77th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Resolution #: 063
Primary Sponsor(s): Cordero
Co-sponsor(s): Bischof, Goldstein, Rios
Short Title: Approval of Wellness Within Reach Initiative
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution would recognize the increased accessibility to healthcare resources in and
around campus, especially residence halls, as a priority of the Student Senate. Thus, the
Wellness Within Reach (WWR) liaison shall be established to advance legislation that
improves access to healthcare resources, beginning with a pilot initiative in the Health and
Wellness Center and ultimately expanding to all 18 residence halls.
Background Information:
Florida State University serves over 44,000 students and of those, more than 6,700 live on
campus across the 18 residence halls. With an emphasis on student well-being, the Division of
Student Affairs created the “Live Well” initiative highlighting 9 dimensions of wellness, physical
being one of them. However, the main medical resource on campus, the Health and Wellness
Center, doesn’t have an on-site readily accessible full-service pharmacy and only operates
from 8AM - 4PM Monday through Friday. This in conjunction with University Housing’s policy
that prohibits residential assistants from providing any over the counter (OTC) medications
leave students and especially on campus residents with limited access to medical resources.
While there is a CVS Pharmacy nearby, similar to the Health and Wellness Center, it operates
on limited hours, 7AM - 12AM Monday through Sunday. This also doesn’t account for
Northwest on campus residents who don’t have a car and thus can’t easily access the CVS.
Thus, students are effectively left with no safe or reliable options: either relying on a roommate
for medication with no guarantee it is accurate or appropriate, venturing into the unsafe streets
of Tallahassee in search of a 24/7 pharmacy, or enduring their illness through the night and
risking missed classes the following day.
Prior requests with the Office of Business Services to install a vending machine with OTC
medications in the Health and Wellness Center have been delayed. University Health Services
has already set aside the funding necessary to cover the initial pilot machine in the Health and
Wellness Center, demonstrating that resources exist to launch this effort immediately. While
this pilot project is an important first step, allowing the university to test whether the
infrastructure can integrate with FSU’s existing systems, such as the FSU Card, it should beDocusign Envelope ID: 89F2D02A-5298-4AFF-9D10-64054F42BD04

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
viewed as a starting point rather than the final solution. The ultimate goal must be to expand
access by placing wellness vending machines in all residence halls, where the need is most
desperate. Therefore, to guarantee both the accessibility and implementation of these
solutions, the WWR liaison will take responsibility for leading this effort. This role reflects an
act of duty to uphold Florida State University’s mission of advancing student health and
wellness, as articulated in the most recent FSU Student Handbook (2025–2026) and grounded
in the values of respect, responsibility, and student well-being.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The 77th Student Senate will formally recognize the increased accessibility to healthcare
resources in and around campus, with particular emphasis on residence halls, as a legislative
priority. Adoption of this resolution will result in the following:
• The Student Senate President shall appoint a Senator to serve as Wellness Within
Reach (WWR) liaison, tasked with leading the Student Senate’s involvement in
expanding healthcare access on campus.
• The WWR liaison will work with University Health Services (UHS) and the Office of
Business Services (OBS) to advance the launch of the pilot vending machine in the
Health and Wellness Center, ensuring its timely implementation and integration with
FSU’s existing infrastructure (e.g., FSU Card system).
• While supporting the pilot, the WWR liaison will begin laying the groundwork for a larger
rollout of wellness vending machines in all 18 residence halls, with the goal of providing
equitable 24/7 access to essential over-the-counter medications and health products to
all on-campus residents.
• The WWR liaison will work in coordination with the Executive Branch’s Secretary of
Health, Wellness, and Safety, as well as other relevant stakeholders across Student
Government and the Division of Student Affairs, to ensure broad support and alignment.
• The WWR liaison will provide recurring updates to the Student Senate on the status of
both the pilot project and the larger residence hall initiative, ensuring transparency,
oversight, and continued legislative momentum.
• By formally establishing this effort as a legislative priority, the Senate affirms its
commitment to advancing student health and wellness, reducing preventable academic
disruptions caused by lack of medical access, and upholding the mission of Florida
State University to support student success in all aspects of life.

Senate Resolution #: 065
Primary Sponsor(s): Ven
Co-sponsor(s): Goldstein
Short Title: Approval of Electric Micromobility Vehicle Charging Stations and Storage Project
Summary of Legislation:
This resolution would recognize the implementation of electric micromobility vehicle (EMV)
charging stations and storage as an initiative supported by the Student Senate. Thus, creating
an EMV liaison entrusted to facilitate meaningful legislation surrounding the effort of
implementing new charging and storage measures around campus, particularly around
residence halls.
Background Information:
Many students on campus make use of electric micromobility vehicles (EMVs) to traverse
campus, including e-scooters and e-bikes, yet there are no locations on campus to charge and
store these vehicles. There are few outlets outside of residence halls that can be used to
charge their EMVs, but this leaves them open to theft. Additionally, bike racks do not have
covers to protect EMVs from weather that can potentially severely damage their electrical
components. These factors make it a more preferable option for students to bring their EMVs
into their residence halls for charging and storage, which is a fire hazard and violation of
University Housing policy. A specific avenue for how to fix these issues has been looked into
(EnerFusion, see attachments), and Transportation and Parking Services have already been
contacted and have expressed interest on working on this project. Therefore, to guarantee
security for EMVs and increase fire safety, an EMV liaison would take on the actions towards
working with relevant offices for the implementation of charging stations and storage.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
The 77th Student Senate formally displays its support for the implementation of electric
micromobility vehicle (EMV) charging stations and storage. The Student Senate President
shall appoint a Student Senator to act as the EMV liaison responsible for collaborating with
FSU Parking and Transportation Services and any other relevant stakeholders for developing
a plan to further this project.Docusign Envelope ID: 2CD5824F-9B30-4897-A02A-4EA8E7417F12

Recent Statistics from the Center For Campus Fire Safety
Between December 2023 to August 9, 2024, there were 16 fires reported to
the CCFS lithium ion battery data collection program. The CCFS program is
designed to collect data on Li-on incidents on a college campus.
• 93% Occurred inside the building. In only 12% of these incidents the
device was able to be moved outside and extinguished.
• While fire incidents were almost 50/50 between residential (on-campus
housing) and non-residential buildings, 100% of these occurred On Cam-
pus (any type of building or outside)
• Devices causing these incidents:
- Scooter 30%
- e-Bike 20%
- SkateBoard 40%
- Other 10%: iPad, drone, percussion massage gun, video camera,
specialized titanium cased battery pack for undersea deployment
• 56% of the devices were charging.
• 87.5% caused damage ranging from limited property/room damage to
approximately $200,000 in damage to building and contents.
What can I do about battery safety?
From the first sign of a problem, you could have less than a minute to escape a battery fire. With the speed
of these fires, the best way to be safe is to prevent a fire from starting. Prioritizing these safety measures
will help you Take C.H.A.R.G.E. of Battery Safety.
C
Choose certified products
• When purchasing lithium-ion battery-powered devices, be sure to look for products that
are listed or safety certified by a nationally recognized testing laboratory to ensure they
meet important safety requirements.
• Countless products sold online do not meet these critical safety standards.
H
Handle lithium-ion battery-powered devices with care
• Follow the manufacturer’s instructions.
• Only use the charging equipment that comes with the product.
• Store batteries away from extreme temperatures, direct sunlight, exits, and anything
flammable.
• Do not modify the battery or the charger in any way.
• Charge larger devices (such as eBikes) outside the home – and never in your exit path.
• Do not charge larger devices overnight.
A
Always stay alert for warning signs
• Check battery-powered devices often for damage or abuse such as swelling or punctures.
• Listen for unusual hissing or popping sounds.
• Watch out for excessive heat or a strange odor.
• If you notice any of these warning signs, stop using the lithium-ion powered devices.
• White or gray wispy smoke indicates immediate danger of thermal runaway.
R
Recycle devices and batteries properly
• Responsibly dispose of old or damaged batteries and devices by taking them to the
nearest battery recycling center.
• Never discard batteries, chargers, or battery-powered devices in regular trash bins.
G Get out quickly if there’s a fire
• Know the warning signs to look and listen for and get out if you see – or hear – one.
• Follow your home fire escape plan to leave immediately and call 9-1-1.
E Educate others on battery safety
• Now that you know what actions to take, spread the word. Protect your friends and loved
ones by sharing how they can Take C.H.A.R.G.E. of Battery Safety.
Learn more at batteryfiresafety.org.

Short Title: Recognizing September as National Recovery Month
Summary of Legislation:
This proclamation recognizes September as National Recovery Month and expresses the
Student Senate’s support for all who have been impacted by mental health and substance use
disorders.
Background Information:
National Recovery Month was established in 1989 by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health
Services Administration. Its primary aim is to raise awareness and bring attention to the
delicate and important topic of recovery and highlight community resources available for those
affected through education, programming, and outreach.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If passed, this proclamation would reaffirm the Student Senate’s passion and care for all
affected by mental health and substance use disorders. It will also reiterate helpful resources
available to members of the campus community to handle these difficult situations and
experiences.

A PROCLAMATION
Recognizing September as National Recovery Month
1 WHEREAS, National Recovery Month has been observed each September since its creation in 1989
2 by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to celebrate the
3 gains made by individuals in recovery from mental health and substance misuse disorders, and to
4 promote the importance of behavioral health as an essential part of overall wellness; and
5 WHEREAS, Florida State University (FSU) is committed to fostering a campus environment that
6 supports mental health, wellness, and recovery, recognizing that these are critical to academic
7 success, personal growth, and community engagement; and
8 WHEREAS, According to SAMHSA, 48.4 million people aged 12 or older (16.8%) had a substance use
9 disorder (SUD) in the past year, including 27.9 million with an alcohol use disorder (AUD), 28.2
10 million people with a drug use disorder (DUD), and 7.7 million people with both an AUD and a DUD;
11 and
12 WHEREAS, University students are especially at risk, with an estimated 21% of college-aged students
13 meeting the criteria for an SUD in 2021 with less than 5% receiving treatment, according to a
14 finding by the National Survey on Drug Use and Health; and
15 WHEREAS, FSU has numerous resources available to the community relating to mental health and
16 substance misuse recovery and prevention, including but not limited to Counseling and
17 Psychological Services (CAPS), the Center for Health Advocacy & Wellness (CHAW), the LIFT

77th STUDENT SENATE
Legislation Cover Sheet
Resolution #: 69
Primary Sponsor(s): Bischof
Co-sponsor(s):
Short Title: Funding a Food Vending Machine in Strozier Library
Summary of Legislation:
This senate transfer resolution seeks to cover residual costs incurred for the installation of a
vending machine mini mart in Strozier that will stock fresh food. This bill will transfer the sum of
$2,710 to FSU Facilities to install an outlet for the fridge and associated electrical equipment
(Work Order #2621191). $1,376.91 will be transferred to FSU ITS to cover installation and
procurement of a CASS security camera (Work order #26009677). The total dollar amount
requested by this legislation is $4,086.91.
Background Information:
This legislation originates from a Student Senate initiative to address the lack of late-night
dining options at Florida State University. Strozier Library, one of the most heavily used study
spaces on campus, regularly hosts hundreds of students well past midnight. On peak days,
Strozier sees an average of 700 students at 10:00 p.m. and approximately 300 students still
present at midnight, with numbers spiking further during midterms and finals.
Current dining options are limited: Starbucks inside Strozier closes at 5:00 p.m. on Mondays
and Fridays and only serves limited items, while The Den, the last available campus option,
closes at midnight and often faces wait times exceeding one hour. This has left students
without reliable access to healthy food during critical study hours.
In response, the sponsoring senator convened discussions with FSU Libraries, Seminole
Dining (Aramark), and the Office of Business Services (OBS). These stakeholders agreed to
support a pilot vending mini mart in Strozier Library that will stock fresh, healthy food produced
daily in campus kitchens. OBS has agreed to cover the cost of the cooler and branding,
Seminole Dining will manage inventory and food safety, and FSU Libraries will host and
advertise the machine.
The Senate’s role is limited to covering essential infrastructure and security costs. FSU
Facilities has quoted $2,710 (Work Order #2621191) to install an electrical outlet and relatedDocusign Envelope ID: 3F50B010-B2A3-4A96-86C7-6867453B5BEE

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
equipment, while FSU ITS has quoted $1,376.91 (Work Order #26009677) for procurement
and installation of a CASS security camera to monitor the machine. The total one-time amount
requested is $4,086.91.
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If approved, this legislation will fund the necessary infrastructure and security to complete
installation of the Strozier vending mini mart. By bridging these final gaps, the Student Senate
enables the six-month pilot program already endorsed by FSU Libraries leadership to move
forward. At the end of the 6-month period, a decision will be made to invest more into the
program by expanding the footprint of the mini mart or instead to leave the program as-is.
The impact of this legislation will be significant for students. It will:
• Provide consistent access to fresh, healthy food during late-night study hours.
• Reduce strain on existing dining venues with limited hours or long wait times.
• Strengthen student well-being during high-stress periods such as midterms and finals.
• Prevent students from having to leave the campus for late-night meals.
In addition, the project will enhance the legitimacy of the Student Government Association. The
vending machine will be co-branded with Seminole Dining and FSU SGA, with clear “Paid for
by SGA” signage displayed on the unit. This visibility directly associates SGA with a tangible
service that benefits the entire student body, reinforcing its role as a responsive and effective
advocate for student needs.
By funding these one-time costs, the Senate ensures that long-term maintenance, food safety,
and operational responsibilities remain with university stakeholders, making this a sustainable
investment with high student impact and minimal recurring expense.

Legislation Cover Sheet
Senate Resolution #: 79
Primary Sponsor(s): Moreno
Co-sponsor(s): Manuel, Stanton, Jackson
Short Title: Funding for MCAT Test-Taking Strategies Workshop Series
Summary of Legislation:
This bill allocates $5,000 from Senate Projects to fund the MCAT Test-Taking Strategies
Workshop Series, coordinated by the Interdisciplinary Medical Sciences (IMS) Division and the
Office of Pre-Health Advising. The series will include four expert-led workshops designed to
improve students' mastery of test-taking strategies essential for MCAT success. The initiative
seeks to enhance academic preparedness, accessibility, and competitiveness among FSU's
pre-health students.
Background Information:
Many pre-health students at FSU face significant financial and accessibility barriers when
preparing for the MCAT, as commercial test preparation courses can cost hundreds to
thousands of dollars. While FSU offers strong premedical coursework, success on the MCAT
requires not only content knowledge but also mastery of the test's unique strategic and
analytical components. These skills are often taught only in costly external programs.
To address this gap, the Interdisciplinary Medical Sciences (IMS) Division and the Office of
Pre-Health Advising have proposed the MCAT Test-Taking Strategies Workshop Series,
designed to teach students effective methods for time management, passage analysis,
question-type recognition, and mental endurance. This program aims to strengthen student
confidence, reduce test anxiety, and improve performance.
By offering expert-led, accessible workshops on campus, this initiative promotes academic
excellence and supports the university's commitment to preparing competitive, well-rounded
pre-health graduates. Additionally, data from this pilot series will help assess student
engagement and inform potential partnerships with national test preparation organizations
such as Kaplan or Jack Westin for future program expansion.
Docusign Envelope ID: 0B29482E-54E9-4E32-8AAD-2CC854436AFB

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Effect of Proposed Legislation:
If enacted, this legislation will provide $5,000 from Senate Projects to the Office of Pre-Health
Advising to implement the MCAT Test-Taking Strategies Workshop Series during Spring 2026.
The program will consist of four 90–120-minute workshops, evaluation assessments, and data
analysis to measure impact. Funds will cover instructional services, materials, AAMC question
pack access, and evaluation costs. The project will be managed by Dr. Elizabeth Foster,
Associate Dean of Interdisciplinary Medical Sciences, in collaboration with Pre-Health
Advising.
This initiative will expand access to affordable, high-quality MCAT preparation, improve
student readiness for medical school, and strengthen FSU’s standing as an institution that
invests in the success of its pre-health population.

MCAT Test-Taking Strategies Workshop Series Overview:
The Interdisciplinary Medical Sciences Division and Prehealth Advising Office would like to
offer a workshop series to help students master the strategic aspects of the MCAT, focusing on
how to approach the test efficiently and effectively rather than teaching subject matter content.
Rationale
The MCAT Test-Taking Strategies Workshop Series is a strategic initiative designed to enhance
the academic preparedness and performance of FSU students pursuing careers in medicine.
While FSU offers robust premedical coursework, success on the MCAT requires not only
content knowledge but also mastery of test-taking strategies specific to the exam’s unique
structure and demands.
This workshop series addresses a critical gap by focusing on the cognitive and strategic skills
necessary for MCAT success, including time management, passage analysis, question-type
recognition, and mental endurance. By equipping students with these tools, the program aims to:
• Improve MCAT performance, particularly in challenging sections like CARS, which
are less content-driven and more strategy-dependent.
• Increase competitiveness of FSU applicants to medical schools, thereby enhancing the
university’s reputation for producing well-prepared pre-health graduates.
• Support equity and access by providing structured, expert-led preparation to students
who may not have the resources for private test prep services.
• Strengthen student confidence and reduce test anxiety, contributing to overall
academic success and retention in pre-health pathways.
By investing in this targeted, high-impact intervention, FSU demonstrates its commitment to
student success, academic excellence, and the advancement of future healthcare professionals.
To implement this initiative effectively, we will need to hire a qualified MCAT test-taking
strategies instructor to develop and deliver the workshop series.
Key Responsibilities
The key responsibilities of the instructor are:
• Teach students how to manage time across sections and within individual
passages/questions.
• Demonstrate techniques for identifying question types and applying appropriate
strategies.
• Coach students on how to approach dense or unfamiliar passages, especially in CARS.
• Provide methods for educated guessing and eliminating incorrect answer choices.
Docusign Envelope ID: 0B29482E-54E9-4E32-8AAD-2CC854436AFB

sections.text:
• Help students develop personalized pacing plans and section-specific strategies.
• Offer guidance on how to interpret AAMC-style questions and avoid common traps.
• Support students in building mental endurance for the 7.5-hour exam.

This resolution proposes the allocation of $8,300 to various Registered Student Organizations
