Statute/Amendment Text:
6. RTAC and PAC Guidelines:
a. Organizations will not be eligible for additional funding from PAC or RTAC within the
same fiscal year if they have received allocations from an Activity and Service Funding
Board, Committee, or specific budget line item. However, organizations are exempt from
this restriction if they receive funding from PAC, RTAC, Senate Projects, or the
organizational fund.
b. Fund Distribution Committees shall not meet during any summer semesters.
(1) RSOs requesting funds to be used in May or June may request three weeks
before the end of the Spring semester. Requests can be accepted later at the
Char's discretion.
(2) RSOs requesting funds to be used after July 1 shall go directly to the Student
Senate to ask for money out of Senate Projects. At the conclusion of the summer
semester, the funds distributed to the RSOs out of Senate Projects shall be
reimbursed from the respective fund distribution committee via a transfer bill.
c. All organizations requesting funding must be financially certified prior to making a
request. At least one financially certified officer must be present at the funding hearing.
d. Committees shall make a good faith effort to meet on Monday or Tuesday of each week,
pending requests from RSOs.
(1) The Chair shall send out a notice of meeting time and location to RSOs via email.
The notification must be sent out by the chair at least twenty-four (24) hours prior
to the meeting time. Notification can be sent out later with a written request from
the RSO if the meeting has been advertised in accordance with Sunshine Law.
e. All submissions must be made prior to 12:00 p.m. on the Friday before the hearing.
Submissions should include three (3) supporting/competitive quotes for each category the
RSO is requesting funds. If less than three quotes were submitted with the application,
the Chair can accept these quotes at the meeting. If an RSO fails to provide these three
quotes, they must submit another application. Requests in the category of contractual
services may be exempted from this rule.
(1) All requests must be submitted at least twenty-one (21) school days prior to event
or activity to receive funding from PAC and at least thirty (30) school days prior to
travel date to receive funding from RTAC. Any request submitted after the
aforementioned dates may still be considered for funding at the discretion of the
chair with the approval of the SGA Business Manager.
(2) All requests must be of a line-item nature with quotes (clothing costs, performer
costs, reservation costs, equipment rental, facility rental, airline ticket quotes,
rental car quotes, hotel quotes, etc.), and an explanation of need and of benefits
to the student body.
(3) Any amount requested by a single organization over $2,000 requires a two-thirds
(2/3) vote of the Fund Distribution Committee, a two-thirds (2/3) vote the Senate
Finance Committee, and a two-thirds vote of the Student Senate.
(4) RSOs can only request for funds that will be used within ninety (90) business
days. A two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Committee can override this rule.
(5) Any PAC or RTAC line item that was previously tabled by the Student Senate
shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student SenateDocusign Envelope ID: AEA5AB15-9C6D-49B1-953B-0C7A8CDCCA96

a ($25.00) dollar fee shall be levied against an

sections.text:
I. General
A. No A&S funded account may pay any stipend, wage, salary, or salary increase
to any positions not funded in the FY 2024-2025 without express consent of the
Student Senate in the form of a bill or resolution.
B. In the event of shortfalls or excesses of entities funded in this budget, the Vice
President of Student Affairs, the SGA Advisor, the Senate President, and the
Student Body President shall meet to review options. No decisions shall be
made without a majority vote of the Student Senate.
C. The FY 2024-2025 Budget was created under the current $12.86 per credit
hour A&S Fee. Should the Local Fee Committee propose a per credit hour
increase that is accepted by the Board of Trustees, the Budget Committee
should reconvene to allocate the additional projected funds prior to the
beginning of the fiscal year.
D. The FY 2024-2025 Budget was created under the terms of the Agreement
between the Division of Student Affairs and the Office of the Student Body
President, as approved by the 76th Student Senate in Resolution (#?). The
Budget Committee, and the Student Senate as a whole, intend to fully comply
with the Agreement and are of the opinion that any proviso language regarding
the covered entities help ensure quality of service and compliance with various
state and university policies, rather than non-compliance with the Agreement.
E. SGA Budgeted Offices, Agencies, Bureaus, Affiliated Projects, Organizations,
and Departments are encouraged to utilize the Sweepings Process for one-time
purchases.
F. Monies allocated in the Food category shall be held in compliance with Student
Body Statute 803.7(A) which states “No SGA branch, office, agency, bureau, or
affiliated project shall be allocated more than fifteen percent (15%) of its annual
budget in the Food category.”
G. Any and all budgeted organizations found in violation of Student Body Statutes
shall be subject to the appropriate sanctions contained in the Finance Code and
recommended by the Finance Committee, the Budget Committee, and the
Student Senate.
II. Campus Recreation
A. It is the position of the 76th Student Senate that the Bobby E. Leach Student
Recreation Center, the Fitness and Movement Clinic, the Intramural fields, the
Rez Lakefront Park and Retreat Center, and the Rec SportsPlex have been
primarily funded by student dollars and that these facilities' primary purpose is
for student recreational purposes.
B. Monies were allocated as a lump sum in the expense category with the
recommendation that the Campus Recreation Board determine its designation.
III. Union
A. It is the position of the 76th Student Senate that the Union Department,
including various buildings and programs across campus, has been funded by
student dollars and that these facilities' primary purpose is for supporting the
student experience.
B. Any event or entertainment provided by the Union shall be free and open to all
students with valid identification. Non-FSU students shall be subject to
admission fees.
C. Revenue placed in the Headliner Account shall be used for the express
purpose of bringing major concert acts for the entertainment of the Student
Body. This account shall be administered by the Union with input from the
Headliners Committee, appointed by the Student Body President. An admissionDocuSign Envelope ID: 096129F4-D1E5-47A7-933F-72407045A6D7

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
price may be charged to students in conjunction with the monies used from this
account. The Headliner Account shall not be swept at the end of the fiscal year.
D. It is the opinion of the 76th Student Senate that the Headliners account should
support the FSU Homecoming expenses of Homecoming Live.
E. Monies were allocated as a lump sum in the expense category with the
recommendation that the Union Board determine its designation.
IV. SGA Offices
A. Executive Branch
1. The Executive Branch account shall fund the Spring Inauguration
Ceremony.
2. No more than $300 allocated in the Clothing & Awards category may be
spent on awards.
B. Senate Branch
1. The Senate Branch account shall fund the Fall Inauguration Ceremony.
C. Supreme Court
1. Funds in Expense shall be used, in part, to fund the printing of
Supreme Court Reporters.
D. Elections Office
1. Funds allocated in Expense shall not be used for nametags.
E. Homecoming
1. Notwithstanding the Proviso of Bill 2023, an amount of $89,000 of the
funds remaining in the Homecoming account from FY 2023-2024 shall
be carried forward and Homecoming shall have the authority to expend
it, in addition to funds allocated in this bill. The remaining unspent
funds from FY 2023-2024 shall be remanded to the Headliner Account.
2. Monies allocated to Homecoming shall be in compliance with Student
Body Statute 615.5 (A)(3) that states: “HEC Shall: Submit the annual
Homecoming Budget for the entire student body to the Senate Budget
Committee”.
3. Monies allocated to Homecoming and expended shall contain the
language “Paid for by SGA” on all necessary expenditures as defined
in Student Body Statutes Chapter 800 of the Finance Code.
4. Homecoming shall not endorse, affiliate with, or publicize any activities
associated with the Burning Spear organization. This decision is based
on the Senate’s opinion as expressed in Resolution 9 of the 73rd
Student Senate.
5. Any A&S monies not spent on Homecoming shall be remanded to the
Headliners Artist Series.
6. The 76th Student Senate requires that Homecoming abides by Student
Body Statute Chapter 616 and includes the Student Body President,
the Student Body Vice President, Student Senate President, Student
Senate Pro Tempore, Homecoming Director, Homecoming Live
Director, and Inter Residence Hall Council Director or their designees,
on the Homecoming Planning Commission
F. Golden Torch Lecture Series
1. No Funds shall be used for billboards or awards. Golden Torch is
encouraged to work with local governmental partners about the
feasibility of joint marketing.
2. Golden Torch is authorized to use funds from previous fiscal years that
have not been swept, pursuant to SBS §612.4(j). Golden Torch isDocuSign Envelope ID: 096129F4-D1E5-47A7-933F-72407045A6D7

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
encouraged to use the funds sparingly, as to allow the use in the
coming years.
G. Class Councils
1. The Budget Committee notes disapprovingly that the Class Councils
admitted to violating the ban on the purchase of nametags, as laid out
in the proviso of Bill 2023. The Committee readopts the position that
the Class Councils are prohibited from using A&S Fees for the
purchase of polos or nametags.
2. The Senior Class Council Treasurer shall prepare and present a report
containing all expenditures for the preceding fiscal year quarter to the
Student Body Treasurer, Senate Budget Committee Chair, and Senate
Finance Committee Chair. The report shall be delivered within fourteen
(14) calendar days of the end of each quarter. Failure to report or
failure to abide by proviso language will subject the Class Council to
the possibility of penalty, under SBS §805.2(c).
H. Agencies
1. Black Student Union
a. BSU shall attempt to work with FAMU SGA in furtherance of
sharing the costs of Bridge the Gap as to create a better event.
b. No funds shall be expended for travel. This proviso may be
waived by resolution passed by three-fourths (3/4) of the Student
Senate.
2. Pride Student Union
a. The Pride Student Union is only authorized to expend up to
$11,000 of the monies allocated in this Bill in Expense for travel
purposes.
3. Veterans Student Union
a. Expense funds in this Budget shall not be used for travel
purposes.
b. VSU is encouraged to work with the College of Music to recruit
students to help with programming for Battle of the Bands.
4. Women Student Union
a. WSU is encouraged to work with OWL orgs on applying for
funding through PAC, RTAC, and the Organizational Fund.
V. Bureaus
A. OGA
1. Funds in this Budget shall not be used to pay for student travel or any
event in the DC area.
2. OGA shall fund, in part alongside Executive Projects and any other
contributing entity, any events for the Florida Student Association's
2025 Rally in Tally.
B. MHC
1. Expense Funds shall not be used to pay for a technology subscription.
C. SCURC
1. SCURC Travel and Conference grants shall not exceed $500 per
student. SCURC shall publish the criteria for reviewing grants on the
SGA website.
VI. Affiliated Projects
A. MRU
1. No A&S Funds shall be used for separate polo shirts for the MRU
Executive Board, as per SBS §803.8(a)(1).DocuSign Envelope ID: 096129F4-D1E5-47A7-933F-72407045A6D7

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
B. WVFS
1. Funds not allocated by WVFS shall not be swept at the end of the
2024-2025 fiscal year. The Student Senate is encouraged to enact
legislation making this exemption permanent.
VII. Funding Boards
A. RTAC
1. For the FY 2024-25 RTAC shall not expend more than $500 per
student for each request that it funds and no more than $15,000 in
total for an RSO within the FY. This provision may be waived by a
unanimous vote of the Student Senate Finance Committee.
B. Sports Club Council
1. The Budget Committee expresses its appreciation for the Sports Club
Council for complying with the reporting requirements of Student Body
Statutes and asks that this compliance be maintained in future fiscal
years.
VIII. OPS Wages
A. Exec
1. The President of the Student Executive Branch shall be paid at
minimum wage for sixteen (16) hours per calendar week in which they
perform the duties and responsibilities of their position. Forty- four (44)
calendar weeks of pay have been made available at this rate; these
weeks of pay shall coincide with the FSU Fall, Spring, and Summer
Academic Calendars.
2. The Vice-President of the Student Executive Branch shall be paid at
minimum wage for fourteen (14) hours per calendar week in which
they perform the duties and responsibilities of their position. Forty- four
(44) calendar weeks of pay have been made available at this rate;
these weeks of pay shall coincide with the FSU Fall, Spring, and
Summer Academic Calendars.
3. The Treasurer of the Student Executive Branch shall be paid at
minimum wage for ten (10) hours per calendar week in which they
perform the duties and responsibilities of their position. Forty- four (44)
calendar weeks of pay have been made available at this rate; these
weeks of pay shall coincide with the FSU Fall, Spring, and Summer
Academic Calendars.
4. The Chief of Staff shall receive minimum wage for ten (10) hours per
calendar week, in which they perform the duties and responsibilities of
their position, for a period of fourty-four (44) weeks, which shall
coincide with the FSU Fall, Spring, and Summer Academic Calendars.
B. Student Senate
1. The President of the Student Senate shall receive minimum wage for
ten (10) hours per fourteen (14) semester weeks in which they perform
the duties and responsibilities of their position. For the Summer
Semester, the President of the Student Senate shall receive minimum
wage for five (5) hours per ten (10) term weeks in which they perform
the duties and responsibilities of their position. Thirty-eight (38)
calendar weeks of pay have been made available at these rates; these
weeks of pay shall coincide with the FSU Fall, Spring, and Summer
Academic Calendars.
2. The Pro Tempore of the Student Senate shall receive minimum wage
for seven (7) hours per fourteen (14) semester weeks in which theyDocuSign Envelope ID: 096129F4-D1E5-47A7-933F-72407045A6D7

sections.heading: Page 7
sections.text:
perform the duties and responsibilities of their position. For the
Summer Semester, the Pro Tempore of the Student Senate shall
receive minimum wage for three (3) hours per ten (10) term weeks in
which they perform the duties and responsibilities of their position.
Thirty-eight (38) calendar weeks of pay have been made available at
these rates; these weeks of pay shall coincide with the FSU Fall,
Spring, and Summer Academic Calendars.
C. The Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court shall receive minimum wage
for five (5) hours per calendar week in which they perform the duties and
responsibilities of their position. Thirty-two (32) calendar weeks of pay have

Calendars. No other OPS positions shall be funded in SGA Agencies, except as

responsibilities of their position, for a period of thirty (30) weeks, which shall
coincide with the FSU Spring and Fall Academic Calendar.

Homecoming Live Director shall receive minimum wage for seven (7) hours per
week for twenty three calendar (23) weeks, starting at the beginning of the
fiscal year.

External Executive Branch Document
Decision to Veto Constitutional Amendment 1
October 3rd, 2024 — By the authority vested in me as Student Body President of the Florida
State University, under the provisions of Article III, Section 3, of the Constitution of the Student
Body, I hereby veto and transmit my objections to Senate Constitutional Amendment 1, passed
during the 76th Session of the Student Senate of the Florida State University Student
Government Association, in the year 2024:
Revision to the Student Body Constitution Article II, §§ 1, 2, 34, 45, 56, and 6; Article V, § 4;
“A Constitutional Amendment Enacting the Recommendations of the Stronger Future Working
Group in Regard to the SGA-COGS Relationship”
As Student Body President, my duty is to ensure that all legislation passed serves the best
interests of the entire student body and aligns with our core principles of representation and
equity. While I commend the intent behind the Stronger Future Amendment—to bring graduate
students closer into the legislative process—I must exercise my veto authority over the Proposed
Constitutional Amendment #1.
It is critical to consider not just the immediate goals, but also the long-term impact of
restructuring the foundation of our student government. The proposed legislation introduces a
bicameral system requiring approval from the Congress of Graduate Students (COGS) for
changes to our Student Body Statutes. This amendment, if enacted, would grant the graduate
student body disproportionate legislative power creating the potential for unequal representation.
The inclusion of graduate students in critical conversations is essential and I fully support efforts
to improve that inclusion. However, this amendment has the potential to substantially delay and
destabilize several facets of our legislative process rather than enhance them.
Florida State University’s Student Government Association 2024

return Constitutional Amendment #1 to the 76th Student Senate without my approval.

Purpose & Description: A Constitutional Amendment Enacting the Recommendations of the
Stronger Future Working Group in Regard to the SGA-COGS Relationship (Attachment #1)
Statement of Intent: The Stronger Future Amendment will further enshrine the role of graduate
students in Student Government by providing the Congress of Graduate Students (COGS) with
the powers to, alongside the Student Senate, jointly amend Statutes, confirm certain nominees
for Student Body office, propose constitutional amendments, and pass resolutions establishing
Joint Rules of Procedure as well as stating the opinion of the Student Body. The Amendment
further makes the Student Senate an undergraduate-only legislative body and makes the
Congress of Graduate Students the sole legislative body representing graduate students. The
Amendment makes further conforming changes.

Body and shall be subject to this Constitution, the Student Body Statutes,
and to all University Rules and Regulations.
Section 3 MISSION STATEMENT
The mission of the Student Government Association (SGA), is to provide
FSU students with representation, services and advocacy within the
university structure. The Student Government Association provides
quality leadership for, and accountability to its constituency by recognizing
that strength arises from diversity, engagement, and dialogue.
Section 4 FRANCHISE
All students shall be entitled to vote in the Student Body elections.

governance of and policy development for the Florida State

ARTICLE II -THE LEGISLATURE
Section 1 LEGISLATIVE POWERS VESTING
The Legislature Legislative Powers of the Student Body shall be vested in
the Florida State University Student Legislature, hereinafter referred to as
the Legislature. The Legislature shall consist of the Undergraduate
Student Senate, hereinafter referred to as the Senate, and the Congress of
Graduate Students, hereinafter referred to as COGS.
Section 2 COMPOSITION OF THE SENATE
A. There shall be an elected group of undergraduate student
representatives known as Senators, who shall be elected as
prescribed in Statutes.
B. From this body, the Senate shall select a Senate President and
President Pro Tempore in the Fall Semester, and they shall be
elected for a one (1) year term during which their seats shall not
come up for election, even if they were initially elected in the Spring.
C. Selection of other officers shall be by statute.
D. The exact number of Senate seats shall be determined by statute,
but at no time shall this number exceed eighty (80).
Section 3 COMPOSITION OF THE CONGRESS OF GRADUATE STUDENTS
A. There shall be an elected group of certain graduate, special,
master, specialist, professional, doctoral and post-baccalaureate
students representatives known as Representatives, who shall be
elected from the individual colleges of the University, as well as at-
large seats, as determined by COGS Code.
B. From this body, the COGS shall elect a Speaker in the Fall
Semester, and they shall be elected for a one (1) year term.
C. Selection of other officers shall be by COGS Code and the COGS
Internal Rules of Procedure.
D. The exact number of COGS seats shall be determined by statute.
E. All elections for COGS Representatives shall be non-partisan.

ARTICLE VII RECALL OF STUDENT BODY OFFICIALS
Section 1 METHOD OF RECALL
History: Revised by Amendment 1, Spring 2020 election.
Every elected official of the Florida State University Student Body is
subject, as herein provided, to recall by the legal voters of the Florida
State University Student Body. The person or persons demanding recall
shall set forth in a petition the reasons for the demand of recall. If the
elected official in question offers their resignation it shall be accepted and
take effect on the day it is offered, and the vacancy shall be filled as
provided by law. If they do not resign within thirty days an election will be
held to determine whether the people will recall the officer. On the
sample ballot at the election shall be printed in not more than two hundred
(200) words the reasons for demanding recall and in not more than two
hundred (200) words the officers justification of their course in office. they
shall continue to perform the duties of their office until the results of their
official election shall be officially declared. The recall petition shall be
filed with the officer with whom the petition for nomination to such office
should be filed, and the same officer shall order the special election when
it is required. No such petition shall be circulated against any officer until
they have actually held office for three months. After one such petition
and special election, no further recall shall be filed against the same
officer during the term for which they were elected.

Whereas: Florida State University’s College of Law Building, B.K. Roberts Hall, is named after
Bonnie Kaslow Roberts, prominent segregationist and racist, and
Whereas: Whereas B.K. Roberts drafted the 1957 Florida Supreme Court Opinion to deny law
school admission to African American student Virgil Hawkins in defiance of federal integration
orders, and
Whereas: Calls to rename B.K. Roberts Hall led to the 2019, 34-1, passage of Senate Bill 7076,
providing Florida State University with the option of removing B.K. Roberts’s name from its law
school building, although the initiative failed in the House, and
Whereas: In 2020, the Board of Trustees unanimously voted on a resolution to rename B.K.
Roberts Hall to “reflect FSU’s core values of justice, equality, compassion, and respect,” and
Whereas: Former President Thrasher noted that “to keep the name of B.K. Roberts on the law
school building would continue to honor someone whose decisions and actions do not reflect
Florida State University’s values or rule of law,” and
Whereas: Florida State University’s Integration Statue on Legacy Walk is a monument to the
legacy to the many “firsts” of African American Students at the university, including Maxwell
Courtney, our first African American graduate, Fred Flowers, our first African American athlete,
and Doby Flowers, our First African American Homecoming Princess, and the many students
who paved the way towards integration which B.K. Roberts vehemently opposed, and
Whereas: Florida State University President Richard McCullough has stated his commitment to
“Creating a learning and working environment where everyone can have a sense of belonging,”
and
Whereas: The existing name of B.K. Roberts Hall serves as both a physical and symbolic
testament to the legacy of segregation, racism, and violence against the African American
community and a visceral reminder of prejudice on campus.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-Sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: We
call on Florida State University to rename B.K. Roberts Hall and to condemn hatred, prejudice,
and racism, both past and present.DocuSign Envelope ID: 4631F153-436E-4BF8-A97A-9B01AB2647E3

Whereas: Human trafficking stands as a serious violation of human rights, impacting millions of
individuals across the globe, involving exploiting people through force, fraud, or coercion, for
purposes such as forced labor and commercial sexual exploitation; and
Whereas: The month of January is designated as Human Trafficking Awareness Month,
offering a chance to shed light on this reprehensible crime, educate communities, and promote
initiatives to combat and prevent human trafficking; and
Whereas: Emphasizing the importance of nurturing a well-informed and vigilant society that can
identify and combat human trafficking, ensuring the protection and support of victims, and
holding perpetrators accountable for their actions; and
Whereas: Florida State University, being an institution of higher learning, is dedicated to
fostering awareness, education, and engagement on critical issues concerning human rights
and social justice; and
Whereas: The month of January is officially recognized as Human Trafficking awareness
month on the campus of Florida State University; and
Whereas: The Student Senate encourages the university community to actively participate in
events, initiatives, and educational programs aimed at raising awareness about human
trafficking and its prevention. Students at Florida State University are encouraged to educate
themselves on Human Trafficking awareness through FSU programs, such as the End-It
Movement and Center for the Advancement of human Rights and are encouraged to attend
educational events put on by the university in the coming months.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-Sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Student Senate reaffirms its commitment to supporting efforts to combat human trafficking,
protect victims, and cultivate a campus culture that values human rights and social justice.

Whereas: the federal Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (P.L. 117-58; the “IIJA”) was a
five-year, $1.2 trillion comprehensive infrastructure package enacted by the U.S. Congress and
signed into law by President Biden in 2021, and
Whereas: the IIJA authorized funding for a variety of surface transportation programs as well as
new investments in the nation’s infrastructure and economy, including the National Electric
Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) program consisting of a $5 billion formula-based grant program as
well as a $2.5 billion discretionary grant program for Electric Vehicle (EV) infrastructure funding,
and
Whereas: the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) is the state-level entity responsible
for implementing Florida’s formula-based funds from the NEVI program, which are crucial for
deploying EV charging stations, and
Whereas: Florida State University (FSU), with its existing commitment to sustainable
transportation exemplified by its all-electric bus fleet, is in a prime position to expand its EV
charging infrastructure to better serve its community, and
Whereas: FSU has a dynamic Campus Master Plan that encompasses the development of its
physical infrastructure, focusing on enhancing transportation and sustainability, and Jack
Hitchcock, as the Student Body President and the sole student representative on the FSU
Board of Trustees, is poised to advocate for the integration of Electric Vehicle (EV) charging
stations into this plan, thus representing student interests and advancing FSU's commitment to
sustainable development, and
Whereas: key considerations under the IIJA for EV charging infrastructure, including public
accessibility and location along designated Alternative Fuel Corridors (AFCs), are directly
relevant to FSU's campus setting and can enhance the convenience and usability for students
and faculty who drive EVs by potentially increasing the number of available charging stations on
campus, and
Whereas: there is an emphasis on prioritizing charging locations along the Interstate Highway
System and in rural, underserved, and disadvantaged communities, which aligns with FSU’s
mission to enhance accessibility and inclusivity within its campus and the broader Tallahassee
community, andDocuSign Envelope ID: 250F2885-C469-4D97-9929-D8C8832A6167

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Whereas: additional considerations for EV charging infrastructure, such as the availability of
publicly accessible restrooms nearby, appropriate lighting, and sheltered seating areas, would
not only benefit EV users but also align with FSU's broader goals for a sustainable, comfortable,
and student-friendly campus environment, and
Whereas: the Capital Region Transportation Planning Agency (CRTPA) oversees
transportation planning in the region, providing a strategic opportunity for Florida State
University to engage with local and regional planning efforts for sustainable transportation.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-Sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: the
University should evaluate the feasibility of including EV charging stations in its Campus Master
Plan, in alignment with the NEVI program's guidelines and FDOT's focus.
Be it further resolved that: the Student Senate also encourages FSU to coordinate with local,
regional, and state transportation planning partners, including the CRTPA and FDOT, to
participate in and contribute to the statewide master plan for EV charging station deployment,
utilizing the available formula funds, and adhering to the key considerations set forth by the
NEVI program.
Be it further resolved that: FSU is also encouraged to actively seek grant funding available
through regional, state, and federal partners under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to
support the deployment of EV charging stations on campus.
Be it further resolved that: FSU is also encouraged to ensure that any deployed EV charging
infrastructure adheres to the guidelines for public accessibility, location preferences, and facility
amenities as outlined in the NEVI program.
Be it further resolved that: FSU is also encouraged to commit to providing regular updates on
the progress of these initiatives to the student body and other stakeholders.

Whereas: During the annual Budget Week proceedings, the composition of the Student Senate
Budget Committee is limited exclusively to Student Senators, despite the active participation
and inclusion of representatives from the Union Board and Campus Recreation Board, along
with the Student Body Treasurer or designee, in discussions and decision-making processes
during the Sweeping Committee Process, thereby limiting the breadth of perspectives and
expertise available directly within the committee, and
Whereas: The inclusion of the Student Body Treasurer or their designee as an Ex-Officio
member of the Student Senate Budget Committee is essential for ensuring a seamless
integration of comprehensive financial expertise and historical budgetary knowledge into the
committee's deliberations, thereby facilitating more informed, transparent, and effective
management of the Senate's fiscal responsibilities and decisions during the annual Budget
Week proceedings, and
Whereas: In the previous fiscal year 2023, a substantial portion of the Student Government
budget, amounting to 72.23% or $10,557,223 of the total $14,615,441, was allocated to
Campus Recreation and the Student Union, highlighting the significant impact and resource
utilization of these entities within the student community, thus underscoring the necessity for
their adequate representation and informed advocacy in the Budget Committee to facilitate
balanced and effective allocation of funds during the annual Budget Week, and
Be it resolved by the Seventy-sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Senate Rules of Procedure be amended as follows:
RULE FIVE – Committees
5.1 Committee Appointments: The Student Senate President shall appoint all
committees of the Student Senate. The Senate body may order the Student
Senate President to redo committee assignments by a two-thirds (2/3) vote.
5.2 Standing Committees shall consist of no less than five voting members.
5.3 Ex Officio Members: The Student Senate President and the Student Senate
Pro Tempore shall serve as ex-officio voting members of all Senate
committees. An exofficio ex-officio voting member shall count towards quorum
but not against it.
a. The Student Body Treasurer or designee shall be considered an ex-
officio non-voting member of the Student Senate Budget Committee for
the purposes of participating in annual Budget Week proceedings.DocuSign Envelope ID: B75C7C87-48E6-44D8-99B4-01A8AA28A76B

sections.heading: Page 2

b. In consultation with the respective leadership, the Student Senate
President shall appoint one (1) member of the Student Union Board and
one (1) member of the Campus Recreation Board to serve as ex-officio
non-voting members of the Student Senate Budget Committee for the
purposes of participating in the annual Budget Week proceedings.

Whereas: The Florida State University Student Government Association's Office of Government
Affairs is tasked with advocating and representing the interests of the student body at the
university, local, state, and federal levels; and
Whereas: The Board of Directors of the Office of Governmental Affairs compiled, debated, and
approved a legislative agenda for the 2024 regular Florida legislative session; and
Whereas: FSU SGA recommends measures to enhance student life and learning in the State of
Florida, including a textbook/course materials stipend awarded through the Florida Academic
Scholars Award in HB 1667, improvements to the Florida Academic Scholars award eligibility
criteria through SB 262/HB 25, and a Bright Futures Scholarship mentorship program
established in SB 1484/HB 895; and
Whereas: FSU SGA recognizes the critical need for mental health awareness, resources, and
services, including a resolution to be entitled “Sunshine Day” acknowledging the mental and
physical impact Covid-19 has had on students in our higher education system, and SB 164/HB
147 establishing a scholarship and loan forgiveness program aimed at providing financial
support to students pursuing mental health professions and encouraging their service in areas
suffering from critical shortages; and
Whereas: FSU SGA recognizes the dedication and sacrifice of service members serving in the
United States Armed Forces and supports initiatives that ease the transition of servicemembers
into advanced academic degree programs, including SB 494/HB 511 which waives GRE and
GMAT scores for military men and women; and
Whereas: FSU SGA recognizes the important work graduate students provide on campus and
in the classroom through associate programs and assistantships, and shall receive fee waivers
provided in SB 1518/HB 183; and
Whereas: FSU SGA recognizes the profound and lasting impact teachers have on the lives of
students, shaping their educational journey, and advocates for policies that reflect the value of
educators, contingent on tenured teachers being adequately supported, provided in SB 136/HB
13; and
Whereas: FSU SGA recognizes and supports scholarships for marginalized groups in our
higher education system, specifically direct descendants of the 1920 Ocoee Election Day Riots,

planning, developing, implementing, and evaluating programs, initiatives, campaigns, and
policies informed by student feedback, covering a wide range of health issues including alcohol,
tobacco, and other drug use, sexual health, nutrition, exercise, mental health, personal safety,
and violence.

affecting students in their academic performance to then design marketing, programs, and
resource allocation, and provide data for campus and community task forces on an array of
health topics.
Whereas: Completing the NCHA survey by March 1st, 2024, will allow timely and
comprehensive data collection, supporting the university's mission to promote holistic student
wellness.

Student Senate acknowledges the importance of the National College Health Assessment
(NCHA) in gathering data to inform and enhance health promotion programs, policies, and
initiatives on campus and encourages all eligible students to complete the survey before the
deadline of March 1st, 2024.

Whereas: February 14th, 2024, marks 6 years of the Marjory Stoneman Douglas school
shooting; and
Whereas: School shootings lead to a massive drop in student enrollment, student graduation
rates, student average test scores, and overall student mental health; and
Whereas: The ramifications of this shooting have changed the Marjory Stoneman Douglas and
Parkland community forever; and
Whereas: The Student Senate not only understands the detrimental effects gun-violence has
had and continues to have on education around the country, but also recognizes the
tremendous potential lost that day, and the bravery each victim showed;
Be it resolved by the Seventy-Sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Student Senate vehemently condemns the availability of military-grade semi-automatic
weapons, much like the weapon used to kill the 17 beautiful souls on February 14th, 2018, for
being available to the general public, and recognizes the failure of the American government in
protecting its children.
Be it further resolved that: This condemnation is rooted in our commitment to the safety and
well-being of the students and citizens alike. The Student Senate recognizes the devastating
impact of gun violence, especially in educational institutions, and stands in solidarity with those
affected by such senseless acts.
Be it further resolved that: The Student Senate undoubtably agrees that guns have no place
in education and that sensible gun control measures are essential to creating a safe
environment for students and citizens across the nation and urges lawmakers to enact
legislation that addresses the root cause of gun violence: the guns.
Be it further resolved that: The Student Senate calls upon lawmakers to address the issue of
gun-violence, and honors and remembers all the 17 victims of the shooting: Alyssa Alhadeff

Whereas: American Heart Month is celebrated in the month of February with the intentions of
spreading awareness on cardiovascular health. With global organizations efforts such as the

information, share tips on how to maintain a heart-healthy lifestyle, and recognizing signs of
cardiovascular disease, and
Whereas: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) affects a significant portion of the US population and
is listed as one of the leading causes of death in the US amongst men, women, and people of
racial and ethnic groups. Despite its highly deadly nature, it is 90% preventable with proper
education and actions taken early on, and
Whereas: Recent studies have considered the prevalent risk factors for cardiovascular disease
and in a study of 148 college-aged participants, 108 had demonstrated signs of a least two
cardiovascular risk factors such as alcohol use and familial history. Furthermore, implementing
educational interventions at a younger age can greatly reduce the manifestation of CVD later
on, and

enhancing student awareness of cardiovascular health such as University Health Services and
Campus Recreation. Through specific programs such as CPR training events hosted by

lifestyle minimizing the risk for CVD,

share information on cardiovascular disease through immersive and interactive programming,

Whereas: The Memorandum of Understanding Activity and Service Fee Annual Allocation
Between the Florida State University Student Government Association, Florida State University
Division of Student Affairs, and Florida State University Division of Finance and Administration,
commonly referred to in the 76th Student Senate Chamber as the “Budget Deal,” is as follows:
“This Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) is entered into by and between the Florida State
University Student Government Association (SGA), Florida State University Division of Student
Affairs (DSA), and Florida State University Division of Finance and Administration (VPFA),
herein referred to collectively as “the Parties.”
Whereas, the Activity and Service Fee revenues are to be expended for the benefit of the entire
student body, and
Whereas, the core and largest sources of student services and activities derive from the
functions of student success facilities and programs including the Student Union, Askew
Student Life Center, Student Services Building, Leach Center, Intramural Sports Fields,
Westside Courts, Rec SportsPlex, FSU Lakefront Park, the Globe, and Student Engagement,
which require a continuing and stable funding for staff and facilities, and
Whereas, SGA recognizes that this funding must be predictable and stabilized over periods of
time to provide these services.
Therefore, the Parties agree as follows:
The Parties agree to allocate the annual Activities and Services (A&S) fee collections as
provided below, for five (5) fiscal years, beginning July 1, 2024, and ending on June 30, 2029.
The University’s fiscal year begins on July 1 and ends on June 30.
Beginning on July 1, 2024, SGA agrees to receive $1,189,132 from A&S fee collections
to be used for purposes allowed for such funds by applicable law and to include SGA
Offices, Agencies, Bureaus, Affiliated Projects, and Funding Boards. This amount shall
annually increase by 4% of the previous year’s amount starting in year 2.
During the term of this MOU, SGA agrees to allocate the remaining annual A&S fee
collections to DSA to support student success facilities, and related expenses, salaries,
and overhead. In return, DSA agrees to sustain the student success facilities and
Student Engagement services and operations of hours at the current levels; in addition,
the same type of expenses will continue to be supported throughout this agreement.
Any reduction of operating hours greater than 10% shall require the Recreation CenterDocuSign Envelope ID: 83DAB58C-BC1C-4364-AEE5-1DB120267D04

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Board or the Union Board approval. DSA will fund the Congress of Graduate Students
(Congress) with their allocation of A&S fees, based on the Congress’s current
agreement terms with SGA.
The Parties agree that if student enrollment changes by more than 5% or if the A&S fee is
increased during the term of the MOU, they will renegotiate the A&S allocation. In addition, the
MOU terms may be renegotiated based on mutual consent of all parties.
On an annual basis, the DSA will provide a presentation on A&S fund allocations to members of
the SGA.
In the case of any alleged dispute between the Parties regarding the terms or implementation of
this MOU, the complaining party must raise such claim by written notice to the other party
including specific details within 30 days of its occurrence to all parties. The Parties shall meet
within 30 days of such notice to resolve any such dispute with the Student Body President,
Student Body Treasurer, Student Senate President, and Student Senate Budget Committee
Chair given at least 24 hours’ notice to attend such meeting. Those attending shall have
authority to resolve the dispute. If the Parties cannot resolve the dispute, final appeal shall be to
a three-person panel. The panel shall consist of one student appointed by the student body
president, the Senior Vice President for Finance and Administration (chair), and one at large
member selected by the University President.
Any individual waiver of MOU terms shall be in writing.
This MOU is executed in good faith, replaces all prior agreements between the Parties in these

Whereas: The presence of organizations like the Collegiate Recovery Program at Florida State
University aims to not only promote healthy conversations among peers, but also to eliminate
the negative stigmas surrounding recovery.
Whereas: The mission of Florida State University’s Collegiate Recovery Program, LIFT (Living
Intentionally, Finding Togetherness), is to allow students who are interested in recovery from
addiction and substance misuse to thrive during their college experience.
Whereas: The program includes mentorship opportunities, accountability checks, peer support,
as well as service projects, all of which are key for providing a sense of purpose while pushing
to eliminate unhealthy habits.

Collegiate Recovery Program’s tools and assistance are crucial for student success and
academic achievement for not only students recovering from substance misuse, but also for any
student looking to make a positive impact. The program should be supported and expanded in
whatever ways it can in order to best serve all students in need. We encourage any student
passionate about student wellness to get involved with the Healthy Noles Program. A program
with the purpose of training student leaders into peer health educators who educate the FSU
community through health advocacy events, presentations, and peer discussions.
Be it further resolved that: We commend the LIFT Program for creating a supportive
community on FSU’s campus for students who may be struggling with addiction and substance
misuse.

autonomy, and preventing unintended pregnancies, and
Whereas: the Florida State University campus is a place of diverse populations where students
may encounter situations requiring emergency contraception; including instances of
contraceptive failure, sexual assault, or unprotected intercourse, and
Whereas: studies have shown that timely access to emergency contraception significantly
reduces the risk of unintended pregnancies and empowers individuals to make informed
decisions about their personal sexual health, and
Whereas: limited access to emergency contraception due to factors such as cost,
stigmatization, or a lack of availability/accessibility can pose significant barriers to individuals
seeking timely and effective healthcare, and
Whereas: According to an AP News article in 2023; 39 universities in 17 states now have
emergency contraceptive vending machines, demonstrating feasibility and demand for an
improvement in access to emergency contraception;
Be it resolved by the Seventy-Sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that:
Florida State University acknowledges the importance of ensuring access to emergency
contraception to its student population and commits to installing sexual health vending
machines in strategic locations across campus such as; the Center for Health Advocacy and
Wellness, the Robert Manning Strozier Library, the Dirac Science Library, and the Student
Union; to provide convenient and confidential access to emergency contraception at any time.

Whereas: The Executive Branch’s Cabinet “Policies” shall be adopted as follows:
“SECTION ONE – Authority and Purpose
1.1. In accordance with the Student Body Constitution, there shall be a cabinet in
the Executive Branch to assist the constitutional officers in the execution of their
duties. The Constitution delegates the authority to define the positions and their
duties to Statutes.
1.2. Pursuant to 301.2 of Student Body Statutes, this policy shall outline the
cabinet of the Student Body President, including the processes and procedures
thereof.
SECTION TWO – Revision Procedure
2.1. Revisions to this document may be initiated by the Student Body President or
their designee, and shall be written in the form of a consent resolution sent to
Senate to be placed on their consent calendar. Senate shall then have the
authority to approve, deny, or amend any changes rendered, if the revision is
objected to on the floor. Revisions shall be enacted immediately upon approval by
the Senate.
2.2. Any revisions made shall be sent to the Webmaster within one business day,
who shall then post these revisions on the website. This document must be kept
up-to-date at all times.
SECTION THREE – Executive Office of the President
3.1. The Executive Office of the President shall be defined as the vehicle through
which the Student Body President and Vice President execute their constitutional

“SECTION ONE – Authority and Purpose
1.1. These rules of procedure shall lay forth the processes and procedures in
which the Student Body President and Executive Branch as empowered through
the President shall exert their constitutionally-granted power of appointment and
dismissal. This document is empowered by the Senate through 304.1 of Student
Body Statutes.
SECTION TWO – Revision Procedure
2.1. Revisions to this document may be initiated by the Student Body President or
their designee, and shall be written in the form of a consent resolution sent to
Senate to be placed on their consent calendar. Senate shall then have the
authority to approve, deny, or amend any changes rendered, if the revision is
objected to on the floor. Revisions shall be enacted immediately upon approval by
the Senate.
2.2. Any revisions made shall be sent to the Webmaster within one business day,
who shall then post these revisions on the website. This document must be kept
up-to-date at all times.
SECTION THREE – Candidate Search
3.1. No position requiring Student Senate confirmation may be filled until the
position has been advertised properly.
3.2. The Chief of Staff, assisted by one designee from the Executive Branch, will
conduct all candidate searches.
a. This designee from the Executive Branch shall be chosen by the Chief of
Staff.DocuSign Envelope ID: FAD6F5CC-D094-42FB-8FA7-2E6E4D92806C

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
b. In the absence of a designee, the Chief of Staff retains all responsibility for
conducting the work of the Candidate Search Process.
3.3. All positions shall be advertised for at least one week on the SGA Website.
SECTION FOUR – Candidate Screening Process
4.1. Upon the receipt of applications for a vacant position in Student Government
Association, a screening process shall be overseen by the Student Body President
to determine the most qualified candidate.
4.2. The Candidate Screening Process shall take no longer than ten (10) school
days from the end of the candidate search period.
4.3. The Candidate Screening Process, conducted by the Chief of Staff, or
designee as stipulated in Section Three of this document, shall include the
following:
a. The Chief of Staff, or designee as stipulated in Chapter 304.2 shall interview
all candidates.
b. All candidates shall provide the appropriate application as defined in Chapter
307.3, in completed format, demonstrating their qualifications for the position.
c. The interview shall be conducted in a standardized and professional form for
all candidates, and shall draw at least five interview questions from the forwarding
interview questions published on the SGA Website.
d. The interview shall consist of a basic questionnaire outlining the candidate’s
experience, qualifications, and goals for the respective position.
e. After all candidates have been interviewed, the Student Body President shall
forward the candidate deemed most qualified to the Student Senate for
confirmation.
4.4. The Student Body President may forego the candidate screening process with
the exception of subsection 4.3, subsection c, in cases where the candidate is
forwarded to the Student Body President, with a written notice of a proper interview
being conducted, by the Student Government Entity to which the candidate is
applying for a position.
4.5. It is the responsibility of the Student Body President, the Chief of Staff, or
designee to ensure that this process is carried out in a fair and constitutional
manner. To that end, any person(s) conducting the interviews shall recuse
themselves from the Candidate Screening Process and the processes ofDocuSign Envelope ID: FAD6F5CC-D094-42FB-8FA7-2E6E4D92806C

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
determining the most qualified candidate in situations where a candidate for any
position has a conflict of interest with the President, Chief of Staff, or designee.

to interview candidates for said office and deem the most qualified of those
candidates to then be forwarded by the President.
a. The forwarding letter sent to the Senate must include a notice when any
recusal occurs for any selection of Officers, stating that there was a recusal and a
signed statement from the non-biased actor(s) of their lack of conflict of interest.
4.6. If during the candidate screening process, the Student Body President finds
that a candidate is better suited for another position within the same Student
Government entity to which the candidate applied, the Student Body President may
reserve the right to forward the candidate, with their consent, for another position
for which they meet all Constitutional and statutory requirements.
a. If a candidate is forwarded to the Student Body President by an agency,
bureau, or other SGA entity for confirmation pursuant to Section 4.4, any changes
to the position for which a candidate is being forwarded to Senate shall also require
the consent of the head of the respective SGA entity.
b. Agency, Bureau, and SGA entity heads may also reserve the right to change
the position that a candidate is being forwarded for with the consent of the
applicant before forwarding the candidate to the Student Body President pursuant
to Section 4.4.
c. The forwarding letter sent to the Senate must include a notice in all cases
when candidates are forwarded to the Senate for positions that are different from
those which they applied for.
SECTION FIVE – Executive Office Positions

writing.

Body Statutes shall require confirmation by the Student Senate.DocuSign Envelope ID: FAD6F5CC-D094-42FB-8FA7-2E6E4D92806C

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
5.5. The Student Body President may appoint an Acting Executive Cabinet Officer

a. The nominees must be confirmed by a majority vote of the Student Senate
b. The confirmed nominee shall be referred to as the "designee" (i.e. Chief of

a. The selection process and appointment of all Bureau personnel below the

Whereas: National Cerebral Palsy Awareness Month is celebrated in March by displaying
support and advocating for the community living with Cerebral Palsy. The Month aims to
disseminate awareness of the challenges individuals face, promote inclusivity, and
acknowledge the need for increased research initiatives. Advocacy is currently centered around
increasing research initiatives towards CP to detect it early in children and prevent it altogether.
Whereas: Cerebral palsy (CP) is a permanent disability that influences a person’s mobility and
muscle strength (coordination and communication). People with CP need to concentrate more
on their movements and sequence of actions than others, so they tire more easily. It may cause
learning difficulties at school, which presents challenges to incorporating into the workforce.
Whereas: Cerebral Palsy is the leading cause of childhood disabilities. Most of those children
are born with it, while a tenth of the population of children in the U.S. develop CP due to injuries
to the developing brain. 3 in 4 children with cerebral palsy experience pain as a result of
impairments, and 1 in 3 children with cerebral palsy cannot walk or sit independently at two
years of age. While CP affects children within the first two years of life, early detection can help
mitigate the traumatic effects into childhood.
Whereas: Individuals with CP might face other health issues later in life, such as spinal and hip
abnormalities, due to these challenges. It may affect their behavior, ability to do things for
themselves, and social relationships. Consequently, individuals are prone to emotional
problems, which may lead them to avoid daily tasks such as attending school and social events.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-Sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Student Senate suggests the Accessibility Council meet with RSOs on campus as they work
closely with individuals on campus and the Tallahassee community, to get insight into their
needs.DocuSign Envelope ID: 88DC4484-9B38-4BEC-8B89-734BB568C599

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Be it further resolved that: The Student Senate urges OAS and the Accessibility Council to
work in conjunction in a continuous effort to prioritize the physical accessibility needs of these
individuals to facilitate their everyday lives and in case of emergency.

Whereas: Florida State University provides programs to support textbook accessibility and
affordability among the student body through initiatives such as etextbooks and course
reserves;
Whereas: The implementation of such programs recognizes the student need for affordable
alternatives, as supported by the Public Interest Research Group’s finding that 63% of students
go without course materials due to cost;
Whereas: Many Florida State University courses have, in turn, adopted inclusive access
programs that are marketed by publishing companies with a claim to offer a low-cost deal to
students;
Whereas: In actuality, these implemented programs subject students to automatic billing for
their course materials, including costs for homework, textbooks, and tests;
Whereas: The implementation of such automatic textbook billing threatens students' ability to
exercise their financial autonomy by automatically placing students into an opt-out model with
difficult to navigate procedures to unenroll from said opt-out model without being charged;
Whereas: Automatic textbook billing programs also threaten students’ ability to navigate the
academia marketplace for cheaper textbook options, given that programs are bundling their
textbooks with homework, leading to students having to purchase these products in order to
protect their course grades;
Whereas: Representatives of Florida PIRG Students at FSU have coordinated a textbook
affordability campaign on campus for three years and, in doing so, have created a connection
with FSU libraries, Faculty Senate, and SGA revolving around a shared goal of an equitable
student experience;DocuSign Envelope ID: 4604922D-4971-4E32-9459-30ABF6FFF7B7

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Whereas: Leaders of Florida PIRG Students at FSU serving on the SPARC National Advisory
Board have contributed to the creation of a National Student Statement against the rise of
automatic billing programs. This statement works in favor of course formats that allow for
greater student choice regarding how much of their finances they will budget for course
materials;
Be it resolved by the Seventy-Sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: the
Florida State University Senate supports the textbook affordability and accessibility initiatives of
Florida PIRG Students at FSU and SPARC;
Be it further resolved that: the Florida State University Senate affirms the sign-on of the
Florida State University Senate to the SPARC National Student Statement against an increase
in the prominence of automatic billing programs on Florida State campus;
Be it further resolved that: a copy of this resolution be sent to:
Jackson Boisvert, Student Body President
Anthony Benn, Student Body Vice President
Graceanne Hoback, Florida PIRG Students at FSU

Whereas: The structure of the Congress of Graduate Students, and its relationship to the
Student Government Association, has been fairly static for the past thirty years, and
Whereas: The current structure of COGS creates a limbo-like state where graduate students
are technically represented by two bodies, but are in fact primarily represented by COGS, and
Whereas: Florida State University has committed itself to the success of graduate students, as
demonstrated by the adoption of the Quality Enhancement Plan, in order to propel FSU into the
upper echelons of universities, and
Whereas: Over the last weeks and months, discussions about a new COGS-SGA relationship
have been ongoing between the Speaker and the Student Body President, as well as Student
Senate leadership, and
Whereas: These conversations have reached such a satisfactory point that the initial consent of
the Congress of Graduate Students and the 76th Student Senate to a roadmap for discussions
surrounding the statutory and constitutional language needed to effectuate the necessary
changes to the COGS-SGA relationship is now proper, and
Whereas: FSU SGA should shift to a quasi-bicameral system, where a fully undergraduate
Student Senate maintains the prerogative in matters of legislating, confirming nominees for
Student Body office, and controlling funds within the Senate’s discretion (with adequate
representation for graduate students on the Budget Committee during consideration of the
Annual A&S Fee Budget), and
Whereas: COGS should become a constitutionally non-partisan graduate chamber, holding the
ability to participate in the legislative process with an opportunity to present and dissent from
revisions to Student Body Statutes and Constitutional Amendments (regarding those which
have an impact on graduate students), confirm Supreme Court Justices (with the advice of the
Senate Judiciary Committee, should COGS take on the Court’s budget), solely enact changes
to the COGS Administrative Code, pass the Annual COGS A&S Fee Budget (with the ability for
undergraduate students to provide substantive comment), and ask for advisory opinions, andDocuSign Envelope ID: 6769F7A3-3A67-40B1-8DB1-DBF101A5D556

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Whereas: The Senate and COGS should have joint powers over resolutions stating the joint
opinion of Senate and COGS and, possibly, the confirmation of certain high-ranking Student
Body officers, and
Whereas: Each chamber would have independent authority over their officers, Rules of
Procedure, the transfer of funds within their discretion, and resolutions that state the opinion of
one particular chamber; now therefore:
Be it resolved by the Seventy-Sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Senate potentially agrees, in principle, to the Stronger Future Framework set out in this
resolution, as well as the accompanying 32nd COGS Resolution 4, and
Be it further resolved that: The Student Senate agrees to a timeline for the implementation of
this framework where an unofficial working group will work over the Summer semester to draft
and finalize the necessary constitutional and statutory changes necessary to effectuate the
Stronger Future Framework (while consulting with Senators, Representatives, the Executive
Branch, and our University partners), reporting back to COGS and the Senate with the proposed
constitutional amendment and statutory revisions during the first weeks of the Fall semester,
and that COGS and Senate look forward to a possible constitutional amendment within the time
necessary to ensure changes agreed upon are on the Fall 2024 SGA ballot, as well as agreed
upon statutory changes within the timeframe necessary for proper implementation, and
Be it further resolved that: The working group shall include, at a minimum, the Speaker of
COGS, two members of COGS (as decided by the Speaker), two Student Senators (as decided
by the 76th Student Senate President), and a representative of the Student Body President, as
well as any other persons deemed necessary by the group, and

Jackson Boisvert, Student Body President,
Joseph Cofer, 76th Student Senate President,

The Members of the 32nd Congress of Graduate Students.

Resolution #: 56
Primary Sponsor(s): Cofer, Randall

Whereas: Student Body Statute §413.8 states, “Membership in the Senate Hall of Fame is the
highest honor a student Senator can achieve. This honor shall be bestowed upon any Senator
who has performed their duty as a member of the Senate with the highest standard of
excellence, beyond that normally expected of a Senator at the Florida State University,” and
Whereas: Samuel Diaz served as a Senator representing the Division of Undergraduate
Studies, and later, the College of Social Sciences & Public Policy from the Fall of 2021 until Fall
2023, during which time he passionately advocated for the constituents of the college he
represented, as well as serving as the Chair of the Internal Affairs Committee and a member of
the Fall 2022 Sweepings Committee, and
Whereas: Senator Diaz went on to serve as the Senate President for the summer term of the
74th Student Senate, and was then elected as the President of the 75th Student Senate during
the fall of 2023, an office where he worked tirelessly to foster an environment of collaboration,
competence, and healthy discussion, improved the image of Senate through the creation of the
Merchandise Ad Hoc Committee and various outreach efforts, and acted as a mentor toward
members of the Senate and Student Government as a whole, and
Whereas: President Diaz authored many important pieces of legislation during his tenure in
Senate, including creating a Judicial Oath of Office for Student Supreme Court Candidates (74th
Senate, Bill 74), granting the Senate President power to call Senate special sessions (74th, Bill
84), welcoming President Richard McCullough to Florida State (74th; Res. 15), streamlining the
questioning process for legislation (74th; Res. 59), granting a Senate Award for Excellence to
the Black Law Students Association (74th; Res. 62), defining the A&S Fee Reserve account
(75th; Bill 39), restructuring Statutes pertaining to Senate Awards and reestablishing a Senate
Leadership team award (75th; Bill 86), modernizing the Senate calendar (75th, Res. 9), adding
the opposition of HB999 to the 2023 Legislative Agenda (75th; Res 27), and a Senate Projects
transfer to fund playground materials for the FSU Childcare Center (75th; Bill 105,) along with
authoring and co-sponsoring many more pieces of legislation, and
Whereas: President Diaz served as liaison to the Hispanic-Latinx Student Union, where he
sponsored legislation including a transfer of funds for HLSU’s annual gala (74th; Bills 22&23),
amending HLSU’s governing statutes (74th, Bill 57), honoring Hispanic Heritage Month (74th;
Res. 49), and amending the HLSU board application process (75th; Res. 21) as well as
consistently acting as an unwavering advocate for the Hispanic community, and
Whereas: President Diaz created the Merchandise Ad Hoc Committee in the Fall of 2023 to
promote the visibility of Senate and increase Senate outreach efforts, a foundation that
successfully carried over into the current administration, andDocuSign Envelope ID: 57137ABD-D36A-4D2F-B768-D04DCE0609DC

sections.text:
Whereas: Senator Benjamin Salazar testifies: “When I first entered the Student Senate at the
beginning of the 75th, Sam Diaz immediately struck me as a natural leader, a man whose
opinion and support carried serious weight inside and outside the chambers. I instantly looked
to him as a mentor of sorts, someone who could help me flourish within the SGA environment,
and I began trying to have conversations with him. Sam was never shy to share his extensive
knowledge of SGA and its inner workings, how to be a good senator, and how to best represent
the Hispanic community within the space, all of which are lessons I hold near to my heart to this
day. His leadership as President of the 75th Student Senate inspired me to seek leadership
within the chambers, and I could not think of a more deserving candidate for the Student Senate
Hall of Fame,” and
Whereas: Senator Jonus Goldstein testifies: “I spent the beginning of my fall semester sitting in
the back of the chambers watching Sam preside from the back of the room, and it was from him
I learned not only how Senate worked, but what kind of person a good Senator is. He is one of
the most intentional and driven leaders that has ever entered the chambers, and has shown me
what it means to dedicate yourself to this space. He is always happy to provide advice and
perspective on any legislation I’m working on, answer any questions, and has been an
invaluable mentor during my time at FSU,” and
Whereas: Senator Malek Mani testifies: “Even before my Fall Semester, Sam had reached out

an exceptional job of showcasing leadership, commitment, and the definition of knowing your

myself more at Florida State University through his achievements and enthusiastic personality,”
and
Whereas: Senator Aashna Anandijwala testifies: “Sam Diaz is definitely one of the most
hardworking and dedicated person I have ever met. From being Senate President and being Mr.
Pickles he has shown his leadership through and through. He truly deserves everything and
more. Thank you for being a great friend and an amazing role model,” and
Whereas: Senate Chief of Staff Isabella LoBianco testifies: “From the moment I met Sam Diaz
at my first Senate meeting during the 75th, I have always viewed him as a hardworking,
dedicated, and passionate individual. During his tenure as Senate President, he upheld these
traits and facilitated a collaborative and insightful community within these chambers. Now
working alongside him in the Office of Student Governance and Advocacy, he still upholds these
traits as an individual. I am excited to see what he continues to do! Yay Sam!” and
Whereas: Former Deputy Treasurer Carson Dale testifies: “Working with Sam was one of the

Student Senates, I am proud to have seen Sam rise above his peers and stand out for his
commitment to the student body and our legislative branch. Sam is one of the hardest workers I

rising junior. He has a clear idea of the branding and operations of the legislative space and

Having traveled the world with him, I’ve seen both Sam the man and Sam the leader. He is a

Whereas: SG&A Program Director Andy Johnson testifies: “Sam Diaz's dedication and
leadership during his time in the Florida State University Student Senate make him an

and
Whereas: Senator Samantha Randall testifies: “Sam was one of the first people I met in the

Whereas: The Student Government Council of Florida State University Panama City is an

Whereas: The turnover in PC SGC has occasionally made its Senate seat vacant, reducing
communication and collaboration between SGA in Tallahassee and SGC in Panama City, and
Whereas: The Panama City campus is seeking to expand its reach with the help of the city,

ideas between the two campuses benefits student life and the university as a whole, and

Senate Rules of Procedure be amended as follows:
2.9 The Student Senate President shall have the authority to assign Senators to
serve as liaisons to campus entities.
a. During the 2nd Senate after Fall inauguration the Student Senate President
shall announce open liaison and designee positions.
b. During the 3rd Senate after Fall inauguration the Student Senate President
shall assign Senate liaisons to campus entities. Liaisons can be replaced, or
added at any time through the authority of the Senate President.

website.
d. The Student Senate President shall, at minimum, assign a liaison to the
Executive Branch, the Union Board, the Campus Recreation Board, the
Congress of Graduate Students, the Class Councils, SGA Elections, SGA
Agencies, SGA Bureaus, SGA Affiliated Projects, SGA-funded Student

Campus, the Facilities Department, Transportation and Parking Services, the

Whereas: For the last several years, during summer Senate sessions, the Senate has decided
to meet on a biweekly basis, and
Whereas: The current Senate Rules of Procedure mandate that Senate meets on a weekly
basis, and
Whereas: Student Body Statute § 400.1 states, “Any changes to [the Senate Rules of
Procedure] must be approved in the form of resolution by a 2/3 vote of the Senate, with any
other requirements adhering to SBS 401.1,” therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: Rule
VIII of the Senate Rules of Procedure be amended as follows:
RULE EIGHT - Senate Business
8.1 When in session, the Senate shall meet weekly on Wednesdays. The meeting shall be
called to order at 7:30 p.m. All regularly scheduled meetings of the Student Senate shall
be publicly posted or advertised on the Student Government website. Any such
advertisement shall include the time and place of the Senate meeting.
a. The Senate shall stand adjourned at 11:00 pm.
1. Any outstanding business shall be tabled at 10:50 p.m. and heard
during “Unfinished Business” in the following Senate meeting. The
Senate shall then immediately move into statements of dissent,
advisor announcements, and final roll call, without deviating from
this order.
b. During summer sessions of the Senate, the Student Senate President
may be empowered to call meetings on a biweekly basis.
8.2 The Student Senate President shall call a special session of the Senate at their
discretion or if requested by a majority vote of the Senate in the form of a petition. All
Senators shall be notified of this special session by the Senate Advisor at least 24 hours
prior to the special session being held, and shall follow the calendar as listed this rule. a.
A petition to call a special session shall include Senators’ names, seats, and FSU IDs.

Whereas: the month of July is known as Ultraviolet (UV) Safety Awareness Month for the
purpose of raising awareness about the dangers of exposure to UV radiation and encouraging
the public to take precautions; and
Whereas: according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), most types
of skin cancer are caused by too much exposure to UV light, and that skin damage can occur in
as little as 15 minutes of exposure; and
Whereas: according to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, skin-damaging UV radiation
in Florida often reaches “very high” or “extreme” levels, particularly in summer months; and
Whereas: University students often spend 30 minutes or more each day walking to and from
campus and between class buildings, frequently during mid-day when UV radiation levels are
highest; and
Whereas: many University students also participate in outdoor recreation opportunities
facilitated by the University; and
Whereas: the Florida Department of Health advises limiting outdoor activities during peak mid-
day hours to minimize the risks of sun exposure, and when limiting outdoor activities is
impossible or impractical, wearing protective clothing and using sunscreen with a sun protection
factor (SPF) of at least 15; and
Whereas: making sunscreen widely available on the Florida State University campus,
particularly during summer months and near Campus Recreation facilities, would be a
significant step toward promoting the prevention of exposure to harmful UV radiation;
NOW THEREFORE be it resolved by the Seventy-sixth Student Senate at Florida State
University that: the Student Senate Liaison to the Campus Recreation Board (CRB) is directed
to coordinate with the Student Government Association Executive Branch and the CRB to
evaluate the feasibility of deploying sunscreen dispensers at various locations around the FSU
Main Campus.

Be it further resolved that: the Student Senate President shall appoint a Florida State

the SGA Accounting Office, within ten (10) business days following the event,” and

Whereas: Tallahassee, Florida, while known for warmer months, can experience average
winter temperatures as low as 39°F, unexpectedly surprising students who come to Florida
State University from out of state or cities with warmer climate; and
Whereas: According to the New York Times’ College Access Index, 2.2% of the 42,000 FSU
students come from low-income families, which can make it difficult for those students to afford
adequate winter clothing; and
Whereas: In conjunction with low-income students, many don’t have cars or don’t have the
general necessary resources to purchase winter clothing once they arrive on campus; and
Whereas: A Winter Clothing Closet would clearly be significantly beneficial to the Florida State
University student body, allowing for all students to easily access articles of winter clothing
when needed without having to further burden or extend themselves financially or in any other
way; and
Whereas: The Winter Clothing Closet will aim to be stored on campus in a storage unit in
Thagard, functioning similarly to the ProfessioNole Clothing Closet, running only in the winter
months of November through February, when jackets, hoodies, etc. are in high demand; and
Be it resolved by the Seventy-sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Student Senate President shall appoint a Florida State University Winter Clothing Closet liaison
(WCC) responsible for collaboration with Division of Student Affairs (DSA) to evaluate the
feasibility of creating a Winter Clothing Closet for winter apparel at Thagard here on Florida
State University’s main campus.
Be it further resolved that: The Student Senate Liaison to the Winter Clothing Closet (WCC) is
respectfully requested to directly coordinate with the Student Government Association (SGA)
Executive Branch to provide an analysis and recommendations to the Student Senate regarding
the WCC, including any one-time and recurring costs to do so and any financial participation
that may be required of the Student Government Association to accomplish this goal.Docusign Envelope ID: E4B11614-7DF4-4AAB-B4D8-F9A811E5E38A
