Whereas: National Disability Employment Awareness Month (NDEAM) has been
recognized every October since 1988 to acknowledge the significant contributions of
those with physical, developmental, behavioral or emotional, and sensory impaired
disorders to the workforce, and to promote the awareness of rights within the workplace
and fair access to quality work for all people with disabilities, and
Whereas: In 1945, Congress declared the first week in October “National Employ the
Physically Handicapped Week"; In 1962, they removed the word ‘physically’ to include
people with all disability types; In 1988, Congress permanently renamed the week to
“National Disability Employment Awareness Month”, expanding it to a month for further
national recognition and appreciation, and
Whereas: Disabilities are classified as both physical and intellectual, and those with all
types of disabilities are deserving of quality job opportunities, and the Americans with
Disabilities Act of 1990 aims to eliminate discrimination based on ability level in areas
such as employment, public spaces and accommodations, transportation,
telecommunications, and governmental operations and facilities at the state and local
level, and
Whereas: An estimated 1.3 billion people, or about 16% of the global population, have a
disability, and 22.5% of people with disabilities in the United States were employed in
2023. 8% of current faculty and staff of Florida State University have reported having a
disability, and over 5,000 FSU students receive accommodations from the Office of
Accessibility Services, and
Whereas: The Student Senate extends its gratitude to the Office of Accessibility Services
and the Office of Equal Opportunity Compliance and Engagement for their work which
ensures a positive and equitable experience for all students, faculty and staff, regardless
of disability status, and
Be it resolved by the Seventy-sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Student Senate formally recognizes National Disability Employment Awareness Month
and sends its best regards and utmost gratitude to those with disabilities who
contribute important and honorable work to the success of Florida State University,
and to FSU students in the workforce who have a disability.Docusign Envelope ID: 553EF87A-29B2-4406-8A95-2044E3B59BC1

Whereas: The Florida State University Student Government Association celebrates 75 years of
service, excellence, and dedication to the campus community and its students. Throughout its
75 years, the Student Government Association has been known as the College Government
Association from 1935-1949, and University Government Association (UGA) till the 1960’s.
Whereas: The history of the Student Government Association is hearty, and representative of
the paths forged from across our campus. In 1973, the university elected its first black Student
Body President, Charles Thompson, and in 1974, David Aronofsky and Jan Pietrzyk were the
first student leaders at Florida State to set and allocate A&S fees. In 1996, Liza Park served as
the first Asian American Student Body President, and under her tenure, the Asian American
Student Union was established as an SGA Agency.
Whereas: The 2000’s, also marked many significant moments for the Student Government
Association. In 2004, Eady/Hanson/Schoonoer administration successfully lobbied against the
implementation of block tuition at FSU. In 2008, the O’Shea/Counts administration collaborated
with the Seminole Student Boosters and created the TRUE Seminole campaign. In 2016, the
Tabares/Pierre-Louis/McGuiness administration lobbied the legislature and received $1.5 million
in PECO funding for the new Black Student Union house. More recently in 2019, the
Pierre/Brown/Pimentel administration successfully lobbied for a on-campus polling place. Finally
in 2022, the university elected Nimna Gabadage as its first Sri Lankan Student Body President.
Whereas: The Student Government Association has worked hard to create many significant
moments for the student body of Florida State University and continues doing so to this day. It is
important to recognize the work of those who have come before us, and the work we continue to
do now as a Student Government Association.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: As
many of us venture into post graduate life and become alumni of the Student GovernmentDocusign Envelope ID: 7C68BF17-F304-41C2-887F-0E4D3176C376

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Association and Florida State University, we should bear in mind the ways we can continue
giving back to the university as alumni, and ensure the longevity of SGA for years to come.

Whereas: Established in 2023, the Raide App was created to decrease purchases of fast
fashion and prevent waste of clothing, by establishing a rental system for students at Florida
State University. Created by two FSU students, Raide has been able to distribute over 1,000
rentals in just less than a year. These students being involved across campus in multiple areas,
were able to establish a network of students to spread the word about Raide in just a short
period of time.
Whereas: The Jim Moran College of Entrepreneurship (the nation's first standalone college of
entrepreneurship at a public university) has frequently spotlighted Raide, and is a proud
supporter of this student created, and now alumni run business. The founders of Raide,
Kennedy Joy Foristall and Noah Romo, won the $10,000 first-place prize in the 2024
InNOLEvation Challenge New Venture Competition. They were also featured on the Innovation
Mindset Podcast, hosted by Dr. Mark McNees from the FSU Jim Moran College.
Whereas: Having now expanded to two other universities across the state of Florida (University
of Central Florida and University of Florida) Raide’s water conservation and C02 conservation
are notable. On average, producing a new garment of clothing can consume 3,000 liters of
water. For the 1,000 rentals through Raide, this saved 792,516 gallons of water. Their 1,000
rentals have also prevented 2,500-5,000 pounds of clothing out of landfills.
Whereas: The Raide app is on its way to being a household name across college campuses,
establishing a brand that has originated at Florida State, and disputing fast fashion all at the
same time. It is important that we as students continue to celebrate the success of Raide and
support our entrepreneurship students across campus.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Student Government Association and seventy-sixth Student Senate support student run
businesses, our alumni, and the success of Raide being established across universities.Docusign Envelope ID: 60D6EB07-D8C4-40F1-8327-B28AFD124B30

limited to; Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Virginia;
Whereas: On Friday, October 4th, 2024, the death toll of this tragedy had officially exceeded
200 persons;

infrastructure, ecosystems, and livelihoods;

family and loved ones that have experienced great loss;

they deal with these trying times;

administration, and any other affected members of our neighboring communities;

Whereas: The Student Government of Florida State University has a vested interest in
upholding the individual rights and personal freedoms of the student body, particularly in matters
concerning personal health and bodily autonomy; and,
Whereas: Amendment 4 is a constitutional ballot initiative that aims to restore the right to
reproductive healthcare in Florida, reversing previous restrictions and ensuring that individuals
have the right to make decisions about their own bodies; and,
Whereas: Access to safe and legal reproductive healthcare is a fundamental aspect of public
health, which impacts the well-being and economic stability of individuals, particularly students
and young adults; and,
Whereas: Denying access to reproductive services disproportionately affects marginalized
communities, including low-income individuals, people of color, and those living in rural areas,
exacerbating existing inequalities; and,
Whereas: The Student Government firmly supports health equity, gender equality, and the
rights of all individuals to make informed decisions about their own bodies; and,
Whereas: Numerous health organizations, including the World Health Organization and the
American Medical Association, affirm that access to safe and legal reproductive healthcare is a
critical component of comprehensive healthcare; and,
Whereas: The restoration of reproductive rights through Amendment 4 will align Florida’s
policies with those of many other states that prioritize the health and autonomy of their
residents; and,Docusign Envelope ID: A5067593-6B31-4859-BBF2-C2F5E5C5891B

student organizations to educate and inform the student body about the importance of
Amendment 4, including hosting informational sessions, registering students to vote, and
distributing literature; and,
Be it further resolved that: The Student Government is a strictly non-partisan body, and this
resolution should not be misconstrued as endorsing any candidate for public office or political
party; and,

Whereas: Almost a quarter of the Student Body of Florida State University falls under the
jurisdiction of the Hispanic/Latinx Student Union, and the Venezuelan Student Association
(Vensa) represents the Venezuelan population on campus, and
Whereas: A huge percentage of Venezuelan students at Florida State University are first-
generation college students and are immigrants themselves after leaving Venezuela and their
families due to the ongoing humanitarian crisis. This crisis has been ongoing since 1998 when
former President Hugo Chavez was elected into power and has gotten drastically worse since
2010. Since then, over 7.7 million Venezuelans have emigrated from the country to various
countries in South and North America, and
Whereas: Every election cycle since, multiple election violations have taken place, invalidating
millions of votes cast by Venezuelan citizens against Chavez to place Chavez and, after his
death, Nicolás Maduro into the presidency. In 2018, Maduro’s re-election was found fraudulent,
however attempts at peaceful transitional government were unsuccessful, so he gained more
control over Venezuela’s state institutions, and
Whereas: In July 2024, another election took place for their democratic election process. From
the beginning, Venzuelan citizens were put at a disadvantage, as citizens outside of Venezuela
were denied their right to vote, polling places inside of the country were not letting people cast
their votes, and polling sites were being closed early all in an attempt to further Maduro’s
agenda of keeping control of the country; however,
Whereas: despite this, the Venezuelan people voted to instill the opposition leader, Edmundo
González, into the presidency. The Venezuelan electoral authorities then concluded, without
presenting any evidence, that Maduro had won, despite the opposition then releasing the official
taly sheets collected by poll watchers from a majority of polling centers showing a landslide
victory for González. Multiple countries including the USA, Perú, Argentina, Uruguay, Costa
Rica, Ecuador, Panama and Chile all have accepted and recognize Gonzalez as the winning
president of Venezuela; however,Docusign Envelope ID: 16D2B615-CC62-4DA3-8F09-D0C59034F948

sections.heading: Page 2

Whereas: After being threatned with “terrorism” arrest charges by the Maduro regime, González
was forced into fleeing the country and received political asylum in Spain, where he has
continued to fight from to validate the election results, and
Whereas: Because of this, protests launched across the country and Maduro’s regime started
incarcerating, kidnapping and killing peaceful protesters off the streets, including children and
teenagers, that disagreed with the fraudulent election results. Additionally,
Whereas: This has furthered the food insecurity crisis in Venezuela, where nearly 50% of the
population experiences food scarcity due to hyperinflation and an corrupt government led by the
Maduro regime. Venezuela has been named the biggest country that is not currently in war that
has the most refugees, despite it once being the richest country in Latin America, and
Whereas: Venezuelan students, many of whom are first-generation or immigrants, may
experience mental health challenges due to the ongoing crisis in their home country, which can
eacerbate the stress of adjusting to life at Florida State University. It is essential that the
university provides adequate resources and support services for these students, therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: We
stand in support with our fellow Venezuelan students who may have come from or have family
in Venezuela and urge others to educate themselves further on this immense humanitarian
crisis.

Whereas: the Veterans Student Union is committed to supporting the educational, professional,

Whereas: travel opportunities can provide valuable experiences, networking, and
representation for student veterans at various forums; and
Whereas: 76th Senate Bill 2024 restricts the use of expense funds allocated to the Veterans

an amendment to 76th Senate Bill 2024. It does not establish a precedent, standard, or
enforceable action for future budget committees to follow this exception or for future
amendments or exceptions to budget proviso restrictions and shall not result in any future
proviso exceptions.

Whereas: Florida State University (FSU) is committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and
respectful environment for all students, faculty, and staff; and
Whereas: Racial discrimination poses significant harm to the academic, social, and mental well-
being of students of color and perpetuates systemic inequities within the university community;
and
Whereas: Students of color (POC) have been deeply offended and disheartened by FSU’s
current lack of an explicit policy addressing racial discrimination in the Student Conduct Code,
feeling unprotected and undervalued as a result; and
Whereas: FSU’s Student Conduct Code currently lacks a specific section explicitly addressing
racial discrimination as a violation of university policies, unlike how it currently addresses sexual
discrimination and misconduct; and
Whereas: The absence of a clearly defined policy on racial discrimination fails to acknowledge
the severity of such actions, leaving students vulnerable without adequate institutional recourse;
and
Whereas: The inclusion of a Racial Discrimination section in the Student Conduct Code would
ensure that students are protected from racial prejudice, bigotry, and injustice while holding
offenders accountable in a clear and direct manner; and
Whereas: Similar institutions of higher learning across the country have explicitly included racial
discrimination in their conduct codes to affirm their dedication to equity and inclusion; and
Whereas: Hate speech, although sometimes protected under the principles of free speech,
remains harmful and disruptive to an inclusive academic environment and should not be
tolerated within the university setting; and
Whereas: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act prohibits racial discrimination in institutions receiving
federal funding, underscoring the need for anti-racism policies at FSU to align with federal
standards;
Be it resolved by the Seventy-sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that:
The Florida State University Student Government Association (SGA) strongly condemns the
current absence of a Racial Discrimination section in the Student Conduct Code under
violations, which has left students of color feeling unsupported and unprotected; and
Be it further resolved that:
The SGA urges the FSU administration, including the Division of Student Affairs, the Office ofDocusign Envelope ID: FD8264C1-1E09-463C-BDB7-0DF65789B992

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
the General Counsel, and the Student Conduct and Community Standards Office, to
immediately amend the Student Conduct Code to explicitly include racial discrimination as a
violation, as it has done for sex/gender-based discrimination; and
Be it further resolved that:
The new section should define racial discrimination as disparate treatment toward a person
based on race, color, or ethnicity which adversely impacts academic, employment, or other
decisions related to University programs and activities; and
Be it further resolved that:
The policy should provide clear definitions for racial harassment and racially motivated actions
and establish transparent guidelines for reporting, investigation, and adjudication of such
incidents; and
Be it further resolved that:
The SGA calls on the administration to engage with student leaders, particularly those from
marginalized communities, in the process of drafting and implementing this new section to
ensure it addresses the needs and concerns of those most affected by racial discrimination; and
Be it further resolved that:
The SGA emphasizes the need for education and training on racial sensitivity and discrimination
prevention across the FSU community, with mandatory workshops for students, faculty, and
staff to foster understanding and accountability; and
Be it further resolved that:
The SGA will actively monitor and advocate for the immediate adoption and enforcement of this
amendment, ensuring that FSU remains a safe and equitable environment for all students; and
Be it further resolved that:
This policy on racial discrimination will undergo a review every three years to ensure it remains
effective and responsive to the evolving needs of FSU’s diverse community; and
Be it further resolved that:
The FSU administration will engage in collaborative discussions with peer institutions to adopt
best practices in preventing and addressing racial discrimination on campus; and
Be it further resolved that:
While free speech protections exist, hate speech that undermines inclusivity and respect should
not be accepted within FSU’s academic community.

Whereas: The current Senate Rules of Procedure state that following the Fall Inauguration, the
most senior member of the Student Senate shall call to order the organizational meeting to elect
the Student Senate President. "Most senior" is defined as the senator with the longest
consecutive term, with alphabetical precedence if terms are equal; and
Whereas: The current definition of "most senior" in the Senate Rules of Procedure does not
prioritize continuity in leadership, which can lead to inconsistencies during pivotal moments
such as the organizational meeting; and
Whereas: An established order of succession, as already outlined in Rule 1.7 for filling
permanent vacancies in the office of Student Senate President, ensures that leadership
transitions are managed by experienced and relevant figures within the Senate, fostering
procedural stability; and
Whereas: Rule 1.7 already provides a clear and effective order of succession during vacancies,
demonstrating the value of structured continuity and experience. This existing standard should
be mirrored in other procedural rules for consistency and ease of use across all Senate
operations; therefore,
Be it resolved by the Seventy-sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: Rule
One, Section 1(a) of the Senate Rules of Procedure shall be amended to redefine “most senior”
as follows:
“Most senior” shall be defined by the following order of succession: Student Senate President
Pro Tempore, Chairperson of Judiciary, Chairperson of Internal Affairs, Chairperson of Budget,
Chairperson of Finance, and Chairperson of Student Life from the previous Senate, if any
remain in office. If no senator from this succession remains, seniority will be determined by the
longest consecutive term of service. If terms are equal, alphabetical order by last name will
apply.
Be it further resolved that: This amendment shall take immediate effect to strengthen
leadership continuity and procedural clarity.Docusign Envelope ID: 8A86D267-7ED7-45AE-B56F-C49028BCC604

the contributions and resilience of Puerto Ricans and their historical ties to the United States;

State University student body, and

Florida State University community, and
Whereas: As representatives of the student body, it is imperative that the Student Senate takes
time to reflect on the lives lost during the 2023-2024 academic year, and
Whereas: The Seventy-sixth Student Senate recognizes that each student holds a unique,
valuable, and irreplaceable position in our community and wishes to honor these students upon
each Sine Die, therefore

“Ellie” Sims

Whereas: Pursuant to Chapter 622 of Student Body Statutes, the College Leadership Council
(CLC) Funding Committee met in the Fall 2024 semester to allocate its $15,000 allocated
budget for the 2024-2025 fiscal year, and
Whereas: The CLC Funding Committee tentatively approved funding recommendations for
petitioning CLCs, but did not draft and pass a resolution approving the funding pursuant to
Student Body Statute §622.3(B)(6), and
Whereas: The CLC Funding committee recommended its allocation as follows:
Leadership Council Amount
College of Business $6,000
College of College of Social Science & Public Policy $2,700
College of Communication and Information $2,000
College of Criminology $1,800
College of Fine Arts $2,500
TOTAL: $15,000

76th STUDENT SENATE
Senate Resolution
Consent Resolution #: 73
Sponsor(s): Lalani, Mastali
Date: 09/16/2024
Whereas: The Student Government Association (SGA) has existed in its current form for over
75 years, allocating hundreds of millions of dollars to enhance student life at Florida State
University; and
Whereas: The Executive Branch of the SGA is responsible for carrying out the administration’s
programs, projects, and agenda, in alignment with the needs and interests of the student body;
and
Whereas: The Executive Branch is structured under the Executive Office of the President,
which encompasses various departments and offices including the Office of the Vice President,
the Office of the Treasurer, and others that support student initiatives; and
Whereas: These revisions seek to improve transparency, efficiency, and communication within
the Executive Branch by updating existing roles, responsibilities, and organizational structures
to better serve the student body.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-sixth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
proposed revisions to the Executive Policies, are hereby approved:
2024-02 - Section 3: Executive Branch Offices and Responsibilities
A. General Provisions
1. The Executive Branch is structured under the overarching Executive Office of the
President, which encompasses the Office of the President, the Office of the Vice
President, and the Office of the Treasurer. Each office has distinct
responsibilities. The head of each office is responsible for working with the
Student Body President or their designee in appointing its members.
B. Executive Office of the President
1. The Executive Office of the President supports the Student Body President and
Vice President in executing their constitutional powers and carrying out their
administration's programs, projects, and agenda.
2. Duties of the Executive Office:
ii. Assist in executing the plan for the Executive Branch.
iii. Represent segments of the student body in accordance with the structure
issued by the Student Body President.
iv. Fulfill the obligations of the job descriptions for each office.
v. Work for the improved quality of life of the student body.
vi. Meet regularly, no less than once every two weeks during the fall, spring,
and summer semesters. Minutes of these meetings will be recorded and
kept on record.
3. Organization and Appointments:Docusign Envelope ID: 690673CF-E8A6-4E06-BB66-106A56E9DCC4

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
ii. The Student Body President may organize the Executive Office as
deemed necessary and proper within the limits imposed by the Student
Body Statutes.
iii. If a new position is created, the Student Body President must notify the
Student Senate in writing.
iv. Within two (2) weeks of inauguration, the Student Body President, in
consultation with the Student Body Vice President, shall present the plan
for the organization of the Executive Office to the Student Senate. This
plan must be published on the SGA website.
v. All members of the Executive Office must be confirmed by the Student
Senate as “Cabinet Offices” and major office positions within the
Executive Branch.
vi. The Chief of Staff, appointed by the Student Body President and subject
to Student Senate confirmation, directs the activities of the Executive
Office and is subject to the will of the Student Body President.
C. Office of the President
1. The Office of the President is responsible for the overall leadership and direction
of the Executive Branch, overseen by the Student Body President.
2. Positions in the Office of the President:
a. Student Body President: Represents the student body, oversees the
execution of SGA policies, and coordinates with university administration
and external entities. Has sole power of appointment within the Executive
Office and may dismiss any individual serving under them at their
discretion.
b. Chief of Staff: Manages and leads the staff, represents the Student Body
President to internal SGA entities, coordinates executive projects, and
interviews and recommends applicants for appointed positions within the
SGA.
c. Deputy Chief of Staff: Supports the Chief of Staff, organizes and prepares
for board meetings, ensures efficient operation, manages
communications with university partners, facilitates collaboration across
departments, and oversees special projects.
D. Sub-Groups within the Office of the President:
1. Executive Cabinet: The Executive Cabinet advises the President on subjects
related to their respective offices and accomplishes work within their positions.
b. Cabinet Director: Manages the Executive Cabinet, holds weekly
meetings, and provides monthly platform updates.
c. Secretary of Sustainability: Leads projects related to environmental
sustainability on campus and within the greater Tallahassee community.
d. Secretary of Health & Wellness: Leads projects to advance health, safety,
and wellness, partnering with various departments on related initiatives.
e. Secretary of Athletics & Recreation: Fosters relationships with the Athletic
Department and advances recreation opportunities for students.
f. Secretary of Student Services: Coordinates projects for student safety,
transportation, and other services, partnering with FSUPD and
Transportation and Parking Services.
g. Secretary of Collegiate Affairs: Assists with Board of Governors and
Board of Trustees preparations, establishes relationships with other
universities, and spearheads statewide student projects.Docusign Envelope ID: 690673CF-E8A6-4E06-BB66-106A56E9DCC4

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
h. Secretary of Diversity, Equity, & Inclusion: Focuses on anti-discrimination
initiatives through student programming, development, and policies,
collaborating with various departments.
2. Office of the Attorney General:
a. The Office of the Attorney General provides legal support and oversight
for the Executive Branch.
b. Attorney General: Represents the Executive Branch in all SGA legal
proceedings, conducts statutory revisions, and creates executive
memorandums.
c. Deputy Attorney General(s): Assists the Attorney General in statutory
revisions and ensures compliance with SGA and Florida law.
3. Communications Team:
a. The Communications Team manages the Executive Branch's internal and
external communications.
b. Press Secretary: Represents the Executive Branch to external outlets,
manages media relations, speechwriting, interviewing for articles, and
oversees SGA's social media presence.
c. Director of Media and Content: The Director of Media and Content
involves managing the development of multimedia content, overseeing
content scheduling, and ensuring that all media output aligns with the
Executive Branch's communication strategy.
d. Director of Communications: Assists the Press Secretary, maintains the
SGA website, and contributes to speechwriting and articulating the
Executive Branch's vision.
e. Graphic Design Coordinator: Documents SGA events and supports other
branches and projects as needed.
E. Office of the Vice President
1. The Office of the Vice President is responsible for supporting and coordinating
various executive projects and overseeing Agencies, Bureaus, and Class
Councils.
2. Positions in the Office of the Vice President:
a. Chief Administrative Officer: Manages the Executive Office of the Vice-
President’s staff, represents the Vice-President to internal SGA entities,
coordinates executive projects, and ensures proper tracking of files,
records, and documents.
b. Deputy Chief Administrative Officer: Assists in the overall management
and coordination of the Vice-President’s staff and supports the Chief
Administrative Officer with assigned duties.
F. Sub-Groups within the Office of the Vice President:
1. Programming Team:
a. The Programming Team handles event planning and student
programming initiatives.
b. Director of Activities & Student Programming: Leads or assists
with any programming effort of the Executive Branch, including
providing support to student government entities as requested.
c. Events & Student Programming Coordinators: Assist the Director
of Activities & Student Programming with programming efforts and
support various SGA entities and projects.
2. Student Logistics Team:
a. The Student Logistics Team focuses on student engagement and the
overall student experience.Docusign Envelope ID: 690673CF-E8A6-4E06-BB66-106A56E9DCC4

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
b. Director of Project Development & Strategic Planning: Performs regular
assessments of SGA Executive Projects, oversees risk management, and
conducts project research and evaluations.
c. Director of Student Engagement: Facilitates relationships between SGA
Officials, Registered Student Organizations, Direct Support
Organizations, and other student life entities, leading student outreach
efforts.
d. Director of Campus Life: Drives innovation in programs, services, and
infrastructure, overseeing new initiatives to enhance institutional
effectiveness and campus experience.
G. Office of the Treasurer
1. The Office of the Treasurer is responsible for managing the financial aspects of
the Executive Branch and is headed by the Student Body Treasurer.
2. Positions in the Office of the Treasurer:
a. Deputy Treasurer: Advises and assists the Student Body Treasurer in
financial actions and supports the Treasurer's roles and responsibilities in
their absence.
b. Internal Budget Analyst: Assists with internal financial projects, provides
financial support to the Executive Branch, and serves on financial
committees as requested by the Student Body Treasurer.
c. External Budget Analyst: Assists with external financial projects, provides
financial support to the Executive Branch, and serves on financial
committees as requested by the Student Body Treasurer.
2024-02 - Section 6: Vacancies in Elected Positions
 Vacancies in Elected Positions shall be filled as other positions are, but shall require 2/3
of a Student Senate quorum for confirmation.
2024-02 - Section 7: Oversight of the Student Body President
A. The Student Body President shall:
1. Provide updates on the affairs of the university and the Student Government
Association at the State of the Student Body Address.
2. Give remarks at the Spring Inauguration.
3. Approve or veto bills submitted by the Student Senate. In the case of a veto,
provide written justification and reasoning alongside an oral explanation within
two Senate meetings of the bill’s failure.
4. Approve or veto the usage of funds from the Campus Development Fund.
5. Fulfill all responsibilities outlined in statutes regarding Presidential Appointments.
6. Issue executive orders recommending the suspension or permanent removal of
an entity's Student Government Association status if they fall within the purview
of the Executive Branch.
7. Ensure that all executive orders, appointments, vetoes, and dismissals of
Student Government Association officers are posted on the SGA website.
8. Oversee the supervision and regulation of the Executive Institutes. The President
shall have the discretion to dismiss Institute Directors and Assistant Directors.
9. Serve as a voting member on or appoint designee to the Homecoming Planning
Commission.
10. Administer and regulate the bureaus. Bureau Directors shall report directly to the
Student Body President, but any action taken by a Bureau Director may be
countermanded by the President if it is in the best interest of the student body.Docusign Envelope ID: 690673CF-E8A6-4E06-BB66-106A56E9DCC4

2024-02 - Section 8: Oversight of the Student Body Vice President
A. The Student Body Vice President shall:
1. Have the responsibility over the supervision and regulation of the Executive
Institutes. The Student Body President shall have the discretion to dismiss
Institute Directors and Assistant Directors.
2. Serve as a voting member of the Homecoming Planning Commission.
3. Oversee the guidance, administration, and regulation of the bureaus. Bureau
Directors shall report directly to the Student Body Vice President, but any action
taken by a bureau Director may be countermanded by the Student Body
President if it is in the best interest of the student body.
4. Supervise and regulate the agencies.
5. Assume the duties of the President in the absence of the President or upon that
individual’s request.
6. Coordinate the efforts of the Cabinet and serve as coordinator for the formulation
and completion of Cabinet projects.
7. Coordinate with the Student Body President, Student Body Treasurer, and
Executive Cabinet to accomplish executive projects.
8. Direct grievances and ideas to the proper functionary and ensure they are acted
upon.
9. Meet at least once a month with the directors of executive agencies, affiliated
projects, bureaus, and class councils to review performance, address questions
and concerns, receive feedback and advice on the functioning of the Executive
Branch, and discuss possibilities of new projects.
10. Serve as the vehicle throughout the Executive Branch to support programming
events and accomplish agency, bureau, and council projects.
11. If time allows, provide updates on the affairs of the university and the Student
Government Association at the State of the Student Body Address.
12. If time allows, give remarks at the Spring Inauguration.
13. Oversee and regulate the activities of the Executive Institutes, ensuring Institute
Directors and Assistant Directors are performing their duties effectively.
14. Administer and regulate the operations of the bureaus, with Bureau Directors
reporting directly to the Student Body Vice President. The Student Body
President retains the authority to countermand actions if necessary.
15. Supervise and regulate the activities of the agencies to ensure alignment with the
goals and priorities of the Student Government Association.
16. Facilitate collaboration and coordination between class councils and other parts
of the Executive Branch, meeting regularly with directors of class councils to
review their performance and support their initiatives.
17. Oversee and support the activities of affiliated projects, ensuring these projects
align with the mission and objectives of the Student Government Association.
18. Conduct monthly meetings with directors of executive agencies, affiliated
projects, bureaus, and class councils to review performance, address questions
and concerns, and discuss new project possibilities.Docusign Envelope ID: 690673CF-E8A6-4E06-BB66-106A56E9DCC4

19. Serve as a key facilitator in supporting programming events across the Executive

2024-02 - Section 9: Oversight of the Student Body Treasurer
A. The Student Body Treasurer shall:
1. Approve or reject all A&S expenditures requested by branches, offices, agencies,
bureaus, affiliated projects, and Recognized Student Organizations (RSOs).
Graduate RSOs shall have their expenditures approved by the COGS Financial
Officer or COGS Speaker in lieu of the Student Body Treasurer.
2. Reject expenditures deemed fiscally irresponsible, excessive, unnecessary, or in
violation of the Student Body Finance Code.
3. Provide information and support to any organization, executive agency, bureau,
and funding board.
4. Meet monthly with the director or financial officer of executive agencies, affiliated
projects, bureaus, and funding boards to review monthly expenditure statements,
address questions and concerns, and discuss upcoming funding opportunities.
5. Assist the Student Body President in preparing the budget of the Executive
Branch.
6. Defend the Executive Branch budget in meetings with university administration,
funding boards, and external entities.
7. Chair the Organizational Fund.
8. Oversee the Programming Allocations Committee (PAC) and the Resource for
Travel Allocations Committee (RTAC).
9. Participate in the Campus Recreation Board and other relevant committees as
needed.
10. Chair the College Leadership Council (CLC) Funding Committee.
11. Serve as an ex-officio member of the Budget Commission.
12. Ensure accurate tracking and reporting of the Executive Branch budget and
expenditures.
13. Oversee the allocation of funds for Executive Branch projects to ensure
alignment with the goals and priorities of the student body.
14. Manage the Executive Projects Fund and the Campus Development Fund,
ensuring proper allocation and oversight.
15. Compile a list of all expenditures that the Treasurer signs, approves, or rejects
and forward it to the SGA Accounting Office, the Student Senate President, the
Senate Finance Committee, and other relevant parties. This list shall be sent to
the Student Senate and the Senate Finance Committee by the first of each
month.
16. Conduct regular audits of SGA financial activities to ensure transparency and
accountability.
17. Review the financial manual periodically and provide official recommendations
for reforms or updates to ensure compliance with applicable regulations and
enhance financial management practices.
18. Expenditures rejected by the Treasurer may be appealed to the Student Body
President, Senate Finance Committee, or the Student Senate. A two-thirds (2/3)
vote by the Senate Finance Committee or the Student Senate is required to
overturn a rejection.
19. If the Treasurer is unavailable to approve or reject an expenditure within two (2)
business days, the Student Body President or Vice President shall have the
power to approve or reject the expenditure.Docusign Envelope ID: 690673CF-E8A6-4E06-BB66-106A56E9DCC4

2024-02 - Section 10: Departmental Relationship
A. Purpose and Responsibilities:
1. Enhance student experience and representation through relationships with
university entities. The Student Body President shall meet with departmental
heads and faculty at the start of the term to establish collaboration and
communication. The President shall direct team members to maintain these
relationships or serve as liaisons with the departments.
B. Departmental Collaborations:
1. University Health Services: Develop health initiatives and promote services;
engage with CHAW, Medical Response Unit, and the Live Well Campaign.
2. Student Support and Transitions: Collaborate with Case Management, Food
Pantry, and Victim Advocate for student support.
3. FSU Police Department: Partner on safety programs, conduct safety audits, and
provide emergency preparedness training.
4. Office of Accessibility Services: Advocate for accessibility, ensure ADA
compliance, and support students with disabilities.
5. Sustainable Campus: Collaborate on environmental programs, sustainability
campaigns, and green initiatives.
6. Student Affairs: Develop programs for leadership, activities, and mental health
services.
7. Governmental Relations: Coordinate advocacy efforts, track legislation, and
engage with policymakers.
8. Athletics Department: Promote sports involvement, enhance athlete support, and
collaborate on events.
9. FSU Marketing Team: Develop marketing campaigns, enhance social media
presence, and ensure consistent messaging.
10. C.A.R.E.: Develop academic support programs, mentor students, and improve
retention for first-generation students.
11. University Libraries: Promote services, collaborate on study programs, and
support research.
12. Academic Center for Excellence (ACE): Support academic initiatives and provide
student resources.
13. The Globe and Multicultural Engagement: Advocate for global engagement,
provide cultural programs, and support international students.
14. Student Finance: Offer financial education, manage aid, and address concerns.
15. TAPS: Address transportation and parking, promote sustainable options, and
enhance mobility.
C. Communication Guidelines:
1. Professionalism: Conduct communications respectfully and professionally with
formal language.
2. Authority: Speak within scope of authority and clarify roles before discussions.
3. Response Times: Make a good faith effort to respond within five business days,
acknowledge immediately, and provide a timeline for full responses.
4. Documentation: Maintain detailed records of all communications and store
securely.
5. Scheduled Meetings: Schedule regular meetings with key contacts, document,
and follow up on action items.
6. Transparency: Communicate SGA goals, priorities, and limitations openly and
provide updates to university partners.
2024-02 - Section 11: Committee AppointmentsDocusign Envelope ID: 690673CF-E8A6-4E06-BB66-106A56E9DCC4

sections.text:
A. General Provisions
1. Appointees to University committees shall uphold the principles of
professionalism, accountability, and transparency. They are responsible for
representing the interests of the student body and ensuring effective
communication between the committees and the Executive Branch.
B. Oversight of Committee Appointments
1. Committee appointments are a responsibility of the Executive Branch, overseen
by the Student Body President or their designee. The Student Body President
shall ensure appointees are properly oriented and supported in their roles.
C. Attendance and Participation
1. Appointees must attend all scheduled committee meetings punctually.
2. Active participation in discussions and decision-making processes is required.
3. Preparation for meetings by reviewing agendas and relevant materials is
mandatory.
4. Excessive absences may result in revocation of committee appointments.
D. Documentation and Reporting
1. Appointees shall record detailed notes from each meeting, including key
discussion points, decisions made, and action items.
2. A good faith effort shall be made for a concise summary of the meeting minutes
to be submitted to the Executive Branch within 48 hours after each meeting.
a. Reports must include:
(1) Summary of meeting minutes.
(2) Notes on significant discussions or decisions.
(3) Action items assigned to members.
(4) Issues requiring Executive Branch attention or intervention.
(5) Reports must be formatted as a single document and submitted via email
to the Chief of Staff and Deputy Chief of Staff.
E. Communication Guidelines
1. Maintain professionalism in all communications.
2. Do not speak on issues beyond the appointee's scope of authority.
3. Use respectful and appropriate language in all communications.
4. Maintain open communication with the Chief of Staff and Deputy Chief of Staff,
addressing concerns or suggestions to improve committee functions.
F. Committee Descriptions and Expectations
1. Academic Honor Policy Committee (AHP)
a. The AHP Committee monitors the Academic Honor Policy and
collaborates with the Faculty Senate and Student Senate to educate
the community on academic integrity. Appointees are expected to
report on the policy's effectiveness and recommend any necessary
changes.
2. Admissions Committee
a. This committee rules on special admission cases and advises on
general admissions policies. Appointees must report on the cases
reviewed and any changes to admissions policies.
3. Alcohol & Other Drugs and Hazing Taskforce
a. Addressing issues related to alcohol, drugs, and hazing on campus,
this taskforce requires appointees to report on initiatives and policies
implemented to combat these issues.
4. Calendar CommitteeDocusign Envelope ID: 690673CF-E8A6-4E06-BB66-106A56E9DCC4

sections.heading: Page 10
sections.text:
a. Responsible for recommending the academic calendar annually,
appointees must report on proposed changes to the calendar and
their implications for students.
5. College Leadership Council Funding Committee
a. This committee distributes funding to student-led College Leadership
Councils. Appointees must report on funding decisions and
deliberations regarding funding levels.
6. Committee on Campus Names
a. The committee reviews and recommends changes to campus names.
Appointees are expected to report on naming decisions and proposals
under consideration.

a. This committee selects speakers and promotes the Golden Torch
Lecture Series. Appointees must report on speaker selections and
event planning.

a. Providing guidance on IT policies and projects, appointees must
report on IT initiatives and decisions regarding technology policies.

a. This committee recommends changes to student fees. Appointees are
expected to report on fee change proposals and their potential impact
on students.

a. Responsible for distributing funding for technology projects,

2024-02 - Section 12: Board of Trustees
A. General Provisions
1. The Executive Branch, specifically the Student Body President and Vice
President, shall maintain open and professional communication with the Board of
Trustees to ensure the effective representation of student interests.
B. Oversight and Communications
1. The Student Body President, or their designee, shall oversee all interactions with
the Board of Trustees to ensure the effective representation of student interests.
C. Composition and Role
1. The Florida State University Board of Trustees is a 13-member governing board
responsible for setting policy and managing the institution's resources. The Board
includes six members appointed by the Governor, five members appointed by the
Florida Board of Governors, the Chair of the Faculty Senate, and the President of
the Student Body.
D. Attendance and ParticipationDocusign Envelope ID: 690673CF-E8A6-4E06-BB66-106A56E9DCC4

sections.heading: Page 11
sections.text:
1. The Student Body President must attend all Board of Trustees meetings.
2. The Vice President shall provide reports to the Board as necessary.
3. Active participation in discussions and decision-making processes is required.
4. Preparation for meetings by reviewing agendas and relevant materials is
mandatory.
E. Reporting
1. Detailed notes must be taken during each Board meeting, including key
discussion points, decisions made, and action items.
2. A good faith effort shall be made for a concise summary of the meeting minutes
shall to be submitted to the Executive Branch after each meeting.
3. Reports must include:
a. Summary of meeting minutes.
b. Notes on significant discussions or decisions.
c. Action items assigned to members.
d. Issues requiring Executive Branch attention or intervention.
F. Trustee Biographies and Meeting Agendas
1. Trustee Biographies: Detailed biographies of the Board members can be found
on the official Board of Trustees page.
2. Meeting Agendas: Agendas for upcoming Board meetings are available on the
Board of Trustees website.
G. Student Government Reports to the Board
1. Previous reports from the Student Government to the Board can be found in the
SGA archives.
2. Current Reports: Current year's reports, including outlines and presentations, are
maintained in the SGA document repository.
2024-02 - Section 13: Accountability and Progress Reports
A. General Provisions:
1. To ensure transparency and accountability within the Executive Branch, the
Executive Office of the President shall design an internal accountability and
progress reporting system.
2. This system shall be reviewed at the beginning of each new administration and
revised to accommodate the goals of the Student Body President, Student Body
Vice President, and Student Body Treasurer.
2024-02 - Section 14: Conduct Policies
A. General Provisions
1. The Executive Branch is committed to maintaining a professional and respectful
environment. All members are expected to adhere to high standards of conduct.
B. Interpersonal Conduct
1. Respect: All members must treat each other with respect and professionalism.
2. Collaboration: Encourage a collaborative and supportive work environment.
3. Communication: Maintain clear and open communication channels.
C. Harassment and Discrimination
1. Zero Tolerance: The Executive Branch has a zero-tolerance policy towards
harassment and discrimination of any kind.
2. Reporting: Any incidents must be reported immediately to an SGA faculty
member.
3. Investigation: All reports will be investigated promptly and confidentially.
4. Consequences: Appropriate disciplinary action will be taken against those found
guilty of harassment or discrimination.
D. Conflict ResolutionDocusign Envelope ID: 690673CF-E8A6-4E06-BB66-106A56E9DCC4

sections.heading: Page 12
sections.text:
1. Mediation: Conflicts should be resolved through mediation facilitated by the Chief
of Staff or an appointed mediator.
2. Documentation: All conflicts and resolutions must be documented.
3. Follow-Up: Regular follow-ups will be conducted to ensure the conflict has been
resolved effectively.
2024-02 - Section 15: Executive Bureau And Agency Operations
A. Purpose:
1. Agencies within the Student Government Association (SGA) are programmatic
divisions of the Executive Branch designed to support and educate specific identity
groups within the Florida State University (FSU) Student Body. Membership is
open to all students, ensuring no one is denied participation based on race, creed,
color, religion, national origin, age, ability, veteran’s or marital status, sexual
orientation, gender identity, gender expression, or any other protected group
status. Committed to fostering an inclusive environment, agencies celebrate
diversity and encourage all students to engage in their activities, contribute to their
objectives, and benefit from their resources. The Uniform Agency Act of 2023, fully
binding upon enactment, standardizes the operation and management of these
agencies, ensuring consistency and transparency. Each agency adopts its own
internal Rules of Procedure, in compliance with the Student Body Constitution and
Statutes, to detail its organization, administration, and general operations without
requiring Senate approval for policy adoption or revision.
B. The supervision and regulation of the agencies is the responsibility of the Student Body
Vice President.
C. Each Agency shall, at minimum, have the following Executive Board members who shall
be appointed in the manner specified in Section 304(6), unless otherwise delineated by
the Agency’s Rules of Procedure.
1. The Director, Assistant Director, Treasurer, and Secretary.
D. Agency Meetings:
1. All meetings of Executive Agencies, and events held thereof, shall be open to all
members of the Florida State University Student Body and remain compliant with
the Florida State University Student Body Statutes.
E. Executive Board Meetings:
1. The Executive Board of each Agency shall meet at least once per month. The
meetings must be publicized, a quorum must be present to conduct business, and
minutes must be taken and posted to the SGA website.
F. General Body Meetings:
1. General body meetings shall be held at least once per semester, with the date and
time of each meeting advertised to the public at least forty-eight (48) hours in
advance of the designated meeting time.
G. Affiliate Organizations:
1. Affiliate Membership is available to all Recognized Student Organizations (RSOs)
that have an interest in contributing to an Agency’s mission statement.
H. Monetary Allocations:
1. Pursuant to the A&S Fee Guidelines, the Student Senate shall be the allocation
and revisionary authority in all budgetary matters pertaining to agencies.
2. The Student Body Treasurer shall be responsible for the financial responsibility of
Executive Agencies. All expenditures of agencies must be approved and have the
signature of the Agency's Director and Treasurer before all purchase requests are
submitted to the SGA Accounting Office. After the SGA Accounting OfficeDocusign Envelope ID: 690673CF-E8A6-4E06-BB66-106A56E9DCC4

sections.heading: Page 13
sections.text:
approves the expenditures, it must be sent to the Student Body Treasurer for
approval or rejection.
I. There shall be a committee known as the “Council of Presidents”.
1. The directors of each agency shall be required to attend Council of President’s
meetings.
2. The Council of Presidents will be chaired by the Student Body Vice President or
their designee.
3. The Student Body Vice President may appoint up to 2 ex-officio members to the

J. There shall be an advisory committee within OGA called the OGA Agency Advisory
Committee.
1. Members shall be appointed pursuant to internal policy procedure.
K. A designee from each agency shall serve on the Garnet and Gold Voting Commission.
1. Members shall be appointed pursuant to internal policy procedure.

701.1 The following words and phrases, when used in this title shall be defined as
follows:
A. Campaigning – The distribution of campaign materials, use of
campaign materials, or the solicitation of support for or against a
ballot item, political party, and or candidate for an elected office
of the Student Body. Campaigning shall begin the Wednesday at
12 a.m. Eastern Time, one week prior to the Election Day.
1. Solicitation of support shall be defined as publishing the
name or likeness of any candidate or political party to
expressly advocate the election or of defeat of a
candidate; that cannot be interpreted as something other
than an appeal to vote, through publishing, for or against
a specific candidate.
2. Nothing in this Election Code shall be construed as to
prohibit a candidate who has been formally approved
for candidacy from stating what office the candidate is
running for.
B. Electronic Communication – campaigning through any transfer of
signs, signals, writing, images, sounds, data, or intelligence of
any nature transmitted in whole or in part by a wire, digital, radio,
computer, cellular or wireless device.
C. Campaign Contribution - The gift or furnishing of money,
materials, supplies, professional services, or any in-kind
contribution to any campaign in any form.
D. Campaign Expenses - The fair market value of any goods or
services paid for or received by the campaign for the purpose
of advertising candidates, advertising political parties during
campaigning, violation penalties accrued during an election,
and/or calling for the action to vote. This shall include setup or
production fees, sales tax, or any other secondary costs for
goods and services.
1. Discounted items that are available to all persons and
political parties at the time of purchase shall be
exempted from fair market value criterion.
2. This section shall not be construed to apply to
speakers, volunteers, and other campaign workers of
a purely voluntary, unpaid nature.
3. To question the “fair market value” of a good or service
declared by a candidate or party, the questioning party
must obtain and submit an affidavit from the contractor or
merchant in question disputing the candidate or party’s
claim of fair market value, when such claims understatesDocuSign Envelope ID: A6664DDA-F8A2-4AB3-AD8F-30732A40F41C

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
fair market value.
E. Campaign Materials - any material, including but not limited to
paid social media advertisements, electronic communication,
videos, posters, placards, signs, signboards, leaflets, folders,
handbills, fliers, banners, t-shirts, buttons, paint, University
owned walls that may be painted on, handwritten
announcements or circulars of any size and consistency that
publicize a political party or candidate for an elected office of the
student body, and calling the action to vote.
F. Candidate - Any student seeking to be elected as an
officer of the Student Government Association.
G. Declaration of Candidacy - Filing of intent to run for
elected office with the Supervisor of Elections.
H. Five Week Period – the three weeks prior to the date of
elections and two weeks after the date of elections.
I. Independent Candidate - Any candidate who is not running with a party.
J. Official Ballot - The medium used by which a vote is recorded.
K. Political Party - Any number of persons properly registered with
the Supervisor of Elections, working together to establish,
promote, or gain acceptance for some kind of government
cause, opinion, etc., which they hold in common.
L. Electorate - The electorate shall be the entire registered student
body at FSU. The electorate shall be divided into divisions and
special seats. Only those enrolled in a specific division may vote
for Senate or COGS candidates seeking to represent that
division. Only those enrolled in the Senior Class shall be
eligible to vote for candidates seeking office in the Senior Class
Council. All students registered for classes during the election
may vote for candidates for campus-wide elected offices, as
well as for Constitutional Amendments and Referenda.
M. General Election: Bi-annual election held for the purpose of
determining the candidate who shall assume office. There shall
be two General Elections per year, one in the fall semester and
the other in the spring.
N. Special Election - an election held at any time other than a
General Election for any purpose.
O. Division – shall be defined as academic colleges and
schools as reported by institutional research.
P. Certificate of Election - A document certifying that aDocuSign Envelope ID: A6664DDA-F8A2-4AB3-AD8F-30732A40F41C

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
candidate has been duly elected.
Q. Final Expense Statement - A document listing all financial
expenditures or contributions in regards to fees and/or
donations. All receipts of expenditures, all banks statements
and their proper relatives, deposit slips, and other
documentation recording expenses and donations received are
part of the Final Expense Statement. The following shall also be
considered part of the Final Expense Statement:
1. A statement of the cumulative campaign
expenditures based on the fair market value, signed
by the candidates and/or party chairman.
2. An itemized list of all expenses.
3. A signed statement provided by the Supervisor of
Elections attesting to the validity of the total campaign
expenses and contributions, and that all campaign
contributions were collected in accordance with student
body statutes.
3. An itemized report containing the full name, residence or
business address of each person who has made one or
more contributions in any form to the campaign.
4. Campaign Contribution Statement, a copy of all account
statements, check stubs, deposit slips, and any other
financial documents shall be submitted on the first
Wednesday of campaigning by 12:00 p.m. as well as in
the candidate for party’s final expense statement.
R. Filing shall be defined as completing the proper form of
candidate filing or paperwork required by the specific statute.
Submission of a candidacy declaration form shall count as filing
to run as a candidate in an election. In the case of a requirement
to file when the election office is closed, unoccupied, or
otherwise unable to serve the students, the submission of an
electronic mail copy with all required information may substitute
for a paper form. The elections office shall work toward having
an on-line filing form where data may be entered on the elections
website. Should such a system be developed, submission shall
count as filing. If some additional documentation cannot be
submitted electronically, the Supervisor of Elections is
empowered to request such documentation within a reasonable
amount of time from the person who filed electronically.
S. Unofficial election results – the election results announced in
Senate and posted in the SGA offices and on the SGA website.
T. Final election results – all votes of an election that have beenDocuSign Envelope ID: A6664DDA-F8A2-4AB3-AD8F-30732A40F41C

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
verified by the Office of Elections as outlined by 711.4.
U. Official election results – the final election results after all final
expense statements have been approved and there are no
outstanding appeals and/or alleged violations.
V. Campaign Contribution Statement – Shall be defined as a copy
of bank account statements, check stubs, deposit slips, receipts
of both campaign expenses and campaign materials as defined
in 701.1 D and 701.1 E, respectively, up to the date of
submission and any other financial documents which shall be
submitted by 12:00
p.m. on the first Wednesday of campaigning and in the candidate or
party’s final expense statement. This shall be submitted on a form
prescribed by the Supervisor of Elections.
W. Internal Data System – Data collective by a candidate or
political party used to contact their party officers, their
candidates, or the electorate through electronic
communication on an electronic form created by the
Supervisor of Elections.
X. A Business Day – Shall be defined as a day during which the
SGA Advising and Accounting Office is open.
Y. Election Cycle – When Title VII goes into force for an election
until the Supervisor of Elections’ deadline for filing violations
according to 711.4J. The Election Cycle begins at the start of
the academic semester and ends the day that Inauguration
for that semester is held.
Z. Advertisement – Shall be identified as notice or
announcement in a public medium promoting a candidate of
political party in which a monetary transaction is made or
considered a campaign material.
1. Organic social media engagement shall not be
considered as a form of advertisement.
2. Non-candidate or non-dues paying political party
members’ posts shall not be considered
advertisements.
AA. Free equal time – Shall be defined as providing equivalent
opportunity for advertising to any opposing political candidates
who request it.
BB. Organic Social Media – The free-of-cost posts, photos, videos,
memes, stories, etc. that Social Media users share with each
other on their feeds.DocuSign Envelope ID: A6664DDA-F8A2-4AB3-AD8F-30732A40F41C

Chapter 415 Senate Legislative Certification Program
History: Added by the 54th Senate Bill 40. Deleted by the 56th Senate Bill 27. Added by
the 71st Senate Bill 19.
415.1 Purpose
This act is to establish a program administered by the Student Senate Pro
Tempore for students who are neither currently nor former members of the FSU
Student Senate who are interested in gaining knowledge of how the Senate
operates through first-hand experiences.
415.2 Name
The name of this program shall be “The Senate Legislative Certification Program.”
415.2 415.3 Administration of Program
The Senate Pro Tempore shall create an application and make it available to
students on the SGA website each semester the program is offered. The Senate
Pro Tempore shall have discretion over which applicants are to be admitted to the
program. The Senate Pro Tempore shall be responsible for holding an orientation
session for admitted applicants to explain the program and answer questions they
may have.
415.3 Professional Development Requirement
The Senate Pro Tempore shall develop a requirement which will help each
candidate develop professional skills.
415.4 Certification Requirements
A. Each candidate enrolled in the Student Senate Certificate Program shall
complete the following requirements:
1. Attend three (3) Student Senate meetings and take notes about
each meeting.
2. Attend three (3) committee meetings and take notes about each
meeting.
a. A candidate must attend the meeting of at least two (2)
different committees, to include no less than one standing
committee meeting.
3. Complete the Professional Development Requirement as
developed and given to the candidates by the Senate Pro
Tempore.
4. 3. Participate in writing a bill or resolution.DocuSign Envelope ID: 16A5DEB1-0EE1-4A66-BFFA-E266EED0AABA

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
5. 4. Meet with a Senate liaison to discuss their role as a liaison and
how they serve the campus entity they are a liaison to.
6. 5. Meet with the Senate Pro Tempore after all other requirements
have been completed to discuss the experiences had through this
program.
415.5 Verification of a Candidate’s Completed Requirements
A. Each candidate shall notify the Senate Pro Tempore upon their completion
of all requirements of the program from the certificate, and the Pro
Tempore shall verify that all requirements have been completed.
1. If the Pro Tempore finds that a candidate has not successfully
completed all requirements by the end of the semester that
candidate is enrolled in this program, that candidate shall not
receive a certificate of completion as outlined in Student Body
Statute 415.5B.
B. Upon the Pro Tempore’s verification, the candidate shall be awarded a
certificate of completion of The Student Senate Certification Program at
the next student government inauguration.DocuSign Envelope ID: 16A5DEB1-0EE1-4A66-BFFA-E266EED0AABA

A. Purpose
The purpose of this chapter is to define and delineate the nature of the

An Institute is an annual Executive Project that is administered under the
auspices and supervision of the Executive Branch through changing
administrations.

A. Upon the receipt of applications for a vacant position in Student Government

807.6 RTAC and PAC Guidelines
A. Organizations which received funds in Student Academic Programs or any other A&S
Funding Board, Committee, or line item in the annual budget except for PAC, RTAC, or
Senate Projects shall be ineligible to receive funding from PAC or RTAC the same fiscal
year in which they receive other funding. This does not apply to RSOs that received
money from the organizational fund.
B. Fund Distribution Committees shall not meet during any summer semesters.
1. RSOs requesting funds to be used in May or June may request before the end
of the Spring semester.
2. RSOs requesting funds to be used after July 1 shall go directly to the Student
Senate to ask for money out of Senate Projects. At the conclusion of the
summer semester, the funds distributed to the RSOs out of Senate Projects
shall be reimbursed from the respective fund distribution committee via a
transfer bill up to $2,000 per Committee.
C. All organizations requesting funding must be financially certified prior to making 147
request. At least one financially certified officer must be present at the funding hearing.
D. Committees will meet on Monday or Tuesday of each week, pending requests from
RSOs.
1. The Chair shall send out a notice of meeting time and location to RSOs via
email. The notification must be sent out by the chair at least twenty-four (24)
hours prior to the meeting time.
E. All submissions must be made prior to 12:00 p.m. on the Friday before the hearing.
Submissions must include three (3) supporting/competitive quotes from approved
vendors for each category the RSO is requesting funds or, or must include sufficient
evidence, at the discretion of the Chair, of a satisfactory attempt to find three (3) or more
quotes. Requests in the category of contractual services may be exempted from this rule
if deemed necessary by the committee.
1. All requests must be submitted at least twenty-one (21) business days prior to
event or activity to receive funding from PAC and at least thirty (30) business
days prior to travel date to receive funding from RTAC. Any request submitted
after the aforementioned dates may still be considered for funding at the
discretion of the chair with the approval of the SGA Business Manager.
2. 2. All requests must be of a line item nature with quotes (clothing costs,
performer costs, reservation costs, equipment rental, facility rental, airline
ticket quotes, rental car quotes, hotel quotes, etc.), and a letter of explanation
of need attached to the request packet, along with an explanation of the
benefits to the student body in general.DocuSign Envelope ID: 686FB83A-EA7D-4C41-A653-E3A27A778323

900.7 The Bureaus
The following is a list of all SGA bureaus and corresponding chapter numbers that appear
in Title IX.
A. Chapter 906 - Office of Center for Participant Education
Chapter 906 Office of the Center for Participant Education
906.1 Creation and Purpose
A. Creation
This act shall create an bureau of the Student Government Association known as
the Center for Participant Education (CPE).
B. Purpose
1. CPE shall be a forum for progressive and alternative ideas on education,
politics, and the arts.
2. CPE shall provide an area where students and local citizens can initiate and
enact new programs that interest them.
3. CPE shall provide guest lectures, movies, classes, and other alternative
programs to traditional programs.
4. CPE shall provide these educational classes and programs without charging a
fee for instruction.
906.2 Membership
Participation is open to students, faculty, and staff of the Florida State University
and the Tallahassee community.
906.3 Board of Directors
A. Membership
The Board of Directors shall consist of five (5) students. The student members
shall be elected by the membership with the approval of the Student Body
President.
B. Powers and Duties
The Board shall:
1. Assist the Director in managing the budget.
2. Assist the Director in planning and maintaining procedural bylaws operations.
3. Approve or reject proposed course offerings.
4. Be responsible for the final approval of CPE programs and catalogue.
5. Ensure that CPE complies with all relevant provisions of Chapters 304 and
900 as well as Title VIII (the Finance Code).
6. Reflect the wishes of the general membership in all decisions possible.
906.4 Meetings
A. The Board of Directors shall hold a minimum of one (1) meeting per month during
the academic year.
B. No official action may be taken by the Board unless a quorum is present.
C. All meetings shall be publicly advertised.
D. All Board members shall be notified at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance of
the designated meeting.
E. The Director shall ensure that minutes are taken at all Board meetings. A file
containing the minutes of all past meetings shall be maintained.

1005.4 Executive Board
A. Membership
The Executive Board shall consist of the Director, Assistant Director,
Secretary, Treasurer, and Outreach Coordinator, Public Relations
Coordinator, and Professional Development Coordinator, and six (6)
Programming Coordinators.
B. Qualifications
The qualifications are as follows:
1. Students in good standing at FSU with a minimum 2.0 GPA
2. Have an interest in promoting and contributing to the
Hispanic/Latinx culture and community on campus
3. Have held at least one leadership position at a college level.
C. Selection and Term of Office
All applications for all positions will be opened in the Spring semester and
closed the second Friday last school day in February of March. Interviews
will be set by the current Executive Board once all applications have been
received.

The Director and Assistant Director shall be nominated with a
majority (50 percent plus 1) vote by the previous Executive Board
and one representative from each affiliate organization, and
appointed by the Student Body President. If a current Executive
Board Member is running for a position on the following year’s
Board, that individual may not be present at any interviews for the
position and shall not cast a vote.

Confirmation

applicants and forward nominees for Treasurer and Secretary to
the Student Senate for confirmation within two (2) weeks of the

officially take office upon Senate confirmation and serve for a full
academic year thereafter.

Chapter 303 The Executive Institutes
History: Added by the 67th Senate Bill 34.
303.1 Creation and Purpose
E. The Institutes
The following is a list of the SGA Executive Institutes and corresponding
section numbers that appear in Chapter 303:
1. Freshman Leadership Institute (Section 303.2)
2. Transfer Leadership Institute (Section 303.3)
3. Diversity and Inclusion Institute (Section 303.4)
303.4 Diversity and Inclusion Institute
A. Purpose
The Diversity and Inclusion (D&I) Institute is an 8-week program held in the Spring
semester dedicated to providing a space for students to fully understand the
range of diversity and multiculturalism, including but not limited to ability, socio-
economic, age, rural/urban, veterans, sexual orientation, ethnicity, race, gender
identity & expression, religion, and faith structures through workshops that are
focused on awareness, discussion and collaborative learning activities.
B. Program
1. Participant Selection
a. The application will be made available to prospective participants at least
three (3) weeks before the end of the Fall Semester and will close on the
last day of the Fall Semester.
b. The selection of the participants shall be conducted at the discretion of the
Executive Board.
2. Meetings
a. The D&I Institute shall meet once a week for the duration of the program
during the Spring Semester.
i. Additional meetings may be held at the discretion of the Director of
the D&I Institute to fulfill the purpose stated in 303.4 Section A.
C. Leadership Team Selection
1. DirectorDocuSign Envelope ID: 985B765F-DDAA-4FB8-A3EB-73E3C807F994

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
a. The Director of the D&I Institute shall be selected by the outgoing
Leadership Team.
i. The Leadership Team is defined as any officer
positions, including the Director, that has been
appointed by the Executive Branch to fulfill the stated
purpose in 303.4 Section A.
b. The application for the Director of the Diversity & Inclusion
Institute shall be made available on the Student Government
Association Website on the 1st Friday after Spring Break and close
two (2) weeks thereafter.
c. Once selected by the outgoing Leadership Team, the candidate will
then be forwarded to the Executive Branch for Student Senate
confirmation.
D. Responsibilities
The responsibilities of the Director shall include, but not be limited to the following:
1. Represent the interests of the Diversity & Inclusion Institute on the campus
of Florida State University in accordance to the stated purpose.
2. Be responsible for the effective operations of the Diversity & Inclusion
Institute.
3. Make and execute decisions on program structure, D&I Institute affiliated
events, finances, and other activities with the advice of the Leadership
Team, Student Body Vice President, and Student Program Coordinator.
4. Be financially certified for the fiscal year.
5. Recommend officer positions, to the Executive Branch, that are needed, in
order to fulfill the stated purpose in 303.4 Section A.
E. Removal from Office
1. If the Director fails to fulfill the stated purpose, it will be up to the discretion
of the Student Program Coordinator or Student Body Vice President to
determine whether the Director shall be removed from office.
F. Vacancies
1. If any vacancy occurs during the duration of the Diversity & Inclusion
Institute that is under the Director, the Executive Branch shall appoint a
person at the recommendation of the Director to fulfill the duties of said
position.
a. If the Director position becomes vacant, the Student Body
Vice President shall fill in as the presiding Director until a
new Director is selected.DocuSign Envelope ID: 985B765F-DDAA-4FB8-A3EB-73E3C807F994

8. Vacancies and Leaves of Absence
A. Junior and Sophomore Class Vacancies
In the event a seat on the JCC or SoCC, becomes vacant
