Whereas: On February 14th, 2018 at 3:18 PM an armed gunman entered Marjory Stoneman
Douglas High School and committed a despicable act that led to the death of seventeen (17)
students and staff and injured seventeen (17) others; and,
Whereas: “Five years ago, Parkland and Coral Springs lost 17 lives. 17 goodbyes that loved
ones didn’t know would be the last. An additional 17 people who were injured began the long
journey of healing. And two more were ultimately lost due to the unbearable pain and trauma.
We remember all 36 lives touched.”; and
Whereas: This senseless act of violence is the deadliest high school shooting in United States
history, and
Whereas: The Student Senate acknowledges that each victim of gun violence is a human
being, a functioning member of society, and a loved family member, and the impact they left on
this world will not be forgotten nor will their death be in vain, and
Whereas: The Seventy Fifth Student Senate at the Florida State University recognizes the lives
lost five years ago: Alyssa Alhadeff, 14; Martin Duque Anguiano, 14; Scott Beigel, 35; Nicholas
Dworet, 17; Aaron Feis, 37; Jaime Guttenberg, 14; Chris Hixon, 49; Luke Hoyer, 15; Cara
Loughran, 14; Gina Montalto, 14; Joaquin Oliver, 17; Alaina Petty, 14; Meadow Pollack, 18;
Helena Ramsay, 17; Alex Schachter, 14; Carmen Schentrup, 16; Peter Wang, 15, and
Whereas: “Every day, we work with them in our hearts and in their honor to end the epidemic of
gun violence in America,” and
Whereas: The Student Senate recognizes that the mental health of many students at Florida
State University and across the nation may still be adversely impacted by this senseless
tragedy, therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: We
honor these students’ memories, and encourage all members of the Florida State student body
to educate themselves on ways to recognize threats to their communities, and

Whereas: The Student Senate and Internal Affairs committee have long heard complaints

Resolution #: 26
Primary Sponsor: Maglin

Brewer, Brown, Burton, Carter, Casiple, Chatellier, Chehaitli, Crocker, Crusey, Dale, Diaz, Dos
Santos, Dlugos, DuChêne, Fineout, Folwell, Gummerman, Hansen, Humberg, Jones, Kariher,
King, Lewis, LoBianco, Mantilla, McMahon, Meunier, Patel, Pedraja, Pruim, Rivera, Salazar,
Seeger, Severy, St. Hilaire, Tevlin, Vollick, Walerio, Widmann
Whereas: College students are inherently at a higher risk for the development of mental health
complications due to the disruptions associated with attending college as well as exposure to
new stressors, substances, and experiences. Additionally, by twenty-five years of age, seventy-
five percent of people who will develop a mental disorder have had their first onset (Kessler et
al. 2005), and
Whereas: Prior to the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, the prevalence of Generalized Anxiety
Disorder (GAD) and Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) amongst undergraduate and graduate
students were fifteen to twenty-five percent and twenty-five to twenty-eight percent respectively
(Chirkov et al. 2020). After the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, those ranges of GAD and
MDD prevalence increased to thirty-one to thirty-nine percent and thirty-two to forty-eight
percent respectively (Soria et al. 2021). This increase in anxiety and depressive disorders is a
result of the emotional turmoil, isolation, and revocation of human experience caused by the
pandemic, and
Whereas: The maintenance of mental health is necessary for student advancement, retention,
and wellness. Florida State University offers a variety of mental health services, but awareness
and utilization of these services lacks across the student population. A variety of circumstances
can impede students’ ability to utilize these services, thus its efficacy is not fully potentiated.
Additionally, the number of students impacted by mental health issues severely outweighs the
number of mental health professionals available, therefore initiatives that impact the entire
student body should be considered to account for these limitations, and
Whereas: According to the Florida State University academic calendars, the Fall semesters
typically consist of seventy-five (75) days of classes and three (3) recognized class
cancellations. These cancellations are as follows: Labor Day (September 5th), Veteran’s Day
(November 11th), and Thanksgiving Break (November 23rd-27th). The Spring semesters
typically consist of seventy-nine (79) days of classes and two (2) recognized class cancellations.
These cancellations are as follows: Martin Luther King Jr. Day (January 16th) and Spring Break
(March 13th-17th), and
Whereas: During the Spring semesters, the first recognized class cancellation typically occurs
within the first two (2) weeks of classes. Thus, there are forty (40) consecutive school days
without reprieve, increasing the likelihood for mental and academic burnout during this period,
and
Whereas: The implementation of one additional recognized class cancellation into Florida State
University’s academic calendar dedicated to the prioritization of mental wellness, decided upon
by the appropriate administrative staff, during which all classes cease for undergraduate,DocuSign Envelope ID: 8C7615C5-A2FF-4BFC-B569-8D7984FB3625

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
graduate, and faculty populations would provide directly observable benefits to student and
faculty mental health, and
Whereas: The intention of this day is to prompt a university-wide advocacy and appreciation for
mental health. Class cancellation removes academic pressure as a stressor from undergraduate
and graduate students’ lives and allows students and faculty an opportunity to address any
outstanding mental, personal, or familial issues, and
Whereas: This day would not prompt university-wide closure, as transportation services, dining
locations, student spaces (Student Union, Campus Recreation facilities, etc.), the libraries, and
administrative staff would continue scheduled operation, and
Whereas: Amendments to the official Florida State University academic calendar cannot take
effect until at least a year after the change is enacted, thus all teaching faculty would receive
ample time and notification to adjust Spring teaching curriculums in response to the selected
calendar day, and
Whereas: Florida State University’s Panama City campus follows the academic calendar
established by Florida State University’s Tallahassee administration, so the undergraduate,
graduate, and faculty populations would cease courses held on the selected day, and
Whereas: Any changes to the official Florida State University academic calendar must be
communicated with the appropriate administration at Florida Agricultural and Mechanical
University via the Registrar offices to account for the students at both universities within the
FAMU-FSU College of Engineering. The Registrar offices of both Florida State University and
Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University meet annually to accommodate the needs of the
College of Engineering and account for any changes to each university’s schedule. The
implementation of this university-wide day for mental wellness will need to be communicated
between the Registrar offices so that courses for undergraduate, graduate and faculty
populations within the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering are effectively canceled on the
selected day, and
Whereas: The professional graduate programs within the Colleges of Law and Medicine
operate under academic calendars that differ from the general undergraduate and graduate
populations, thus it shall be up to the discretion of the administration within these programs and
the university Registrar office to determine if annual participation is appropriate, and
Whereas: Florida State University’s International Program campuses follow academic
calendars that are adjusted to best align with their residing country’s customs and program
needs. Therefore, it shall be up to the discretion of the administration within these programs to
determine if annual implementation and participation in this initiative is appropriate, therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: This
body strongly encourages the appropriate Florida State University administrative offices to
deliberate this request and consider the implementation of a university-wide class cancellation
dedicated to the advocacy, appreciation, and prioritization of mental wellness which would
produce observable, tangible benefits to overall student and faculty well-being at this University,
and
Be it further resolved that: In addition to removing academia as a stressor from students’
lives, this additional class cancellation produces an excellent opportunity for wellness-basedDocuSign Envelope ID: 8C7615C5-A2FF-4BFC-B569-8D7984FB3625

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
programming to take place on the selected day. Potential programming opportunities on the
selected day would center around mental health awareness, appreciation, and de-
stigmatization. Entities within Florida State University’s Student Government Association (i.e.,
Identity-Based Agencies, the Bureaus, the Executive Branch, etc.) and a variety of Registered
Student Organizations (RSOs) may work in conjunction with other facets of student life to
generate programming which would ultimately generate a larger sense of community on both
Panama City and Tallahassee campuses, and
Be it further resolved that: The mission of the Mental Health Council at Florida State
University is to “empower students with mental health resources through de-stigmatization,
community involvement, and advocacy” (Student Body Statutes, 915.1.C.). As the intention
surrounding programming for this proposed day aligns with the purposes outlined in the Florida
State University Student Body Statutes, primary organization of events, initiatives, and
programs will be annually led by the Mental Health Council, and
Be it further resolved that: This body urges Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University’s
Student Government Association to meet with their appropriate administration to begin
processes to enact their own university-wide mental wellness initiative to be determined in
conjunction with Florida State University’s administration to account for the Florida Agricultural
and Mechanical students within the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering. If this initiative is held
on the same day between Florida State University and Florida Agricultural and Mechanical
University, then logistical concerns regarding the College of Engineering will cease, as the
College will directly follow the changes to the academic calendars. Additionally, if enacted on
Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University’s campus, then Florida Agricultural and
Mechanical University’s and Florida State University’s Student Government Associations can
increase overall communication and accountability to annually work together to plan events and
initiatives that will bring the two universities together to appreciate and advocate for mental
health on the selected day, and
Be it further resolved that: In the event that Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University
cannot implement their own day for mental respite held in conjunction with Florida State
University, the students within the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering are up to the discretion of
appropriate academic administrators to decide if the university-wide class cancellation is
appropriate. If this is the case, mental-health-based programming will still be held at the FAMU-
FSU College of Engineering campus to promote mental health resources, awareness, and
advocation for these undergraduate and graduate students, and
Be it further resolved that: Student Senator, Isaiah Long, representing the Student
Government Council at Florida State University’s Panama City campus has written a statement
on behalf of the Student Government Council’s perspective on this initiative which reads:
“Members of the Florida State University Student Government Association Senate, I am writing
to express the support of the FSU Panama City Student Government Council for the Mental
Health Day resolution. We believe that mental health is a critical component of overall well-
being, and that prioritizing mental health awareness and resources is essential to ensuring the
success and happiness of our student body. As a branch of the larger FSU community, we
recognize the importance of taking action to promote mental health, particularly considering the
challenges and stresses faced by students in today's world. We believe that dedicating a day to
mental health awareness and education would be a valuable step in this direction. We
appreciate the efforts of the FSU Student Senate in advocating for this important issue and urge
you to continue to prioritize the well-being of our fellow students. I additionally, encourage the
FSU Student Senate to offer Zoom accommodations for future matters of FSU Panama City.DocuSign Envelope ID: 8C7615C5-A2FF-4BFC-B569-8D7984FB3625

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
Please feel free to contact us if we can be of any assistance on this matter. Go Noles, Isaiah
Long, Senator, 41st Student Government Council, Florida State University Panama City,” and
Be it further resolved that: If implemented, the Mental Health Council in conjunction with other
facets of student life will draft a contingency plan to be completed prior to the Spring of 2024
which would outline the logistics, funding allocations, events, and ideas for future Student
Government Association, Registered Student Organizations, and administrative leaders to

Be it further resolved that: The implementation of this day emphasizes the value that Florida

This initiative will create a longstanding legacy of community, understanding, and academic

Whereas: The mission of the Student Government Association (SGA) is to provide FSU
students with representation, services, and advocacy within the university structure. The SGA
provides quality leadership for, and accountability to, its constituency by recognizing that
strength arises from diversity, engagement, and dialogue, and
Whereas: Diversity, equity, and inclusion are all central pillars of a modern, world-class
education in the 21st century, and
Whereas: Through their rhetoric, political leaders in the State of Florida have, for months,
attacked, downplayed, and belittled the importance and impact that diversity, equity, and
inclusion have had in our society, and
Whereas: State Representative Alex Andrade has filed HB 999 in the Florida House of
Representatives, which would block Florida State University’s ability to “expend any funds,
regardless of source” on efforts to “promote, support, or maintain any programs or campus
activities that … espouse diversity, equity, and inclusion or Critical Race Theory rhetoric,” and
Whereas: This provision in the proposed legislation has the potential to wholly dismantle
entities promoted by Florida State University and this Student Government Association, which
have been the backbone of student life for decades, including the Center for Leadership &
Social Change, CARE, the RISE Office, and the Student Government agencies, including the
Asian American Student Union, Black Student Union, Hispanic/Latinx Student Union, Jewish
Student Union, Pride Student Union, Veterans Student Union, and Women’s Student Union, and
Whereas: This erasure would constitute an unprecedented attack on the minority communities
served by these entities, and would be a shameful step backwards in our efforts to form a united
community and Student Body, and
Whereas: This bill would also overhaul the educational standards for general education courses
by suppressing more nuanced views of events in American history while promoting ethnocentric
“philosophical underpinnings of Western civilization,” and
Whereas: This bill would take steps toward prohibiting state universities from offering majors or
minors in the fields of “critical race theory, gender studies, or intersectionality, or any derivative
major or minor of these belief systems,” and
Whereas: The changes made in the bill to the faculty hiring and tenure review process further
weaken academic freedom in Florida by threatening professors and the curricula they teach by
allowing for tenure review “at any time with cause,” andDocuSign Envelope ID: 480520F4-22F8-468C-8ABA-AF948BC6678F

sections.text:
Whereas: HB 999 specifically targets the Florida State University’s Institute of Politics (IOP) by
removing references to the Institute’s mission to “nurture a greater awareness of and passion
for public service and politics” and to “provide students with an opportunity to be politically active
and civically engaged” erode the purpose of the Institute, and
Whereas: The Institute of Politics is further made weaker in its purpose by removing its stated
intent to provide fellowships and internships to students interested in non-profit and community
organizations, and strictly limits IOP fellows to pursue internships in government through its
programming, and
Whereas: Student Body Statute 908.7(B) allows for the Student Senate to amend the Student
Body Legislative Agenda in conjunction with the Office of Governmental Affairs (OGA), therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Student Senate, in its efforts to live up to the Student Government’s motto of promoting “unity
and diversity,” condemns House Bill 999, as proposed in the 2023 Regular Session of the
Florida Legislature, in the strongest possible terms, and
Be it further resolved that: Pursuant to Student Body Statute 908.7(B), the 75th Student
Senate hereby amends the 2023 Student Body Legislative Agenda by stating its strong and
steadfast opposition to HB 999 for the aforementioned reasons, and
Be it further resolved that: In line with Resolution 15 of the 75th Student Senate, the Senate
reiterates its opinion that higher education is an opportunity for interested students to pursue
academia in a way that is expansive and exploratory in nature, and thus condemns any
attempts to limit instruction of the following topics: critical race theory, gender studies,

Be it further resolved that: As long as it is in operation, the Student Senate at Florida State
University will always stand with marginalized communities at Florida State University, and with
the entities across the breadth of this university that work tirelessly to support said communities,
and

Whereas: On March 7, 2023, Florida State Senator Erin Grall proposed Senate Bill 300,
“Pregnancy and Parenting Support”; and
Whereas: This bill outlines a near-complete ban on abortions that occur after six weeks of
gestation in the state of Florida, with exceptions for survivors of incest and rape, whose abortion
access is limited to occur before fifteen weeks of gestation; and
Whereas: This transgression of reproductive rights is just the latest in a long series of attacks
from a local, state, and national level, which started with the decision of the U.S. Supreme Court
case Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization, which overturned the historical
precedent set in Roe v. Wade that legalized abortion nationwide, and the Florida passage of the
“Reducing Fetal and Infant Mortality Act”, which banned abortions after fifteen weeks of
gestation; and

door for legislators to attempt to institute such bans, as can be seen through the archaic Senate
Bill 300; and
Whereas: Florida’s Constitution guarantees the right to privacy in Article I, Section 23, which
would seem to prohibit any bans such as the ones already passed and proposed; and
Whereas: The most effective way to reduce abortions does not come through the restriction of
reproductive freedoms, but rather through the expansion of access to contraceptives, which
sees far higher rates of success, according to the Guttmacher Institute; and
Whereas: Abortion bans disproportionately affect college students, as 42% of all abortions are
obtained by individuals aged 18-24, according to the Guttmacher Institute; and
Whereas: Abortion bans have been proven to decrease college enrollment, specifically for

training, encourage qualified faculty to discontinue their employment in anti-abortion states, and

Whereas: It is the duty of the Student Senate to defend the rights and wellbeing of students
with or without uteruses at Florida State University; and
Whereas: Although the Student Senate cannot directly introduce legislation on a state or
national level to alleviate the concerns that have resulted from recently proposed legislation andDocuSign Envelope ID: 89D7E59F-B995-4CD2-91DA-0A5109F6567F

court decisions, it can address the issues and urge lawmakers to consider the implications of

Whereas: In October of 2022, the City of Tallahassee Commission proposed an ordinance
change for the City of Tallahassee that would amend sections 12-93, 12-94, and 12-96 of the
Code of General Ordinances; and
Whereas: The proposed changes to the City Ordinances would allow Tallahassee Police
personnel to take necessary precautions to restrict audible noise from select establishments
after the hour of 11:00PM on Sunday through Thursday, and 12:00AM on Friday through
Saturday, regardless of circumstance; and
Whereas: The language of the amendment reads: “to restrict outdoor amplified sound which is
plainly audible 200 feet from the establishment”; and,
Whereas: The city of Tallahassee is home to three educational institutions, making the city the
home of over 54,000 college and university students; and
Whereas: The proposed amendments to the City of Tallahassee Code of General Ordinances
would heavily limit and restrict the operations of several bars, clubs, and restaurants (“nightlife”)
in the City of Tallahassee, as confirmed by the personal accounts of several employees and
managers of these establishments; and
Whereas: Tallahassee nightlife establishments employ almost exclusively FSU students,
helping many students pay for tuition, and other necessary personal expenses; and
Whereas: Florida State University is home to 54 total fraternities and sororities, whose
operations would also be limited and restricted by the proposed amendments to the City of
Tallahassee General Ordinances, as confirmed by the personal accounts of several members of
these esteemed organizations; and
Whereas: These Greek organizations regularly contribute to the betterment of the City of
Tallahassee through support of both local and national philanthropic efforts, city cleanups,
community engagement, social advocacy, and much more; and
Whereas: The area designated by the city code as the “Urban Core” is an area that a significant
portion of FSU students live, as well as an area with many Greek houses and nightlife
establishments; andDocuSign Envelope ID: 1DC9E96A-FD50-45E4-A198-0585BF87D522

from their reputations of being home to some of the largest and most prominent Greek
organizations and nightlife establishments in the nation, contributing to both tourism and a large

FSU Student Senate is sympathetic to the negative aspects that the proposed changes to the
Tallahassee City Ordinances for noise would have on FSU’s Greek organizations, Tallahassee’s
nightlife, and the FSU student body as a whole; and
Be it further resolved that: The FSU Student Senate formally opposes all proposed changes

Whereas: 2022 Florida Statute 1006.53 on Religious Observances delegates responsibility for

public postsecondary educational institution, and

shall, upon notifying their instructor as soon as possible upon receipt of the course syllabus, but

observe a religious holy observance of their faith,” and

observed holy days fall outside those deemed excused holidays per the University Calendar,

different faiths who are impacted negatively by the time-sensitive nature of this policy, therefore

weeks prior to the respective religious holy day in which they choose to request absence, and

Faculty Senate and all other administrative entities to support a change to this policy to only
require one week’s notice of absence before the holy day to promote accessibility to students of
all religious backgrounds, and

deaths each year, and
Whereas: Gun violence costs Florida $40.3 billion each year, of which $875.9 million is paid by

engaged community, and

Whereas: Since 1965, global production of sugar cane has quadrupled in scale, with two billion
metric tons of the crop being produced in recent years; and
Whereas: Harvesting sugar cane can be difficult due to the buildup of dried leaves at the base
of the sugar cane crop, which accumulates over the course of the season; and
Whereas: Sugar cane producers across the state of Florida resort to the burning of this leafy
material to simplify the farming process, leading to several issues in Floridian communities; and
Whereas: This “sugar cane burning” releases harmful particulate matter into the air, which
pollutes the Florida environment, rivalling even the amount of pollution created by automobiles,
with research done by Florida State University finding that sugarcane fires resulted in 5,100
metric tons of this particulate matter every year, whereas on-road motor vehicles in Florida
emitted about 6,100 metric tons every year; and
Whereas: Sugar cane burning has also been linked to environmental racism, with marginalized
communities being disproportionately affected by the burns, due to the proximity of many of
these communities to the burn sites and there being many more active burn permits in these
historically marginalized communities than in other parts of the state and area; and
Whereas: The particles produced by sugar cane burning negatively affects the life of all
residents in Florida, with the matter being linked to respiratory issues and exacerbating
conditions such as asthma and bronchitis, and directly leading to an estimated three deaths per
year; and
Whereas: There are many tried and tested alternatives to sugar cane burning, such as “green
harvesting”, which involves cutting sugar cane while it is still green for immediate processing, in
order to preserve the soil and air quality of our great state, among other methods; and
Whereas: Even though Florida’s cane sugar industry is the largest in the nation, producing a
two billion dollar economic impact to the state, the burning process leading to pollution and long-
term environmental damage, and disadvantaging already-marginalized communities, despite
there being safer and more environmentally-friendly alternatives, is a willful neglect of the
corporate responsibility to public wellbeing; therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Seventy-fifth Student Senate opposes the practice of sugar cane burning, and urges sugar cane
producers in Florida and the Florida government to explore other options to replace this
outdated practice.DocuSign Envelope ID: C99D1B5A-EB41-4B83-A38B-5CE87B83547A

fraction of her proficiency. The Student Body shall be forever changed due to Abril's stance as a
liaison between students, administration, and the Student Government Organization. It has
been an honor to meet her and observe her thrive in all facets of her life, and an even greater
honor to support her nomination for Senate Hall of Fame,” and
Whereas: Former Senator Cassidy Rider testifies: “Abril Hunter is the change she wants to see
in the world. She leads with such kindness and integrity because she knows the change, she
wants to create will help the world become a better place. Abril took a chance on me and helped
me learn who I was as a leader. Being a Senator while Abril was President was one of the most
enjoyable experiences of my college career. Abril created a safe and inclusive environment for
all of us Senators to get work done for the student body. Even on Abril’s busiest day she always
acted with such selflessness helping all Senators. Looking up to Abril and the extraordinary
change she made as Senate President was an honor. No one is more deserving of this award
than Abril Hunter. Her leadership has changed my life for the better and I can’t wait to see what
she does next,” and
Whereas: Dr. Craig Filar testifies: “Abril Hunter builds consensus, advocates for her positions
and her peers, and creates inclusive and collaborative environments and programs, as she
interacts effectively with students, with administrators, with faculty, even with policymakers and
politicians. She works tirelessly on behalf of the communities that she serves, without seeking
personal praise or recognition. Yet, her work has been recognized, receiving three prestigious
national scholarships: a Truman Scholarship, a Udall Scholarship, and a NOAA Hollings
scholarship, demonstrating the reach of the impact Abril has had during her time at FSU. I am
so proud of her and her accomplishments and am thankful to have had the last four years
working alongside her on her journey,” and
Whereas: Former Senator Gabriel Pfeuffer-Ferguson testifies: “Most of the people in this
chamber and on campus know Abril in many different ways. They see her as the intelligent
Truman and Udall Scholar who served as the Chair of FSU’s Presidential Scholars Program.
People think of the Homecoming Queen who bleeds Garnet and Gold while unconditionally
loving Florida State. Some people think of the student leader version of Abril where she served
her communities as an Executive Board member of both the Alliance for Black Women and the
Renegade Leadership Honor Society. Most know Abril as the best Senate President to ever
bless the chambers, where she led with compassion and diligence while maintaining highDocuSign Envelope ID: 0E775FD8-C765-48F2-9B3D-310CACE6205E

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
standards for herself and her senators. I get the blessing of knowing Abril as just herself. The
woman who brightens any room she walks into, shows empathy and kindness to anyone she
meets, and makes sure to go out of her way to leave a lasting impression on everyone she
comes across. There is nobody more deserving of joining the Senate Hall of Fame. Abril served
on multiple committees within the Senate Chambers, ran an Ad Hoc focused on promoting DEI,
stepped up as Summer Senate President Pro-Tempore, wrote legislation promoting better
environmental practices on our campus, and completely bodied the role of Senate President.
This campus is going to have a huge hole to fill once Abril leaves, and that speaks volumes on
her character and work. Abril, I personally want to thank you for dragging me into SGA. You
made the 6 hour nights worth it. Our trips to Taco Bell after Senate and the drives to the
Thomasville Road What-A-Burger are core memories for me. Our FaceTimes while on Zoom
where I would ask you what was going on and if the people on the call were genuinely ok were
some of my favorite talks with you. Your new outfits every week that proved to be hotter than
the previous one slayed the house boots down. You epitomized work hard and play hard by
bringing fun into the Senate Chambers. You truly are and will forever be known as the most
impactful Senate President Florida State University will ever have. I love you through time and
space, and then back,” and
Whereas: Former Senate Press Secretary Ashley Allen testifies: “I had the honor of working
alongside Abril Hunter within the 74th Student Senate, and there is no doubt in my mind that she
is the definition of a strong and true leader. She was dedicated to standing up for FSU’s
students, and she demonstrated kindness and compassion in every circumstance. I am so
proud of the person she has become, and I cannot wait to see what amazing things she will
accomplish in her life,” and
Whereas: Victoria Paul testifies: “President Abril Hunter has left a mark on the hearts and
minds of all who have had the pleasure of working with her. Her compassionate and innovative
spirit has led to transformative change on campus and beyond. President Hunter’s exceptional
leadership skills and unwavering commitment to excellence have set a new standard for what it
means to be a leader and will continue to motivate others for years to come. Honored to call her
my friend and sister, it is with great pleasure that I express my gratitude and appreciation for
President Hunter’s incredible leadership, impact, and friendship,” and
Whereas: Lindsey Wood testifies: “Since knowing Abril, I have continued to be astounded by
her heart, character, and determination. It is clear to everyone around her that Abril is intelligent
and hard-working, but Abril's work and accomplishments at our university can only begin to
illustrate all that she embodies. Abril is the epitome of leading by example, always inspiring
those around her to act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly. An intentional friend, a passionate
advocate, and an absolute shining light, to know Abril Noel Hunter is to love her, and I am
extraordinarily lucky to call her a best friend,” and
Whereas: Student Leader and Athlete Alexandria Hilton testifies: “Abril Hunter leads with poise
and preparedness. She demonstrates respect and love for everyone with whom she works and
to say she is bound for success would be stating the painfully obvious. She is a very special
human,” and
Whereas: Savannah Hill testifies: “Abril Hunter is a force to be reckoned with. She is a fierce
advocate for her communities and operates with candor and care. There is no doubt she has
made her mark on this university as a whole, but also on every individual who has had the
privilege of interacting with her. She is my closest confidant and the greatest friend one couldDocuSign Envelope ID: 0E775FD8-C765-48F2-9B3D-310CACE6205E

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
have. There is no one more deserving of this honor. Abril serves her spheres of influence with
her whole heart and shines a glimmer of light on all who pass her,” and
Whereas: Mallory Mallman testifies: “Abril Hunter is an amazing leader and my best friend. She
is incredibly hard-working, dedicated, and kind. Abril truly cares about helping people and
changing the world for the better. She goes above and beyond in every aspect of her life. Her
work in Student Government has been invaluable to this campus. It has been such a joy over
these past four years to watch her grow. I have no doubt that she will accomplish anything she
sets her mind to,” and
Whereas: Lana Alexis testifies: “I have known Senator Hunter for less than a year. However, it
has been more than a pleasure to get to know her. She has tremendous accomplishments that
most people can only dream of having. Being around her has made me work harder in every
aspect of my life, whether school, work, or our sorority. Senator Hunter, without a doubt, wants
the best for everyone; she is not only a fantastic member of Zeta Phi Beta Sorority, Inc, but a
reliable and loyal friend. I consider Senator Hunter to be a sister to me. I cannot wait to see
what she does in the future. I do not doubt that whatever she accomplishes will be monumental.
I am saddened to see her go after knowing her so briefly. However, our sisterhood is a lifetime. I
am pleased to call Senator Hunter my friend and sister. I would like to wish Senator Hunter the
best of luck,” and
Whereas: Alexander Chang testifies: “I’ve known Abril since our first days at FSU and seeing
how far she has come as a woman, student, friend, scholar, and leader has been the privilege
of a lifetime. Abril has contributed so much to almost every area of our campus and does it all
with a kind, generous heart. It is specifically in her role as Senate President that I have seen her
make a profound impact. Within your chambers you fostered a culture of respect and love for
one another and not only recognized each senator’s hard work, but also celebrated each other’s
character and personalities. Your devotion to your leadership has built a legacy on the Senate
floors will be felt long after you have graduated. I cannot think of anymore more deserving of tis
accolade than you so congratulations President Hunter. You deserve the world,” therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: Former
Senator Abril Hunter is nominated to the Student Senate Hall of Fame, and is applauded for her
honorable service to Florida State University and to the Student Senate thereof, and
Be it further resolved that: A copy of this resolution be sent to:
Abril Hunter, President of the 74th Student Senate at Florida State University
OFFICIAL: _________________________________________________________
Student Senate President
Senate Vote: 50-1-1
PASSED: April 5th, 2023DocuSign Envelope ID: 0E775FD8-C765-48F2-9B3D-310CACE6205E

sections.heading: Page 1
sections.text:
75th STUDENT SENATE
Senate Resolution
Resolution #: 40
Primary Sponsor: Diaz, DuChêne
Co-Sponsor(s): Anderson, Barrett, Bettley, Boisvert, Brewer, Casiple, Chehaitli, Crocker, Dale,
Fineout, Folwell, Kariher, Mantilla, Patel, Pedraja, White, Widmann, Wyatt
Whereas: Student Body Statute 413.8 states, “Membership in the Senate Hall of Fame is the
highest honor a student Senator can achieve. This honor shall be bestowed upon any Senator
who has performed their duty as a member of the Senate with the highest standard of
excellence, beyond that normally expected of a Senator at the Florida State University,” and
Whereas: Sarah Nemeth served as a Senator representing the Division of Undergraduate
Studies, and later, the College of Social Sciences & Public Policy from the Fall of 2020 until Fall
2022, having served as a member of the 2021 Rules of Procedure Ad Hoc (ROPAH) committee,
Vice Chair of the Student Life & Academic Affairs committee, and as President Pro-Tempore of
the 74th Student Senate, and
Whereas: Senate President Samuel Diaz testifies: “Pro-Tempore Nemeth is an example for
each of us in this chamber to look up to. Each week, she would come to the Senate with grace
and a radiance about her that would light up the room. The effort she put into the job of being
our President Pro-Tempore did not go unnoticed, and she truly set an example for me of what
an effective Senator and Senate leader should look like. I greatly appreciate her friendship, the
support she’s given me in my role, and for the example she set for us all. It is an honor to hold
the seat that used to be hers, and I could not recommend her highly enough for this award” and
Whereas: Senate President Pro-Tempore Patrick DuChêne testifies: “Sarah Nemeth, among
many other things, is someone who cares. In both her personal relationships and her
professional responsibilities Sarah has exhibited only the utmost care. I have lived this first-
hand. When I entered the 73rd Student Senate, I must admit that I expected high drama. I
expected divisive party politics and cold polarization. Sarah Nemeth proved this theory wrong
for me. From different campus backgrounds and, indeed, different parties, Sarah turned my
entire theory of SGA on its head. She represented someone who could give her utmost
dedication to her involvements without forsaking the personal relationships around her. The
colours I wore on election day were not a prerequisite to her friendship. Sarah, thank you for
being a friend - to me and to Sam. Thank you for always going above and beyond. Thank you
for setting an example for what a strong, active, engaged Senator is. Thank you for showing me
what an ideal Pro-Tempore looks like. There's no one I'd rather follow in the Student Life to Pro-
Tempore pipeline,” and
Whereas: Senator Hannah Carter testifies: “Sarah is a light on Florida State’s campus. She
continuously works to make others feel more confident in their abilities by investing her time and
energy into their success. As one of the most welcoming and dedicated individuals to enter the
Senate chambers, I can think of no other who is more deserving of this honor,” and
Whereas: Senator Autumn Anderson testifies: “Sarah Nemeth is an outstanding and exemplary
member of the Florida State Community. Upon first time meeting her she was extremely warm
and welcoming. I had the pleasure to work with her not only within Senate but as a RecruitmentDocuSign Envelope ID: D1EAB56A-7A7D-4E46-B513-521A66B55D73

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
Counselor, and I can say with full confidence that she puts her 100% effort into everything she
does. She is extremely deserving and I am thankful to know her,” and
Whereas: Senator Kyle Casiple testifies: Sarah Nemeth is one of the most passionate student
leaders I've come across on Florida State's campus. Through her work as Pro-Tempore she has
touched so many individuals and created a space where Senators feel invited and always
challenged to grow. As a Senator in the 74th Senate, Sarah was an extremely integral part to my
growth as a Senator and leader. Sarah's impact has reached even further than these Senate
Chambers and I'm so excited to see where she goes in the future,” and
Whereas: Senator Megan Bettley testifies: “Serving in Senate with Sarah as Pro-Tempore was
always such a joy. Sarah radiates such happiness and positivity, and she really helped turn
Senate into a more welcoming environment. I always knew that I could come to her with any
concerns, and she would help me in any issue I faced. She is an excellent leader, an inspiration
to many, and someone I am honored to call her a friend. Good luck with all of your endeavors
Sarah, I know you’ll do amazing things,” and
Whereas: Student Leader Kaitlynn Adams testifies, “Sarah Nemeth is a steadfast, servant
leader who brings ambition, compassion, and innovation in every position she occupies inside
and outside the chambers. In every space she is involved in Sarah is dedicated to empowering
the next generation of women leaders and is intentional in leaving a legacy that paves the way
for the campus community to reach new heights. Her vision, passion, and loyalty to everything
she does continue to inspire me and I am immensely grateful to call Sarah my colleague and
friend,” and
Whereas: Former Senator Sara Weintraub testifies: “Sarah Nemeth is one of the most
passionate and dedicated people I know. She is deeply committed to advocating for others in
and outside of SGA. Aside from her extensive list of accomplishments in this body, she is
respected for leading with integrity and kindness. Sarah truly demonstrates these qualities in
everything that she does. She has inspired me and so many of the people around her and I
cannot picture what my journey at FSU would look like without her. The student senate has
been as lucky to be served by Sarah as I am to call her a best friend,” and
Whereas: Student Leader Katie Simon testifies: “Sarah Nemeth is without a doubt the most
exceptional leader and kindest soul I have ever known. She is a hardworking, supportive, and
empathetic individual who values connection with others. Sarah has a natural ability to motivate
and inspire those around her, and I can confidently say that without her encouragement, I would
not be the leader and person I am today. I cannot think of anyone better to receive this honor
and be inducted into the Senate Hall of Fame,” and
Whereas: Student Body President-elect Jack Hitchcock testifies: “Sarah and I were elected
together during the Fall in our freshman years during COVID. Despite the bounds of Zoom, Sarah
was a staunch advocate for others, never ceasing to stand for what was right. Sarah challenged the
status quo each and every day and challenged people to be and do better. She has been an
inspiration for many, including myself. I could not recommend Sarah more highly for this honor,” and
Whereas: Student Leader Alexander Chang testifies: “I’ve been fortunate enough to get to
know Sarah for the better part of my collegiate experience and I am so honored to call her a
friend. Her jokes and laughter light up a room but it is in her dedication to serving others that
she especially shines. Though I never had the privilege to work directly with her, I have seen herDocuSign Envelope ID: D1EAB56A-7A7D-4E46-B513-521A66B55D73

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
step up in leadership when things get hard and stand up for what she believes in.
Congratulations Sarah!” therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: Former
Senator and Senate President Pro-Tempore Sarah Nemeth is nominated to the Student Senate
Hall of Fame, and is applauded for her honorable service to Florida State University and to the
Student Senate thereof, and
Be it further resolved that: A copy of this resolution be sent to:
Sarah Nemeth, President Pro-Tempore of the 74th Student Senate
OFFICIAL: _________________________________________________________
Student Senate President

PASSED: April 5th, 2023DocuSign Envelope ID: D1EAB56A-7A7D-4E46-B513-521A66B55D73

sections.text:
75th STUDENT SENATE
Senate Resolution
Resolution #: 41
Primary Sponsor: Maglin, Bettley
Co-Sponsor(s): Allgoever, Alvarez, Anandjiwala, Burton, Carter, Chehaitli, Crocker, Dale, Diaz,
Fineout, Humberg, Kariher, LoBianco, Mantilla, McMahon, Salazar, Severy, Rivers
Whereas: Student Body Statute 413.8 states, “Membership in the Senate Hall of Fame is the
highest honor a student Senator can achieve. This honor shall be bestowed upon any Senator
who has performed their duty as a member of the Senate with the highest standard of
excellence, beyond that normally expected of a Senator at the Florida State University”, and
Whereas: Senator DuChêne has been a member of the 73rd, 74th, and 75th Student Senates,
where he served as the Chair of the Student Life during the 74th Senate, Pro-Tempore and
Chair of the Rules Committee during the 75th Senate, a member of the Seminole and Peoples
Imagery and Education (SIPIE) Ad Hoc in the 73rd Student Senate, and a member of the
Sustainability Ad Hoc during the 75th Student Senate, and
Whereas: Senator DuChêne was voted Senator of the Month in March 2022, New Senator of
the Year in the 74th Student Senate, and the Robert Brandewie Student Life Senator in the 74th
Student Senate, and
Whereas: Senator DuChêne served as the liaison for the Jewish Student Union in the 74th
Student Senate, where he passionately advocated for Jewish students on this campus,
condemning every instance of antisemitism at Florida State University. Senator DuChêne
consistently upheld the mission of the Student Government Association by ensuring that there is
no space for hatred on this campus, and he actively ensured that all of the Student Government
Association was a safe and welcoming space for all, and
Whereas: Senator DuChêne has worked diligently throughout not only his time as a Senator,
but also as a student, to acknowledge the deep-rooted Native American heritage and history at
Florida State University. He has consistently advocated for Native American education,
representation, and appreciation, ensuring that Native American students at Florida State
University are recognized and that Native American culture, especially the Seminole Tribe, is
protected at this University, and
Whereas: As a member of the LGBTQ+ community, Senator DuChêne has continuously
advocated for, supported, and uplifted members of the LGBTQ+ community, not only on this
campus, but throughout the state of Florida. With the rise of hate perpetrated against the
LBGTQ+ community, Senator DuChêne has condemned any acts of homophobia and
transphobia committed at Florida State University at every opportunity. Despite the homophobic
and transphobic legislation circulating the Florida Legislature, Senator DuChêne has maintained
and unwavering mission to ensure that LGBTQ+ students at Florida State University are
protected, respected, and appreciated, and
Whereas: Senator DuChêne went above and beyond to organize, advocate for, and pass six
(6) amendments to the 2023 OGA Legislative Agenda to ensure that the Agenda aligned with
the values of and represented the best interests of both the Florida State University studentDocuSign Envelope ID: 82EC3B0C-925D-43A7-9500-3EC579147C5C

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.text:
body and the Student Senate. These amendments were in the interest of lowering costs,
increasing accessibility, public health, safety, inclusivity, and Florida State University’s
relationship with the Seminole Tribe of Florida. With the 2022 Legislative Agenda, Senator
DuChêne ensured that the recommendations from the FSU President’s Task-Force on Anti-
Racism, Equity, and Inclusion were acknowledged. This includes, but is not limited to, the
support for funding the creation of a Center of Native American & Indigenous Studies at Florida
State University, and
Whereas: Senator DuChêne has proposed, co-sponsored, and passed legislation during his
first entrance to Senate in the 73rd Student Senate regarding issues including but not limited to:
Hall of Fame Resolutions for Jason Randall and Alex Harmon (Resolution 85, 87), 9/11
remembrance (Resolution 69), encouraging a Native American ’land acknowledgement’ be
adopted by the Schools of Theater, Dance, and the College of Music (Resolution 72), and the
redirection of Pay-To-Park revenue towards free student spaces (Resolution 75), and
Whereas: Senator DuChêne has proposed, co-sponsored, and passed an array of legislation
during the 74th Student Senate regarding issues including but not limited to: OGA statutory
revisions (Bill 1), prohibition of weapons bought with A&S monies (Bill 13), creating internal
accountability for the financial certification of senators (Bill 15), revising statutes for the Jewish
Student Union (Bill 29), amending language pertaining to FSU Student Senate Awards for
Execellence (Bill 36), allowing seats without sworn-in senators to be filled (Bill 41), changing
Student Body Elections results to be read during Special Introductions (Bill 42), increasing
amount of PAC funding towards clothing (Bill 75), waiving rule 803.7 for the Jewish Student
Union Banquet 2022 (Resolution 2), celebrating the end of Britney Spears’ conservatorship
(Resolution 3), congratulating and supporting newly selected university administrators
(Resolution 4, 15) condemning the Florida ‘Don‘t Say Gay’ Bill and any homophobic and
transphobic legislation in Florida (Resolution 17, 55), Hall of Fame Resolutions for Tyler Roy,
Renee Wang, and Gabbi Little (Resolution 30, 31, 32), FSU Student Senate Awards for
Execellence (Resolution 51, 62), recognizing Florida State University as a Top 20 University
(Resolution 58), urging Homecoming to consult the Religious Holiday Calendar when planning
events (Resolution 61), condemning acts of antisemitism towards the Jewish community, and all
acts of hatred, at Florida State University (Resolution 63), and recognizing Indigenous People‘s
Day (Resolution 67), and
Whereas: Senator DuChêne has proposed, co-sponsored, and passed legislation during the
75th Student Senate regarding issues including but not limited to: the revitalization of the
Legislative Certification Program (Bill 1), acknowledging Native American Heritage Month
(Resolution 1), condemning actions taken by the Florida Legislature that infringe on student’s
rights (Resolution 15, 27, 28, 29), the implementation of a university-wide ‘mental health day‘
(Resolution 26), condemning acts of hate against Jewish and LGBTQ+ communities both on
Florida State’s campus and in the United States (Resolution 5, 24), advocating against gun
violence (Resolution 21, Amendments to the 2023 Legislative Agenda), misrepresentation of
SGA offices (Bill 17), and the codification of the Diversity and Inclusion Institute, and
Whereas: Senate President Diaz testifies that, “Patrick. From the day I became a member of
the Student Senate and saw him run for the position he would one day earn, I knew he was a
special person. The passion he has for his community, college, and beliefs are second-to-none,
and the attention to detail he put into the job of being our President Pro-Tempore is
unparalleled. Senator DuChêne’s oratory abilities are no doubt one of the reasons he is beloved
inside and outside the Senate chambers, and his ability to persuade, doubtless why he
transcends partisan divides and earns the respect of virtually every person in the Senate. InDocuSign Envelope ID: 82EC3B0C-925D-43A7-9500-3EC579147C5C

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
Patrick, I’ve found a friend, ally, and tireless partner in my position over the last semester. He is
one of the reasons the job of Senate President has been so rewarding, and I could not endorse
him highly enough for this honour,” and
Whereas: Senator Kariher testifies that, ”Senator DuChêne truly an incredible leader and his
presence in Senate provides a level of comfort and familiarity to everyone. His comedic
interjections and voting memes made Senate much less stuffy. Senator DuChêne always stood
for what he believes in and articulated himself in a way that is respectful and unabashedly true
to his morals. Thank you for being a mentor to me and so many others,” and
Whereas: Senator Humberg testifies that, ”Pro Tempore DuChêne has served as a guiding light
within the senate for me since the beginning of my term, going as far as reaching out to me
online despite our party difference to offer me advice and assistance as I fulfilled a new role.
Beyond his dedication to building up those within the professional sphere of the chambers, he is
an irreplaceable joy to be around and his dashingly good looks nearly outweigh his wit. Love
you Patrick!”, and
Whereas: Senator Bettley testifies that, ”It has been an absolute honor, and truly the best time,
serving alongside Patrick. I would not have wanted to enter the Senate with anyone else, and I
am proud to call him a friend outside of these chambers. Patrick is not only an amazing human
being; he is the model for what a Senator should be. He carries himself with such respect,
passion, and kindness at all times, and I am sad to see him go. I know Patrick will do amazing
things in his life, and I cannot wait to cheer him on as he does. Love you Patty <3,” and
Whereas: Senator Maglin testifies that, ”I have never met someone with the ability to transcend
political contention and adversity to be such an advocate for equality for everyone. Patrick is the
true definition of a leader. He is selfless, using his position as a Senator to fight for communities
who lack representation both on campus and across the United States. He is compassionate,
creating an environment of acceptance and understanding whenever he walks into a room. He
is assertive, unafraid to voice his opinion and ensure that those he represents are protected.
From my first meeting until now, I have tried to emulate Patrick and follow in his footsteps. I, like
many of my fellow senators, find myself in awe of Patrick’s sharpness, eloquence, and poise.
These qualities can be seen as much in his speech as in his writing. His numerous pieces of
legislation are so well-written, thoughtful, and the prime example of what a senator should be.
The Florida State University Student Senate was extremely lucky to have such a superb senator
grace its chambers. I am honored to have served in the Senate alongside you and even more
honored to call you a friend. Love you Patty,” and
Whereas: Senator Dale testifies that, ”Working with Pro Tempore DuChêne has been a great
gift to me as I’ve become adjusted to the ins and outs of the Student Government Association.
Patrick offered his kindness to everyone and anyone around him, and ensured that new
senators always felt welcome. Patrick handled his leadership position with neutrality and
wisdom, while still keeping his flame for advocacy alive. He knows the world he wants to see
created, isn’t afraid to fight for it, and has used his time in the Senate to bring us closer to it,”
and
Whereas: Senator Carter testifies that, ”I chose Student Life as my #1 committee preference
because Chair Patrick DuChêne seemed funny, and I couldn’t resist a fellow theatre kid.
Although Pro-Tempore DuChêne is an incredibly hilarious performer, he is far more than that.
Patrick’s influence on the Student Senate and Florida State University is one of passionate
advocacy for marginalized communities. He never fails to defend others and, in doing so, hasDocuSign Envelope ID: 82EC3B0C-925D-43A7-9500-3EC579147C5C

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
fostered a greater, safer community for all individuals at our University. Florida State is more
accepting, bold, and celebratory, due to Pro-Tempore DuChêne’s student leadership, and I’ll
always be thankful that his passion ignited mine. Go Student Life!!!“, and
Whereas: Senator Rivers testifies that, ”Pro Tempore DuChêne is a senator that truly works to
uphold the ideals of the students he represents. As a student in the College of Fine Arts, I am
happy to have someone like Pro Temp DuChêne in the Student Senate to ensure that one of
the smallest colleges on campus has one of the strongest voices in the Senate to speak for it.
Senator DuChêne has always made sure that he speaks up for FSU’s LBGTQ+ community and
that they are being protected and uplifted. For this I want to thank Senator DuChêne and happily
recommend him for the Senate Hall of Fame,” and
Whereas: Senator Chehaitli testifies that, “I cannot express how deeply I admire Patrick’s work
ethic and passion, only outdone by my love for his heart. Everything Patrick does both within
and outside the Senate Chambers is a product of the intersection of his empathy and strength;
Patrick is the epitome of doing the good work, advocating for everyone to the best of his ability.
He is a Pro-Tempore that I am proud to have served my first Senate term under, and I could not
be more ecstatic to see his nomination for the Student Senate Hall of Fame,” and
Whereas: Senator Burton testifies that, “I am thrilled to lend my voice in support of Patrick's
candidacy for the Senate Hall of Fame. Throughout his tenure, Patrick has demonstrated an
unwavering commitment to doing what is right and just, even in the face of opposition. He has
dedicated countless hours to serving both his fellow students and the broader campus
community, embodying the ideals of what John Lewis referred to as "good trouble." Patrick's
leadership as Pro Tempore of the 75th Student Senate has been nothing short of remarkable.
His tireless efforts and dedication to the betterment of the student body have not gone
unnoticed. Patrick has consistently advocated for what is in the best interest of his constituents,
even when it meant standing up to those who did not agree with him. It is Patrick's steadfast
commitment to serving his community and his unwavering moral compass that makes him such
an exceptional candidate for the Senate Hall of Fame. I do not doubt that he will continue to
serve as a beacon of inspiration for all those around him, and I wholeheartedly endorse his
candidacy for this esteemed honor,” and
Whereas: Senator Mantilla testifies that, “Patrick DuChêne is an exceptional senator, a natural-
born leader, and a compassionate friend. His relentless devotion to the student body should not
go overlooked. Patrick is someone I initially looked up to as a new senator, and one year later,
that has not changed. His ability to speak with poise and intensity on pressing matters while
overlooking party politics is precisely what makes him a powerful, uniting force within SGA. His
dedication to the student body here at FSU is unlike any other I have seen. Senator DuChêne

Whereas: The Internal Affairs often time gets overwhelmed by the amount of confirmation
hearings that need to take place, and

oversight to “debate, amend, reject, or recommend the passage of measures pertaining to fiscal
matters and to Chapter 800 of the Student Body Statues,” and
Whereas: The Finance Committee should assume the responsibility of all financial nominations
for agencies and bureaus, therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: to help
our committees work more efficiently that the Student Senate Rules of Procedure be amended
as follows:
6.2 The Senate Finance Committee shall:
a. Debate, amend, reject, or recommend the passage of measures pertaining to fiscal
matters and to Chapter 800 of the Student Body Statutes.
b. Review Chapter 800 of the Finance Code and suggest possible amendments.
c. Conduct reviews and provide legislative oversight for all A&S fee recipients and
expenditures as deemed necessary by the Student Senate President in
consultation with the Chair.
d. Review Senate Funds Distribution Committee consent resolutions, approve or
disapprove nominations to the Funds Distribution Committees, and inform the
Senate of any relevant actions.
e. Forward or deny all nominations for agency, bureau, and affiliated project
nominees for financial officers, excluding Executive Cabinet officers.

Whereas: According to the American Psychological Association, during the 2020-2021 school
year, “more than 60% of college students met the criteria for at least one mental health
problem,” which can include anxiety, depression, and stress; and

inevitably at higher risk to develop mental health issues. Thus, this increases the necessity of
the accessibility of resources on campus for mental health in order to promote student wellness
and advancement; and

“with the mission to empower students with mental health resources through de-stigmatization,
community involvement, and advocacy;” and
Whereas: The Mental Health Council executive board was built from the ground up this past
semester by Ashley Boudreaux. Subsequently, the council succeeded in hosting an all-day
event on Landis Green, “Recharge with MHC,” with over 500 attendees; and
Whereas: The Counseling Center on Florida State’s campus provides free therapy and other
educational resources for all students on campus as well as outreach to assist students in
finding help off-campus; and
Whereas: The Mental Health Council and Counseling Center work in tandem to develop
programming surrounding the education and de-stigmatization of mental health; thereforeDocuSign Envelope ID: 3E633B79-4C66-4DAE-9D66-D582545D1D39

in the fiscal year of 2022. That is 1 out of 8 people which is higher than the national average of 1
out of 9 people, and
Whereas: In Leon County, 67% of the residential population’s annual income is below SNAP
and Other Nutrition Programs threshold requirements of 200% poverty, and
Whereas: 1 out of 3 college students face food insecurity nationally as many college students
faced food insecurity for the first time, and

academic year. Many of these students are EBT recipients or are qualifying, and

teaches students about Snap Benefits/Assistance programs included, but not limited to, how to

Post, and

payment at the EBT terminal on the Florida State University campus, and

campus could not tell you where an EBT terminal is located.DocuSign Envelope ID: D763D783-68F5-4045-A61E-2045A94115F3

Resolution #: 55
Primary Sponsor(s): Pedraja
Co-Sponsor(s): Arellano, Bevis, Hellman, Hirji, Kerley, Randall, Sparling

Whereas: the Student Senate recognizes the need to ensure efficient and effective procedures
for committee referral and consideration of legislations.
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: the
Rules of Procedure be amended as follows:
Section 5.9 Committee Referral shall be revised as:
“The Student Senate President shall refer all bills and constitutional amendments to the
appropriate standing committee for consideration and action, and the Student Senate President
may refer any resolution to committee or directly to the calendar for second reading. In the
occurrence of a bill being referred to multiple committees, the committee assignments shall be
considered a sequential order. The bill must be passed in sequence by all the relevant
committees to be placed on Second Reading. In the case of a bill being referred to multiple
committees, the committee assignments shall not be bound by a specific sequential order. The
bill must receive approval from all relevant committees, regardless of the order, to be placed on
Second Reading. Each committee shall review the most recently passed version of the bill.
Once a bill passes an individual committee, it shall proceed, along with any amendments, to the
next committee for consideration. Failure of a bill in any assigned committee shall result in its
defeat, and it shall be removed from the Calendar.”
Be it further resolved that: this amendment to the Rules of Procedure shall take effect
immediately upon approval.

Senate Resolution
Resolution #: 56
Primary Sponsor(s): Randall
Co-Sponsor(s): Cofer, Gorelick, Waldie
Date: July 24, 2023
Whereas: Electing a Student Senate President and Pro-Tempore is among the most important
and sacred duties the Senate must conduct at the beginning of a new session, or when a
vacancy should arise, and
Whereas: Senators should be able to ask candidates for Senate President and Pro-Tempore
more than what our current 2-question limit provides for, and
Whereas: The “roll” that is kept of Senators is not standardized, nor are there codified rules for
how the Senate roll should be organized, potentially leading to dispute as to who the presiding
officer of an organization session should be if there is a tie in seniority, therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Student Senate Rules of Procedure be amended as follows:
1.5 Each candidate shall be allowed, in alphabetical order, to give a presentation to the
Senate for no more than five (5) minutes. Immediately following each candidate’s
presentation, no more than four (4) Senators will be allowed to address a question to
the candidate who just presented. The Chair shall allow two minutes of pro-debate per
candidate. No con- debate shall be permitted during the election process. All nominees
not addressing the Senate shall be requested to exit the chambers when not speaking,
including during all debate on the candidates. Upon the completion of the final vote all
nominees may enter the Chambers.
Be it further resolved that: The Student Senate Rules of Procedure be amended as follows:
1.1 Following the Fall Inauguration and installation of the new Student Senate, the most
senior member of the Student Senate shall call to order an organizational meeting of the
Senate for the purpose of electing a Student Senate President. During that meeting, the
Senate Rules of Procedure from the previous session shall be adopted in order to
conduct business.
a. “Most senior” shall be defined as the senator that has served the longest
consecutive term. Should more than one senator have served for the same
amount of time, the senator whose last name takes precedence in alphabetical
order shall be considered the most senior.DocuSign Envelope ID: 471D2C54-5745-47ED-85A2-A8EB7FCA6D59

Whereas: Changing the format of debate for candidates for confirmation could be beneficial to
ensure fairness and a spirit of positivity within the Chambers, and
Whereas: The proposed changes in this resolution change the format of debate from pro/con to
roundtable-style discussion, delineate the procedures for debate in a list style, and change the
language of “forwarding candidates individually” to “calling the question on the candidates,” as is
standard with legislation, and

resolution and adopted by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate,” therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Student Senate Rules of Procedure be amended as follows:
10.9 All nominees to Student Government offices requiring Senate confirmation shall
have their completed applications forwarded to the appropriate Senate
committee for consideration. The committee shall interview and question the
nominee and then vote on whether to forward or deny them. Following the vote of
the committee, all nominees forwarded by the committee shall be called to the
floor of the Senate at its next meeting. The structure of debate for Senate
confirmations shall be as follows: and shall be allowed to give an opening
statement, lasting no longer than five (5) minutes, with their remaining time being
allocated to their closing. Upon conclusion of all opening statements, candidates
may be questioned by any Senator. During questioning, any Senator may move
to enter debate via a majority vote or confirm the nominees individually via a 2/3
(two-thirds) vote.
a. Nominees shall be allowed to give an opening statement lasting no
longer than five (5) minutes, with their remaining time being allocated to
their closing.
b. Nominees may be questioned by any Senator on matters of their
experience, qualifications, and goals for the respective position.
c. Upon passage of a motion to enter debate by majority vote, Senators may
speak freely as to the qualifications of any candidate. Nominees shall be
permitted to remain in the Senate Chamber during debate if they so

Whereas: Fentanyl-related problems have surged on college campuses, posing a grave
threat to the health and safety of the student population at Florida State University, and
Whereas: The presence of fentanyl in various forms, including pills, powders, and
adulterated substances, has led to an alarming increase in overdoses and fatalities
among college students, and
Whereas: It is well-documented that a lethal dose of fentanyl can be as little as 2
milligrams, underscoring the extreme potency and deadly nature of this substance, and
Whereas: Limited knowledge and education about fentanyl risks contribute to students'
susceptibility to its dangers, necessitating immediate action, and
Whereas: Peer pressure and experimentation with drugs in college environments have made
students vulnerable to unknowingly consuming fentanyl, further exacerbating the crisis,
therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: The
Seventy-Fifth Student Senate recognizes the urgent need to address the fentanyl crisis on our
campus and commit to safeguarding the welfare of our student body, and
Be it further resolved that: The Seventy-Fifth Student Senate endorses CS/SB 164,
which recently legalized fentanyl test strips, as a proactive and life-saving measure to
combat the fentanyl crisis on our campus and supports the work of the Commission on
Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder, and
Be it further resolved that: The Seventy-Fifth Student Senate encourages university
administration and health services to collaborate in making fentanyl test strips readily
available through campus health centers and other relevant channels, ensuring
accessibility to all students, and

profound impact on their families, friends, and communities;
Whereas: Florida State University seeks to promote the welfare and well-being of its community

large;

children with cancer, therefore

families, and the healthcare professionals that care for them, and

participate in initiatives and activities aimed at raising awareness and providing support to
children with cancer and their families.

Whereas: This resolution contains potentially sensitive or triggering content such as mentions
of suicide.
Whereas: September is National Suicide Prevention Month, and according to Lifeline, an
organization dedicated to preventing suicide, during this month, “mental health advocates,
prevention organizations, survivors, allies, and community members unite to promote suicide
prevention awareness,” and
Whereas: With the stressors of college, many students struggle to maintain their mental health,
and although it is seldom discussed, suicide is the second leading cause of death among
college-aged students, and
Whereas: Counseling and Psychological Services has a 24/7 support line, free counseling,
psychoeducational workshops via Zoom which focus on anxiety and depression, and other
resources available to support mental health, and
Whereas: The Mental Health Council at FSU strives to “empower students with mental health
resources through de-stigmatization, community involvement, and advocacy,” and
Whereas: The National Suicide Prevention Lifeline is another critical resource for those in need
of immediate support and is available 24/7, similar to the Telephonic Crisis Support provided by
Counseling and Psychological Services, with vital information on the signs of mental health
crisis and suicide found on their website, therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: We
recognize the importance of National Suicide Awareness Month, especially on a college
campus, and
Be it further resolved that: We urge everyone to check in on the people they care about, learn
the signs of a mental health crisis, prioritize their own mental health, and not to delay in seeking
help, and if in crisis, do not hesitate to call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1(800)
273-8255 or 988 for free and confidential support or the Telephonic Crisis Support Line
mentioned above, and
Be it further resolved that: We urge everyone to visit this link, https://afsp.org/national-suicide-
prevention-week/, to find resources as well as social media graphics to help bring awareness to
suicide prevention, and
Be it further resolved that: The Student Senate Press Secretary and Executive Branch are
strongly encouraged to advocate for student’s mental health through the promotion ofDocuSign Envelope ID: BEDA013D-8DE5-41B9-A243-681559137B7A

Whereas: Local fees are defined as the Activity & Service (A&S) fee, the Athletics fee, and the
Health fee, which are paid by students each semester as part of their overall tuition fees, and
Whereas: Florida Statute 1009.24 stipulates that the local fees “a student is required to pay to
register for a course may not exceed 40 percent of the tuition established in law,” and
Whereas: The current local fees per credit hour consist of an A&S Fee of $12.86, an Athletics
Fee of $7.90, and a Health Fee of $13.97, and
Whereas: These local fees combined add up to $34.73 per credit hour, which represents 16.1%
of the total cost of tuition for in-state, undergraduate students, and
Whereas: Local fees for Florida State University have not increased since the 2012-2013
school year, and
Whereas: According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, $1 in January 2012 now has the same
buying power as $1.32 in January 2023, representing a 32% increase in inflation since the last
time local fees were increased, and
Whereas: Florida Statute 1009.24 establishes an annual Local Fees Committee for FSU that is
roughly composed of half-student and half-faculty members, which reviews and recommends
potential Local Fee increases for Florida State University, and
Whereas: The 2023 Local Fees Committee recommended a per-credit-hour increase in the
A&S Fee of $0.65 ($13.51 total), an Athletics Fee increase of $0.39 ($8.29 total), and a Health
Fee increase of $0.69 ($14.66 total), and
Whereas: Should these recommended increases go into effect, the new local fee total would be
$36.46 per credit hour, representing 16.9% of the total current tuition cost of $215.55 for in-
state, undergraduate students, and
Whereas: Florida Statute 1009.24 establishes the maximum possible increase permitted by the
Local Fees Committee to be 5%, or $1.73 per credit hour, and
Whereas: These recommendations represent a 5% increase in the current fee levels, in
compliance with state law, therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: It is the
opinion of the Student Senate that tuition rates have not kept up with the rate of inflation, andDocuSign Envelope ID: F43087E8-84E8-4BAE-94AB-ED710C88A073

sections.heading: Page 2

that it is incumbent upon this body to support FSU students by advocating for ample funding
and resources, and
Be it further resolved that: In keeping with these beliefs, the Student Senate supports the
above-referenced recommendations made by the 2023 Local Fees Committee, and urges the
FSU Administration and the Board of Trustees to approve said recommendations, and

Whereas: Deaf Awareness Month is observed annually during the month of September to
promote awareness, understanding, and inclusion of the deaf and hard of hearing community,
and
Whereas: The deaf and hard of hearing community face unique challenges and barriers in
various aspects of life, including education, employment, healthcare, and social interactions,
and
Whereas: Promoting awareness and advocating for equal opportunities and access for the deaf
and hard of hearing can lead to a more inclusive and equitable society, and
Whereas: On April 8, 1864, President Abraham Lincoln signed the charter of Gallaudet
University in Washington D.C, the first school for the advance education of the deaf and hard of
hearing in the world, and
Whereas: Acknowledging the invaluable contributions, remarkable talents, and outstanding
achievements of individuals such as Helen Keller, a trailblazing disability rights advocate,
Marlee Matlin, an acclaimed and award-winning American actress, and Nyle DiMarco, a
groundbreaking pioneer as the first deaf contestant on America's Next Top Model, within the
deaf and hard of hearing community stands as an imperative cornerstone in our collective
endeavor to construct a more inclusive and diverse society, therefore
Be it resolved by the Seventy-fifth Student Senate at Florida State University that: In
unwavering pursuit of justice and inclusivity, hereby work to raise awareness about the unique
challenges faced by the deaf and hard of hearing community and recognize the paramount
importance of fostering accessible communication channels and ensuring equitable
opportunities for all, regardless of hearing ability, and
Be it further resolved that: The we pledge to advocate for the implementation of policies and
practices that guarantee equal rights, opportunities, and unfettered access to essential services.
This commitment extends to ensuring that every individual, irrespective of their hearing ability, is
treated equitably, and
Be it further resolved that: Creating an inclusive and empowering environment that enables
the deaf and hard of hearing community to pursue their goals and aspirations without
encountering discrimination or insurmountable barriers, is of the upmost importance, and
Be it lastly resolved that: A copy of this resolution be sent to
