BILL 2010
Activity and Service Fee Budget
Proviso Language
Special Instructions
I. General
A. No A&S funded account may pay any stipend, wage, salary, or salary
increase to any positions not funded in Bill 2010 without express
consent of the Student Senate.
B. Monies allocated for the Homecoming Powwow may be used in
conjunction with a ticket price charged to students.
C. In the event of shortfalls or excesses, the Vice President of
Student Affairs, the SGA Advisor, the Senate President, and the
Student Body President shall meet to review options.
D. The suggestion for A&S Fees shall be $10.47 per credit hour.
II. CAMPUS RECREATION
A. It is the position of the 61st Student Senate that the Bobby E.
Leach Student Recreation Center, the Intramural fields, and the Rec
SportsPlex have been primarily funded by student dollars and that
these facilities' primary purpose is for student recreational
purposes.
B. Any and all use of the Bobby E. Leach Student Recreation Center,
the Intramural fields, and the Rec SportsPlex for activities other
than student recreational purposes must be approved by the Campus
Recreation Board. If the policies of this Board are violated, or
if the Board is not consulted, the Senate will recommend to the
Student Body Treasurer that the funds for Campus Recreation be
frozen immediately until corrective action is taken.
c. The money allocated in the OCO category is a one-time allocation
due to lack of Sweepings and Central Reserves money in the last two
years. This money shall used solely for the purpose of replacing
aged and unsafe fitness equipment.
III.UNIVERSITY UNION
A. Any event or entertainment provided by the University Union shall
be free and open to all students with valid identification with the
exception of Breakfast for a Buck. Non-FSU students shall be
subject to admission fees.

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
r 2
B. Revenue placed in the Headliner Account shall be used for the
express purpose of bringing major concert acts for the
entertainment of the Student Body. This account shall be
administered by the Student Activities Office with input from a
committee appointed by the Headliners Concert Committee, appointed
by the Student Body President and approved by Senate. An admission
price may be charged to students in conjunction with monies used
from this account. The Headliner Account shall not be swept at the
end of the fiscal year.
C. Oglesby Union was allocated $80, 100 in Expense solely for the
purpose of the following programs: Last Call Before Fall, Halloween
Celebration, Spring Fling, and Breakfast for a Buck.
IV. STUDENT ACTIVITIES AND ORGANIZATIONS
A. Agencies, bureaus and affiliated projects are strongly encouraged
to utilize the event planning and contract negotiation services
offered by the Student Activities Center throughout the planning
and execution of any A&S funded events. Events involving a
contractual service (speaker, musician, comedian, trainer,
performer, etc.) exceeding $2000 are to be planned and negotiated
in consultation with a representative from the Student Activities
Center prior to any verbal or written commitment of such A&S
funds. This clause shall only pertain to the contractual service
(speaker, musician, comedian, trainer, performer, etc.) for
negotiation and not necessarily for other arrangements such as
space reservations, advertisement or any other component of the
program.
B. Monies in the Food category shall never be used for Executive Board
meetings and not more than three times each semester for General
Body meetings.
C. Monies allocated to the Student Government Administration Account
are expressly intended for the payment of the Newspaper Readership
Program, the FSView, telephone, computer assessment, the Milestone,
the Torch, maintenance contracts, office supplies, printing,
advertisement, the library DVD program, and miscellaneous expenses.
D. Homecoming may not allocate funds to any concerts other than War
Chant. The 61st Student Senate strongly recommends that War Chant
include at least 2 "named acts" and that they be diverse and as
inclusive as possible.
E. No money shall be used to fund conferences with more than twenty
students attending without specific approval by Senate by a 2/3
majority.

elections any A&S fees not needed for the Black Student Union
elections shall be reverted back to the Senate Unallocated

solely for the purpose of purchasing LobbyTools. This rule may be
waived with a majority vote of Senate if the Director decides not
to renew LobbyTools or decides to purchase a different program.
H. FSU Service Corps shall publish the SPEAR online in order to
reduce costs of production and allow for a more efficient means of
distribution.
I. Lecture Series was allocated $2000 in expense for the purpose of
purchasing food and beverages at the events hosted by the series.
The budget committee recommends that food and beverages be served

V. Specific Instructions
A. Any A&S monies not spent on Homecoming shall be remanded to the
Senate Projects Account.
B. The 61st Student Senate recommends that at least 1 Senate
Representative serve on all Homecoming Committees that involve A&S
fees.
VI. SEVERABILITY CLAUSES
A. All clauses in the Proviso Language for Bill 2010 shall be
considered fully severable.

202.11 Student Government Applications
202.12
A. The Senate Internal Affairs Committee shall determine
what format Student Government applications will take.
Once a format has been originally selected, the Internal
Affairs Committee may propose any changes it deems
necessary, which must pass the committee as well as the
Senate by a two-thirds {2/3) vote in order to be
formally adopted.
B. Applications must be consistent with all rules and
regulations of Student Government, as well as those of
the university, state and federal government.
C. In changing or creating forms, the Internal Affairs
Committee shall seek the advice of the Chief Justice of
the Supreme Court, the Vice President for Student
Affairs, the Business Manager of SA&O Accounting and the
Student Government Administrative Assistant.
There shall be two inauguration ceremonies held per year,
following the Fall and Spring SGA elections, on the dates
specified in the Student Body Election Code. The oath of
office will be administered to all students who have been duly
elected to office by the Chief Justice of the Student Supreme
Court. If the Chief Justice is unavailable, then he/she may
appoint an Associate Justice to administer the oath in his/her
place. If no Justice to the Student Supreme Court is
available, then the Supervisor of Elections shall choose any
judge or justice who is currently serving on the bench in the
State of Florida. The candidates for the offices of Student
Body President, Student Body Vice President and Student Body
Treasurer must be administered the oath individually. All
duties, rights, privileges, and responsibilities of office
shall vest upon taking the prescribed oath of office.

711.4 Polling Site Procedures
A. The Supervisor of Elections shall ensure that there
shall be no electioneering or campaign materials within
ten (10) feet of polling sites. The Supervisor of
Elections shall be authorized to remove any campaign
materials posted in violation of this rule.
B. Bands, loud speakers and any other use of audio
amplification for campaigning shall be prohibited within
one hundred (100) feet of any polling place.
c. Voters shall be entitled to vote in privacy.
D. Two or more authorized poll workers, or one Deputy
Supervisor shall run the poll at each polling site.
Polls must be attended at all times by two or more poll
workers or a Deputy Supervisor.
h In the event of extenuating circumstances. at the
discretion of the Supervisor of Elections. all
polling sites other than the two most heavily used
in the previous SGA General Election may be allowed
to operate with one poll worker for a period not to
extend thirty (30) minutes.
E. No candidate or person closely affiliated with a
political party shall serve as a poll worker.
F. There shall be no "roving precincts" or polling places
situated on moving vehicles.
G. The Supervisor of Elections or deputies shall lock or
seal ballot boxes before the polls open.
H. Voters shall use a valid FSU Card as a student voter
registration card. The photograph depicted on the card
must match the student using it.

Chapter 1011 INSTITUTE FOR LIBERAL AND PROGRESSIVE STUDIES
Added by the 59 th Student Senat e Bill 8
•
1011 . 1 Creation and Purpose
~ Creation
This act shall create an agencv of the Student Government
Association known as the "Institute for Libera l and
Progressive Studies" (ILPS)
Purpose
The ILPS shall:
L Be a forum for presenting a liberal and
perspective t o thought on educational,
philosophical and social issues .
progressive
political ,
Facilitate and foster communication between like-
minded liberal and progressive organizations .
.1..:_ Work with other campus and community organizations in
order to encourage collective action campaigns , which
will benefit FSU students and the community .
1...:.. Provide guest lectures, workshops , and other liberal
and progressive programs.
2....:.. Provide this programming without charging a fee .
1011 . 2 Membership
Participation is open to all students, faculty, and staff of the
Florida State University and to members of the Tallahassee
community.
1011.3 Executive Board
!L
Membership of the Executive Board shal l consist of
students. The Executive Board will include the positions of
Director, Assistant Directo r, Secre tary , Financial Officer,
Communications Director, and a Public Relations Officer .
The other two Executive Board positions will be assigned
and tit l ed based on the Director and Assistant Director's
prerogative. There will also be an ex-officio advisor who
shall serve on the board; he or she will be selected by the
Board.
Selection and Term of Office
L Director and Assistant Director
5

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
The Board will interview all applicants for director
and assistant director and forward their
recommendation(s) to the Student Body President. The
process then follows in accordance with Chapter
1000.5 C and D of the Executive Agency Act.
If the Director or Assistant Director intends to
serve ILPS again in either position. they may
not take part in the interviewing and forwarding
of applicants for the position of Director and
Assistant Director.
The Director and Assistant Director's term in
office shall end at the close of the spring
semester. However. the Director or Assistant
Director mav serve more than one term if
reappointed by the proper authority in
accordance with Chapter 1000.5 C and D.
Other Executive Board Positions
Once a new Director and Assistant Director are
approved they then will interview candidates for all
positions on the Executive Board. Former Executive
Board members may apply but are not guaranteed a
position on the new Executive Board. The Director and
Assistant Director will-f6rward their recommendation
to the Student Body President. The process then
follows in accordance with Chapter 1000.5 C (2) of
the Executive Agency Act.
The Executive Board will oversee the day-to-day
operations of the agency until the newly appointed
Director and Assistant Director take office.
~ Meetings
The Executive Board may not schedule any events
or place any orders requiring the expenditure of
agency funds during this oversight period.
h The Executive Board shall meet at least twice a month
during the academic year. The "academic year"
commences on the first official day of classes for
the fall term and ends on the last official day of
classes for the spring term. The official dates are
those so stipulated by the Office of the Registrar.
a. Meetings during the summer term shall be held at
the discretion of the chairperson.
6

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
The Executive Board may take no official action
unless a quorum is present .
.d...:.. All Executive Board members shall receive at least
forty-eight (48) hours notice prior to an unscheduled
meeting or cancellation of the regularly scheduled
meeting. This provision may be waived if the Director
can demonstrate that exigent circumstances exist .
.i...:.. The Director shall designate the time and place for
regular Board meetings at the beginning of the
academic year. The Director or Assistant Director or
a majority of the Board in accordance with paragraph
3 above may call any other Board meetings.
~ Powers and Duties of the Executive Board
The Executive Board shall work towards identifying,
developing and monitoring programs and campaigns that
express the needs of liberal and progressive students while
giving them a voice at Florida State University, thereby
increasing awareness of liberal and progressive views.
1..:.. The Director shall:
fl.:.. Be the chairperson of all functions, meetings,
or any related activities concerning ILPS, with
the approval of the Executive Board unless the
chairperson responsibility is delegated.
12..:.. Have the power to create and oversee all
standing committees.
~ Be responsible for the efficient and effective
operation of the ILPS Office on a daily basis.
Q..:.. Execute decisions on policy, procedure, and
activities in the best interest of the agency .
.§..:.. Appoint and remove staff members at his/her
discretion, upon consultation with the Assistant
Director.
i..:_ Be one of the two signatures from ILPS required
to spend funds.
Ensure,.-that all voices on the Executive Board
are heard and given due consideration .
.a..:_ The Assistant Director shall:
Assume all duties and responsibilities of the
Director in the event that he or she is absent.
7

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
h
Be the co-chair of all functions, meetings or
any related activities concerning ILPS, with the
approval of the Executive Board unless the co-
chair's responsibility is delegated.
Serve on the Student Government and university
committees that require executive agency
representation.
9-:.. Have the power to implement ad hoc committees.
The Secretary shall:
Prepare the minutes for the Executive Board.
Post the minutes of the Executive Board by at
least 72 hours following the meeting.
Maintain an updated ILPS member roster and email
list.
Be responsible for the upkeep of files and
records in the ILPS Office.
The Financial Officer shall:
Be notified and consulted before the Director
and Assistant Director authorize the expenditure
of any ILPS funds.
1;L_ Be responsible for the upkeep of financial
records for ILPS.
~ Be the second of two signatures from ILPS
required to spend ILPS funds.
~ The Communications Director shall:
a. Act as the agency's liaison to other like-minded
campus and community organizations.
1;L_ Be responsible for maintaining the agency's
correspondence and responding to inquires in a
prompt fashion.
The Public Relations Officer shall:
Ensure that the agency is aware of all campus
events especially those of other agencies.
8

sections.heading: Page 7
sections.text:
Be responsible for publicizing all ILPS events.
Publicizing includes but is not limited to press
releases, chalking, posting and flyers.
Remaining Two (2) Executive Board Members
The two (2) remaining Executive Board positions will
be filled based on the needs of the agency as decided
by the Director and Assistant Director. The title of
these two (2) positions is left to the discretion of
the Director and Assistant Director.
1011.4 The Steering Committee
!h_ The Steering Committee will exist to help foster
communication and enccmrage collective action amona all
liberal and progressiv~ organizations on campus.
~ Voting membership in the Steering Committee will include
the entirety of the Board of Directors, as well as
representatives from like-minded organizations, and at
large members appointed by the Director. The Director or
his/her designee will chair the commmittee.
L Each "like-minded" oraanization status will be
determined by the Board.
At no point will at-large membership constitute more
than two-thirds (2/3) of the committee's membership.
The Steering Committee will oversee the collective action
campaigns with which the agency is involved, and appoint
subcommittees for purposes specified by the committee.
The Steering Committee will have no authority over agency
resources of any kind, and can only utilize agency
resources with the consent of a majority of the Board.
1011.5 Removal from Office
Director
The Board may, by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of its members,
recommend the removal of the Director.
Staff
The Director shall have the authority to dismiss staff
members upon consultation with the Assistant Director.
1011.6 Vacancies
L Director
9

sections.heading: Page 8
sections.text:
Upon vacancy of the Director's position. the Assistant
Director shall assume the position of director until a
replacement is secured.
Assistant Director and Executive Board Member Positions
The vacancy will be advertised for three (3) days. The
recommendations will then be forwarded to the Student Body
President. This process will then follow in accordance with
Chapter 1000.5 C, (2) and D of the Executive Agency Act.
Vacancies shall be filled by the original process set forth
herein and the person filling the vacancy shall serve the
remainder of the term of office. In the event that the
Student Body President. or other statutorv authority
rejects recommendation by the Board said authority must
provide written explanation for rejection.

The Supervisor of Elections shall be responsible for

Chapter 706 Conditions for Victory
706 .1 The candidate who receives the most votes in any election
shall be declared the winner of that election.
706.2 In the event of a tie between two or more candidates, all
candidates involved will go before the Senate to determine a
winner, at the next scheduled regular session of the Senate
prior to inauguration.
706.3
A. The Senate shall conduct the election via secret ballot,
and the candidate receiving the most votes shall be
declared the winner. No speeches or debate shall be
permitted for the purposes of this election, unless all
candidates are present for the Senate meeting. In the
event that all candidates are present, the Senate
President shall ensure equal time for all candidates to
speak, and equal time for Senators to speak in favor of
each candidate. At no time shall any negative or "con"
debate be allowed.
B. The Senate President shall vote only to break a tie.
In the event of candidates or voting blocs running unopposed
in any election at the deadline of declaration of candidacy
filing, the candidates or voting blocs shall be declared the
winner of the election, in accordance with Chapter 703 o.

Title
This act shall be known as the Medica l School Council Act of
2007
IL:.. Authority
There shall be an organization of the Student Government
Association known as the Medical School Council (MSC) . which
shall be bound by these student body statutes including, but
not limited to the Finance Code. and which shall be placed
under the operational and allocation authority , and oversight
of the Congress of Graduate Students (COGS). Both COGS and MSC
shall be authorized to create rules pertaining to the day-to-
day operation of the Board, and to expand upon this statute ,
but all rules shall not conflict with Chapter 806 . 6 of the
Student Body Statutes.
Purpose:
The purpose of the Medical School Council (MSC) shall be to
represent the Recognized Student Organizations of the Medical
School before other entities of the Student Government
Association , as well as before the budgetary committees of the
Congress of Graduate Students, and to sub-appropriate funds to
recog nized student organizations under the j urisdiction of MSC
and to enhance medical education at the Florida State
University by promoting a variety of s peakers . conference and
academic projects and to expre s s the wi l l of the medical
students through resolutions and to monitor and coordinate the
budget activities of the various medi cal school organization s
with in their jurisdiction .

elected by the medical students . A seventh member of
the Board, the MSC reoresentative to COGS shall be a
medical student appointed by the MSC President, who must

The Homecoming Executive Council
Title
There shall be an entity of Student Government known as
the Homecoming Executive Council .
Purpose and Intent
The Homecoming Executive Council, hereinafter referred
to as HEC, shall unite the Florida State University's
administration, faculty, alumni and students in an
inclusive celebration of the University's past
accomplishments, present projects and future
initiatives.
Membership
A. The Advisor to the Homecoming Executive Committee
shall be the Assistant Director of Student
Activities for Special Event Planning in the
Oglesby Union .
B. The Homecoming Executive Council shall include , but
not be limited to, Director of Homecoming and
Assistant Director of Homecoming appointed by the
Student Body President.
C. The Student Body President must forward his/her
candidates to the Senate by January 31 of every
year . In the case that this is not done , all
applicants will be sent to the Senate for
appointment at the next regularly scheduled
session .
Procedures for Selection of Homecoming Committee
There shall be a committee that interviews
candidates for Homecoming Committee positions.
L This committee must consist of the Homecoming
Director and Assistant Director, Chief of
Staff. three (3) Senate appointments, SGA
Advisor and the Homecoming Advisor. The two
( 2) advisors will be non-voting members of
the committee.
£.:_ The Senate President must appoint his/her
three (3) Senate appointments for the
committee by January 31 of every year.

JL The Homecoming Director has the a uthority to set
the schedule for the committee but all candidates
must be forwarded before Spring Break .
No candidates for committee positions can be
forwarded until the committee interviews and
deliberates on all possible applicants.
Power and Duties
A . HEC shall :
1. Govern the time line and event purposes set
forth by the Homecoming Commission.
2. Organize events and spirit activities to
unite the campus.
3 . Submit the annual Homecoming Budget for the
entire student body to the Senate Budget
Committee.
4. Be the student body's representative member
of the Overall University Homecoming
Committee as appointed by the Student Body
President.
S. Govern the rules and regulations of spirit
activities .
6. Pursue and include all Student Government
entities in events and activities.
B . The Advisor for the HEC shall:
1. Work in collaboration with the Homecoming
Director and Deputy Director in recruiting a
committee to plan and execute Homecoming
events.
2. Support and advis e the Homecoming Executive
Committee in planning, marketing and
executing homecoming events and activities.
3 . Exercise fiduciary responsibility by aiding
in negotiations of all contracts and
agreements related to Homecoming activities.
4. Initial all requisitions for expenditure of
funds before forwarding them to the SGA
Accounting Office for signature and
processing.
C. The Homecoming Director shall appoint Assistant

1. HEC shall adopt bylaws for its organization,

3. HEC shall hold two (2) "Student Homecoming Feedback
Meetings" where all students and organization heads
are invited to provide feedback and suggestions for
the next year. These meetings shall be promoted
and publicized 48 hours in advance in the FSView,
and should be held within three (3) weeks of the
conclusion of Homecoming Week.
4. HEC shall hold fall meetings to distribute

BILL 33
Chapter 416
416.1
416.2
416.3
Annual Budget Procedures Act of 2007
Purpose
This act is to establish a procedure by which the annual
A&S Fee Budget of the Senate is produced and passed.
Scope
The.Annual A&S Fee Budget (the Budget) shall be passed
in compliance with the provisions of this act and all
applicable State of Florida Administrative Code. No
exceptions are authorized other than those specified
within.
Procedures for Passage of the Budget
A.:. The Budget shall not be approved by the Senate in a
Summer Session.
B. An estimated amount of the Budget shall be used to
submit to the Senate President for First Reading by the
Chairperson of the Budget Committee no later than the
second Senate meeting of the Fall semester. Hearings
may be held at the discretion of the Chairman of the
Budget Committee.
C. When the Budget has been approved in whole by the Budget
Committee it will be heard in Second Reading. The
Chairperson of the Budget Committee will provide to the
Senate Program Assistant copies of the Budget as
presented. All Senators will have copies available to
them of the proposed allocations. The Budget shall be
on the calendar for a minimum of one (1) week with
proposed allocations before passage.
D. The Budget shall be approved by Senate no later than the
beginning of the fiscal year of which it affects. The
Chairperson of the Budget Committee shall make a good-
faith effort to complete the Budget no later than
October 15 of each year.
E. The Budget and Proviso language cannot be approved
separately. Chanaes to the Proviso language may be made
via resolution at any point before the Budget is
approved by the Board of Trustees. This resolution
shall be passed with a two-thirds (2/3) vote of Senate.

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
~
F.
G.
H.
I.
Amendments to the Budget must follow a two-thirds (2/3)
vote to unlock a specific line item and category of the
Budget or a line of the Proviso language. Any amendment
which affects the allocation amount in any line of any
recipient shall require a three-fourths (3/4) vote of
Senate.
1. The majority by which amendments must be passed may be
increased to no more than four-fifths (4/5) via
resolution of the Senate.
2. Amendments may only be made to a specific category of
one recioient. Each amendment to a category shall
require a separate four-fifths (4/5) vote.
Hearings, deliberations. and meetings of the Budget
committee are public and shall be advertised in Senate.
The Chairperson of the Budget Committee shall not
exclude any student from witnessina the hearings or
deliberations in accordance with Chapter 409 of the
Student Body Statutes.
The Budget shall be passed by a roll-call vote.
simple majority is required for passage.
A
If the Budget is failed in Senate, the Budget Committee
shall create a new budget with substantial chanaes
within three ( 3) weeks of the Budget's failure in
Senate.
J. Each recipient of monies from the Budget shall make a
budget request. The Budget Committee shall hold
hearings during which budget requests are defended.
Each recipient of the Budget shall have a seoarate
hearing. The Budget Committee is authorized to fund
more than the amount requested.

To receive funds an organization must officially

Bill 51
Chapter 205 Code of Ethics
205.1
205.2
205.3
History: Amended 44th Senate Bill 140. Amended by 49th Senate
Bill 14. Revised by the 50th Senate Bill 2. Revised by the
56~ Senate Bills 23 and 109.
This act shall be entitled "the Student Government Code of
Ethics." The intent of this code is to strengthen the faith
and confidence of the Student Body in Student Government.
Legislative intent and declaration of policy.
A. It is essential to the proper conduct and operation of
Student 8overnncent Body that its officials be
independent and impartial, and that public office not be
used for private gain. Student Sove?:nncent Body officers
and employees hold their position for the benefit of the
Student Body. Such officers and employees are bound to
observe in their official acts the highest standards of
ethics consistent with this code, recognizing that
promoting the public interest and maintaining the
respect of the student body in their Student Government
must be the foremost concern.
B. It is the intent of this act to protect the integrity of
Student Government by prescribing conflicts of interest
and unethical practices. It shall serve as the basis of
discipline for those who violate its provisions.
C. Any student has the right to file a complaint when they
feel that a violation of the Code of Ethics has occurred
with the Student Supreme Court.
1. Any organization has the right to establish
additional ethical criteria or penalties in its
constitution and bylaws.
Standards of Conduct
A. In order to preserve the integrity of the Florida State
University Student Government Association, its officers
and employees must disclose all potential or actual
conflicts of interests.
1. Conflict of Interest means any business or
professional activity or direct or indirect
financial interest that would place a person in a
position where there is an opportunity to disregard
the public interests of the student body for his or
her own private interests.

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
B.
2. No officer or employee will judge or vote on any
matter which would affect his or her private gain.
3. Any vote, action, or j udgencent judgment performed
by an officer or employee who has a conflict of
interest may be appealed with the Student Supreme
Court. This must be done in a written, signed
complaint submitted no later than three (3) days
after the vote, act, or judgencent judgment in which
the conflict occurs.
a. In Student Senate, a written and signed
complaint shall be filed with the chair of
Rules of Calendar, who will investigate that
matter within 48 hours of receipt of
complaint. Upon cause, the Chair shall
forward the complaint and findings and a
recommendation for penalties to the Student
Supreme Court. The Student Supreme Court
shall assign penalties for any Senator or
officer of Senate who acts, judges, or votes
with a conflict of interest.
Misuse of Student Government Property: No officer or
employee will use or attempt to use Student Government
property, facilities, resources, or personnel to secure
a gift, reward, privilege, benefit or exemption for
anyone.
1. No officer or employee will disclose information
not available to the general public for his or her
personal gain or for the personal gain of any other
person or organization.
C. Unlawful Compensation: No officer or employee shall
solicit, accept, provide or attempt to provide any
material items of value in cases that would influence or
appear to influence any vote, action, or judgement
judgment.
D. Inducing to Act: No officer or employee shall knowingly
aid, advise, encourage or threaten another officer or
employee of Student Government or student to act in
violation of this chapter, Federal, State and local
laws, the Florida State University Student 9overument
Association Body Constitution and Statutes, the Student
Code of Conduct or Academic Honor code.
E. Fraud in Student Government
1. No officer or employee will willfully misrepresent
himself or herself while acting in his or her
official capacity.

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
205.4
205.5
2. No officer or employee will withhold information or
documentation when mandated or provide false or
misleading information or documentation.
3. No officer or employee will bring false charges or
provide false or misleading evidence against
another officer, employee or student.
F. No officer or employee will practice any discrimination
as defined in the Student Government Anti-Discrimination
Policy.
1. No officer or employee will deny any student rights
guaranteed by the Federal and State Constitution,
or the Florida State University Student Sove:r:nn,ent
Body Constitution and Statutes.
2. No officer or employee will deny any student the
right to due process or the right to an impartial
hearing or trial.
Penalties
Any violation of this chapter may be grounds for impeachment,
suspension or dismissal from employment.
A. Conviction of violating this Code shall not preclude
prosecution as a violation of the Student Code of
Conduct or, where applicable, Academic Honor Code.
B. Any person found guilty of violating two (2) or more
provisions of this Code shall not be allowed to hold a
Student Government office in the future.
Protection Against Adverse Action Against Disclosing
Information: No officer or employee of Student Government will
dismiss, discipline or take adverse action against a Student
Government officer or employee for disclosing information
pursuant to the provisions of this section.
A. Disclosure protected under this rule shall be defined
as:
1. Any violation or suspected violation of any
Federal, State, or local laws, the Florida State
University Student 8ove:r:nn,ent Association Body
Constitution and Statutes, the Florida State
University Student Code of Conduct or Academic
Honor Code.
2. Any act or suspected act
malfeasance or nonfeasance as
constitution and Statutes.

defined by SGA

Procedures:
A. Enforcement of the SGA Ethics Code shall be the
jurisdiction of the Student Supreme Court. All ethics
complaints shall be heard by the Student Supreme Court.
B. Upon receipt of a written signed complaint of any
student, the Student Supreme Court shall hear the
complaint within 48 hours of receipt.
C. The court may issue any writs necessary.
Penalties
Upon finding a violation (s) of the SGA Ethics Code, the
Student Supreme Court shall assign penalties. Such penalties
shall consist of, at the Court's discretion: suspension, or
recommendation to begin impeachment proceedings, or
recommendation to Senate to freeze an organization's funding.
1. Violation ( s) of the Ethics Code does not preclude
prosecution under the Student Conduct Code or Academic
Honor Code.
Appeal:
Both plaintiff and defendant have the right to appeal the
decision of the Student Supreme Court to the Vice President
for Student Affairs. Appeals must be submitted within three
(3) days of the decision of the Supreme Court.
In accordance with the laws of the State of Florida, any
elected or appointed officer of the Student Body who has been
convicted of a felony shall be immediately dismissed from
Student Body office, and shall be prohibited from ever holding
a Student Body office again, unless his or her conviction is
vacated in a court of law, or upon pardon by the Governor of
the State of Florida or the President of the United States of
America.

712.1 Ballot Form
A. An electronic ballot shall be defined as the official
format chosen by the Supervisor of Elections which
shall include the official rules, instructions,
candidates and other information pertinent to
elections.
B. Should a problem occur with the defined electronic
ballot which prevents a student from voting, a paper
ballot with the same content as the electronic ballot
shall be distributed to those students wishing to
vote.
c. The official ballot contains the list of all vacant
offices to be filled, referendum questions, and
constitutional amendments. Absentee ballots shall
consist of a copy of the official ballot, and
instructions for voting.
h No colors shall be used to designate or
accentuate any choices on the official ballot.
including but not limited to: candidates for
office. political party affiliation or lack
thereof. referendum questions, and constitutional
amendments.
D. Candidates shall be listed by seat in alphabetical
order of their last names and the name shall be
printed in the same form as requested at the time of
filing.
1. For the election of Student Body President and
Vice President, the names of the candidate for
President and Vice President within the same
party (if applicable) must appear on the ballot
as one voting bloc.
2. For elections for the Black Student Union, the
names of the candidates for Director and
Assistant Director positions within the same
party (if applicable) must appear on the ballot
as one voting bloc.

BILL 75
Chapter 1109
1109.1
1109.2
Men Advocating Responsible Conduct at Florida State
University
Adoption and Purpose
~ Adoption
There shall be an affiliated project of the Student
Government Association known as Men Advocating
Responsible Conduct, hereinafter referred to as
"MARC."
Campus Affiliation
MARC shall be affiliated with the Florida State
University Division of Student Affairs, whose
relationship is severable providing that another
campus affiliate has been found and approved in
accordance with the Student Body Statutes, or the
Student Government Association should lawfully end
this affiliation.
Purpose
1...:.. MARC shall serve as a forum for male students
at the Florida State University who seek to
educate their male peers concerning the
importance of appropriate and responsible
behavior in all aspects of university life.
L MARC shall provide programming whose purpose
is to raise awareness and disseminate
information concerning the ideals of
responsible conduct and the message of rape
prevention and education to students at FSU.
h MARC may, in conjunction with the Victim
Advocate Program at FSU, provides individual
and group intervention for male students who
are either primary or secondary victims of
sexual violence.
Campus Board of Directors
Function

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
There shall be a campus wide Board of Directors,
hereinafter referred to as the Board, which shall
serve as a liaison between the MARC support staff
and leadership, the Student Government Association,
and the campus affiliate. The Board will establish
its own criteria for meetings and rules of
procedure within the confines of this legislation.
Powers and Duties
.!..:.. The Board shall ensure that all university
policies and procedures are followed, make
recommendations regarding the selection and
termination of the MARC Coordinator and
Assistant Coordinator; the establishment of
the Board's meeting criteria and rules of
procedure; the approval of annual budget
requests to the Student Government
Association; the aooroval of any budget
amendment recommendation; and shall approve
all new MARC programming.
£.:.. The Board shall meet no less than once a
month and all meetings must be advertised in
a widely distributed campus publication.
Composition
The Board of Directors shall consist of seven
(7) voting members, no less than four (4) of
which shall be students at Florida State
University and no less than two (2) of which
shall\be members of the FSU faculty/staff.
The student members shall consist of one (1)
member selected by Greek Life, one (1)
student member selected by University Housing
and two (2) student members selected by the
Student Body President subject to Senate
confirmation.
~ These positions must be advertised to
all students in both an internal forum
and in a widely distributed camous
publication chosen by the Board.
h The three (3) faculty/staff positions shall
include, the Director of the Victim Advocate
Program as well as two (2) additional
faculty/staff members selected by the
Director of Victim Advocate.

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
1109.3
The Director of the Women's Center or their
designee shall serve as an ex-officio non-
voting member.
IL.. Term of Office
L The student positions shall serve a one-year
term.
£..:.· The faculty/staff members shall serve as long
as they hold their appropriate positions in
the university or until they shall
voluntarily relinquish this position.
Minutes
All meetings of the Board shall be recorded by a
member of the Board in accordance with its own
rules of procedure. These minutes will be provided
to all members of the Board within two (2) weeks of
the meeting and copies will be provided to the
Director of the Victim Advocate Program where they
must be kept on file for a period of three (3)
years for public inspection.
In order to protect the identities of
sensitive participants, names shall be
omitted in the minutes, but shall be kept by
a faculty/staff member of the Board and only
surrendered to appropriate authorities with
appropriate authorization.
The MARC Coordinator
A.:_ Adoption
There shall be a Coordinator of MARC.
Powers and Duties
The MARC Coordinator will ensure the
compliance of MARC with all Student
Government, University. and State
regulations.
The MARC Coordinator shall serve as the
administrator of the day to day program
operations of MARC and in the application and
implementation of programs approved by the
Board.
The MARC Coordinator shall supervise the
appropriate expenditure of all funds
available to the program either through A&S

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
1109.4
1109.5
or self-generated in conjunction with the
SA&O Office. The Coordinator will submit
monthly expenditure reports to the Board.
The MARC Coordinator shall serve as an
authorized signature authority .
.2..:,. The MARC Coordinator shall attend and Chair
all Board meetings.
MARC Assistant Coordinator
a.:.. Adoption
There shall be an Assistant Coordinator of MARC who
shall be supervised by the Coordinator.
Powers and Duties
L The Assistant Coordinator shall serve and
assist the Coordinator as he/she sees fit
providing that such service does not violate
any other duties outlined herein.
The Assistant Coordinator shall publicize
MARC to the university campus and surrounding
community.
J....:.. The Assistant Coordinator shall serve as the
primary liaison between the MARC and other
campus and community organizations.
!...:.. The Assistant Coordinator shall serve as an
authorized signature authority .
.2..:.. The Assistant Coordinator shall attend all
Board meetings and serve as Chair in the
Coordinators absence.
Operations
Program Policy
The policies of MARC shall be established by the
Board and implemented by the appropriate personnel.
Copies of all program proposals. rules of
procedure. policies and guidelines shall be
submitted to the Senate Program Assistant for
public inspection and all other relevant university
supervisory entities.
Facilities

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
MARC will operate in the space provided by the
appropriate entities and shall be maintained by the
Florida State University. MARC will not share
space with any other organization other than its
affiliate in order to maintain its autonomy.

BILL 79
Chapter 1011
1011.1
1011.2
1011. 3
Institute for Liberal Studies
Creation and Purpose
A.:.. Creation
This act shall create an agency of the Student
Government Association known as the "Institute for
Liberal Studies" (ILS).
Purpose
The ILS shall:
L
Membership
Be a forum for presenting a liberal
perspective to thought on educational,
political, philosophical and social issues.
Facilitate and foster communication between
like-minded liberal and progressive
organizations.
Work with other campus and community
organizations in order to encouraae
collective action campaigns which will
benefit FSU students and the community.
Provide guest lectures, workshops, and other
liberal and progressive programs.
Provide the programming without charging a
fee.
Participation is open to all students, facultv and staff
of the Florida State University and to members of the
Tallahassee community.
Executive Board
Membership of the Executive Board shall consist of
students. The Executive Board will include the
positions of Director, Assistant Director,
Secretary, Financial Officer, Communications
Director and a Public Relations Officer. The other
two Executive Board positions will be assigned and
titled based on the Director and Assistant
Director's prerogative. There will also be an ex-

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
officio advisor who shall serve on the Board, he or
she will be selected by the Board.
Selection and Term of Office
Director and Assistant Director
The Board will interview all applicants for
director and assistant director and forward
their recommendation(s) to the Student Body
President. The orocess then follows in
accordance with Chapter 1000.5 C and D of the
Executive Agency Act.
sl:.. If the Director or Assistant Director
intends to serve ILS again in either
position, they may not take part in the
interviewing and forwarding of
applicants for the position of Director
and Assistant Director.
The Director's and Assistant Director's
term in office shall end at the close
of the spring semester. However, the
Director or Assistant Director may
serve more than one term if reappointed
by the proper authority in accordance
with Chapter 1000.5 C and D.
Other Executive Board Positions
Once a new Director and Assistant Director
are approved they then will interview
candidates for all positions on the Executive
Board. Former Executive Board members may
apply but are not guaranteed a position on
the new Executive Board. The Director and
Assistant Director will forward their
recommendation to the Student Body President.
The process then follows in accordance with
Chapter 1000.5 c (2) of the Executive Agency
Act. The Executive Board will oversee the
day-to-day operations of the agency until the
newly appointed Director and Assistant
Director take office.
sl:.. The Executive Board may not schedule
any events or place any orders
requiring the expenditure of agency
funds during this oversight period.

sections.heading: Page 5
sections.text:
Meetings
L The Executive Board shall meet at least twice
a month during the academic vear. The
"academic year" commences on the first
official day of classes for the fall term and
ends on the last official day of classes for
the spring term. The official dates are
those so stipulated by the Office of the
Registrar.
Meetings during the summer term shall
be held at the discretion of the
chairperson.
The Executive Board may take no official
action unless a quorum is present.
All Executive Board members shall receive at
least forty-eight (48} hours notice prior to
an unscheduled meeting or cancellation of the
regularly scheduled meeting. This provision
may be waived if the Director can demonstrate
that exigent circumstances exists.
The Director shall designate the time and
place for regular Board meetings at the
beginning of the academic year. The Director
or Assistant Director or a majority of the
Board in accordance with paragraph 3 above
may call any other Board meetings.
Powers and Duties of the Executive Board
The Executive Board shall work towards identifying,
developing and monitoring programs and campaigns
that express the needs of liberal and progressive
students while giving them a voice at the Florida
State University, thereby increasing awareness of
liberal and progressive views.
L The Director shall:
Be the chairperson of all functions,
meetings, or anv related activities
concerning ILS, with the approval of
the Executive Board unless the
chairperson responsibility is
delegated.
Have the power to create and oversee
all standing committees.

sections.heading: Page 6
sections.text:
Be responsible for the efficient and
effective operation of the ILS Office
on a daily basis.
Execute decisions on policy, procedure,
and activities in the best interest of
the agency.
~ Appoint and remove staff members at
his/her discretion, upon consultation
with the Assistant Director.
L Be one of the two signatures from ILS
required to spend funds.
9..:.. Ensure that all voices on the Executive
Board are heard and given due
considerations .
.6..:.. The Assistant Director shall:
~ Assume all duties and responsibilities
of the Director in the event that he or
she is absent.
Be the co-chair of all functions,
meetings or any related activities
concerning ILS, with the approval of
the Executive Board unless the co-
chair's responsibility is delegated.
Serve on the Student Government and
University committees that require
executive agency representation.
Have the power to implement ad hoc
committees.
The Secretary shall:
Prepare the minutes for the Executive
Board.
Post the minutes of the Executive Board
by at least 72 hours following the
meeting.
£.:.. Maintain an updated ILS member roster
and email list.
Be responsible for the upkeep of files
and records in the ILS Office.

sections.heading: Page 7
sections.text:
1011. 4
L The Financial Officer shall:
Be notified and consulted before the
Director and Assistant Director
authorize the expenditure of any ILS
funds.
Be responsible for the upkeep of
financial records for ILS.
Be the second of two signatures from
ILS required to spend ILS funds .
.2...:.. The Communications Director shall:
~ Act as the agency's liaison to other
like-minded campus and community
organizations.
Be responsible for maintaining the
agency's correspondence and responding
to inquiries in a prompt fashion .
.§..:_ The Public Relations Officer shall:
Ensure that the agency is aware of all
campus events especially those of other
agencies.
12....:_ Be resoonsible for publicizing all ILS
events. Publicizing includes but is
not limited to press releases,
chalking, posting and flyers.
Remaining Two (2) Executive Board Members
The two (2) remaining Executive Board
positions will be filled based on the needs
of the agency as decided by the Director and
Assisted Director. The title of these two
(2) positions is left to the discretion of
the Director and Assistant Director.
The Steering Committee
The Steering Committee will exist to help foster
communication and encourage collective action among
all liberal and progressive organizations on
campus.
Voting membership in the Steering Committee will
include the entirety of the Board of Directors, as
well as representatives from like-minded
organizations, and at-large members appointed by

sections.heading: Page 8
sections.text:
1011. 5
1011. 6
the Director. The Director or his/her designee
will Chair the committee.
L Each like minded organization will appoint no
more than three members to the Committee.
~ "Like-minded organization" status will
be determined by the Board.
l..:_ At no point will at-larqe membership
constitute more than two-thirds (2/3) of the
committee's membership.
The Steering Committee will oversee the collective
action campaigns with which the agency is involved,
and appoint subcommittees for purposes specified by
the committee.
The Steerinq Committee will have no authority over
agency resources of any kind, and can onlv utilize
agency resources with the consent of a majority of
the Board.
Removal from Office
Director
The Board may. by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of its
members, recommend the removal of the Director.
Staff
The Director shall have the authority to dismiss
staff members upon consultation with the Assistant
Director.
Vacancies
Director
Upon vacancy of the Director's position. the
Assistant Director shall assume the position of
director until a replacement is secured.
~ Assistant Director and Executive Board Member
positions.
The Vacancy will be advertised for three (3) days.
The recommendations will then be forwarded to the
Student Body President. This process will then
follow in accordance with Chapter 1000.5 C (2)and
1000.5 D. of the Executive Branch.

sections.heading: Page 9
sections.text:
Vacancies shall be filled by the original process
set forth herein and the person filling the vacancy
shall serve the remainder of the term of office.
In the event that the Student Body President, or
other statutory authority rejects recommendation by
the Board said authority must provide written
explanation for rejection.

The Florida State University Student Government in the
Sunshine Law
This Act is to be entitled the "Florida State University
Student Government in the Sunshine Act" referred to hereafter
as the "Sunshine Act."
Definitions
The following definitions shall be fully applicable for the
purpose of this act.
"The Public" shall be defined as any member of the
Student Body who is neither an officer nor candidate for
office in the Student Government Association, as well as
University faculty and staff unaffiliated with Student
Government, as well as any person not affiliated with
the Florida State University or the Student Government
Association.
"Student Government Affiliates" shall be defined as all
officers and candidates for office in the Student
Government Association, as well as all staff members of
the same.
All meetings held under the auspices of Student Government,
except as otherwise provided in the Constitution, at which
official acts are to be taken, are declared open to the public
at all times. No resolution, rule, or formal action shall be
considered binding, except if enacted at such meeting.
Student Government Affiliates shall be entitled to attend all
meetings held under the auspices of Student Government except
as provided for in these statutes, in the Senate Rules of
Procedure, or any other duly authorized Rule of Procedure.
There shall be no less than five (5) minutes aggregate
reserved at the beginning of any meeting held under the
auspices of Student Government for members of the Public and
all Student Government Affiliates to address those assembled
upon application by any member of the Student Body.
The minutes of any meeting under this chapter shall be
recorded at the time of the meeting and such records shall be
open to the public and to Student Government Affiliates. The
Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction to issue injunctions to
enforce the purposes of this chapter upon application by any
member of the Student Body.

Dear Mr. Senate President:
Below is the justification for the presidential veto of Senate Bill 94:
Although I appreciate the spirit of Bill 94, I have vetoed the bill because of the proposed
section C of 806.7. This section, which prohibits all transfers_from the contractual
services category, does not allow for the level of flexibility required given such a
transient population of student leadership and the upcoming tight fiscal years.
Since the Student Government Association budget is done a year in advance before the
money can- be used, and new students assume leadership roles in organizations in each
year, we must allow for flexibility in the different visions for programming (e.g.,
programming that does include a contractual service exp~nditure) that comes with new
leadership. Moreover, the student government association is entering into very
conservative fiscal years, with frozen enrollment andlnew fees being assessed by the
university. In the years to come, we will need to be creative in our budgeting, and we
~ should not limit ourselves before the process has even begun.
Finally, since the largest of these transfers from the contractual services category must
already be approved by Senate, there is still strong oversight over these allocations. I
hope that the bill can be resubmitted for a Senate vote with the section C of 806. 7
removed.
Sincerely,

History: Amended by the 56 th Senate Bill 72. Revised by the

Title and Purpose
Title
This act shall be known as the Funding Board Act.
Purpose
This Act shall apply to the Funding Boards: Greek Council,
Law School Appropriations Council, Business School
Allocation Committee, Sport Club Distribution Council,
College of Music Allocation Committee, the Black Student
Assembly, and the College of Engineering Allocation
Committee. Hereinafter, these Funding Boards shall
individually be referred to as Greek Council, LSAC, BSAC,
SCDC, CMAC, BSA, and CEAC respectively and collectively as
Boards.
Compliance with the A&S Guidelines
Each Board will be required to make a report to Senate
President and the Student Body Treasurer whenever business
has been conducted as a committee.
All funding boards must meet at least once a month as long
as unallocated funds in their accounts exist.
The Student Body Treasurer and the Business Manager of SGA
Accounting shall have the responsibility and oversight of
the funding boards for purposes of enforcing the Finance
Code and Student Body Statutes.
Funding boards may not allocate funds in the semester in
which they will be spent, with the exception of emergency
funding, Sweepings and Central Reserves. Funding Boards
with full time advisors may submit allocations for funds
used in the same semester as the allocation hearings with
the approval of the SGA Advisor.
Procedures and Requirements to Receive Funds
To receive funds an organization must officially register
with the Florida State University Student Activities
Center.

In Fall 2007, the opposite situation
happened. The Senate passed Bill 99, which
was subsequently signed into law. Just
before this bill was passed, the polls were
scheduled to open approximately 27 days
and 12 hours later. Bill 99 moved the
election forward by one week, such that
there were then just 20 days and 12 hours
before the election was to begin.

· Chapter 700 of the Florida State
Student Body Statutes states "[t]he Election
Code shall not be changed within three (3)
weeks of an election." This statute has been
in effect for at least the past three years,
meaning that both Bills 79 and 99 were
subject to this limitation that the Senate
placed on itself by statute.
It is clear that the Senate can limit its
own power by enacting Chapter 700. See
Grimes v. O'Shea, SP07-02 (FSU SSC
2007), POOLE, J., dissenting. H9wever,
what is not clear is how Chapter 700 should
be applied. Did the Senate violate Chapter
700's limitation on changing the election
code "within three (3) weeks" by enacting
Bill 79, which moved the election from
slightly less than three weeks in the future to
slightly less than four weeks in the future, or
by enacting Bill 99, which did the reverse?
To answer this question, we must
first analyze the purpose of Chapter 700.
The wording of this section makes it clear
that its purpose is to preyent s~Wf:antive
changes to the election code just prior· ~? an
election. But what happens when the
change being made is the date of the
election? How then is three weeks to be
measured?
Bill 79's change extended the time
before the election was to take place. Thus,
the end result was an expansion of the time
period from slightly less than three weeks to
more than three weeks. In contrast, Bill 99's
change reduced the time period, such that
the end result was slightly less than three
weeks. Therefore, while Bill 79 did not
interfere with the three-week period during
which no substantive changes could be
made, Bill 99 did so interfere. Accordingly,
we hold that BjlJ 79 was lawfully enacted in
conjunction with Chapter 700, but that Bill
99 violated the terms of Cha2ter 700.
To be clear, Chapter 700 is a statute,
not a Constitutional provision. This means
the Senate could have repealed it before
passage of Bill 99, and that bill would have
been completely legitimate. However, the
Senate failed to recognize this self-imposed
limitation. As a result, all of Bill 99 must be
ex.duded from the Student Body Statutes.
III.
If the content of Bill 99 is eliminated
from the Student Body Statutes, what
remains is the prior language, the content of
Bill 79. This means that Statute §704.4
should currently state that the election is to
occur on the "seventh Wednesday" of the
Fall semester, Statute §704.3 should state
that the filing deadline is the "sixth
Monday" of the Fall semester, and Statute
§704.4 should state that campaigning shall
begin on the "sixth Wednesday" of the Fall
semester.
These statutes correspond to the
following dates in 2007: The filing deadline
is 12pm on Monday, October 15\
campaigning may begin on Wednesday
October 3rd, and the election must occur on
Wednesday, October 10th. We hold these to
be the correct dates for the Fall 2007
elections.
IV.

not professionals witl1 large staffs and that
as a result the type of sloppiness that
occurred here should be excused. While we
recognize that we are all students with busy
lives, we also recognize .that we all
voluntarily undertook the responsibilities
with which we are currently charged. There
is absolutely no reason why any of us should
fail to at least make a serious attempt to
carry out those responsibilities to the fullest

The Student Government Association Training Act
History: Added by the 48th Senate Bill 165. Revised by
the 52nd Senate Bill 66. Revised by the 54~ Senate Bills
17 and 57. Revised by the 56 th Senate Bills 70 and 109.
The purpose of this legislation is to insure that all
officials of the Florida State University, Student
Government Association have received adequate training
in the areas of fiscal and ethical responsibility in the
allocation and expenditure of state funds collected
through the Activity and Service Fee.
All SGA officials holding a major office as well as
members of the Congress of Graduate Students are
required to conform to the provisions of this Statute.
The Student Body President, Chief Justice of the Supreme
Court, Chairperson of the Union Board, Chairperson of
the Campus Recreation Board, Senior Class Council
President, Speaker of the Congress of Graduate Students,
and the Directors of all Executive Agencies, Bureaus and
Affiliated Projects, as well as all Funding Board
Chairpersons shall conduct an appropriate training
program suitable to the needs of the members of their
respective organizations within four (4) weeks of the
fall SGA elections in which the members of their
respective organizations have been elected. The content
of such training programs shall be at the discretion of
the officers listed in the beginning of this section,
and shall be directed at teaching new members about the
SGA Constitution and St~tutes, and all pertinent
procedures encountered during the operation of their
respective organizations.
The Student Senate President in conjunction with the
Vice President for Student Affairs shall and the
Director of Student Affairs be required to conduct a
seminar for newly elected Senators d1:1rin9 the first
three (3) weeks of the Pall and Spxing Senate sessions
following SSls: elections. To fall some time between
elections night and the second official session of the
new Senate. The Senate President may appoint a Senator
to fulfill all or part of this duty if he/she so
chooses. The seminar will be a training session.:.. to
cover the Stodent Body Constit1:1tion and Stat1:1tes, the
Senate Rules of Proced1:1re, Robex t Rules of Ordex, as
well as any applicable paxlian~ntary pxoced1:1res.

207.5 A.

Though not mandated, it is recommended that the training
agenda include:
1...:.. A thorough tutorial in Senate Rules of Procedure .
.6...:.. The organization and structure of the Student Body
Constitution and Statutes.
h The budgetary and fiscal structure of SGA funding
sources, regulations, and expenditures.
~ Workshops for Bill, Constitutional Amendment, and
Resolution writing .
.2...:.. The purpose and functions of each standing Senate
Committee .
.2....:.. Conclude with a mock Senate emphasizing proper
adherence to the Senate Rules of Procedure, the
details of which are to be determined by the Senate
leadership.
Following the Senate Retreat or informational seminar,
it shall be the responsibility of the Senate Pro Tempore
to assign a Senior Senator (one who has been in office
for more than one term) to an incoming Senator as
his/her mentor. Like procedures shall be followed for
forwarded Senators. The purpose of such a mentoring
program shall be to help new Senators learn the
appropriate techniques for writing legislation, master
the rules and procedures that govern Senate and
understand the responsibilities and duties of being a
Senator. If a significant problem (such as differences
in campus party ideology) arises between a mentor and
mentee, either Senator may petition the Senate Pro
Tempore for reassignment.
A voluntary survey to ascertain the efficiency of the
program will be conducted by the Senate Pro Tempore at
the last meeting of each Senate term.
Throughout the term it shall be the purview and
responsibility of the Senate Pro Tempore to provide
continuing education for new Senators and to ensure that
they are equipped with all the tools necessary for being
an active participant in the legislative process.

Chapter 701 Definitions
701.1 The following words and phrases, when used in this title shall
be defined as follows:
A. Campaigning - The publicizing or solicitation of support

office of the Student Body, and calling forth the action

or services paid for or received by the campaign for the
purpose of advertising candidates, advertising political

-an the action to vote. This shall include setup or
production fees, sales tax, or any other secondary costs
for goods and services.

campaigning that do not call for the action to vote
shall not constitute a campaign expense. This
shall include all campaign materials.

Composition of the Elections Commission
702.1 A. The Elections Commission shall be composed of five (5)
FSU students selected by the Chief Justice of the
Student Supreme Court. Alternate(s) shall be selected
by the Supreme Court Chief Justice to fill absences.
The Business Manager of SA&O, the SGA Advisor, and the
Supervisor of Elections shall serve as ex-officio non-
voting members. Quorum for meetings shall be no less
than three (3) of the five (5) voting members.
702.2
B.
1. The Elections Commission must convene for the first
time no later than three (3) weeks prior to any
election. The Commission shall elect a chair by a
majority vote of no less than quorum. The Business
Manager of SA&O and the Supervisor of Elections
shall be jointly responsible for convening this
meeting.
No member of the Elections Commission shall be a
candidate for Student Government office. No member of
the Elections Commission shall be affiliated in any way
with a political party.
C. Upon just cause and in a written and signed request to
the Student Government Association Advisor, any
candidate for office shall have the right to request a
recusal of any member of the Elections Commission. The
SGA Advisor shall investigate the complaint and upon
finding merit, that member must recuse himself or
herself.
Powers and Duties of the Elections Commission
A. All actions of the Elections Commission shall require
the approval by a majority of present, voting members.
B. Submit recommendations regarding the Elections Code to
the Student Senate.

The Student Performing Arts Council
Title
There shall be an entity of the Student Government
Association known as the Student Performing Arts
Council.
Purpose and Intent
The Student Performing Arts Council, hereinafter
referred to as SPAC. shall unite the Florida State
University's student performance arts groups in an
effort to promote the arts on the campus of the Florida
State University and to educate the student body through
an arts initiative.
Membership
SPAC shall be led by two (2) members appointed by the
Student Body President and confirmed by the Senate:

organizations or his/her designee shall serve as a
board member of SPAC.

welcomed as affiliated members of SPAC.
Powers and Duties
SPAC shall:
h

performing arts groups on campus.
Produce and distribute a monthly calendar
that details the events being put on by SPAC
affiliated organizations.
Promote the student performance arts to the
Florida State University student body.
Provide a forum for the arts on the campus of
the Florida State University.

if a change of status is required.

G. Hear and act upon appeals against decisions of the

decisions by majority vote. The Rules of Procedure for
the Elections Commission shall be the _following:
1. The Elections Commission shall post their meeting
time 24 hours in advance.
2. The meeting time shall not conflict with Student
Senate, therefore not allowing a candidate running
for re-election to attend. If a conflict of
schedule exists. the affected candidate has until
three (3) hours prior to the Elections Commission

of the Spring semester, except, in the cases where the
election is within three (3) two (2) weeks of Spring Break.
In this case the election shall be at least held three (3)
weeks before Spring Break.

be held the Wednesde::y following the Sp:i: ing Break. No later
than the third Wednesday prior to the end of the Spring

BILL 33
400.5 "Majority" and "Two-Thirds" Votes
A majority vote shall be more than half of the votes cast by
Senators entitled to vote, excluding bl~nks o~ abstentions, at
any properly called meeting at which a quorum is present. A
two-thirds vote shall be at least two-thirds of the votes cast
by Senators entitled to vote, excluding blenks or abstentions,
at any properly called meeting at which a quorum is present.
A four-fifths vote shall be at least four-fifths of the votes
cast by Senators entitled to vote. ·excluding abstentions. at
any properly called meetings at which a quorum is present. In
both all three cases "entitled to vote" refers to Senators
actually casting a vote. for or against a measure before the
floor voting, not all Senators formally eligible to vote, with
no more than 15% of the votes cast being abstentions. In the
case that 15% or more of the votes cast are abstentions. a re-
vote is necessary. After three (3) consecutive votes. if no
decision is made. the bill will be sent back to committee.

r BILL 2006
Activity and Service Fee Budget
Proviso Language
Specia1 Instructions
I. General
A. Bill 2006 does not establish precedent for future funding levels of
annual budgets.
B. The Student Body Auditor shall insure that no A&S recipient charge
admission to students to any funded event, except as provided for
in the A&S Fee Guidelines, and shall recommend to the Student Body
President that any recipient that violates this provision have
their entire budget frozen immediately.
C. No A&S funded account may pay any stipend, wage, salary, or salary
increase to any positions not funded in Bill 2006 without express
consent of the Student Senate.
D. The Student Senate must be notified of any position
reclassification request before such requests are initiated through
the University Personnel Office which concerns moneys allocated in
Bill 2006. New budgets submitted to the A&S Fee Committee and
Senate Budget Committee shall note in writing any positions
reclassified during the previous year.
E. Monies allocated for the Homecoming Powwow may be used in
conjunction with a ticket price charged to students.
F. In the event of shortfalls in the budget due to clerical errors,
funds shall be withdrawn from Senate Projects, Senate Unallocated,
and Central Reserves, in that order. In the event of excess funds
in the budget due to clerical errors, the funds shall be deposited
into Senate Projects.
G. The 57th Student Senate strongly suggests that the VPSA consult
with the Student Senate in cases where projects will result in
future A&S fee increases.
H. The 57th Student Senate strongly recommends to the VPSA that
whenever USPS and A&P positions become vacant she consult with the
Student Senate in order to review the need for the positions.
II. CAMPUS RECREATION
A. It is the position of the 5 7th Student Senate that the Bobby E.
Leach Student Recreation Center and Intramural fields have been
primarily funded by student dollars and that these facilities'
first purpose is for student recreational purposes.

sections.heading: Page 7
sections.text:
B.
2
Any and all use of the Bobby E. Leach Student Recreation Center and
Intramural fields for activities other than student recreational
purposes must be approved by the Campus Recreation Board. If the
policies of this Board are violated, or if the Board is not
consulted, the Senate will recommend to the Student Body President
that the funds for the entire Bobby E. Leach Center be frozen
immediately until corrective action is taken.
C. No A&S dollars shall be used for the construction nor maintenance
of any facilities where students are not privy to at least 50% of
the usage.
III.UNIVERSITY UNION
A. All mini entertainment under Student Campus Entertainment shall be
free of charge to students with valid FSU identification cards,
excluding Breakfast for a Buck.
B. Revenue placed in the Headliner account shall be used for the
express purpose of bringing major concert acts for the
entertainment of the student body. This account shall be
administered by the Student Campus Entertainment office with input
from a committee appointed by the Headliners Concert Committee,
appointed by the Student Body President and approved by Senate. An
admission price may be charged to students in conjunction with
moneys used from this account. The Headliner Account shall not be
swept at the end of the fiscal year.
C. The 57 th Student Senate recommends that any A&S affiliate of the
Union to include Union Administration, consult with the Senate
before committing A&S dollars to any prospective program or
construction resulting in A&S dollar liability. Furthermore, the
57 th Student Senate requests that a representative sit on all
committees that govern the Union expenditures of A&S dollars.
IV. STUDENT ACTIVITIES AND ORGANIZATIONS
A. Monies allocated to the Student Government Administration
Account/Other are expressly intended for the payment of the
Newspaper Readership Program, membership within the Florida Student
Association, WRC, lobbyist, and telephones.
B. No SA&O recipient shall fund any Salary or OPS Wages position
without approval of the Student Senate.
c. Under no condition may A&S money be allocated to any organization
that is involved in political activity with the exception of the
lobbying office in the Executive Branch.
D. Funds for Greek Council shall be used only for activities that are
available to all FSU students. No more than thirty percent (30%) of

sections.heading: Page 8
sections.text:
3
the Greek Council budget shall be allocated for travel, food, other
materials and supplies (trophies}, and other. No OPS Wages shall be
funded by Greek Council.
E. OPS Wages for SA&O Accounting and Elections will be funded in a
lump sum.
F. The 5 7th Student Senate and its graduate representatives request
that COGS provide appropriate funding for OPS wages needed by
Alumni Village.
G. Funding Boards may not allocate more than 20% to the food category
total for any organization.
H. Any expenditure from the Safer Connection allocation requires the
signature of both the student body president and senate president.
They may only act upon recommendations from the Safer Connection
committee.
I. The 57 th Student Senate recommends that future senates fully fund the
WRC and the SGA lobbyist.
Specific Instructions
A. Any monies not spent on Homecoming shall be shifted to the Senate
Projects Account.
B. The 57 th Student Senate recommends that at least 1 Senate
Representative serve on all Homecoming Committees that involve A&S
fees.
VI. SEVERABILITY CLAUSES
A. All clauses in the Proviso Language for Bill 2005 shall be
considered fully severable.

BILL 3
Chapter 324 Leaves of Absences During the Summer Session for Members
of the Executive Branch
A.:_ Purpose
1..:.. The purpose of this chapter shall apply to the following
officers of the Executive Branch to take a leave of
absence during the summer session. and set forth the
procedures to select their temporary replacements during
that term .
.§..:.. Applicability and Scope
The provisions of this chapter shall apply to the
following officers of the Executive Branch:
The Student Body Treasurer
The Executive Chief of Staff
The Student Body Attorney General
The Executive Cabinet· Members
All Executive Bureau Directors
All Executive Agency Directors
All Affiliated Project Directors
~ Individual Executive Agencies. Executive Bureaus. and
Affiliated Projects may make their own rules regarding
summer leaves of absences for their officers. including
restricting their Directors from taking a summer leave
of absence. If no such rule exist. then the procedure
outlined in this chapter shall apply.
h The Student Body President and Student Body Vice
President shall not be permitted to take a leave of
absence during the summer session.
Procedure
1..:.. All eligible officers shall notify the Student Body
President in writing on or before the last day of spring
final examinations at the University of their intention
to take a leave of absence during one or more summer
academic sessions.
At the conclusion of spring final examinations at the
University. the Student Body President shall appoint
temporary officers to fill all or some of these vacated
seats at his/her discretion. These temporary officers

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
must meet all of the qualifications for the office to
which they are being appointed as if they were appointed
in the normal. permanent manner. All temporary officers
appointed to positions requiring Senate confirmation
must be confirmed by a majority vote of Senate. These
nominations by the Student Body President shall go
directly to the floor at the earliest possible summer
session of the Senate.
All appointees to the Executive Branch during the summer
session shall be on notice that their appointments are
of a temporary nature. Their term of office shall
terminate on the last day of final examination for the
summer academic term .
.i..:.. All temporary executive officers are subject to
impeachment by the Student Senate and dismissal by the
Student Body President according to the appropriate
statutes.

Chapter 507
507 A.
Court Review of Legislative Bills
Title and Purpose
1. This act shall be called the "Student Supreme Court
Legislative Bill and Review Act of 1998",
hereinafter referred to as the "Legislative Bills
Review Act".
2 . The purpose of this act is to provide for an
effective procedure for the review of properly
filed legislative bills upon the request of the
Judiciary Committee or the sponsors of bills. The
purpose of this review is only· to provide assurance
that if the bill were to become law, it would be in
compliance with all applicable federal, state,
local and university laws, as well as
constitutional. The Supreme Court is expressly
prohibited from using this power of review to make
public policy or any similar judgments on the bill
that would be inconsistent with the fair and
impartial role of the Judicial Branch.
