TITLE VII STUDENT BODY ELECTION CODE
Chapter 700 Short Title
History: Amended by 44th Senate Bills 104, 161, 162, 163
and 166. Revised by 45th Senate Bills 155 and 172.
Revised by the 46th Senate Bills 34 and 35. Revised by
the 47th Senate Bills 14, 61, 62, 71, 78, 99, 174, 177
and 186. Revised by the 48th Senate Bills 19, 31, 65,
66, 75, 109, 119, 152 and 156. Revised by the 49th
Senate Bills 6 and 116. Revised by the 50th Student
Senate Bills 51, 146 and 162. Revised by the 51st Senate
Bills 16, 17, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 30, 72, 105 and 121 A,
121 C. Revised by the 53 rd Senate Bills 8, 12, 47 and
119. Revised by the 54 th Senate Bills 11, 25, 64, 82 and
106, 110 (A), 113 and 117. Revised by the 55~ Senate
Bills 45, 71, 92 and 103.
Chapters 700 through 719 of the Student Body Statutes
shall be known and hereby referred to as the "Student
Body Election Code".
The Election Code shall not be changed within three (3)
weeks of an election.
Chapter 701 Definitions
701.1 The following words and phrases, when used in this title shall
be defined as follows:
A. Campaigning - The publicizing or solicitation of support
for or against a ballot item or candidate for an
elective office of the student body, and calling forth
the action to vote.
B. Campaign Contribution - The gift or furnishing of money,
materials, supplies, professional services, or any in-
kind contribution to any campaign in any form.
C. Campaign Expenses - The fair market value of any goods
or services paid for or received by the campaign for the
purpose of advertising candidates, advertising political
parties during active campaigning, and/or calling for
an action to vote. This shall include setup or
production fees, sales tax, or any other secondary costs
for goods and services.
1. All items posted prior to the beginning of active
campaigning that do not call for the action to vote
shall not constitute a campaign expense. This
shall include all campaign materials.

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
D.
2. Fair Market value of a single item shall be defined
as the retail (non-discounted) value of that single
item.
3. Discounted items that are available to all persons
and parties at the time of purchase shall be
exempted from fair market value criterion.
4. This section shall not be construed to apply to
speakers, volunteers, and other campaign workers of
a purely voluntary, unpaid nature.
5. To question the "fair market value" of a good or
service declared by a candidate or party, the
questioning party must obtain and submit an
affidavit from the contractor or merchant in
question disputing the candidate or party's claim
of fair market value, when such claims understates
fair market value.
Campaign Materials - any material, including but not
limited to posters, placards, signs, signboards,
leaflets, folders, handbills, fliers, banners, tee
shirts, buttons, chalk, paint, handwritten announcements
or circulars of any size and consistency that publicize
a candidate for an elected office of the student body,
and calling the action to vote.
E. Candidate - Any student seeking to be elected as an
officer of Student Government.
F. Current Inflation Adjustment - A multiplier to the
campaign expense limits based on the current Consumer
price Index (CPS) used to index campaign expense limits
to inf lat ion or deflation. The Current Inf lat ion
Adjustment, hereinafter referred to as the CIA, shall be
determined as follows:
CIA=(Current CPI)/(Based CPI).
The Base CPI is the CPI of September 1998 (163.6). The
Current CPI is the CPI reported for the first month of
the semester during which the election is held, or the
most recent CPI report by the US Government at the
beginning of the filing period should that month's CPI
not yet be available. In all cases, the CPI for All
Urban Consumers (the CPI-U) reported by the US
Government shall be used. The Supervisor of Elections
and the SGA Business Manager shall be responsible for
promulgating the adjusted expense limits to all
candidates and political parties.
2

elected office with the Elections Supervisor.
H. Independent Candidate - any candidate who is not running
with a party.

recorded.
J. Political Party Any number of persons properly
registered with the Supervisor of Elections, working
together to establish, promote, or gain acceptance for
some kind of government cause, opinion, etc., which they
hold in common.
K. Electorate The electorate shall be the entire
registered student body at FSU. The electorate shall be
divided into colleges and special seats. Only those
enrolled in a specific college may vote for candidates
seeking to represent that college.

determining the candidate who will assume off ice by
majority vote.

Recall Elections
The Elections Supervisor shall conduct recall elections in
accordance with Article VII of the Student Body Constitution.
The official ballot shall state the name of the office of the
official in question, and two hundred words or less, the
reasons for demanding recall of the officer(s) as set forth in
the recall petition(s), and in no more than two hundred words
of the officer's defense. The ballot must include the
statement: "Shall the following officers retain their seats."
Voters shall vote "YES" or "NO" on the recall. A sample
ballot shall be available at each polling site in accordance
with Article VII of the Constitution.
If a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the students voting elect to
recall the official, his term of office shall cease upon
certification of the election results by the Elections
Commission. The vacancy created shall be filled as provided
by the Student Body Constitution and the Student Body
Statutes.
The Supervisor of Elections shall print the recall petition
and the officer's defense in a campus newspaper during the
week preceding the recall election.
Senate shall provide the funds for conducting a recall
election.

BILL 23
A revision to the Student Body Statutes Chapter 205, the Code of Ethics
Chapter 205 Code of Ethics
205 .1 This act shall be entitled "the Student Government Code of
Ethics." The intent of this code is to strengthen the faith
and confidence of the Student Body in Student Government.
205.2 Legislative intent and declaration of policy.
205.3
A. It is essential to the proper conduct and operation of
Student Government that its officials be independent and
impartial, and that public office not be used for
private gain. Student Government officers and employees
hold their position for the benefit of the Student Body.
Such officers and employees are bound to observe in
their official acts, the highest standards of ethics
consistent with this code recognizing that promoting the
public interest and maintaining the respect of the
student body in their Student Government must be the
foremost concern.
B. It is the intent of this act to protect the integrity of
Student Government by prescribing conflicts of interest
and unethical practices. It shall serve as the basis of
discipline for those who violate its provisions.
C. Any student have the right to file a complaint when they
feel that a violation of the Code of Ethics has occurred
with the Student Supreme Court.
1. Any organization has the right to establish
additional ethical criteria or penalties in its
constitution and bylaws.
Standards of Conduct
A. In order to preserve the integrity of the Florida State
University Student Government Association, its officers
and employees must disclose all potential or actual
conflicts of interests.
1. Conflict of Interest means any business or
professional activity or direct or indirect
financial interest that would place a person in a
position where there is an opportunity to disregard
the public interests of the student body for his or
her own private interests.

Corrective Actions
Freezing of Funds
1. The Student Body President or the Student Body
Treasurer may, upon finding an organization,
executive agency, bureau or funding board in
violation of the Finance Code, freeze an account
(excluding the accounts of the Senate and Student
Supreme Court) for a period not to exceed ten
school days. Two school days prior to such
freezing, the Student Body President or the Student
Body Treasurer must notify in writing the chief
officer of the organization, agency, bureau or
funding board whose funds are being frozen and the
Senate, the reason of such action and the duration
of the account freeze. Upon two-thirds vote of the
Senate the reason of such action pertaining to this
section by the Student Body President or the
Student Body Treasurer may be rescinded.

Student Government Statutes. The President of the
Senate must notify, the Chief Officer, the Business
Manager of SA&O Accounting and the President of the
Student Body, the reason of such action and the

Budget deficits
Any organization, executive agency, bureau, or funding
board that acquires a deficit may be placed on probation
by a joint action requiring the consent of both the
Student Body President and the Student Body Treasurer
and the Student Senate President have been notified in
writing of such action.
During the probation period the organization shall:
1. Be required to eliminate the deficit by self-
generated monies, or transfer of funds as
recommended by the Student Body Auditor.
2. Not be eligible to receive additional funding
without a two-thirds vote of the Senate.
Notice of probation and removal from probation shall be
given in writing by the Student Body Auditor to SA&O

Penalty Measures
If an SA&O recipient is found to be in violation of the
Finance Code the following actions may be taken.
1. On a first offense an organization's funds will be
frozen as provided in Chapter 805.1.
2. On a second offense, during the current fiscal
year, impeachment proceedings may be initiated by
the Senate against the Director and Financial
Officer of the organization. The organization may
also be placed on probation for a period of 16
weeks.
3. If the organization, while on probation, violates
the Finance Code the Senate may bring proceedings
to restructure or disband the organization.
If an SA&O recipient has been placed on probation, the
following procedures must be followed by the probationer
for the duration of the probationary period.
1. Bimonthly reports must be presented to the Student
Senate on the organization's efforts to correct the
violations. This presentation will be made by the
organization's Director and Financial Officer.
2. All expenditures, budgetary matters, and funding
requests of the organization must have the written
approval of the Student Body President.
3. All officers and Board members of the organization
will be required to attend and complete a Finance
Code counseling session set up by the Business
Manager of SA&O Accounting.
4. All financial records of the organization must be
submitted for review to the Student Body Auditor's
Office at the end of each month.

BILL 39
Chapter 607 Congress of Graduate Students
607.1 A. An organization entitled Congress of Graduate Students
{hereafter referred to as COGS} is established on the
main campus of the Florida State University to implement
the general policies of the Florida State University
Student Government Association {hereafter referred to
FSU-SGA} and the specific policies of COGS.
B . Purpose of COGS
1. To provide graduate and professional students at
FSU, through COGS, an opportunity to participate in
the decision-making process.
2. To consider, make recommendations and act upon
phases of graduate/professional student life at
FSU.
3. To serve as the principal forum for decisions on
matters of broad concern to the
graduate/professional students at FSU.
4. To serve as the chief means by which
graduate/professional students may express their
university concerns for FSU-SGA.
c. Membership
1. COGS shall be composed of representatives as
defined by the COGS Constit~tion Code.
2. The COGS Faculty Advisor shall be an ex-officio
member of COGS.
3. The Speaker of COGS shall preside over COGS and
shall vote only in the case of a tie among the
representatives.
4. A Financial Officer shall be elected by COGS to
serve in the absence, removal, or resignation of

Veto of Bill 43
Please accept this memo as an explanation of my Veto of senate Bill 43. I agree with the
sentiments behind bill 43 but I would rather see the Senate be more specific in its
reference to elected officials. My specific concerns are in reference to the clause that lists
"all elected Bureau, Agency, and Affiliated Projects perso1mel" as elected officials. I feel
it would be more beneficial for us all if we delineated the elected officers that we are
refen-ing to. We are aware of the fact that the Black Student Union and Hispanic/Latino
Student Union are the only agencies that elect its upper leadership and we should have no
problem actually listing these agencies by name in Section 405.1 (A) and classifying
them as elected positions. We do not have elected Bureau and Affiliated Project leaders
and mentioning these groups could perhaps add confusion. A veto will allow the Senate
to reconsider this action and hopefully conect this issue without having to resubmit a new
bill. I respect the work of Senate and perhaps it is this respect that drives me to ensure
that we are passing and signing bills that are above reproach and interpretation.

Chapter 700 Short Title
Chapters 700 through 719 of the Student Body Statutes
shall be known and hereby referred to as the "Student
Body Election Code".
The Election Code shall not be changed within three (3)
weeks of an election.
Chapter 701 Definitions
701.l The following words and phrases, when used in this title shall
be defined as follows:
A. Campaigning - The publicizing or solicitation of support
for or against a ballot item or candidate for an elected
office of the ~tudent ~ody, and calling forth the action
to vote.
B. Campaign Contribution - The gift or furnishing of money,
materials, supplies, professional services, or any in-
kind contribution to any campaign in any form.
C. Campaign Expenses - The fair market value of any goods
or services paid for or received by the campaign for the
purpose of advertising candidates, advertising political
parties during active campaigning, and/or calling for
an action to vote. This shall include setup or
production fees, sales tax, or any other secondary costs
for goods and services.
1. All items posted prior to the beginning of active
campaigning that do not call for the action to vote
shall not constitute a campaign expense. This
shall include all campaign materials.
2. Fair Market value of a single i tern shall be defined
as the retail (non-discounted) value of that single
item.
3. Discounted items that are available to all persons
and parties at the time of purchase shall be
exempted from fair market value criterion.
4. This section shall not be construed to apply to
speakers, volunteers, and other campaign workers of
a purely voluntary, unpaid nature.
s. To question the "fair market value" of a good or
service declared by a candidate or party, the
questioning party must obtain and submit an
affidavit from the contractor or merchant in

Current Inflation Adjustment - A multiplier to the
campaign expense limits based on the current Consumer
price Index (CPS) used to index campaign expense limits
to inflation or def lat ion. The Current Inflation
Adjustment, hereinafter referred to as the CIA, shall be
determined as follows:
CIA=(CUrrent CPI)/(Based CPI).
The Base CPI is the CPI of September 1998 (163.6). The
Current CPI is the CPI reported for the first month of
the semester during which the election is held, or the
most recent CPI report by the US Government at the
beginning of the filing period should that month's CPI
not yet be available. In all cases, the CPI for All
Urban Consumers (the CPI-U) reported by the US
Government shall be used. The Supervisor of Elections
and the SGA Business Manager shall be responsible for
p~omulgating the adjusted expense limits to all
candidates and political parties.

some kind of government cause, opinion, etc., which they
hold in common.

BILL 95
A revision to the Student Body Statutes Chapters 506 Band C, and 712.2.
Chapter 506 Review of Constitutional Amendments
History: Added by the 48th Senate Bill 28. Revised by
the 49th Senate Bill SO. Revised by the 51 st Senate Bills
106 and 118.
B. All proposed constitutional amendments and referenda
shall be reviewed by the Student Supreme Court for
vagueness and inconsistency with Federal and State laws
and regulations, within twenty-one (21) days of receipt,
before the Senate approves the measure(s) to be placed
on the ballot. it is voted on in Senate.
h The decision of the Court shall be advisory only.
If a bill or constitutional amendment is amended
after an opinion has been rendered, said bill must
be resubmitted for a new opinion. In no case may
the Supreme Court block vote prevent the student
body from voting on a proposed constitutional
amendment from the ballot except if unless such
amendment is found to clearly violate federal,
state, or local law, including the Student Body
Constitution and Statutes. Nor has it the
authority to overturn the passage of a
constitutional amendment, except in the
aforementioned circumstance.
h_ All Statements of Intent regarding proposed
constitutional amendments and referenda shall be
reviewed by the Student Supreme Court to insure
that the language of the statement adequately and
fairly reflects the intent of the ballot proposal.
~ No ·proposed constitutional amendment or
referendum shall be placed on the ballot
until the adequacy and fairness of the
Statement of Intent is approved.
!t:_ In the event that the Student Supreme Court
does not offer an opinion within 21 days of
receipt of the Statement of Intent, the
statement and its accompanying proposed
constitution amendment or referendum shall be
considered approved and be immediately
certified for placement on the ballot.

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.text:
C.
Chapter 712.2
If a provision does not satisfy the vagtteness e:nd
inconsistenc~ requirements enumerated in Chapter 506 B.
as reviewed by the Student Supreme Court, the sponsors
shall have an opportunity to correct the deficiencies
and resubmit the provision to the Student Supreme Court.
The Student Supreme Court shall submit a written opinion
detailing the findings of its review.
Statement of Intent
All ballot questions proposing constitutional amendments
and referenda shall display a "Statement of Intent" to
be placed above the amendment or referenda text.
h The Statement of Intent shall be no longer than 100
words.
The Statement of Intent shall be written by the
primary sponsor of the proposed constitutional
amendment and/or his/her designee(s).
The Statement of Intent shall be presented to the
Senate when the amendment is put up for Senate
approval. The Statement of Intent shall be
considered part of the piece of legislation being
voted on for approval by the Senate. and shall pass
or fail jointly with its accompanying legislation.
The provisions of Chapter 712.2 apply to both measures
proposed by the Senate and by petition process as
enumerated in Article VI of the Student Body
Constitution.
The provisions of Chapter 712.2 shall not apply to any
proposed constitutional amendment pending the ballot at
the time of its enactment.

Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court and subject

standing with the University. The General Counsels

fall within the court's jurisdiction.

drafting and execution of all motions before the

court.

Supreme Court. Additionally, the General Counsels shall
be subject to impeachment by the Student Senate in the
ordinary manner.

BILL 110
Chapter 324 Leaves of Absences During the Summer Session for Members
of the Executive Branch
History: Added by the 56 th Senate Bill 3.
A. Purpose
It.!...:.. The purpose of this chapter shall be to allow for
certain members of the Executive Branch to take a leave
of absence during the summer session. and to set forth
the procedures to select their temporary replacements
during that term. apply to the following officers of the
Elxecutive Branch to take a leave of absence dttring the
sttmmer session, and set forth the procedures to select
their tentporary replacenrents during that term.
B. Applicability and Scope
1. The provisions of this chapter shall apply to the
following officers of the Executive Branch:
a.
b.
c.
d.
e.
f.
g.
The Student Body Treasurer
The Executive Chief of Staff
The Student Body Attorney General
The Executive Cabinet Members
All Executive Bureau Directors
All Executive Agency Directors
All Affiliated Project Directors
2. Individual Executive Agencies, Executive Bureaus, and
Affiliated Projects may make their own rules regarding
summer leaves of absences for their officers, including
restricting their Directors from taking a summer leave
of absence. If no such rule exist, then the procedure
outlined in this chapter shall apply.
3. The Student Body President and Student Body Vice
President shall not be permitted to take a leave of
absence during the summer session.
C. Procedure
1. All eligible officers shall notify the Student Body
President in writing on or before the last day of spring
final examinations at the University of their intention
to take a leave of absence during one or more summer
academic sessions.

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
2. At the conclusion of spring final examinations at the
University, the Student Body President shall appoint
temporary officers to fill all or some of these vacated
seats at his/her discretion. These temporary officers
must meet all of the qualifications for the office to
which they are being appointed as if they were appointed
in the normal, permanent manner. All temporary officers
appointed to positions requiring Senate confirmation
must be confirmed by a majority vote of Senate. These
nominations by the Student Body President shall go
directly to the floor at the earliest possible summer
session.i§.) of the Senate.
3. All appointees to the Executive Branch during the summer
session shall be on notice that their appointments are
of a temporary nature. Their term of off ice shall
terminate on the last day of final examination~ for the
summer academic term(s) that they are serving for.
subject to section 7 below.
4. All temporary executive officers are subject to
impeachment by the Student Senate and dismissal by the
Student Body President according to the appropriate
statutes.
All temporary officers of the Executive Branch who are
entitled to compensation shall be compensated for the
summer term(s) in question as if they were permanent
officers. This compensation shall cease at the close of
the summer academic term(s) that they are serving for.
or should they resign from off ice. which ever comes
first .
.2..:.. All of the permanent officers of the Executive Branch
who take a leave of absence for the summer term(s) shall
receive no compensation for any summer term that they
are not enrolled in. Such compensation shall only
resume when they assume their permanent offices at the
opening of classes in the fall semester. or if and when
they begin attending classes for a subsequent summer
session.
L All temporary Executive officers are entitled to serve
throughout the summer session for which they have been
appointed to. al though they shall immediately vacate
their off ice if and when their permanent counterpart
begins attending classes for a subsequent summer session
in the same academic year.

807.6 Business School Allocations Committee (BSAC)
History: Revised by the 49th Senate Bill 14. Revised by
54 th Senate Bill 126. Revised by the 56 th Senate
C. Selection
Selection of BSAC shall be as stated below.
1. BSAC shall at all times be composed of eight {8)
students at the FSU College of Business. n,embers
of the Interorganizational Business Council (IBC).
2 . 'fhe These students ncentbers of IBC, as e!ltablished
in Chapter 606 of the Student Body Statutes, will
be elected representatives from the various student
organizations within the College of Business.
These organizations must be recognized by the
student advisory committee advisor within the
College of Business.
3 . The eight representatives n,entbers of IBC who serve
on the BSAC Board will rotate each semester after
the initial eight {8) organizational
representatives have been selected by a process of
number drawing. New organizations coming into the
FSU College of Business Business School will be
added to the bottom of the current listed order of
organizations.
4. An administrative representative appointed by the
Dean of the College of Business shall be a non-
voting and advisory member of the BSAC Board. This
representative shall assist the Board in ensuring
that BSAC follows the guidelines established by
these Statutes and the Student Government Finance
Code. This administrative representative shall
serve as long as the Dean of the College of
Business deems appropriate.
s. A Student Senator from the College of Business
shall be appointed by the Student Senate President
to serve as an "ex-officio member" of the BSAC
Board. The Student Senator will also act as BSAC' s
liaison to the Student Senate. This appointment
will be made at the beginning of each Fall semester
and shall be in effect for one year. The appointed
Senator shall not be a voting member of BSAC.

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
6. Vacancies of the BSAC Board, other than those of
the Administrative Representative and Student
Senator, shall be filled by the organization whose
member vacates their position. This position shall
be held for the remainder of the prior
organizational member's term.
7. If the organization whose turn for representation
on the BSAC Board waives their respective turn to
serve, the next organization in line for a seat on
the Board, as determined under Statute 807. 6 C (3) ,
will fill that vacancy. The organization that has
waived their turn to serve must then wait for their
next regular rotation before serving on the BSAC
Board.

A revision to the Student Body Statutes Chapter 318.6, to clarify the

318.6 Executive Agency Positions
A. Agency Directors
1. The Directors of the agencies shall be chosen in
accordance with Chapter 318 . 6, unless otherwise
stipulated in their individual chapter in Title X.
B. In all cases other than elected Directors, the Board of
Directors (Board) shall choose two nominations by a
majority vote for Agency Director and forward those
applicants to the Student Body President. The Student
Body President will then choose a candidate from the
applications forwarded from the Board and the applicants
from the candidate search period and forward the
candidate to the Senate within two weeks for
confirmation.
C. In the event that the Student Body President feels that
any of the candidates are ungualif i·ed he/she may request
an additional candidate search period.
D. Within two weeks of the Director's confirmation, that
Director will appoint any non-elected Assistant
Director. This appointment shall be ratified by
majority vote of the Board and then forwarded to the SGA
Senate.
1. In the event that the Agency Directorship is
vacated, the Assistant Director shall assume the
Directorship and proceed with filling the Assistant
Directorship as outline in Chapter 318.6.
2. Agency Directors and Assistant Directors who are
appointed shall remain in office until they are
dismissed, impeached, or upon installation of their
successor.
E. The Director shall serve, protect and promote the
mission statement of the agency.

Creation and Purpose
A. Creation
This act shall create an Agency of the Student
Government Association known as the Black Student Union
(BSU) .
B. Purpose
The BSU shall serve primarily to promote and provide for
the social welfare of the Black Student Body at the
Florida State University. The BSU shall be limited
neither to the aforementioned objectives nor to the
Florida State University in scope. The BSU shall also
strive to provide and promote economic, political and
academic enrichment through its activities, and it shall
serve as a catalyst to the enlightenment of the Florida
State University community to the distinct and proud
cultural heritage of Black people in America as well as
on the African continent. Finally, it shall be a source
of edification of the Black experience at Florida State
University.
Membership
Membership shall include all students that take an active role
in the furtherance of the cause of justice and equality for
Blacks without regard to race, creed, color, religion, sex or
national origin.

BILL 69
A revision to the Student Body Statutes Chapter 805.7 and 100.
805.7
CHAPTER 100
C. All money transfer requests within an organization's
budget, excluding Campus Recreation and Union, during
the last thi:ee (3) months thirty days of a budget year
must include a document showing the need for the
transfer, explaining why the recipient budget category
was inadequately funded, and showing that the transfer
is not intended to circumvent the Sweepings process.
B. 1. Each Chapter may be subdivided by means of a
decimal arrangement. For instance, Chapter 199 may
be divided into sections 199.1, 199.2, 199.3, etc.
Each section may in turn be subdivided by means of
letters and further decimal places (after the
letters) so that as many subsections are obtained
as necessary.
2. Each section or subsection in the statutes shall
have printed after it, a history giving the Senate
and Bill numbers in which it was amended.
C. All Student Body officers must comply with the Student
Body Statutes. Willful and deliberate disregard of
these Statutes and/or section thereof shall be grounds
of impeachment in accordance with Article VII, Section
3 of the Student Body Constitution.
D. Within the Executive Branch the following elective or
appointed offices shall be considered major offices:
E.
President
Vice President
Cabinet Officers
Director of Agencies, Bureaus and Affiliated Projects
Within the Legislative Branch the following elective or
appointed offices shall be considered major offices:
Senators
Union Board

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.text:
F.
Campus Recreation Board
Funding Board Chairpersons
Within the Judiciary Branch the following elective or
appointed offices shall be considered major offices:
Justices of the Supreme Court
University Defender
General Counsels
Clerk of the Court
G. Miscellaneous
Speaker of COGS
Supervisor of Elections
H. Major offices may only be held by FSU students
registered for at least six (6) hours in both the fall
and spring semesters, respectively, and at least three
I.
( 3) hours during the summer session. Senators not
taking three (3) hours in the summer session may go on
leave of absence rather than being expelled from their
office.
To be considered a student for purposes of holding OPS
positions, an individual must be enrolled for and taking
one semester hour.
J. All Student Government officers may take a leave of
absence in the summer term. At other times they must
have approval of the Student Body President (for the
Executive Branch) or the Chief Justice of the Student
Supreme Court for the Judicial Branch).
K. To hold any SGA office undergraduates must maintain a
2.0 or higher and graduate students must maintain a 3.0
or higher cumulative FSU GPA.
